t: *n.* –Used as the name of the letter *a* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*verbal suf.* –Used added to the end of the verb to indicate the past, the passive, or completed action. ⟨**Aínbo yákatara nokon wáata iki.** The woman who is sitting is my maternal aunt.⟩ ⟨**Ja yákatatonra ea óinai.** The one who is sitting is looking at me.⟩ –Used with a verb compounded of the past participle and *iqui* to indicate the past tense, especially in a narrative. ⟨**Moátianronki Yóashiko Inkaki rétekana iki. Réteaxonki westíora jóni jawen xenín síkita iki.** They say that long ago the Stingy Inca was killed, and that a man painted himself with his fat.⟩ –Used at the end of the subordinate verb in an adverbial clause. ⟨**Papán yóiara, en átapa béai.** If dad sends me, I bring the hen.⟩ –Used at the end of the subordinate verb in a subordinate-conjunction clause. ⟨**Nokon wái óroa pekaora, ea náshiai.** After clearing my garden, I go to bathe.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.1.5.b; 5.3.2; 7.4.3.1; 7.4.3.2
*verbal suf.* –Used added to the verb root with the meaning of "to make/cause". ⟨*axeati* to make learn, to teach⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2

*postp. suf.* : from –Used with adverbs of place to indicate the origin of the subject of the sentence. –Often used with *-ax* in the compound form *-ax* to indicate a place of origin. ⟨**Eara nénoa iki.** I am from here.⟩ ⟨**Jára ónoax jóke.** He came from over there.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5; 8.3.2

*n.* **ábionin** [from Spanish] 1 : airplane ⟨**Rimámea ápo ábionin jóketianra noa rároke.** When the President came from Lima by airplane, we were glad.⟩ 2 : small plane ⟨**Káshiboainoa ábionbora moa masáti keyóke. Ixónbira nato simánanin moa bénxoaribakanai.** All the small planes from Cashibococha have broken down, but this week they are going to repair them.⟩ *syn.* naíwaporo
*n.* **abón** : manshaco (a wading bird) ⟨**Moátianronki Inkánki jawen sontárobo axánti ráanxon áboanike.** They say that long ago the Inca sent his soldiers to fish and turned them into manshacos.⟩
*n.* **ábokoman** [from Shipibo *ábo* manshaco (a wading bird) + *kóma* panguana (a tinamou)] : camungo (the horned screamer bird)
*also* **háche** *n.* [from Spanish *hache*] –Used as the name of the letter *h* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*v.i.* **aéika** : to burp ⟨**Eara oránshi shéash aéike.** I burped after drinking a soda.⟩ ⟨**Eara íno pisi áeike —akín manánxawen aká iki.** The motelo (tortoise) said: —My breath reeked of jaguar when I burped.⟩

*verbal suf.* –Used in the main verb to indicate non-past tense. ⟨**Moara néteai.** Day is already breaking.⟩ ⟨**Bakísha ea kái.** I am going to go tomorrow.⟩ –Used to indicate the active, present, or habitual-action participle. ⟨**Isára nóyai jawékibo iki.** Little birds are flying creatures.⟩ –Used as a suffix on the verb of a subordinate clause with a conjunction. ⟨**Icha binónra en píke, pórokan chéshai kaman.** I have eaten so many aguajes (a palm fruit) that my stomach hurts.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2; 7.4.3.1; 7.4.3.2

*postp. suf.* **-nko** –Used added to a noun with the meaning of "to" or "toward" (the place indicated by the noun). –Used to indicate the destination of the subject of an intransitive verb of motion. ⟨**Máioshiain kaíra jóni réokooke táxa tsákaax.** While he was going to Pucallpa, the man ran into a palizada (a mass of drifting logs) and his canoe capsized.⟩ ⟨**Kontámanain yamébi kaíra noa Tiróntainoax néteke.** When we traveled to Contamana, we reached dawn at Tiruntán.⟩ ⟨**Jóni Iparianko káitianra, jawen bonánti yómetsoakanke.** When the man went to Iparía, they stole his bag.⟩ 1 : in –Used to indicate the location of the subject of a copulative verb or of an intransitive verb that indicates an action. ⟨**Rámara pápa Ikítoain iki.** Dad is now in Iquitos.⟩ ⟨**Rámara títa Kakónko iki.** Mom is now in †Caco.⟩ ⟨**Rabé báritiara ea Jépeweain téeke.** I have worked for two years in †Yarinacocha.⟩ ⟨**Básibiresa pápa Róaboyanko téeke.** For a long time my father worked in †Roaboya.⟩ –Used in the combined form *-ainoa* or *-nconia*, meaning 'in', to indicate the location of the direct or indirect object of a transitive verb of action. ⟨**Kokánronki Xánayainoa witábo neníchina oínkato.** They say that in †Shanaya my uncle saw posts stuck upright in the water.⟩ –Used in the combined form *-ainxon* or *-nkoxon* to indicate the place of an action. ⟨**Róoyainxonra nokon kokán xóboayantanke.** While in †Roya my uncle built a house.⟩ 2 : of : from –Used combined with *-oa* or *-nia* in the forms *-ainoa* or *-nconia*. –Used to indicate the origin of the subject of a copulative verb or the origin of the object of a transitive verb. ⟨**Eara Ikítoainoa iki.** I am from Iquitos.⟩ ⟨**Jénepanshiainoa koríkinin títa bíi katira en shínanai.** I am thinking of going to the Genepanshea stream to get raw silver from there.⟩ ⟨**Oropampankonia non Inka bíi kátira westíora jonín shínanai.** A certain man is thinking of going to bring our Inca from the Urubamba River.⟩ 3 : of : from –Used combined with *-oa* and *-ax* in the form *-ainoax* or with *-nia* and *-ax* in the form *-nkoniax* –Used to indicate the origin of the subject of an intransitive verb of motion. ⟨**Eara Yarínainoax jóke.** I have come from †Yarina.⟩ ⟨**Eara Kakónkoniax nokóke.** I have arrived from †Caco.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2

*verbal suf.* [from Shipibo *-ai*, present-verb suf. + *-n*, subordinate-verb suf.] –Used at the end of the subordinate verb with the meaning of "when", "while", "because", or "if". ⟨**Títa náshiainra, jawen báke níi meran káke.** While the mother was bathing, her son went to the forest.⟩ –Used postposed at the end of the subordinate verb and before the suffix *-bi*, so that the compound suffix *-ainbi* has the force of "although". ⟨**Ja ói beáinbira, ea kái.** Although it may rain, I am going.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2 *syn.* -aitian; -anan; -ax; kopí; -i; -ketian; -tian

*n.* **aínbon** *Konibo* **aínbaon** *pish.* **aínbaen** [from Shipibo *awin* wife + *-bo* people] : woman : a person or human being of the female sex : the female of the human species ⟨**Jenényoshin aínbaonronki jóni bónike béneanoxon.** They say that long ago a mermaid carried off a man to make him her husband.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.5
*n.* **aínboapon** [from Shipibo *aínbo* woman + *ápo* chief] : queen. See Grammar Sketch 7.1.5
*n.* **aínbobaken** [from Shipibo *aínbo* woman + *báke* child] : girl ⟨**Aínbobakera jawen titán tsískike.** This girl's mother painted her groin.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.5

*verbal suf.* [from Shipibo *-ain* in + *-nko* in] –Used added to the verb root in a verb phrase that functions as a noun or as an adverb of place, with the meaning of "in the place where (a specific action) happens". ⟨**Ea náshiainkora benés ike.** Where I bathe is not deep.⟩ ⟨**Jan tóo akaínko káxa, ea ráketai.** I am afraid to go where he is shooting.⟩

*Konibo* **awínwetsa** *xet.* **aíntsa** *n.* **aínwetsan** *Konibo* **awínwetsan** *xet.* **aíntsan** [from Old Shipibo *ainwetsa* the wife's sister, another wife] : a man's sister-in-law ⟨**Joninronki jawen awínwetsa paénxon wéxanike.** They say that once a drunken man cut off his sister-in-law's head with a *wéxati* knife.⟩

*verbal suf.* [from Shipibo *-ai*, present participle + *-tian* when] –Used after the subordinate verb with the sense of "while," "when," "because," or "if." ⟨**Papán píaitianra, Jósikan átapa bénake.** While dad was eating, José was looking for his hen.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2 *syn.* **-ain**

*also* **ajénte** *n.* **ajíntinin** *also* **ajéntenin** [from Spanish *agente*] : municipal officer ⟨**Ajíntinra tíati ákai jawen káibo kénakin.** The municipal officer sounds the horn to summon his fellow townspeople.⟩
*also* **Afrika** *n.* **Ajirikanin** *also* **Afrikanin** : Africa

*modifying suf.* : around –Used after the verb root and followed by *–tan.* ⟨**Nato xóbo kátekinra non oínhaketanke; ixónbira non jáwebi mérayamake.** We looked around this house, but we found nothing.⟩ ⟨**Báke míinkana wíniaitianronki jonín bénaaketankin Inkán báke méranike máno meranoa.** They tell that long ago a child was crying and a man was searching for him in the surrounding area and found him buried in the mud: it was the Son of the Inca.⟩
*n.* **akéninin** : a small species of heron that feeds on the horseflies of cattle ⟨**Epánra akéni réteke wakán peníketian.** My uncle killed an akéni heron while it was perched on top of a cow.⟩
*also* **awé** *interj.* [from Shipibo; subordinate forms of *áti* to do] –Used in reduplicated form with the sense of *do it* (fam.) or *do it* (formal).
See **-i**
*v.t.* **ákina** [from Shipibo *áti* to do + *–kin* helping] : to help ⟨**Jawen ráyosen wáiaitianra papán akínke.** When his son-in-law was clearing the garden plot, dad helped him.⟩ *syn.* –kin

*adj.* **akón** 1 : thin : skinny ⟨**Papán piára sarámpinin ikax áko banéke.** My cousin, dad's nephew, had measles and grew thin.⟩ 2 : dried up ⟨**Ipo máwatax áko bánetara poínkoskon píai.** The vulture eats the dead, dried-up carachamas (armored catfish).⟩ 3 : empty : hollow; *specif.* : without pulp ⟨**Káchio kakínra ochítinin manánxawe áko mérake, moa inón piá; ja biáxa pápa rároke jíria íti shínanax.** On going to the forest, the dog found an empty tortoise shell that a jaguar had eaten; and on picking it up, dad was glad, thinking it was still alive.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbora jakóma shinánya** **iki; paránta ákora ea ménike.** This woman is mean, because she gave me a plantain with no flesh.⟩ *syn.* AKO, WIRISH, OSHI, SHEPA can all be translated as "thin," but WIRISH focuses on a naturally small or narrow diameter (e.g., of a tree), whereas AKO can imply an illness that thins the body; OSHI suggests a body lacking its normal or expected thickness (e.g., of bread made with too little dough), and SHEPA implies the stunted growth of a living thing (e.g., of a plantain that hasn't filled out). *syn.* jáwebioma
*n.* **akómpanan** : rattlesnake ⟨**Noa akómpanan nátexara xetán jími béai.** When the rattlesnake bites us, blood comes from our gums.⟩
*adv.* : truly : sincerely ⟨**En mia akónkin yóiabira, mia jóyamaibake.** Even though I spoke to you sincerely, you didn't come yesterday.⟩
*n.* **akónteman** : cornegacho (a bird) ⟨**Akónteman jíwi xáteara sirán aká keska íkai.** When the cornegacho gnaws at a stick, it leaves a mark like the cut of a saw.⟩

*n.* **ákoronin** [from Shipibo *áko* hollow + *ronín* anaconda] : yacumama (a mythical water-boa) ⟨**Akoronronki máshi keska páro napon píkotai.** They say the yacumama appears in the middle of the river and looks like a sandbank.⟩ ⟨**Wapóro keskaribironki ákoron yamé píkotai.** They say the yacumama also appears at night in the form of a boat.⟩ *syn.* ronín

*v.i.* **ákoa** 1 : to grow thin ⟨**Nato jónira moa xoá iká iki; rámara moa ákoke ísinax.** This man used to be fat, but he got sick and grew thin.⟩ 2 : to dry out ⟨**Papán ronón ewa réteibatara moa ákoa iki.** The boa my father killed the other day has already dried out.⟩ *syn.* náxpeti; óshiti

*n.* **ákotirin** [from Shipibo *akótiri*, imitative of its call] : a small species of bird small and black, similar to the woodpecker and the víctor-díaz (a bird) ⟨**Xéna píaitianra nokon wetsán ákotiri tsákake.** While the little *ákotiri* was eating grubs, my brother shot it with an arrow.⟩
See **arámpiri**
See **Arimania**
See **árimintanti**
*n.* **amákanin** [from Spanish] : hammock ⟨**Jenényoshiman amákaronkiki nato ronón ewa.** They say the boa is the hammock of the yacurunas (water spirits).⟩ *syn.* **weyóti**

*n.* **ámakirin** : gamitana (a river fish) ⟨**Amakiri wákanawa ákaitianra jóni kétokan mápoke.** While the man was spearing gamitanas at a mijanada (fish run), a landslide on the riverbank buried him.⟩ [illustration: *ámakiri*]
*v.t.* **ámaa** [from Shipibo *áti,* *a-* + *-ma* to do/make] : to invite or offer (e.g., food)

*temporal suf.* [from Shipibo *a-,* root of *áti* to do + *-ma* not + *-tian* when + *-bi* although] : before : until ⟨**Ea joámatianbi nato warápo xéayamakanwe —akinki Inkán jato aká iki** The Inca told them: —Do not drink this guarapo (a fermented cane drink) until I come.⟩
*n.* **ámeman** : ronsoco (capybara) ⟨**Moátianronki jonínki amén mápoa iki rikán-** **kin.** Long ago a man caught a capybara while net-fishing (with a cast net).⟩ [illustration: *amén*]

*n.* **améntamon** [from Shipibo *amén* ronsoco (capybara) + *támo* cheek] : member of the amenture ethnolinguistic group : amenture ⟨**Améntamo jónibora moa shípiboya méskota iki.** The Amenture are now thoroughly intermixed with the shipibo.⟩
*n.* **aménwakan** : member of the amahuaca ethnolinguistic group : amahuaca ⟨**Aménwaka jónibora raómis ikí.** The Amahuaca have the custom of casting spells with plant potions.⟩
*n.* **ámikan** : cagüena (a dye plant) ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen chitónti ámikan pókoai.** The woman dyes her pampanilla (wraparound skirt) with cagüena dye.⟩

*n.* **ámikan éwan** [from Shipibo *amí,* *ámikan* a species of tree + *ewa,* augmentative] : itaúba (a hardwood tree) ⟨**Imirianra ámikan ewa ichá yóikanai.** They say itaúbas are abundant at Imiría.⟩
*adj.* **amíkeskatonin** [from Shipibo *amí* a species of tree + *keska* resembling] : violet-colored

*n.* **amíkon** *Konibo* **amíkonin** [from Spanish *amigo*] 1 : member of an ethnic group living at Cashiboya : person from Cashiboya ⟨**Nato amíko jónira chipónkiash nokóke.** This person from Cashiboya has come from downriver.⟩ 2 : member of the cocamilla ethnic group
*also* **Amérika** *n.* **Amírikan** *also* **Amérian** : America
*also* **Nórte Amerika** [from Spanish] : North America
[from Spanish] : South America : South America
*n.* **Ampón** [from Spanish *amb*, *o*, element of *Ambrosio*] –Used as a male name.
*also* **-en** *suf.* *n.* –Used as an ending marking the non-basic form of a noun or adjective. ⟨**Wítaxanra ea chéxai.** My leg hurts.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1
*n.* **ánakan** 1 : catahua (a tree) 2 : a demon identified with the catahua ⟨**Anakan bákeronkiki tónkobires.** They say the child of the catahua demon has bumps all over its body.⟩
*n.* **Anán** [from Spanish] –Used as a female name.
See under **átsa**

*subordinate-verb suf.* –Used with the sense of "while," "when," "because," or "if" as the final suffix on the subordinate verb. –Used to imply the coordination of two actions carried out by the same subject. ⟨**Néte xábatai mánaananra chíikan yóotai.** While waiting for dawn, he warms himself by the fire.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2 *syn.* -ain

*verbal suf.* **-ananan** *also* **-nan** –Used with the force of "mutually" to indicate reciprocity. –Used added to the root of a transitive verb, making the verb intransitive. ⟨**Ja átapa rabéra reteananai.** Those two hens are fighting each other.⟩ ⟨**Jónibora mashá iki bíananankana iki.** As they performed the traditional march, the men gathered together.⟩ ⟨**Nokon pápara jawen pátoron betan yómetsoananke kónxaman.** My father and his boss used to steal timber from each other.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2

*adj.* **anín** : big ⟨**Nokon papán áni inó retenike.** My dad killed a big jaguar.⟩ *syn.* ANI, ASPA, OE can all be translated as "big," but ANI refers to bigness in general, whereas ASPA implies a recep-tacle that is roomy and large, and OE refers to what is abnormally large.
See under **átapa**

*v.t.* **ániaa** *Konibo* **ániaka** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *-ati* to make] 1 : to raise (rear) ⟨**Títashokonbichora jawen bába ániake.** The little grandmother raised her grandchild all by herself.⟩ 2 : to enlarge : to expand ⟨**xóbo ániati** to enlarge the house⟩
*n.* **ánibon** *Konibo* **ánibaon**, *pish.* **ánibaen** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *-bo*, *plural suf.*] : parents ⟨**Jawen ánibaon pótaara báke mawáke.** The boy died abandoned by his parents.⟩
See under **íti**

*n.* **ánijeman** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *jéma* town] : a very large city ⟨**Anijema oínyosma ikáxa, Rimán káx nokon epán báke ratéke.** My paternal uncle's son went to Lima and was amazed, because he had never seen a big city.⟩
See under **kapé**
*n.* **ánikocharanin** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *kochára* spoon] : spoonful
See under **kóma**

*adj.* **ániman** *also* **ánimaan** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *-ma* not] : small : little ⟨**Anima átapara awápanin bóke.** The tigrillo (ocelot) carried off a small hen.⟩ ⟨**ánimashoko** tiny⟩ *syn.* ANIMA, MASHKO, SOTO can all be translated as "small." Whereas ANIMA refers to smallness in general, MASHKO is more specific for "short in stature" and may imply young age; and SOTO implies something (a bread roll, e.g.) that is short and thick as well as small.

*n.* **ánimain** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *mái* land] : region : zone ⟨**Píro iki kímisha áni máia: ániparo kexa Máshi; napon iki Ánimanan; néke iki Manísh Nía.** Peru has three regions: along the seashore is the Coast; in the center, the Highlands; and at the far end is the Jungle.⟩
*n.* **ánimanaman** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *manán* highlands] : mountain range

See under **motóro**
See under **paránta**

*n.* **ániparon** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *páro* river] : sea : ocean ⟨**Aniparomea béchomanra westíora aínbo bóke.** The sea waves carried off a woman.⟩ ⟨**Aniparoronki táshi iki.** They say the sea is salty.⟩
See under **póko**
See under **ríka**
See under **santíra**

*adj.* **anítaman** *Konibo* **anítamanin** [from Shipibo *aníta*, participle of *aníti* to grow + *-ma* not] : very small ⟨**Papán nóntira anítama iki, ja ráma aká.** The canoe dad made recently is very small.⟩

*v.i.* **ánia** : to grow (of an organism) ⟨**Inkán báke máno meran míina bexónronki joninki béchota iki; jainoaxonki já báke ishtónbires ánia iki.** They tell that the Inca's son was buried in mud and that a man dug him out and washed his face; then the child grew quickly.⟩ *syn.* xóxoti
See under **wanín**

*n.* **áni xéatinin** [from Shipibo *áni* + *xéati* drink] : a large festival formerly held to cut the girls' hair or to slaughter a monte (forest) animal raised especially for such an occasion ⟨**Ani xéatinin xéai en jóti kénaabira, jokáshamake.** Even though I invited him to come drink at the *áni xéati* festival, he would not come.⟩
*n.* **ánjirinin** [from Spanish] : angel
*n.* **anón** : majás (paca) ⟨**Taxbakan nónoaira epán áno réteke.** The uncle killed a paca that was swimming in the tahuampa (seasonally flooded forest).⟩
*adj. and n.* **ánsianon** [from Spanish] : elderly; an old person
*n.* **antán** : guayabo akuátiko (a water guava tree) ⟨**Nato ánta nia namanra, koríki miin iki.** Beneath this water guava tree there is money buried.⟩

*n.* **ántiojon** [from Spanish] : eyeglasses
*n.* **Antónyonin** [from Spanish *Antonio*] –Used as a male name.

*n.* **áokan** : a species of small tree; *also:* the fruit of the *aó* tree, which resembles that of the huito ⟨**Aó bimi píaitianra papán ámakiri cháchike.** Dad speared the gamitana (river fish) while it was eating the fruit of the *aó* tree.⟩
*n.* **Aón** [from Spanish *au*, element of *Aurora*] –Used as a female name
*n.* **ápacharaman** : apacharama (a plant) ⟨**Apacharan bénai kaáxa nokon pápa benóke.** My dad went off to look for apacharama and got lost.⟩ *syn.* méi

*v.t.* **ápakea** [from Shipibo *áti* to do + *-pake* downward] : to bring/take down ⟨**Abionimeara jóni ísinai íchaxon ápakekanke.** Several of them together brought a sick man down from the airplane.⟩

*n.* **ápasawan** : a species of mythological animal –Used to picture a large monkey or a bear. ⟨**Moátianronki westíora bákeki ápasawan bónike.** They tell that long ago the *ápasawa* carried off a child.⟩
*n.* **ápashiron** : iguana ⟨**Jóni bénotaronki moátian ápashironki píkonike.** They tell that long ago the iguana rescued a man who had gotten lost.⟩ [illustration: *ápashiro*]
See **ápichiro**
*also* **ápechido** *n.* **ápichironin** *also* **ápechironin** [from Spanish] : surname, family name ⟨**¿Jáwe jánerin mia? ¿Min ápichirokan?** What is your name? Your surname?⟩ *syn.* jáneteki

*n.* **apón** [from Quechua *apu* ruler] 1 : chief, leader 2 : subprefect : prefect 3 : president ⟨**Non ápo píkokanketianra non réteananti píkoai.** If they expel our president, we will go to war.⟩ 4 : king ⟨**ispányorobaon ápo** the king of Spain⟩ 5 : government ⟨**Apónra noa koríki ménike ískoira xóboati.** The government has given us money to build the school.⟩ *syn.* APO, PIRISIRINTI both can be translated as "president", but APO, the native word, is more common. *syn.* kóshi

*interj.* –Used in the sense of "oh!" as an expression of dismay on making a mistake or on remembering something forgotten. *syn.* APO, ARI, ARIRISH, AYAO, ERI, JII, SHII are all used as emotional expressions of pain, fear, or surprise corresponding to the interjection "¡ay!" in Spanish. ARI means a cry of pain; ARIRISH, the anguished cry of a demon; ERI, a cry of surprise; JII and SHII, both a cry of fright; and AYAO, a loanword from Spanish and less used than ARI, a cry of pain. APO may be softer and imply less emotion than the other synonyms.
*n.* **apón ániyakatinin** [from Shipibo *ápo, apón* king + *áni* big + *yákati* seat] : throne
*adj. and n.* **arán** *adj.* : rusted *n.* : rust ⟨**Machíto arara papán rásake.** Dad scraped the rust off the machete.⟩ *syn.* yámipoi
*n.* **Arán** [from Spanish *ala*, element of Aladino or Aladina] –Used as a masculine or feminine name.
*v.t.* **áraa** *Konibo* **áraaka** : to make holes in several places ⟨**Nato bakénra jawen titán tasón áraake, rabón pékaxon.** This boy made holes in his mother's bowl with a nail.⟩
*n.* **arábinin** [from Spanish] : Arab
*adj.* [from Shipibo *arábi* Arab + *–baon,* non-basic form of *–bo, plural suf.*] : Arabic ⟨**1, 2, 3 riki arábinbaon nómiro.** 1, 2, 3 are Arabic numerals.⟩
*n.* **Arabiritonin** [from Spanish *Alberto*] –Used as a masculine name.

*also* **alámbre** *n.* **arámpirin** *also* **alámbrenin** [from Spanish *alambre*] : wire; *specif.* : barbed wire ⟨**Máioshiainra meskó arámpiri jáke; nokon papánra jáinoa ícha béke jato máromati.** In Pucallpa there are different kinds of wi-re; and from there my father brought many to sell.⟩
See under **keré**
*also* **árpa** *n.* **árapanin** *also* **árpanin** [from Spanish] : harp

*v.i.* **áraa** 1 : to become pitted on the surface ⟨**Titán yámikentira moa árake, ján táshi nápota ikax.** Mom's pot became pitted because they put salt in it.⟩ 2 : to rust ⟨**Moa áraketianra nato yamín moa tsóa téeyamai.** Since it has already rusted, no one works with this axe.⟩
*v.t.* **áraxa** : to grip (e.g., with two sticks) like tongs ⟨**Jiwín aráxonra nato kíni meranoa en chíchika bíke.** I took the knife out of this hole by gripping it with two little sticks.⟩
*v.t.* **áresa** : to permit, allow ⟨**Nato jawékibora áresti iki.** These things are permitted.⟩ *syn.* --ma

*v.t.* **--aresa** [from Shipibo *áti*, *a-* to do + *-res* only + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to overcome, defeat --Used with the pronominal forms *éa-*, *mia-*, *ja-*, *nóa-*, *máto-* and *játo-* which function as the direct object. ⟨**éaaresti, míaaresti, jáaresti, nóaaresti mátoaresti, játoaresti** to defeat me, to defeat you, to defeat him *or* her, to defeat us, to defeat you (pl.), to defeat them (m.) *or* them (f.)⟩ ⟨**En arós sako pápiara éaareske.** The sack of rice I was carrying was too much for me.⟩ ⟨**Ja jónira moa yósiora iki; jákopira míaareske.** That man is already very old; that is why he defeated you.⟩ ⟨**Ichaxon non tapán níniabira nóaareske.** Even though several of us pulled the raft, it was too much for us.⟩ ⟨**Maton jéneketianra, mátoareske.** Since you (pl.) gave up trying, it has defeated you.⟩ ⟨**Pirótanin tsínikin non játoaresara sinákanke.** They got angry because we beat them playing soccer.⟩ *syn.* --ARESTI, BINSINTI both are translated as "to overcome/defeat", but --ARESTI, as a form always combined with the personal pronoun, is more limited in its use. On the other hand, BINSINTI implies only a person as the victor; whereas --ARESTI can imply either a person or a thing that defeats one.
*interj.* --Used in the sense of "oh!" as an exclamation of pain. *syn.* See under **ápo**
*n.* **Arín** [from Spanish *Arturo*] --Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **aríarikan** *Konibo* **aríarin** : ashara ⟨**Kokán awínra aríari píosma iki.** My uncle's wife has never eaten ashara.⟩
*n.* **árimanin** [from Spanish] : German ⟨**Arimanboronki áni jónibo iki.** They say that Germans are tall people.⟩
*also* **Alemania** *n.* **Arimanianin** *also* **Alemanianin** : Germany

*also* **álimentanti** *v.t.* **áriminta- na** *also* **álimentana** [from Spanish *alimentar* + Ship. *-n*, verbal-derivation suf.] : to feed, to nourish ⟨**Noara árimintanai meskó yóinanin i bánakan.** We feed ourselves with the meat of various animals and with some plants.⟩
*n.* **arínanin** [from Spanish] : flour ⟨**kímisha weá arínaya meskóti** to mix with three measures of flour⟩
*interj.* [from Shipibo *arí* exclamation + *ish*, exclamation] --Used in the sense of "oh!" as an expression of the anguished cry of a demon. *syn.* See under **ápo**
*n.* **Arisin** [from Spanish *aris*, element of *Arístides*] -Used as a masculine name.

*suf.* *v.t.* **-arita** [from Shipibo *-ati* to do + *ri*, unidentified element] : to make (something) ring out suddenly ⟨**Nato bakénra jawen titán chómo ríshkikin tan arike.** This child struck his mother's jar, making it ring out suddenly.⟩

*n.* **áriwanin** [from Shipibo *áriwa*, imitative of its call] : tarahui : churo-hawk (snail-eating hawk) ⟨**Nócho píkasironki áriwa kéotai.** They say the tarahui calls when it wants to eat churos (snails).⟩
See under **páoti**
*n.* **Aroman** [from Spanish *alon*, element of *Alonso*] -Used as a masculine name.

*n.* **árosen** [from Spanish] : rice ⟨**Aínbaonronki arós kobínhaa xanánki wísoino rachíxon rétenike.** They tell that in ancient times a woman killed a yanapuma (black puma) by throwing hot cooked rice at it.⟩
See **árapa**

*n.* **asápan** *also* **asápanin** : paco (a freshwater fish) ⟨**Moátianronki asápaninki chorónkin jóni rétenike.** They tell that in ancient times a paco killed a man by leaping onto him out of the water.⟩

*n.* **áshakan** 1 : a large species of toad ⟨**Ashakanronki aínbo chópaaxonike.** They tell that once the *ashá* toad made clothing for a woman.⟩ 2 : Campa (Asháninka person) ⟨**Jainra ashá jóai.** There comes a Campa.⟩ *syn.* ASHA, KAMPA both can be translated as "Campa", but ASHA has another meaning as well and is therefore less used to denote the ethnolinguistic group.
*adv.* [from Quechua *ashwan* more] : very : more -Used mostly among speakers of Shetebo. *syn.* bebónbires; -bi; -cha; kikín; -riba; –shaman; -yora
*adj.* **ashpán** : bow-legged, having crooked legs ⟨**Nato aínbo áshpara kikínbires íshto iki, bénbo níai keskati níaiikax.** This bow-legged woman is very fast because she walks like a man.⟩
*v.t.* **áshpana** : to spread the legs of ⟨**Kapónhanoxonra papán kochi ashpánke.** Dad spread the pig's legs in order to castrate it.⟩
*v.i.* **áshpata** : to spread one's legs apart : to remain with the legs open ⟨**Raínshikaxa ea ashpáke.** When I slipped, I ended up with my legs spread apart.⟩
*v.t.* : to cross : to put in the shape of an X ⟨**Maín yakáxonra titán jawen witáx ashtáake.** When she sat down on the ground, mom crossed her legs.⟩
*interj.* –Used repeatedly to urge on dogs.
*n.* **Asín** [from Spanish *Alkibíades*] -Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **Asiakan** [from Spanish] : Asia
*also* **aséiti** *n.* **asíitin** *also* **asíitinin** *also* **aséitin** [from Spanish] : oil; *specif.* : machine oil ⟨**asíiti botíria** a bottle of oil⟩
*n.* **ásiitonanin** [from Spanish] : olive
See **asójiri**
*also* **asófri** *n.* **asójirin** [from Spanish] : sulfur
*n.* **asókaron** [from Spanish] : sugar ⟨**Asókarora bátashaman iki.** Sugar is very sweet.⟩
*adj.* **aspán** : of great volume or capacity : large ⟨**Titán chómo áspara kochín tóeke.** The pig broke mom's large jar.⟩ *syn.* See under **áni**
*prep.* [from Spanish] : until, up to -Used in a construction where it precedes a number followed by *caman* "up to". ⟨**Topónwe asta pácha kaman.** Count up to one hundred.⟩ *syn.* kamán
*adj.* **ástokan** : full of thread -Used with reference, e.g., to a spindle or a bobbin. ⟨**Titán yomán xeira astó iki.** Mom's ball of yarn is full of thread.⟩
*v.t.* **astóaa** *Konibo* **astóaka** : to fill (e.g., a spindle or a bobbin) with thread ⟨**Westíora íwira titán rabé néte astóai.** Mom fills a spindle by spinning for two days.⟩
See under **níshi**
*v.i.* **ástota** : to become full of thread (e.g., a spindle or a bobbin) ⟨**Moa ástotaxa titán íwi sekéke.** Mom's spindle broke because it filled up with thread.⟩

*n.* **átapan** *Konibo* **átapanin** : hen : rooster : chicken ⟨**Jawen báke sontáro kátanax jóketianra epán átapa réteke.** The uncle killed a hen when his son returned from the army.⟩ ⟨**Atapa kéotainra ea jishténwanke.** This morning I woke up when the rooster crowed.⟩ *syn.* átapaawin; átapabene
[from Shipibo *áni* big + *átapa* hen] : a chicken of a large breed
: a breed of chicken
[from Shipibo *chóshka* ruffled + *átapa*] : a breed of chicken
[from Shipibo *mátsi* cold + *átapa* hen] : a breed of chicken with little plumage
[from Shipibo *ómo*, unidentified + *átapa* hen] : a short-legged breed of chicken
[from Shipibo *sése* speckled with dots + *átapa*] : a black breed of chicken spotted with white
[from Shipibo *texné* of plucked feathers + *átapa*] : a breed of chicken
*n.* **átapaawinin** *Konibo* **átapaawiman** [from Shipibo *átapa* rooster + *awín* female] : hen ⟨**Atapaawininra kéntikan tsíwai.** The hen lays eggs in the clay pot.⟩ *syn.* átapa; átapabene
See under bákeshoko
*n.* **átapabenen** [from Shipibo *átapa* hen + *béne* male] : rooster. See Grammar Sketch 7.1.8 *syn.* átapa; átapaawin
See under xóbo
*interj.* –Used as a scornful expression.

*v.t.* **aká** 1 : to do : to make –Used also with a variety of more specific senses that depend on the context of the sentence. ⟨**Rámara en ákai.** I am going to do it now.⟩ ⟨**Titónra jawen wetsán xóbo ákai.** Tito is building his brother's house.⟩ –Used with the same sense that the transitive verb has in a previous sentence, functioning as a substitute for that verb. ⟨–¿**Minki jankenhaa?** —Akáma. –Have you finished? —I have not finished.⟩ 2 : to speak ⟨**Miara ákai.** He is speaking to you.⟩ 3 : to say –Used with direct quotation as direct object. –Used often with *akín* (subordinate form of *áti*) which introduces a direct quotation. ⟨**Jaínxon Titón aká iki** —¡Oínwe! Then Tito said to him: —Look!⟩ ⟨**Bakísh jotánwe —akínra rókotoron aká iki.** The doctor said to me: —Come back tomorrow.⟩ 4 : to put ⟨**Nokon machítora en xóbo chicho áke, bákebaon ea potanaanaketian.** I have put my machete inside the house so that the children do not lose it.⟩ 5 : to add (the same number) a certain number of times –Used in the subordinate form *aquin.* ⟨**4 rabé aká páketai 8.** 4 plus 4 equals 8.⟩ 6 : to multiply (a specific number) by ⟨**2 chósko aká iki 8.** 2 times 4 equals 8.⟩

[from Shipibo *jato, jabo* them + *–res* only + *áti* to do] : to lose : to lose a game ⟨**Jaton kápitan yámaketianra, pirótanin tsíniaibo jábaonreske.** Since their captain was not there, the soccer players lost.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóni, jonín* + *áti, aká* to do] : transformed by man : artificial ⟨**Párora jonín akáma iki; ikáxbi repínti jonín aka riki.** The river is not artificial; the port, however, is.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóni, jonín* + *áti, a–* to do + *–res* only] : handmade : of handicraft

[from Shipibo; lit., 'careful that I not bump into you'; from *mia* you + *–ra*, indicative-mood suf. + *áti, a–* to do + *–na* warning suf. + *–ke*, verbal suf.] : excuse me. See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3.2.a *syn.* íti; sáwemati; sománti; yóiti

*transitive-verb suf.* **–aa** *Konibo* **–aka** 1 : to make (something with the indicated sound) –Used with a subject of non-basic form and following an onomatopoeic element. ⟨**tíati** to make (a musical instrument) sound⟩ ⟨**Nimánra tíati shónake.** Nima made the horn sound.⟩ 2 : to build (a specific thing) –Used combined with a noun. ⟨**xóboati** to build a house⟩ ⟨**nóntiati** to make a canoe⟩ 3 : to make have (the indicated quality) –Used combined with an adjective. ⟨**joshínhati** to redden⟩ ⟨**nenkéati** to lengthen⟩ ⟨**naxbáati** to widen : to broaden⟩ *syn.* —ma; -n

*adj.* **átikoman** [from Shipibo *áti* to do + *–kon* true + *–ma* not] 1 : difficult –Used also with *–res*, yielding the form *átikomares* with the sense 'difficult for lack of time'. ⟨**Ea maístoron taría áti méniabira átikoma iki.** The task the teacher gave me is difficult⟩ 2 : impossible ⟨**Jawen xóno tárani káaxbira pápa jákiribi joríbake, jánbicho aká átikoma íketian.** Dad went out to roll his lupuna (a giant kapok tree); but he came back, because it was impossible for him to do it alone⟩
*n.* **átikoma jawekinin** [from Shipibo *átikoma* difficult + *jawéki* thing] : problem ⟨**Ja átikoma jawéki akánwe.** Solve the problem⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *áti* to do + *–o*, particle of direction] : by the correct side ⟨**Bakénra átio machíto yatánke.** The child grabbed the machete by the correct side⟩

*v.i. & v.t.* **átipana** [from Quechua *atipay, atipan* to be able] : to be able –Used with transitive or intransitive force according to the corresponding infinitive complement. –Used in the preterite form but with a present sense. ⟨**Eara Rimán káti átipanke.** I can go to Lima⟩ ⟨**Oa aínbaonra chómoati átipanke.** That woman can make the large jar⟩
[from Shipibo *jatíbi* all + *jawéki* thing + *átipana*, past part. of *átipanti* to be able] : almighty : omnipotent ⟨**Riós jatíbi jawéki átipana** Almighty God⟩
*n.* **átoman** : red lupuna ⟨**Non réraketianronki átoman ói bémai.** They say that when we cut down the red lupuna, it makes it rain.⟩
*n.* **atsán** : yuca (cassava) ⟨**Atsa píaitianra jonín áno réteke.** The man killed the paca when it was eating the yuca⟩
[from Shipibo *aná* catahua (a tree) + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca
[from Shipibo *báwa* parrot + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca
[from Shipibo *báke* girl + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca that matures in three months and grows little
[from Shipibo *chíkaro* harpoon + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca with long, thin leaves
[from Shipibo *jóati* with which to boil + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca
[from Shipibo *joshín* red + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca with red skin
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca with white skin
*Konibo* **nonbéxatsa** [from Shipibo *nobéx* dove + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca similar to common yuca, grows up to a meter tall, and has thick roots
[from Shipibo *nóma* a species of partridge + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca similar to *nobéxatsa* yuca
[from Shipibo *panshín* yellow + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca whose edible part is yellow
[from Shipibo *kéen* desire + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca
[from Shipibo *róno* snake + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca with a twisted stem
[from Shipibo *xáma* bud + *yankón* blue + *átsa* yuca] : a variety of yuca with reddish-blue buds
[from Shipibo *xóno* lupuna (a giant tree) + *átsa*] : a species of manioc with a thick stalk and thick roots
[from Shipibo *táma* peanut + *átsa* manioc] : a species of manioc

*n.* **atsántitan** [from Shipibo *átsa* manioc + *títa* mother] : yucamama (the mother-spirit of manioc) ⟨**Atsántita xákixon jawen jéne xéaaxonki, noa xoáti iki.** They say that when you drink the juice of grated yucamama, you get fat.⟩
See under **póto**
See under **xéna**
*n.* **áwakan** [from Old Shipibo *awara* tapir] : tapir : sachavaca ⟨**Awakanronki ronón ewaki kóshi méenike.** They say that long ago the tapir and the boa held a contest of strength.⟩
[from Shipibo *tára*, unidentified + *awá* tapir] : a species of sachavaca (tapir) with a white chest
*n.* **awáberon** [from Shipibo *awá* tapir + *béro* eye] : a species of tree
See under **chépa**
*n.* **áwainin** : gull ⟨**Awai xetánra chópa kenéati iki.** Designs are painted on cloth using the gull's beak.⟩

*n.* **awájoran** [from Shipibo *awá* tapir + *jóra* semen] : a species of tree with a resin like that of rubber ⟨**Jonínra aínbo awínhakin bíke awájoran raónxon.** A man won a woman as his wife by giving her pusanga (a love charm) made with resin from the *awájora* tree.⟩
See **áwarampiti**

*n.* **awántsonin** : calabash tree; *also* : the hard fruit of the calabash tree used to make the pate (a gourd bowl) ⟨**Moátianronki isónki awántsonin róo tetónki tsákanike; jáskatironki róo teton áni iki.** Long ago the spider monkey struck the howler monkey on the neck with a calabash, and that is why it was left with a thick neck.⟩
*n.* **awápan** *Konibo* **awápanin** : ocelot : wildcat ⟨**Awápara yamé jóai átapa píkasi.** The ocelot comes at night to eat the hens.⟩
[from Shipibo *wishí* striped + *awápa* ocelot] : huamburusho (a small wildcat)
[from Shipibo *xopó* woolly + *awápa* ocelot] : a small species of ocelot
See under **pempén**
*n.* **awápishin** [from Shipibo *awá* tapir + *pishi* rib] : pashaca (a tree) ⟨**En awápishi nóntiaara ea yómetsoakanke.** They stole the canoe I made from pashaca wood.⟩ *syn.* yonshín

*also* **áwakampiti** *n.* **áwarampitin** *also* **áwakampitin** [from Old Shipibo *awara*, *awaran* tapir + *píti* food] : a species of vine with wide leaves and long, curved fruits ⟨**Awarampiti naman rákatara en manánxawe bíke.** I got a tortoise that was underneath this vine.⟩
See under **róno**

*n.* **awátepoman** [from Shipibo *awá* tapir + *tepón* neck tendon] : a species of plant; *also* : an infusion prepared from the *awátepon* plant ⟨**Awátepon ochíti xéamaara méchai.** When the dog is given the *awátepon* plant to drink, it becomes a good hunter.⟩
See **akín**

*n.* **áwinin** 1 : wife ⟨**Jawen áwininra bíke.** His wife received him.⟩ 2 : the female of a species that has both sexes ⟨**Atapaawin kéotaronki máwakanon íkai.** They say that when a hen crows, it announces that someone is going to die.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.5

*v.t.* **awínhaa** *Konibo* **awínhaka** : to take as a wife : to marry ⟨**Moátianronki jonínki xábue ainbo awínhanike.** They say that once a man took as his wife a charapa (a river turtle) that had turned into a woman.⟩

*verbal suf.* **-xon** –Used at the end of the subordinate verb, often carrying the force of "having", "when" or "upon" in the adverbial clause. ⟨**Non ápo nokóketian óinaxa noa kikínbiresi rároke.** We were very glad when we saw our president arrive.⟩ ⟨**Níma óínxonra, Josíkan kénai.** Upon seeing Nima, José calls him.⟩ ⟨**Bóchiki tsamáxon ninkákana iki.** They gathered up above and listened.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2

*adverbial suf.* –Used following an adverb, a postposition, or a postpositional suffix, generally with the sense of "of" or "from" but in certain contexts with the sense of "in". ⟨**-¿Jaweranoaxki mia joá? -Onoaxa ea jóke.** -Where have you come from? -I have come from over there.⟩ ⟨**Níi meranoaxa ea jóke.** I have come from the forest.⟩ ⟨**Róyain yamébi káxa, Kakónkoniax noa néteke.** When we traveled by night to Roya, we reached daybreak at Caco.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5; 8.3.5 *syn.* -ain

*n.* **axán** : huaca (a fish-poison plant); *also* : the fruit of the huaca or its extracted juice, which serves as a remedy against intestinal worms or otherwise as a poison (e.g., to kill fish) ⟨**Paénxon áxa xéaaxa jóni mawáke.** Being drunk, the man drank the huaca and died.⟩ *syn.* maráx
*v.t.* **áxana** : to fish with poison (e.g., from huaca or barbasco) ⟨**Axánketianra pórisiabaon yatánke.** The police arrested him because he fished with huaca.⟩
*v.t.* **áxbita** : to carry astride (on the hip/shoulders) ⟨**Jawen báke taskéketianra axbíxon bóke.** When his son dislocated his foot, he carried him astride.⟩
*n.* **áxekan** : cilantro ⟨**Pápashokonra axéya aká píti pixón kinánke.** Grandpa vomited when he ate food prepared with cilantro.⟩
*n.* **áxekan** : custom ⟨**Ja jónibora jaton axé jénekashamai.** These people do not want to give up their custom.⟩
*n.* **áxeamiston** [from Shipibo *áxeati, axea-* to teach + *-mis,* actor suf.] : teaching professional : educator : teacher *syn.* jawéki akai; maístoro

*v.t.* **áxeaa** *Konibo* **áxeaka** 1 : to accustom ⟨**Maístoron jato pirótanin áxeaara bákebaon jénekashamai.** Because the teacher has accustomed them to playing with the ball, the children do not want to stop playing with it.⟩ 2 : to teach ⟨**Jánra kírika ákaibo áxeakai.** He teaches the students.⟩ *syn.* onámati

*v.i.* **áxea** 1 : to become accustomed : to be accustomed ⟨**Eabicho íitira ea moa áxea iki.** I am now accustomed to being alone.⟩ 2 : to learn ⟨**Eara min jói áxekasai.** I want to learn your language.⟩ *syn.* onánti

*n.* **áxeyosman** [from Shipibo *áxeti, axe-* to learn + *-yosma* one who never does (a specific thing)] : one who is never willing to learn or obey : rebel ⟨**Nato bákera áxeyosma iki.** This child is a rebel.⟩

*n.* **axón** : capirona (a hardwood tree); *also* : a demon identified with the capirona tree ⟨**Axoronki kóshi jóni iki, rashíko jóni keska, wíso.** They say the demon of the capirona is a strong man, resembling a dark-skinned Brazilian.⟩

*n.* **ayán** : a species of small bird resembling the parrot that eats aguaje (the fruit of the moriche palm) ⟨**Non áya óinaronki chikíshti iki.** They say that when we see the *áya* bird, we become lazy.⟩
*adj.* **ayán** : lazy : idle ⟨**Nato jónira, áyayora ikaxbi, wánokasai.** Even though this man is very lazy, he wants to get married.⟩ *syn.* chikísh
*interj.* –Used with the sense of "ouch!" as an expression of pain. *syn.* See under **ápo**

*n.* **áyawaskan** [from Quechua *aya* the dead + *waska* vine] : ayahuasca (a hallucinogenic vine and brew) ⟨**Ayawaska xeaxonronki jonínki mawáyoshin méranike.** They tell that in ancient times a man drank ayahuasca and saw the spirits of the dead.⟩ *syn.* AYAWASKA, NISHI, and ONI can all denote ayahuasca. AYAWASKA and NISHI are used in Shipibo speech to designate both the drink and the plant; ONI, however, is little used. In Konibo speech NISHI is used to denote the vine, while ONI is the name of the substance derived from it, and AYAWASKA is little used.

*n.* **ayáxen** : tamshi (a climbing plant whose stems are used for weaving) ⟨**Ayáx tásakan noa namáketian mápotaronki inón bíti iki.** They say that when we dream we cover ourselves with a basket of tamshi, it is a sign that the jaguar will attack us.⟩ *syn.* kamári
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *b* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*modifying pref.* 1 : in the armpit : of the armpit ⟨**bánoti** to pierce in the armpit⟩ 2 : on or of the chest near the armpit ⟨**baxáxti** to scrape the chest near the armpit⟩ 3 : on or of the arm near the armpit ⟨**banénti** to feel a burning in the arm near the armpit⟩ 4 : short-sleeved ⟨**bakéxti** to sew (a shirt) at the short sleeve⟩ 5 : at or of the side of the stump ⟨**baxóxti** to sprout at the side of the stump⟩

*verbal suf.* –Used added to the verb root in the exhortative form to encourage oneself or a third person. ⟨**Eapari kabánon.** I'll go first.⟩ ⟨**Eabicho téebanon; máto oxakanwe.** Now I alone am going to work; you all sleep.⟩ ⟨**Jáa kabátanon.** Let him go.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3.4

*n.* **babán** 1 : grandson : granddaughter; *also* : grandchild of a brother or sister or of a brother-in-law or sister-in-law –The vocative form *chió* (from *chío* "younger brother") is used with the sense of "grandson!" or "granddaughter!" ⟨**Jawen babánra pápashoko temáxkoroake.** The grandson cut his grandfather's hair.⟩ 2 : husband or wife of a grandchild 3 : grandchild of a brother-in-law or sister-in-law 4 : great-grandchild 5 : relatives of the second descending generation –The plural form *bábabo* is used to indicate the whole group of blood and affinal relatives of the grandchildren's generation. *syn.* chío

*n.* **babán ewan** [from Shipibo *bába*, *babán* grandchild + *–ewa* mother] : daughter-in-law; *also* : wife of the son of a brother or sister -The vocative form *yoxán* "son's wife" is used to address the person referred to. ⟨**Jowe, yoxán.** Good morning, daughter-in-law.⟩ ⟨Oa aínbaon **babán ewara jakóma shinánya iki.** That woman's daughter-in-law is very bad.⟩

*also* **bába nákaxonti** *n.* **bába pímatinin** *also* **bába nákaxontinin** [from Shipibo *bába* grandchild + *pímati, pímatinin* something to feed with, or *nákaxonti,* something to chew with] : wisdom tooth ⟨Nato aínbo baquera jahuen **bába pímati xeta pikóke.** This girl's wisdom tooth is coming in.⟩

*n.* **bachín** 1 : egg ⟨Kabóri **bachira nóe iki.** Taricaya (a river turtle) eggs are tasty.⟩ 2 : mosquito net ⟨**Ráma yamékiri bachín íi ítira, ea bári keyáke.** By staying in the mosquito net this morning, I got up at midday.⟩
*v.t.* **báchi aká** : to lay eggs (e.g., a hen) ⟨Takínra **báchiakai maxín.** The tibe (a river bird) lays its eggs on the beach.⟩
*v.i.* **báchimeeta** : to pull one's own hair ⟨Aínbora **páenax janbíx báchimeeke.** A drunken woman pulled her own hair.⟩
*v.t.* **báchina** : to pull the hair of ⟨Nato **aínbaonra jawen benén mérati bachínke.** This woman pulled the hair of her husband's lover.⟩
See **–bo**

*n.* **baín** 1 : trail ⟨**Káx, noa píkota iki, shirínkanin téetaibaon bái ikáin.** Going straight ahead, we came out on the trail of the rubber-tappers.⟩ 2 : road ⟨**Ríma bain káxa ea Aweitin nokóke.** Going along the central road, I arrived at Aguaytía.⟩ 3 : current ⟨**Baí íketianra shitátikoma iká iki.** It was very hard to cross the river because there was a strong current.⟩ *syn.* BAI and KARITIRA can both be translated as "road," but BAI, the native word, unlike KARITIRA, the loanword, has other more traditional senses.

*modifying suf.* **–bait** : all day –Used added to the verb. –Used in the form *–bait* before a final suffix beginning with a vowel and in the form *–bai* in all other cases. ⟨**Pirótanin tsínikanaitianra en oínbaiibake.** Yesterday I watched them play soccer all day.⟩ ⟨**En oínbaita iki.** I watched them all day.⟩

*v.t.* **báia** 1 : to make a trail ⟨**Jónibaonra báikanke ján konxán taránoxon.** The men made a trail to roll the cedar logs.⟩ 2 : to make a road ⟨**Iparia pekaora náwabaon moa báia iki, Koskón pákekin.** Behind Iparía the mestizos made a road that reaches all the way to Cuzco.⟩
*v.i.* **báita** : to become torrential ⟨**Tamánya weanra moa ráma baíke, jénetian ikáx.** The Tamaya river has become torrential because it is the rainy season.⟩
*adj.* **bakán** : smooth : soft ⟨Papán yámi **táxora bákashaman iki.** The handle of dad's axe is very smooth.⟩ *syn.* sibá; yenkén; wácho; páchi
*v.t.* **bákaa** *Konibo* **bákaaka** : to smooth : to soften ⟨Kárapintironinra jatíbi mísabo **bákaake síkaxon.** The carpenter smoothed all the tables by painting them.⟩ *syn.* wáchoati; páchiati
*v.i.* **bákaa** : to become smooth ⟨Nato yakátira moa **bákake, ján noa yákata.** This seat has become smooth because we have sat on it.⟩

*n.* **bakén** 1 : boy : girl ⟨**Bákebaonra tsínikin xánbo tsákai.** The children play at spearing lizards.⟩ 2 : son : daughter ⟨**Papán bokáshamaketianra jawen báke nótsia iki.** The little son got angry when his dad did not want to take him.⟩ ⟨**Báke pikóbenatonin póko páketaishokora wáste jenen nachéxti iki chóskoakin.** Into the navel of a newborn child one must pour piripiri (a medicinal sedge) juice four times.⟩ 3 : pupil : student ⟨**Bákebora maístoron yoia, yoiti iti iki.** Pupils must obey the teacher.⟩ 4 : offspring ⟨**Wétsa netén westíora jawen nétemea kánsa iká iki íaman nónononoi jawen bákeboya.** One day, a wild goose was swimming with her offspring in the cocha (an oxbow lake).⟩ *syn.* bákeshoko

*also* **jawéki** *n.* **bákeai jawékinin** *also* **jawékinin** [from Shipibo *báke* offspring + *-ai*, participial suf. + *jawéki* animal] : animal : species of the animal kingdom ⟨**Jatíbi níi meran iká jawéki, non kaíati jawéki, jéne meran iká jawéki: jábo riki bákeai jawékibo.** The animals of the monte (forest), domestic animals, and aquatic animals belong to the animal kingdom.⟩ *syn.* jawéki

*v.t.* **bákeaa** *Konibo* **bákeaka** 1 : to father (a child or children) ⟨**Atsa xena awínhaxonronki jonínki bákeaníke.** They say that once a man married the female of the cassava worm and had a son with her.⟩ 2 : to incubate ⟨**Ani kíniosinra nato póinkoskon bákeake.** This female vulture has incubated in a very large hole.⟩ *syn.* menkóti
See under **átsa**

*n.* **bákebenbon** [from Shipibo *niño* + *bénbo* male] : boy (young man) ⟨**Westíora bákebenboronki isóntitan boá iki.** They say that an apasahua (a mythical forest being) carried off a boy.⟩ *syn.* ranón
See under **náneti**
See under **chéxati**

*n.* **bakénkin** *Konibo* **bakénkinin** [*from Old Shipibo* *báke, bakén* son + *ki,* unidentified element] : a woman's father-in-law –Used little nowadays. ⟨**Jawen bakénkira aínbaon santíra boxónke.** The woman brought watermelons for her father-in-law.⟩ *syn.* BAKENKI, BENENPAPA both denote a woman's father-in-law, but BENENPAPA is used more frequently nowadays. *syn.* See under rayós
See under **wáste**

*v.t.* **bákena** : to give birth ⟨**Aínbora rókotoron póteke, iósmanix bákeni bakénkaskimaitian.** The doctor performed a cesarean on the woman, because it was her first time giving birth and she was having difficulty.⟩

*n.* **bakénxan** *Konibo* **bakénxanin** [*from Old Shipibo* *báke, bakén* son + *xáni,* a woman's pubic hair] : a woman's mother-in-law –Used little nowadays. ⟨**Nokon poín bakénxara jakóma shinánya iki.** My sister's mother-in-law is very mean.⟩ *syn.* BAKENXA, BENENTITA both denote a woman's mother-in-law, but BENENTITA is used more frequently nowadays.
*adj.* **bákeomatonin** [*from Shipibo* *báke* child + *–oma* without] : childless ⟨**Wánoya ikáxa, bakeoma iki ea.** Although I am married, I have no children.⟩

*n.* **bákeonaman** [*from Shipibo* *báke* offspring + *onán-,* root of *onánti,* to know] : a species of hawk that typically hunts chicks ⟨**Bákeonamanra róno píai.** The *bákeonan* hawk eats snakes.⟩
*n.* **bákeranoman** [*from Shipibo* *báke* child + *ranón* young] : young male ⟨**Bákeranonbo betan yósibora tsínikanai.** The young men are playing with the adults.⟩
*n.* **bákeranoman** [*from Shipibo* *báke* child + *ranón* underage youth] : an adolescent over thirteen years old

*n.* **bákeshokon** [*from Shipibo* *báke* child + *–shoko,* diminutive suf.] 1 : baby : infant ⟨**Bákeshoko kankan kókomaara óshiai.** If the baby is fed pineapple, it grows thin.⟩ 2 : young (of an animal) ⟨**Nato joshínshino bákeshoko biára moa jiwéke; rámara ícha píai.** This young huapo colorado (a red uakari monkey) brought from the monte (forest) has now recovered and eats a lot.⟩

[*from Shipibo* *átapa* hen + *bákeshoko* young] : chick ⟨**Jawen títa máxokan réteketianra, átapa bákeshokobo chéonkicheonkiikai.** The chicks are peeping because the zorro (opossum) killed their mother.⟩ *syn.* báke
*adv.* [*from Shipibo* *báke* child + *–tian* when] : in childhood ⟨**Báketianra nokon pápa en akínkatitai.** When I was a child, I used to help my father.⟩
*v.t.* **bákexa** [*from Shipibo* *ba–* on the sleeve + *kéxkti* to sew] : to sew (e.g., a shirt) on the short sleeve

*adv.* 1 : yesterday ⟨**Pishtatian áti titán bakísh xéatiaibatara moa páea iki.** The drink that mom prepared yesterday for the festival is already fermented.⟩ 2 : tomorrow ⟨**Piróta ákaiboronki ráma béyamaax bakísh békanai; yánkara non pítibo áke.** They say that the soccer players, instead of coming today, will come tomorrow. We prepared the food in vain.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5 *syn.* –iba; -ya
*v.i.* **bákosha** : to exert oneself : to make an effort ⟨Eara **bakóshai jíwi wákei.** I strain to lift the tree.⟩
*n.* **bákoxen** : foam ⟨Titánra **átsaxeati bakox pótake.** Mom threw out the foam of the masato (a fermented manioc drink).⟩ *syn.* makásh
*v.t.* **bakóxaa** *Konibo* **bakóxaka** : to make foam ⟨Chópa **patsánoxonra titán ompáx bakóxake yámikentin axón.** Mom put water in a metal basin and then made foam to wash the clothes.⟩
*v.i.* **bákoxa** : to foam up ⟨Chomómea **ompáxa bákosha iki, bakén jabón nénana.** Foam has formed in the water jar because a child put soap in it.⟩
See **baránsa**

*v.i.* 1 : to appear suddenly (a hidden mitayo, i.e. game animal) ⟨**Iitimaibi bámaketianra en wáme cháchike.** I speared the paiche (a large river fish) when it suddenly appeared in a place where it had not been before.⟩ 2 : to be suddenly declared ⟨**Ikóma ikax bámaketianra, non ónanai.** When something false is suddenly declared, it is soon found out.⟩
*n.* **bámpisin** [from Shipibo *ba–* in the armpit + *pis*, element of *písi* stinking] : underarm odor

*adj. and n.* **bánakan** *adj.* : sown : planted ⟨**Rashíkoronki jawen xáwi banakan yóashi ikátiai.** They say that a Brazilian used to be stingy with his planted sugarcane.⟩ *n.* : plant ⟨**Jatíbi baná jawéki iki xóxoai jawékibo.** All plants belong to the plant kingdom.⟩ *syn.* xóxo
See under **boánhis**
*v.i.* **bánakaata** : to take root ⟨**En xóbi óroabi ói béketian jákiribi bánakaake.** I cultivated the grass; but when it rained, it took root again.⟩
*n.* **banáshokon** [from Shipibo *baná* plant + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : seedling : seed plant ⟨**janra banáshokobo ompáx táchitai** the one who waters the seedlings⟩
*v.t.* **bánaa** : to sow : to plant ⟨**Papánra arós bánake koríki bínoxon.** Dad planted rice to earn money.⟩
See **bantíra**
*v.i.* **bánena** : to feel a burning sensation in the arm near the armpit

*v.t.* **bánea** 1 : to make return : to give back ⟨**Pátoronhibakea chópa bixónbira en moa báneke kopíora íketian.** I got cuts of cloth from a boss; but I returned them, because they were expensive.⟩ 2 : to exchange for something else ⟨**Papán jóno bichi méniara jawen pátoronin asókaro sako bánexonke.** When Dad gave him the hide of a sajino (collared peccary), his boss exchanged it for an empty sack of sugar.⟩

*v.i.* **báneta** 1 : to return ⟨**Nato jónira téeti kakáxamai, jákiribi xobón banéke.** This man returned home because he did not want to go to work.⟩ 2 : to stay ⟨**Nokon títa banéketianra, non já yoáati jíkimai.** When my mother stays, we appoint her cook.⟩ 3 : to turn into ⟨**Yóashiko Inkán shinánketianronki, rabé jóni kapé banénike.** They say that when the Stingy Inca merely imagined it, two men turned into caimans.⟩ 4 : to equal –Used as the main verb in a division. ⟨**8 ikénbi 2 ixón káxkeara bánetai 4.** 8 divided by 2 equals 4.⟩ *syn.* BANETI, ITI, PAKETI can all be translated as "to equal" in arithmetic operations; but BANETI is used in subtraction or division, while ITI is used in addition, and PAKETI in addition, multiplication and division. *syn.* nókoti
*n. and adj.* **banjírikon** [from Spanish] : evangelical (Protestant) *syn.* bánjirista
*n.* **banjírion** [from Spanish] : gospel *syn.* BANJIRIO, BENAKAWE both mean "gospel" with no difference; but BANJIRIO, the borrowed form, is more common.
*n.* **bánjiristan** [from Spanish] 1 : evangelist 2 : evangelical *syn.* banjíriko
*n.* **bankán** [from Spanish] : bench
*n.* **bankón** [from Spanish] : bank

*v.t.* **bánoa** [from Shipibo *ba–* on the arm + *no*, unidentified element + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to completely wrap the arm of ⟨**Máioshiyainoaxa westíora báke ainbo menóke jawen poyán; jaskáketianra rókotoron bánoxon bóke.** In Pucallpa a girl had burned her arm; so the doctor wrapped it completely and took her to the clinic.⟩
*v.t.* **bánoa** [from Shipibo *ba–* in the armpit + *nóati* to prick] : to prick in the armpit
*n.* **bantán** : gaiter (legging) ⟨**Píshtatianra sontárobo bántayabo márachanai.** During the festival the soldiers march with their gaiters.⟩
*n.* **bantíjanin** [from Spanish] : tray ⟨**Bantíjaninra en ompáx nachíke.** I spilled water on the tray.⟩
*also* **bandéra** *n.* **bantíranin** *also* **bandéranin** [from Spanish] : flag ⟨**Yoshínbaon jémaronki bantíraya iki.** They say that a village of demons has its flag.⟩
*v.t.* **bánxoxa** [from Shipibo *ba–* on the stump + *xóxoti* to grow] : to sprout beside the stump

*Konibo* **baón** *n.* **baón** *Konibo* **báoman** [from Konibo and Old Shipibo *-baon*, plural suf.] 1 : twin ⟨**Aínbora rabé baón bakénke.** The woman gave birth to twins.⟩ 2 : two units together ⟨**Titánra rabé baon paránta jóake.** Mom boiled a cluster of two plantains.⟩
See **–bo**
*n.* **báotismon** [from Spanish] : baptism
*n.* **bapín** : armpit sweat ⟨**Rabé néte náshiamaikaxa nato jóni bápia iki.** Because he has not bathed for two days, this man has dark sweat in his armpit.⟩

*also* **balánsa** *n.* **baránsanin** *also* **balánsanin** [*from Spanish*] : scale (balance) ⟨**Bákebaonra baránsa jan topónkanai jawéki ískoiranko bekánti iki.** The pupils are to bring a scale to school for weighing.⟩
*n.* **barín** : sun ⟨**Moátianronki bári namánshoko ípaonike, Inka janóntian.** They say that long ago, in the time of the Inca, the sun was very low.⟩

*also* **bári káio** *also* **bári jíkiai** [*from Shipibo* *bári* sun + *kái,* present of *káti* to go + *–o,* element of *óri* over there, or *jíkiai,* present of *jíkiti* to enter] : west *syn.* oísti

[from Shipibo *ipákeai*, pres. of *ipáketi* to go down + *-tian* when] : in the afternoon : at about four in the afternoon ⟨**Moátianra noa bénota iki, níi meran káchio kash; játianra noa píkota iki moa bári ipakeaitian.** Many years ago we got lost while walking through the forest; then we came out when it was already about four in the afternoon.⟩
[from Shipibo *bári* + *jíkiai*, form of *jíkiti* to enter + *-tian* when] : at about six in the evening
[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *jíkiti* to enter] : for the sun to set ⟨**Bári jíkiai, jawen xánayabi.** The sun sets, taking its heat with it.⟩

[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *jóai*, form of *jóti* to come + *naman* under] : toward the east ⟨**Jíwi bochikishonra en paro méraa iki, bári joai naman.** Up in the tree, I spotted the river to the east.⟩

*also* **báriapan** [from Shipibo *bári* sun + *maníketian* while standing still, from *maníti* to stand + *-ketian*, subordinate-verb suf.; or *bári* sun + *áti* to do + *pan*, unidentified element] : at midday ⟨**Bári maníketianra kabóri barínhameetai —akin papán aka iki.** Dad told him: —The taricayas (river turtles) sun themselves at midday.⟩ ⟨**Báriapan ráo shéatira ea rókotoron yóike.** The doctor told me to take the medicine at midday.⟩

[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *maníti* to stand on top] : to be midday ⟨**Moa bári maníkenbira nokóyamai; jáwera winóbirake.** It is already midday and he has not arrived; something must have happened to him.⟩

[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *tánxameeti* to lean + *-tian* when] : at about one in the afternoon ⟨**Yamékirishoko káwanaxa, moa bári matánxameketian ea néno íkeanke.** If I had left in the early morning, I would already have been here by one.⟩
*also* **bári píkotaiori** [from Shipibo *bári* + *píkotai*, pres. of *pikóti* to come out + *óri* over there] : east : the east *syn.* ísti
: at about six in the morning
[from Shipibo *kéyatai*, pres. of *kéyáti* to rise + *-tian* when] : at about nine in the morning ⟨**Bakísh bári kéyataitianra ea joí kai.** I will come tomorrow at nine.⟩

*n.* **barímpoin** [from Shipibo *bári*, *barín* sun + *pói* dung] : aquatic bloom : algae : moss ⟨**Barímpoironkiki jenényoshiman xékixeatl.** They say algae is the chicha (a fermented drink) of the yacurunas (mythical water beings).⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.8
*adj.* [from Shipibo *barímpoi* algae + *keska* similar to] **barímpoikeskaton** : dark green
*v.i.* **barínhameeta** : to sun oneself –Used mostly among Konibo speakers. ⟨**Matsín akára ea barínhameeke, jéma napon rákatax.** Because it was cold, I lay down and sunned myself in the yard.⟩
*v.t.* **barínhaa** *Konibo* **barínhaka** : to put out in the sun ⟨**Chópa patsáxonra aínbaon barínhake.** The woman washed the clothes and put them out in the sun.⟩

*n.* [from Shipibo *bári* sun + *-tia* time] 1 : a time of much sun : summer (the dry season) 2 : year ⟨**Rabé chónka báritiaya ikaxa nokon pápa sontáro kayántanke.** My father served in the army at twenty years of age.⟩ ⟨**Icha báritiara noa chipónki jakátiai.** For many years we lived downriver.⟩
[from Shipibo *báritia* year + *-ya* with + *íti* to be] : to be ... years old ⟨**Nokon bákera ískon báritiaya iki.** My son is nine years old.⟩
[from Shipibo *báritia* summer + *napón* inside of] : in the middle of the summer (dry season)
*adv.* [from Shipibo *bári* sun + *-tian* when] : in the summer (dry season) ⟨**Báritianra máshi píkotai.** In the summer the sandbanks in the river emerge.⟩
*v.i.* **báritiaa** : for the summer (dry season) to come ⟨**Moara báritiake; rámara kabóribaon tsíwai.** It is now summer, and the taricayas (river turtles) are going to lay eggs.⟩
See under **báritia**
See under **xánati**

*Konibo* **báshakaati** *n.* **basháatin** *Konibo* **báshakaatin** [from Shipibo *ba-* on the arm + *shakáati*] : a kind of rattle-bracelet made of seeds and worn on the upper arm ⟨**Bakénra jawen papán basháati tésake.** The child broke his father's seed bracelet.⟩ ⟨**Oa pishánra epán báshakaati iki.** My uncle's rattle-bracelet is in that little bag.⟩

*n.* **báshoshin** *Konibo* **báshoshen** : a kind of large bayuca (a stinging caterpillar) ⟨**Noa báshoshen tékaketianronki reshón síkati iki.** They say that when the *bashósh* bayuca stings us, we should cover the sting with mucus.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *bashósh* bayuca] : a kind of large, yellowish bayuca
[from Shipibo *róo* howler monkey + *bashósh* bayuca] : a kind of large, reddish bayuca

*adv.* 1 : delayed : late ⟨**Bási ea jóketianra ea maístoron kastíkanke.** The teacher punished me because I arrived late.⟩ 2 : for a long time ⟨**Néno bási ikáxparira ea Kakónko kái.** After having been here for such a long time, I am going to Caco.⟩ *syn.* yantán. See Grammar Sketch 7.5
*adv.* [from Shipibo *bási* for a long time + *-bo*, plural suf.] : from time to time ⟨**Básibora íkai nato jóni nóoiba mérati.** This man visits us from time to time.⟩

*v.i.* **bási ika** [from Shipibo *bási* for a long time + *-iti* to do] : to last ⟨**Non kantsín pei xóboaara básima íkai; xebón péikayara bási ikai.** Roofs made with shapaja palm leaves do not last; those made with shebón palm leaves last the longest.⟩
See under **páyoti**

*v.i.* **básia** [from Shipibo *bási* for a long time + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to be delayed ⟨**Maístoronra báke kastíkanke, ompáx xéati ráanabi básiketian.** The teacher sent the boy to drink water, and punished him because he took too long.⟩
*n.* **basón** [from Spanish *vaso*] : drinking glass

*adj.* **batán** 1 : sweet : sweetened ⟨**Rabé óxera non bátaoma xéake, asókaro yámaketian.** For two months we drank without sweetening, because there was no sugar.⟩ 2 : sweet : unfermented ⟨**Paénkashamakinra non bátares xéai.** When we do not want to get drunk, we drink only unfermented beverages.⟩
*v.t.* **bátana** : to sweeten ⟨**Titánra jawen átsaxeati asókaron batánke.** Mom sweetened her masato (a fermented drink) with sugar.⟩
See under **rimón**
*n.* **bátaron** [from Shipibo *ba-* in the armpit + *táro* dirt] : armpit dirt
*v.i.* **bátaa** : to become sweet ⟨**Nato waránra moa bátake bási bénxoa ikax.** This squash became sweet from being stored for a long time.⟩
*n.* **batáyoman** [from Spanish] : battalion
*also* **báteria** *n.* **bátirian** *also* **báteria** [from Spanish] : battery
*also* **báteria jéne** *n.* **bátiria jenen** *also* **báteria jenen** [from Spanish *batería* + Shipibo *jéne* water] : acid
*n.* **bátoman** : lisa (a freshwater fish) ⟨**Jéne tsósinaitianra bátoman míshkia bíai.** When the flood recedes, the lisas bite the bait on the hook.⟩

[from Shipibo *moxó* lopa + *batón* lisa] : a kind of lisa similar to the boquichico (a river fish) but with black stripes on its body ⟨**Westíora kirínko ainbora** **moxóbatonki ráketi sión ike, natéxti shínani.** A certain foreign woman screamed in fear, thinking that a *moxóbaton* lisa would bite her.⟩
*n.* **bawán** [from Shipibo *báwa,* imitative of its cry] : parrot ⟨**Báwara non yóyoiti onámai.** We teach the parrot to talk.⟩
[from Shipibo *kóro* gray + *báwa* parrot] : a species of parrot of a greenish-gray color
[from Shipibo *rexté* with a notch in the beak + *báwa* parrot] : a species of parrot with a red-edged beak
[from Shipibo *xómi* ojé (a fig tree) + *báwa* parrot] : a species of parrot that usually perches on the ojé tree and eats its fruit
[from Shipibo *tanchan*, unidentified element + *báwa* parrot] : a species of parrot with a yellow stripe on both sides
See under **átsa**
See under **bóna**
See under **káshi**

*n.* **bawán ewan** [from Shipibo *báwa, bawan* parrot + *–ewa* mother] : a species of large parrot ⟨**Moátianronki bawán ewaki Inkán ináaka ípaonike.** They say that in ancient times the *bawán ehua* parrots were raised by the Inca.⟩

**báwanixo** *n.* **báwanixon** 1 : a species of tree 2 : a demon identified with the *báwanixo* tree ⟨**Báwanixoronkiki nenkéyosi; ikáxbi jawen táechipon iki pextín; járonkiki jawen béma.** They say the demon of the *báwanixo* tree is very tall and broad-heeled: that heel is the buttress root of the tree.⟩
See under **sémpa**
See under **paránta**

*n.* **báwareshiman** [from Shipibo *báwa* parrot + *reshín* yellowish on the beak] : a species of small parrot with a yellow stripe on its beak ⟨**Nato báwareshimanra ea natéxke.** This little *báwareshin* parrot bit me.⟩
See under **róno**

*n.* **báwataen** [from Shipibo *báwa* parrot + *táe* foot] : cetico blanco (a fast-growing riverside tree) ⟨**Báwatae bimi máana píaitianra en asápa cháchike.** I wounded the paco (a fish) while it was eating the fruits that had fallen from the cetico blanco.⟩
*n.* **báwiman** : súngaro (a large catfish) ⟨**Bawínronki tókoroninki kenéai.** They say the toad draws the patterns found on the body of the súngaro.⟩
[from Shipibo *bícha* phlegm, slimy + *bawín* súngaro] : a species of súngaro with slimy skin
**ínobawin** [from Shipibo *íno* jaguar + *bawín* súngaro] : pumasúngaro (a kind of catfish)
**jóxobawin** [from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *bawín* súngaro] : golden súngaro : súngaro blanco (a kind of catfish)
[from Shipibo *moxó* topa (the balsa tree) + *bawin* súngaro] : a species of very large súngaro with faint stripes on its body
*v.t.* **báxaxa** [from Shipibo *ba-* on the chest near the armpit + *xáxati* to scratch] : to scrape on the chest near the armpit
*n.* **báxexen** : low voice ⟨**Nato aínbora jóni óinax báxexen yóyoikai.** This woman speaks in a low voice when she sees a man.⟩
*v.t.* **baxéxaa** *Konibo* **baxéxaka** : to speak in a low voice to ⟨**Jawen tsabénra** **aínbo baxéxake.** His sister-in-law spoke to the woman in a low voice.⟩

*v.i.* **báxexa** : to speak in a low voice ⟨**Tsóabi yóyoitima maístoron yóiabi báke baxéxketianra ríshkike.** Even though the teacher had ordered that no one speak, a child spoke in a low voice and the teacher hit him.⟩
*n.* **báxkaten** *Konibo* **báxkakan** : armpit ⟨**Rimón betan chíimaponronki baxká itsa tóxkotai.** They say that armpit odor goes away if you apply lemon juice mixed with ash.⟩
*n.* **baxón** : shirúe (a kind of dragonfly) ⟨**Baxónra báchiai, jíwi pei jenénko ikábaon.** Shirúes lay their eggs on the leaves lying on the water.⟩ *syn.* taránki

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *béro* eye] 1 : on the eye ⟨**betóshti** to burst someone's eye⟩ 2 : on the eyebrow : on the eyebrows ⟨**bextéti** to cut oneself on the eyebrow⟩ 3 : on the cheekbone : of the cheekbone ⟨**bexpó** cheekbone hairs⟩ 4 : on the forehead ⟨**bestéti** to cut one's hair at the forehead⟩ 5 : on the face : of the face ⟨**béchokiiti** to wash one's face⟩ 6 : on the surface : of the surface ⟨**bebíti** to remove from the surface⟩
*v.t.* **béaxa** : to mix (a fermented drink) with a less fermented one ⟨**Xéati paera bakísh beáxkanai.** Tomorrow they are going to dilute the fermented drink.⟩
*v.t.* **bébana** : to pierce through ⟨**Nato ponkósh jonínra rabón jíwi bebánkin cháchike.** This burly man nailed the board and drove the nail right through it.⟩
*v.i.* **bébaa** : to cross or pass to the other side over something solid ⟨**Bákera kampón bébake, ábion páketainbi.** The child was crossing the field just as an airplane was landing.⟩
*adv.* : on the surface ⟨**Tóxpira chichóma iki; bebí riki.** Warts do not go deep; they stay on the surface of the skin.⟩
See **bénbo**

*adv. and postp.* *adv.* : ahead : first –Used often with *-yora*. ⟨**Bebónyora íkasi íitira, jóni namán pakéke.** The man, because he wanted to be first, ended up being last.⟩ *postp.* 1 : in front of : facing ⟨**Oa átapara ochíti bebon iki.** That hen is in front of the dog.⟩ 2 : before : ahead of –Used after a possessive form of a pronoun or noun. ⟨**ja bebon** before him⟩ *syn.* BEBON, PONTE both can be translated as "in front of", but unlike BEBON, PONTE implies, more specifically, that one thing is in a straight line in front of another. *syn.* –pari; rekén

*also* **bebónyora** *adv.* [from Shipibo *bebon* ahead + *-bires* only, or *-yora* very] : more : more than : the most –Used in the degrees of comparison of the adjective. ⟨**Nokon wétsara riki ea bebónbires xoá.** My brother is fatter than I am.⟩ ⟨**Nokon wétsara bébonbires xoá jóni iki nénoa.** My brother is the fattest man there is around here.⟩ ⟨**Piróta atínkora ea jató bebónyora iki.** Playing soccer, I am better than they are.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.3.1 *syn.* ashón
*v.t.* **bebónhaa** *Konibo* **bebónhaka** : to put ahead ⟨**Maístoronra báke joyómaxon, ja yóitima báke bebónhake.** The teacher had the children line up, and put the disobedient child in front.⟩
*v.i.* **bébona** : to go ahead ⟨**Nato jóni yóitimara bebónke; jákopira benóke.** This reckless man went ahead, and for that reason he got lost.⟩
See under **ípo**

*v.i.* **béchexeeta** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *chéxeati* to turn black + *-ee*, reflexive suf.] : to anoint one's own eyes ⟨**Bérorao márowe, mia jan béchexeenon.** Buy yourself ointment to anoint your eyes.⟩

*adj.* **bechín** : against the grain : with opposing fibers –Used about wood. ⟨**Pácho bechi non wíntiaara wexatikoma iki.** When we make a paddle of remocaspi (a tree) against the grain, it is hard to scrape.⟩

*v.t.* **béchitea** : to hold back : to stop : to catch ⟨**Ea kakákakataibira jonín joxón ea béchiteke.** I kept walking, and a man caught me.⟩ *syn.* BECHITETI, BITI both can be translated as "to catch", but BECHITETI implies an obstacle that stops, while BITI refers rather to the act of getting something desired (e.g., clothing or a fish from the water).
*v.t.* **béchia** : to meet (another) ⟨**Bakénronki yoshín béchixon kína-** **nai.** They say that children vomit when they meet a spirit.⟩
*v.i.* **béchia** : to become hard to work ⟨**Barín akára nato pácho moa béchike.** From being in the sun, the wood for making the paddle has become hard to work.⟩
*v.i.* **béchokiita** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *chokíiti* to wash oneself] : to wash one's face
*n.* **béchoman** : wave : waves ⟨**Béchoman jóni réoara saíikai.** The man shouts as he is tossed about by the waves.⟩
*v.t.* **bechónhaa** *Konibo* **bechónhaka** : to form waves or swells in ⟨**Níwe kóshi pakéxonra páro bechónhake.** A strong wind came and formed swells in the river.⟩
*v.i.* **béchona** : for waves to form ⟨**Moa ián bechónketianra noa jóyamake.** We did not come because swells had formed on the cocha (an oxbow lake).⟩

*v.t.* **béchoa** 1 : to knit the eyebrows ⟨**Bexnán xéaaxa jóni béchoke.** The man drank the liquor in a single gulp and frowned.⟩ 2 : to float to the surface ⟨**Ríkaton béchoman réoara jawen jawékibo béchoke.** When the waves tossed about the river trader, his things floated up.⟩
*v.t.* **béchota** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *chókati* to wash] : to wash the face of
*n.* **béikan** : shadow ⟨**Min béikanra ea mápotoshike.** Your shadow covered me.⟩ *syn.* káya; wéa; óta
*v.t.* **béisa** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *jísti* to see] : to stare fixedly ⟨**Béisxonra jonín —¡Ea oínwe! —akín aká iki.** Staring fixedly at him, the man said: —Look at me!⟩
*v.t.* **békana** : to spread out the boll of (cotton) ⟨**Titán waxmén békanaitianra jawen báke náshiai.** While the mother spreads out the cotton boll, her child bathes.⟩

*postp.* [from Shipibo *be-* with + *-ke*, suf. of completed action + *-iba* yesterday, the other day] : directly across from (a point indicated on the other side of a stretch of water) –Often used with *-keax*. ⟨**Iparia bekeibakeaxa nato jóni joíbake.** This man came yesterday from a place exactly across from Iparía.⟩

*v.i.* **békepia** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *-ke* at the indicated side + *-pi* on the ribs + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to prostrate oneself face down on the ground ⟨**Jónira ja bebon chiránkotax békepia iki.** The man knelt and prostrated himself before him.⟩
*n.* **békoten** *Konibo* **békokan** : remocaspi (a tree) ⟨**Imiriankora bekó ícha iki.** Remocaspi is abundant in Imiría.⟩
See under **kári**

*adj.* **békoman** : with poor eyesight : lacking normal vision; *specif.* : nearsighted ⟨**Nokon pápashokora moa bekón iki; jákopira ochó oínyamai.** My grandfather is nearsighted now, and that is why he cannot see far away.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákeranonra yósima ikáxbi moa bekón iki; jawen pápara ja isínya ikátiai.** This young man is nearsighted now, even though he is not old; his father had the same illness.⟩

*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *-be* with + *-kon* true] : between the two : the two together –Used added to the verb, and it specifies the number of the subject. ⟨**Néte xábataitian noa jobékonke.** While day was breaking, the two of us came together.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2

*v.t.* **bekónhaa** *Konibo* **bekónhaka** [from Shipibo *bekón* of poor eyesight + *-ati* to make] : to fog up : to cloud over ⟨**Nokon ispíkora en xon aká bekónke.** I breathed on the mirror and it fogged up.⟩

*v.i.* **békona** : for one's vision to become blurred ⟨**Non manánxawe bachi piáronki bekónti iki.** They say that when we eat motelo (tortoise) eggs, our vision can become blurred.⟩ ⟨**Kírika yóyoaabichoira noa békonai.** When we devote ourselves only to reading, our vision becomes blurred.⟩
See under **bóna**
*adj. and n.* **békoshin** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *kóshi* strong] *adj.* : able to look at the sun directly *n.* : power of sight

*n.* **bemán** : buttress root : the fin-shaped extension of the trunk at the base of a tree ⟨**Béma kéexonra inábaon jóni tsákake.** Hiding behind the tree's buttress root, the savages wounded the man.⟩

*n.* **bémananin** : face ⟨**Ipo píironki jóni iká iki: Nokon bémananbira en píai —ikironki iká iki.** They say that when he was eating carachama (an armored catfish) a man said: —I am eating my own face.⟩
*v.i.* **bémaa** : to have buttress roots –Used about a tree. ⟨**Nato jíwira moa bémaya iki; jákopira choríshiki.** This tree already has buttress roots, and that is why it is very solid.⟩

*v.t.* **bémaa** [from Shipibo *be-*, root of *béti*, to bring + *-ma* to make + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to send : to send off ⟨**Rimánxonra jonín jawen pápa kírika bémake.** From Lima, the man sent a letter to his father.⟩ ⟨**Jonín jawen báke koríki bemá ikénbira, aínbaon yómetsoake.** A woman stole the money that the man had sent for his son.⟩ *syn.* ráanti; yóiti; yónoti
*v.t.* **beméxa** 1 : to pull out facial hair of 2 : to uproot *(newly planted plants)* from the surface of the ground
*adj.* **bénakan** : new ⟨**Ráma nétera bená maístoro nókotai.** Today a new teacher arrives.⟩
*v.t.* **benáa** *Konibo* **benáaka** : to renew ⟨**Papánra jawen nónti benáake jákiribi tayánxon.** Dad renewed his canoe by carving it again.⟩
*n.* **bénakawekan** [from Shipibo *béna* new + *kawé*, a form of farewell] : gospel ⟨**Bénakawe Márokos** the Gospel according to Mark⟩ *syn.* See under **banjírio**
*n.* **Bená Main** [from Shipibo *bená* new + *mái* land] : New World ⟨**Kírisitobara Korónmara aká iki Bená Mai nokókin.** Christopher Columbus discovered the New World.⟩

*v.t.* **bénaa** : to look for ⟨**Titánra jawen báke ía bénaxonai.** The mother looks for lice on her child.⟩ ⟨**Moa béna riki; ráma bénawetsayamawe.** He has already been looked for; do not look for him anymore.⟩
*adv.* **benáakin** : anew : again ⟨**Rámara benáakin apón esé áke ja noa akínti.** The government has given, again, a law to help us.⟩ ⟨**Nato jónira benáti nokóke.** This man arrived again.⟩
*v.i.* **bénata** : to become new ⟨**Nato xóbo payora moa benáke, jawen ibón bénxoaa.** This old house became new, because its owner repaired it.⟩

*Konibo* **bébo** *n.* **bénbon** *Konibo* **bebón** 1 : male : person of masculine sex ⟨**Epán rekénbakera bénbo iki.** My uncle's firstborn is male.⟩ 2 : man ⟨**Jatíbi bénbobo jíkimaxonbira aínbobobicho non ímayamai.** We let all the men in; but the women, no.⟩ *syn.* BENBO, BENE, JONI all can carry the sense of "male of the human kind". BENBO, then, can denote a male of any age, while JONI applies only to adult males. BENE suggests rather the quality of strength or courage that is characteristic of the male animal of any kind.
*n.* **benchén** : blind person ⟨**Westíora benchénra, Kakónkoxon Ríosen jói ikónhake.** In Caco a blind man converted to the Gospel.⟩

*v.t.* **béncheaa** *Konibo* **béncheaka** : to blind : to make blind ⟨**Kampánra jawen kaíbo pián tsákaxon béncheake.** A campa (an Asháninka person) blinded another by striking him in the eye with an arrow.⟩
*v.i.* **bénchea** : to become blind ⟨**Ronón nátexara nato jóni béncheke.** This man became blind from a snake's bite.⟩
See **bínirisinti**

*n.* **benén** 1 : male ⟨**Nóara béne ikáx, rakéyamai.** We are not afraid because we are males.⟩ 2 : husband : spouse ⟨**Jawen béne pótaira aínbo jabáke.** The woman fled, abandoning her husband.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.5 *syn.* See under **bénbo**
*adj.* **benén** : happy ⟨**Kikínbires béne ikáxxa nokon shinán rároshaman iki.** I am very happy; I feel very glad.⟩
*v.t.* **béneaa** : to gladden : to make happy ⟨**Rimámeax joxónra titán noa béneake.** It made us happy when mother arrived from Lima.⟩
*Konibo* **bénewetsa** *n.* **béneitsan** *Konibo* **bénewetsan** : a woman's brother-in-law ⟨**Aínbo jábatara jawen béneitsan bíke.** Whenthe woman fled, her brother-in-law took possession of her.⟩

*n.* **benénpapan** [from Shipibo *béne, benén* husband + *pápa* father] 1 : a woman's father-in-law –Used the vocative form *pápa* "papa" to address him. 2 : brother of a woman's father-in-law; *also* : husband of the father-in-law's sister *syn.* See under **bakénki**

*n.* **benénpiakan** [from Shipibo *béne, benén* husband + *piá* nephew] : son or daughter of the husband's brother –Used the vocative form *yosí* "old man" or the form *yoxán* "old woman" to address the person in question. –Used little nowadays.

*n.* **benéntitan** [from Shipibo *béne, benén* husband + *títa* mother] 1 : a woman's mother-in-law; *also* : sister of a woman's mother-in-law –Used the vocative form *titá* "mother-in-law!" (from *títa* "mother") in these senses and the following ones. 2 : wife of the brother of a woman's father-in-law; *also* : wife of the mother's brother *syn.* See under **bakénxa**
*adj.* **bénesen** *Konibo* **bénesan** : shallow : not deep ⟨**Xóno tapanra bénesan rakáke.** The lupuna-wood raft ran aground in a shallow spot.⟩
*v.i.* **bénesa** : to become low or shallow ⟨**Moa tsosínketianra páro benéske.** The river is shallow because the water has gone down.⟩
