*v.i.* **bénea** : to be glad : to rejoice ⟨**Nokon papán chonka waránka sóro méniara ea íchabires béneke.** When my father gave me ten thousand soles, I was very glad.⟩ *syn.* BENETI, RAROTI both translate as "to be glad"; but BENETI implies more the joy of receiving, e.g., a gift, whereas RAROTI is more the joy of seeing a cherished person.
See under **íno**

*n. and adv.* **bénkexen** [from Shipibo *ben,* unidentified + *kexá* mouth] *n.* 1 : half 2 : the other side –Used with reference to an object. ⟨**Benkéx wáanon íxonra jonín bóe ránbeke.** The man turned the boquichico (a fish) over so that it would cook on the other side.⟩ *adv.* : on the other side –Used before the last number in a sum introduced by *néke* "on this side", so that the pair *néke...benkéx* means "plus". ⟨**Néke 4 benkéx 4 iki 8.** 4 plus 4 equals 8.⟩ *syn.* napónbekon
*n.* **benón** : a species of huapapa (a heron) ⟨**Táwakoa wéamaanra béno ícha iki.** In the Tabacoa stream the *béno* huapapa species is abundant.⟩

*n.* **benón** : one bigger than another or than the rest –Used immediately after a possessive adjective, which it modifies. ⟨**Nato kabóri bachira en bíke jawen bénoya.** I have obtained these taricaya (a river turtle) eggs and I have another one even bigger than the rest.⟩
See under **bénomaati**

*v.i.* **bénomaata** [from Shipibo *béno* husband + *mawáti* to die] : to become a widow : to be widowed ⟨**Moara westíora simána iki, nato aínbo bénomaata.** It has already been a week since this woman was widowed.⟩
: widow ⟨**Jonínra bénomaata aínbo awínhakin bíke.** A man took a widow as his wife.⟩
*n.* **bénoomatonin** [from Shipibo *bénoti, beno-* to marry (of a woman) + *-oma* without] : unmarried woman ⟨**Aínbo rabe bénoomara Rimán káke.** Two unmarried women went off to Lima.⟩
*v.i.* **bénoa** : to marry (of a woman) ⟨**Rimán káaxa aínbo bénoke.** The woman went to Lima and married there.⟩
*v.t.* **bénoa** 1 : to forget : to lose ⟨**Janra jawen tóoati bénoke níi meran.** He has forgotten his shotgun in the monte (the forest).⟩ 2 : to make a mistake

*v.i.* **bénota** : to get lost ⟨**Jóni benóketianronki yawámasemanki píkonike.** They say that long ago, when a man got lost in the monte (the forest), the toropisco (a bird) helped him find his way out again.⟩ ⟨**Maístoron bákera Rimán káx benóke.** The teacher's son went to Lima and got lost there.⟩
*adj.* **bénoyaton** [from Shipibo *bénoti, beno-* to marry + *-ya* with] : married (of a woman) ⟨**Bénoya aínbora wétsa jóni betan jabáke.** A married woman ran off with another man.⟩

*n.* **bentán** [from Old Shipibo *bénta*, a variant form of *bénoa*, past participle of *bénoti* to marry (said of a woman)] : potential husband : the man whom one may or should marry ⟨**Nato aínbora jawen bénta betanbi bénoa iki.** This woman married the person she was supposed to marry.⟩
*n.* **bénxaman** : scab ⟨**Nato bákera sarámpinin ikax benxán máanai.** This child, who caught the measles, is having his scabs fall off.⟩
*v.t.* **bénxana** : to have scabs ⟨**Bakén yórara moa benxánke, sarámpinin ikáx.** The child has scabs because he has the measles.⟩
*n.* **Benxón** [from Shipibo *benxó* stored away] –Used as a woman's name.

*v.t.* **bénxoaa** *Konibo* **bénxoaka** 1 : to heal ⟨**Nokon pápashoko isínketianra miríkonin bénxoake.** When my grandfather got sick, the healer cured him.⟩ 2 : to mend : to repair ⟨**Nokon epánra tóoati bénxoati onánke.** My uncle knows how to repair shotguns.⟩ 3 : to tidy up ⟨**Matsóxonra aínbaon xóbo bénxoake.** The woman tidied up the house by sweeping it.⟩ 4 : to store away ⟨**Táshira non botíria meran bénxoai.** We store the salt in bottles.⟩ ⟨**Nato wíshati mákina moa benxó ikénbira, jemán píkoxon ói ámakanke.** They took out this typewriter that had been well stored away, and let it get soaked in the rain.⟩ *syn.* níati; téxeati
*v.i.* **bénxokaata** : to tidy oneself up : to be clean ⟨**Maístoronra bákebo óinai bénxokaatarinixon.** The teacher checks the children to see whether they have cleaned themselves up.⟩
*v.i.* **bénxoa** : to get well ⟨**Rabé óxe ísinaxa moa bénxoke, rókotoron ráo xéamaa.** The one who was sick for two months got well because the doctor gave him a remedy.⟩
*n.* **beóman** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + Old Shipibo *ono* water (Shipibo *ómpax*)] : tear ⟨**Mía shinánkinra en ícha beón pótake.** Thinking of you, I have shed many tears.⟩

*v.i.* **béona** : to cry; *also* : to water (of the eyes) ⟨**Nokon pápashoko máwata nínkataxa ea beónke, masá shínani.** On hearing that my grandfather had died, I cried, because I felt grief.⟩ *syn.* wíniti
*v.i.* **béota** : to bend down ⟨**Beóketianra en aínbo wínobainke.** While the woman was bent down, I passed by without her seeing me.⟩
*v.i.* **béotita** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *jotíti* to have a twitch] : to have a twitch in the eye
*adj.* **bepén** : with the face tilted down
*v.i.* **bépea** : to bow one's head ⟨**Oa aínbora yóyoikibi bépeai.** That woman bows her head while she talks.⟩
*n.* **bepón** : rheum (matter in the eye) ⟨**Kanáyoshinronki bépoya iki.** They say that the lightning demon has rheum in its eyes.⟩
See under **bóna**
*v.i.* **bépokoota** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *pokóti* to be stained] : to have something in one's eye ⟨**Eara nisá bépokooke.** I have a bit of dirt in my eye.⟩
*n.* **bépoman** : resin ⟨**Paránta xókakinra bákeainbaon jawen bepón biónke.** While peeling the plantains, the girl got completely stained with the resin.⟩
*v.i.* **bépona** : to ooze resin ⟨**Nato jíwi réraara bepónke; shirínka jiwira íbirai.** This felled tree has oozed resin; it is surely shiringa (a rubber tree).⟩

*v.i.* **bépoa** : to end up with rheum in the eyes ⟨**Nato bákera bépoke, bonán kópiaikax.** This child ended up with rheum in his eyes because the bee cutipó him (afflicted him by supernatural means).⟩

*v.t.* **bépota** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *po*, unidentified (cf. *pótoti* to become dusty); + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to cover the eyes of; *also* : to get into the eyes of ⟨**Niwén akára máshi janbíske; ja mashínra báke bepóke.** The sand scattered in the wind and got into a child's eyes.⟩
*v.i.* **bépota** : to cover one's own eyes
*also* **béxni** *n.* **béranin** *also* **bexnín** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *ráni* body hair] : eyebrow; *also* : eyelash –The form *béxni* is rarely used. *syn.* bérokarani; bérokexni
*v.i.* **bériika** : to blink : to blink one's eyes ⟨**Joé óinaxa ea bériike.** When I looked at the light, I blinked.⟩ *syn.* bexníti

*n.* **berón** 1 : eye ⟨**Nato bakénra jawen wétsa bínoman béroki tsákake.** This child hit his brother in the eye with an aguaje (a palm fruit).⟩ 2 : seed ⟨**Westíora bákera isónxoma bero xéaax mawákeanke.** A child nearly died from swallowing a zapote (a fruit) seed.⟩
*n.* **bérochipoman** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *chipón* rear tendon] : outer corner of the eye ⟨**Jawen bérochiponainra binán tékake.** The wasp stung him at the outer corner of the eye.⟩
*n.* **bérochonin** : a small species of sardine ⟨**Jenénkoniax chóronira bérochon nontín nanéke.** Leaping out of the water, the little *bérochon* sardine landed in the canoe.⟩
*n.* **béroisiman** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *isín* sick] : eye ache; *specif.* : conjunctivitis
*n.* **bérokapoxkon** *Konibo* **bérokapoxkonin** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *ka-* on the spine + *póxko* a species of shirúe (a fish)] : the bone below the eyebrows

*n.* **bérokaranin** *Konibo* **bérokaraninin** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *ka-* on the spine + *ráni* hair] : eyebrow : eyebrows ⟨**Oa jónira bérokaranioma iki.** That man has no eyebrows.⟩ *syn.* bérani

*n.* **bérokexnin** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *ke-* at the edge + *ráni* hair] : eyelash ⟨**Non bérokexni xátearonki óxatikoma iki.** They say that when one's eyelashes are cut, it is hard to sleep.⟩ *syn.* bérani
*n.* **béronamin** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *námi* flesh] : cataract ⟨**Yósibora béronamia iki.** Several old people have cataracts.⟩
*v.i.* **berón ika** [from Shipibo *béro, berón* eye + *iti* to be] : to have an eye ache
*n.* **béroraon** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *ráo* remedy, medicine] : eye drops; *also* : eye ointment ⟨**Bérorao márowe, mia jan béchexeexon.** Buy yourself some ointment to anoint your eyes with.⟩

*n.* **bérotapokon** *Konibo* **bérotapokonin** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *ta-* at the foot + *póko* stomach] : the inner corner of the eye, near the nasal septum ⟨**Berón ikara bérotapokoain bépo jókonai.** When the eye swells, rheum comes out at the inner corner of the eye.⟩
*n.* **bérotapoman** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *tapón* root] : eye muscle ⟨**Aínbora jawen bérotapon sóoika iki.** The woman's eye muscle swelled up.⟩
See under **wáste**
*n.* **béroxantokan** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *xánto* hole] : eye socket ⟨**Wanín pianra béroxantoki tsákake.** He struck him in the eye socket with an arrow made of pijuayo (peach-palm wood).⟩
*n.* **béroyoshíman** [from Shipibo *béro* eye + *yoshín* demon] : a spirit identified with the pupil of the eye and with a person's soul
*n.* **besbén** : a species of red wasp similar to the huairanga (a large wasp) ⟨**Besbén tékaara nato jonín rabé néte yonáke.** From the sting of a *bésbe* wasp, this man had a fever for two days.⟩
*postp.* : level with : over the surface of ⟨**Abionra jéne besenen jóai.** The airplane is coming over the water.⟩
*adj.* **bésesen** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *sése* freckled] : with spots on the face –Also used in the reduplicated form *besésbeses*.

*adj. pl. and n. pl.* **béshekan** *adj. pl.* : very small ⟨**Jopóxa beshéshoko ikax mératikoma iki.** It is very difficult see the isangües because they are very tiny.⟩ *n. pl.* : offspring ⟨**Komán Kenéya Iamanxonronki jonín áni máke cháchiamanike, méeyamawe ján jawen beshébo jákina riki —akin jawen papán áketian.** They say that in the cocha (oxbow lake) Comán Quineya a man was going to spear an enormous paña (piranha), but he did not, because his father told him: —Do not touch it, for it is the one that sustains its young.⟩

*v.t.* **beshéaa** *Konibo* **beshéaka** : to shatter or break into small pieces : to smash to bits ⟨**Westíora jonínra íno beshéakin rérake.** A man macheted a jaguar until he cut it to pieces.⟩ *syn.* páyoti; róroti; tésati
See under **póko**
*v.i.* **béshita** : to be shattered or broken into small pieces ⟨**Titán chómora bochikiax páketi beshékainke.** Mom's clay jar shattered when it fell from high up.⟩
*n.* **beshpín** : sty (in the eye) ⟨**Nato bakénra béshpi pikóxon yonáke.** This child has a fever because he got a sty.⟩
*n.* **bésipoman** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *sipón* wrinkle] : wrinkle on the face

*v.t.* **béskia** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *síkati* to paint] 1 : to paint the face of : to paint on the surface ⟨**Janra báke béskiai.** He is painting the child's face.⟩ 2 : to stain the face of. See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*v.i.* **béskita** [from Shipibo *béskiti* to paint the face of + *-ii*, reflexive suf.] 1 : to paint one's own face without designs 2 : to stain one's face ⟨**Ja bákebora méskitax beskíkanai.** The children are staining their hands and faces.⟩

*n.* **béskoman** [from Shipibo; imitative of its call] : chirriclés (a bird) ⟨**Moátianronki Inkán chíitsistoki béskoman bónike.** They tell that in ancient times the *chirriklés* carried off a firebrand from the Stingy Inca.⟩
*adj.* **besmín** [from Shipibo *be-* to the forehead + *smi*, unidentified] : filled to the brim
*v.i.* **bésmia** : to fill up to the brim ⟨**Jawen chómo bésmitiakinra titán xéati nachíke.** Mama poured the drink into her jar, filling it to the brim.⟩
*v.i.* **bésoikiita** : to rub one's face

*n.* **bésoikiitinin** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *sóikiiti, sóikii-* to rub oneself + *-ti* with which] : handkerchief ⟨**Nokon bésoikitira ea niwén boónke.** The wind carried off my handkerchief.⟩ *syn.* panyón
*v.i.* **bésoa** : to wake up ⟨**Néte béaitian átapa kéotaitianra ea bésoke.** I woke up when the rooster crowed at dawn.⟩
*v.t.* **bésoa** [from Shipibo *be-* in the eye + *sóiti* to rub] 1 : to rub the face, forehead, eye, or eyes of 2 : to remove the excess contents of (a jar)
*v.t.* **béstea** [from Shipibo *be-* on the forehead + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut the forehead hair (bangs) of
*v.i.* **bésteta** [from Shipibo *be-* on the forehead + *ste*, element of *xáteti* to cut + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to cut one's own forehead hair (bangs)

*n.* **bestétinin** [from Shipibo *besté-*, root of *bestéti* to cut one's forehead hair + *-ti* with which] : scissors ⟨**Ikítoainoara bestéti kopíma ea mároke.** I bought some very cheap scissors in Iquitos.⟩

*postp. and conj.* **-be** *postp.* : with –Used the postpositional form *-be* with one-syllable complements and the form *betan* mostly with the other complements. ⟨**Rámara nokon awín betan ea Kakónko kái.** Now I am going to Caco with my wife⟩ ⟨**Ochítira mibé kákasai.** The dog wants to go with you⟩ *conj.* : and –Used between two nouns in a coordinated phrase. ⟨**José betan Títora yóyo ikai.** José and Tito are talking⟩ *syn.* BETAN, I, ITAN, JAINOAX, JAINXON all are translated as "and", as conjunctions of coordinated phrases or words. BETAN, I, and ITAN are invariable, whereas JAINOAX, JAINXON alternate according to the transitivity of the main verb. *syn.* -ya

*v.t.* **bétanea** [from Shipibo *be-* on the forehead + *táneti* to press] : to press and deform the forehead of (a newborn baby) with a board ⟨**Rámatianra jatíxonbi báke bétaneyamaikanai.** Nowadays only some women press the foreheads of their children⟩

*n.* **bétanetin** [from Shipibo *bétane-* to press and deform the forehead (of a newborn baby) + *-ti* with what] : a kind of board traditionally used to press and deform the forehead of a newborn baby ⟨**Shawányainoa aínbora rókotoron bétaneti pótanaanke.** The doctor threw away the board belonging to a woman from Shahuaya⟩
See under **óxati**
*v.t.* **bétana** [from Shipibo *betan* with + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to pass by the side of
*n.* **bétaronin** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *táro* dirty] : dirtiness of the face : dirty face ⟨**Bakénra jawen bétaro chókai.** The child is washing his dirty face⟩

*v.i.* **bétashia** [from Shipibo *be-* on the surface + *tash*, imitative of the sound + *-iti* to make] : to bob up to the surface ⟨**Wáme bétashiketianra papán cháchike.** When the paiche (arapaima) surfaced, dad speared it with the harpoon.⟩
*n.* **béteman** : thick porridge (e.g., of fish) ⟨**Betén xanara ráchikiike.** The hot porridge fell on his body⟩
*v.t.* **bétena** : to prepare porridge (e.g., of fish) ⟨**Titán ámakiribetenketianra kóka nokóke.** While mom was preparing gamitana (a river fish) porridge, my uncle arrived⟩

*v.t.* **beá** : to bring ⟨**Wétsa neténki inón cháxo yóia iki: -Min píti béketianra en mia píamai; min béyamakenra en mia píai -akin.** One day the jaguar said to the deer: -If you bring mitayo (wild game meat) I will not eat you; but if you do not, I will eat you⟩ *syn.* bíti
*v.i.* **bétita** : to close one's eyes ⟨**Oraní bétitaxa jóni óxake.** A man fell asleep when he closed his eyes to pray⟩

*also* **békoten ewa** *Konibo* **békokan ewa** *n.* **bétoken ewan** *also* **békoten ewan** *Konibo* **békokan ewan** [from Shipibo *békoten ewa*, by metathesis of the *-k* (*-k*) and the *-t*, and this from Shipibo *bekó, békoten* remocaspi + *-ewa, -ewan*, augmentative] : red remocaspi (a hardwood tree) ⟨**En bétokenewa wíntiaara ea kokámen yómetsoake.** A cocama stole the paddle I made of red remocaspi.⟩ ⟨**Békoten ewa wíntiaara bási íkai.** A paddle made of red remocaspi lasts a long time.⟩
*n.* **betónkonin** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *tónko* round] : forehead : upper part of the face ⟨**Rírora jawen betónkoain** **seréya iki.** The musmuque has a stripe on its forehead.⟩

*v.t.* **bétoshbaaka** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *toshbáati* to spit on] : to spit in the face of ⟨**Bakénra jawen wétsa bétoshbaake tsinikin.** The boy spat in his brother's face while playing.⟩
*v.t.* **bétosha** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *tóshati* to burst] : to burst the eye of

*v.t.* **bétsaa** 1 : to finish (an expanse) ⟨**Papánra jawen waínko xéki bánakin moa bétsake.** Dad has already finished planting corn across the whole expanse of his garden plot.⟩ 2 : to go to the end of
*v.i.* **bétsekeeta** [from Shipibo *be-* of the eye + *tsekéti* to take out] : to take out one's own eyes
*v.i.* **bétseta** : to spread all over ⟨**Páronaponra bechón moa betséke.** The waves are all over the river.⟩
*v.t.* **bétseta** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *tséketi* to take out] : to take out the eye of
*v.i.* **bétsina** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *tsínati* to reduce swelling] : for one's eye to go down in swelling
*v.i.* **bétsisa** : to put out (a fire) with water ⟨**Titán chíi ketéakenbira oín betsísnaanke.** Mom lit the fire, but the rain put it out.⟩

*v.t.* **betsóaka** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *tso*, imitative of the sound + *áti* to make] : to kiss in the Western style ⟨**Injinironra Rímameax nokóxon jawen awín betsóa-** **ke.** On arriving from Lima, the engineer kissed his wife.⟩

*v.i.* **bétsoa** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *tso*, unidentified element + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to close one's eyes in fear ⟨**En xómoxen átiaara bétsoke.** He closed his eyes in fear because I threatened him with a needle.⟩ ⟨**Jónira kampón bétsoax níke.** The man is standing on the airstrip with his eyes closed in fear.⟩
*n.* **béwakan** 1 : song ⟨**Bewá onán onanbires jónira chipónkiax jóke.** The man who knows the songs very well has come from downriver.⟩ 2 : hymn 3 : music
[from Shipibo *shíro* joke + *bewá*] : a kind of comic song with *jée* as an interjection at the end of each verse *syn.* íno
*v.i.* **béwaa** : to sing ⟨**Jawen joné xáwekira béwai.** She is singing to her sweetheart.⟩
*v.t.* : to call (a person) with the hand
*v.t.* : to take a little (e.g., of the contents of a jar of masato (a fermented drink)) off the top
*v.i.* **béweta** [from Shipibo *be-* on the forehead + *weyóti* to sway] : to nod off ⟨**Oxakasira pápashoko bewébewetai.** As he dozes, the grandfather nods off.⟩

*adj.* **bexan** [from Shipibo *be-* on the surface + *xa*, unidentified] 1 : rough ⟨**Nato jonín poyánra kikínbires béxa iki.** This man's arm is very rough.⟩ 2 : covered or full of boils ⟨**Ochítinin pókora béxa iki.** The dog's belly is covered with boils.⟩ *syn.* BEXA, XAXA both can be translated as "rough", but BEXA refers more to a soft surface (e.g., of the skin), whereas XAXA refers more to a hard surface (e.g., the shell of a chelonian).

*v.i.* **béxaa** : to become covered or be full of boils ⟨**Nato aínbaon ponyánra moa béxake; jákopi non ráomeeti yóiabira ikáshamai.** This woman's arm is full of boils; and although we advise her to get treated, she does not want to.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*v.t.* **béxeta** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *xéteti* to sniff] : to kiss in the Shipibo style as a sign of affection
*n. and adj.* **bexkán** *n.* : a kind of mythological people resembling dogs, but shrunken and dwarfish –Seldom used nowadays. *adj.* : small –Seldom used nowadays.
*n.* **bexkón** : a small species of toad ⟨**Baín kakínra en béxko jamáke.** As I went along the path, I stepped on a toad.⟩
*adj.* **bexmín** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *xmi*, unidentified] : cross-eyed : one-eyed ⟨**Nato béxmi jónira sináyora iki.** This cross-eyed man is very ill-tempered.⟩ *syn.* beyósh
*v.t.* **béxmiaa** *Konibo* **béxmiaka** : to make one-eyed ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke béxmiake bétanexon.** A woman made her son one-eyed by placing a board on his forehead.⟩
*v.i.* **béxmia** : to become one-eyed ⟨**Nato bákeranonra pirótanin béroki tsákaa béxmike.** This young man became one-eyed because a ball hit his eye.⟩

*adj.* **béxnaman** : clear : transparent –Used of a liquid. ⟨**Aroyaninra jéne bexnán ikax píti jíshti iki.** In the Aruya stream the fish can be seen, because the water is transparent.⟩ *syn.* páxna
*n.* **béxnaman** [from Shipibo *bexnán* clear] : cane liquor : aguardiente : rum ⟨**Ténamanra bexnán mároai ríkaton iki.** At the port is the itinerant river trader who sells aguardiente.⟩
See **bérani**

*v.i.* **béxnita** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *ráni* hair + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to blink ⟨**Báke béxnitainbira rókotoron béroraon bechéxke.** Even though the child was blinking, the doctor put eye drops in his eyes.⟩ 2 : to wink ⟨**Nato sontárora** **bexníke.** This soldier winked⟩ *syn.* bériiti
*adj.* **bexpén** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *xpe*, unidentified] : with sunken eyes

*n.* **béxpetonkon** [from Shipibo *béxpetonko*, imitative of its call] : a large species of dove ⟨**Non béxpetonko máwaketianronki noa bonán tékati iki.** They say that if we imitate the call of the *béxpetonko* dove, the isula (bullet ant) may sting us⟩

*v.i.* **béxteta** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eyebrow + *xatéti* to cut oneself] 1 : to cut oneself on the eyebrow or forehead 2 : to paint one's forehead so that it looks like straight-line cuts ⟨**Noa namáketian nanén béxtetaronki xenón keyóti iki.** They say that when we dream we paint our forehead with huito (a dye plant), it means we are going to get scabies⟩
*adj.* **béyakan** : sharply painful : painful ⟨**Non rimón moxa jámatara beyá iki.** Stepping on a lemon thorn is very painful.⟩ *syn.* móka
*v.i.* **beyáa** *Konibo* **beyáaka** : to make (someone) feel sharp pain ⟨**En móxa jámatara nato jonín ea beyáakanke.** This man made me feel even more pain than when I stepped on the thorn.⟩
*v.i.* **béyata** : to feel sharp pain ⟨**Nokon pokónkora ea béyatai en píti xao xéaa.** I feel a sharp pain in my stomach because I swallowed a thorn.⟩
*n.* **béyosin** *Konibo* **béyosan** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *yoshín* demon] : madness : bewilderment ⟨**Nato béyosanra ea masá ténemai.** This madness makes me suffer.⟩

*v.t.* **beyósaa** *Konibo* **beyósaka** 1 : to stun : to daze ⟨**Mapónko jiwín ríshkixonra beyósake.** He stunned him by hitting him on the head with a stick.⟩ 2 : to drive mad : to make crazy ⟨**Kámamanronki noa beyósaxon réteti iki.** They say the *kamán* ghost drives us mad and then kills us.⟩
*adj.* **béyoshin** [from Shipibo *be-* on the face + *yoshín* demon] : one-eyed : with a twisted face *syn.* béxmi

*v.i.* **béyoshina** [from Shipibo *be-* on the eye + *yoshínti* to become possessed] 1 : to be seized by fear 2 : to go mad ⟨**Ayorakin óni xéaax moa béyoshina riki.** He went mad from drinking too much ayahuasca.⟩

*v.i.* **béyosa** [from Shipibo; short form of *béyoshinti* to go mad] 1 : to feel dizzy : to feel dizziness ⟨**Piróta aki íshtoaxa ea beyóske.** When I was running around playing soccer, I felt dizzy.⟩ 2 : to be seized by fear ⟨**Nato bákera béyosi yamé sión iwanke.** Last night this child screamed and cried, gripped by fear.⟩ ⟨**Béyosira nato báke jéne meran káke.** Gripped by fear, this boy jumped into the water.⟩ 3 : to go mad : to be crazy ⟨**Béyosai ikaxa nato aínbo jabáke.** On going mad, this woman ran away.⟩

*modifying suf.* –Used postposed to any part of a clause, whether main or subordinate. 1 : self : on the part of (a specific person) –Used in either of these two senses especially when *-ribi* "also" or "again" functions as a suffix in the sentence. ⟨**Sápemantitan nínia. Wísoinonribi níniribiai.** The water animal *sápeman tita* pulled the rope, and the yanapuma (a mythical water-jaguar) in turn pulled the opposite end.⟩ ⟨**Enbiribira mia áyamai.** For my part, I am not going to do anything to you.⟩ ⟨**Nóabiribira néno iki; jáboribira jaín iki.** By our own will we are here, and by their will they are there.⟩ 2 : own ⟨**Paénxonra, jonín jawen pápabi réteke.** Drunk, a man killed his own father.⟩ 3 : even ⟨**Koáratianinra jóni bóke; jaínxon jawen bákebi inónbira bóke.** The guard took the man away; what is more, he also took his son.⟩ –Used with the sense of "although" when added to the infinitive or the subordinate verb. ⟨**Jawen titán kátima yóiabira báke karéske.** Although his mother told him not to go, the boy went.⟩ ⟨**Jawen papán jóno rétekenbira, Josékan píamai.** Although his father killed a sajino (collared peccary), José does not eat it.⟩ –Used postposed to the participle plus the negative suffix *-ma* to mean "without", "un-", or "before". ⟨**Jawen pápa nokótamabira, ja níi meran káke, jóno bénai.** Before his father had arrived, he went into the monte (the forest) to look for a sajino.⟩ –Used postposed to the participle plus the suffix *-ma* "not" and the suffix *-tian* "when" with the sense of "before". ⟨**Tántiamatianbira, en nokon wái óroke.** Before taking a rest, I worked my garden plot.⟩ –Used in the compound form *-bires* with the sense of "only", "just", "very", or "completely". ⟨**Bénbobobiresa non kóboranai; aínbobora non áyamai.** We charge only the men; not the women.⟩ ⟨**Kikín ánibires ábionra Máioshiain nokóke, já non oínyosma.** A very large airplane, such as we had never seen before, arrived in Pucallpa.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.1.3; 5.3.2.2 *syn.* ashón; -bix; kikín
*v.i.* **bíakaata** : to be captured : to come to belong to a group ⟨**Nato jónira sontárobo márachanai óini káx bíakaake.** This man went to watch the soldiers march and was captured.⟩

*v.t.* **bíbana** [from Spanish *haker vivas* + Shipibo *-n*, verbal-derivation suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to cheer : to acclaim ⟨**Apo jóketianra non bibánhibake.** Yesterday, when the president came, we cheered him.⟩

*adj. and n.* **bichán** *adj.* 1 : phlegmy : viscous 2 : slippery ⟨**Nóshara bíchayora ikax, yátanabi síiiresai.** The puñuisiqui (a slippery fish) slips away when grabbed, because it is very slippery.⟩ *n.* : viscous liquid (e.g., phlegm or sap) ⟨**Tóoyaxon bokón bicha xéaaxonki jákoni bakénti iki.** They say that when a pregnant woman drinks the sap of the cetico (a tree), her delivery will be easier.⟩ *syn.* bishtón
See under **bawín**

*v.i.* **bíchaa** 1 : to become phlegmy or viscous ⟨**Titán átsaxeatira moa bíchake, asókaro máxkatax.** Mom's masato (a fermented drink) has turned viscous for lack of sugar.⟩ 2 : to become slippery ⟨**Oi béketianra non jéma moa bíchake.** With the falling of the rain, our yard has become slippery.⟩ *syn.* sibá

*n.* **bichín** 1 : dermis ⟨**Nato aínbo rérakaatara jawen bíchi jíshtibires iki.** Because of the cut this woman got, her dermis is clearly visible.⟩ 2 : skin ⟨**Non bawín bichi piáronki chópa keyóti iki.** They say that if we eat the skin of the súngaro (a large catfish), we may run short of clothing.⟩ 3 : leather : hide ⟨**Non róo bichi bómpoaaronki bebón kestén iki.** They say that when we make a drum with the hide of a cotomono (howler monkey), it sounds louder.⟩ 4 : bark ⟨**Mánkoa bichi kobínhaxon xéaaronki kóojison ítima iki.** They say that when we drink the water of boiled mango bark, it is very unlikely that we will catch gonorrhea.⟩
See under **chópa**
*v.i.* **bíchimeeta** : to come off

*v.t.* **bíchina** : to take away ⟨**Yánkabiresa jaton pátoronbaon jato jawéki bichínkatitai.** Their bosses used to take their things away without paying them.⟩ –Used in participle form *bíchinai* with the sense of "minus" in a subtraction. –Used after the number subtracted. ⟨**8 ikénbi 4 bíchina bánetai 4.** 8 minus 4 equals 4.⟩ *syn.* tsáati

*modifying suf.* : only : just –Used added to a noun, an adjective, a pronoun, or a verb. ⟨**Míabichora en shínanai.** I am thinking only of you.⟩ ⟨**Nokón wáatara pásianbichoai.** My aunt only strolls about.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.6 *syn.* -res
*n.* **bídirion** [from Spanish] : glass ⟨**Bídirio tsosakan nokon táe xáteke.** A piece of glass cut my foot.⟩
*n.* **bíikan** : mosquito; *specif.* : zancudo (the long-legged mosquito) ⟨**Bíikanra ea píai.** The zancudos are bothering me.⟩
*adj.* **bíiman** : sticky ⟨**Papán mishkínhaara moa bíin iki.** The honey that dad prepared is already sticky.⟩ *syn.* nakó; xetín

*v.t.* **bíinhaa** *Konibo* **bíinhaka** : to make sticky ⟨**Titánra parántaxeati bíinhake, ompáxoma cháchixon.** Mom made the chapo (a plantain drink) sticky, because she mashed it without adding water.⟩
*interj.* : grab it –Used in repeated form.
*n.* **bikónyanin** [from Spanish] : vicuña

*n.* **bimín** : fruit ⟨**Ea naránxa inánwe -akin en akára ea wanín bimires ménike.** When I asked him for an orange, he gave me only a pijuayo (peach-palm) fruit.⟩ *syn.* BIMI, YOBIN both have the meaning of "fruit", but YOBIN specifies a fruit that is edible without cooking.

*n.* **bimínkeyon** [from Shipibo *bími* fruit + *kéyoti, keyo-* to finish] : a species of small parrot, green with a yellow breast ⟨**Nato aínbo bénomaataton bimínkeyo kéenainbira en mónso méniamake.** Although the mestizo wanted this widow's little *bimínkeyo* parrot, I did not give it to him.⟩
See under **paránta**

*v.i.* **bímia** : to bear fruit ⟨**Wanín bímiketianra en mia píkoai -akinki manánxawen maxó aká iki.** They tell that the motelo (tortoise) promised the zorro (fox) to get it out of the hole when the pijuayo (peach palm) bore fruit.⟩

*n.* **bímpachin** [from Shipibo *bími* fruit + *páchi* soft] : a species of tree with round, yellow fruits ⟨**Bímpachi kókoaitianra papán awá réteke.** While the tapir ate the fruits of the *bímpachi*, dad killed it⟩

*n.* **bímpishin** [from Shipibo *bimi* fruit + *pish*, unidentified] : guava tree ⟨**Bimpísh kókokokokinronki bákebaon awá mapónko tsákanike.** They tell that once, many years ago, some boys were eating guavas and throwing the peels on the head of a tapir⟩
*n.* **binán** : wasp ⟨**Bína méeyamawe; miara tékanake.** Don't bother the wasps; they can sting you.⟩
[from Shipibo *boshí* penis + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp with an elongated body
[from Shipibo *kóyo* a small species of ant + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp similar in color and size to the *kóyo* ants
[from Shipibo *chána* a small species of paucar (an oropendola) + *bína* wasp] : a species of black wasp with a yellow back like the paucar
[from Shipibo *chorísh* hard + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp very similar to the shinguto
[from Shipibo *wáka, wakán* cow, or from Old Shipibo *wáka, wakán* fish + *bína* wasp] : shirushiru
[from Shipibo *wápa* a species of bird + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp with a gray body like that of the *wápa* bird
[from Shipibo *wása* fraile (a monkey) + *bína* wasp] : a yellow species of wasp
[from Shipibo *íwi* stingray + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp similar to the huairanga in both its size and its somewhat reddish color
[from Shipibo *íno* jaguar + *bína* wasp] : a gray species of wasp, striped like a jaguar, and similar to the ronsapa
[from Shipibo *joshín* red + *bína* wasp] : a reddish species of wasp
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp with a blackish body
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *bína* wasp] : a black species of wasp the size of the shirushiru that builds its nest in the ground
[from Shipibo *mapó* clay + *bína* wasp] : a reddish species of wasp of medium size that builds its nest in clay
[from Shipibo *mári* añuje (an agouti) + *bína* wasp] : huairanga
[from Shipibo *máshi* sand, beach + *bína* wasp] : a small yellow species of wasp that builds its nest in the sand
[from Shipibo *níi* jungle + *wáka, wakán* cow or Old Shipibo *wáka, wakán* + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp that lives in the jungle or the monte (the forest)
[from Shipibo *óxe* moon + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp with a reddish body and white wings, whose nest has been compared in appearance to the moon
[from Shipibo *xébi* vulva + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp whose nest has been compared in appearance to the vulva
[from Shipibo *táxa* palizada (a driftwood tangle) + *bína* wasp] : a species of wasp that typically builds its nest in the palizada
[from Shipibo *taxnáti, taxna-* to moor + *bína* wasp] : a reddish species of wasp of medium body that builds its nest in leaves
[from Shipibo *yawísh* armadillo + *bína* wasp] : a blackish species of wasp with black-tipped wings whose nest has been compared in appearance to that of the armadillo
*also* **binágre** *n.* **binákirin** *also* **binágren** [from Spanish] : vinegar
*also* **béndisinti** *v.t.* **bínirisina** *also* **béndisina** [from Spanish *bendekir* + *-n*, verbal-derivation suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to bless
See under **íno**
*adj.* **bínkoman** : sticky (e.g., to the teeth) ⟨**Titán átsaxeati binkónra páema iki.** Mom's sticky masato (a fermented drink) is not fermented.⟩
*n.* **binón** [from Spanish] : wine
*n.* **bínoman** : aguaje (moriche palm fruit) ⟨**Nónti bócho binón beíra épa réokooke.** My uncle capsized while bringing a canoe full of aguaje fruits.⟩

*n.* **binóntaxon** [from Shipibo *binón* aguaje (moriche palm) + *táxo* section] : a branch of the aguaje palm used, e.g., in the loom and to make mats ⟨**Papánra mératabo yasánke, binóntaxo kawínhaatonin.** Dad seated the visitors on a mat made from the aguaje palm.⟩
*adj.* **bínshiman** [from Shipibo *bin-*, unidentified + *joshín* red] : ruddy at birth ⟨**Báke binshínra rókotoron bíke.** The doctor picked up the newborn ruddy baby.⟩

*v.t.* **bínsina** [from Spanish *venker, venke-* + Shipibo *-n*, verbal-derivation suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to defeat ⟨**Chóyachakinronki noa binsíntiki máiki pótakin.** They say the demon of the chullachaqui can defeat us in a contest of strength, throwing us to the ground.⟩ *syn.* See under **áresti**
*n.* **bintánan** [from Spanish] : window

*also* **bintísho** *n.* **bintín** *also* **bintíshon** : guarapo (a fermented sugarcane drink) ⟨**Atsaxeati bíntishoaman xéaaxa jóni páena iki.** The man got drunk from drinking masato (a fermented drink) well seasoned with guarapo.⟩ *syn.* **warápo**
*n.* **bíntiochon** [from Spanish *veintiocho*] : the twenty-eighth of July

*modifying suf.* 1 : more or less ⟨**Noara Máioshiain bókanai; jáwekeska ikáxa noa chónka nétebira jóti iki.** We are going to Pucallpa; and, depending on what happens, we will return in about ten days.⟩ 2 : maybe : perhaps –Used added to the verb. ⟨**Miara yóshiman bíbirake —ixonra en shinánshinan nai —akinronki aínbaon jawen béne ánike.** Many times I thought that maybe a demon had taken you —said his wife.⟩
*n.* **Birín** [from Shipibo *bíriti, biri-* to flash] –Used as a masculine or feminine name.
*n.* **Bíriaaben** [from Shipibo *bíriti, biri-* to flash + *aabe*, unidentified] –Used as a feminine name.
*v.t.* **bíriaa** *Konibo* **bíriaka** : to make flash ⟨**Ea rátekaskinra nato aínbaon ispíko bíriake.** This woman made a mirror flash because she wanted to scare me.⟩
*n.* **bíribinan** [from Spanish] : verbena
*n.* **Bírimenin** [from Shipibo *Bíri*, a feminine name + *méniti, meni-* to give] –Used as a masculine name.
*v.i.* **bíria** : to flash (e.g., lightning, a firefly, or a mirror) ⟨**Ispiko barín ténaara bíriai.** The mirror flashes from the rays of the sun.⟩
*n.* **bíshkoten** *Konibo* **bíshkokan** : scrape : wound ⟨**Jawen bishkókira binán tékake.** A wasp stung him on his wound.⟩ *syn.* tsewé
*v.t.* **bíshkona** : to scrape (e.g., an infection) on the skin ⟨**Tsákakinra nokon bobón ea pirótanin bishkónke.** The ball, when it hit me, scraped the wound on my skin.⟩
*v.t.* **bíshkoa** : to scrape the skin of ⟨**Nato bakénra ea paránxon bonbón bíshkomake.** When I was distracted, this child made me scrape off the scab (that I had because of an infection).⟩
*v.i.* **bíshkota** : to scrape one's skin ⟨**Méchataxa nokon bonbón bishkóke.** I scraped off the scab when I got wet.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákera páketi bishkóke.** This child scraped himself when he fell.⟩
*v.t.* **bishnóaa** *Konibo* **bishnóaka** : to make fester ⟨**Nato báke yóitimanra nokón nonbé bishnóake.** This wretched child made my boil fester.⟩
*v.i.* **bíshnota** : to fester (*a wound*) ⟨**Jóni pokónko ménotara moa bishnóke, raónyamaa.** The burn the man had on his belly festered because it had not been treated.⟩
*adj. & n.* **bíshtoman** *adj.* : slimy *n.* : slimy liquid ⟨**Atapa bachi tóshitara bishtón bóai.** When the hen's egg breaks, a viscous liquid runs out.⟩ *syn.* bícha
*adj.* **bisín** : having warts or tiny growths on the skin ⟨**Nato aínbaon ponyánra bísi iki.** This woman's arm has little warts.⟩

*n.* **bísikiritanin** [from Spanish] : bicycle ⟨**Xónoronki bísikiritanin níai; péiaronkiki ja bísikirita.** They say the demon of the lupuna (a giant kapok tree) rides a bicycle, and that this bicycle has wings.⟩
*v.t.* **bískiaka** : to whisk ⟨**Paránta korára titán bískiake pápa xéamati.** Mom whisked the cooked ripe plantain to give dad to drink.⟩

*n.* **bískiatin** [from Shipibo *biskia-* root of *bískiati* to whisk + *-ti* with which] : a kind of whisk that is twirled between the hands and is used to make chapo (a plantain drink) ⟨**Jawen bakén bískiati pótanaanara, aínbaon jawen báke ríshkike.** The mother whipped her son because he lost her *bískiati* whisk.⟩
*v.i.* **bískiika** : to shake oneself ⟨**Náshii sénenaxa ochíti bískiike.** The dog shook itself after finishing bathing.⟩

*v.t.* **bismánhaa** *Konibo* **bismánhaka** 1 : to fail to reach ⟨**Nato bákera nontín nanékasi bismánhax jenénko káke.** This boy wanted to get into the canoe, but he did not reach it and fell into the water.⟩ 2 : to lose one's breath ⟨**Ishtoxon joín bismánhaxa, mawákeska pakéke.** While running, he lost his breath and fell as if dead.⟩

*v.i.* **bísmana** : to fall short : to be lacking : to not reach ⟨**Nokon chópa bochiki pánia bíkasabira ea bismánke.** I want to take down my clothes hanging up above, but I can't reach them.⟩ ⟨**Bochikixon risbí pákexonabiki bísmana iki.** It is said that when they lowered the rope down to him, it did not reach.⟩ *syn.* máxkati; pishínti
*n.* **Bitán** –Used as a masculine name.
*v.i.* **bítaxameeta** : to get squeezed : to get stuck : to get crushed ⟨**Jawen onáma kopira nato báke bítaxameke.** Through his clumsiness, this boy got stuck.⟩

*v.t.* **bítaxa** : to squeeze : to jam : to crush ⟨**Bákera mawáke, jiwín bítaxa.** A child died when a tree crushed him.⟩ *syn.* BITAXTI, POTSITI both are translated as "to squeeze"; but BITAXTI is used more about a person, and POTSITI is used about things pressed together that get squeezed.

*v.t.* **biá** 1 : to get : to take ⟨**Nato chópara papán ea bixónke.** Dad got me these clothes.⟩ 2 : to pick up ⟨**Jéne meran káketianra báke biríbakanke.** When the child fell into the water, they picked him up.⟩ 3 : to bring ⟨**Káro bitáwen.** Go bring the firewood.⟩ 4 : to receive : to welcome ⟨**Meráketianra papán jakónhakin bíke.** When he visited us, Dad welcomed him kindly.⟩ *syn.* béti; tsáati
*n.* **biwín** : shihui (a kind of snake) ⟨**Jónira biwín mái chicho bókeana iki.** A shihui almost carried a man into a cave.⟩

*reflexive pron.* **-binix** [from Shipibo *-bi* only + *-ix*, short form of *ikáx*, subordinate form of *íti* to be] –Used added to the *en-*, *min-*, *jan-*, *non-*, *maton-*, and *jaton-* forms of the personal pronoun with reflexive or emphatic force (e.g., of "self" or "own") that is added to the pronoun. ⟨**Enbíx ea joá riki nato maná keyá mápeti.** I have come alone to climb this high hill.⟩ ⟨**Enra mia íoyamai; minbíx katánwe.** I am not going to guide you; go by yourself.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákera janbíx tápitinin mapéke.** This child climbed the ladder by himself.⟩ ⟨**Máto pátoron betan téeyamai, matónbinix téetakayara íti iki jakónyora.** It would be much better for you to work for yourselves, and not for a boss.⟩ ⟨**Jatónbinix boáxa moa béyamakanai.** Since they have gone on their own accord, they no longer return.⟩ 1 : by myself, yourself, himself/herself or ourselves : alone ⟨**Ea méeyamawe; enbíx ea joáma riki —akin jato akábironki Ínkán Báke míinkana iki.** Leave me be; I have not come of my own accord —said the Son of the Inca. But even so, they buried him (in the mud at the water's edge).⟩ ⟨**Káyamawe; minbíx mia joáma riki.** Don't go, because you have not come of your own accord.⟩ ⟨**Jáwetianbira jáskara jawékibo janbíx jónitima iki.** Such things could never create themselves.⟩ 2 : to myself (yourself, himself/herself or ourselves) ⟨**Tóoati pishíketianra enbíx ea retékeanke.** If the shotgun had gone off, I would have killed myself.⟩ ⟨**¿Minbíx mia rérakaatarin? —akinra rókotoron ea áke.** —Did you cut yourself? —the doctor asked me.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbora janbíx yamín rérakaake, jawen benén jakómakin aká mawákasi.** This woman wanted to die because her husband mistreated her, and that is why she cut herself with the axe.⟩ ⟨**Nonbíxa noa jakómain níakaake.** We ourselves got into a bad situation.⟩ 3 : among (ourselves, yourselves, or themselves) : alone –Used in this sense with plural pronouns. ⟨**Nonbíx íti riki náshii; moa noa ján ímaira yámake.** We are going to bathe by ourselves, because the one who supervises us at the bath is not here.⟩ ⟨**Máto pátoron betan téeyamai, matónbinix téetakayara íti iki jakónyora.** It would be much better if you just worked among yourselves.⟩ ⟨**Rámara aínbobo jatónbinix pirótanin tsíniai; moátianra bénbobaon ímakatitai.** Nowadays women play soccer by themselves; formerly, the men guided them.⟩ ⟨**Jatónbinixa kámpabo réteananke.** The Campa fought among themselves.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.1.2 *syn.* -bi

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *bóo* hair] 1 : on the hair ⟨**boéxti** to comb the hair of⟩ 2 : on the side of the head ⟨**bopéti** to pierce on the side of the head of⟩ 3 : at the topmost point ⟨**bobésti** to climb to the topmost point of⟩ 4 : on the stump or from the stump ⟨**boxóxti** to sprout from the stump⟩ 5 : on the roof beams or from the roof beams of the house ⟨**bocháxti** to hew the roof beams⟩ 6 : on the handle or of the handle of a knife or machete ⟨**bonéxti** to fasten onto the handle⟩ 7 : at the mouth or of the mouth of a sack ⟨**bokéxti** to sew at the mouth of a sack⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*noun suf.* **–bón** *Konibo* **–baon** *xet.* **–baen** *pish.* **–baen** –Used to form the plural of nouns that often refer to groups of human beings. ⟨**Bákebaonra nato xóbo ménoke.** Some boys burned this house.⟩ 1 : with companions : with others of the same kind *–Used in this sense with proper names.* ⟨**Kósibaonra nato xóbo ménoke.** Pepe and his companions burned this house.⟩ 2 : with other species of the same genus or class –Used generally with nouns that do not refer to human beings. ⟨**yáwabo** white-lipped peccaries together with others (e.g., collared peccaries and pigs) of the same genus⟩ –Used following repeated numbers in an expression that has the sense of, e.g., "ten at a time". ⟨**Topónwe chónkabo chónkabo asta pácha kaman.** Count by tens up to a hundred.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.4
*n.* **boánhisin** : sacha ajo (a wild garlic plant) ⟨**Non boánhis jene xéaara ísiman ítima iki.** When we drink the juice of the sacha ajo, illnesses rarely attack us.⟩
[from Shipibo *baná* planted (past part. of *bánati* to plant) + *boánhis* sacha ajo] : a species of sacha ajo with elongated leaves that grows up to half a meter tall
[from Shipibo *niá* standing (past part. of *níti* to stand) + *boánhis* sacha ajo] : a species of sacha ajo that grows in the form of a tree

*v.i.* **bóana** [from Shipibo *bo–*, *bóti* to go (several) + *–wan* today + *–ti* inf. suf.] : to pass by (many or a mass) ⟨**Nato neténra ícha jóni boánke Máioshiain boí.** Today many people passed by on their way to Pucallpa.⟩
*v.t.* **bóbesa** [from Shipibo *bo–* at the topmost point + *bétsati* to go to the end of] : to climb to the topmost point of

*also* **bonbón** *n.* **bóboman** *also* **bónboman** : a spot anywhere on the body infected with a boil ⟨**Jawen bobónki pirótanin tsákaara nato jonín máxkaxon mái tsákake.** This man fell to the ground unconscious when the ball struck his infected sore.⟩
*v.t.* **bobónhaa** : to cause boils on ⟨**Jimánra nokon báke bobónhake, tékaxon.** The ants stung my little boy and gave him little boils.⟩

*Konibo* **bonbónti** *v.t.* **bóbona** *Konibo* **bónbona** : to break out in boils ⟨**Nokon maponkora ea bobónke, binán tékaa.** Boils broke out on my head because the wasp stung me.⟩ ⟨**Pítsokori piáx bonbónketianra rókotoron báke raónke.** The doctor treated the child who had boils from having eaten matamata.⟩
*v.t.* **bóchaxa** [from Shipibo *bo–* on the roof beams + *cháxati* to hew] : to hew the roof beams of (a house)

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *bo–* on the side of the head + *chi–* inside + *–ki* toward] *adv.* : above ⟨**Abion bóchiki wínotainbira non mérayamake, ishtóira iken.** Even though the airplane was passing overhead, we could not locate it because it was going very fast.⟩ *postp.* : above ⟨**Xóbo bochiki báwa nóyainbira kampán tsákake, mécha ixon.** Even though the parrot was flying high above the house, the Campa shot it with an arrow, for he was a good hunter.⟩ *syn.* manaon
*adj.* **bochón** [from Shipibo *bo-* on the side of the head + *cho*, unidentified] : full : full of ⟨**Nato tasára moa naránxa bócho iki.** This basket is already full of oranges.⟩ *syn.* póto
*v.t.* **bóchoaa** *Konibo* **bóchoaka** : to fill ⟨**Icha péibora en nontín bóchoake.** I filled the canoe with many palm leaves.⟩
*v.i.* **bóchoa** : to become full ⟨**Titan chomoran moa xeati bochoke.** The masato (a fermented drink) filled up in Mother's jar.⟩
*n.* **boén** : boquichico (an edible river fish) ⟨**Rébokira bóe wákanawa iki.** Upriver there is a mijanada (a fish migration) of boquichicos.⟩

*n.* **bóeatin** [from Shipibo *bóe* boquichico + *-a* to make] : huahuasapa (a kind of fishing net) ⟨**En koshóshka cháchiara ea bóeati boónke.** I speared a river dolphin without realizing it, and it carried off my huahuasapa.⟩
*v.i.* **boéxeketa** : to comb one's hair
*n.* **boéxetin** [from Shipibo *boéxti, bokx-* to scratch the hair + *-ti* with which] : comb ⟨**Ríkatonin boéxeti beára kopíora iki.** The combs the trader has brought are very expensive.⟩
*v.t.* **bóexa** [from Shipibo *bo-* on the hair *wéxeti* to scratch] : to comb
*n.* **bóiman** : woodpecker ⟨**Xena píi íitaitianra en boín tsákake.** While the woodpecker was eating grubs, I shot it with an arrow.⟩
[from Shipibo *chóncho* solitary chick, this in turn from Quechua *kwnkw* + Shipibo *boín* woodpecker] : a tiny species of woodpecker of a yellowish-reddish color
[from Shipibo *joshín* reddish + *téo* neck + *-ya* with, having + *boín* woodpecker] : atún carpintero (a species of woodpecker)
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *boín* woodpecker] : a species of small woodpecker, white with black wings
[from Shipibo *méshi* thin + *boín* woodpecker] : a species of small woodpecker, gray, with little flesh, similar to the tuquituqui
*interj.* : well then –Used to begin, e.g., an explanation.
*also* **bófalo** *n.* **bójaronin** *also* **bófalonin** [from Spanish] : buffalo ⟨**Bójaro riki tóro jisá, ikaxbi ánichabires.** The buffalo resembles the bull, but is a bit larger.⟩
*n.* **bokán** : one-armed (person) ⟨**Bokánra pócha píai.** One-armed people eat papaya.⟩
See under **íno**

*v.t.* **bóketa** [from Shipibo *bo-* in the hair + *kékoti* to go leaning] : to interweave (the reeds of a mat) at one end ⟨**En bokékin jankénhaamabira titán kawín bóke.** Although I had not finished interweaving the reeds of the mat at the ends, mother took it away.⟩
*v.t.* **bókexa** [from Shipibo *bo-* + *kexeti* to sew] 1 : to sew at the side of the head of 2 : to sew shut the mouth of (a sack)
*n.* **bokín** [from Spanish *buke* (ship)] : gunboat ⟨**Bóki jóaitainronki non ánibo raképaonike.** When the gunboat came, our ancestors were afraid.⟩
*interj.* : take it away –Used in repeated form. –Little used nowadays.

*n.* **bokón** : small intestine –Used about a chelonian. ⟨**Kabórinin bóko xóiara ochítinin bóteke.** The dog took the roasted intestines of the taricaya (a river turtle) out of the fire and carried them off.⟩
*n.* **bókoman** : cetico (a fast-growing riverside tree) ⟨**Nato simánaninra nokon bokón tapan en Máioshiain bóai.** This week I will take my cetico-wood raft to Pucallpa.⟩
[from Shipibo *yawísh, yáwishin* armadillo + *bokón* cetico] : a species of tree with bark and leaves like those of the cetico
*n.* **boín** : tar : pitch ⟨**Moátianronki ból jóniakana shinón tímanike joni shinankin.** They say that in ancient times the monkey punched a human-shaped figure of tar, thinking it was a person.⟩
*v.t.* **bómana** : to bewitch by means of a curse and throat-clearing ⟨**Yómetso bómanira yobé jóke.** The sorcerer has come to curse the thief.⟩

*n.* **bómanyaton** *Konibo* **bómanyaton** *also* **bómanyanin** [from Shipibo *boman-, bománti* to bewitch + *-ya* with, having] : cursing sorcerer ⟨**Oa chipónkiax joá jónira bománya iki.** That man who has come from downriver is a cursing sorcerer.⟩

*v.t.* **bómaa** [from Shipibo *bo-* root of *bóti* to carry + *-ma* to cause] : to send as an errand or commission : to send with another person ⟨**Kóka Ikítoain káitianra titán jawen téoti bómake.** When my uncle was about to go to Iquitos, my mother sent his necklaces with him so he would sell them.⟩ ⟨**Moa kírika bomá ikáxbira, ishtón jóni jóyamaiki.** Although a letter had been sent to him, the man did not come right away.⟩ ⟨**Néno ika mibé ráenanaibaonra, mia sároro bómakanai.** Your good friends who are here send you greetings.⟩
*n.* **bómatinin** [from Shipibo *bómati, boma-* to send + *-ti* with which] : a parcel sent with someone : a commission/errand
*n.* **bomén** : bombonaje (a palm used for weaving) ⟨**Bóme xama máitiaara kopíora iki.** A hat made from the shoot of the bombonaje palm is very expensive.⟩ *syn.* itsón
*n.* **bompán** : a beetle that eats the shapaja (palm) ⟨**Bómpa mapora ráma téoti ákanai.** Nowadays they make necklaces out of the heads of the *bómpa* beetle.⟩
*n.* **bompón** [from Spanish] : bass drum ⟨**Bakísh píshta íkaitianra yame bómpo íishinai.** They are going to play the bass drum all night, because tomorrow is a fiesta.⟩
*n.* **bonán** : isula (a large stinging ant) ⟨**Westíora yósishokora bonán tékaxon réteke.** A certain little old man died from an isula sting.⟩
*n.* **bonán** : bee; *specif.* : a species of wild bee ⟨**Níi meran bóna bénaitianra jóni oín mecháake.** While the man was looking for bees in the monte (forest), the rain soaked him.⟩
[from Shipibo *báwa* parrot + *jána* tongue + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *be-* eye + *kóro* gray + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *bépo* eye discharge + *bóna* bee] : a tiny species of bee that pesters by coming near the eyes
*also* **bóya** [from Shipibo *bóya* the honeycomb of the *bóyabona* bee + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee whose honeycomb resembles a termite nest
[from Shipibo *íso* spider monkey + *poínki* anus + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *nakáx* termite + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee whose honeycomb resembles a termite nest
[from Shipibo *pítsokori* matamata (a turtle) + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *ke-* mouth, edge + *jóxo* white + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee that is black and reddish in color
[from Shipibo *róo* coto (howler monkey) + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *xáe, xaén* anteater + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *xára* a small species of bee + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *xéki* corn + *kexbón* stripe + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *tepí,* unidentified + *bóna* bee] : a species of bee
[from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear + *sése* speckled + *bona* bee] : a species of bee with a white-speckled abdomen
*n.* **bónajenen** [from Shipibo *bóna* bee + *jéne* water] : honey : bee honey ⟨**Non bónajene íchayora xéaaronki chikíshti iki.** They say that if we drink too much bee honey, we can grow weak.⟩
*n.* **bónamishkiman** [from Shipibo *bóna* bee + *mishkín* cane syrup] : honeycomb

*n.* **bonánchain** [from Shipibo *bóna, bonán* isula (a stinging ant) + *chái* brother-in-law] : a species of ant similar to the isula ⟨**Bonánchainra noa tékayamai.** The *bonánchai* ant does not sting us.⟩

*n.* **bonántinin** [from Shipibo *bo-* on the side of the head + *náneti* cradle] 1 : trunk (chest) ⟨**Bonánti pékatemeáxa báke pakéke.** The child fell off the top of the trunk.⟩ 2 : suitcase : small case ⟨**Jónira jawen bonánti yómetsoakanke.** A man had his case stolen.⟩ *syn.* **maríta**
See under **pópo**
*adj.* **bónayaton** *Konibo* **bónayanin** : gluttonous ⟨**Nato jóni bónayara yóashi iki.** This gluttonous man is stingy.⟩ *syn.* **póto**
*v.i.* **bónbia** : to sway while standing

*n.* **bónchibon** *Konibo* **bónchibaon** *pish.* **bónchibaen** [from Shipibo *bonchi*, unidentified + *-bo*, plural suf.] : the bonchibo ethnolinguistic group : Bonchibo : Bonchibo people ⟨**Moátianra bónchibo sinábo ikátiai.** In ancient times the Bonchibo were very fierce.⟩
See under **písa**

*adj.* **bónchoman** [from Shipibo *bo-* in the hair + *nchon*, unidentified] : with bristling, tousled hair ⟨**Bóexeetama ikax bonchón íketianra, jawen maístoron nato báke kastíkanke.** The teacher punished this boy for having his hair bristly and uncombed.⟩
*v.i.* **bónexeeta** : to tie up one's own head at the side
*v.t.* [from Shipibo *bo-* on the side of the head + *néxati* to tie] 1 : to tie (something) onto the head at the side 2 : to bind the handle of (a knife or machete)

*n.* **bónkaten** *Konibo* **bónkakan** : a species of large palm with a trunk like that of the siamba palm and ash-gray leaves ⟨**Papánra manánxawe bíke káchio kaxón bonkánaman rákata.** While going through the monte (forest), father caught a motelo (tortoise) that was lying under a *bonká* palm.⟩

*v.t.* **bonkéaa** *Konibo* **bonkéaka** : to move the head of (someone) from side to side ⟨**Jóni jenén rétea íketianra en bonkéake joimakaskin.** I moved the drowned man's head from side to side to make him breathe.⟩

*v.i.* **bonkébonkeika** : to move one's own head from side to side several times ⟨**Nato bákera bonkébonkeikai, órokashamai.** This child moves his head from side to side to show that he does not want to cultivate.⟩

*v.t.* **bónketa** : to shake the head from side to side as a sign of (refusal) ⟨**Jawen pátoronin téeti bókasara kakáshamai bonkéke.** When his boss wanted to take him to work, he shook his head from side to side because he did not want to go.⟩
*n.* **bonkón** : virgin or impenetrable forest ⟨**Tée méekinra en bónko wáiake.** With hard work I made a garden plot in the virgin forest.⟩

*v.t.* **bónkoaa** *Konibo* **bónkoaka** 1 : to form a thicket ⟨**Xóbibo óroxonra en jaínbicho tsamánxon bónkoake.** When I cleared the weeds, I piled them up in one place, forming a thicket.⟩ 2 : to form a heap of similar things ⟨**Yámikenti ícha mároxonra en bónkoake.** Since I bought many aluminum pots, I piled them up.⟩

*v.i.* **bónkoa** 1 : for impenetrable forest to form ⟨**Nokon wáira moa jákiribi bónkoa iki, en óroyamaa.** My garden plot has turned back into forest because I have not cultivated it.⟩ 2 : for a cluster of things to form up high ⟨**Binón bimira ícha bónkoke.** The fruit of the aguaje (moriche palm) forms up high, in clusters of many fruits.⟩ 3 : for similar things to pile up ⟨**Káchiora isán bimi bónkoa en mérake.** In the monte (forest) I saw some ungurahui (palm) fruits piled up.⟩

*n.* **bónshishin** 1 : copaibo (the copaiba tree) 2 : a species of demon identified with the copaiba tree ⟨**Bonshíshonki nenkéyosi jóni iki.** They say that the demon of the copaiba tree is a very tall man.⟩
*n.* **bónsiman** : a species of small otter ⟨**Bonsín riki ochíti keska, ikáxbi yobé.** The otter is very much like a dog, but it is a bewitched animal.⟩

*n.* **bóntoishin** *also* **bóntoishnin** [from Shipibo *bóntoish*, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird ⟨**Titán bóntoish ináara xoyán píanaanke.** A mouse ate the little *bóntoish* bird that mother was raising.⟩

*n.* **bónxaman** : lung ⟨**Non bónxaman shinánronki béroyoshiman náikan bóai.** They say that when we die, the spirit of the pupil of the eye carries our thoughts, which reside in our lungs, up to the sky.⟩
*n.* **bóokan** : hair : hair of the head ⟨**Ea bóokan yatánkebira en jénemake.** He grabbed me by the hair, but I made him let go.⟩
[from Shipibo *wápawapa* *wapapa* (a bird) + *bóo* hair] : the fine, broad, black feathers characteristic of the huapapa
[from Shipibo *manxán* heron + *bóo* hair] : the fine, long feathers characteristic of the white heron
*n.* **bóokan** : a healed place on the skin ⟨**Nato aínbora jawen rérakaata bóo ikáinbi ronón natéxke.** The snake bit this woman on the spot where a cut she had had healed.⟩
*v.i.* **bóota** : to heal (of a wound or boil) ⟨**Chóchawashanronki ishtón xáteta bóoti iki.** They say that with chuchuhuasi (a medicinal plant) cuts heal quickly.⟩
See under **wáste**
*adj.* **bóoxen** [from Shipibo *bo-* hair + *jóxo* whitish] : gray-haired
*n.* **borón** [from Spanish] : donkey

*n.* **bórokan** [from Shipibo *bo-* in the stump + *ro*, unidentified] : rootstock (stump) ⟨**Ráma nétera non boró tsékakanai, bakísha non óroibake.** Today we are pulling up the rootstocks that we planted yesterday.⟩

*n.* **bóroman** [from Shipibo *bo-*, unidentified + *róno* snake] : a species of aquatic jergón (fer-de-lance viper) ⟨**Weán shítaitianra bóroman áke.** When he was crossing the stream on foot, an aquatic *borón* jergón bit him.⟩
*also* **brónse** *n.* **borónsinin** *also* **brónsenin** : bronze

*n.* **bórosan** *also* **bórosanin** [from Spanish] : bag ⟨**Nokon bórosara ea Máioshiainxon yómetsoakanke.** They stole my bag in Pucallpa.⟩ *syn.* BOROSA, PISHA both can be translated as "bag"; but BOROSA has a general reference, whereas PISHA refers mainly to the small typical bag woven from cotton by the Shipibo.

*v.i.* **bóroxa** [from Shipibo *bo-* at the top + *rox*, unidentified + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : for only (the heads or upper part of several things) to show ⟨**Sísion ákaibora en winókin óina bóroxa iki.** As I passed by there, I saw that only the heads of those who were in the meeting were showing.⟩
*n.* **bosán** : raccoon : chosna (a kinkajou) ⟨**Káchiokeara epán bósa bake beíbake.** Yesterday my uncle brought a baby chosna from the monte (forest).⟩ *syn.* mapáchi
*n.* **bóshikan** : penis ⟨**Jonín boshí ikáronkiki nato tsismán.** They say that the puñuisiqui fish emerged from a man's penis.⟩ *syn.* jína
See under **bína**
*n.* [from Shipibo *boshí*, *bóshikan* penis] : unknown man –Used as a vocative form.
*n. and adj.* **boshtín** [from Shipibo *bo-* in the hair + *shtin,* unidentified] *n.* : pubic hair *adj.* : kinky (hair) ⟨**Nato rashíko jonira bóshti iki.** This Brazilian has kinky hair.⟩
*v.t.* **bóshtiaa** *Konibo* **bóshtiaka** : to curl the hair of ⟨**Náwa ainbaonra nokon báke bóshtiake.** A mestizo woman curled my daughter's hair.⟩
*v.i.* **bóshtia** : to curl one's hair ⟨**Rímameax bóshtia riki nato aínbo.** This woman curled her hair in Lima.⟩
*v.t.* **botésa** [from Shipibo *bo-* of the head + *téseti* to pull out] 1 : to forcefully pull the hair out of the head of 2 : to tear off the top part of (a plant)

*v.t.* **bótea** : to take off the flame or fire ⟨**Titán póa joara moa wáaketian bóteke.** Mom took the boiled sachapapa (an edible tuber) off the fire because it was already done.⟩ ⟨**Nato yámikentí botéara kochín weránke.** The pig shoved the metal pot that had been taken off the fire.⟩
*v.t.* **boá** : to carry, to take ⟨**Kókara jawen pátoronin téeti bóke Tamáyanin.** My uncle was taken by his boss to work on the Tamaya river.⟩
See under **káti**
*n.* **bótikanin** [from Spanish] : pharmacy ⟨**Bótikainra ráo icha jáke.** There are many medicines in the pharmacy.⟩
*n.* **botírian** [from Spanish] : bottle ⟨**Táshira non botíria meran bénxoai.** We store salt in bottles.⟩
*n.* **bótoman** : a kind of edible snail; *specif.* : concompe ⟨**Non botón píketianronki non báke chíxotai.** They say that if we eat concompes, our children may get diarrhea.⟩
[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *botón* concompe] : a kind of small orange snail

*also* **botón** *n.* **botónisnin** *also* **bótoman** [from Spanish *botones* or *botón*] : manufactured button ⟨**Botónis xéaketianra, rókotoron báke tsékaxonke.** When the boy swallowed the button, the doctor took it out.⟩
*v.i.* **bóxoxa** [from Shipibo *bo-* in the stump + *xóxoti* to sprout] : to sprout again from the stump of a tree
*v.t.* **bóxtea** [from Shipibo *bo-* on the side of the head + *xáteti* to cut] 1 : to cut on the head 2 : to decapitate 3 : to cut off the top of *syn.* téxteti

*n.* **boyán** 1 : a hive built by the *bóyabona* bee and resembling a termite nest ⟨**Non bóya méeketianronki báke kópia bépoai.** They say that if we touch a *bóya* hive, our children become cutipados (afflicted by supernatural harm) and begin to secrete a lot of eye discharge.⟩ 2 : the *bóyabona* bee
See under **bóna**

*v.i.* **bóyakaata** 1 : to get trapped in something very sticky ⟨**Manón bóyakaataxa báke jokáskimake.** Getting stuck in the mud, the child could not get out despite his efforts.⟩ 2 : to close up by itself (something very sticky)

*v.t.* **bóyaa** 1 : to caulk with pitch ⟨**Papán jawen nónti bóyaara moa jéne béyamai.** Since dad caulked his canoe, no water gets in.⟩ 2 : to patch ⟨**Moa bóyakana ikénbira papán nonti bóyakanke.** Dad's canoe had been patched, but they took it away.⟩ 3 : to fill (a tooth) ⟨**Nokon xéta péketaton ea chéxayoraitianra, en rókotoro bóyamake.** The dentist filled my decayed tooth that hurt me so much.⟩ ⟨**Nato bonánti tíayamakanwe; moa boyá ríki.** Don't touch this trunk, because it has been patched.⟩
See **borónsi**
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *ch* in the Shipibo alphabet. See **Grammar Sketch 2.1**

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *chápata* fork, crotch, confluence] : in both legs ⟨**chánto** without the use of both legs⟩ –**cha** *also* –**chaa** *modifying suf.* –**chaakan** *also* –**chaaton** *also* –**chaatonin** *Konibo* –**chaanin** : a little or somewhat more ⟨**Ochóchaa káxa nokóke.** Going a little farther, he arrived.⟩ –Used added to an adjective with the meaning of "more" of the comparative degree. ⟨**¿Jáweratoki nénkecha iki, papán nónti o epána?** Which is longer, papa's canoe or uncle's?⟩ *syn.* ashón

*n.* **cháakan** [from Shipibo *cháa*, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird, black in color and smaller than the locrero ⟨**Yamé cháa kéotaronki róati íkai.** They say that when the little *cháa* bird sings at night, it is a sign of bad omen.⟩
See under **íno**
*also* **yábi** *also* **yabínti** *n.* **chabín** *also* **yabín** *also* **yabíntinin** [from Spanish] : key ⟨**Chabínra papán xepóti kepénke.** The father opened the door with the key.⟩
*v.i.* **chacháa** *Konibo* **chacháaka** : to paint with tiny dots ⟨**Titánra papán bémanain maxén chacháake.** Mama painted papa's face with little dots of achiote (a red dye plant).⟩
*v.i.* **cháchata** : to paint oneself with tiny dots ⟨**Non axé riqui báke mawáketian nanén chacháti. It is our custom to paint ourselves with little dots of huito (a dye fruit) when a child dies.⟩

*n.* **cháchikan** 1 : sting, bite ⟨**Jawen chachí isín íketianra pápa jóyamai.** Papa cannot come because his sting hurts him.⟩ 2 : injection ⟨**Rámara mia rabé chachíres maxkáke —akinra ea rókotoron áke.** The doctor told me that now I only have two injections left.⟩ *syn.* cháchiti

*n.* **cháchimisin** [from *Shipibo* *cháchiti,* *chachi–* to sting + *-mis* that always does] : one that pricks (e.g., with a spine) ⟨**Tonón, íspiara cháchimis iki.** The bagre (a catfish) is a fish that pricks because it has spines.⟩

*v.t.* **cháchia** 1 : to prick, to sting (e.g., with a beak or a sharp instrument) ⟨**Atapa benekira ea ráketai, ea chachinaketian.** I am afraid the rooster is going to peck me.⟩ ⟨**En kapé cháchiara chikáro bóke.** When I speared the caiman, it carried off my harpoon.⟩ 2 : to give an injection ⟨**Yoná jéneyamaitianra sánitarion cháchike.** The health worker gave him an injection because the fever would not leave him.⟩

*n.* **cháchitinin** [from *Shipibo* *cháchiti,* *chachi–* to sting + *-ti* with which] 1 : hypodermic syringe ⟨**Moa kopíora ikénbira ea cháchitinin mároke.** I bought a syringe even though it was very expensive.⟩ 2 : injection ⟨**Nokon bákera cháchitiki ráketai, moa íchaakin ákana ikax.** My son is afraid of injections, because they have been given to him many times.⟩ *syn.* chachí

*v.i.* **cháchita** 1 : to prick or sting oneself with an instrument ⟨**Xomóx méeresira mekénhain chachíke.** Playing with the needle, she pricked herself on the hand.⟩ 2 : to get or receive an injection ⟨**Ráomeeti xobónxonra ea chachíwanke.** They gave me an injection at the clinic.⟩ 3 : to feel a stabbing pain in the stomach or the sides ⟨**Piróta akí cháchitaxa** ea pikóke. While playing soccer, I felt a stabbing pain and left the game.⟩

*n.* **chaín** [from *Shipibo* *cha–* on both legs + *i,* unidentified] : a man's brother-in-law ⟨**Jawen chaínra ribínxonbi kopíayamai.** His brother-in-law does not pay him, even though he owes him.⟩

*n.* **cháikonin** [from *Shipibo* *chái* brother-in-law + *kóni* eel] : a species of forest spirit ⟨**Noa cháikonin yótoaronki jími kínani noa máwatai.** They say that when the forest spirit *cháikoni* bewitches us, we can die from vomiting blood.⟩

*v.t.* **chaíshaka** [from *Shipibo* *chash,* imitative of a sharp sound + *-iti,* to make/do] : to break (a dry branch) noisily ⟨**Jíwi chaíshakin ráteara nato báke winike.** This child got scared and cried when a dry branch of the tree broke.⟩
*v.i.* **chaíshika** : to break (a dry branch) noisily ⟨**Jíwi ponyan páketira chaíshirike.** The branch broke and made a sudden sound.⟩

*adj. and n.* **chákaten** *Konibo* **chákakan** *adj.* 1 : crushed, mashed ⟨**Nato bákera paránta chaká píkasai.** This child wants to eat mashed plantain.⟩ 2 : split, cracked open ⟨**Paranta satanaxa chakatai.** When the plantain swells, it splits.⟩ 3 : cracked ⟨**Mái chaká ikain jámataxa jóni taskéke.** When stepping on the cracked ground, the man dislocated his foot.⟩ *n.* : crack : crevice ⟨**Bákera meskéke mái chaká meran káax.** The child broke his hand when he fell into the crevice in the ground.⟩ *syn.* chopé; waxá
*v.t.* **chakásh aka** : to beat noisily against (of waves) ⟨**Chakásh akinra noa béchoman réoke.** When the waves beat against our boat, we capsized.⟩
*v.i.* **chakásh ika** : to beat noisily (of waves) ⟨**Nóntiki bechón chakásh ikinra báke jéne xéamake.** When the waves beat against the canoe, water got into the child's mouth.⟩

*v.t.* **chákaa** 1 : to crush, to mash ⟨**Kárapintironinra jawen mekén chákake.** The carpenter smashed his hand.⟩ 2 : to hammer ⟨**Nokon pápashokonra yámi chákaxon chikároai.** My grandfather makes a harpoon by hammering a piece of iron.⟩

*v.i.* **chákata** 1 : to get crushed (e.g., a finger) ⟨**Nokon pápanra jawen *metoti* maratíchon chakáke.** My papa smashed his finger with a hammer.⟩ 2 : to split ⟨**Non paránta chákataronki aínbo bakeati iki.** They say that when the plantain splits for some reason, it means we will have a daughter.⟩ 3 : to crack ⟨**Báriaitianra mái chákatai.** In the dry season, the ground cracks.⟩

*n.* **chakín** : a kind of small toad ⟨**Oi benónronki cháki kéotai.** They say that when it is about to rain, the little *cháki* toad sings.⟩ –Used in the vocative form *chakí* to call children. ⟨**Néri joé, chakí.** Come here, little boy.⟩
*n.* **chákipatan** : a kind of tree not yet identified
*v.i.* **chakóika** : to chew noisily ⟨**Miara kóchi keskayora, píi chakóikai.** You eat like pigs, chewing noisily.⟩

*n. voc.* [from *Shipibo* *cha–* on both legs + *ma,* unidentified] 1 : companion –Used as a form of address among boys. ⟨**Jaínra xánbo kai chamá —íkira ikánke bákebo já bénai.** Looking for lagarscissors, the children would say —There goes one, friend!⟩ 2 : scoundrel –Used as a form of address among men. ⟨**Néri jowé chamá noa wéxaananon —ikira jóni íkai.** The man says to his enemy —Come fight, scoundrel.⟩
*n.* **chamín** 1 : smallpox 2 : a kind of demon identified with smallpox ⟨**Chámironkiki wirákocha jisá.** They say the smallpox demon looks like a white man.⟩ *syn.* kítamoro
*n.* : a kind of vine from the monte (the wild forest) *which produces boils and also serves as a remedy for boils*
*n.* **champón** : cricket ⟨**En poróto bánaabira ea champón kéyonaanke.** The crickets destroyed the beans I planted.⟩
[from Shipibo *potó* pot-bellied + *chámpo* cricket] : a kind of cricket three or four centimeters long
[from Shipibo *shirí* imitative of its call + *chámpo* cricket] : a kind of greenish cricket that is the largest of all the species
*n.* **chanán** : a kind of small paucar (a cacique bird) ⟨**Binán kómparonki chána iki.** They say the wasp's compadre is the little paucar.⟩
See under **bína**
See under **yápa**
See under **yáwa**
*v.t.* **chánia** : to invite ⟨**Nokon pápara chánikanabi xéai káyamake.** My dad did not go to drink, even though they had invited him.⟩
*v.i.* **chánita** : to be invited ⟨**Nonra xéatiapariai; jákopira chánitain noa káyamai.** We are going to keep preparing the drink, and that is why we are not yet going to where we are invited.⟩

*adj.* **chankán** [from Shipibo *chankáti, chanka-* to stand up] : protruding ⟨**Moátianronki iká iki westíora mápijoni, jawen béro chánka.** They tell that in ancient times there was a shrimp-man who had protruding eyes.⟩
*v.t.* **chánkana** : to make stand : to set upright ⟨**Jaín chankánwe.** Stand it up there.⟩

*v.t.* **chánkata** [from Shipibo *cha-* on both legs + *nka*, unidentified element + *-ti* inf. suf.] 1 : to stand on both legs ⟨**Niósma ikáxbira nato báke chankáke.** Although he did not know how to walk, this child stood up⟩ 2 : to stand up (e.g., hair or feathers) ⟨**Nato aínbora bóexeetama iki; jawen bóora chánkata iki.** This woman is not combed; her hair is standing up⟩ 3 : to go visiting ⟨**Noa chánkati kakénbira noa kénakana jóke.** We had gone visiting but came back, because our family called us.⟩

*v.i.* **chánketa** [from Shipibo *cha-* on both legs + *nket*, unidentified element + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to walk on tiptoe ⟨**Nato bákera xáo jámatax chánketai.** This child walks on tiptoe because he stepped on a thorn.⟩

*n.* **chankón** 1 : protuberances on the body ⟨**Chánkoya ikáx cháchitara moa keyóke.** The protuberances on his body have disappeared thanks to the injection he was given.⟩ 2 : cuchipe (a skin disease) : pián (yaws) ⟨**Non átsapoto pímaaronki átapa chánkoai.** They say that when a hen eats fariña (manioc meal), the cuchipe attacks it.⟩

*v.i.* **chankóa** 1 : for protuberances to appear on the body ⟨**Nokon títashokora chánkoax mawáke.** My granny died when protuberances appeared on her body.⟩ 2 : to catch cuchipe (a skin disease) ⟨**Nokon átapabora moa chánkoke.** My hens have caught cuchipe.⟩

*n.* **chánkoxawen** [from Shipibo *chánko* protuberances on the body + *xáwe* charapa (a river turtle)] : matamata (a river turtle) –Used as a euphemistic name to avoid the proper name. ⟨**Non chánkoxawe osánketianronki noa nonbémai.** They say that if we laugh at the matamata, boils resembling its protuberances may break out on us.⟩ *syn.* CHANKOXAWE and PITSOKORI denote the matamata, but while PITSOKORI, with its variant form KOPITSORI, is the normal and proper word, CHANKOXAWE is used as an alternative to avoid the direct name.
*n.* **chantán** [from Spanish] : tire ⟨**Nato bísikirita chántara en otsíaama iki; nato jonínra áke.** I did not deflate the tire of this bicycle; this man did it.⟩ *syn.* See under **károtae**
*n.* **chantín** [from Spanish] : plantain (the llantén weed)

*n.* **chantón** [from Shipibo *cha-* on both legs + *-nto* without] : lame : lacking the normal use of the legs ⟨**Jatíbi jawen yóra jakón ikáxbira chántores iki.** He is in good health, in spite of being lame.⟩ *syn.* nítikoma

*v.t.* **chántoaa** *Konibo* **chántoaka** 1 : to make lame ⟨**Nato bákera jawen titán chántoake sináxon.** That boy was made lame by his mother in a moment of anger.⟩ 2 : to make limp ⟨**Jonínra jawen báke chántoake sontáro kámakaxamakin.** A man made his son limp so that he would not go into the army.⟩

*n.* **chantómarin** : a spring that forms at the edge of a caño (a small channel) when the river drops ⟨**Chantómari jeneronki xéatima iki.** They say the water of the *chantómari* spring is not potable.⟩
*v.i.* **chántoa** : to become lame ⟨**Kimisha óxe ísinaxa nokon báke chántoke.** My little son became lame because he was ill for three months.⟩
*n.* **cháopinin** : a kind of vine used to make a poultice

*v.t.* **chapáa** *Konibo* **chapáaka** 1 : to make fork 2 : to divide : to split : to cut ⟨**Nokon táera en chapáake rérakin, jíwi ati shinánkin.** When I meant to cut the tree, I accidentally cut my foot.⟩ *syn.* káxketi

*n.* **chápatanin** 1 : the crease between the fingers or toes ⟨**Nokon mekén chapatainkora ea bonán tékake.** A isula (bullet ant) stung me in a crease between my fingers.⟩ 2 : the fork of trees ⟨**Jíwi chapatainoara papán róo tóoake.** Dad shot the coto (howler monkey) that was sitting in the fork.⟩ 3 : confluence –Used of rivers and streams. ⟨**Nato páro chapatainkora motóro réokooke.** The motor (motorboat) capsized upstream at the confluence of this river.⟩

*v.i.* **chápata** : to fork (e.g., a road) ⟨**Nato párora sénenainbi chapáke.** The Ucayali River forks at its end (that is, at the confluence of the Tambo and Urubamba rivers).⟩ ⟨**Nato bái káara moa sénenain chapáke.** The road ahead forks at the end.⟩

*v.t.* **charáa** *Konibo* **charáaka** : to melt : to soften with heat ⟨**Jawen titán asókaro charáakatoninra nato báke menóke.** This child got burned by the sugar his mother had melted.⟩ ⟨**Sémpara en charáakai nónti bóyanoxon.** I am melting copal (a tree resin) to caulk the canoe.⟩ ⟨**En ípo bachi biábira barín charáake.** The carachama (armored catfish) eggs I got melted in the sun.⟩

*v.i.* **cháraika** : to rattle/resonate (a set or group of long, non-metallic things) ⟨**En táwa nea pótaara chárairike.** The group of tied cañabravas (wild cane) that I threw down rattled as they fell to the ground⟩
*n.* **charánwanin** : achacubo (a fruit) ⟨**Epán charánwa beá pikáshamaira báke wíniai.** The child cries because he does not want to eat the achacubo his uncle has brought.⟩
*v.t.* **cháraaka** : to shake (a set of non-metallic things, e.g., arrows, isanas (reed stalks) or cañabravas (wild cane)) ⟨**Papánra jawen píabo chára akai.** Dad is shaking his arrows.⟩

*v.i.* **chárata** 1 : to melt ⟨**Barín akára nokon téri charáke, en bénxoayamaa.** I did not put away the *téri* pitch, and it melted from the heat of the sun.⟩ 2 : to melt down ⟨**Titán átsa jóaara jéne kéyotax yámikenti charáke.** The water of the manioc mom was cooking dried up and the aluminum pot melted down.⟩

*n.* **cháráxen** : catalán (a bird) ⟨**Charáx báke riki kikín xoáxoko.** The katalán's chick is very plump.⟩ ⟨**Charáx joninronki aínbo awínanike.** They tell that once a katalán-man married a woman.⟩
*n.* **charín** : shamiro (a bird) ⟨**Papán xéki bánaara charín kéyoai.** The shamiros devour the corn dad planted.⟩
See under **móxa**
*adj.* **chárishin** : stiff : hardened : rigid

*v.t.* **charíshaa** *Konibo* **charíshaka** : to make stiff, rigid, or hard ⟨**Moátianronki westíora yósishokoki matsín charíshaa nókokanike.** They tell that in ancient times they came by chance upon a little old man stiffened by the cold.⟩

*v.i.* **chárisha** [from Shipibo *cha-* on both legs + *rish*, element of *chorish* hard + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to stiffen : to become rigid (e.g., a corpse) ⟨**Aínbo máwatara moa charíshke, rabé néte ikax.** The dead woman's body stiffened because two days had passed since she died.⟩

*n.* **charón** : baby turtles in large numbers ⟨**Moa kabórinin cháro jokonaitianronki jóo kéotai.** They say that when the taricaya (a river turtle) hatchlings come out of the eggs, the gualos (a kind of toad) sing.⟩

*v.t.* **chárona** 1 : to line up (e.g., several people in formation) ⟨**Wáiroronra jato yatánxon charónke jato katónoxon.** The guard recruited them and lined them up to select them for the army.⟩ 2 : to set things upright ⟨**Papán rábo cháronara yómetsonín jamáke.** The thief stepped on the upright nails dad had set.⟩
*v.i.* **chárota** : to be standing (people) ⟨**Jatíbi jónira kampón charóke tsínikanai óini.** All the people are standing in the field watching the players.⟩

*n.* **cháshikan** : a small broken branch ⟨**Noa bénotaxbira noa jóke chashí méraaxes.** We had gotten lost in the monte (the forest), but came back only because we found the little broken branches marking the trail.⟩
*v.t.* **cháshia** : to break (small branches) ⟨**Machítooma ixonra en cháshireske.** I had no machete; I just broke off a few little branches.⟩
*v.i.* **cháshita** : for a small branch to break ⟨**En tíiakamabíra janbíx chashíke.** Without my touching it, it broke.⟩
*n.* **chatín** : a species of leche-caspi (a latex-bearing tree)

*n.* **chawán** : a species of forest vine used by shamans and by those who want to become better hunters ⟨**Chikísh ixonronki cháwa xéati iki.** They say that when someone is lazy, he should drink the juice of the *cháwa* vine.⟩

*n.* **cháwakan** : mud : mire ⟨**Jóni paenará cháwakan tárameeke.** The drunk man wallowed in the mud.⟩ *syn.* CHAWA, MANO both can be translated as "mud" or "mire", but MANO specifically means the black mud or mire found at the edge of a river.
*v.i.* **cháwata** : to become muddy ⟨**Oi bekénra moa bái chawáke.** The path became muddy from the rain.⟩
*v.t.* **cháxaa** : to hew with an axe or machete ⟨**Nokon chaín wíntianoxon jíwi cháxaara jóni yómetsoke.** A man stole the timber my brother-in-law had hewn to make a paddle.⟩

*n.* **chaxón** 1 : deer ⟨**Manánxawenronki cháxo piní rétemanike.** They tell that the motelos (tortoises) killed a deer by wearing it out.⟩ 2 : the constellation called "The Deer," located in the Milky Way –Used in this sense spelled with a capital initial letter *C*.
[from Shipibo *kóro* gray + *cháxo* deer] : a species of small ash-colored deer

*n.* **cháxobichin** [from Shipibo *cháxo* deer + *bíchi* hide] : a strip of deer hide used to fasten the warp to the loom ⟨**Titán cháxobichi chínexetira ochítinin bóke.** The dog carried off the deer-hide strap mom had tied on.⟩
See under **íno**

*n.* [from Shipibo *cháxo* deer + *íno, inón* jaguar + *chibáni,* verbal complement of *chibáni* to follow] : the constellation called "The Jaguar," which appears behind the constellation "The Deer" and is formed of dark patches in the Milky Way
See under **kóma**
See under **mawís**
See under **móxa**

*n.* **cháxoxen** : a species of red tadpole found in the streams ⟨**Moátianronki káochonin téekin chaxóx pikátikanai.** They say that back when people worked the rubber trade, they used to eat *chaxóx* tadpoles.⟩

*v.t.* **cheáa** *Konibo* **cheáaka** : to make posheco (sickly-pale) : to make anemic ⟨**Icha néte náshimayamakinra aínbaon jawen báke cheáake.** A mother made her child anemic by not bathing him for many days.⟩
*v.i.* **chéata** : to become posheco (sickly-pale) : to become anemic ⟨**Mapó píai ikax chéata riki.** He became posheco from the habit of eating clay.⟩
*interj.* –Used repeated, meaning "come here," to call a dog.
*n.* **chéikan** [from Shipibo *cheí,* imitative of its call] : a species of parakeet ⟨**Titán cheí ináara tétekan bóke.** The hawk carried off the *cheí* parakeet that mom had raised.⟩
*v.t.* **chékerena** : to tickle ⟨**Jawen wétsa chékerenara wínike.** He cried because his brother tickled him.⟩
*adj.* **chekón** 1 : smelling of urine ⟨**Nato bákera chéko póatai.** This child smells of urine.⟩ 2 : smelling of stale or musty water 3 : having the taste of stored water
