*v.t.* **chékoaa** *Konibo* **chékoaka** : to make smell of urine ⟨**Nokon kotónra ochítinin chékoake, jáki jisónxon.** A dog made my shirt smell of urine because it urinated on it.⟩

*v.i.* **chékoa** 1 : to smell of urine 2 : to have a stale taste or smell ⟨**Chómomea ompáxa moa chékoa iki, moa rabé simána ikax.** The water in the jug has a stale smell because it has been there for two weeks already.⟩
*n.* **chéokan** : a species of small llavarachi (frog) : chiuchiu ⟨**Jénetianra cheó kéotai jawen báchi potai.** During the flood season the chiuchiu frogs call out when they release their eggs.⟩

*Konibo* **cheónkicheonkiiti** *v.i.* **cheón ika** *Konibo* **cheónkicheonkiika** : to chirp, to cheep ⟨**Jawen títa máxokan réteketianra átapa bakeshokobo cheónkicheonkiikai.** The chicks cheep because the fox killed their mother.⟩
See under **níshi**
*n.* **chepán** : a species of small horsefly ⟨**Non ménoketianronki chépa káitai.** They say that when horseflies are burned, they multiply.⟩
[from Shipibo *awá* tapir + *chépa* a species of small horsefly] : a species of large horsefly
[from Shipibo *joshín* reddish + *chépa* a species of horsefly] : a species of horsefly of a reddish-yellowish color

*n.* **chepán ewan** [from Shipibo *chépa, chepán* + *-ewa,* augmentative] : a species of horsefly resembling the cicada ⟨**Pástonapon óxaketianra chepánewan wáka píke.** While the cattle slept in the middle of the pasture, the horsefly fed by biting them.⟩

*v.i.* **chéreta** : to render fat from meat while roasting ⟨**Titán jonokishi xóia xéni chéretaira papán átsapotoya méskoxon píke.** Dad mixed the fat rendered from the sajino (collared peccary) leg mom roasted with fariña and ate it.⟩ ⟨**Wáme nami xóia chéretaira ochítinin táxoke.** The dog licked up the fat that rendered from the roasted paiche meat.⟩
*n.* **chéxakan** [from Shipibo *chéxati, chéxá-* to hurt] : pain ⟨**Jawen chéxá ráora jahúanke.** There was medicine for the pain.⟩
*v.t.* **chéxaa** : to hurt, to ache (transitive) ⟨**Ea shetán chéxaketianra, en rókotoro tsékamake.** The dentist pulled my tooth when it hurt.⟩
: to have labor pains ⟨**Néte xábataitianra bakén chéxakin péoanke.** Today at dawn she began to have labor pains.⟩
*adj.* **chéxén** : black : vivid colors ⟨**Ea nanén síkitabira chéxematani iki.** Even though I painted my face with huito, it is not very black.⟩ *syn.* níkoro
*v.t.* **chéxeaa** *Konibo* **chéxeaka** : to turn black, or a vivid color ⟨**Titánra ompáx chéxeake náneya méskoxon.** Mom blackened the water by putting huito in it.⟩
See under **ínka**
See under **ísko**
*v.i.* **chéxea** : to turn black, or a vivid color ⟨**Nanén síkitara nato aínbaon bémanan chéxea iki.** This woman's face turned black because she painted it with huito.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *chíxo* buttock] 1 : on the buttocks : of the buttocks : by the buttocks ⟨**chinéxti** to tie by the buttocks⟩ 2 : on the anus : of the anus ⟨**chixén** small worms in the anus⟩ 3 : on or of the female genitals 4 : on the rear parts or of the rear parts ⟨**chixéti** to sniff at the rear parts⟩ 5 : backward ⟨**chitíti** to back up⟩ 6 : on the tail or of a bird's tail ⟨**chínto** tailless⟩ 7 : on the eaves of a house ⟨**chikóshkinti** half a cañabrava (cane) placed crosswise on the eaves⟩ 8 : in the stern ⟨**chíakati** to sit in the stern⟩ 9 : on the seat or of the seat of a pair of trousers ⟨**chikéxti** to sew (trousers) at the seat⟩ 10 : on the base of a pot ⟨**chikósh** with a strong base⟩ 11 : on the tip or of the tip of an arrow ⟨**chimápo** a species of four-pointed arrow⟩ 12 : on the handle : of the handle –Usually used of the larger of two handles. ⟨**chixteti** to cut at the handle⟩
*v.t.* **chíaa** : to hang (a mosquito net) ⟨**En báchi chíaketianra bii wéike.** When I hung the mosquito net, the mosquitoes got in.⟩

*Konibo* **chiáréxti** *n.* **chíaraxtin** *Konibo* **chiáréxtin** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the buttocks + *aráxti* with which to press] : trousers ⟨**Westíora chíaraxti kopira jawen pátoronin rabé konxán xate bichínke.** For the price of a pair of trousers his boss charged him two logs of cedar.⟩

*n.* **chíatinin** 1 : knife for weaving ribbons ⟨**Rámatian bákeranonbora chíati ati onánkashamakanai.** Young people today do not want to learn to make the *chíati* knife.⟩ 2 : medium-sized stick that forms part of the loom ⟨**Titán chíatira bakén bóke.** The boy took my mother's beater (weaving stick).⟩
*v.i.* **chíata** : to be (a mosquito net) hung or stretched taut ⟨**Báchi chíatatonra tsóabi yámake.** There is no one in the mosquito net that is hung taut.⟩
*adj.* **chíaxkanin** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the tail + *axka*, unidentified] : forked-tailed
*n. voc.* : girl -Used as a word to call someone. *syn.* chimín; shónta

*v.t.* **chíbana** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *ban*, unidentified + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to follow ⟨**Nokon waránka sóro boónketianra en chibánxon bichínke.** When he stole my thousand soles, I followed him and took it back.⟩ *syn.* káchibanti
*n.* **chíberonin** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *béro* seed] : small pimples on the buttock or rear part

*v.t.* **chíbita** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the stern + *bi*, unidentified + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to steer (a boat) : to handle (a craft) from the stern ⟨**Moa néno bási ixónbira nato lamístonin chibíti onányamake.** This person from Lamas does not know how to steer even though he has been here a long time.⟩
*v.t.* **chíbita** [from Shipibo *chi-* from the buttocks + *bíti* to take] 1 : to take from someone else's buttock 2 : to take from the stern of *syn.* chiwínti
*n.* **chibón** [from Spanish] : goat ⟨**Chíbo itsanronki báke kópiai.** They say the smell of a goat cutipa (causes sympathetic illness) in a baby.⟩
*n.* **chíbokan** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the eaves + *bo*, unidentified] : large eaves of a roof ⟨**Shóbo chibó namanra béwai íkanai.** They are singing under the large eaves of the house.⟩
*n.* **chíboman** [from *chi-* on the buttock + *bon*, element of *bobón* boil] : a boil on the buttock ⟨**Nokon chibónra isín iki.** The boil I have on my buttock hurts.⟩

*n.* **chichín** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the vulva + *chi-* on the vulva] 1 : maternal grandmother ⟨**Non chichínra noa jatíbi áti yóiai.** Our maternal grandmother gives the orders.⟩ 2 : supreme authority –Used with this sense mostly among the Conibo. ⟨**Nato yantán sísion átira jatón chichín jato kénai.** The supreme authority calls them to a session tonight.⟩
*n.* **chíchikan** *Konibo* **chíchikanin** : knife ⟨**Bákebaonra pápashokon chíchika pótanike.** The boys threw away grandfather's knife.⟩

*v.t.* **chíchina** [from Shipibo *chi-* buttock, stern + *-chi* buttock, stern + *-n* derivational suf. verbal + *–ti* inf. suf.] 1 : to turn the buttock in another direction 2 : to turn the stern in another direction

*n.* **chichínwitáxen** [from Shipibo *chíchi, chichín* maternal grandmother + *witáx* leg] : shiripira (a fish species) ⟨**Parónra chichínwitáx wákanawa bóai.** A mijanada (mass migration) of shiripira fish is going down the river.⟩

*n.* **chichíporon** [from Shipibo *chichíporo*, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird, bald, ash-colored, and similar to the arrocero (rice bird) ⟨**Chichíporon axé riki xobónkobo bákeati.** The *chichíporo* bird has the habit of nesting in houses.⟩
*v.i.* **chíchia** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the stern + *chi–* on the stern + *–ti* inf. suf.] : to put the stern into view
See **chípiyoxan**
*adj.* **chichón** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the buttocks + *cho*, unidentified element] : having boils on the buttock

*n.* **chíchokan** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the back parts + *cho*, unidentified element] : the interior ⟨**Bémakayanra jakónira iki nato chómo; jawen chichóra jakóma iki.** This jar looks very pretty on the outside, but its interior is ugly.⟩ *syn.* nápo

*postp. and adv.* *postp.* : deep inside of ⟨**Pishtákobaon rétenaketianra nokon pápa xóbo chichó jonéke.** My father hid deep inside the house so the pishtacos would not kill him.⟩ ⟨**Jéne chichó káketianra westíora aínbo jenén réteke.** A woman drowned from going too deep into the water.⟩ *adv.* : inside ⟨**Chichó riki nokon bonánti.** My trunk is inside.⟩
*v.t.* **chichóaa** *Konibo* **chichóaka** : to put deep inside ⟨**Yómetsobaon méranaketianra, koríki en chichóake.** So the thieves would not find it, I put the money deep inside.⟩
*v.i.* **chíchokiita** : to wash one's own buttock
See under **nobé**
*v.i.* **chíchota** : to go deep inside : to penetrate inward ⟨**Weán meran kaíra motóro chichókainke. As it went along the stream, the motor (outboard motor) went in very deep.⟩
*v.t.* **chíchota** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the buttocks + *chókati* to wash] : to wash the buttock of
*n.* **chíikan** : fire : flame ⟨**En piróta jámata káaxa chíiki pakéke.** The ball I kicked rolled and fell into the fire.⟩

*n.* **chíijexkon** [from Shipibo *chíi* fire + *jéxko* little piece] : firebrand ⟨**Tókoroninra chíijexko xéai.** Toads swallow firebrands.⟩ ⟨**Yoxínronki chíijexko keska béroya iki.** They say that demons of that kind have eyes like firebrands.⟩

*n.* **chíikan ewan** [from Shipibo *chíi*, *chíikan* fire + *ewa*, augmentative] : hell located in the sky beside the house of the Inca and that appears like a burning garden plot ⟨**Aínbaonronki mawáxon chíikanewa óina iki.** They tell that a woman in a coma saw hell.⟩
See under **koín**

*n.* **chíimakaman** [from Shipibo *chíi* fire + *makán* stone] : flint (spark stone) ⟨**Chíi yámaketianra non chíimakaman káro ketéake.** For lack of fire, we lit the firewood with the spark of a stone.⟩
*n.* **chíimapon** [from Shipibo *chíi* fire + *mápo* head, or *mápo* clay] : ash ⟨**Mitántianra chíimapobaonbi sikíkanai.** At carnival they even painted themselves with ashes.⟩
*n.* **chikáronin** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the stern + *káro* firewood] : harpoon ⟨**Jawen épán chikároninra papán wáme cháchike.** Dad speared the paiche with his uncle's harpoon.⟩
See under **átsa**
See under **risbí**
See under **wáste**

*n.* **chíketen** *Konibo* **chíkekan** 1 : fence ⟨**Chiké rásakaxa kóchi pikóke.** The pig got out by breaking the fence.⟩ 2 : wall ⟨**Non ískoirara tábara chikeya iki.** Our school has wooden walls.⟩ 3 : room of a house *syn.* CHIKE, CHITE both can denote "room of a house" without any difference; but each in turn has a second sense different from the other's.
*v.t.* **chíkena** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the stern + *kenéati* to paint with designs] : to paint designs on the stern of
*v.t.* **chíkexa** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the rear parts + *kéxeti* to sew] : to sew (trousers) at the seat

*also* **bárichiki** *n.* **chikín** *also* **bárichikin** [from Shipibo; *bári* sun + *chiki*, imitative of its call] 1 : a species of small hawk ⟨**Mérati kakín non chíki óinaronki,** **kaxón píti iki.** They say that when we go visiting and see a little *chíki* hawk on the path, we are sure to be given food.⟩ 2 : constellation called "Little Hawk" and located in the Milky Way –Used in this sense spelled with a capital initial letter *C*.

*n.* **chíkirayan** [from Spanish; influenced, by popular assimilation, by Shipibo *chíki* a species of hawk and by *rayá* worker] : cowpea : black-eyed pea ⟨**En chíkiraya mashín bánaara ea kokámebaon keyónke.** The cowpeas that I planted on the beach were all harvested by some cocamas.⟩

*adj.* **chíkishin** : lazy : idle : slothful ⟨**Westíora jonínra jawen báke chikísh ímake, jatíbitian téetiain íoyamakin.** A certain man got his son used to being lazy by never taking him to work.⟩ *syn.* áya
See under **jáka**
*v.i.* **chíkisha** : to become lazy or idle ⟨**Ichayora mishkín kókoaxa nato jóni chikíshke.** This man became lazy from eating a great deal of honey.⟩
*n.* [from Shipibo *chíki* hawk + *táro* dirty] : constellation called "Dirty Little Hawk" and not located precisely

*n.* **chikóron** *Konibo* **chikóronin** [from Shipibo *chíkoro*, imitative of its call] : a species of demon ⟨**Chikóro keóketianronki merákanti iki.** They say that the call of the *chikóro* demon announces the arrival of visitors.⟩
See under **wáste**
*adj.* **chíkoshin** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *kóshi* strong] : with a strong base –Used, e.g., of a pot.

*n.* **chikóshkintin** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the eaves + *koshkínti* with which to place crosswise] : half a cañabrava (cane) laid crosswise that forms part of a house's eaves ⟨**Nokon epán xóbora chikóshkintioma iki.** My paternal uncle's house has no *chikóshkinti* crossbeams.⟩

*v.t.* **chíkoa** : to spill ⟨**Min chíkoketianra en mia méniwetsayamai** -aquin aká iqui. He told her: -If you spill it, I won't give you any more.⟩ ⟨**Xéati chikóra kochín táxoai.** The pig licks up the spilled drink.⟩

*v.i.* **chíkota** : to spill, to be spilled ⟨**Chómo tóetaxa ompáx chikóke.** When the jug broke, the water spilled.⟩ *syn.* CHIKOTI, SHOITI both can be translated as "to spill", but SHOITI implies that the amount spilled is small.

*n.* **chimakayaman** : the mouth of a river, stream, or caño (side channel) ⟨**Orobampa chimakayanra samán onsá iki; jaínra jóni réoke.** At the mouth of the Urubamba there is a very dangerous whirlpool that capsized a man in his canoe.⟩ ⟨**Nato táe chimakayainra en nónti pótake.** At the mouth of this caño I left the canoe.⟩
*v.t.* **chímana** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *mamánti* to feel] 1 : to feel the buttock 2 : to feel (a hen) at the backside to see if it has an egg to lay

*n.* **chimáponin** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the thick end + *mápo* head] : a kind of fishing arrow that has four points ⟨**En íwi cháchiara ea chimápo boónke.** When I speared a stingray, it carried off my *chimápo* arrow.⟩
*n.* **chímiman** : girl ⟨**Nato chímiman póira náshiaitian jenén réteke.** This girl's little brother drowned while he was bathing.⟩ *syn.* chibá

*n.* **chimpán** [from Shipibo *chi(m)-* on the back parts + *paná* curtain] : crisneja (a woven palm-leaf roofing panel) ⟨**Ráma yaméra chímpa xobo naman ránsakanai.** Tonight they are going to dance in a house made of crisnejas.⟩

*also* **chimpansé** *n.* **chimpánsinin** *also* **chimpánsenin** [from Spanish; and this in turn from a West African language] : chimpanzee ⟨**Ja chímpansi riki Ajírikamea íso, nekea isón ewa keskaribi. Ikaxbira jínaoma iki.** The chimpanzee is a monkey from Africa, similar to the large monkeys here, but without a tail.⟩
*v.i.* **chínexeeta** : to tie oneself by the waist

*also* **mórochinexeti** *n.* **chínexetin** *also* **mórochinexeti** [from Shipibo (*móro* glass beads +) *chínexeti* to tie by the waist] : a white beaded belt highly prized by women ⟨**Nokon poín mórochinexetira bakén tésake.** A boy broke my sister's beaded belt.⟩
*v.t.* **chínexa** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *nexati* to tie] : to tie by the waist or by the buttocks

*n.* **chínikan** : excavation : a dug hole ⟨**Yamé íshtoira ea chiní meran káke.** Running at night, I fell into the excavation.⟩ ⟨**Koríke míinkana bíkanara mái chiní áni iki.** The excavation in the ground is large, the one where they found the hidden money.⟩
*adj.* **chínikan** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the back parts + *ni,* unidentified element] : last ⟨**Mia chiníora jóketianra mia namán kopíake.** Because you came last, they paid you less.⟩
*v.i.* **chínita** : to be or remain last ⟨**Eapari nokókasira ea chiníke motóro masáketian.** I hoped to arrive before the others, but I arrived last because the motor (outboard motor) broke down.⟩
*n.* **chínkaman** : a kind of ornamental plant
*adj.* **chínokan** [*from Shipibo chi-* in the anus + *nóati* to prick with something pointed] : with an enema inserted ⟨**Nato bákebora chinóbires íkanai.** All these children were given an enema.⟩
*v.t.* **chínoa** : to give or insert an enema to ⟨**Nokon bákebenbo ésteketianra rókotoron chínoke.** When my son's stomach swelled up, the doctor gave him an enema.⟩
*n.* **chínotinin** [*from Shipibo chínoti, chino-* to give an enema + *-ti* with which] : an enema syringe ⟨**Nato bákera chínotiki ráketai.** This child is afraid of the enema syringe.⟩
*adj.* **chínshiman** [*from Shipibo chi-* at the tip + *nshin,* element of *panshín* yellow] : dry and yellowish at the tip —Used of a leaf.
*n.* **chintín** : a weaving knife (loom knife)

*adj.* **chintón** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the tail + *-nto* without] : tailless —Used of a bird. *syn.* CHINTO, JINTO, JINAOMA can all be translated as "tailless." JINTO implies anything at all, without restriction, that has lost its tail, whereas CHINTO is limited to birds. JINAOMA refers to a kind of animal that has no tail.

*n.* **chintón** [*from Shipibo chi-* at the tip + *-nto* without] : a kind of arrow for hunting birds, having a tip in the shape of a small circle split in half ⟨**Papánra jawen chintón píno réteke.** My father killed a hummingbird with his bird-hunting arrow.⟩

*n.* **chión** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the back parts + *o,* unidentified element] 1 : younger brother or sister ⟨**Min chión báwa méeyamawe.** Don't bother your little brother's loro (parrot).⟩ 2 : great-grandchild *syn.* **bába**

*also* **chío** *n.* **chíobaken** *also* **chión** [*from Shipibo chío* younger sister + *báke* daughter] : nephew : niece : the son or daughter of a woman's brother —The vocative form *choré* "son" or the vocative form *yoxán* "daughter" is used to address the person in question. ⟨**Bákeoma ixon jawen chiobakebi onánhan riki.** She adopted her own niece because she had no children.⟩ *syn.* See under **kókobake** *syn.* nóxa; pía; piaká
*adj.* **chíoshin** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the buttocks + *yósho* crooked] : having a crooked buttock
*adj.* **chíoxen** [*from Shipibo chi-* of the buttocks + *jóxo* whitish] : having a whitish buttock

*n.* **chípaman** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the eaves + *pani,* unidentified element] : low eaves ⟨**Xóbo chipán namanra pápa páenax rakáke.** Papá is drunk and is lying down under the eaves of the house.⟩

*n.* **chípekenin** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the back parts + *péke* hole] : a hole in the thick end or in the lower part ⟨**Titán chómo benara chípeakeya iki.** Mamá's new jar has a hole in the lower part.⟩
*v.i.* **chípekeeta** : to become holed at the thick end
*v.t.* **chípeta** : to make a hole in the thick end
*n.* **chipéxkonin** : iliac bone (hip bone) ⟨**Jawen chipéxko tóbitaxa nato báke chántoti níai.** This child limps because he dislocated his iliac bone.⟩
*n.* **chipín** : older sister ⟨**Jaínra min chípi jóai káro papía.** There comes your older sister carrying firewood.⟩
*n.* 1 : the mouth of a river 2 : the end of an island or beach
*v.i.* **chípishiita** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the stern + *píshiti* to unhook + *-ii,* reflexive suf.] : for the stern to free itself (e.g., from mud or from a stick in the water)
*v.t.* **chípisha** [*from Shipibo chi-* on the stern + *píshati* to unhook] : to free the stern of (e.g., a stick in the water, or a place where something has run aground)

*Konibo* **chíchiyoxan** *n.* **chípiyoxaman** *Konibo* **chíchiyoxaman** [from Shipibo *chípi* older sister + *yoxán* old woman] : great-grandmother; *also* : sister of a great-grandfather or a great-grandmother –Used the vocative form *chipí* or the vocative form *titá* "mama" to address the person indicated.

*adv.* [from Shipibo *chi-* in the rear parts + *pon*, unidentified + *-ki* on] 1 : downriver : downstream : below ⟨**Moa chipónki káinbira jawen papán ráanyamake.** Even though he was already going downriver, his father did not send him.⟩ 2 : to the north *syn.* CHIPONKI, NORITI both can be translated as "north", but CHIPONKI, the native word, is more widely known and established.

*v.i.* **chípota** [from Shipibo *chi-*, in the rear parts + *po*, unidentified + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to cover oneself with ⟨**Chiárextioma ikaxa nato báke kótoman chipóke.** This child covered himself with his shirt because he had no trousers.⟩ 2 : to join (a person) ⟨**Mia éki chipóketianra mia tsón jáweatima iki.** If you join me, no one will be able to do anything to you.⟩

*v.i.* **chiránkoota** [from Shipibo *chiranko*, unidentified + *-oo*, reflexive verbal suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to kneel ⟨**Chiránkootaxa aínbo maíkibi békepike.** The woman bent down to the ground when she knelt.⟩

*n.* **chirápanin** [from Cocama *chirapa*] : rainbow ⟨**Chiráparonki non métotima iki, póntsekeenaketian.** They say we must not point at the rainbow with a finger; for we may dislocate our arm.⟩ *syn.* CHIRAPA, NAWANBAI, YOSHINKOSHKI, all mean "rainbow"; only that CHIRAPA belongs to shetebo speakers, NAWANBAI to shipibo speakers, and YOSHINKOSHKI to regionally conibo speakers.

*n.* **chírewinin** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the rear parts + Old Shipibo *réwe* (Shipibo *rekín*) nose] : point of land at a bend in the river ⟨**Tapán bokínra non chírewin tsákake yamé íketian.** While steering the raft, we struck a point of land because it was night.⟩
*v.t.* **chírina** : to root with the snout ⟨**Jawen jéma napon mái chirinaitianra papán kóchi tóoake.** Dad shot the pig because it was rooting in his yard.⟩

*adj.* **chirón** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks, at the waist + *-ro*, unidentified] : too short –Used about cushmas (a traditional tunic) or shirts. ⟨**Nokon pápara tári chíroshokotonin kéenyamai; nenkéshamantoninra kéenai.** My dad does not like the cushma too short, but on the contrary he likes it long⟩ ⟨**Rámatian jónibaonra jaton kotón chíroshoko sáwekanai.** Men nowadays wear shirts that are too short.⟩ *syn.* CHIRO, CHIXKO have the same meaning "too short", and both are used about the cushma. But whereas CHIRO is used only to name a shirt, CHIXKO is also used to designate a pampanilla (a wrap skirt) and trousers.
*v.t.* **chíroaa** *Konibo* **chíroaka** : to make too short ⟨**Onáma ixonra, nato aínbaon chíroakin xáteke.** This woman, being foolish, cut the cloth too short.⟩
*v.i.* **chíroa** : to shrink ⟨**Nokon kotón en pátsatara moa chíroke.** The shirt I washed has shrunk.⟩
*adj.* **chísesen** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttock + *sése* freckled] : with spots on the buttock

*v.i.* **chíshbita** [*chi-* in the rear parts + *shbi* unidentified + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to move about while seated on the ground ⟨**Mémironki níi chíshbitai.** They say that the demons in abandoned houses move about seated when they leave.⟩
*n.* **chishpín** [from Shipibo *chi-* of the rear parts + *shpi*, unidentified] : protruding genitals of the female cotomono (howler monkey), maquisapa (spider monkey), and choro (woolly monkey)
*n.* **chítakan** *Konibo* **chítakanin** [from Shipibo *chi-* deep inside + *táka* liver] : gizzard ⟨**En átapa chitaka xóiara ochítinin bóke.** The dog carried off the roasted chicken gizzard.⟩
*v.t.* **chítáxa** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *táxo-*, root of *táxoti* to lick + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to lick on the rear parts

*adj. and n.* **chitén** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the tail + *téxe* that remains] *adj.* : leftover : remaining ⟨**Min píti chítebires ea méniwe —akin akábiki méniamaa iki.** He did not give him food even when he begged him to give him whatever was left over.⟩ *n.* 1 : a leftover part; *specif.* : tip : stub ⟨**Jaton báke ísinaitian yobébo** **róme xéixon ákanai xóon amakin; ja chíte ámakanai téomakin.** When their children get sick, a cigarette is made so the shamans can blow smoke over them and then place the stubs of these on their necks.⟩ 2 : fish left behind by the receding water

*n.* **chítekan** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the tail + *te*, unidentified] 1 : pen, corral ⟨**Ja chínita chité ikainoara máxokan atapa boke.** The fox carried off the hen from the last pen.⟩ 2 : room of a house ⟨**Jawen chité meran óxaa iketianra ráteke.** I woke him while he was sleeping in his room.⟩ *syn.* See under **chiké**
*v.t.* **chíteaa** *Konibo* **chíteaka** : to make (something) be left over ⟨**Mia jóai onánxonra en píti chíteake.** Knowing you were coming, I made sure food was left over.⟩ *syn.* *téxeati*
*v.i.* **chítea** : to be left over (food) ⟨**Píti chíteketianra en ochíti ménike.** When there was food left over, I gave it to the dog.⟩

*v.t.* **chítea** 1 : to be against : to oppose ⟨**Niwén noa chíteketianra noa káyamake.** We did not leave, because the wind was against us.⟩ 2 : to hold back (floodwater) with a wall ⟨**Ichayora jéne béaitianra en chíteke, noa máponaketian.** When the flood came, I made a wall to keep it from flooding us.⟩ 3 : to forbid : to prohibit ⟨**Níweabatai oínxonra en mia chíteke.** Seeing that the storm was coming, I forbade you to leave.⟩
*v.t.* **chíteta** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *tékati* to sting] : to sting (e.g., a wasp) on the buttock

*v.t.* **chítéxa** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *téxeati* to be left over] 1 : to pull off the abdomen of (an insect) ⟨**Ea tékaketianra en bína chítéxke.** I pulled off the wasp's abdomen because it stung me.⟩ 2 : to loosen or pull all the way down someone's pampanilla (wrap skirt) ⟨**Chítéxketianra, áinbaon jawen tsábe bachínke.** A woman pulled her sister-in-law's hair when the latter loosened her pampanilla.⟩

*v.t.* **chitíaa** *Konibo* **chitíaka** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *ti*, unidentified + *-ati* to make] 1 : to make (someone/something) retreat ⟨**Ikáraninra yoshín chitíake.** With *ikára*-type songs he made the demon retreat.⟩ 2 : to lower (a price) ⟨**¿Minki jawen kopí ea chitíaxontima iki?** Can't you lower the price for me?⟩
*v.t.* **chítina** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear + *chíniti* to dig] : to adze (a canoe) at the stern
*v.t.* **chítina** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *tímati* to hit] : to bump one's buttock against (something in the way)

*v.t.* **chítina** [from Shipibo *chi-* at the stern + *tínati* to pack] : to stuff (things) into the stern ⟨**Sontárobaonra wapóro poinkiain ícha jawéki chitínke.** The soldiers stuffed many things into the stern of the boat.⟩

*v.t.* **chítita** : to back up; *specif.* : to back away to escape ⟨**Ochítinin jojóakara noa chitíkanke, noa natéxnaketian.** When the dog barked at us, we backed away for fear it would bite us.⟩ ⟨**Jawen pátoron méraaxa chitíke.** On seeing his boss, he backed away because he didn't want to go to work.⟩

*v.t.* **chitóaa** *Konibo* **chitóaka** : to make (something) shrink : to shorten lengthwise ⟨**Nato aínbaonra kotón chitóati onánke Yarínain áxea íxon.** This woman knows how to take in shirts because she studied it in Yarina.⟩

*v.t.* **chítona** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *tónko* round + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to put on (a pampanilla, a wraparound skirt) ⟨**Titánra jawen chitónti béna chitónke.** Mom put on her new pampanilla.⟩
*n.* **chitóntinin** : pampanilla (a wraparound skirt) ⟨**Jawen chitóntinin yómetsoaitianra titán jawen tsábe mérake.** Mom caught her sister-in-law stealing her pampanilla.⟩

*v.t.* **chítoa** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *to*, unidentified + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to spread apart the legs of ⟨**Kapónhanoxonra nato kóchi non chítoke.** To be able to castrate this pig, we had to spread its hind legs apart.⟩

*v.i.* **chítota** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *to*, unidentified + *-ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to shrink or get shorter lengthwise ⟨**Chiárexti áni biára moa pátsata chitóke.** My trousers, which were too long for me, have shrunk from washing.⟩ ⟨**Nokon chiárexti chitó iketianra ea kéenyamai.** I don't like my trousers because they shrank.⟩ 2 : to draw one's feet up toward the groin : to squat ⟨**Chítoti yakáketianra jawen titán sináake.** When she sat down squatting, her mother scolded her for sitting in an indecent position.⟩
*v.t.* **chíwata** [from Shipibo *chi–* of the waist + *wáketi* to lift] : to lift (+ by the waist)
See under **paránta**
*v.t.* **chíwea** [from Shipibo *chi–* of the stern + *wéati* to remove (liquid or powder)] : to scrape (e.g., mud) off the stern
*v.t.* **chíweta** : to hook from behind at the waist
*v.i.* **chíwimeeta** : to stir by itself ⟨**xéati kobínhaara kóbini chíwimeeke.** The cooking drink stirred itself as it boiled.⟩

*v.t.* **chíwina** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the backside + *wínati* to paddle] : to beat, to stir ⟨**Jawen chícha chiwínira epán awín menóke.** My paternal uncle's wife burned herself while stirring her chicha.⟩
*v.t.* **chíwina** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the back parts + *wínati* to paddle] : to stir

*v.t.* **chíwina** [from Shipibo *chi–* on the stern + *wínati* to paddle] : to steer : to handle (a boat) from the stern ⟨**En rewínbanon, mín chiwínwe —akin aká iki.** And he told him: —I will paddle at the bow and you will steer.⟩ *syn.* chibíti

*n.* **chiwíntinin** [from Shipibo *chiwín–*, *chiwínti* to stir + *–ti* with which] : a beater, a stirrer : a skimmer ⟨**Papánra chiwínti jakón akai, titán ján chícha chiwínti.** Papá is making a good beater so that mamá can stir her chicha.⟩
[from Shipibo *moxó* topa (balsa wood) + *chiwínti* beater] : a kind of medium-sized beater made of topa (balsa wood) used to mash plantains

*adj.* **chíxakan** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *xa*, unidentified] : afflicted with a disease of the uterus ⟨**Chixá ikaxa aínbo mawáke.** A woman died from contracting a disease of the uterus.⟩

*n.* **chixánanin** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *xána* hot] 1 : belly ⟨**Bakénketianra títa chixánanin chéxake.** After giving birth, mom felt pain in her belly.⟩ 2 : lap ⟨**Néri jowé nokon chixánain yakánti.** Come here and sit on my lap.⟩ *syn.* xábi
*n.* **chíxeman** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the anus + *xéna* small worm] : small worms in the anus
*v.t.* **chíxeta** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *xéteti* to sniff] : to sniff at the rear parts, the way dogs do

*n.* **chíxkán** [from Shipibo *chíxka*, imitative of its call] 1 : chicua (a bird) ⟨**Nopatax chíxka kéotaira noa jawéki yóii íkai.** The chicua, singing near us, is announcing something to us.⟩ 2 : a constellation called "Chicua" that is not precisely located –Used in this sense written with an initial capital *C*.
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *chíxka*] : a species of chicua
*v.i.* **chíxkita** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttock + *xákiti* to grate] : to drag oneself along seated on the ground
*adj.* **chixkón** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *xko*, unidentified] : too short –Used of cushmas (tunics), pampanillas (wrap skirts), or trousers. *syn.* See under chíro
*n.* **chixnín** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the rear parts + *ráni* body hair] : hairs of the anus
*n.* **chíxón** : buttock ⟨**Jawen chíxónkora bonán tékake.** An isula (bullet ant) stung him on the buttock⟩

*n.* **chíxokan** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the anus + *xo*, element of *xókati* to peel] : diarrhea ⟨**Chíxó betan kínamanra Kakónkonia jóni rétekeanke.** A man from Caco nearly died of diarrhea and vomiting.⟩
See under **paránta**
See under **peká**

*v.i.* **chíxota** : to have or come down with diarrhea or dysentery ⟨**Ichayora kóchi xeni piáxa ea yamé chíxóshinai.** Because I ate something with a lot of pork fat, I have had diarrhea all night.⟩
See under **wáste**
*v.i.* **chíxoxa** [from Shipibo *chi-* in the stern + *xóxoti* to sprout] : to grow in the cracked stern of an old canoe
*n.* **chíxpokan** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttocks + *xopó* hairy] : bristles or fine hairs on the buttocks
*v.t.* **chíxtea** [from Shipibo *chi-* on the buttock + *xáteti* to cut] 1 : to cut on the buttock 2 : to cut at the larger handle

*voc. n.* [from Shipibo *choré*, a word for calling a son or daughter] : my dear –Used with the sense of "my dear" as an expression of affection among adults. –Used added to a vocative noun (e.g., a personal name). ⟨**Jowé, Sinácho.** Greetings, my dear **Siná!**⟩
*n.* **choán** : a species of tree similar to the zapote (sapote) that is considered to be bewitched

*also* **niáchochowasha** *Konibo* **chóchoasha** *n.* **chóchawashan** *also* **niáchochowashan** *Konibo* **chóchoashan** [from Quechua *kwkwwasi*; and this from Quechua *kwkw* teat + *wasi* house] 1 : chuchuhuasi 2 : a demon identified with the chuchuhuasi ⟨**Chóchawashayoshinronki benkéx táe máxkoshoko iki.** They say the demon of the chuchuhuasi has one foot smaller than the other.⟩
[from Shipibo *níshi* vine + *chóchawasha* chuchuhuasi] : a species of vine

*n.* **chóiman** : a species of sweet ashipa with leaves like those of the bean plant and roots larger than those of the sachapapa ⟨**Péokin choín kókoaxa nato báke chixóke.** This child got diarrhea from eating ashipa for the first time.⟩
[from Shipibo *píti* food + *choín* a species of sweet ashipa] : a species of ashipa with roots similar to those of the carrot, but purple or white in color

*v.t.* **chókaa** : to wash (something that is not cloth) ⟨**Nokon yónotininra en tápo chókati yóiabi áyamake.** Even though I ordered my servant to wash the floor, she hasn't done it.⟩ See *Grammar Sketch 8.3.1* [illustration: *chókati*]
*n.* **chóke** –Used as a word for calling the perico or the pihuicho.
*n.* **chokín** : wrinkle in cloth or paper
*v.t.* **chókiaa** *Konibo* **chókiaka** : to form wrinkles in : to wrinkle ⟨**Tsínikinra nato bakén jawen kotón chókiake**. The child wrinkled his shirt while playing.⟩

*v.i.* **chókita** : to wash oneself ⟨**Nato aínbora nanén síkitaxbi moa chokíke**. This woman has washed the hands that she had painted with the fruit of the huito.⟩ ⟨**Jatíbi rátora moa chokíbires iki, maístoron jaskáati yóiketian en aká**. The dishes are already washed because I did it when the teacher ordered me to wash them.⟩ ⟨**Min bemana chokímaiketianra rókotoron mia osánke**. The doctor laughed at you because your face is not washed.⟩
*n.* **chomán** : clouds ⟨**Moa ói béaitianra chóma kextó iki.** When it is going to rain the clouds are dark.⟩ *syn.* koín
*v.i.* **chómaa** : to be cloudy ⟨**Naí chómaara moa bári jíshtima iki.** When the sky clouds over, the sun cannot be seen.⟩
See under *wári*
*n.* **chomón** : large earthenware jar ⟨**Títara moa jawen chomón mároke.** Mom sold her earthenware jar.⟩
*v.t.* **chómoaa** *Konibo* **chómoaka** : to make earthenware jars ⟨**Jawen ribín kopiatira titán chómoake.** Mom made earthenware jars to pay off her debt.⟩
*n.* **chompán** : a species of tree with fruit similar to the ubos (hog plum)
*n.* **chompén** : a species of monte (forest) vine with fragrant leaves that are used for dyeing, imparting their fragrance
*n.* **chompín** [from Quechua *kwmpi*] : a woven cotton sash used as a belt
*n.* **chonchón** : chick; *specif.* : chuncho ⟨**átapa betan chónchobo** a hen with her chicks⟩ ⟨**Nato yaméra chóncho matsín rétewanke.** Last night the chuncho died of cold.⟩
See under *boín*
*adj.* **chonkán** [from Quechua *kwnka*] : ten ⟨**Eara Máioshiain kái chónka néte wínotapekaopari.** I am going to Pucallpa in ten days.⟩

*n.* **chónkéxen** [from Shipibo *chonkéx*, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird that resembles a dove small and speckled gray in color ⟨**Chónkexben náa meranoara tétekan róno píai**. The hawk eats snake in the nest of the little *chonkéx* bird.⟩
*n.* **chonón** : swallow ⟨**Non chóno ináaketianronki non báke máwatai.** They say that when swallows are raised, our children die.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *chóno* swallow] : a species of light-black swallow
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *chóno* swallow] : a species of swallow
[from Shipibo *yankón* blue + *chóno* swallow] : a species of swallow with bright blue wings

*n.* **chonóninintinin** [from Shipibo *chóno, chonón* swallow + *inínti* fragrance] : a species of fragrant tree used for dyeing ⟨**Nokon títashokonra chonóninintinin jawen chitónti pókoke.** My grandmother dyed her pampanilla with dye from the *chonónininti* tree.⟩

*n.* **chopán** 1 : clothing ⟨**Nokon áwininra nokon chópa ea patsáxonai**. My wife washes my clothes.⟩ 2 : cloth ⟨**Máioshiainra ráma chópaati mákina ákanai; játianronki waxmén wai ati íkai**. They are now going to set up a textile factory in Pucallpa, and they say that is why cotton can be cultivated.⟩
[from Spanish *vichy* + Shipibo *chópa* cloth] : gingham (vichy)
[from Spanish *kaki* + Shipibo *chópa* clothing] : khaki
[from Shipibo *máshi* sandy beach + *chópa* clothing] : beach cloth
[from Spanish *orán* + *chópa* clothing] : floral-print cloth
*n.* **chópaiton** [from Shipibo *chópa* cloth + *-ai*, present-participle suf.] : weaver
See under **mákina**

*adj.* **chópaoman** *Konibo* **chópaomatonin** [from Shipibo *chópa* clothing + *-oma* without] : naked, either completely or only on the upper part of the body ⟨**Rámabi níi meranoa píkokana jónira chópaoma ikátiai**. The man who was recently brought out of the monte (forest) was naked.⟩
See under **peká**

*n.* **chópekan** 1 : crack; *specif.* : crack in wood ⟨**Jíwi chopetain métoti níaketianra báke ninbón tékake**. A scorpion stung the child when he put his finger into the crack of a tree.⟩ 2 : crack in the ground 3 : part in the hair *syn.* chaká

*v.t.* **chópea** 1 : to open (e.g., the mouth, the eye, a trunk, or a book) ⟨**Títashokon kexá chópexon oínkanara íke jawen xétabo yáma**. When they opened grandmother's mouth, they saw that she had no teeth.⟩ ⟨**Rókotoron béro chópenaankasara nato báke wíniai**. This child is crying because the doctor wants to open his eye.⟩ ⟨**Nokon kokánra kírika chópekin jawen pápa máwataton jóto mérake**. *On opening a book, my uncle, my mother's* brother, found the photo of his late father.⟩ 2 : to spread out : to unfold

*v.i.* **chópeta** 1 : to open (e.g., a mouth, eye, or book) ⟨**Niwén akára kírika chópetai**. The book is opening, from the effect of the wind.⟩ 2 : to split (e.g., a tree, wood, or canoe) 3 : to crack (e.g., ground or fruit)
*n.* **chópianantinin** : sandieta ⟨**Chópiananti chákaxon ochíti xéamaara máwatai**. When a dog is made to drink crushed sandieta, it causes its death.⟩
See under **níshi**
*n.* **chopítinin** [from Spanish] : pacifier
*v.i.* **chórameeta** : to be together (of turtles) ⟨**Kopítsoya kabóribo chórameetara non oínke**. We saw the cupisos and the taricayas together.⟩

*v.i.* **chórana** 1 : to be piled up (logs or entrails) ⟨**Nato bokón xate chóranara mároti ákana iki.** The logs of cetico piled up there are for sale.⟩ ⟨**En rabé awá réteara jawen póko pótakana chórana iki.** The entrails of the two tapirs I killed are piled up where they were thrown out.⟩ 2 : to coil up (snake) ⟨**En róno jámatabira ea natéshamake chórana ixon.** I stepped on a snake but it did not bite me because it was coiled up.⟩ 3 : to get tangled (rope) ⟨**En níniara nato risbí choránke.** This rope got tangled because I pulled it.⟩ 4 : to get wrinkled (e.g., cloth, paper, or skin) ⟨**Ménotaxa nato bakén póko choránke.** The skin of this child's belly wrinkled when it got burned.⟩ ⟨**Nato bakén sáyara chórana iki.** This girl's dress got wrinkled.⟩
*n.* **chorén** : wrinkle ⟨**Nato aínbaon yórara chórebiresiki, ménota ikax.** This woman's body is covered with wrinkles because she got burned.⟩ *syn.* sipón
*n.* –Used as an affectionate vocative for a relative (e.g., from grandparents to grandchildren, or from uncles or aunts to nephews and nieces).
*adj.* **chórishin** : hard ⟨**Chóríshora ikénbira en rimán xáteke.** Although it was very hard, I cut it with a file.⟩
*v.t.* **choríshaa** *Konibo* **choríshaka** : to harden ⟨**Xóixonra mái chóríshakanai.** If they burn the earth, it becomes as hard as brick.⟩
See under **bína**
*v.i.* **chórisha** : to harden : to become hard ⟨**Bási ói béyamaketianra moa mái chóríshke.** The earth has hardened because it has not rained for a long time.⟩

*v.i.* **chórokoota** 1 : to uncoil (snake) ⟨**Nato róno chórokooketianra báke íxtoke.** The boy ran when this snake uncoiled.⟩ 2 : to unwrap (e.g., a package) ⟨**Páketira nato mixé chórokooke.** This package unwrapped when it fell.⟩
*v.i.* **chórona** : to jump : to leap ⟨**Róno jámataxa ea chorónke.** When I stepped on the snake, I gave a jump.⟩

*v.t.* 1 : to untangle ⟨**Papánra jawen risbí chóroke.** Dad untangled his rope.⟩ 2 : to untie (e.g., a canoe or mosquito net) ⟨**Nato bakén nónti chóroara báikan bóke.** The canoe was carried off by the current because this child had untied it.⟩ ⟨**Moara néte iki; báchi chóroe.** It is already daytime; untie the mosquito net.⟩ ⟨**Jawen tapán chóróiketian oínxonra, pátoronin jawen jónibo notsínke.** The boss scolded his workers when he saw that his raft had come untied.⟩ 3 : to take the stitches out of ⟨**Jakómakin kéxexonra báchi chóroke.** He took the stitches out of the mosquito net because he had sewn it badly.⟩ 4 : to open (e.g., a package) ⟨**Jawenama ikénbira jonín nato pakíti chóroke.** This man opened the package even though it was not his.⟩

*v.i.* **chórota** 1 : to come untied ⟨**Yómetso joni néxakanabira choróke.** Although they had tied up the thief, he got loose.⟩ ⟨**Janbíxa nato báchi choróke.** The mosquito net came untied by itself.⟩ ⟨**Papán xóbo néxaara choróke.** The house that dad tied up in his construction has come untied.⟩ 2 : to come unwrapped (e.g., a package) ⟨**Kírika míxeabira risbí páyo ikax choróke.** The wrapped-up papers have come unwrapped because the rope was old.⟩ 3 : to come uncoiled ⟨**Risbí chórota oínxonra jonín jawen báke ríxkike: Ján akára íbiraí —ixon.** The man saw that his rope was uncoiled and hit his son, thinking he had done it.⟩

*v.t.* **chóshaa** 1 : to break (e.g., a bone or shell) by striking ⟨**Atapa xao chóshakinra papán jawen métotires chóshake.** Dad struck his own finger while trying to break a chicken bone.⟩ ⟨**Jóxoshinonronki manánxawe chóshanike, jíwibochiki boxón.** They say that once the white monkey broke the shell of the motelo (tortoise) by carrying it to the top of a tree.⟩ 2 : to kill (e.g., a turtle) by breaking open the shell along the edges with machete blows ⟨**Píshtatian pítira titán kabóri chóshake.** Mom killed the taricaya (a river turtle) with machete blows to eat it at the festival.⟩ 3 : to strike *syn.* tsákati
*adj.* **choshín** [from Shipibo *choshíti, choshi-* to dry] : dry –Used of leaves or twigs. *syn.* mecháma

*v.i.* **chóshia** : to dry : to be dry (leaves or twigs) ⟨**Moa jépe pei chóshiketianra bakén ménoke, yóitima ixon.** When the yarina leaves were dry, the naughty child burned them.⟩ ⟨**Moa jíwibo chóshiaiketianra papán wái ménoke.** Dad burned his garden plot because the leaves and twigs were already dry.⟩

*v.i.* **chóshita** 1 : to break (e.g., a bone) from a blow ⟨**Bóchikiax páketira choshíkainke.** When he fell from a height, his bones broke.⟩ 2 : to strike oneself against something ⟨**Bóchikiax chóronira ea makánki choshíkainke.** When I threw myself down from a height, I struck myself against a rock.⟩ ⟨**Piróta akira nato jóni choshíke.** This player crashed hard into another while playing soccer.⟩
See under **átapa**

*v.t.* **chóshkaa** *Konibo* **chóshkaaka** : to make (roof thatch) lift up ⟨**Jépe pei xoboaara barín chóshkaake, péi benáiketian.** The new yarina leaves, used in building the house's roof, were lifted up by the sun.⟩

*v.i.* **chóshkata** 1 : to make one's own bristles or feathers stand up ⟨**Atapa sínára jawen ráni choshkáke.** The angry hen made its plumage stand up.⟩ 2 : to project upward (leaves of a roof) ⟨**Benáyora xóbo ikaxa péi choshkáke.** The leaves bent upward because the house was newly built.⟩
*adj.* **choskón** [from Quechua *kwsku*] : four ⟨**Chósko joni yometsora koáratiabaon bóke.** Four thieves were taken away by the guards.⟩
*adv.* **chóskoakin** [from Shipibo *chósko* four + *-i, -akin*, subordinate verbal suf.] : four times
*v.t.* **chótaa** : to have sexual relations
*n.* **chótata** : the experiencing of sexual relations

*n.* **chotáyosma aínbon** *Konibo* **aínbaon** *pish.* **aínbaen** [from Shipibo *chotáyosma* ; and this from *chotá-*, root of *chótati* to have sexual relations + *-yosma* never + *aínbo* woman] : virgin

*n.* **chóyachakin** [from Quechua *kwllachaki* ; and this from *kwlla* uneven + *chaki* foot] 1 : chullachaqui 2 : a demon identified with the chullachaqui ⟨**Chóyachakin táeronki tónkoshoko iki.** They say the foot of the chullachaqui demon is twisted.⟩

*n.* **choyón** 1 : a species of tree similar to the cetico 2 : the red ants that infest the *chóyo* tree; *also* : one of those ants ⟨**Noa choyón tékaara bási isín tóxkotai.** When a *chóyo* ant bites us, it hurts for a long time.⟩

*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *e* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*pers. pron.* en : I : me : to me ⟨**Ea yóyoikaitianra mato netéti iki.** When I speak, you all must be quiet.⟩ ⟨**Enra onánke jáskati jóyamaa.** I know why he did not come.⟩ ⟨**Ea áyamaabira jáwekeskaamabi iki.** It does not matter that he does not do it for me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.1

*verbal suf.* **–eet** : to oneself or themselves ⟨**Eara menexeetai.** I put on the bracelet.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.6

See **írijanti**
*n.* **emón** : mold : dirt stains
*v.i.* **émoa** : to get moldy : to get stained ⟨**Oín mecháara titán chitónti moa** **émoke.** Mom's pampanilla (a wraparound skirt) got moldy because the rain soaked it.⟩
See **-an**
*v.i.* **énika** : to complain : to groan : to whimper ⟨**Nokon epán bákera pórokan chéxai éniltai.** My paternal uncle's son is groaning because he has a stomachache.⟩ *syn.* íshiiti

*also* **jenjén** *also* **jénjen** *interj.* –Used as a response with the sense, e.g., of "yes" to express various reactions such as admiration, affirmation, doubt, or agreement. ⟨–¿**Minkiea méniai?** –**Jénjen.** –**Ichabires iráke.** –Will you give it to me? –Yes. –Thank you very much.⟩ *syn.* ENJEN, IKI both can be translated as "yes", but ENJEN, unlike IKI, takes no suffix and has no grammatical relation to the preceding verb.
See **intíro**

*n.* **epán** 1 : paternal uncle –The vocative form *epá* or *papá* "dad" is used to address the person in question. ⟨**Jawen épa betanra Máioshiain káke.** He went to Pucallpa with his paternal uncle.⟩ 2 : stepfather ⟨**Jawen epán jakómaara báke jabáke.** The child ran away because his stepfather mistreated him.⟩ *syn.* kóka; onánpapa

*also* **éeri** *interj.* –Used as an exclamation (e.g., of surprise, fear, or sorrow, with the sense of "ouch!" / "oh!"). ⟨¡**Eeri! Moara min ea toenaanke.** Oh! You made me break it.⟩ *syn.* See under **ápo**

*n.* **ésekan** 1 : advice ⟨**Nato esébora en mia yóiai, jaá min senénhati.** I give you this advice so that you may follow it.⟩ 2 : law ⟨**Rámara moa benáakin apón esé áke jaan noa akínti.** Now the government has made a new law to help us.⟩ ⟨**Riósen esé** the law of God⟩
*v.i.* **ésekaata** : to make and keep one's own advice or plan ⟨**Jawen ráwikan aká kópinoxa ésekaake.** In order to take revenge on his enemy, he devised a plan.⟩
*v.t.* ésea : to advise : to give good advice to ⟨**Mín áyamanon íxonra en mia éseai.** I advise you not to do it.⟩
*v.i.* éseta : to be advised : to be warned ⟨**Moa eséketian non íokasara nato jóni kakashamai.** This man did not want to go when we wanted to take him, because he had already been warned.⟩
*n.* eshín : carahuasco (a plant) *syn.* tashbánishi
See **iskóro**
See **ískoira**
See **Ispánya**
: United States

*adj.* estén 1 : taut –Used of a rope. ⟨**Nato risbí moa éste ikáxbira teséyamai naíron ikax.** Even though this rope is taut, it does not break because it is made of nylon.⟩ 2 : swollen : bloated ⟨**Yápa máwatara éste iki.** The dead fish is bloated.⟩

*v.t.* ésteaa *Konibo* ésteaka 1 : to make taut (e.g., a rope) ⟨**En risbí ésteakenbira ea bakén tésanaanke.** The boy broke the rope that I tightened.⟩ 2 : to stretch (e.g., the skin of a bass drum or drum) ⟨**Yamé ránsanoxonra bómpo ésteakanai.** They are stretching the drumhead so they can play at tonight's dance.⟩ 3 : to inflate ⟨**Moa kikínhakin ésteaara piróta toáike.** The ball burst because they inflated it too much.⟩ *syn.* jotóati; toshmón áti

*v.i.* éstea 1 : to swell ⟨**Ichayora betén piáxa ea ésteke.** When I ate too much *betén* fish mush, my belly swelled.⟩ ⟨**Ronón ewan kópia nato báke éstea riki.** This little child's belly swelled because it was cutipado (afflicted by an animal spirit) by the boa.⟩ ⟨**Kirínko bákeainbo jenén réteara, moa ésteax toxbáketian mérakanke.** A drowned little foreign girl was found when her body swelled and began to float.⟩ 2 : to inflate with air ⟨**Níwe xéaax ésteaxa tókoro toáike.** A toad burst when it inflated itself by swallowing air.⟩
See **ístiroja**

*n.* etsén : bad smell (e.g., of an unwashed body, of an old dirty rag, or of an already rotten corpse) ⟨**Jawen ochíti étse póataitianra jawen ibón náshimake.** The owner bathed his dog because it was giving off a bad smell.⟩ ⟨**Mawá míinkanara étse póataí, chichómashoko ákana.** The corpse they buried gives off a bad smell because they buried it too shallow.⟩
*modifying suf.* **–ewan** –Used with the force of "mother or origin of (a gigantic thing)" in compound words. ⟨**jenén ewa** flood⟩ ⟨**ronón ewa** boa⟩ ⟨**iwin ewa** stingray⟩
*adj.* expán : slack –Used, e.g., of a rope. ⟨**Tapán néxaa níshira moa éxpayora iki.** The forest vine with which the raft is tied is very slack.⟩

*v.t.* éxpaa *Konibo* éxpaaka : to loosen : to make sag ⟨**Papánra jawen báke notsínke éxpaakin risbí néxanaana.** The father scolded his son for having tied the rope in a way that let it come loose.⟩ ⟨**Báchi chíaketianra wakán noa éxpaanke.** When we had the mosquito net set up, the cow left it sagging.⟩ *syn.* kápoti; yéxketi; yóshoti
*v.i.* éxpaa : to loosen : to sag ⟨**En báchi chíaara moa éxpake.** The mosquito net that I set up has loosened.⟩

*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *i* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1
*conj.* [from Spanish] : and ⟨**Papán píchika sapén i chósko wáme réteke.** Dad killed five manatees and four paiche (a giant Amazonian fish).⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.7.1 *syn.* See under betan

*adverbial suf.* **-akin** [from Shipibo; subordinate form of *-ati* to do] : -ly –Used added to certain descriptive adjectives to form the adverb. ⟨**jakón, jákoni** good, well⟩ ⟨**ikón, íkoni** true, truly⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5

*verbal suf.* **-kin** –Used at the end of a subordinate verb meaning "when" or "while". ⟨**Poxóti koíshirita iki.** When it fell to the ground, it made a crashing noise.⟩ ⟨**Enra pikín yamé xáo xéawanke.** Last night I swallowed a bone while I was eating.⟩ –Used with the sense of "to" to form a verbal complement that occurs with certain main verbs according to their transitivity. ⟨**Titára jawen báke óini káke.** The mother went to see her daughter.⟩ ⟨**Ea natéxkasira íbiral ochíti.** Maybe the dog wants to bite me.⟩ ⟨**Enra xóbo akín péoai.** I am starting to build my house.⟩ *syn.* -ain. See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.1; 7.4.3.2
*modifying suf.* –Used with the imperative sense of "come," "you come," or "you all come," added to the imperative verb. ⟨**Ea akíniwe.** Come help me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*n.* **ián** : human louse ⟨**Non bóokan ía kaíshonronki noa téxteti iki.** They say that when lice multiply on our heads, they can behead us.⟩

*n.* **íajexen** [from Shipibo *ía* louse + *jéxe* sphere] : nit (louse egg) ⟨**Iajexe piáronki, ókoti iki.** They say that when you eat the nits from someone else's hair, you get attacked by a cough.⟩
*adv.* **íamaxon** [from Shipibo *íti, i–* to be + *–yama* not + *–ax, –xon,* subordinate-verb suf.] : that is : in other words ⟨**2, íamax 1 betán 1 riki.** It's 2; that is, 1 plus 1.⟩

*n.* **íaman** : lake : lagoon : cocha (an oxbow lake) ⟨**Tson oínyosma íaman káketianra jóni cháikonin bachínike.** When a certain man went to a totally unfamiliar cocha, one of the wild demons, the *cháikoni*, grabbed him by the hair.⟩
See under **táe**
*v.t.* **íata** : to put or carry on the shoulder ⟨**Arós sakora en moa iáke íwematani iketian.** I already carried the sack of rice on my shoulder because it wasn't very heavy.⟩
*n.* **Ibán** [from Spanish *Eva*] –Used as a female name.
*n.* **Ibán** [from Spanish *Evaristo*] –Used as a male name.

*postpositional suf.* : to (a person's house) –Used with the letter *h* prefixed if the complement ends in the letter *n*. ⟨**Bénxokasira ea miríkoiba katáyantanke** I went to a healer because I wanted to get well.⟩ ⟨**Eara ríkatonhiba káke.** I went to the river trader's place.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2

*modifying suf.* **–ibat** : yesterday : the other day –Used with the letter *h* prefixed if the verb root ends in the letter *n*. –Used in the form *–iba* or *–hiba* before a final suffix with an initial consonant, and in the form *–ibat* or *–hibat* before a final suffix with an initial vowel. ⟨**Rókotoronra báke íweibake néno raónkin.** The doctor brought the child here yesterday to cure him.⟩ ⟨**ikónhibake** believed yesterday⟩ ⟨**Bakísh jóibata riki.** He came yesterday.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2 *syn.* bakísh
*interj.* [from Shipibo *íti, ik–* + *–ba* + *–non,* exhortative suf.] –Used with the sense of "it doesn't matter". ⟨**Ibánon; eara kéenyamai.** It doesn't matter; I don't want it.⟩
*v.t.* **íbena** [from Shipibo *in–* at the temple + *bénati* to search] : to search (e.g., for lice) at the temple
*n.* **Ibín** [from Spanish *Elvira*] –Used as a female name.

*v.t.* **íbina** : to scare away ⟨**Moa ibínkana iketianra nokon kokán jóno mérayamake.** My uncle didn't find the collared peccary because someone had already scared it away.⟩ ⟨**Jawen arós bana píaitian non ísabo ibínkenbira noa jonín kopíayamake.** We scared away the little birds that were eating from the rice field, but the owner didn't pay us.⟩

*also* **ébreo joi** *also* **joríobaon joi** *also* **jodíobaon joi** *n.* **íbirio join** *also* **ébreo join** *also* **joríobaon join** *also* **jodíobaon join** : Hebrew : the language of the Hebrews or Israelis
*also* **ébreojoni** *n.* **íbiriojonin** [from Spanish *hebreo* + Shipibo *jóni* man] : Hebrew : a Hebrew man

*v.i.* íbia 1 : to withdraw or flee out of shame ⟨**Yómetsoketian en jáwe akámabira oa jóni íbia iki.** Even though I didn't do anything to him when he stole, that man withdrew from me out of shame.⟩ 2 : to escape (e.g., *a canoe*)

*n.* ibón 1 : owner ⟨**Atapa yómetsoaitianra nato jóni jawen ibón mérake.** When this man was stealing the hen, the owner discovered him.⟩ 2 : Lord : God as creator of heaven and earth who lives in heaven –Used in this sense with a capital *I.* ⟨**non Ibo** our Lord⟩ *syn.* Ríos

*n.* ibón [from Shipibo *íbo* owner] 1 : wood weevil ⟨**En konxán xáteara nokon pátoronin ea bixónyamake jawen ibón piáiketian.** My boss rejected the cedar log I brought him because it had weevils.⟩ 2 : ants that live in a tree ⟨**Nokon bákera jíwi ibon tékake, pitso bake bíkasaitian.** The tree ants stung my son when he wanted to catch a pihuicho (a small parakeet).⟩ 3 : moth (in manioc flour or other flour) ⟨**Nato jónira pórokan chéxake átsapoto jawen íboyabi píketian.** This man got a stomachache after eating manioc flour with moths in it.⟩

*also* **íboti** *v.t.* **íboaa** *Konibo* **íboaka** *also* **íboa** : to take ownership of : to seize ⟨**Nokon epán ochítira en íboake.** I have taken ownership of my uncle's dog.⟩ ⟨**Nato pátoronra nokon papán konxán xaten íboai.** This boss is seizing my father's cedar log.⟩

*adj.* **ichán** 1 : a lot ⟨**Joménwe píi chaí; ixónbi íchayora áyamawe.** Come eat, brother-in-law; but don't eat too much!⟩ 2 : many ⟨**En ícha néte téexonabira ea yómetsoake.** Even though I worked with him many days, he cheated me.⟩ 3 : more ⟨**—¿Bénboki bebón ícha iki o aínboki ícha iki? —Aínbo ícha iki.** —Are there more men or more women? —There are more women.⟩

*n.* **ícha jawékia jonín** [from Shipibo *ícha* many + *jawékia* possessor of things + *jóni* man] : one who is rich, wealthy, or well-off –Usually used in plural form. ⟨**Icha jawékia jónibaonra noa akínkashamai, yóashi ixon.** Rich people don't want to help us because they are stingy.⟩

*adj.* **íchamaton** [from Shipibo *ícha* much + *–ma* not] : less ⟨**—¿Jakia íchama bóti o íchama nónti?** —Nóntira íchama iqui. —Are there fewer boats or fewer canoes? —There are fewer canoes.⟩ *syn.* namánbires
*n.* **ichán janen** [from Shipibo *ícha, ichán* many + *jáne* name] : plural number –Used as a grammatical term. See Grammar Sketch 7.1.4
*adj.* **ichátaman** *Konibo* **ichátamatonin** : very little : very few ⟨**Ea ichátama méniketianra en ichátamaribi ménike.** He gave me very little, so I also gave him very little.⟩

*v.t.* **íchata** : to mock (e.g., someone with a physical defect) : to insult ⟨**Jawen béne icháketianra, papán jawen bákeainbo ríshkike.** The father whipped his daughter for having mocked her husband.⟩ ⟨**Moa icháxonra jawen ráwikan ríshkike.** His enemy mocked him, and afterward he whipped his enemy.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákera ichákana wínike.** This child cried because they mocked him.⟩
*n.* **ichínkanin** : a species of tree lizard
*adj.* **iean** [from Shipibo *in–* at the temple + *yenkén* bald] : bald at the temples
See **íkobimi**
See **íkojiwi**

*verbal suf.* **-iit** : oneself or themselves –Used added to a verb root that has three syllables with *i* as the last vowel, or that has two syllables and ends with the letters *is, ish, ix, os, osh,* or *ox.* ⟨**Eara máchoshiike.** I bumped my head.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.3

*n.* **íironin** [from Spanish] : ice ⟨**Nokon papánra íiro róroai.** My father is crushing ice.⟩ *syn.* IIRO, MATSI — both are used with the sense of "ice." IIRO, unlike MATSI, has no other meaning; it is a word borrowed from Spanish.
*also* **Ijipto** *n.* **Ijipiton** *also* **Ijipton** : Egypt

*also* **éjersisio** *n.* **íjirisisionin** *also* **éjersisionin** [from Spanish *ejerkikio*] : exercise : physical education ⟨**Maístoronra bákebo íjirisisio ámati iki.** The teacher will have his students do physical education.⟩

*n.* **íkai itan ákai join** [from Shipibo *íkai*, present participle of *íti* to be + *itan* and + *ákai*, present participle of *áti* to do + *jói* word] : verb –Used as a grammatical term. See Grammar Sketch 7.4
See under **keskáati**

*adv.* **akáma** [from Shipibo *iká, aká* done + *-ma* not] : no –Used as *ikáma* or *akáma*, a negative answer to a question with an *intransitive* or *transitive* verb respectively. ⟨**– ¿Miaki óxai? –Ikáma.** –Are you sleeping? –No.⟩ ⟨**– ¿Minki piá? –Akáma.** –Have you eaten? –No.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5 *syn.* —ma; -yama
*n.* **ikáranin** : healing song ⟨**Ikáraninronki yoshinbo chitíakanai.** They say that with *ikára* songs, they make the demons retreat.⟩

*adv.* **ixónbi** [from Shipibo *ikáx, ixón*, subordinate forms of *íti* (root *ik-*) to be + *-bi* although] : *nonetheless* : however ⟨**Moa xobón nokóxon non piá iki. Ikáxbi, non yóra yósmares iká iki.** When we arrived home, we ate; however, our bodies remained weak.⟩ ⟨**Káxiboainoa ábionbora moa masáti keyóke. Ixónbira, nato simánanin moa bénxoaribakanai.** All the small planes in Cashibococha have broken down; however, this week they are going to repair them.⟩

*n.* **ikín** 1 : animal fleas ⟨**Ochíti ikin piára nokon tita nonbéke.** My mother got boils from the bites of the dog's fleas.⟩ 2 : bird lice ⟨**Nato átapara íkia iki; báke patáxmayamakanwe.** This hen has lice; don't let it get near the baby.⟩ 3 : a species of ant that lives in a tree; *also* : an ant of the *íki* species ⟨**Westíora jónira íki paíkiax pábeke.** A certain man went deaf because an *íki* ant got into his ear.⟩

*adv.* **akín** [from Shipibo *ikí, akín,* subordinate-verb suf. of *áti* to do and *íti* to be, to do] : yes –Used in the forms *ikí* and *akín* in affirmative answers to questions with intransitive and transitive verbs, respectively. *syn.* See under **énjen** ⟨**—¿Moaki máwata? —Ikí.** —Has he died already? —Yes.⟩ ⟨**—¿Minki óina? —Akín.** —Have you seen it? —Yes.⟩ –Used as the first word in a direct quotation. ⟨**Játian báke: —¡Ea bíiwe; ea bíiwe, koká! —iki iká iki.** Come take me; come take me, uncle —he said.⟩ *syn.* See under **énjen**
*n.* **íkirisianin** [from Spanish; which comes from Latin *ekklesia*; from Greek; from *ek-* out + *kálein,* *klet-* to call + *-sia,* nominal suf.] : church *syn.* jaín Ríos rábiti xóbo
*n.* : Iquitos ⟨**Ikítoainxonra nokon ánibaon ea ániaa iki.** My parents raised me in Iquitos.⟩
*also* **ígobimi** *n.* **íkobimin** *also* **ígobimin** [from Spanish *higo* fig + Shipibo *bími* fruit] : fig
*also* **ígojiwi** *n.* **íkojiwin** *also* **ígojiwin** [from Spanish *higo* fig + Shipibo *jíwi* tree] : fig tree

*adj. & n.* **ikoman** [from Shipibo *íti, ik-* to be + *-kon* true] *adj.* : true : reliable ⟨**Nokon jói ikón íketianra ítiki min báke jawen isín bénxoi –akinra yóbekan tita áke.** If my word is true, your child will get well —the shaman told mom.⟩ *n.* : truth ⟨**– ¿Ikónrin? –Ikónra en mia yóiai.** –Is it true? –I'm telling you the truth.⟩ *syn.* -kon

*v.t.* **ikónhaa** *Konibo* **ikónhaka** 1 : to believe (someone) ⟨**Nokon báke bénxoti yóbekan yóiketianra en ikónhake –ikira tita íke.** I believed the shaman when he said my child would recover —mom said.⟩ 2 : to believe in (e.g., God)

[from Shipibo *Ríosen Jói* Word of God, Bible + *ikónhati* to believe] : to convert to the Gospel : to become a Christian –Used in this sense among Christian believers. ⟨**Westíora benchénra Kakónkoxon Ríosen Jói ikónhake.** There is a blind man in Caco who converted to the Gospel.⟩
*adv.* **inkónhakin** [from Shipibo *ikón* true + *–i*, verbal-complement suf.] : truly ⟨**Ikoni kéenaxa mia sontáro káti iki.** You can go into military service if you truly want to.⟩

*v.t.* **íkota** 1 : to hug ⟨**Rímameax nokóxonbira papán títa ikóyamake, non axé jáskarama íketian.** Dad arrived from Lima, but he didn't hug mom because that's not our custom.⟩ 2 : to take (a child) in one's arms ⟨**Pápashokonra jawen bábabo ikóke, moa manuáti ochóma ixon.** The grandfather took his grandchildren in his arms as a farewell, because death was already near.⟩
*n.* **Imán** [from Spanish *Ema*] –Used as a female name.
*v.t.* **ímaa** [from Shipibo *ti* to be + *-ma* to make] : to make : to cause to reach (an indicated position or state) ⟨**Kóshira íma-kanke.** They made him chief.⟩
*adj.* **ínmesen** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple, at the edge + *metsá* beautiful] 1 : with beautiful temples 2 : with beautiful eaves 3 : with beautiful edges –Used regarding a canoe.
*n.* **Imikan** [from Spanish *Emilia*] –Used as a female name.
*v.i.* **ímoshiita** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *móshiti* to suffer a blow] : to receive a strong blow to the temple
*v.t.* **ínmosha** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *móshati* to give a blow] : to strike (someone) hard on the temple
*v.i.* **impania** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *pániti* to hang] 1 : to hang from the temple 2 : to hang from the edge (e.g., of a cushma or a canoe)
*n.* **impéitin** : temple (of the head) –Used mostly among speakers of the Konibo dialect. ⟨**Epara jawen impéitiki jiwín ríshkikanke.** They hit my paternal uncle on the temple with a stick.⟩
*v.i.* **impekeeta** : to get a hole in one's temple
*v.t.* **ímpeta** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *pékati* to hollow out] : to make a hole in (someone else's) temple
*v.t.* **impisha** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *píshati* to unhook] : to remove the house frame at the level of the wall plates
*v.i.* **ímpota** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *po,* unidentified element + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to cover one's temples with sideburns

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *impéiti* temple] 1 : at the temple : to the temple : from the temple ⟨**inchán** horns growing from the temples⟩ 2 : at the cheek : to the cheek : from the cheek ⟨**intóti** to apply dots of achiote to the cheeks⟩ 3 : on the side : to the side : from the side : along the side ⟨**insénti** to open (an animal) along the side⟩ 4 : at the level of, or from the level of, the wall plates or eaves of a house ⟨**impíshti** to remove (a house frame) at the level of the wall plates⟩ 5 : at the edge, from the edge, or on the edge (e.g., of a canoe, a table, a pot, a cushma, a shirt, or a blouse) ⟨**incháxti** to carve the edge of (a canoe)⟩ 6 : on the side (lateral part) of a fish ⟨**ísketi** for (the spines) to break on the side of a fish⟩

*n.* **inakan** 1 : the young of a domestic animal or fowl ⟨**Báwa inara bakén réteke.** A child killed the domesticated young of a parrot.⟩ 2 : wild Indian ⟨**Westíora sánitaríora inábaon yatánxon bími xéamayantanke.** A health worker was captured by wild Indians and they made him swallow a fruit.⟩

*verbal suf.* **–inat** : going up; *specif.* : going upstream –Used regarding the action of poling upstream or of getting up. –Used with the letter *h* prefixed if the verb root ends in the letter *n*. –Used in the form *–ina* or *–hina* before a final suffix with an initial consonant, and *–inat* or *–hinat* before a final suffix with an initial vowel. ⟨**Jáinoaxa noa jojóinake, jawébi wínotama.** From there we came upstream without incident.⟩ ⟨**jojóinatai** is coming upstream⟩

*v.t.* **ináa** *Konibo* **ináaka** 1 : to raise (small wild animals or birds) 2 : to capture (a wild person) ⟨**Káshibo ináakanaronki ishtón ráeyamakatitai.** They say that in past times, captured Cashibo were slow to become tame.⟩

*v.t.* **inana** : to obtain or hand something to another person ⟨**Min ea asókaro méniketianra énbiribi mia táshi inánti iki.** If you give me sugar, I'll hand you salt.⟩ ⟨**Maístoronra ea jakónhira kírika inán-** **ke.** The teacher got me a very good book.⟩
*n.* **inárion** [from Spanish] : hymnal

*v.i.* **ínata** : to pole upstream : to go upstream ⟨**Moátianra westíora pápashoko ínataitian kétokan máponike.** Long ago, while a certain grandfather was poling upstream, he was buried when the riverbank collapsed into the river.⟩
*v.t.* **ínbena** [from Shipibo *in–* at the temple + *bénati* to search] : to search for lice at the temples
*v.t.* **ínbesa** [from Shipibo *in–* at the edge + *betséti* to extend all over] : to finish (e.g., a canoe) along the edge
*adj.* **inchaman** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *chánko* protuberance] : with horns growing from the temples
*v.t.* **inchásha** : to carve (e.g., a canoe) along the edge
*v.i.* **inchokiita** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *chokíti* to wash oneself] : to wash one's temple
*v.i.* **inchoshiita** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *choshíti* to get hit] : to receive a blow to the temple
*v.t.* **ínchosha** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *chóshati* to break by striking] : to strike (someone) on the temple
*v.t.* **ínchota** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *chókiti* to wash] : to wash (someone's) temple
See **Inria**
*v.t.* **ínexa** [from Shipibo *in-* at the edge + *néxati* to tie] : to tie (a canoe) at the edge

*also* **ínibake** *n.* **inín** *also* **ínibaken** 1 : niece : a woman's sister's daughter –Used in the form *ínibake* to express affection. –The vocative form *chimín* "girl" is used to address the person referred to. ⟨**Moátianronki aínbo jawen íni betanbi inón bínike, károai kabékonketian.** They say that in ancient times a jaguar attacked a woman and her niece when they had gone to cut firewood.⟩ 2 : a woman's stepdaughter ⟨**Titara jawen íni betan káchio káke manánxawe bénai; kaxónra wísoino mérakanke.** The mother went to the forest with her stepdaughter, and they saw a black panther.⟩ *syn.* See under **kókobake**

*n.* **iníchintin** [from Shipibo *in-* at the edge + *níchinti* something to fasten with] : minor forked post ⟨**Xóbo inichintiki jawen awín néxaxonra jonín ríshkike.** A man tied his wife to a small forked post of the house and whipped her.⟩ *syn.* witá
*adj.* **íniman** : fragrant ⟨**Cháikoni jónibaon tárironki inín íki.** They say the cushmas of the wild demons, the *cháikoni*, are fragrant.⟩
*v.t.* **inínhaa** *Konibo* **inínhaka** : to perfume ⟨**Titánra papán tári inínhaxonai.** Mom puts perfume on dad's cushma.⟩
See under **níshi**
*v.i.* **ínina** : to perfume oneself ⟨**Pishtánko ránsai kanóxa nato aínbo inínke.** This woman perfumed herself to go dance at the party.⟩
*n.* **ínjiniron** [from Spanish] : engineer

*n.* **inkan** [from Quechua *inka*] : Inca –Used in this sense with a capital *I*. ⟨**Non Inka jáketianronki noa jawékiati onánbo íkeanke.** If our Inca were present, we would be experts at making anything.⟩
[from Quechua *kori* gold + *inka* Inca] : an as-yet unidentified Inca

[from Shipibo *chéxe* dark, ebony + *inka* Inca] : Dark Inca : an Inca described as dark-skinned, associated with the Yuruá River in Brazil ⟨**Ja Chéxeinkaronki wíso jóni ikátiai.** They say the Dark Inca was a black man.⟩ ⟨**Chéxeinkanronki jato mashínti onámaa iki, onáyamakenbi.** They say the Dark Inca made red earth known to his people when they had not yet known it.⟩
[from Quechua *inka* Inca + Spanish *rubio* blond] : Blond Inca ⟨**Inkarobioronki joné Inka iki.** They say the Blond Inca is a hidden Inca.⟩

*n.* **ísón ewan** [from Shipibo *íso, ísón* spider monkey (maquisapa) + *-ewa,* augmentative suf.] : a giant mythical monkey ⟨**Isón** **ewanronki kámpa ainbo bónike.** They say that long ago an *isón ehua* monkey carried off a campa (Asháninka) woman.⟩

*n.* [from Shipibo *íso, isón* spider monkey (maquisapa) + *títa* mother] : apasahua (a mythical monkey-spirit) ⟨**Westíora bákebenboronki isóntitan boá iki.** They say an apasahua carried off a boy.⟩
*n.* **isónxanhexen** [from Shipibo *íso, isón* spider monkey (maquisapa) + *xanhex* hernia] : a type of vine

*n.* **isónxoman** [from Shipibo *íso, isón* spider monkey (maquisapa) + *xóma* breast] 1 : sapote ; *also* : fruit of the sapote tree ⟨**Isónxoma kókaitianra papán sókota shíno réteke.** My father killed six monkeys while they were eating sapote.⟩
[from Shipibo *níi* monte (forest, wild) + *isónxoma* sapote] : a type of small-fruited sapote

*n.* **isónyonkeman** [from Shipibo *íso, isón* spider monkey (maquisapa) + *yonken*, unidentified element] : a type of tree with a long, straight trunk, leaves like those of the avocado tree, and large fruit

See under **róno**
