See under **wáiti**

*n.* **ísoxetan** [from Shipibo *íso* spider monkey (maquisapa) + *xéta* tooth] : a type of bracelet made of cotton and spider-monkey teeth ⟨**Nato chipónkiax joá aínbora ísoxeta sawéya iki.** This woman who has come from downriver is wearing bracelets of spider-monkey teeth on her arms.⟩
*also* **Espánya** *n.* **Ispányanin** *also* **Espanyanin** [from Spanish; and this from Latin *Hispania*] : Spain

*adj.* **ispányoron** [from Spanish] : Spanish ⟨**Jakóma íketianronki jawen jónibaonbi jaton pátoron ispányoro joni rétekanike.** They say that long ago the workers killed their Spanish boss because he was bad.⟩

*n.* **ispáranin** [from Spanish] : sword ⟨**Rónoyainxonra westíora jóni ispáraya mérakanke; méraxonra pishtáko shinankanai.** In Runuya they saw a certain man with a sword; seeing him, they think he is a pishtaco (a legendary fat-stealing killer).⟩

*n.* **ispín** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *spi*, unidentified element] 1 : side of the head ⟨**Jónira mawáke, jawen mápo ispínko jakómakin xátekana.** A man died because they operated badly on the side of his head.⟩ 2 : side (of the body) ⟨**Nokon ispínra en báke chákake.** I bumped into the child with my side.⟩ *syn.* pishpachi

*n.* **ispín** [from Shipibo *in-* at the side + *spi*, unidentified element] : spine on the upper part of a fish's pectoral fin, or on the front of its dorsal fin ⟨**San Rantsískoainoa korákara tonón ispi métasaake.** The curaca (community leader) of San Francisco stuck a cunchi (a type of catfish) spine into his hand.⟩

*n.* **ispíkon** *Konibo* **ispíkonin** [from Spanish] : mirror ⟨**Páeribaonronki non ánibo ispíko ménixonki jato ráeanike.** They say the friars tamed our ancestors by giving them mirrors.⟩ ⟨**Ispiko barín ténaara bíriai.** The mirror glints with the sun's rays.⟩

*n.* **ispiman** [from Shipibo *in-* at the side + *spin*, unidentified element] : lateral spine of a fish ⟨**Chichínwitax ispinronki kikín móka iki.** They say that if the shiripira (a type of catfish) stings us with its lateral spine, it hurts a lot.⟩
*n.* **ispíntanon** : espintana (a type of tree) ⟨**Papánra ispíntano bíke ja xóboanoxon.** My father got espintana wood to use in building the house.⟩
*n.* **istín** [from Spanish] : east *syn.* bári píkotai
*also* **estrófa** *n.* **ístirojan** *also* **éstrofan** : verse (of a song) ⟨**Bewá riki jawen kóroya jaínoax jawen rabé ístirojaya.** The hymn has a chorus and two verses.⟩

*conj.* [from Shipibo *íti, ik-* + *-tan*, going and returning] : and ⟨**Nokon pápayosin kéni riki jóxo itan kebóx.** My grandfather's beard is white and streaked with gray.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.7.1 *syn.* See under **betan**
*n.* **itántantan** [from Shipibo *itántanta*, imitative of its call] : a type of demon that lives in hollow logs
*n.* **Itárian** : Italy
*adj.* **itáshon** *Konibo* **itáshonin** [from Spanish] : Italian ⟨**Westíora itáshojonira Puerto Kayáoainxon náshiaitian jenén réteke.** A certain Italian drowned while swimming in Puerto Callao.⟩

*v.i.* **iká** 1 : to be –Used in the form *iqui*, or, prefixed, *riqui*, present tense, or *íke* or *iká iqui*, past tense, in the indicative mood. ⟨**Nátora nokon pápa iki.** This is my father.⟩ ⟨**Pítira jakón iká iki.** The food was good.⟩ ⟨**En winókin óinara nokon pápa jaín íke jawen jabé ráenanaibobetan.** In passing, I saw that my father was there with his friends.⟩ ⟨**Jawen chópara néno iki.** His clothes are here.⟩ 2 : to happen : to occur –Used with an indirect object. ⟨**–¿Jáskaraboki mia iká? –Jáskarabora ea íke.** –Did such things happen to you? –Those things happened to me.⟩ –Used in the form *iqui* with the past participle to indicate narration of a completed action. ⟨**Moátianronki Yoashi Inka rétekana iki. Réteaxki westíora jóni jawen xenín síkita iki.** They say that long ago they killed Inca Mezquino (the Stingy Inca, a legendary figure) and that a man painted himself with his fat.⟩ –Used as an auxiliary in the form *íke* with the subordinate verb form in *-i*, in a compound verb expressing a just-completed action. ⟨**Eara moa íke téeti séneni.** I have already finished working.⟩ –Used as an auxiliary in the form *íke* with a past participle, in a compound verb expressing a previously completed action. ⟨**Epán nóntira moa jankénhaa íke.** Uncle's canoe was already finished.⟩ –Used in the form *icai*, present, or *íke* or *iká iqui*, past, sometimes with the subordinate form *ikí* added, all with the meaning "to say," to introduce a quotation. ⟨**Játian Títo: –¡Jéje, kawé! –ikí iká iki.** Then Tito said to him: –Fine; see you later.⟩ –Used in the form *itai* with the verbal complement in *-i* to produce the compound form of the definite present tense. ⟨**Eara kaí itai.** I am going right now.⟩ –Used in the forms *ikénbi* and *iquetian* in mathematical operations. ⟨**8 ikénbira 4 bíchinai bánetai 4.** 8 minus 4 equals 4.⟩ ⟨**21 íketian, 3 tsamá akára páketai 7.** 21 divided by 3 equals 7.⟩ 3 : to equal –Used in the form *iqui* in addition. ⟨**3 jáinoax 1 iki 4.** 3 plus 1 equals 4.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.4.3 *syn.* See under **báneti** *syn.* áti; wínoti; -rin
[from Shipibo *áni* big + *íti* to be] : to be a certain age; *also* : to be a certain size ⟨**Ea játio áni iketianra, nokon pápashoko máwata iki.** When I was that age, my grandfather died.⟩

*n.* **itín** [from Shipibo *íti, i-* to be + *-ti* with what] : residence : dwelling ⟨**Nénora nokon ítima iki; ea mératí jóresa riki —akinra chaín jawen épa áke.** My brother-in-law said to his uncle: 'This is not my home; I have only come to visit.'⟩

*suf.* *v.i.* **-ika** [from Shipibo *íti* to be] –Used with the meaning "to do" and added to a word or onomatopoeic element indicating what is done with a more or less loud sound. ⟨**saí íti** to shout⟩
*adj.* **ítimaton** [from Shipibo *íti* to be + *-ma* not] : that which should not be : contrary to proper custom

*adj.* **itsán** : having a strong odor –Used, e.g., regarding the *underarm* of the sajino (collared peccary), used shirts or blouses that have not been changed for several days, garlic, wild garlic (sacha ajo), burnt rice, or other burnt substances. ⟨**Nato jónira ítsayora iki; náshiosmara íbirai.** This man gives off a very strong smell; maybe he never bathes.⟩
*n.* **ítsoman** : bombonaje (a palm used for weaving) *syn.* bóme

*adj. & n.* **iwén** *adj.* : heavy ⟨**Nokon pátoronin káocho pápiti yóiabira en béyamake, íwe íketian.** My boss ordered me to load and bring the rubber, but I didn't bring it because it was very heavy.⟩ *n.* : weight ⟨**Jawen íwe iká iki pácha kíro.** Its weight was about one hundred kilos.⟩
*v.t.* **íweaa** *Konibo* **íweaka** : to make heavy ⟨**Ichayora jónibo nanéxonra, moa nónti íweake.** Too many people boarded, and they made the canoe heavy.⟩
*v.i.* **íwea** : to become heavy ⟨**Oín mecháara nato bórosa moa íweke.** This bag became heavy because the rain got it wet.⟩
*v.t.* **íwea** : to bring (a person) ⟨**Jokáshamainbira en méereskin íweke.** She didn't want to come, but I brought her by pleading.⟩

*n.* **íwín** 1 : stingray ⟨**Iwínronki ketó bímai.** They say that stingrays cause the riverbank to erode.⟩ 2 : a constellation called "The Ray," formed by part of Sagittarius –Used in this sense written with a capital initial letter.
[from Shipibo *obán* pashaca (a spiny catfish) + *íwi* stingray] : a species of stingray with spines like those of the pashaca
*n.* **íwín** : spindle ⟨**Jonínra íwiati áti-panyamake, jawen rayósainbaon áti yóiabi.** The man could not make a spindle even though his mother-in-law asked him to make one.⟩
See under **bína**
*n.* **íwichiexen** [from Shipibo *íwi* spindle + *chi-* at the tip + *jéxe* sphere] : clay whorl on the spindle
*n.* **íwikanin** : sapo cunchi (a type of toad) –Used mostly among speakers of the Pisqui dialect.

*also* **íwín ewa** *n.* **iwíntitan** *also* **íwín ewan** [from Shipibo *íwi, íwín* stingray + *títa* mother] : a species of large stingray ⟨**Iwíntitanronki ketó bímai.** They say that the *íwíntita* stingray causes the riverbank to erode.⟩
*adj.* **íxmén** [from Shipibo *in-* at the temple + *xénkti, xkine-* to shell/shed grains] : bald at the temples
*n.* **íxnekan** : a type of thorny vine with tiny leaves that spreads over trees and other plants and has no use
See under **móxa**

*adj. and pron.* **jan** *adj.* 1 : that ⟨**Ja jónira ikónbires jánso itan siná iki.** That man is a big liar and very quick-tempered.⟩ *pron.* : he : she : that one ⟨**Ja riki chipónkiax jóai non ninkápachoai.** He is the one we always heard was going to come from downriver.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbora jakóma shinánya iki; jara wétsa jóni betan jabáke.** This woman is very bad; she ran off with another man.⟩ *syn.* JA, NATO, OA can all be translated as "that"; however, in its primary sense NATO is translated as "this" and JA as "he" or "she". Thus OA "that" is normally opposed to NATO "this", and is always opposed to NATO when OA indicates the farther of two locations. JA, although it can be translated as "that", is not normally opposed to NATO "this". See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.3; 7.1.6; 7.2.1; 7.2.3; 7.2.4
*adv.* : once
*n.* **Jabán** –Used as a masculine name.

*v.i.* **jabákina** [from Shipibo *jabáti* to flee + *-akin* accompanying] : to flee taking (someone) along ⟨**Nato jonínra aínbo jabákinti shínanai.** This man is thinking of running off with a woman.⟩

*v.i.* **jábata** 1 : to flee : to withdraw : to take off ⟨**Yaméra yómetso jabáwanke motóronin yómetsoax.** Last night a thief stole the motor (outboard motorboat) and fled.⟩ ⟨**Nokon wáatanin amén inara jabáke, risbí tésaax.** The capybara that my maternal aunt raised ran off, breaking the rope it was tied with.⟩ 2 : to come loose (canoe) ⟨**Yamé pochinikonra nokon nónti jabáke, jatíbi jawékia.** At midnight my canoe came loose, with everything loaded in it.⟩ ⟨**Nato nónti jábatara Orobampamea iki.** This loose canoe comes from the Urubamba River.⟩ 3 : to escape (a person) ⟨**Yómetso chibánkanabira jabákin moa jato potake.** They followed the thief; but he escaped, leaving them behind.⟩ *syn.* JABATI, KISHPIMEETI can both be translated as "to escape"; but while JABATI refers to the escape of a person being pursued, KISHPIMEETI generally implies any danger from which one escapes.
*adj.* **jabénanen** [from Shipibo *ja* he/she + *-be* with + *náneti, nane-* to embark/be born] : born of the same mother
*conj.* [from Shipibo *ja* that + *-bi* even] : but ⟨**Jábira áke en átima yóiabi.** But even so, he did it, even though I had forbidden it.⟩

*pron. and adj.* **jábichonin** [from Shipibo *ja* he, she + *-bicho* only] *pron.* : one : only one ⟨**Noa játikaxbi tééti békanaitianra wétsa jábicho bánetai, yoá akí.** While all of us go to work, one person stays behind to cook.⟩ *adj.* : only him or her ⟨**Tínintira Rimán káke; jánbichoresa náto jéma akínkasai.** The lieutenant governor has gone to Lima; only he wants to help the town.⟩ *syn.* See under **westíora**

*Konibo* **janbísati** *v.t.* **jabísaa** *Konibo* **janbísaka** 1 : to disperse ⟨**Béwatiain weíkankenbira koáratianin jato janbísake.** Although they had entered the church service, a guard dispersed them.⟩ 2 : to scatter ⟨**Yómetsoninra koríki janbísake.** The thief scattered the money.⟩ 3 : to dissolve ⟨**Titánra jawen átsaxeatinin asókaro nepóxon janbísake.** Mother dissolved the sugar by putting it in the manioc drink.⟩

*Konibo* **janbísti** *v.i.* **jábisa** *Konibo* **jánbisa** 1 : to scatter (people or a mass) ⟨**Jónibora moa janbíske, chámi jaton jemánko moa nokóketian.** The people scattered because smallpox had reached the community.⟩ ⟨**Xéatiki xéni máanara moa janbíske.** The fat that fell into the drink spread out.⟩ 2 : to spread out : to disperse ⟨**Niwén akára máshi janbíske; ja mashínra báke bépoke.** The sand scattered in the wind, and got into a child's eyes.⟩ 3 : to become fluffy : to swell up ⟨**Titán waxmén barínhaara janbíske.** The cotton that mother sunned became fluffy.⟩ 4 : to dissolve
See **játo**
*Konibo* **janbón** *n.* **jáboman** *Konibo* **jánboman** [from Spanish] : soap ⟨**Janbón piáxa wáka mawáke.** A cow died after eating soap.⟩
*Konibo* **janbón** *n.* **jáboman** *Konibo* **jánboman** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *bobón, bonbón* boils] : boils on the tongue
See under **áti**
*also* **jachomá** *n.* –Used as a vocative form to call the spider monkey (maquisapa).
*adv.* [from Shipibo *jaín* there + *-ma* not + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : very slowly ⟨**Jaímashoko ea yóiwe.** Tell it to me very slowly.⟩
*adv.* : there : over there ⟨**Jaín íketian, ishtón jonón kénawe.** If he is there, call him to come quickly.⟩ *syn.* jáinoa; óno
See under **xóbo**
*adv.* : there : from there –Used with a transitive main verb to indicate the location of the object. ⟨**Jáinoara non wapóro nókoa iki.** There we found a steamship.⟩ *syn.* jaín

*adv. and conj.* **jaínxon** [from Shipibo *jaín* there + *-oa*, suf. of origin + *-ax, -xon*, subordinate-verb suf.] *adv.* 1 : from there –Used to indicate the origin of the subject. ⟨**Jáinoaxa joá iki jawen pátoron.** His boss came from there.⟩ ⟨**Jaínxonra min sotánti iki.** From there you are going to spy on him.⟩ 2 : then –Used at the beginning of a sentence to indicate a temporal relation to a previous sentence. ⟨**Káchio káketianra jóni inábaon yátana iki. Jáinoax ja jóni saíika iki.** A man who went to the monte (forest) was captured by savages. Then the man screamed.⟩ ⟨**¿Miaki jáweranoax joá?** –**akin akára jaínxon en yóia iki.** 'Where have you come from?' —he asked, and then I answered him.⟩ *conj.* : and –Used before the final item in a series of coordinated words (e.g., nouns). ⟨**Jóno bíchi, yáwa bichi, jáinoax westíora íno bichi, jabo boí, ea iká riki.** That happened to me when I was carrying hides of collared peccary, white-lipped peccary, and a jaguar hide.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5 *syn.* See under **betan** and **jaskáketian**
*n.* **jain póitinin** [from Shipibo *jaín* there + *póiti, poi-* to defecate + *-ti* with what] : restroom : bathroom
See under **xóbo**

*also* **ínojaka** *n.* **jakán** *also* **ínojakan** [from Shipibo *íno* jaguar (tigre) + *jáka*, imitative of its call] : tiger-heron (pumagarza) ⟨**Yáminawabaonronki jáka píamai, kópinaketian.** They say that the Yaminahua do not eat tiger-heron, because they fear being cutipados (afflicted by its harmful spell-like effect).⟩
[from Shipibo *chikíx*, imitative of its call + *jáka* tiger-heron (pumagarza)] : a type of tiger-heron

*adv.* : afterward again ⟨**Nato báritiabichora ea néno íkai téeti; jáinoaxa moa ea jákiribi nokon jemánko kái.** This year only, I am going to work here; afterward I will go back to my community again.⟩

*adj.* : bad ⟨**Nato aínbora jakóma shinánya iki; jara wétsa jóni betan jabáke.** This woman is very bad; she ran off with another man.⟩ *syn.* JAKOMA, MECHO, RAMI, YOITIMA, -KOMA are all translated as "bad". JAKOMA and RAMI vary only regionally; JAKOMA is used more among speakers of the Upper Ucayali, while RAMI is used more by those of the Lower Ucayali. MECHO is also translated as "ugly" and, like JAKOMA, is used mostly among the Konibo. YOITIMA implies an extreme of badness. -KOMA can have the sense of JAKOMA and also the sense of "difficult" or "impossible".
[from Shipibo *jakóma* bad + *-bires* only + *shinánti* to think] : to gossip : to think ill (e.g., of a person)
See under **jakóma**
See under **namáti**
See under **shinán**
*v.t.* **jakómaa** [from Shipibo *jakóma* bad + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to curse *syn.* *rámiati*
*adj.* **jakómayoran** [from Shipibo *jakóma* bad + *-yora* very] : unpleasant

*adj.* **jákoman** 1 : good ⟨**Chéxeinkaronki jakón jóni ikátiai; játian jatíribibo jáskarama.** They say the Inca Prieto (the Dark Inca, a legendary figure) was a good person, while others say he was not.⟩ 2 : pleasant *syn.* -kon
*v.t.* **jakónhaa** *Konibo* **jakónhaka** : to treat well ⟨**Nato aínbaonra ea jakónhake.** This woman treated me well.⟩

*adv.* **jakónhakin** : well ⟨**Jákoni jáinbi niwé —akin titán akábira jawen báke maín rakáke.** Even though the mother told him: 'Stand up properly!' her son threw himself on the ground.⟩ ⟨**Nokon báke min jakónhakin koíranaitianra en mia kopíati iki.** If you take good care of my little child, I will pay you.⟩ *syn.* -kon
*adv.* **jakónresakin** [from Shipibo *jákoni* well + *-res* only] : fortunately ⟨**Jakónresi noa réokootainkora benés iantanke.** Fortunately, where we capsized wasn't very deep.⟩
See under **shinán**
*adj.* **jakónshokon** [from Shipibo *jakón* + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : pretty *syn.* JAKONSHOKO, METSA, METSASHOKO, TSIRI can all be translated as "pretty" with no difference in meaning.
*v.i.* : to feel better ⟨**Róokoya jóni nokon xóbomeax pikóketianra ea jakónke.** When a man with whooping cough left my house, I felt better.⟩
See under **níti**
*adv.* : for that reason : that's why ⟨**Nato jonínra nokon machíto ea sékenaanke; jákopira en moa bómayamai.** This man broke my machete, and that's why I no longer let him borrow it.⟩
*n.* **jámakan** : footprint : track ⟨**Káshibaonronki awá réteai, jawen jamá tánaxon.** They say the Cashibo kill the tapir by following its tracks.⟩
*n.* **jamámatin** [from Shipibo *jamáti* to step on + *-ma* to cause + *-ti* with what] : scissors ⟨**Kokámen xóbora jamámatioma iki.** The Cocama house has no scissors.⟩

*v.t.* **jámata** 1 : to step on ⟨**En róno jámatabira ea natéshamake.** Although I stepped on a snake, it didn't bite me.⟩ 2 : to kick ⟨**Piróta jamáketianra jawen báke ésteke.** Her little son's belly swelled up because he kicked a ball that was cutipada (afflicted with a harmful spell-like effect).⟩
*v.t.* **jámita** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *mi-* small ball of food + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to put food or seasoning on the tongue or in the mouth of *syn.* See under **jampóti**
*v.t.* **jámosha** [from Shipibo *jan-* in the mouth + *móshi* brittle + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to break (e.g., an animal) through the mouth
*v.i.* **jámota** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *mókati* to become sour or bitter] : to feel sourness, bitterness, or a stinging sensation in the mouth

*v.t.* **jámpasa** 1 : to hit on the tongue 2 : to throw (something thick) into the mouth of ⟨**Pápa óshaketianra báke yóitiman átsasheati jampáske.** While father was sleeping, a naughty child threw manioc masato (a fermented drink) into his mouth.⟩

*v.t.* **jámpeta** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *pékati* to hollow out] 1 : to hollow out the tongue of (e.g., an animal) 2 : to irritate or infect (of acidic fruits) the tongue of ⟨**Kankámanra ea jampéke.** The pineapple irritated my tongue.⟩
*adj.* **jámpisin** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *písi* stench] : having bad breath
*v.t.* **jámpisha** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *píshati* to unhook] : to remove a hook from the mouth of (a fish)
*n.* **jámpononin** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *póno* tendon] : frenulum of the tongue

*v.t.* **jámpota** [from Shipibo *jan-* in the mouth + *pótati* to throw] : to throw (a handful of something specific) into the mouth of ⟨**Asókaro jampókaskinra táshires en pápa jampóke.** I put salt in father's mouth when I meant to put in a handful of sugar.⟩ *syn.* JAMPOTI, JAMITI both have the meaning "to put a substance into someone else's mouth"; except that JAMPOTI implies throwing something in from some distance, while JAMITI has the meaning of putting something into the mouth up close, touching it with the hand.

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *jána* tongue] 1 : on the tongue : to the tongue : of the tongue 2 : in the mouth : to the mouth : of the mouth ⟨**jampóti** to throw (a handful of something specific) into the mouth of⟩ 3 : in the voice : to the voice : of the voice ⟨**jankósh** loud-voiced⟩ 4 : at the open mouth of (e.g., a sack, a can, or a pot) ⟨**janchínti** to tilt the open mouth of a can toward.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*n.* **janán** : tongue ⟨**Ronín jánaronki chíibires iki.** They say the tongue of the yacumama (a mythical water-boa) is pure fire.⟩

*n.* **jánakan** *also* **jánakanin** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : manacaraco (a type of bird) ⟨**Jéne benónronki jánaka kéotai.** They say that when the manacaraco sings, it signals that the river will rise.⟩

*n.* **jánatapoman** [from Shipibo *jána* tongue + *tapón* root] : an not-exactly-identified part of the tongue ⟨**Nato bákera jóikoma iki, jánataponhoma ikax.** This child doesn't speak well because he lacks the *jánatapon* part of the tongue.⟩

*v.t.* **jánaa** 1 : to return to its place : to put back in place ⟨**Bestéti bexónbira en jaínribi moa jánake jawen íbo yóashiaitian.** I brought the scissors, and on purpose I put them back in their place because their owner doesn't want to lend them.⟩ 2 : to keep (leftover food)

*Konibo* **jánchikiiti** *v.i.* **jánchikoota** *Konibo* **jánchikiita** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *chikóti* to spill (+ *-ii*, reflexive suf. in the Konibo variants)] : to spill (something) on one's own tongue : to pour onto one's own tongue

*v.i.* **jánchita** : for the mouth of (e.g., a can) to tilt toward one

*n.* **janén** 1 : name ⟨**Jáneoma íketianra nato báke rókotoron jáne ménike.** Since this child had no name, the doctor gave him one.⟩ 2 : noun –Used as a grammatical term. See Grammar Sketch 7.1

*n.* **jánekonin** [from Shipibo *jáne* name + *-kon* true] : a Shipibo or Konibo person's proper name in their own language : name in Shipibo or Konibo –Used regarding the proper name that the person does not mention themselves, by traditional custom. ⟨**Nokon jánekon riki Senénkopi.** My name in Konibo is Senénkopi.⟩
*n.* **janén janetitianbi janen** [from Shipibo *jáne, janén* name + *-tian* when + *-bi* although] : pronoun. See Grammar Sketch 7.2
*v.t.* **jánena** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *néneti* to feel a burning sensation] : to feel a burning sensation on the tongue

*n.* **jánetekikan** [from Shipibo *jáne* name + *tekí* joint] : surname ⟨**Nokon jánetekira en onányamake, ea báketianbi nokon ánibo moa máwata iketian.** I don't know my surname, because my parents died when I was a little child.⟩ *syn.* ápichiro

*v.t.* **jánea** 1 : to name ⟨**Nokon papánra jawen wetsán janén ea jáneke.** My father gave me the name of his brother.⟩ 2 : to mention by name ⟨**Non máwatabo jáneketianra noa yamé kékeati iki.** If we mention a dead person by name, we will have nightmares at night.⟩

*v.i.* **jáneta** : to give oneself a name ⟨**Nato náwaaainbora nokon wetsán janén janéke, jakónira jáne íketian.** This mestiza woman took my sister's name for herself, because she thought it was pretty.⟩

*n.* **jániman** 1 : tangarana (a tree that hosts biting ants) : palo santo ⟨**Moátianronki joninki jawen awín janínki néxaxon, jawen *ibo* rétemanike.** They say that long ago a man tied his wife to a tangarana tree and let the ants sting her to death.⟩ 2 : tangarana ants : the ants that infest the tangarana tree ⟨**Westíora bákeronki jániman tékaxon rétenike.** They say a certain child died from the stings of the tangarana ants.⟩
*v.t.* **jánia** [from Shipibo *jan-* in the mouth + *níati* to insert] : to put in the mouth of

*v.t.* **jankénhaa** *Konibo* **jankénhaka** 1 : to finish –Used with the complement of a verb ending in *-quin*. ⟨**Moara wái órokin jankénhake.** He already finished planting the field.⟩ 2 : to finish making (a solid thing) –Used with a noun functioning as the direct object. ⟨**Moara xóbo jankénhake.** He already finished building the house.⟩ 3 : to finish (work) –Used with *tée* "work" as the object. ⟨**Moara jawen tée jankénhake.** He already finished his work.⟩ *syn.* JANKENHATI, SENENHATI can both be translated as "to finish"; while JANKENHATI implies a task, SENENHATI can imply other activities in general that are finished (e.g., eating).

*v.i.* **jánkena** : to be finished ⟨**Moara xóbo jankénke.** The house is already finished.⟩ *syn.* JANKENTI, SENENTI can both be translated as "to be finished"; while JANKENTI implies a concrete thing (e.g., something being built) that is already finished, SENENTI refers to an action one has already completed (e.g., bathing).
*v.t.* **jánkexa** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *kéxeti* to sew] : to sew (a sack) shut at the mouth
*adj.* **jánkoshin** [from Shipibo *jan-* of the voice + *kóshi* strong] : loud-voiced
*v.t.* **jánoa** [from Shipibo *jan-* in the mouth + *nóati* to sting/peck] : to force into the mouth of (an animal)
*v.i.* [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *rasáti* to untie] : to undo the stitches at the mouth of (a sack)

*v.t.* **jánsena** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *sénoti* to cut through the skin] : to cut the frenulum of the tongue of
*n.* **janshón** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *sho*, element of *shóati* to spill] 1 : infant thrush (mouth ulcers) 2 : patco (a scurvy-like disease) : scurvy
*v.i.* **jánshoa** 1 : to have infant thrush ⟨**Jánshoshon shóma áyamaira báke isínke.** Because it had thrush, the infant would not nurse and became ill.⟩ 2 : to have patco (a scurvy-like disease)
*v.t.* **jánsita** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *si*, unidentified element + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to pull (the tongue) out of

*adj. and n.* **jansón** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *so*, unidentified element] *adj.* : lying : untruthful; *also* : slanderous ⟨**Nato jónironki jánso iki; ja ikónhayamakanwe.** They say this man is a liar; don't believe him.⟩ *n.* 1 : lie ⟨**Nokon epánra jawen jánsobi ikónhake.** My paternal uncle deceived himself; that is, he believed his own lie.⟩ 2 : slander ⟨**Jawen jánso kopibira jóni káraboso meran níakanke.** Because of his own slander, they put a man in jail.⟩ 3 : slanderer ⟨**Jánso íketianra nato jóni káraboso meran níakanke.** Because he was a slanderer, they put this man in jail.⟩ 4 : foolishness —Used in the form *jansón* as a woman's exclamation. *syn.* joín imamis

*v.t.* **jánsoa** 1 : to lie ⟨**Nokon báke yóyoikama ikénbira nato jóni** **jánsoke**. My son had not said anything, but this man lied, making things up about him.⟩ 2 : to slander ⟨**Ekira jánsokanai** They are slandering me.⟩
*v.t.* **jántasa** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *tásati* to prick] : to prick on the tongue
*v.t.* **jánteta** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *tékati* to sting] : to sting (e.g., a wasp) on the tongue
*v.t.* **jántina** [from Shipibo *jan-* in the mouth + *tínati* to insert] : to insert into the mouth until touching the palate
*adj.* **jantón** [from Shipibo *jan-* tongue + *-nto* without] : tongueless
*v.t.* **jántsati** [from Shipibo *jan-* on the tongue + *tsákati* to hit] : to hit on the tongue with some weapon
*v.t.* **jántseta** [from Shipibo *jan-* the tongue + *tséketi* to extract] : to extract the tongue of
*v.i.* **jántsina** [from Shipibo *jan-* of the tongue + *tsínati* to reduce swelling] : for the tongue to become less swollen
*v.t.* **jánxaxa** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *xáxati* to scrub/grate] : to scrub (a pot) inside at the rim
*v.t.* **jánxbana** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *xabánti* to cause to open] : to open the mouth of
*v.t.* **jánxbata** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *xabáti* to yawn] : for the mouth to open
*adj. and n.* **janxón** *adj.* : having an odor : foul-smelling (e.g., of decomposing blood, watermelon, or grated green or ripe plantain) *n.* : odor : stench *syn.* písi

*n.* **janxóxponin** : a type of large red stinging ant ⟨**Janxóxponin náaki jisónketianronki noa mapón chéxati iki.** They say that when we urinate on the nest of the *janxóxpo* ant, it can give us a headache.⟩
*v.t.* **jánxoxa** [from Shipibo *jan-* in the mouth + *xóxoti* to sprout] : to grow in the mouth of
