See under **pótati**
*n.* **járamasianin** [from Spanish] : pharmacy *syn.* ráoxobo
*v.t.* **járeta** [from Shipibo *jan-* at the mouth + *rérati* to cut] : to cut open the mouth of with a single blow
*n.* **jashín** : ritual arrows for the festival

*n.* **jásiman** : curassow (paujil) ⟨**Yoshíntetekanronki jasínbires píai.** They say the ghost hawk eats curassows.⟩ ⟨**Moátianronki Inkánkijawen jónibo jasín réteti ráana boxónbiki áyamakana iki, jóni jisá íketian.** Long ago the Inca sent his people to kill curassows. They went, but did not kill them or discover them because they resembled human beings.⟩
[from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *jasín* curassow (paujil)] : a type of curassow
*n.* [from Shipibo *jasín* curassow (paujil) + *kené* cage] : a constellation called "Curassow's Cage," formed from the lion-hide part of the Orion constellation
See under **níshi**
See under **teté**
See under **wáiti**
*adv.* [from Shipibo *ja* that + *ska*, unidentified element; cf. *jáskati* to behave] : thus : like this ⟨**nítikoma jaskábi píkota** born lame (lame from birth)⟩ *syn.* jáskati
See under **pikoti**

*adv.* : then : afterward; *also* : however –Used to indicate the result of something said in the previous sentence. ⟨**Méeyamawe —akin en aká iki; jaskáketian ea yóia iki: Miara íboma iki —akin.** I told him: 'Don't touch it.' Then he said to me: 'You are not the owner.'⟩ ⟨**Pátoroninra noa téeti bokáskin koráka yókatia. Jaskáketianra korákanin kéenxonyamake.** The boss wanted to take us to work and asked the curaca (community leader) for permission; however, the curaca would not be persuaded.⟩ *syn.* JASKAKETIAN, JASKATAX, JASKAAXON, JATIAN, JAINOAX can all be translated as "then". JASKAAXON and JASKATAX relate the main verb to the subordinate verb: JASKAAXON is used when the main verb is *transitive*, and JASKATAX, when it is intransitive. JASKAKETIAN and JATIAN, on the other hand, have no grammatical relation to the main verb. JASKAKETIAN relates to something said in a previous sentence; it is used to indicate the result narrated in the current sentence. JATIAN, with the more specific sense of "back then", implies antiquity or a time in the remote past. JAINOAX implies a temporal relation between two main verbs.
*pron.* **jáskaranin** [from Shipibo *jaska–* thus + *ra*, unidentified element] : such a thing ⟨**Jáskarabora ea íke.** Such things happened to me.⟩

*adj.* **jáskaranin** : thus : such : also : of that kind ⟨**En óinara jáskara iká iki; rámara jáwekeskabira iki.** When I saw it, it was like that; I don't know how it might be now.⟩ ⟨**Nokon epán nóntira áni iki jáskara jisáribira nokon pápana iki.** My paternal uncle's canoe is big, and so is my father's.⟩ ⟨**Jáskara jói jato yóiwe.** Give them such a message.⟩ *syn.* jáskati

*adv.* **jaskáaxon** [from Shipibo *jaskáti, jaska–* to behave + *–ati, –aa* to do + *–ax, xon*, subordinate-verb suf.] 1 : thus ⟨**En mia onámaakeskaakin jaskáaxon awé.** As I taught you, do it that way.⟩ ⟨**Jáskatax káara ea yóikanke. Enra óinamaribi iki.** They told me he had left that way. I didn't see him leave, either.⟩ 2 : then : from there –Used with a main verb whose subject is the same as the subject of the main verb in a preceding clause. ⟨**Chipónkiax jóketianra jóni yatánkana iki. Játian jato yóia iki: Ea méeyamakanwe —akin. Játian jénekana iki. Jáskatax moa jóni káa iki jákiribi.** A man came from downriver and they detained him; but he told them to release him, and they then did so. Then he went back to his community.⟩ ⟨**Mia** **téetiain ionoxonra min pápapari en yókatai. Jaskáaxonra min títa betan pápashokoribi en yókatai.** To take you to work, I will first ask your father's permission; then your mother's and your grandfather's.⟩ *syn.* See under **jaskáketian** *syn.* jáskati

*adv.* **jaskáakin** : thus : doing it this way –Used with a main verb that is transitive. ⟨**En mia ámanon jaskáakin awé.** As I show you, do it that way.⟩ *syn.* JASKAAKIN, JASKAAXON, JASKATI can be translated as "thus" or "doing it this way"; except that JASKAAKIN or JAKAAXON is used when the main verb is transitive, while JASKATI, on the other hand, is used when the main verb is intransitive. *syn.* jáskatax; jáskara; neskáakin; néskatax; jaská

*v.i.* **jáskata** [from Shipibo *jaska*, element of *jáskara* thus + *–ati* to do] : to behave ⟨**Jaskátima ikénbi jaskáketianra maístoron bákebo kastíkanke.** The teacher punished the children because they behaved improperly.⟩

*v.i.* **jáa** [from Shipibo *ja* that, he + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to exist —Used in this and the following senses in the preterite form but with the meaning of continuous or present time. ⟨**Ríosen jóniaketiamparira jatíbi jawéki jáke.** All things exist only because God created them.⟩ 2 : there to be ⟨**Nato jemánra ícha yómetsobo jakánke; koíramekanwe.** In this city there are many thieves; be careful.⟩ 3 : to live; *specif.* : to inhabit ⟨**Mia kopiresa nokon báke jáke; mia jóyamaketianra moa mawákeanke.** My son lives only because of you; if you hadn't come, he would already have died.⟩ ⟨**Riónra Ajírikain jáke.** The lion lives in Africa.⟩ 4 : to have to ⟨**Nokon pápa betan ea iaman kátira jáke.** I have to go with my father to the cocha (oxbow lake).⟩ *syn.* JATI, YAKATI can both be translated as "to live" with no difference; while JATI can have the more general sense of "to be alive", YAKATI is limited to the more restricted sense of "to reside".
*n.* **játinin** [from Shipibo *játi, ja-* to live + *-ti* in what] : area where people live

*adv. and adj.* [from Shipibo *játi, ja-* to exist + *ti*, unidentified element] *adv.* : so much ⟨**—¿Jatí íchaki min beá? Ichamashoko bétira en mia yóiwanke.** 'Did you bring that much?' I told you to bring only a little.⟩ *adj.* : so many ⟨**Jatí báritiaya ikaxa ea moa játima iki.** If I were as old as he is, I would not have lived until now.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *játi, ja-* to exist + *-tian* when] : then : at that time —Used in some cases to separate the parts of a dialogue. ⟨**Moatian niwánontianra ea Rimán iká iki. Játianra en óina iki jóni kéyotai.** When there was the earthquake a while back, I was in Lima, and I saw how many people died at that time.⟩ ⟨**Nokon papán ea aká iki neskáakin: Báketianbi téetinin áxewe —akin. Játian en yóia iki: Eara íkai, papá. Min jóira en senénhai —akin.** My father spoke to me like this: 'Learn to work from childhood.' Then I said to him: 'Yes, father, I will follow your advice.'⟩ *syn.* See under **jaskáketian**

*adj.* **jatíbinin** [from Shipibo *jatí* so much + *-bi*, emphatic suf.] : all ⟨**Nato maín jáa jatíbi jónibora jenén ewan jato kéyoa iki, Inkán báke míinkanketian.** All the people who lived on the earth died at because of the flood, for having buried the Son of the Inca.⟩ ⟨**Yómetsobaonra jatíbi nokon koríki ea bóonke.** The thieves took all my money.⟩ ⟨**Bíntiochotianra noa jatíbi bákeboyabi márachankanai.** On the twenty-eighth of July we all marched together with the schoolchildren.⟩ *syn.* intíro
*adv.* [from Shipibo *jatíbi* all + *-ain* in] 1 : everywhere 2 : omnipresent ⟨**Riós jatíbiain** God, omnipresent⟩
See under **átipanti**
See under **onán**
*adv.* [from Shipibo *jatíbi* all + *-tian* when] : always ⟨**Jatíbitian páenai jónira moa jenén réteke.** The man who always got drunk drowned.⟩ *syn.* -pacho

*adv.* **játixonbi** [from Shipibo *jatí* so many + *ikáxbi, ixonbi*, forms of *íti* to be] : all : all together ⟨**Nato simánaninronki játikaxbi téeti iki; ja téeyamaaboronki kóboranai.** They say that this week everyone must work, and those who don't work will be fined.⟩ ⟨**Jáskatax téeti jatíxonbi non jaskárabires shínanara jakónira iki.** It is very good if we all agree on how to work.⟩

*adv.* : of that or such indicated measure : of equal measure ⟨**Ea játio áni íketianra, nokon pápashoko máwata iki.** When I was that size, my grandfather died.⟩ ⟨**Ikítoain kaxónra en áni wapóro oínke; játio ániribira en Máioashiain jokín oínke.** When I went to Iquitos, I saw a big steamship; when I was coming back, I saw one just as big in Pucallpa.⟩ ⟨**Nato wapórora naxbá iki; játio naxbá óinaxa ea ratéke.** This ship is so wide; seeing something that wide amazed me.⟩ ⟨**Játio nemín ikáinoara rabé jóni jenén réteke.** In a place with water that deep, two people drowned.⟩ ⟨**Motórooma ixónbira játio nenké** nocon papán tapán bóke. Even though there was no motor (outboard motor) and the raft was that long, my father steered it.⟩ ⟨**Játio ochó íketianra en íso tóoakinbi réteyamake.** I shot at a spider monkey (maquisapa) that was that far away, but I didn't kill it.⟩ ⟨**Kakónkonia kámpo riki kikín pextín; játio pextínribi riki Xarárayainoa.** The sports field in Caco is very wide, and the one in Xarara is just as wide.⟩ ⟨**Játio keyá wapórora non óinamapari iki.** We still have not seen a steamship that tall.⟩ ⟨**Játio rastón jíwira non oínyosma iki.** We have never seen a tree that thick.⟩ ⟨**Nokon pápa riki xoá jóni; játio rastónribi riki nokon wétsa.** My father is a fat man; my brother is just as fat too.⟩

*adj.* **jatíribin** [from Shipibo *jatí*, element of *jatíbi* all + *ribi* again] 1 : some -Used in singular and plural sense. ⟨**Jatíribi máyoronabora moa níi meranoax jokónkasai.** Now some matsés (Matsés people) want to come out of the jungle.⟩ 2 : the others -Used in the plural form *jatíribibo*. ⟨**Chéxeinkaronki jakón jóni ikátiai; játian jatíribibo jáskarama.** They say the Inca Prieto (the Dark Inca, a legendary figure) was a good person, while others say he was not.⟩ *syn.* See under **wétsa**

*v.i.* **játishanika** [from Shipibo *játishan*, imitative of a sneeze] : to sneeze ⟨**Non kaíbobaon noa shínanaitianronki noa játishanikai.** They say we sneeze when our relatives are thinking of us.⟩

*also* **jábo** *pers. pron.* **jaton** *also* **jabaon** : they : them : to them : (as object) them ⟨**Nóara nato jémameabo iki; jábora jáama iki.** We are from this community; they are not.⟩ ⟨**Mía yóikinra en áyamake; játo yóikinra en áke.** I was not speaking about you; I was speaking about them.⟩ ⟨**Onántibiresakin en jato yóiabira ninkáyamakanai.** Even though I spoke to them very clearly, they did not understand.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.1

*adj.* : their -Used as a possessive modifier preceding the noun. ⟨**Jónibaonra téetiainoax jabákin jaton pátoronbobicho pótakanke.** The men fled from the workplace and left their bosses alone.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.3.3
See under **-na**

*also* **jatsán** *adj.* **jatsán** *also* **játsaman** : annoying : tiresome ⟨**Máioshiainoax Ikítoain tápaman káara játsa iki.** The raft trip from Pucallpa to Iquitos is very tiresome.⟩ ⟨**Bákebora wínii jatsányora iki; netémakanwe.** The children are crying and are very annoying; make them be quiet.⟩

*v.t.* **jatsánhaa** *Konibo* **jatsánhaka** : to annoy ⟨**Néno rókotoro íketianra sáa ikin bákebaon jatsánhaa iki.** When the doctor was here, the children shouted at him and annoyed him.⟩ *syn.* téati

*v.i.* **játsana** 1 : to become annoyed 2 : to grow bored : to grow tired ⟨**Nato jemánkora ea moa bási jáke; jáskatira ea jatsánke.** I have already lived a long time in this village; that's why I'm already bored.⟩ ⟨**Eara námi píi moa jatsánke.** I've already grown tired of eating meat.⟩

*pron.* 1 : what? –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**¿Jáweki jaín jóai?** What is coming?⟩ 2 : from what tribe? –Used in a question with *aínbo* "woman" or *jóni* "man" immediately following it. ⟨**Westíora jónira mia onánkasai, jáwe ainborin mia ixon.** A man wants to meet you and wants to know what tribe you're from.⟩ ⟨**¿Jáwe joni ikaxki, nato jóni jaskati yóyoikai?** What tribe might this man be from, who talks like this?⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.2

*adv.* : why? –Used in a question with an intransitive main verb. ⟨**¿Jáweakiki mia ráketai?** Why are you afraid?⟩ *syn.* JAWEAKI, JAWEATI, JAWEKOPI, JAWEKESKATI all mean "why". However, JAWEATI is used only with a transitive main verb, JAWEAKI and JAWEKESKATI are used only with an intransitive main verb. There is no such restriction on the use of JAWEKOPI.
*adv.* : why? –Used in a question with a transitive main verb. ⟨**¿Jáweatiki min ea paránxon ráana?** Why did you send me off with lies?⟩ *syn.* See under **jáweaki**
*pron.* : nothing –Used with a verb with a negative suffix. ⟨**Nato jónira moa jáwebi kéenyamai, kíkini sínata ikax.** This man doesn't want anything because he is very angry.⟩
See under **néeti**

*adj.* [from Shipibo *jáwebi* nothing + *-oma* without] 1 : without anything ⟨**Níweabanaponbi kaíra ríkaton réokooke; jáskataxa jáwebioma banéke.** The trader was shipwrecked going down the river in the middle of a windstorm; and so he was left with nothing.⟩ 2 : empty ⟨**Nato botíriara jáwebioma iki.** This bottle is empty.⟩ *syn.* áko
See under **wínoti**

*adv.* [from Shipibo *jáwe* what + *keská* like] –Used as a word marking a question. 1 : what kind? ⟨**¿Jáwekeska jónirin náto?** What kind of man is this?⟩ 2 : how? ⟨**¿Miaki jáwekeska iki?** How are you?⟩ *syn.* JAWEKESKA, JAWEKESKATAx, JAWEKESKAAxON can all be translated as "how". However, JAWEKESKATAx and its grammatical variant JAWEKESKAAxON imply an action on the part of the subject, while JAWEKESKA only asks about its state of being.

*v.t.* **jáwekeskaa** : to do or say what thing, or how –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**Yatánxonki mia, ¿jáwekeskaa?** What did he do to you when he grabbed you?⟩ ⟨**¿Játianki jáwekeskakaa?** Then what did they do?⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *jáwekeska* how + *-ra*, unidentified element + *-ain* in] : where? : in what place? ⟨**¿Jáwekeskarainrin min ánibo?** Where are your parents?⟩ *syn.* jáwerano

*adv.* **jáwekeskaaxon** : how : doing what thing or in what way ⟨**Eara Rimán katánke jáwekeskaaxonki chópaakanai ixon óini.** I went to Lima to see how they make cloth.⟩ ⟨**¿Moa yatánkana ikáxbiki, mia jáwekeskatax píkota?** How did you escape even though they had caught you?⟩ *syn.* See under **jáwekeska**

*adv.* : why? –Used in a question with an intransitive main verb. *syn.* See under **jáweaki** ⟨**¿Jáwekeskatiki mia wíniresai? Rámara en mia ráo xéamai.** Why do you keep crying? Now I'm going to give you medicine.⟩

*v.i.* **jáwekeskata** : to happen, occur, or take place, what thing or in what way ⟨**Jóni jáwekeskatara non oínbirake bái napon rákata.** We saw a man lying on the path. What could have happened to him?⟩

*n.* **jawékinin** 1 : thing : object ⟨**Icha jawékironki biántanke.** They say he acquired many things.⟩ 2 : animal –The variant form *bákeai jawéki* is also used in this sense. ⟨**Inora siná jawéki iki.** The jaguar (tigre) is a fierce animal.⟩ 3 : bird ⟨**Jawéki bóchiki nóyai en óinabira, naíkoinman bépoke.** Although I spotted birds flying up there, the clouds covered them.⟩ 4 : fish ⟨**Káchiora ea katánke; kaxón óinara íaman jawéki páeni ícha íke.** I went to the monte (forest) and saw that many fish were stupefied in the cocha (oxbow lake).⟩ 5 : tree ⟨**Nokon jawéki banara ea niwén póxanaanke.** My planted trees were knocked down by the wind.⟩ 6 : a thing done or to be done : action ⟨**Jatíbira min jakón aká iki; ikáxbira mia westíora jawékibicho maxkáke.** You did everything well, but you are missing just one thing.⟩ *syn.* JAWEKI, YOINA can both be translated as "animal"; but JAWEKI (or its variant BAKEAI JAWEKI) is said of animals in general, while YOINA refers more to animals, domestic or wild, whose meat is edible. *syn.* ísa; jíwi *syn.* See under **wáka**
*adj.* **jawékiaton** [from Shipibo *jawéki* thing + *-ya* with] : rich : wealthy ⟨**Páto**ronbora jawékia jóni ikátiai. The bosses were rich men.⟩

*adj.* **jawéki akaiton** [from Shipibo *jawéki* thing + *ákai*, a form of *áti* to make] : skilled at making things (e.g., canoes) from wood : master : expert : skilled at working with wood ⟨**Jawéki akai jonínra, jakónhakin nónti ákai.** A skilled man makes a good canoe.⟩ *syn.* áxeamis; maístoro
*v.t.* **jawékiakasa** [from Shipibo *jawékiati* to eat something + *-kas* to want] : to be hungry : to feel like eating
*adj.* **jawékiaomaton** [from Shipibo *jawéki* thing + *-oma* without] : poor ⟨**Noara jawékioma iki, tééti onáma ikax.** We are poor because we don't know how to work.⟩ *syn.* ónitsapishoko

*v.t.* **jawékiaa** [from Shipibo *jawéki* thing + *-ati* to make] : to eat something –Used without a direct object. ⟨**Yamé nokóxonra potókin jawékiake.** Arriving at night, he ate something until he was full.⟩ *syn.* See under **kókoti**
*n.* **jawéki kimisha paroyaton** [from Shipibo *jawéki* thing + *kimisha* three + *paró* squareness + *-ya* with] : triangle
*n.* **jawéki tsamanti xobón** [from Shipibo *jawéki* thing + *tsamánti* to pile up + *xóbo* house] : storehouse
*adv.* : why? ⟨**¿Jáwekopiki min ea téemaa koríkioma ixónbi?** Why did you make me work if you had no money?⟩ *syn.* See under **jáweaki**

*adv.* : from where? –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**Bóchikiax nokon báke pakéketianra ea jonín yokáke: ¿Jáwemeaxki min báke páketa? —akin. Játian en yóike: Kaímitomeax —akin.** When my son fell, a man asked me: 'Where did your little boy fall from?' And I said: 'From the caimito (star-apple) tree.'⟩

*pron.* [from Shipibo, non-basic form of *jáwe* what] 1 : what? : what animal? –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**¿Jawénki nato piá?** What animal ate this?⟩ 2 : with what? ⟨**¿Jawénki nato wísoino min rétea? —akinki jonín jawen awín aká iki.** They say a man asked his wife: 'What did you kill this yanapuma (black jaguar) with?'⟩ 3 : in what? : in what thing? ⟨**¿Jawén**qui mia Kakónkoniax joá? What did you come from Caco in?⟩

*adj.* : his : her –Used as a possessive modifier preceding the noun. ⟨**Aínbaonronki jawen benén yamín íno rétenike.** They say that once a woman killed a jaguar (tigre) with her husband's axe.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.3.3
See under **-na**
See under **yorónti**
See under **néte**

*adv.* 1 : where? : in what location? –Used as a word marking a question. –Used with the copulative suffix *-rin*. ⟨**¿Jáweranorin min pápa?** Where is your father?⟩ 2 : to where? : to what place? –Used with a verb of motion. ⟨**¿Jáweranoki káa nokon títa?** Where has my mother gone?⟩ 3 : where? : in what place? –Used with a transitive verb indicating transfer. ⟨**¿Jáweranoki min aká machíto?** Where have you put the machete?⟩ 4 : in approximately what location? : whereabouts? –Used with *-oa*, suffix of origin or place, added, and with a transitive verb. ⟨**¿Jáweranoaki min nokon épa óina?** Where did you see my paternal uncle?⟩ 5 : where? : from where? : from what place of origin? –Used with *-oa*, suffix of origin or place, added, and with a transitive verb. ⟨**¿Jáweranoaki min yámi biá?** Where did you get the axe?⟩ 6 : from where? : from what place of origin? –Used with the suffix *-ax* and with an intransitive verb of motion. ⟨**¿Jáweranoaxki mia joá?** Where have you come from?⟩ ⟨**¿Míaki jáweranoax joá?** Where have you come from?⟩ 7 : at which site of action or operation –Used with the suffix *-xon* and with a transitive verb. ⟨**¿Jáweranoxon akárin en mia jáskara jói yóikin?** At what place did I say such words to you about this matter?⟩ *syn.* JAWERANOAX, JAWERANOA can both be translated as "from where"; while JAWERANOA is used with any transitive verb, JAWERANOAX is limited to use with an intransitive verb of motion. Accordingly, JAWERANOAX and JAWERANOA ask about the origin of the subject and the origin of the object, respectively. *syn.* JAWERANOXON, JAWERANOA, JAWERANO can all be translated as "where", but each differs from the others regarding the group of verbs it can be used with. JAWERANOXON and JAWERANOA are used with the transitive verb, and JAWERANO with the copulative verb. According to the different verb groups associated with each, JAWERANOXON and JAWERANO ask about the location of the subject's referent, while JAWERANOA asks about the location of the object's referent. *syn.* jáwekeskarain

*adv.* 1 : in what direction? –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**¿Jáwerao kákasiki mia íiwana?** In what direction did you want to go a while ago?⟩ 2 : which way? ⟨**Jáweraoki mia kái, jáinra ea kái.** 'Which way are you going?' —'I'm going that way.'⟩ 3 : what direction : from approximately what place –Used with the suffix *-quea, -keax* or *-xon* as a word marking a question. ⟨**¿Jáweraokea báirin nato jan noa kái?** What direction does this path we're taking go?⟩ ⟨**¿Jáweraokeaxki jóni saíika?** From approximately what place did the man shout?⟩ ⟨**Nenónxonbi mánawe, jaweraokeaxki jóai min oínon.** Wait right here to see from what direction he is coming.⟩ ⟨**¿Jáweraoxon tóoati píshakanaki non nínkata?** From what direction did we hear them firing their weapons?⟩ *syn.* JAWERAOXON, JAWERAOAKEA, JAWERAOKEAX can all be translated as "in what direction", but each differs in the restriction on its use. While JAWERAOXON is used in a sentence with a transitive verb, JAWERAOAKEA is used only in an intransitive sentence with the suffix *-rin* replacing the verb, and JAWERAOKEAX is used only in a sentence with an intransitive verb.
*pron.* : which? –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**¿Jáweratoki mia kéenai?** Which one do you want?⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *jáwe* what + *-tian* when] : when? : at what time? –Used as a word marking a question. –Also used with the plural suffix *-bo* to indicate that several times are being asked about. ⟨**¿Jáwetianki mia réboki kái?** When are you going upriver?⟩ ⟨**¿Jáwetianboki íno níai?** At what times does the jaguar (tigre) move about?⟩
*adv.* : never –Always used with a verb bearing the negative suffix. ⟨**Min nokon jói sénenhayamaitianra, en mia jáwetianbi kopíayamanox iki.** If you don't follow my orders, I will never pay you.⟩
*adj.* : how many? –Used as a word marking a question. ⟨**¿Jáwetii jóniki Máioshiain bókana?** How many people have gone to Pucallpa?⟩

[from Shipibo *jáwetii* how many + *kopía* price] : what price : how much –Used with *-rin* in a question. ⟨**¿Jáwetii kopíarin min chitónti kewéaa?** What price is the pampanilla (traditional skirt) that you embroidered?⟩
See under **jáwetii**

*adv.* : how much (measurement of size or distance)? –Used as a word marking a question. –Used with an adjective or adverb indicating size or distance. ⟨**¿Jáwetio áni jawen wíshpo réraarin?** How big is the cut on his leg?⟩ ⟨**¿Jáwetio naxbárin ja min papán bená nóntiaa?** How wide is the inside of the new canoe your father made?⟩ ⟨**¿Jáwetio naxbáki min nónokin ián shítakato?** How wide a stretch did you swim across the cocha (oxbow lake)?⟩ ⟨**¿Jain áblon jéne meran káaki jáwetio nemín iki?** How deep is the place where the plane fell into the water?⟩ ⟨**¿Jáwetio nenkéki min konxán xátea, epá?** Uncle, how long did you cut the wood?⟩ ⟨**¿Nénoaxki min jéma jáwetio ochó iki?** From here, how far away is your town?⟩ ⟨**¿Jáwetio keyá áni wapóroki min óina iki?** At what height did you see the big steamship?⟩ ⟨**¿Papán ronón ewa méraaki jáwetio rastón iká?** The boa constrictor father saw — how thick was it?⟩

*n.* **jáxkaten** *Konibo* **jáxkakan** : a hand of plantains (a cluster of fruit) ⟨**Rámara paránta jaxká kikínbires kopí iki, mírikaronko.** Nowadays a hand of plantains is very expensive in the market.⟩

*v.t.* **jáxkaa** : to tear a limb off the body of ⟨**Moátianronki jóniki inón jáxkayonike konxán xátei káketian.** They say that long ago, a man who had gone to cut cedar (cedro) was completely dismembered by a jaguar (tigre).⟩

*v.i.* **jáxkata** 1 : for a limb to tear off one's own body ⟨**Jíwibochikiax páketira jonín poyán jaxkákainke.** Falling from the top of a tree, the man tore off his arm.⟩ 2 : for the parts of something to break and fall off ⟨**En paránta texkan pápixon beára moa kéyoti jaxkáke.** The bunch of plantains I was carrying on my back has completely fallen apart.⟩

*adj.* **jayáomatonin** [from Shipibo *ja* it, that + *-oma, -yaoma* without] : with nothing ⟨**Nokon épara píti bénai káshbi jayáoma jóke, jawen pía jéne meran káketian.** My paternal uncle went to hunt for game (mitayo); but he came back with nothing because his arrow fell into the water.⟩

*interj.* –Used as an exclamation at the end of lines of a song. ⟨**Amaabira, je, min ámaabira, je, warón rakáyamai, je. Era rakáyamai, je.** Although I take to drinking, although because of you I take to drinking, drunk I do not lie down. I do not lie down.⟩
*interj.* –Used with the meaning "okay" to indicate consent to a request or an order. –Used to answer when one is called by name.

*n.* **jéekan** : pucacuru (a type of worm) ⟨**Moátianronki jéekanki áwakan poínki meran kaxón jawen joínti xaténike.** They say that long ago the pucacuru worm entered through the tapir's anus and killed it by cutting its heart.⟩
*interj.* –Used as a man's response to a greeting. *syn.* JEJE, JOJO are used equally as a response to a greeting, but JEJE is used by men, and JOJO by women.

*n.* **jemán** 1 : cleared land ⟨**Nato jemánkora ícha jóni yakánoxikanai.** Many people will settle in this cleared place.⟩ 2 : street of a native community : open plaza ⟨**Kakónkora jémaponbi ábionbo páketai.** In Caco, small planes land right in the middle of the street.⟩ 3 : village, community, or town with authorities; *specif.* : colonia (a settlement) ⟨**Nato nétera ápo nókotai non jéma óini.** Today a high-ranking official will arrive to visit our community.⟩ ⟨**Páoianbichoronkiki shípibaon jéma ani.** They say that Paococha alone is the large Shipibo village.⟩ ⟨**Máioshinya jemánra moa yómetso ícha iki.** In the town of Pucallpa there are quite a lot of thieves these days.⟩ 4 : town : city *syn.* JEMA, YAKATI can both be translated as "community", but JEMA suggests more of a free, open place where a community can exist, while YAKATI implies the stable location of residences.

*v.t.* **jémaa** *Konibo* **jémaaka** : to found (a settlement, a village, a town, or a city) ⟨**Ichaxonra nato báritia réboki bená jémaakanke.** This year, many founded new settlements (colonias) upriver.⟩ ⟨**Konchória náwabaonra bená** **jémaati shinánkanai.** The people of Cunchuri, who are not Konibo, are thinking of founding a new village.⟩ ⟨**Máioshinya pekaora moa áni jémaakanke.** Behind Pucallpa they have founded a large town.⟩ ⟨**Ispaniorobaonronki Ríma jémaanike.** They say that long ago the Spaniards founded the city of Lima.⟩
See under **ochíti**
See under **óroti**
*n.* **jémashokon** [from Shipibo *jéma* town + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : small village

*v.i.* **jémaa** : to form into a new community : for a new community to be founded ⟨**Maníx kextó ikátiibira Otokoro jémake, jóni icha boxón ákana.** Many people went to found the community of Utucuro even though it had previously been dense forest.⟩
*n.* **jéma xabakan** [from Shipibo *jéma* town + *xabá* open space] : plaza ⟨**Jéma xabátiibira jáke yakátibo.** In all plazas there are benches.⟩ *syn.* párasa
*v.t.* **jen aka** : to consent to : to accept ⟨**Jawen wái óroxonti ea yóiketianra en jén ake, koríki bikáskin.** When he told me I could farm his field, I agreed, because I wanted to earn money.⟩

*n.* **jenén** 1 : water (e.g., of a lake or a river) in a natural setting ⟨**Jonín ríkanaitianronki aínbaonki nókoa iki, jéne meranoax joxón.** They say that while a man was casting his net, a woman came out of the water to meet him.⟩ ⟨**Papánra jenén kaxón yawámasen mérake.** When father went to the oxbow lake (cocha), he came across a *yawámasen* bird.⟩ 2 : flood : river rise ⟨**Nato báritiara jenén noa mápoyamake.** This year the river's flood did not inundate our community.⟩ 3 : fruit or cane juice ⟨**Xáwi jene báke xéamaaronki chíkishai.** They say that if we give a child sugarcane juice to drink, he becomes lazy.⟩ 4 : soup : broth ⟨**átapa jene** chicken soup⟩ *syn.* JENE, OMPAX can both be translated as "water", but JENE implies more the natural state (e.g., in the river) where the water is found, while OMPAX refers to water outside its natural environment, typically stored for human use.
[from Shipibo *jéne* flood + *tsosíni* to recede + *-tian* at the time of] : during the time when the water recedes

*n.* **jénekawen** [from Shipibo *jéne* water + *kawé* (imperative of *káti* to go) goodbye] : a type of aquatic toad with a yellow chest, whose call, according to some reports, is heard when a flood is receding
See under **wáste**

*n.* **jéne máanaitonin** [from Shipibo *jéne* water + *máanai*, active participle of *máanti* to fall] : waterfall ⟨**Káchio kaxónra non jéne máanai méraa iki; ja jénera iká iki mátsi.** *Going into the monte (forest), we found a waterfall, and the water was cold.*⟩
See under **mabán**
See under **masén**
See under **ráanti**
See under **móe**
n. [from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *bimpish* guava] : water guava
See under **néa**

n. **jenén ewan** [from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *-ewa*, augmentative] : flood; *specif.* : the primordial flood of traditional stories –Used in the specific sense with capital *J*. ⟨**Jenén ewa benónronki non jemánkoki nócho ani pikóti iki.** They say that to signal a flood is coming, a large churo (a snail) will come out into our yard.⟩ ⟨**Nakáxonki, Jenén ewaítian jabáti kaí, tóoya aínbo iní iki.** They say the termite mound originated when a pregnant woman was fleeing from the Flood.⟩
See under **jasín**
See under **páketi**
See under **réteti**

n. **jenéntitan** [from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *tita* mother] : a species of very large fish ⟨**Jenéntitaronki weán tsosímayamai.** They say the *jenéntita* fish keeps the streams from drying up.⟩

n. **jenényawan** [from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *yáwa* white-lipped peccary] : esquila (a species of aquatic insect) ⟨**Non jenényawan ponyán síkaaronki nontín kaí noa íshto íti iki.** They say that when we rub our arms with an *esquila*, we can paddle faster.⟩
See under **yoshín**
See **ronín**
See under **róno**
See under **shanó**

v.t. **jénea** 1 : to leave (a person or thing) ⟨**Nato báritiabira jónibaon jaton pátoronbo moa jéneke.** This year the men have left their bosses.⟩ 2 : to stop (doing a specific thing) –Used with a transitive subordinate verb as its complement. ⟨**Nato jóninra xóboakinbi jéneke, jawen báke wáiroron yatánketian.** This man was building a house, but he stopped doing it because his son was captured by the police.⟩

v.i. **jéneta** : to stop being or doing a specific thing –Used with an intransitive infinitive. ⟨**Yóyoitibira rário jenéke, nato bakén masáaka.** The radio stopped working because this child broke it.⟩

n. **jénetian** [from Shipibo *jéne* flood season + *-tia* time] : flood-season time : winter ⟨**Awakanra níshi píaia moa jénetia íketian.** During flood season, the tapir eats vine-like grass.⟩ syn. JENETIA, MATSI both can be translated as "winter," but JENETIA emphasizes the time of the rising waters, while MATSI emphasizes the cold, less sunny time.
[from Shipibo *jénetia* winter + *napon* inside of] : in the middle of winter

adv. [from Shipibo *jéne* flood season + *-tian* when, at the time of] : in winter : during flood season ⟨**Nato jénetianra jéne písi iántanke, manán réokootax.** During that winter, the water smelled bad because hills that had collapsed fell in.⟩

v.i. **jénetiaa** : to have a rise in the river's water level ⟨**Jénetiaketianra rébokiax páeri mawá toxbá pákeyantanke.** When there was a rise in the water, the current brought the corpse of a priest floating down from upriver.⟩
See under **jéne**
See under **xenán**
*v.i.* **jén ika** : to consent : to accept ⟨**Nokon títaiba mérati kanón kawe —ákara jén ike.** When she said to him, "Let's go for a walk to my mother's," he accepted.⟩
See **énjen**

*adj.* **jénkoten** *Konibo* **jénkokan** : rancid : smelling of rancid oil or fat ⟨**Nato bákera ámakiri xenin ráchikiike; jáskatira jawen yóra jenkó iki.** This child spilled gamitana fish (gamitana) fat on himself; that's why his whole body smells rancid.⟩ ⟨**Xéni jenkó piáxa nato báke chíxotai.** Because he ate something with rancid oil, this child has diarrhea.⟩
*v.t.* **jenkóaa** *Konibo* **jenkóaka** : to make smell of oil ⟨**Ichayora xéni axónra nato xóntakon xée jenkóake.** By putting in too much oil, this girl made the fried food smell of pure oil.⟩
*v.i.* **jénkota** : to have a strong oily smell ⟨**Kabóri pexkan en xóiara jawen xéni jenkóke.** When I roasted the taricaya turtle (taricaya) shell, the fat took on a strong oily smell.⟩

*n.* **jéokan** [from Shipibo *jéo*, imitative of its call] : gualo (a bird) ⟨**Moa xawén cháro jókonaitianronki jeó kéotai.** They say the *gualo* bird sings when the young of the charapa (river turtles) hatch.⟩
*n.* **jepén** : yarina (ivory-nut palm) ⟨**Jépe pei bíi kaxónronki jonín wísoino rétenike.** They say that long ago a man killed a yanapuma (black puma) when he had gone to gather yarina leaves.⟩
See under **isán**
*v.t.* **jéshaka** : to make a sucking noise ⟨**Yobébaonra noa óyokin jéshakai; noara isínhakai.** Sorcerers make a sucking noise when they suck on us, and it makes us hurt.⟩
*n.* **jeshín** : a species of tree with a trunk like that of the shimbillo tree, tiny leaves, and seeds used to make necklaces

*v.i.* **jésika** : to make the sound of an isula (bullet ant) : to make the isula's characteristic sound ⟨**Xaén bóna píkoara jésikai; ja xaénra bóna píai.** The isula ant makes a "jes!" sound while the anteater pulls it out of its nest, and then it eats it.⟩
*adj.* **jéstekan** : very narrow, tight, snug, or reduced ⟨**Nato meósotira jesté iki; nokon awín betan senéma.** This ring is very narrow; it doesn't fit on my wife's finger.⟩
*v.t.* **jestéaa** *Konibo* **jestéaka** : to make very narrow, tight, snug, or reduced ⟨**Nato jonínra nokon sapáto jestéake.** This man made my shoe too narrow.⟩

*v.i.* **jésteta** : to get caught in a narrow spot : to get blocked : to get stuck ⟨**Jónironki manón jestéketian áni inón bínike.** They say a man was once attacked by a jaguar after getting stuck in the mud.⟩
*n.* **jétekan** : a smell that chokes or makes one sneeze ⟨**Bákeainbora koín jetekan joín rétemake.** The girl was choked by the smell of something burning.⟩
*v.i.* **jétea** : to choke : to gag ⟨**Osánhananbi átsapoto pikínra nato aínbaon jéteke.** This woman choked while eating fariña (toasted manioc flour), because she was laughing.⟩
*n.* **jexkón** [from Shipibo *jéxe* small sphere + *-ko*, unidentified element] : small piece
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *jéxko* small piece] : clod of earth ⟨**Nato báke yóitimanra máijexkon jawen wétsa tsákake.** This spoiled child deliberately hit his brother with a clod of earth.⟩
[from Shipibo *námi* meat + *jéxko* small piece] : a small piece or bite of meat ⟨**Nato ochítininra námijexko bóke.** This dog carried off a little piece of meat.⟩
*n.* **jíboman** [from Shipibo *jin-* on the penis + *bon*, element from *bobón*, also *bonbón* boil] : boil on the penis
*interj.* –Used in the sense of "ay!" as an exclamation of fear or fright. *syn.* See under **ápo**

*n.* **jiín** [from Spanish] : faith *syn.* JII, OINXONMABI IKONHATI both can be translated as "faith" with no difference in meaning. JII, the word borrowed from Spanish, is used more among evangelical believers. OINXONMABI IKONHATI is a native expression that refers to the quality of "believing without seeing" that characterizes a person who has faith.
*interj.* –Used in the sense of "you don't say!" as an expression of doubt or disbelief.

*v.t.* **jíkimaa** [from Shipibo *jíkiti, jiki–* to enter + *–ma* to make, to cause] : to install in a post or office ⟨**Nato simána jóaitonra nokon epán báke non koráka jíkimai.** Next week we will install my paternal uncle's son as curaca (village chief).⟩

*v.i.* **jíkia** 1 : to enter : to be inside ⟨**Moa kinimeran jíkia íketianra en píkoyamake.** I didn't take it out because it was already inside the hole.⟩ 2 : to get in : to lodge itself ⟨**Nokon nóntira wapóropoinki naman jíkike.** My canoe got wedged under the launch's stern.⟩ 3 : to come to hold a post or office ⟨**Tinínti jíkiaxa nato jóni siná banéke.** When he became lieutenant governor, this man became a despot.⟩ 4 : to sink ⟨**Páro memiora motóro jíkike.** On the left bank of the river the motor (outboard motor) sank.⟩ *syn.* See under **weíti**
*n.* **jimán** : a species of red ant ⟨**Non ponyán jíma icha tékamaaronki ponkóxti iki.** They say that when we let many *jíma* ants bite our arm, we will gain vigor.⟩

[from Shipibo *jína* ant + *shía*, unidentified element] : a small, dark reddish ant species, similar to the pucacuru species but a bit larger ⟨**Non jímashiaya shéaronki yóashitima iki.** They say that if we drink a beverage mixed with *jímashia* ants, we become generous.⟩ ⟨**Non jímashiayabi piáronki yóashitima iki.** They say that if we eat something with a *jímashia* ant present, it can take away our stinginess.⟩
[from Shipibo *pói* dung + *písi* foul-smelling + *jína* ant] : a species of black, foul-smelling ant
*adj.* **jímesen** [from Shipibo *jin-* on the tail + *metsá* pretty] : pretty-tailed : having a pretty tail
*n.* **jimín** : blood ⟨**Inkán jimín sikínironkiki xawán joshínshaman.** They say the macaw *kabezón* is bright red because long ago it was painted with the blood of the Inca who had been killed.⟩
[from Shipibo *jími* blood + *boánti* to pass] : to bleed
[from Shipibo *jími* blood + *jéneti* to stop] : to be, or have completed, one month of pregnancy ⟨**Nokon awínra jími jenéke.** My wife is one month pregnant.⟩
See under **manxán**
*v.i.* **jímia** : to menstruate ⟨**Moa chónka rabé báritiaya ikaxa nato xóntako jímike.** At twelve years of age, this young woman menstruated.⟩
*n.* **jímpaman** : caudal fin (tail fin)
*adj.* **jímpaxen** : undercooked at the tail ⟨**Amakiri shoira jimpáx iki.** The roasted gamitana (tambaqui fish) is undercooked at the tail.⟩
*adj.* **jímpisin** : having a foul-smelling penis

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *jína* tail] 1 : to the tail : on the tail : of the tail ⟨**jínxteke** to cut at the tail⟩ 2 : to the penis : on the penis : of the penis ⟨**jinbón** boil on the penis⟩ 3 : to the male parts : on the male parts : of the male parts. ⟨**jinchóti** to wash the male parts of⟩
*n.* **jinán** 1 : tail ⟨**Imirianronki jóni jínayaboki pikóke.** They say that in Imiría men with tails once appeared⟩ 2 : penis *syn.* boshí
See under tsóntsoro

*n.* **jinán ewan** [from Shipibo *jína, jinán* tail + *–ewa*, augmentative suf.] : charapilla (a small river turtle) ⟨**Moátianronki jinánewanki jóni bónike.** They say that long ago the *charapilla* carried off a man⟩

*adj.* **jínaoman** [from Shipibo *jína* tail + *–oma* without] : tailless : naturally without a tail ⟨**Chimpansíra íso jínaoma iki.** The chimpanzee is a tailless monkey⟩ *syn.* See under **chínto**
*v.t.* **jínbesa** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *betséti* to spread over completely] : including the tail
*n.* **jínchaman** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *chánko* protuberance] : spines on a fish's tail
*v.t.* **jínchexa** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *chéxati* to hurt] : to have a painful tail
*v.t.* **jínchexa** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *chéxeati* to paint] : to put (e.g., drops of medicine) on the tail of
*v.i.* **jínchia** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *chi–* backward + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] : to turn the tail in another direction
*v.t.* **jínchita** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the male parts + *chíkoti* to spill] : to spill onto the male parts
*adj.* **jinchón** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the male parts + *cho–*, modifying pref.] : having boils on the male parts
*v.t.* **jínchota** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the male parts + *chókati* to wash] : to wash the male parts of
*n.* **jínketen** *Konibo* **jínkekan** : soldier ant
*adj.* **jínkoshin** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *kóshi* strong] : having a strong tail

*n.* **jíntakan** [from Shipibo *jími* blood + *ta*, unidentified element] : blood clot ⟨**Nato jóni yamín táxtetara jintá pánike.** When this man cut his foot with an axe, a blood clot stayed hanging in the cut⟩
*v.t.* **jíntina** [from Shipibo *jin–* to the male parts + *tínati* to strike] : to jab or strike the male parts of
*adj.* **jintón** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *–nto* without] 1 : tailless 2 : having a very short tail *syn.* See under **chínto**
*n.* **jíntokan** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *totóti, totot–* ripened, turning color] : spots on a fish's tail
*v.t.* **jíntseta** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *tséketi* to pull out] : to pull the tail off of
*v.i.* **jíntsina** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *tsináti* to become deswollen] 1 : for the tail to become deswollen 2 : for the penis to become deswollen

*n.* **jínwachorin** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *wácho* soft + *–rin*, interrogative suf.] : a species of lisa fish –Used mostly among Konibo speakers. ⟨**Non jínwachori píketianronki, non báke jímia chíxotai.** They say that if we eat the *lisa* fish, our little child gets bloody diarrhea⟩
*v.t.* **jínxaxba** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the male parts + *xáxati* to scrape] : to scrape the male parts of
*v.t.* **jínxtea** [from Shipibo *jin–* on the tail + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut (at the tail)

*n.* **jiráfanin** [from Spanish; and this from Arabic *zarafa*] : giraffe ⟨**Jírafa jáke Ajírikain. Jawen níti iki keyá, téxo nenké.** The giraffe lives in Africa. It is very tall and has a very long neck.⟩

*adj.* **jíriaton** [from Shipibo *jíriti, jíri-* to survive + *-ya* with] : alive : living ⟨**Nato jóni jenén réteara máwatama iki; jíriapari riki.** This drowned man is not dead; he is still alive.⟩

*v.t.* **jíriaa** *Konibo* **jíriaka** 1 : to revive : to bring back to life ⟨**Piróta áakinra jonín máxkake; játianra ompáx jáki chikoxonres jíriakanke.** While playing soccer, a man fainted; then they threw water on him until they revived him.⟩ 2 : to save the life of ⟨**Ronón nátexa máwatainbishokora rókotoron nato jóni jíriake.** The doctor saved the life of this man who was about to die from a snakebite.⟩ 3 : to resurrect ⟨**Ríosenronki Jísokiristo jírianike.** They say God resurrected Jesus Christ.⟩ *syn.* jiwéati

*adj.* **jírioman** *Konibo* **jíriomatonin** [from Shipibo *jíriti, jíri-* to survive + *-oma* without] 1 : paralyzed ⟨**Rabé báritia riki nato jonín yóra moa jírioma.** It has been two years for this man's body to be paralyzed.⟩ 2 : without feeling ⟨**Nato aínbaon kíshira jírioma iki; jáwekeska ikáxa jíriamai.** This woman's thigh has no feeling; perhaps it will not recover.⟩ 3 : dead : lifeless ⟨**Bóchikiáx páketa bákera, jawen papán jírioma bóke.** The boy who fell from a height was carried by his father, lifeless.⟩

*v.i.* **jíriribia** [from Shipibo *jíriti* to live + *ribi* again] : to revive ⟨**Máwatáxbira nato aínbo jíriribike, rókotoron ráo xétemaa.** This woman was unconscious, but she revived when the doctor made her smell a medicine.⟩ *syn.* jíriti

*v.i.* **jíria** 1 : to survive ⟨**Abion pakéketianra westíora aínbobicho jíria iki.** A plane crashed and only one woman survived.⟩ 2 : to revive ⟨**Kakónkonia jónira jiwín réteabi jírike, ráo xéamakana.** A man from Caco was crushed by a tree but revived when they made him drink medicine.⟩ 3 : to resurrect ⟨**Nato néte sénenketianra noa jírinonxiki —akinra jóni máwatataton jawen báke áke, namá meranxon.** A deceased man told his son in a dream: —We will be resurrected at the end of the world.⟩ *syn.* jíriribiti
*n.* **jisátonin** : appearance ⟨**Nato jónira kíkin yóashi iki itan jawen jisáribira jakómayora iki.** This man is truly wretched, and of very ugly appearance.⟩

*postp.* **jisákeskatonin** [from Shipibo *jisá* appearance + *keska* like] : like : looking exactly the same as (another) ⟨**Nokon papán nóntira nato jónina jisákeskaribi iki.** My father's canoe looks exactly like this man's.⟩
*v.t.* [from Shipibo *jísti, jis-* to see + *-we*, imperative suf.] –Used in the sense of "here, take this" to indicate that someone should take something being handed to them.
*adv.* –Used in the sense of "e.g." –Rarely used nowadays.

*Konibo* **jisténhati** *v.t.* **jishténhaa** *Konibo* **jisténhaka** : to wake (someone) up ⟨**Papánra jawen bákebo paénxon oxá jishténhake.** The drunken father woke up his children while they were sleeping.⟩ *syn.* ráteti
*Konibo* **jisténti** *v.t.* **jíshtena** *Konibo* **jístena** : to wake up ⟨**Báke wíniaitianra ea oxá jishténke.** When the baby was crying, I woke up from my sleep.⟩

*adj.* **jishtín** [from Shipibo *jísti, jis-* to see + *-ti* with which] : visible ⟨**Moátianronki róookon yoshín jíshtibires ikátiai.** They say that long ago the demon that causes whooping cough was quite visible.⟩

*adj.* **jíshtiman** *Konibo* **jíshtimanin** [from Shipibo *jishti* visible + *-ma* not] : invisible ⟨**Máwataboronki yamé níai, ikáxbi jíshtima.** They say the dead walk about at night, but they are invisible.⟩
*n.* **jísisin** : ischimi (a small biting insect) ⟨**Westíora bákera jisís jawen pabíkiain jíkiax mawáke.** A boy died because an *ischimi* got into his ear.⟩

*also* **Jisóskiristo** *also* **Jésukristo** *n.* **Jísokiristonin** *also* **Jisóskiristonin** *also* **Jésukristonin** [from Spanish] : Jesus Christ ⟨**Jísokiristonra áke aínbo benche oímakin.** Jesus Christ made a blind woman see.⟩ ⟨**Jisóskiritonra mawá jíriake tsón áyamainbi.** Jesus Christ resurrected a dead person, something no one else could do.⟩
*n.* **jísoman** : urine ⟨**Sarámpinin íkín jisón xéaaronki noa benxontiki.** They say that when someone has measles and drinks urine, they can be cured.⟩
*v.i.* **jísona** : to urinate ⟨**Ja chiraparonki ronín iki noki jísonai; jákopi ói béai.** They say the rainbow is a boa that urinates on us, and that is why the rain falls.⟩
*also* **Jesós** *n.* **Jísosen** *also* **Jésosen** [from Spanish] : Jesus –Also used in the vocative form *Jisosé*. *syn.* Kisós

*v.t.* **jisá** : to see ⟨**Pápa chopán mároara en jisá iki métsama; játian titánbiribi jisára jakón iki.** I see that the cloth papa bought is ugly, but mama sees it as pretty.⟩ ⟨**Ochó jóainbira en jíske jawéki papía jóaitian.** He was far away, but I saw that he was coming carrying the things.⟩ ⟨**Westíora yóximanronki jóni nókoxon yókata iki: ¿Minki néno jóni wínotai oínyamaa? Jánra nokon kabáyo bóke yómetsokin —akin aká iki. Játian yóia iki: Enra jisáma iki; westíora aínbobichoresa en oínke; ikáxbira kabáyooma íke —akin aká iki.** A certain demon met a man and asked him: —Haven't you seen a man pass by here? He stole my horse and took off with it. Then the man answered: —I haven't seen him. I only saw a woman, but she had no horse.⟩ *syn.* JISTI, OINTI both translate as "to see," but OINTI, the usual word, is found much more frequently.

*v.t.* **jiwéaa** *Konibo* **jiwéaka** **1** : to restore from a very serious illness or from an apparent state of death : to bring back to life : to revive ⟨**Moa máxkakenbira rókotoron jiwéake.** Although he was already as good as dead, the doctor revived him.⟩ **2** : to raise (small animals or birds) carefully so that they don't die young ⟨**Róo bakera titán jiwéake, yamébobi xéamakin.** The mother raised a baby howler monkey so carefully that it didn't die; she even gave it something to drink at night.⟩ *syn.* **jíriati**

*v.i.* **jíweta** **1** : to recover from a very serious illness or from a mortal state ⟨**Nato báke ísinai ikax óshishoko ikátiaira moa jiwéke jawen yóra moa** **bénxoax.** This child, who was so thin from having been sick for a long time, has recovered and is now healthy.⟩ 2 : to survive (birds and small animals taken in from the forest) ⟨**Nato joshínshino bakeshoko biára moa jiwéke; rámara ícha píai.** This baby pucahuapo (red uakari monkey) that I got from the forest has survived, and now it eats a lot.⟩

*n.* **jiwín** 1 : tree ⟨**Chósko pácha jíwira non xáteke; jánra non motórobo bíai.** We have cut down four hundred trees, with which we will buy motors (outboard boat motors).⟩ 2 : stick : wood ⟨**Nétetiibira non jíwi pápiai pátoronin yónoa.** Every day we carry wood by order of the boss.⟩ *syn.* jawéki
See under **kenchá**
See under **kíni**
*n.* [from Shipibo *jíwi* tree + *máxka* upper part] : treetop ⟨**Jíwimaxkainoax páketaxa báke mawáke.** The boy died from falling out of the treetop.⟩
See under **ráo**
See under **sánto**
*n.* **jíwi xakitinín** [from Shipibo *jíwi* wood + *xákiti* grater, rasp] : wood rasp

*pl.* **–be** *modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *jóti,* pl. *béti* to come] : upon coming : while coming ⟨**Nato páena jónira yantán joí tatíipatanjoke.** This drunken man came stumbling along at dusk.⟩ ⟨**Káchiokeáx jokínra en iso rétepatanbeke.** On my way back from the forest, I came along killing spider monkeys as I went.⟩
*n.* **joán** : flower ⟨**Bíntiochotianronki non ískoira xobo joán raóati iki.** They say that for the 28th of July we should decorate the school with flowers.⟩

*v.i.* **jóaa** : to bloom : to put out flowers ⟨**Manánxaweronki noa nátexaxki wanín jóaketiampari xépishitiki** They say that when the tortoise bites us, it won't let go until the pijuayo (peach palm) flowers.⟩

*v.t.* **jóaa** : to boil (food) ⟨**Jonín átsa jóaaronki yóshimanki píanana iki.** They say a demon ate the manioc that the man had boiled.⟩ ⟨**Nato paránta joára mératabo méniti iki.** This boiled plantain is for the visitors.⟩
See under **átsa**
*n.* **jobón** : a lump in the muscles ⟨**Káshibaon pía méetaxonki noa jóbo píkotai.** They say that if we touch the arrows of the Cashibo, a lump can appear on us.⟩

*v.t.* **jóboaa** *Konibo* **jóboaka** : to carry (something wrapped in one's clothing) ⟨**Jawen jawéki jóboaxon bóaitianra, yómetsobaon jóni bichínke.** While a man was carrying his belongings wrapped in his clothing, thieves stole them from him.⟩
*v.i.* **jóboa** : to have or develop a tumor ⟨**Jónira wetsa nawabaon jawéki méetax jóboke.** The man touched things belonging to other tribes and developed a tumor.⟩

*v.i.* **jóboa** : to get or have a lump in the muscle ⟨**Noa nanén tsákaaronki jóboti iki; jóboxonronki náne bimin xeyóti iki.** They say that if the huito fruit hits us, it raises a lump, and that the lump can be made to disappear by massaging it with the same fruit.⟩

*n.* **jobóxkon** *Konibo* **jobóxkonin** : testicles ⟨**Westíora yósishokoronki jawen babánki jobóxkoki pián tsákaxon rétenike.** They say that long ago a little old man was killed by his grandson, who had shot him in the testicles with an arrow.⟩
*n.* **jochín** : older brother of a man or woman ⟨**Jawen jochín jói ninkáxonyamaitianra nato báke jawen papán ríxkike.** When this child did not obey his older brother, his father whipped him.⟩

*Konibo* **jóchipapa** *n.* **jóchiyosin** *Konibo* **jóchipapan** [from Shipibo *jóchi* older brother + *yósi* old man, or *pápa* father, dad] : great-grandfather; *also* : brother of the great-grandfather –The vocative form *jochi papá* is used both among Shipibo speakers and Konibo speakers to address the person in question. *syn.* yósi
See **jorío**
See under **íbirio joi**
See **joríoma**

*n.* **jóekan** : light; *specif.* : electric light ⟨**Xawányainronki yamé joé píkotai jaton jémanapon.** They say that in Shahuaya, a light appears at night in people's yards.⟩ ⟨**Nokon xóbora joéya iki.** My house has electric light.⟩

*v.t.* **joéaa** *Konibo* **joéaka** : to shine on : to focus (a light) on ⟨**Papánra rintírinaman jónibo joéake, tsóaborin ixon oínkaskin.** Dad shone the flashlight on the people to see who they were.⟩
*v.i.* **jóeta** : to shine ⟨**Ja manánkini meranronkiki makán jóetairibi.** They say there was also a stone in the cave that shone.⟩ *syn.* penéti; soíti

*n.* **joín** 1 : word; *specif.* : a word as a grammatical unit of a language ⟨**Ja jóira en yóiti átipanyamake.** I can't pronounce that word.⟩ 2 : message ⟨**Aínbaonra Páokochankoxon Máioxiain jawen béneki jói ráanke, jawen pápa pishtákonin réteketian.** A woman sent a message to her husband from Paococha to Pucallpa, informing him that her father had been murdered by the pishtacos.⟩ 3 : language ⟨**Inkán jónibaonronki non joínbi jato yóikatitai.** They say the Inca's messengers used to speak to them in our language.⟩ 4 : voice ⟨**Jawen jói móa wiríshke.** His voice has broken into falsetto.⟩ *syn.* yóia
*n.* **joí akaitonin** [from Shipibo *jói* word + *áti* to do] : disciple

*adj.* **jóikoman** [from Shipibo *jói* word + *-koma* difficult, impossible] : stuttering ⟨**Báke kári pímaaronki jóikomatai.** They say that giving sweet potato to a small child makes them stutter.⟩ *syn.* JOIKOMA, YOSHINBAKE both can be translated as "stuttering," but JOIKOMA emphasizes the inability to speak, while YOSHINBAKE may faintly suggest a demonic influence that the stutterer might be suffering from.
See under **réteti**
See under **ísa**
*n.* **jóiman** : breathing : breath ⟨**Nato jóninra join bismánhaxon mái tsákake.** This man lost his breath and fell to the ground.⟩
*n.* **joín imamiston** : slanderer *syn.* jánso
See under **ninkáti**
*v.t.* **jóina** : to breathe ⟨**Nato jenén rétea aínbaonra moa jóinai.** This woman who was drowning is breathing now.⟩

*n.* **jóintinin** [from Shipibo *joínti, join-* to breathe + *-ti* with which] : heart ⟨**Róniman joíntironki bómpo keska iki.** They say the heart of the yacumama (mythical water-boa) is like a bass drum.⟩
[from Shipibo *joínti, jóintinin* heart + *-shoko*, diminutive suf. + *-res* only + *íti* to be] : to die —to be at the point of death

*adj.* **jóioman** *Konibo* **jóiomatonin** [from Shipibo *jói* word + *-oma* without] : mute ⟨**Westíora jóni, jóioma ikénbi onánya-** **maxonra sontari iti koáratianin yatánike.** A guard detained a certain man for military service without knowing that he was mute.⟩ *syn.* kénto
*interj.* —Used by women as a response to a greeting. *syn.* See under **jéje**
*v.t.* **jojóaka** : to bark in the direction of ⟨**Ochítinin jojóakara báke íshtoi káke, natéxnaketian.** When the dog barked at him, the boy ran off, afraid it would bite him.⟩
*v.i.* **jojóika** : to bark ⟨**Nato ochítira yamé jojóishinai yómetsobo akí.** This dog has been barking all night at thieves.⟩

*n.* **jokán** [from Spanish] : seal ⟨**Jókara jáke Asiain jainoax Nóriti Amírikain. Jara jáke jene meran. Jainoax maínribira níai, ikáxbi nikáskimai.** The seal lives in Asia and in North America. It lives in the water, but it also moves about on land, although with difficulty.⟩

*v.t.* **jókaa** : to skin (an animal) : to flay ⟨**Nokon pátoroninra ea ronón ewa jókamake.** By order of my boss I skinned a large boa.⟩ ⟨**Moa joká ikénbira nato báke ínoki ráketai.** This child is afraid of the jaguar even though it is already skinned.⟩
*v.i.* **jókata** : to end up skinned or flayed (e.g., an animal)
*interj.* [from Shipibo *jóti, jo-* to come + *-ki* to, against] –Used in repeated form as a phrase to call someone to come. –Used mostly among speakers of Pishquibo.
*n.* **jókonaton** [from Shipibo *jókona*, participle of *jokónti* to come out (e.g., blisters)] : a rash of blisters or pimples over the whole body

*v.i.* **jokónhaa** *Konibo* **jokónhaka** : to bring out, or make come out (a group or a mass) ⟨**Maístoronra bákebo jokónhake tsínikanon ixon.** The teacher sent the students out to play.⟩ ⟨**Titánra jawen mapó mein jokónhake.** The mother brought out her batch of clay prepared with charcoal from burnt apacharama bark.⟩

*v.i.* **jókona** : to come out (e.g., a group of animals, or otherwise blisters, pimples, blood, or measles) ⟨**Nato jónira jawen yóránko toxbábo jokónke.** This man broke out in blisters all over his body.⟩ ⟨**Yáwara jokónke.** A herd of white-lipped peccaries has come out.⟩ ⟨**Westíora jóni máwatara jawen kéxakan jími jókona iki.** Blood came out of a dead man's mouth.⟩ ⟨**Sarámpi jokónxonra en yonáke, rabé néte.** When I broke out with measles, I had a fever for two days.⟩ *syn.* JOKONTI, PIKOTI both can be translated as "to come out," but JOKONTI implies several things or a mass coming out, while PIKOTI implies only one.
*v.t.* **jómexa** [from Shipibo *jon–* on the scrotum + *méxati* to pull out, pluck] : to pull out (a man's) pubic hair

*v.i.* **káchoa** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *cho*, an element also in, e.g., *béchoti* to furrow (the brows)] : to have or be (e.g., from old age) with wrinkles on the back

*v.i.* **kaéxika** : to clear one's throat ⟨**Sipán píi míshkitasha ea kaéxike.** While eating sardines, I choked on a bone and cleared my throat to get it out.⟩
*n.* **kaéxkaexen** [from Shipibo *kaéx*, imitative of its call] : a kind of small white bird resembling a gull and having red eyes
*adj.* **kaíaitonin** [from Shipibo; pres. part. of *kaíati* to make increase] : indigenous : typical : native ⟨**Yáma riki kaíakanai jawéki Piróoain jaá.** Llamas are animals native to Peru.⟩
*v.t.* **kái aka** [from Shipibo *kái*, from *móara ea kái* I'm leaving now + *-ati* to do] : to take leave of –Used of the one who takes leave upon departing.

*v.t.* **kaíaa** *Konibo* **kaíaka** : to make something that reproduces increase ⟨**Nato báritianra non átapa moa kaíaa íkeanke, noa jenén mápoyamaketian.** This year we would have increased our hens if the flood had not covered our land.⟩

*n.* **kaíbon** *Konibo* **kaíbaon** *pish.* **kaíbaen** [from Shipibo *kaíati*, *kai-* root of *kaíati* to increase + *-bo* pl. *suf.*] 1 : fellow countryman : a person who speaks the same language and is from the same place or region as another ⟨**Nato bákera kaíbooma iki; jákopira jábichoshoko iki.** This child is all alone because he has no fellow countrymen nearby.⟩ 2 : animal of the same species ⟨**Nato ochítira jawen kaíbaon aká iki.** This dog was attacked by another dog.⟩ 3 : others –Used to point out a second group distinguished from a first group of the same species. ⟨**Jatíribi jónibora jakóma iki; kaíbora jakón iki.** Some people are bad; others are good.⟩

*n.* **kaímiton** [from Spanish] : caimito (a tropical fruit tree); *also* : the fruit of the caimito ⟨**Papán kaímito beá kókoaxa báke képoke.** The child stained his lips eating the caimitos that dad had brought.⟩
*n.* **káiman** : a kind of blue and red macaw ⟨**Papánra kaín pei máitiake.** Dad made a crown from the feathers of the *kaín* macaw.⟩

*modifying suf.* **-bain** [from Shipibo *ka-*, root of *káti* to go, or *-bo*, pl. *suf.* + *-ain*, locative *postp.* *suf.*] –Used with the meaning of "upon leaving" or "and to leave," added to the verb's action. –Used in the form *-cain* with intransitive verbs and in the form *-bain* with plural intransitive verbs and transitive verbs. –Used with a reduplicated verb root to imply action and coordination of movements. ⟨**Ishto káyamaketianra báke yómetsobaon yatánke; jaskáaxonra ríshkikanke.** The thieves grabbed and beat the boy because he did not run away.⟩ ⟨**Xóbo meranoax íshtobaini boshónra páenabaon jéne tsákakanke.** A group of drunks ran out of the house and threw themselves into the water.⟩ ⟨**Kakónkoniabora kampánya aki Jonín Páboroain béwabewabaini bokánke.** Many people from Caco went off singing to attend a campaign in Junín Pablo.⟩ ⟨**Ishtón pikín jétejetebainira jóni káke.** By eating quickly, the man went off choking.⟩ ⟨**Jónibora ápo jóai óini raóbaini bokánke.** Everyone adorned themselves and went off to watch the President coming.⟩ ⟨**Bái napon jóni páena rákatara en kakín oínibake.** As I went, I saw a drunk man lying in the middle of the road, and I passed on by.⟩ ⟨**Kaíronki réokookainyantanke.** They say he turned around as he was leaving.⟩ ⟨**Jara tántikainke.** She rested and left.⟩
See under **keó**

*n.* **káinsin** : a kind of palm with small fruit like that of the shapaja ⟨**Moátianronki jóxoshinonki manánxawe kaínsbochiki bónike.** They tell that once the white monkey carried the tortoise to the top of the *kaíns* palm.⟩
*n.* **Káisan** –Used as a female name.

*v.i.* **káita** : to increase (living beings) ⟨**Non wákabo káita ikénra non jéma moa weníke.** Our community has prospered because our livestock has increased.⟩ ⟨**Máioshiainra moa yómetsobo kaíke.** The thieves have increased in Pucallpa.⟩
See under **wása**
*n.* **kaján** [from Spanish] : box ⟨**Rákexto paróyara kája keska iki.** The cube resembles a box.⟩
*n.* **kájikan** [from Spanish] : coffee ⟨**Yamékiritiibira nokon pátoronin kají shéai.** Every morning my boss drinks coffee.⟩
*n.* **kajónshokon** [from Spanish *kajón* + Shipibo *-shoko*, diminutive *suf.*] : small box : little box

*v.t.* **kákaa** *Konibo* **kákaaka** : to spread out (e.g., a mat) on the ground ⟨**Mératabo nokóketianra papán jawen kawín benáshaman kákaake.** When the visitors arrived, dad spread out the brand-new mat for them to sit on.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbaon jawen chópabo moa kákaakenbira ói máanke.** When this woman had spread out her clothes in the sun, it began to rain.⟩
*n.* **kákaman** : hump of a tapir ⟨**Papánra awá jawen kakánki rérake.** Dad struck the tapir's hump with a machete.⟩
*n.* **kakín** [from Spanish] : khaki ⟨**Píshtatianra bákebo káki chópayabíres márachankanai.** During the festival the children all march dressed in khaki.⟩
See under **chópa**
*n.* **kákiman** : small basket ⟨**Moa waxmén bekánxonra titán jawen kákiman napóke.** After spreading out the cotton boll, mom put it in her small basket.⟩ *syn.* sintán

*n.* **kámaman** 1 : a kind of animal whose cry is expressed as *béx* in Shipibo ⟨**Kámparonki moátianki kámaman chibánike.** They tell that once a Campa was pursued by a ca*mán.*⟩ 2 : animal *kamán* ghost : a kind of ghost the size of a jaguar, with brown skin, with rainbow stripes on each side and with hair hanging over its forehead ⟨**Kámamanronki noa beyósaxon réteti iki; jaskáaxonronki noa jíwi poyanbo jantísati iki.** They say that the *kamán* ghost drives us mad, then kills us, and afterward fills our mouth with branches.⟩

*postp. and conj.* [from Quechua *-kaman* until + Ship. *-me* in, at] *postp.* : until, up to –Used with a person or place complement bearing a postposition suffix, or with a thing or time complement without such a suffix. ⟨**Min yónoara en mia xóbo kamanres bóxonai, íweyora íketian.** I will carry what you entrusted to me only as far as the house, because it is very heavy.⟩ ⟨**Eíba kaman mia káketianra, en jawéki máromati iki; mia káyamakenra en wétsabo ímai.** If you go as far as my house, I will sell you something; if not, I will sell it to others.⟩ ⟨**¿Nénoax Máioshiain kamanki min ea jáwetii kopíati iki?** From here to Pucallpa, how much will you pay me?⟩ ⟨**Nato jonín ribínxonbi ea kopíayamaitianra, báritia kamanres en mánai; ea áyamaitianra en pórisiabo yatámai.** I will wait for this man to pay me only until the summer (dry season); if not, I will have him arrested by the police.⟩ *conj.* : until –Used to introduce a subordinate clause with a verb in -ai. ⟨**Icha binónra en píke, pórokan chéxai kaman.** I ate many aguajes (fruit of the aguaje palm) until my stomach began to hurt.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.1; 7.7.2 *syn.* asta

*n.* **kamárinin** : tamshi (a climbing vine used for lashing) ⟨**Kamári kóshi íketianra papán ján xóbo kano néxake.** Dad lashed the house frame with tamshi, because he knows it is very strong.⟩ *syn.* ayáx

*n.* **kámaronkan** : a kind of seed that comes from abroad and is the size of olives ⟨**Kámaronka béroya bexnán méskoxon xéaaxa jóni paénke.** Upon drinking the liquor he had mixed with *kámaronka* seeds, the man got dizzy.⟩
*n.* **kámarontin** : an inferior kind of ayahuasca ⟨**Kámaronti xéaaxbira paényamake.** Although he drank *kámaronti* ayahuasca, he had no vision.⟩
*adj.* **kámesen** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *metsá* beautiful] : having a beautifully painted back –Used of the cushma (a traditional robe).
*v.t.* : to pluck the back feathers of

*also* camello *n.* **kamíchonin** *also* **kaméllonin** : camel ⟨**Kamíchora jáke Ajírikain, jáinoax Asiain; ikáshbi ja jatíbitian jaín ói béyamainbores.** The camel lives in Africa and Asia, where the climate is always dry.⟩
*n.* **kámisin** : pituca (an edible tuber) ⟨**Papánra waínkonia kamís pápike.** Dad carried the pitucas from the garden plot.⟩

*v.i.* **kámita** 1 : to strain when lifting something : to bear down ⟨**Atsa sako pápiira épa kamíke.** When loading the sack of manioc, my uncle strained to lift it.⟩ 2 : to bear down or strain when giving birth ⟨**Kikínbiresi kámitaxa aínbo bakénke.** The woman gave birth straining hard.⟩ 3 : to strain or bear down when defecating ⟨**Póiira báke kamíke.** When defecating, the child bore down.⟩
*v.t.* **kámosa** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the upper surface + *mótsati* to press] : to knead (bread or clay) on the upper surface
*n.* **kámoxen** : shushupe (a bushmaster snake) ⟨**Kámoxen noa nátexaronki noa sóoiti iki.** They say that when the shushupe bites us, the bitten part swells up.⟩

*n.* **kampán** : campa : a member of the Campa ethnolinguistic group ⟨**Jónoronkiki kámpa iní.** They say that the collared peccary is the transformation of a Campa from ancient times.⟩ *syn.* See under **ashá**
*n.* **kampányanin** [from Spanish] : campaign ⟨**Kakónkoniabora kampánya aki Jonín Páboroain béwabewabaini bokánke.** Many people from Caco went along singing to attend a campaign in Junín Pablo.⟩

*v.t.* **kámpiana** [from Spanish *kambiar* + Ship. + -n + verbal-derivation suf. + -ti inf. suf.] : to exchange for another ⟨**Yóshiman tárira en biá iki kámpiankin.** I obtained a demon's cushma (a traditional robe) by exchanging my own for it.⟩
*n.* **kampón** [from Spanish] : field (e.g., a sports field or a landing strip)
*modifying suf.* : well, then (emphatic particle) ⟨**Akínkan.** Yes, of course.⟩

*interrogative-mode suf.* –Used with the sense of "and" to introduce a question in an abbreviated clause without a verb. ⟨**¿Mínkan; jáwe jáneati shínanai?** And you, what name are you thinking of giving him?⟩

*verbal suf.* –Used added to the verb to indicate plural number. ⟨**Yóashiko Inka kíni chiní meran pakéketianronki rétekanike.** They tell that when the Inca Mezquino (the Miserly Inca) fell into the dug hole, they killed him.⟩ –Used added to the verb to indicate an indefinite subject. ⟨**Ekira jánsokanai.** Someone is slandering me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*noun suf.* –Used as an ending for the non-basic form of a noun or adjective. ⟨**poró: estómago Pórokanra ea chéxai.** poró: stomach. My stomach hurts.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1

*n.* **kanán** : a kind of macaw with a yellow breast and blue body ⟨**Kána iki xóchi panshín; járonki Inkán xénin sikíniki.** This macaw has a yellow breast because when it was human it painted itself with the fat of the Inca Mezquino (the Miserly Inca).⟩
*n.* **kánakan** : lightning : lightning bolt ⟨**Kaná yoshínronkiki bépobires.** They say that the lightning demon is very bleary-eyed.⟩

*n.* **kánachiarinin** : toé (a hallucinogenic plant, Brugmansia) ⟨**Kánachiarinin kópiaronki báke jími chíxotai.** They say that when the toé cutipas a child (harms it by supernatural means), it becomes sick with dysentery.⟩
*n.* **kánainin** : a kind of súngaro (a large catfish) that lives in turbulent streams ⟨**Amakiria wéamanra kánain ícha iki.** In the Amaquiría stream the *kánain* súngaros are abundant.⟩
See under **máni**

*n.* **kanán ewan** [from Shipibo *kána*, *kanán* a kind of macaw + *-ewa*, augmentative] : a kind of parrot or large macaw that eats pijuayos (peach-palm fruit) ⟨**Komún bími píaitianra papán kanánewa tóoake.** While the *kanán ehua* macaw was eating the fruit of the shihuahuaco (a hardwood tree), dad shot it.⟩

*n.* **kanántanchon** : a kind of large lizard, bluish-green in color, with a gray head ⟨**Kanántanchonronki mái chínikinki, wétsa néteori píkoai.** They say that the *kanántancho* lizard digs a hole in the earth until it reaches the other side of the world.⟩

*v.t.* **kánana** [from Spanish *ganar* + Ship. -n, verbal-derivation suf. + -ti, inf. suf.] 1 : to earn (money) ⟨**Káritiran téexonra en ícha koríki kanánke.** Working on the road, I have earned a lot of money.⟩ 2 : to beat (e.g., in a game) people ⟨**Non pirótanin tsínikin kánanabira nato jónibo rároshaman iki.** Even though we beat them at soccer, these men are very happy.⟩ *syn.* mawínti; xewínti

*also* **kánao** *n.* **kánaooman** *also* **kánaon** [from Shipibo *kána* macaw + *oon*, imitative of its call] : a kind of bird with a yellow breast, bright blue back, and reddish tail ⟨**Kánaooman kéenkinbira en méraya****mai.** I want to have a little *kánaoon* bird and I cannot find one.⟩

*n.* **kánapon** *also* **kánaponin** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *nápo* inside] : spinal cord ⟨**Jonín jawen rawí réraaronki kánapo jíshtibires iká iki.** They tell that a man struck his enemy on the spine with a machete until he reached the marrow.⟩
*also* **Kanadá** *n.* **Kanáranin** *also* **Kanádanin** [from Spanish] : Canada
See under **róno**

*n.* **kánasen** : a toy crossbow or small toy arrow ⟨**Bákebaonra jaton kanás sékeke.** The children broke their toy crossbows.⟩ ⟨**Bákebaonra wanín kanás ákanai.** The children make their little arrows out of pijuayo (peach-palm wood).⟩
See under **yoshín**
*n.* **kánchaman** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *chánko* protuberances on the body] : dorsal fin of a fish
*adj.* **kánchisin** *Konibo* **kánchisen** *also* **kánchisnin** [from Quechua *kanchis*] : seven ⟨**Kánchis báritiara en mia óinama iki.** I have not seen you for seven years.⟩

*v.t.* **kanchónhaka** : to fold in the middle –Used mostly among speakers of Konibo. ⟨**En báchi chíakenbira ea niwén kanchónhake.** I hung up the mosquito net, but the wind folded it in the middle.⟩
*Konibo* **kanchónti** *v.i.* **kánchoa** *Konibo* **kánchona** [*ka-* on the spine + *chon,* imitative of a blow + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to bend in the middle

*n.* **kanénanin** : a kind of tree that causes wounds and swelling and whose leaves are sometimes smoked mixed with tobacco ⟨**Jawen papán kanéna méeketianra báke kópia mawáke.** The child died cutipado (harmed by supernatural means) because his father touched a *kanéna* tree⟩
*v.t.* **kánexa** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *néxake* to tie] : to tie (palm leaves) by joining the midribs

*v.t.* **kánkaa** *Konibo* **kánkaaka** [from Quechua *kanga* spit + Ship. *-ati* to make] 1 : to roast by skewering on a spit ⟨**Titánra mári kánkaake, yámikenti yámaketian.** Mom had to roast the añuje (agouti) by skewering it on a spit, because there was no metal pot.⟩ 2 : to make a spit ⟨**Jíwi kánkaaxonra titán píti xoike.** Having made spits out of sticks, mom roasted the fish.⟩
*n.* **kankámporon** [from Shipibo *kankán* pineapple + *poró* stomach] : a kind of black spider with a large abdomen and yellow stripes that builds its web in the form of a net
*n.* **kánkaman** : pineapple ⟨**Bákeshoko kankán kókomaara óshiai.** When we feed pineapple to a baby, it loses weight⟩
[from Shipibo *bári, barin* sun + *kankán* pineapple] : ayupa
[from Shipibo *pása,* unidentified + *kankán* pineapple] : a kind of pineapple with spines on the edges of its leaves

*also* **kangóro** *n.* **kankóronin** *also* **kangóronin** [from Spanish; and this in turn from Australian English] : kangaroo ⟨**Kankórora jáke Aostaráriain. Ja rékena táe rabé riki nenkémashoko. Ikáxbi ja chínita táe rabéresibi iki neké. Jawen jína riki rastón.** The kangaroo lives in Australia. Its two front legs are very short; the hind ones, long; and its tail, thick.⟩

*n.* **kanón** 1 : house frame ⟨**Xóboanoxonra jawen witábo en moa nichínke; rámara jawen kánobichores maxkáke.** I have set up the house posts to build the house; now only the frame is missing.⟩ 2 : a broad design based on the house frame ⟨**Kánoakin kenéaakayara kéenkanai; wétsa quesca kénera kéenyamakanai. They like the framework-shaped design more than any other.⟩
*n.* **kanótinin** : crossbow : bow ⟨**Nokon kanótira ea torístanin boónke.** A tourist has taken my crossbow.⟩
See under **risbí**

*also* **gánsa** *n.* **kansán** *also* **gansán** [from Spanish] : female goose ⟨**Wétsa netén westíora jawen nétemea kánsa iká iki íaman nónononoi jawen bákeboya.** One day a wild female goose was swimming in the lake with her young.⟩

*adj.* **kánshiman** [from Shipibo *ka-* lengthwise + *panshin* yellow] : dry and yellowish on both faces –Used of a leaf. ⟨**Báke yóitimanra paránta pei kanshin ménoke.** A naughty child burned the yellowish plantain leaves.⟩ ⟨**Paránta ménoxonra jawen péi en kanshínhake.** When burning the plantain, I dried its leaves.⟩
*v.i.* **kánshina** : to dry out yellowish on both faces (of a leaf) ⟨**Yamékiri mechá íwanaxbira nato péi moa kanshínke.** In the morning these leaves were wet, but now they are dry.⟩
*also* **gánso** *n.* **kansón** *also* **gansón** [from Spanish] : goose ⟨**Kánso riki nonón jisábi. Ikáxbi riki téxo nenkéira.** The goose is similar to the duck, but has a longer neck.⟩
*n.* **kantínanin** [from Spanish] : tavern
See under **paránta**

*n.* **kántsiman** : shapaja (a palm) ⟨**Non kantsín pei xóboaara básima íkai; xebón peikayara bási íkai.** A roof built with shapaja leaves does not last; those built with shebón leaves are more durable.⟩
*n.* **kaón** [from Shipibo *káo*, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird
*n.* **káochon** *also* **káochonin** : rubber ⟨**Moátian káochonin téeti káx ítira moa jóke.** He finally came, after having worked rubber for a long time.⟩
*n.* **káochobepoman** [from Shipibo *káocho* rubber + *bepón* resin] : latex
*n.* **kapán** : huáyhuash (a squirrel) ⟨**Kápa naikan benóketianronki tirín ikai.** They say that when the wáywash misses in the sky, thunder sounds.⟩
[from Shipibo *kóro* gray + *kápa* huáyhuash] : a species of huáyhuash
[from Shipibo *yoshín* demon, spirit + *kápa* huáyhuash] : a large red species of huáyhuash

*n.* **kapábonin** : a species of tree with fruit like that of the shimbillo ⟨**Kapábo jíwira choríx iki; já nóntiaara bási íkai.** The wood of the *kapábo* tree is very hard, and the canoes made from it last a long time.⟩

*n.* **kápajoboxkonin** [from Shipibo *kápa* huáyhuash + *jobóxko* testicle] : a species of shrub with small bristly fruit; *also* : the fruit of the *kápajoboxko* shrub ⟨**Kápajoboxkora Pishkín ícha iki; jára kókoti iki.** The *kápajoboxko* fruit is abundant on the Pisqui River and is good to eat.⟩
*n.* **kápaketin** [from Shipibo *ka-* lengthwise + *pakéti* to fall] : shortcut : portage ⟨**Mia máyati káitianra ea kápaketin kái.** You go around, I go by the portage.⟩

*Konibo* **kápananti** *n.* **kápapitin** *Konibo* **kápanantin** [from Shipibo *ca-* on the back + *pápiti* to carry on the back] : an ornament worn on the back ⟨**Pishtánko kakínra kápapiti pápikanai.** When going to the festival, they wear the *kápapiti* ornament hung on the back.⟩

*n.* **kápeten** *Konibo* **kápetan** *ib.* **kápekan** : caiman : lagarto (a caiman) ⟨**Játiobi kapé xéaaxa ronón ewa íaman toxbáke.** The boa floated in the lake because it had swallowed a whole caiman.⟩
[from Shipibo *áni* large + *kapé* lagarto] : crocodile ⟨**Ja ánikapera Ajírikain jáke.** The crocodile lives in Africa.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *kapé* lagarto] : a species of lagarto, black on the upper side and black and white on the underside
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *kapé* lagarto] : a species of caiman of yellowish white color

*n.* **kapéshinin** [from Shipibo *kapé* lagarto + *shin*, element of *panshín* yellow] : a species of white caiman ⟨**Kapéshininronki jóni kíshi tsekánike.** They say that in ancient times it was the white caiman who left a man without a thigh.⟩

*Konibo* **kápetanaxa** *n.* **kápeten axan** *Konibo* **kápetan axan** [from Shipibo *kapé, kápeten* lagarto + *áxa* huaca] : a species of vine with reddish fruit and leaves like those of the sacha ajo
