*v.t.* **kápeta** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *pekéti* to become hollow] : to hollow out (e.g., a roof) at the top

*n.* **kápiman** : a species of weed with a slender reddish stem, small round leaves, and yellow flowers that grows up to ten centimeters tall ⟨**Kapín píaitianra kokán kabóri tsákaibake.** Yesterday, while a taricaya (a river turtle) was eating the *kapín* weed, my uncle wounded it with an arrow.⟩

*n.* **kápitaman** [from Spanish] 1 : military captain ⟨**Jaton kápitaman sínáara moa sontárobo bokánke, banépariti shínanaxbi.** Although the soldiers were thinking of staying longer, they left because their captain scolded them.⟩ 2 : team captain ⟨**Pirótanin tsíniaibora jaton kápitanhoma bekánke; rámara kánameekanai.** The soccer players have come without their captain, and now they are going to lose.⟩

*pl.* **-bo** *modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *káti*, pl. + *bóti* to go] –Used added to the verb, with the sense of "upon going" or "going," and expresses a continuous action. ⟨**Bákera jawen títa chíbani kaí wínipatankake.** The child went along crying while following his mother.⟩ ⟨**Rámashamankayara non ián tánaboai.** Right now we are getting to know this new oxbow lake.⟩ ⟨**Nontín kakínra en isábo oímpatanboke.** While traveling in the canoe, I went along looking at several little birds.⟩
*v.i.* **kápokaata** : to bend : to warp ⟨**Nokon papán xóbo witara moa kápokaake.** The wooden support post of dad's house has bent.⟩
See under **wáme**
*v.t.* **kapónhaka** [from Spanish *kapón* + *áti, -ati* to make] : to geld : to castrate ⟨**Kapónhanoxonra nato kóchi non chítoke.** In order to geld this pig, we had to spread its hind legs.⟩

*n.* **káposoron** [from Spanish *kápsula*] : percussion cap used for a muzzleloader shotgun ⟨**Nokon káposoron yómetsoketianra en báke mérake.** I found the boy who had stolen my percussion caps for firing the shotgun.⟩

*v.t.* **kápoa** : to bend : to warp ⟨**Níwe koshínra jíwi kápoke.** A strong wind bent the tree⟩ ⟨**Jíwi kapó namanra jóni páena rakáke.** Under the bent tree the drunk man lies.⟩ *syn.* éxpaati; kátoti
*v.i.* **kápota** : to bend : to warp ⟨**Nato jíwira niwén aká kapóke; ikáxbira sekéyamai.** This tree has bent from the action of the wind, but it is not going to break.⟩
*v.t.* **kápota** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *pótati* to throw or *pókoti* to dye] : to apply powder to the back of (e.g., a person or fish)
*n.* **karán** : a species of large toad ⟨**Karánronki chíi tsisto xéai.** They say that the *kára* toad swallows embers of fire.⟩
*also* **káda** *adj.* [from Spanish] : each : every ⟨**kára néte** each day⟩ ⟨**Maístoronra kára báke méniti jáke jawen teé.** The teacher has to give each student their work.⟩ *syn.* –tiibi
*n.* **káraboson** [from Spanish] : jail cell ⟨**Paénketian káraboso meran níakanara** **sináke.** When they put him in the jail cell for being drunk, he got angry.⟩
*n.* **karájonin** [from Spanish] : demijohn (a large jug) ⟨**Jaton pátoronin bexnán karájonra bikánke ribínkin.** They got their boss's demijohn of liquor on credit.⟩
*v.t.* **karánbea** : to turn something over
*also* **kárnero** *n.* **káraniron** *also* **kárneron** [from Spanish] : ram ⟨**Korákan pátoronin káranirora manóke.** Our curaca's boss's ram got lost.⟩
*also* **kárnerobake** *n.* **káranirobaken** *also* **kárnerobaken** [from Spanish *karnero* + Shipibo *báke* young] : lamb
*also* **kárnerobichi** *n.* **kárinirobichin** *also* **kárnerobichi** [from Spanish *kamíro* ram + *bíchi* skin] : wool
*also* **kárpintero** *n.* **kárapintironin** *also* **kárpinteronin** [from Spanish] : carpenter ⟨**Kárapintirora tábaranin téetai.** The carpenter works with boards.⟩
*also* **kárpeta** *n.* **kárapitan** *also* **kárpetan** : folder
*n.* **kárasiran** [from Spanish] : jail ⟨**Moa kárasira meran ákanabira kopíaax pikóke.** Although they put him in jail, he got out through a bribe.⟩
*n.* **káratanin** [from Spanish] : letter *syn.* kírika
*n.* **karékonin** : kidney ⟨**Ospitariainoaxa jóni mawáke, karéko sóoiketian pótekana.** In the hospital a man died after an operation for inflammation of the kidney.⟩
*n.* **karín** : sweet potato ⟨**Báke kári pímaaronki jóikomatai.** They say that when we feed sweet potato to a little child, it becomes a stutterer.⟩
[from Shipibo *bekó* remocaspi + *kári* sweet potato] : a species of sweet potato of purple color like that of the remocaspi
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *kári* sweet potato] : a species of sweet potato of dark purple color
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *kári* sweet potato] : a variety of sweet potato that is white on the inside
[from Shipibo *panshín* yellow + *kári* sweet potato] : a variety of light-yellow sweet potato
[from Shipibo *xáni* maracana (a small macaw) + *kári* sweet potato] : a variety of sweet potato
[from Shipibo *tokónti* something to put in the mouth + *kári* sweet potato] : a variety of yellow sweet potato
*n.* **karíbonin** [from Spanish] : caribou ⟨**Ja karibó riki nékea cháxobebon áni, ikaxbi ja jisáribi.** The caribou is bigger than the deer, but similar to it.⟩
*n.* **karínanin** [from Spanish] : chain ⟨**Yómetso jónira karínanin néxaxon kárasira meran akánke.** They put chains on the thief and threw him in jail.⟩
*n.* **karítinin** [from Spanish] : spool ⟨**Sinyóro, ea máromawe rabé karíti yomán.** Sir, sell me two spools of thread.⟩
*n.* **káritiran** [from Spanish] : highway ⟨**Játianra ea káritiran téekatitai.** At that time I worked on the highway.⟩ *syn.* See under baí
*n.* **karón** : firewood ⟨**Papánra káro bénai kaxón westíora jóno réteke.** When dad went to look for firewood, he killed a collared peccary.⟩
*n.* **karón** [from Spanish *karro*] : truck ⟨**Kóarintaiochotianra ea Aweitin káa iki, karón.** In 1948 I went to the Aguaytía river by truck.⟩
*n.* **Károkan** [from Spanish *Karlota*] –Used as a female name.
*v.t.* **károaka** [from Shipibo *káro* firewood + *-ati* to do] : to cut firewood

*Konibo* **karónchompa** *n.* **karónchempaman** *Konibo* **karónchompan** [from Shipibo *káro* firewood + *chempán*, unidentified] : a species of ant very similar to the isula (a large stinging ant) ⟨**Káro béaitianra títa karónchempaman natéxke.** While mom was bringing firewood, a *karónchempan* ant bit her.⟩
*n.* **Károsen** [from Spanish *Karlos*] –Used as a male name.

*n.* **károtaen** [from Shipibo *káro* car + *táe* foot] : tire ⟨**Káochobepon bixónra károtae ákanai.** Tires are made from rubber.⟩ *syn.* KAROTAE, CHANTA both mean "tire," but the word CHANTA, which is a form derived from Spanish, is more common.

*modifying suf.* 1 : to want –Used added to the verb root. ⟨**Nokon wétsaribira kákasai ápo óini.** My brother also wants to go see the president.⟩ ⟨**Nokon títashoko oínkaskin kénamaabira moa máwata ea yóikanke.** When I wanted to see my grandmother and sent for her, they told me she had already passed away.⟩ ⟨**Apo jóti nínkataxa ea oínkasa iki; ixónbira en káti átipanyamaa iki.** On hearing that the president was coming, I wanted to see him; but I couldn't go.⟩ 2 : to want but be unable : to fail to achieve –Used added to the verb root and followed by the suffixes *–quin* and *–ma*, giving the sense of "to fail to achieve." ⟨**Manón bóyakaataxa báke jokáskimai.** When he got stuck in the mud, the boy couldn't manage to get out.⟩ *syn.* –KAS, KEENTI, a verbal suffix and a verb, both can be translated as "to desire," but the use of KEENTI extends more broadly to things that are desired or wanted to be possessed; whereas the verb with –KAS as a suffix and the verb KEENTI take a complement indicating a desired action. Thus "Eara kákasai." and "Eara katín kéenai." can both be translated as "I want to go." with no difference at all. See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*n.* **kashín** : bat ⟨**Moátianronki jonínki káshi ainbo awínhaa ípaonike.** They say a man was once married to a bat woman.⟩
[from Shipibo *báwa* parrot + *káshi* bat] : vampire bat : a species of large bat that feeds on fruit, insects, and blood it sucks from sleeping animals
[from Shipibo *táxa* palizada (a driftwood pile) + *káshi* bat] : a species of tiny bat that typically lives in driftwood piles
See under **pópo**

*n.* **káshibon** *Konibo* **káshibaon** *pish.* **káshibaen** [from Shipibo *káshi* bat + *-bo*, pl. suf.] : the Cacataibo or Cashibo ethnolinguistic group : the Cacataibo or Cashibo : the Cacataibo or Cashibo people
See under **níshi**
*n.* **kashímponin** [from Spanish] : smoking pipe ⟨**Jawen pápashokon kashímpo jótiaxa, nato báke paénke.** This child got dizzy when he smoked his grandfather's pipe.⟩
See under **paránta**

*v.t.* **káshkakashka aká** [from Shipibo *kashka*, imitative + *áti* to do] : to gargle –Used especially with regard to sorcerers and healers. ⟨**Yóbekanra romé káshkakashka akai.** The sorcerer gargles the tobacco liquid.⟩ *syn.* KASHKAKASHKA ATI, TIAN ATI both are translated as "to gargle" and there is no difference. They may share the same orientation toward sorcery.
*n.* **kashón** 1 : casho : the cashew (tree and fruit) 2 : the edible nut of the casho ⟨**Bákera kásho xóo kókoax jampáyooke.** A child's tongue got infected from eating unripe casho.⟩
[from Shipibo *níi* monte (the forest) + *kásho* casho] : a species of wild casho

*v.t.* **kashóaka** [from Shipibo *ka-* lengthwise + *shóati* to pour out] : to sprinkle (over an area) ⟨**Maístoronra jóa banabo ea ómpashen kashóamake.** The teacher had me sprinkle water on the planted flowers.⟩

*also* **gáseosa** *n.* **kásiosan** *also* **gáseosan** [from Spanish] : soft drink ⟨**kásiosa botíria** a bottle of soda⟩ *syn.* KASIOSA, ORANSHI both mean "soft drink" with no difference at all, but ORANSHI is the more established and well-known word.

*Konibo* **kásoaka** *v.t.* [from Quechua *kasuy kasun-* to obey; and this from Spanish *kaso* + *áti* to do, or *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to obey : to heed ⟨**Min ea kásoayamaitianra en mia ríshkiai —akinra papán áke.** Papá said to him: —If you don't obey me, I'll give you a lashing.⟩ *syn.* yóiti íti
*n.* **kásorinan** [from Spanish] : gasoline
*v.t.* [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *sóati* to dust off] : to rub on the back

*n.* **kástichanon** *Konibo* **kástichanonin** [from Spanish] : Spanish (the language) ⟨**Kímisha óxebicho Rimán ikáxa nato aínbo kástichanonin yóyoikai.** After living only three months in Lima, this woman already speaks Spanish.⟩
*v.i.* **kastíkameeta** : to be punished : to suffer punishment ⟨**Kastíkameetash rábinira jóni jabáke.** The man fled out of shame because he was punished.⟩

*v.t.* **kastíkana** [from Spanish *kastigar* + Shipibo *-n*, verbal-derivation suf. + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to punish ⟨**Taría áyamaketianra maístoron bákebo kastíkanke.** Because they didn't do their homework, the teacher punished the pupils.⟩
*n.* **kastíkonin** [from Spanish] : punishment ⟨**Nato yómetso jónira jawen kastíko moa ménikanke.** They have already given this thief his punishment.⟩

*also* **kastór** *n.* **kastóronin** *also* **kastórnin** [from Spanish] : beaver ⟨**Kastóro jáneya yóinara jáke Orópain jaínoax Nóriti Amírikain. Jíwi poyánbo tsínkixonra, jenénko náa ákai.** The animals called beavers live in Europe and in North America. These animals join tree branches and build their nest in the water.⟩
*n.* **katán** 1 : layer (e.g., of an onion) 2 : cape (garment) ⟨**Oinaponra jawen káta sáweax jóke.** He came in the middle of the rain with his cape on.⟩

*v.t.* **kátaa** *Konibo* **kátaaka** 1 : to put one thing on top of another ⟨**Nato jonínra jawen kotón íchayora kátaa áke, mátsiora íketian.** This man put on several shirts, because the day was very cold.⟩ 2 : to build with stacked levels ⟨**Xóboaxonra en kátaakin tápoake.** When I built the house, I put stacked levels at intervals.⟩

*v.i.* **kátaa** 1 : to be in layers or stacked ⟨**Xéki pei kátaara já matsótiaa jakón iki.** Stacked corn husks are good for making brooms.⟩ 2 : to be joined together (long things) with others of the same kind ⟨**Nokon bakén xétara kátake.** My son's molars are crowded together.⟩

*v.i.* **kátaxameeta** 1 : to huddle (hens or animals) 2 : to gather to-gether or be pressed together (people) ⟨**Matsín akára noa kátaxameekanke.** Because of the cold weather, we have huddled closer together.⟩
*n.* **Katáxon** *Konibo* **Katáxonin** [from Spanish *Katalino* + regional Spanish *-xo*, diminutive suf.] –Used as a male name.
*v.i.* **kátaxomeeta** : to be side by side : to be juxtaposed ⟨**Titán chómo kátaxomeetara jatíbi yómetsokanke.** They stole mom's clay jars that were standing side by side.⟩
*v.t.* **kátaxa** : to place side by side ⟨**Papánra jawen nónti katáxke.** Dad placed his canoes one next to the other.⟩
*v.t.* **kátaxa** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *táxoti* to lick] : to lick on the back
*n.* **Katén** –Used as a female name.

*v.t.* **kátea** : to surround : to be around ⟨**Tímaanankanaitian en óinaira ea kátekanke.** While I was watching some people fighting, others came around me.⟩ ⟨**Nato yómetsora moa katé ikax jabáyamaitian yatánkanke.** They caught this thief because they surrounded him and he couldn't escape.⟩
*v.t.* **káteta** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *tékati* to sting] : to sting (e.g., a wasp) on the back

*pl.* **bóti** *v.i.* **káa** *pl.* **boá** 1 : to go; *also* : to leave : to depart –Used in the plural *bóti* when it refers to a subject indicating "several," "many," or "a massive thing." ⟨**Pápara yómerai kawánke.** Dad went off to fish.⟩ ⟨**Níwe béketianra naíkoin boá iki.** When the wind came, the clouds went away.⟩ ⟨**Píshta nete sénenamabira boí íkanai, korákanin jato pára-** **na.** The day of the festival hasn't arrived yet, but they are already leaving because the curaca deceived them.⟩ 2 : to fall (e.g., into the water) ⟨**Min átapara jéne meran kánake.** Careful! Your hen is going to fall into the water.⟩ –Used in the form *katánwe* instead of *kawé* as the imperative. ⟨**Jákiribi min xobón katánwe.** Go back to your house again.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3.2.b

*also* **moara kái** *also* **eara moa kái** [from Shipibo; lit., "I'm leaving now"; from *moa* now + *-ra*, indicative-mood suf. + *ea* I + *kái* I go, from *káti* to go] –Used as a farewell by the one who is leaving; the normal farewell reply is the expression *kawé*, literally "go."

*verbal suf.* **–katit** –Used to indicate the imperfect tense and a distant past. –Used added to the verb and followed by *-ai*, the imperfect suffix. ⟨**Kákonkoxonra non pítibo pikátiai; rámara non arósbicho ákai, Yarínain ixon.** When we were in Caco, we used to eat fish of various kinds; but in Yarina, we eat only rice.⟩ ⟨**Jóriji Bakerínra noa meskó téebo ámakatitai ícha koríkia ixon.** Don Jorge Baker used to send us to do various kinds of work, because he was very rich.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2

*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *-kati*, imperfect-tense suf. + *-ke*, preterite suf.] –Used added to the verb with no other following suffix, to indicate a very distant past tense. ⟨**Ea máxkotianra en Ápo oínkato.** When I was small, I saw the President.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.1
*v.i.* **kátokaata** 1 : to fold ⟨**Nokon papán tárira niwén aká kátokaake.** Dad's cushma (a tunic) got folded by the wind.⟩ 2 : to wrap oneself up
*also* **katóliko** *adj.* **katórikon** *also* **katólikon** [from Spanish; and this from Latin *katholikus*; and this from Greek *kathólikos* universal] : Catholic

*also* **tákatoti** *v.t.* **kátoa** *also* **tákatoa** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *kátoti*] : to fold ⟨**Chópa kátoti onányamaketianra, jawen papán nato báke xóntako sináake.** Her father scolded the girl because she did not know how to fold clothes.⟩ ⟨**Moa chópa kató ikénbira nokon titán mecháake.** Mom soaked the clothes, even though they were already folded.⟩ : to wrap ⟨**Yómetsoninra nokon titán chópa kató bóke.** The thief carried off mom's clothes wrapped up.⟩ *syn.* káwati; kápoti

*v.t.* **kátota** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the upper surface + *tópiti* to gradually pick up] 1 : to sort the grains of (beans or rice), removing what is no good ⟨**Nónbiribi arós kátotaitian, já xéki sako pápiti yóikanke.** While we were sorting the rice, they told him to carry the sack of corn.⟩ 2 : to select (people who are needed) ⟨**Moa jato katókin senénhaxonronki, réteanantiain jato ráanai.** They say that when he finishes selecting them, he is going to send them off to war.⟩

*n.* **katóxkonin** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the top surface + *toxko*, unidentified] : protruding part (e.g., of a branch) ⟨**Jíwi katoxkonimeaxa jóni chorónke.** The man threw himself into the water from the protruding branch of the tree.⟩

*v.i.* **kátsata** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the spine + *tsa*, unidentified + *-ti*, inf. suf.] 1 : to be lying on one's back ⟨**Nato bákera katsáke jawen titán jóintiki ríshkia.** This child is lying on his back because his mother hit him near the heart.⟩ 2 : to stretch the body with the head thrown back ⟨**Nato jónira pirótanin jóintiki tsákaa kátsatai.** This man fell backward because the ball struck him near the heart.⟩
*v.t.* **kátsata** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *tsa*, element of *tsákati* to hit + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to hit on the back by throwing something at

*v.t.* **kátseta** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *tse*, element of *tsékati* to take out + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to take from the back (e.g., a piranha or another carnivorous fish) a bite of flesh from
*n.* **kawán** : a kind of plant with many leaves ⟨**Non káwa xéamaara ochíti méchai.** If we make a dog drink the juice of the *káwa* plant, it becomes a good hunter.⟩
*n.* **káwakan** [from Shipibo *káwaa, kawá*, past part. of *káwati* to package] : package ⟨**Bakísha en mia rabé kawá koríki bómaibake.** Yesterday I sent you two packages of money.⟩ *syn.* mixé

*also* **kawánwanti** *v.i.* **káwana** *also* **kawáwana** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *-wan* just now + *-ti* inf. suf.] 1 : to pass by ⟨**Néno ábion kawánhibake, kikínbires íshto.** Yesterday a very fast airplane passed by here.⟩ 2 : to go from one side to the other : to wander about –Used with reduplicated root. ⟨**Jéma napon kawánkawankinra bakén chíi jamáke.** From wandering about the yard, the child stepped on the fire.⟩ *syn.* wínoti

*v.t.* **káwaa** : to wrap : to package ⟨**Kabóri bachira máni pein káwaxon, titán jawen babán ewa boxónke.** Mom wrapped the taricaya eggs in a banana leaf and took them to her daughter-in-law.⟩ *syn.* kátoti; rákoti

*v.i.* **káwata** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the surface of something long *wa-*, an element of *wáketi* to raise + *-ti* completed-action suf.] : to walk along a height ⟨**Bóchiki jíwi pónyamanra jóni káwatai.** Up among the branches of the tree the man walks.⟩

*n.* **kawátinin** [from Shipibo *kawa-*, root of *káwati* to walk along a height + *-ti* means-by-which] : bridge (e.g., made of crosswise logs) ⟨**Weán shítakin kawáti raínshakaxa jenénko pakéke.** While crossing the stream, he slipped on the bridge and fell into the water.⟩
*interj.* [from Shipibo *kawé*, sing. imperative of *káti* to go] : goodbye –Used at any time of day as a word of farewell addressed to the one who is leaving.
*v.t.* **kawé aka** [from Shipibo *kawé* goodbye + *áti* to do] : to see off –Used of the one who sees off the person leaving.

*n.* **káwiman** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the upper surface + *win*, unidentified] : mat of palm reeds *syn.* KAWIN, PISHIN both can be translated as "mat," but PISHIN, unlike KAWIN, implies a construction made from a single palm leaf.
*n.* **káwiman** : mota (a kind of fish) ⟨**Nokon míshkitira káwiman bóke.** A mota took my fishhook.⟩
[*jóxo* white + *kawín* mota] : a kind of mota that is gray with an elongated body
[from Shipibo *páka* paca + *kawín* mota] : a kind of mota with tiny black spots over its body like those of the paca and also resembling the *jóxokawin* fish
*adj.* **káwisin** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *wíso* black] : blackish on the back
*n.* **kawíshponin** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *wíshpo* long] : a long ridge or hill
*adj.* **kaxán** : crybaby : whiny ⟨**Nato bákera káxayora iki.** This child is very whiny.⟩ *syn.* wíni
*v.i.* **káxaa** : to become whiny ⟨**Ikónbiresi káxaketianra en moén ríshkike.** This child has become very whiny, and I whipped him with ishanga (a stinging nettle).⟩
See under **níshi**

*n.* **káxbakan** [from Shipibo *ka-* lengthwise + *xábati* to yawn] : a flood-prone lowland behind a stretch of cañabrava (wild cane) ⟨**Papánra westíora manánxawe bíke kaxbáin rákata.** Dad picked up a motelo (a tortoise) that was lying in the lowland.⟩
*n.* **kaxkén** [from Shipibo *ka-* to divide + *xke*, unidentified] : part ⟨**Amakiri kaxkera en títa ménike.** I gave mom a part of the gamitana (a fish).⟩

*v.t.* **káxkea** 1 : to split lengthwise : to split in half ⟨**Non kókonon náto santíra káxkewe.** Split this watermelon in half so we can eat it.⟩ 2 : to divide : to do division in arithmetic ⟨**8 ikénbi 2 káxkeara bánetai 4.** 8 divided by 2 equals 4.⟩ *syn.* chapáati
*v.i.* **káxketa** : to split : to crack ⟨**Barín akára náto epán wínti kaxkéke.** My uncle's paddle split from the heat of the sun.⟩
*v.t.* **káxkia** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the top surface + *xákaati* to loosen] : to wear down (wood) on the top surface with a rasp
*v.i.* **káxkita** : to scrape one's back
*n.* **kaxnín** [from Shipibo *ka-* of the back + *ráni* body hair] : back hair
*n.* **kaxón** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *xo*, unidentified] : lower part of the back : loin ⟨**Pápashokora jawen kaxónko chéxaa bachín rakáke.** Grandfather is lying in bed with back pain.⟩
*n.* **kaxón** : amasisa (a tree) ⟨**Xotó bake bíkasira ea nato kaxón néeke.** I wanted to catch the chicks of the *xotó* dove, so I climbed this amasisa.⟩
*n.* **kaxón** : estoraque (a storax tree) ⟨**Nokon káxo banara niwén póxake.** The wind knocked down my estoraque planting.⟩ *syn.* páxaininti
*n.* **káxopanín** : sole (a flatfish) ⟨**Non báke káxopa pímaara jími chíxotai.** If we feed a baby sole, it causes bloody diarrhea.⟩
*n.* **káxo xaon** [from Shipibo *káxo* loin + *xáo* bone] : spine
See under **móxa**
*v.t.* **káxtea** [from Shipibo *ka-* on the back + *xáteti* to cut] 1 : to cut on the back 2 : to crush (e.g., palm leaves) lengthwise
*v.i.* **káxteta** : to get cut on the back

*n.* **kayán** 1 : shadow ⟨**Jawen káyabi méraaxa báke ratéke.** Upon seeing his own shadow, the child got scared.⟩ 2 : reflection ⟨**Jenénkonia jawen káyabimeraaxa ochíti jojó iitai.** The dog is barking because it discovered its reflection in the water.⟩ 3 : soul : that which makes us exist ⟨**Noa óxaketianronki non káya píkotai.** They say that when we sleep, our soul comes out to see what happens in dreams.⟩ *syn.* beí; wéa

*adj.* **kayán** 1 : straight 2 : of high and pure lineage ⟨**Nato parónra káya jónibires jakátikanai, náwabo yámaatian.** In the old days, only people of high and pure lineage lived on the Ucayali River, long before there were Indians, mestizos, and other outsiders.⟩

*-caya* *modifying suf.* 1 : actually ⟨**Bóna xéaaxbira ompáxkaya akáske.** He took bee honey, but what he actually wanted was to drink water.⟩ 2 : with certainty : without doubt ⟨**Rámakayara nato Inka non réteai —ikira ikánike.** Now —they thought— we are surely going to kill this Inca.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.6

*n.* **kayánarin** : a species of large tibe (a fish) ⟨**Kayánarin berón béchexeetaronki méchati iki.** They say that when we put the liquid from the tibe's eye in our eyes, we become good fishermen.⟩

*n.* **káyanenketen** *Konibo* **káyanenkekan** [from Shipibo *káya* straight + *nenké* long] : long straight stretch of the river ⟨**Konchóri íkain riki páro káyanenke.** Where Cunchuri is, there is a very long straight stretch of the Ucayali.⟩
See under **ísa**
See under **tsáwi**
*n.* : Callería ⟨**Kayáriankoniaboronki róookon íkai.** They say that the inhabitants of Kallería have whooping cough.⟩
*n.* **káyatsawin** [from Shipibo *káya* straight + *tsáwi*, unidentified] : dorado (a fish) ⟨**Anirikan ákaibaonra nóntibocho káyatsawi bikánke.** The fishermen filled a canoe with dorados.⟩

*n.* **káyatsekakan** [from Shipibo *káya* shadow + *tsékati, tseka-* to take out] : photo ⟨**nokon káyatseka** my photo⟩ *syn.* KAYATSEKA, JOTO both mean "photo" without distinction. KAYATSEKA, the purely Shipibo word, is used less than JOTO, a loanword from Spanish that is more established in the language.
*n.* [from Spanish] —Used as the name of the letter *q* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *kexá* lip] 1 : at the upper lip : on the upper lip : of the upper lip ⟨**kébichi** upper lip of the mouth⟩ 2 : through vertical extension ⟨**keónti** to skewer, thread through⟩ 3 : across the edge ⟨**kemóntanti** to overflow (a river)⟩ 4 : with the teeth ⟨**keróxati** to crunch⟩ 5 : to the taste ⟨**kebá** sweet to the taste⟩ 6 : in the mouth : on both lips ⟨**kempís** having bad breath⟩ ⟨**kekóx** blowing hard⟩ ⟨**kewínti** to answer energetically⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.4

*verbal suf.* —Generally used as a preterite to indicate a past, completed action of a verb in the indicative mood. ⟨**Moara jawén xobón káke.** He has already gone to his house.⟩ —Used with some verbs to indicate the present tense of the indicative for certain verbs that express a mental fact or a state of being. ⟨**Jaínra yakáke.** He is sitting there.⟩ ⟨**Enra mia akínti átipanyamake.** I can't help you.⟩ ⟨**Enra jawen pápa onánke.** I know his father.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.1

*postpositional suf.* : of, from —Used in a sentence attached to a noun, adverb, or postposition ending in *x* or in a non-nasalized vowel, or to the postposition *manaon*, to indicate a place of origin. —Often used together with *–ax* in the compound form *–keax* to indicate a place of provenance. ⟨**Enra xóbo patáxkea binón béke.** I brought aguaje fruits (a palm fruit) from beside the house.⟩ ⟨**Jara xóbo chichokeáx jóke.** He has come out from inside the house.⟩ ⟨**Papánra xóbo manaonkea pía béke.** Papa got the arrow from above the house.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2

*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *an*, element of *jankénti* to finish] : on the verge of happening : almost —Used attached to the main verb when it is not followed by a subordinate verb. ⟨**Karónra ea rétekeanke.** The car almost killed me.⟩ —Used attached to the verb that specifies the unrealized result of a contrary-to-fact condition. ⟨**Amakiri cháchixonra en nokon títa betan píkeanke yonánhaxon.** If I had speared the gamitana (a large river fish), my mother and I would have roasted and eaten it.⟩ ⟨**Oi béyamaketianra, ea jókeanke.** If it hadn't rained, I would have come.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*n.* **kébakan** [from Shipibo *ke–* to the taste + *báta* sweet] : sweet to the taste

*n.* **kébawanin** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *báwa* parrot] : bocón (a big-billed parrot) ⟨**Kebáwa —akinra non ákai jawen kexa áni íketian.** We call it "bokón" because its mouth/beak is wide.⟩

*v.i.* **kebénokoota** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *benóti* to go astray + *–koo* reflexive suf.] : to mispronounce : to make a mistake while speaking or singing ⟨**Béwaira nokon pápa kebénokooke; játianra osánkanke.** My father made a mistake while singing, and they started laughing at him.⟩ ⟨**Kebénokooyamanon min kírika onánwe.** Review the book so that you can read it without making mistakes.⟩

*v.t.* **kébena** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *bénati* to search] : to search carefully on the lips ⟨**Enra titán jopóx bénakin kebénke.** I carefully searched mama's lips for isango (a small biting insect).⟩
*v.t.* **kébesa** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *bétsati* to finish] : to finish off along the edge of (e.g., a canoe)
*adj.* **kébexen** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *béxa* rough] 1 : jagged along the edge —Used, e.g., of a file, emery, or a whetstone. 2 : having pimples on the edge of the lips

*Konibo* **kébichi** *n.* **kébikan** *Konibo* **kébichin** *Konibo* **kébichinin** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *bichi* skin] : lower lip ⟨**Kebí nenké, kebí áni, kebí rastón riki mía.** Of wide lip, of big lip, of thick lip are you.⟩ ⟨**Eara** **kébichiki binán tékake.** A wasp stung me on the upper lip⟩

*v.i.* **kébiika** : to mutter through clenched teeth : to speak in a low voice ⟨**Nímara kébiike parántanin yóashii, ikáxbira non ninkáyamake; jaskárake janbíx ea akí.** Nima himself told me that he spoke in a low voice to keep his plantains from us, but nobody understood him — that's what he told me.⟩ ⟨**Anara sínati kébi ikai ichámisi; ikáxbira tsón ninkáyamai yóyoikai.** When Ana is upset, she insults everyone in a low voice, but nobody hears what she says.⟩
*adj.* **kébisin** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *bísi* rash] : having a rash on the inside of the lips

*n.* **kébisasan** [from Shipibo *kebí* lower lip + *sése* freckled] : a species of small snail that lives attached to aquatic plants ⟨**Kébisasa riki nóchoribi; nóchora áni iki nonra já píai; kébisasa riki máxko.** The *kébisasa* is also a churo (river snail); the churo is big and we eat it, but the *kébisasa* is smaller.⟩ ⟨**Kébisasa piáxa báke jími chíxotai.** If a boy eats *kébisasa*, he gets dysentery.⟩
*n.* **kébita** [from Shipibo *ke–* from the edge + *bíti* to take] : to remove from the edge or border
*n.* **kebón** : pucacunga (a type of guan) ⟨**Kébora jatíbiain jáke; kébo riki píti átapa keskaribi.** There are pucacungas everywhere, and they serve as food just like chickens.⟩

*n.* **kéboroxnin** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *boróxti, boróx–* to appear] : the part of the mouth between the upper lip and the nose ⟨**Xetan chéxaara nokon** **báke jawen kéborox sóoike.** My son's upper lip area has swollen up because he has a toothache.⟩
*adj.* **kéboxen** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lip + *bóo* hair + *jóxo* white] : having a speckled/grizzled beard
*v.t.* **kéchata** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *chákati* to crush] : to flatten/dent along the edge ⟨**Titánra jawen ráto kecháke.** Mama dented the edge of her plate.⟩
*v.t.* **kéchata** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *cháchiti* to sting/pierce] : to sting someone on the lips : to pierce someone's lips
*v.t.* **kéchexa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *chéxati* to hurt] : to make the lips hurt by applying a liquid that causes swelling
*v.t.* **kéchina** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *–n* verbal derivational suf. + *chi–* backward + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] : to turn someone's mouth in another direction
*v.i.* **kéchia** : to turn one's own mouth in another direction
*v.i.* **kéchokiita** : to wash one's mouth : to wash one's lips

*v.t.* **kéchona** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *chon*, unidentified element + *–ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to put to the mouth 2 : to add firewood to : to stoke ⟨**Aínbaonra yamékirishoko chíi kéchonai jawékiati anoshon.** Early in the morning, the woman stokes the fire to prepare breakfast.⟩
*v.t.* **kéchota** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *chókati* to wash] : to wash someone's mouth

*verbal suf.* **—keet** : oneself, themselves —Used attached to the root of certain transitive verbs, producing verbs that become reflexive. ⟨**Títara pápekeetai.** Mama is piercing a hole in her own ear.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.3
*n.* **kéeman** : desire, wish ⟨**Nokon kéen riki westíora xóntako betan ea wánoti.** My wish is to marry a young lady.⟩
See under *átsa*

*v.i.* **kéena** 1 : to want : to love —Used in both senses with the object in the basic indirect-object form or in the non-basic medium-complement form. ⟨**Eara Rosán kéenai metsáxoko íketian.** I love Rosa because she is very beautiful.⟩ 2 : to want : to desire : to want to have or achieve ⟨**Eara kírika kéenai.** I want the book.⟩ ⟨**Ompíra tóatin márotinin kéenai; mónsora kochín kéenai.** Humberto wants to buy the shotgun, and the mestizo wants to buy his pig.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.4.2 *syn.* See under *–kas* *syn.* *nóiti*
*v.t.* **kéeta** : to hide behind ⟨**Katénra jawen títa kéeke.** Cate hid behind her mother.⟩

*n.* **kéetinin** [from Shipibo *kéeti, kee–* to hide behind + *–ti* instrumental "with which"] : defense; *also* : shield ⟨**Róma sontárobaonra réteanani kakín jaton kéeti bokátikanai.** The Roman soldiers carried shields when they went to war.⟩ *syn.* **iskóro**

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *–iba* to] *adv.* : to the side/bank : on the side/bank : from the side/bank ⟨**Keíbara westíora tonbó yáwa en oínbeiranke.** In passing, I just saw a herd of white-lipped peccaries on the bank.⟩ *postp.* : to the side of : on the side of : from the side of ⟨**Ián keibara westíora xóbo iki kámpabaona.** On the side of the cocha (oxbow lake) there is a house belonging to some Campa people.⟩
*v.t.* **kékena** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *kenéati* to paint with designs] : to put designs on the mouth/rim of (e.g., a clay pot)
*v.i.* **kékea** : to have a nightmare ⟨**Nokon épara kékeke, namáketian yoshínbo óinax.** My uncle had a nightmare, seeing demons in his dream.⟩

*v.i.* **kékexeeta** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *kexéti* to sew itself shut] : to keep one's mouth shut : to be or become mute ⟨**Bákera jawen papán notsina kékexeeke jáwebi yóyoiamai.** When his father scolded him, the boy fell silent.⟩ *syn.* See under **netéti**

*v.t.* **kékexa** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth, on the edge + *kéxeti* to sew] : to sew at the mouth/opening or along the edge ⟨**Titánra bórosa kekéxke.** Mama sewed the opening of the bag shut.⟩

*n.* **kékokan** [from Shipibo *kékoti* to tie in a series] : lashings tied in a series ⟨**Nokon pápayosin kéni riki jóxo itan kebóx.** My grandfather's beard is white and speckled.⟩ ⟨**Tapán kekora rásike béchoman aká.** The raft's lashings came undone from the waves.⟩

*v.t.* **kékoa** 1 : to tie in a series ⟨**Nokon épara táwa kékoi íitai chikékin.** My uncle is tying cañabrava (a wild cane) stalks together in a series, making a fence.⟩ 2 : to string together by tying ⟨**Tómasen áwininra ísoxeta kékoai máronóxon.** Tomás's wife strings spider monkey teeth together, making decorated bracelets to sell.⟩
*v.i.* **kékota** : to walk leaning on a stick or cane ⟨**Pápara jiwín kekóke.** Papa walked leaning on a cane.⟩

*n.* **kekótinin** [from Shipibo *kekóti*, *keko–* to walk leaning + *–ti* instrumental "with which"] : cane, walking stick ⟨**Yósishokobora íkai kekótia níi.** The little old men go about walking with their canes.⟩

*adj.* **kékoxin** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *kóshi* strong] : blowing with strong breath ⟨**Non rekénbora ípaonike kikín kekóx, bóchikiabi íso tékai.** Our ancestors used to blow very strongly because they could shoot blowgun darts high up at spider monkeys.⟩

*v.t.* **kémana** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *mamánti* to feel/grope] 1 : to feel inside someone's mouth 2 : to search by groping along the edge of ⟨**Aínbobaonra ián kexa kemánkin ipón báchi bíke.** Some women were searching for carachama (an armored catfish) eggs by groping along the edge of the cocha, and they found some.⟩
*v.t.* **kémexa** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *méxati* to pull out] : to pull out hairs from someone's mustache or beard
*v.t.* **kemóntana** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *montánti, montáti* to cover (the river)] : to cover/submerge (of a river, swollen and overflowing)
*v.t.* **kémosa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *mótsati* to squeeze] : to squeeze —to press someone's lips together

*v.i.* **kémota** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *mókoti* to put in the mouth without chewing] : to hold or keep one's mouth closed with the lips drawn back (e.g., out of interest or surprise that one feels) ⟨**Netéshamanxon jói nínkatira jónibo kemóbainke.** While the people listened to the message in the service attentively and in silence, they kept their lips drawn back.⟩
*v.t.* **kémoxa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *móxati* to hit, to strike] : to chip/break the edge of (e.g., a clay pot or a canoe)
*adj. and n.* **kémpisin** [from Shipibo *ke(m)–* in the mouth + *písi* stench, foul-smelling] *adj.* : having bad breath *n.* : bad breath

*n.* **kempón** [from Shipibo *kéne* + *póko* stomach] : a type of medium-sized cup : a mocahua (a traditional painted ceramic cup) used for drinking ⟨**Kémpo akí riki nokon yoxántita.** My grandmother is the one making a mocahua for drinking⟩
*n.* **kémpokan** [from Shipibo *kémpo* mocahua] : convexity : bulge, curvature
*adj.* **kémpokan** : having a narrow, boxed-in outlet ⟨**lántae riki kempó nemín.** The stream is narrow and deep⟩

*adj.* **kempóyaton** [from Shipibo *kempó* convexity + *–ya* with] 1 : convex ⟨**Chómora kempóya iki.** The clay pot is convex⟩ 2 : boxed-in : with concave edges ⟨**lántaera kempóya iki.** The stream is boxed-in⟩

*verbal suf.* [from Shipibo *-ke*, completed-action suf. + *-n*, subordinate-verb suf.] —Used at the end of the subordinate verb in a subordinate clause, where it frequently carries the conditional force of "if." —Also used together with the suffix *-bi* added on, in a form where the two suffixes together carry the force of "although" in the subordinate clause. ⟨**Ja jokénra, ea kái.** If he comes, I'll go.⟩ ⟨**Jawen papán jóno rétekenbira, Josíkan píamai.** Although his father killed the collared peccary, José doesn't eat it.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2 *syn.* **-ketian**; **-tian**
*n.* **Kenán** —Used as a female given name.
*n.* **kénaman** : a type of small, single-piece bench/stool ⟨**Jíwira ákanai kenánhakin.** The little *kenán* bench/stool is made of wood.⟩
[from Shipibo *kapé* caiman + *kenán* type of bench] : a type of small, elongated bench/stool
[from Shipibo *xáwe* charapa (a river turtle) + *kenán* type of bench] : a type of small, square-shaped bench formerly used for giving birth and now used as a seat for visitors
*v.t.* **kénaa** : to call ⟨**Ochíti o átapa jawen ibón kénai pímanoshon, játianra jóai píi.** When the owner of the dog or the hen calls them to feed them, they come.⟩
*v.i.* **kénata** : to shout calling for help ⟨**Keíbakeash jóni kénatai bitánkanwe.** Go and pick up the man on the riverbank who is shouting for help.⟩

*n.* **kénchakan** [from Shipibo *kéne* pottery + *chákati* to hammer/shape] : an earthenware dish used for eating : a plate ⟨**Kenchá bewé non píti metéxnon.** Bring the earthenware dish to serve the food.⟩ *syn.* KENCHA, RATO — both can be translated as "plate"; but RATO, being a loanword, refers more to the factory-made product, while KENCHA, the native word, refers more to the traditional clay product of the Shipibo.
[from Shipibo *jíwi* stick/wood + *kenchá* earthenware dish] : a type of small tray-like dish used for mashing plantain for tacacho (a mashed fried plantain dish)
*adj.* **kénchexen** [from Shipibo *ke(n)–* on the lips + *chéxe* black] : having black lips

*v.i.* **kénchona** [from Shipibo *ke(n)–* on the lips + *chómo* clay pot + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] : to twist one's mouth (e.g., out of annoyance or disdain) as if for a kiss ⟨**Ea óinasha** **aínbo kenchónke.** When she saw me, the woman signaled to me with her lips.⟩

*v.i.* **kénchontina** : to have a swelling/bump (e.g., from a sting or from puckering as if to kiss) on the lip ⟨**Nokon bákera kexá kenchóntinke binán tékaa.** My son has a bump on his lip because a wasp stung him.⟩

*Konibo* **kené** *n.* **kenén** *Konibo* **kénekan** [from Shipibo *ke–* through horizontal extension + *néati* to tie] 1 : corral, pen ⟨**Kéne meran wákabo weímakanwe non raónon.** Put the cattle into the corral so we can treat them.⟩ 2 : room (e.g., of a rustic hut) ⟨**Noara kéne meran óxai játibi.** We all sleep together in one room.⟩ 3 : design; *specif.* : a ceramic design in the form of parallel rays ⟨**Náto riki titán kené.** This is the design mama made.⟩ *syn.* **chíte**
*v.t.* **kenéaa** *Konibo* **kenéaka** : to paint designs on ⟨**Nokon poínra jawen chópa kenéakai.** My sister is painting designs on her clothing.⟩
See under **sabán**
See under **táma**

*v.t.* **kénea** : to miss (a target) ⟨**Enra wáme cháchikin kéneke.** I missed when I tried to spear the paiche (a giant Amazonian fish).⟩ ⟨**Píkeronra manxán tóoakin kéneke.** Pedro shot at the heron but missed it.⟩
*v.i.* **kéneta** : to paint designs on oneself (e.g., on the face) ⟨**Ainbora nanén kénetai jawen bémanain.** The woman paints designs on her face with huito (a black body-paint dye).⟩
See under **wáste**
*v.t.* **kénexa** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *néxati* to tie] : to tie the mouth of (e.g., a sack)
*adj.* **kenéyaton** : having designs —Used mostly among those who speak Konibo. ⟨**Jóxo chópa kenéyatonra torísta ainbo kéenai.** A tourist woman wants white cloth with designs.⟩

*also* **kéxni** *n.* **kenín** *also* **kexnín** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *ráni* body hair] 1 : mustache ⟨**Nato jóni riki kéni nenké.** This man has a long mustache.⟩ 2 : beard ⟨**Nokon kokánra jawen kéni óroai.** My uncle is shaving his beard.⟩ 3 : fish barbel ⟨**Bawín keni riki nenké; tonón keni máxko.** The súngaro's (a type of catfish) barbel is long, and the cunchi's (a small catfish) is shorter.⟩

*n.* **kénibitin** [from Shipibo *kéni* beard + *bíti, bi–* to obtain + *–ti* instrumental "with which"] : a special type of tweezers for plucking facial hairs, made from two shells joined by a cord through a hole drilled in their edges ⟨**Chirí yámaketianra ápaonike yósibaon páo beshe kénibitiakin.** Long ago, when there were no razors, the old people made shell tweezers for shaving.⟩ ⟨**Papán kénibitira nokon wetsán jéneki pótanaanke.** My brother threw papa's *kénibiti* tweezers into the stream.⟩
*adj.* **kénikenin** [from Shipibo *kéni* beard + *kéni* beard] : thick-bearded ⟨**Nokon pápa riki kénikeniosi, bákeranon ikáxbi.** My father has a thick beard even though he is young.⟩
*n.* **kéniomatonin** [from Shipibo *kéni* beard + *–oma* without] : beardless
See under **óroti**
*v.i.* **kénita** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *níti* to stand] : to stand on the edge

*n.* **kénkexen** [from Shipibo *kéne* pottery + *kexá* edge] : a broken piece or shard of pottery used as temper to give strength to the clay of pottery ⟨**Nokon titánra kenkéx pakéx tópiai.** My mother collects the potsherds.⟩
*v.t.* **kénoa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *nóati* to pierce] : to pass a needle through someone's lip
*n.* **kenshín** [from Shipibo *ke(n)–* on the lips + *joshín* white] : foam at the mouth

*v.i.* **kénshia** : to foam at the mouth ⟨**Nokon awínra kénshike; bakóxra jawen kéxakan pótake.** My wife foamed at the mouth; she spat foam from her mouth.⟩ ⟨**Aínbora tóotax kénshiai pítibo pikáshamai.** When a woman is pregnant, she suffers from foaming at the mouth and doesn't want to eat fish.⟩ *syn.* KENSHITI, KESPOTI — both mean "to foam at the mouth," with no difference at all.

*adj.* **kenshón** [from Shipibo *ke(n)–* on the edge + *–sho*, unidentified] 1 : sharp : sharp-edged ⟨**Nato machítora kénsho iki.** This machete is sharp.⟩ 2 : pointed ⟨**Jíwi kenshón cháchixonra en róno réteke.** After sharpening a stick to a point, I stabbed a snake and killed it.⟩ *syn.* **rekénsho**

*v.t.* 1 : to sharpen ⟨**Enra machíto kénshoke sépanoxon.** I sharpened the machete to clear the underbrush.⟩ ⟨**Enra yámi kénshoke jíwi réranoxon.** I sharpened the axe to fell a tree.⟩ 2 : to file to a point ⟨**Arámpiri pía axonra Tómasen rimán kénshoke.** Tomás made an arrow out of wire and filed it to a point.⟩

*n.* **kénshotinin** [from Shipibo *kénshoti, kénsho–* to sharpen + *–ti* instrumental "with which"] : whetstone, sharpening stone ⟨**Ja kénshotinin kénshotanwe jaínra makán rakáke.** Go sharpen it on that stone lying there.⟩

*n.* **kéntikan** [from Shipibo *kéne* pottery + *–tio* (element of *jawétio* "of what size") of a specific size] : clay pot ⟨**Titánra kéntikan ípo napóke.** Mama put several carachama (an armored catfish) in the clay pot.⟩
*adj.* **kentón** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *–nto* without] 1 : speechless : mute 2 : without a rim or edge —Used of pottery. *syn.* **jóioma**

*also* **kéo** *n.* **kéokan** *also* **keón** : caimitillo (a type of star apple); *also* : the fruit of the caimitillo ⟨**Kéo riki bepónya kaímito keska.** The caimitillo has sap like the caimito (star apple).⟩ ⟨**Keó riki kókoti; bími báta, béroya.** The caimitillo is edible; it is a sweet fruit that has seeds.⟩
[from Shipibo *kaín* macaw + *keó* caimitillo] : yellow caimitillo

*v.t.* **kéona** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *joyónti* to put in a row] : to string/skewer ⟨**Nonra píti keónke ochó bóti íketian.** We strung the fish together because we had to carry them a long way.⟩ ⟨**Enra ámakiri keónke, páenai cháchixon.** When the gamitana (a large river fish) was dazed, I speared it and then strung it up.⟩

*v.i.* **kéota** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *joo*, imitative of the cry + *–ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to make an animal sound; *specif.* : to howl : to screech —Used of monkeys (e.g., the howler monkey or the white monkey). ⟨**Jóxoshinora maníshain keóke; bénanon kawé.** A white monkey screeched in the forest; let's both go look for it.⟩ 2 : to roar (of a jaguar) ⟨**Inora kéotai jáwetianki jawéki yátanai; áno, amén, o awá.** The jaguar roars every time it catches something: a paca, a capybara, or a tapir.⟩ 3 : to cluck : to crow (of a rooster or hen) ⟨**Báchiaxa átapa kéotai.** The hen clucks when she lays an egg.⟩ ⟨**Néte xábatainra átapa keóke, néte xábatai ónanax.** This morning the rooster crowed because it knew dawn had come.⟩ 4 : to sing/call (of a parrot or parakeet) ⟨**Nokon beskónra kéotai, –shíin shíin.** My little parrot sings, "—shin shin."⟩ 5 : to honk/quack (of a goose, duck, or vaca-muchacho (a type of bird)) 6 : to hoot (of an owl) 7 : to croak (of certain species of toad and frog) *syn.* See under **kokoríiti**
*adj.* **keóxen** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *jóxo* white] : white-mouthed : having a white mouth
See under **bóna**
*v.t.* **képasa** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *pátsati* to slap] 1 : to slap someone on the mouth 2 : to slap along the edge of
*v.i.* **képekeeta** [from Shipibo *kepéti* to pierce someone's lip + *–kee*, reflexive suf.] : to practice the traditional custom of piercing one's own lip to insert an ornament

*Konibo* **xépemeeti** *v.i.* **képemeeta** *Konibo* **xépemeeta** : to open up (e.g., a door, the plug of a hole, the lid of a drum, a pot, a bottle, or the vertical side of a mosquito net) ⟨**Iskoira xepótira janbíx képemeeke.** The school door suddenly opened.⟩ ⟨**Nokon átapa kenéra xépoti xépemeeke.** The door of our henhouse has opened.⟩

*Konibo* **shepénti** *v.t.* **képena** *Konibo* **shépena** 1 : to open (e.g., a door or window) ⟨**Yómetsobaonra nokon xóbo bintana kepénke.** The thieves opened a window of my house.⟩ ⟨**Enra xepóti xepénke.** I opened the door.⟩ 2 : to uncover, unplug ⟨**Nokon titánra póso kepénke ompáx bínoxon.** My mother uncovered the well to draw water.⟩ *syn.* **mapénti**
*v.t.* **képeta** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *péti* hole + *–ti* infinitive suf.] : to pierce someone's lip. See Grammar Sketch 8.4

*v.t.* **képina** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *pi–* against the side + *–n*, verbal derivational suf. + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] : to lean (something) vertically : to prop up ⟨**Papánra wínti jiwín kepínke.** Papa leaned the paddle against a tree.⟩
*v.i.* **képishiita** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *pishíti* to come unhooked + *–ii*, reflexive suf.] : for the mouth to open wide (e.g., in crying, speaking, or singing)
*v.t.* **képisha** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *píshati* to open] : to open someone's mouth

*v.i.* **képita** : to lean vertically against something : to recline ⟨**Jóni páenara jiwín képita iki moa kátira átipanyamake.** A drunk man is leaning against a tree trunk because he can no longer walk.⟩

*v.i.* **képoa** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *po*, element of *mápoti, mapo–* to cover + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to have one's mouth covered 2 : to get one's mouth dirty ⟨**Káimito kókoaxa noa íkai képoi jawen bepón bíonax.** When we eat caimito (star apple), we get our mouths dirty with its gummy sap.⟩
*adj.* **kérasen** : dirty : filthy : disgusting ⟨**Nato bákera mentsís kerás iki.** This child has dirty fingernails.⟩ *syn.* See under **oshtá**
*v.t.* **kerásaa** *Konibo* **kerásaka** : to make disgusting (e.g., by dirtying) ⟨**Ochítininra ráto kerásake.** The dog dirtied the plate and made it disgusting.⟩
*adj.* **kerásmanin** [from Shipibo *kerás* dirty + *–ma* not] : clean ⟨**Noara kerásma bákebo iki.** We are clean children.⟩

*v.t.* **kérasaa** *Konibo* **kérasaaka** : to be disgusted by ⟨**Ja aínbokira ea kérasai náshiosma íketian.** I'm disgusted by that woman because she doesn't bathe.⟩ ⟨**Wáka pisi óinaxa nokon awín keráske.** Seeing the rotting carcass of a cow, my wife was disgusted.⟩
*n.* **kérekan** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *rérati* to cut] : a series of barb-shaped notches carved into various work or hunting tools
[from Shipibo *arámpiri* wire + *keré* barb] : the barb of barbed wire
[from Shipibo *míshkiti* fishhook + *keré* barb] : the barb of a fishhook
[from Shipibo *móxa* thorn + *keré* barb] : the barb of a thorn

[from Shipibo *pía* arrow + *keré* barb] : the barb of an arrow ⟨**Káshibaon píakerera ániora iki.** The barbs of Cashibo arrows are very large.⟩ ⟨**Wanímpia riki keréya.** Arrows made of peach palm wood have barbs.⟩
[from Shipibo *sira* saw + *keré* barb] : the tooth of a saw or handsaw
*v.t.* **keréaa** *Konibo* **keréaka** : to make and attach a barb, tooth, or point to ⟨**Papánra arámpiri píaaxon keréake.** Papa made an arrow with a wire point and attached its barb.⟩
*v.t.* **kérena** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *rénkati* to smooth] : to smooth along the edge with a special small stone
*v.t.* **kerés aka** : to even out (e.g., clay) by rubbing : to smooth (e.g., clay)

*v.t.* **kéreta** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *rérati* to cut by striking] 1 : to cut the lip by striking 2 : to hack with an axe or machete along the edge ⟨**Sámoiron bakénra nokon papán nónti kéretai.** Samuel's son is hacking at the edge of papa's canoe with a machete.⟩

*adj.* **keréxen** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *–rex* (from *réxiti*, to be about to slip), imitative of the friction of sticks] 1 : narrow or closely packed in a row ⟨**Epán chikéaara keréx iki.** The fence my aunt made is very narrow/tight.⟩ 2 : tightly woven —Used, e.g., of cloth.

*v.t.* **keréxaa** *Konibo* **keréxaka** : to make or set narrow/tight ⟨**Enra jíwi xate néxakin keréxai chorísh inón ixon.** He tied the little sticks together tightly so that everything would be rigid.⟩
*n.* [from Shipibo *keréx* dense/tightly-packed + *meské* a species of shrub] : a species of *meské* shrub

*v.i.* **kérexa** : to pile up (of long objects all oriented the same direction) : to accumulate ⟨**Táxara máximaxkaten keréxke tsósinax.** The driftwood has piled up on the edge of the beach as the river has receded.⟩

*n.* **keríronin** 1 : a species of tree with numerous branches ⟨**Keríro riki wánawana keskaribi ikáxbi kókotima.** The *keríro* tree closely resembles the soursop tree, but its fruit is not edible.⟩ ⟨**Kabórinin keríro píaitianra epán yatánke.** When the taricaya (a river turtle) was eating the fruit of the *keríro* tree, my uncle caught it.⟩ 2 : a species of aquatic plant with thick, round leaves that taricayas eat

*v.i.* **kerón ika** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *ron*, imitative of the sound of paddling + *–iti* to do] : to make the edge of a canoe sound rhythmically while paddling ⟨**Xobón nokóti ochómara noa kerónkeron ibeiranke.** As we approached the house, we came along tapping our paddles rhythmically against the sides of the canoe.⟩
See **kírosin**
*v.t.* **kérota** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *róroti* to shred] : to cut in a zigzag pattern along the edge

*v.t.* **keróxaka** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *rox*, imitative of the sound + *–ati* to do] 1 : to grind/crunch (the teeth) ⟨**Páenabaonra jaton xéta keróxakai.** Drunk men grind their teeth.⟩ 2 : to chew (e.g., something roasted and well toasted) 3 : to suck (a bone)
*v.t.* **késena** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *sénoti* to cut] : to tear someone's lip from one side to the other
*adj.* **késesen** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lip + *sése* freckled] : having spots on the lip
*n.* **keshán** : bush rat ⟨**Náto riki késha: keshán ákai paránta texkan meran bákeakin.** This is the bush rat; the bush rat breeds inside a bunch of plantains.⟩
*n.* **kesháatin** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *shákaati* ladybug] : a border/trim of seeds that rattle on a garment
*v.t.* **késhana** : to inform, to warn ⟨**Nokon bákera jabé ráenanai yómetsoketian keshake.** My son informed me when his friend had stolen something.⟩

*v.i.* **késhaa** : to confess ⟨**Rióskira nokon óchabo ea késhai, jánbi jawen Bakén jimínbi ea chókanon ixon.** I confess my sins before God so as to be washed with the very blood of his Son.⟩ *syn.* **ócha késhati**
*adj.* **keshkán** [from Shipibo *kexa* upper lip + *–ka*, unidentified] : having a protruding lip
*v.t.* **késhkana** : to raise someone's upper lip
*v.i.* **késhkata** : to raise one's own upper lip
*adj.* **késhmoman** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *shomón* blistered] : blistered — having a blistered lip
See under **main**

*adj.* **keshpán** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *–shpa*, unidentified] : having a protruding rim —Used of a container. ⟨**Katénra chómo keshpa tóeke.** Cate broke the clay pot with the protruding rim.⟩
*v.t.* **késhtina** [from Shipibo *kexá* lips + *tímati* to hit] : to hit — to hit someone on the lips causing pain
*v.i.* **késhtita** : to move one's own lips up and down

*v.t.* **kesíaka** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *síi*, imitative of a sound heard up close + *áti* to do] 1 : to pass something close by ⟨**Pápara jawen bakén chíi joekan kesíake.** The son burned his father by passing a flame close by his chin.⟩ 2 : to go along the edge of, to skirt
*n.* **késiman** [from Shipibo *ke–* from the edge + *–sin*, unidentified element] : strip
*v.t.* **késina** : to cut into strips from the edge
*postp.* : like, as ⟨**Ja bákeranon riki téetai jawen papa keska.** That young man is hardworking like his father.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.1; 7.7.2
*nominal suf.* [from Shipibo *keska* like] —Used as a suffix with the force of "like," added to a noun to turn it into an adjective. ⟨**amíkeska** violet-colored⟩

*conj. and postp.* **késkati** [from Shipibo *keska* like + *akín*, participle of *áti* to do] : like : just as : in the same way that ⟨**Xéka jóai keskatiribira jawen awín ábionin jóke.** In the same way that don Sheca came, his wife came too.⟩ ⟨**Chóyachaki yoshínronki íkai jóni keska píkoti; pikóxon jato yóyoakin jonín ákai keskáakin.** They say the demon chullachaqui (a shapeshifting forest spirit) turns into a person; and when it appears before people, it speaks to them as if it were just another person.⟩
*v.t.* **keskáaka** [from Shipibo *keska* like + *–ati* to do] : to do in such a manner
[from Shipibo *íkai*, present participle of *áti* to be, to do + *keskáti* to do in such a manner] : to imitate ⟨**Ea íkai keskáwe.** Imitate me.⟩
*v.t.* **késoa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *sóati* to wipe off dust by rubbing] : to dry someone's lips
*n.* **késpiman** : small dry leaves from a roof
*adj.* **kespón** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *sopóati, sopo–* to bulge] : having an abundant, long beard

*v.t.* **késpota** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *sopóati* to bulge] : to spit foam from the mouth ⟨**Bákera náne xéamakana keyón késpotai kinánkasi.** When the boy is given huito (a black body-paint dye) to drink, he foams at the mouth wanting to vomit.⟩ *syn.* See under **kénshiti**
*v.t.* **késtaa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut (e.g., a pamacari, a woven palm-leaf canoe awning) in a straight line along the edge
*v.i.* **késtata** : to trim one's own mustache, tidying it up

*adj.* **késteman** [from Shipibo *ke–* through the mouth + *–sten*, unidentified element] : loud in sound ⟨**Abionra íkai kesten rón iki píshitax.** The airplane, when running, makes a very loud roar.⟩ ⟨**Motórora moa kestényora rón ikai.** The motor is sounding louder than before.⟩

*v.t.* **kesténhaa** *Konibo* **kesténhaka** [from Shipibo *kestén* loud in sound + *áti* to do] : to rev up (an internal-combustion engine) ⟨**Káro makinára jawen ibón kikínhakin kesténhake.** The car's engine was revved up hard by its owner.⟩

*adj.* **kestón** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *–sto*, unidentified element] 1 : having no rim to grip a vessel by 2 : having a thick edge or rim; *specif.* : thick-lipped/thick-muzzled ⟨**Papán nónti kebí riki kesto.** Papa's canoe has a thick rim.⟩ ⟨**Kabáyora kexá kesto iki.** The horse has a thick muzzle.⟩ ⟨**Wíso jónin kebí riki kesto.** The black man has thick lips.⟩
*v.t.* **kétana** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *tánati* to try/taste] : to go along the edge of
*v.t.* **ketáshaka** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *tashati* to slap] : to slap, smack, or strike on the mouth
*v.i.* **ketáshika** : to hit oneself with a slap, smack, or blow on the mouth ⟨**Eara jiwín enbíx ketáshike.** I hit myself on the mouth with a stick.⟩
*v.t.* **kétasa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *tásati* to nail] : to nail on the edge of
*v.t.* **kétaxa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *táxoti* to lick] : to lick someone's lips
*v.t.* **ketéaa** *Konibo* **ketéaka** : to set fire to ⟨**Nokon bakénra péi chóshi ketéake.** My son set fire to dry leaves.⟩

*v.i.* **kéteta** 1 : to catch fire ⟨**Míxioniron xóbora ketéke.** The missionary's house has caught fire.⟩ 2 : to burn ⟨**Bákebaon chíikan xóbo cháchiara kétetai nókaakanwe.** The house that the children set fire to is burning. Put it out.⟩ *syn.* **tiríti**
*v.t.* **kéteta** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *tékati* to sting/bite] : to sting/bite someone on the lip

*verbal suf.* [from Shipibo *-ke*, completed-action suf. + *-tian* when] —Used at the end of the subordinate verb to say "when," "because," or "if." ⟨**Nonra biamaibake, bítikoma iketian.** We didn't get it because it was difficult.⟩ ⟨**Ja jóketianra, ea kái.** When he comes, I'll go.⟩ ⟨**Oi béyamaketianra, ea jókeanke.** If it hadn't rained, I would have come.⟩ —Used attached to the suffix *-na* in the subordinate clause, expressing fear or meaning "lest" in the subordinate clause. ⟨**Nokon átapa inón pínaketianra ea ráketai.** I'm afraid that the jaguar will eat my hen.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2 *syn.* **-ain**; **-ken**
*v.t.* **kétina** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *tímati* to hit] : to strike or punch on the mouth

*n.* **kétokan** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *tóoti* to conceive] 1 : a bluff/ravine on the bank of a river ⟨**Kapéra ketó naman típike.** Some caimans are lying at the foot of the bluff.⟩ 2 : the collapse of a riverbank ⟨**Iskóirara kétokan bóke.** The school that was on the riverbank disappeared due to the collapse of the bank.⟩

[from Shipibo *ketó* riverbank/bluff + *bímati* to cause to happen] : to cause a landslide/bank collapse (e.g., on the edge of a river) ⟨**Iwínronki ketó bímai.** They say stingrays cause riverbanks to collapse.⟩

[from Shipibo *ketó, kétokan* riverbank collapse + *bíti* to get/obtain] : to collapse into the river (of land at the river's edge) : to be destroyed or lost through a landslide —Used in a sentence where the object is the thing destroyed by the collapse. ⟨**¡Non kámpora kétokan bíai! —ikira saíitai Kósi.** José is shouting: "Our sports field is collapsing into the river!"⟩
See under **kíni**
*v.t.* **kétosha** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *tóshiti* to burst] : to burst — to burst a blister or boil on someone's upper lip

*v.t.* **ketsámaa** *Konibo* **ketsámaaka** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *tsamáati* to pile up] : to pile up or stuff into someone's mouth : to feed (e.g., food) to ⟨**Katénra jawen wétsa píti ketsámaake.** Cate fed her sibling, spooning the food into their mouth.⟩

*v.t.* **ketsán aka** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *tsaan*, imitative of the sound + *–ati* to do] : to make (something) ring by striking its edge ⟨**Enra tasón kesha machítonin ketsán ake.** By striking the edge of the bowl with the machete, I made it ring.⟩
*v.i.* **ketsán ika** : for the edge to ring when struck ⟨**Bantíja kesha ketsán ikai ninkáwe.** Listen, because the edge of the tray is going to ring when it's struck.⟩

*v.t.* **kétsana** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *tsamánti* to pile up] 1 : to pile up (e.g., food) on the lips 2 : to have something added to the edge ⟨**Titánra kentíanoshon mapó ketsánke.** Mama had a coil of clay added to the rim of the pot so she could keep working it.⟩
*v.t.* **kétseta** [from Shipibo *ke–* from the mouth + *tséketi* to remove] : to remove something from one's own mouth
*v.t.* **kétsosa** [from Shipibo *ke–* from the edge + *tsósiti* to remove] : to remove a piece from the edge of
*v.t.* **kéwata** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *wáketi* to lift] : to lift by the edge

*also* **keyé** *n.* **kéwekan** *also* **kéyekan** 1 : embroidery ⟨**¡Chitónti kewé jakónyora riki mía!** What lovely embroidery your pampanilla (a traditional woven skirt) has!⟩ 2 : workmanship ⟨**Titán chitóntira kewé jakónyora iki.** Mama's pampanilla is of very fine workmanship.⟩

*v.t.* **kewéaa** : to embroider ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen benén wiso kotón kewéake.** The woman embroidered her husband's black shirt.⟩ ⟨**Náto riki nokon poín chitónti kewéaka.** This is my sister's pampanilla, which she embroidered herself.⟩
*v.t.* **kéwea** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *wéati* to remove (liquid or dust)] : to clean someone's mouth
*v.t.* **kéwexa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lips + *wéxati* to scratch] : to scratch on someone's lips
*adj.* **kewéyaton** [from Shipibo *kewé* embroidery + *–ya* with] : embroidered ⟨**Jatíbi aínbobaon chitónti riki kewéya.** All the women's pampanillas are embroidered.⟩

*v.t.* **kéwina** [from Shipibo *ke–* in the mouth + *wínoti* to pass by the side] : to answer : to respond ⟨**Jawen papán yóiara bakén kewínke akáshamakin; atánbue mín —akinra áke.** When his father sent his son to do something, the boy answered that he didn't want to do it, and said to him, "Go do it yourself."⟩ ⟨**Noa koshín saí iketianra nákaxen noa kéwinai.** When we shout loudly, the echo answers us.⟩
*v.i.* **kéwita** [from Shipibo *ke–* along the edge + *wekíti* to bend] : to bend, or to be bent, in the shape of an arc

*n.* **kéxakan** 1 : lip : lips : mouth ⟨**Mía riki kexá rastónyora.** You have very thick lips.⟩ ⟨**Noara íkai kéxakan yóyo iki, béwai, saí iki, wínii.** With the mouth we speak, sing, shout, and cry.⟩ 2 : edge —In this sense often preceded by a noun that functions as its modifier. ⟨**Jaínra ián kexa iki.** That is the edge of the cocha (oxbow lake).⟩

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *kexá, kéxakan* lip] *adv.* : along or to the bank/shore (e.g., of a river) ⟨**Kexára ea kái wapóro óini.** I'm going to the riverbank to watch the steamboat.⟩ *postp.* : at the edge of : along the edge of : to/from the edge of ⟨**Ián kexara jóni paenabo tsamáke.** The drunk men are gathered at the edge of the cocha (oxbow lake).⟩ ⟨**Eara nónti kexa kawánkawanhibake.** Yesterday I was walking along the edge of the canoe.⟩
*v.i.* **kéxata** : to draw near to the edge ⟨**Moara tapán kexáke.** The raft has already drawn near to the edge.⟩
*v.t.* **kéxaxa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *xáxati* to scrape, to scratch] : to scrape on the lip (e.g., from the bony plating of a carachama, an armored catfish, when it bites)

*n.* **kéxboman** [from Shipibo *kexá* lip, edge + *bóo* hair] : corn silk ⟨**Xeki kexbó riki bóo keskaríbi ikáxbi jóxo kóshima.** Corn silk looks a lot like hair, except that it is white and breaks easily.⟩

*n.* **kéxboman** [from Shipibo *kexbó* corn silk] : fringe, border trim ⟨**Kexbónya riki chópa, tári, báchi, rasára, kórocha jábo.** The things that usually have fringe are clothing, cushmas (traditional woven tunics), mosquito nets, blankets, and bedspreads.⟩

*v.t.* **kéxea** : to sew ⟨**Nokon áwininra chiárexti kéxeai.** My wife is sewing the pants.⟩ ⟨**Marianinra jawen sáya kéxeke.** María sewed her skirt.⟩ ⟨**Eara chópa kéxekan mároke.** I bought clothing that was already factory-sewn.⟩

*v.i.* **kéxeta** 1 : to close up (of guama, an aquatic plant) in the wake of a boat 2 : to become blocked (of the nose) with mucus swollen/inflamed 3 : for the eye to swell shut 4 : to scar over, to heal ⟨**Pápa rérakaatara moa kéxetai.** Papa's wound is already healing/scarring over.⟩
*v.i.* **kéxkana** : to become or be tilted ⟨**Nóntira moa kexkánke.** The canoe has already tilted.⟩
*v.t.* **kéxkeaa** *Konibo* **kéxkeaka** : to put side by side ⟨**Jóamanra witá kéxkeakinra tipínke.** The forked posts were placed side by side on the ground by Juan.⟩

*v.i.* **kéxkea** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *–xke*, unidentified element + *–ti* infinitive suf.] : to be placed side by side —Used mostly of pairs. ⟨**Konxánra kéxkeke.** The wooden logs were placed side by side.⟩ ⟨**Atapara kéxkei bóchiki yakábekonke.** The two hens are sitting up above, side by side.⟩ ⟨**Pápara títa betan kéxkeke.** Papa and mama are sitting side by side.⟩

*adj.* **kexmén** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *xémeti, xeme–*, to pluck out] : to pull out (a beard) by tugging ⟨**Nokon pápayosin kénira en kéxmeke.** I pulled out my grandfather's beard by tugging on it.⟩

*adj.* **kexmín** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *–xmi*, unidentified] : unequal in length or size —Used as a modifier of a plural noun or pronoun. ⟨**Enra jíwi rabé nenké xáteke, ikáxbi kéxmi.** I cut two sticks, but they came out unequal.⟩
*v.t.* **kexmiaa** : to make parts unequal —Used in a sentence with a plural subject. ⟨**Siróchonin tábara xátekinra en kéxmiake.** I cut the board with the handsaw and the sides came out unequal.⟩

*v.i.* **kéxmia** : to become or be unequal in length or size —Used in a sentence with a plural subject. —Used in the preterite form with present-tense meaning. ⟨**Min táera kéxmiki; benkéx áni, benkéx máxko.** Your feet are unequal; one is big and the other small.⟩

*v.i.* **kéxmita** : to shift or be out of square —Used mostly among those who speak Konibo. ⟨**En kírika tsámanabira kexmíke.** I put the notebooks in place properly, but they've ended up out of square.⟩
See **kéni**
*v.t.* **kéxota** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *xókati* to peel (fruit)] : to peel skin from someone's lip
*v.i.* **kéxoxa** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *xóxoti* to grow] : to grow along the edge
*adj.* **kéxpaman** [from Shipibo *kexá* lip + *pánati* to hang] 1 : having a drooping lower lip 2 : having a protruding lip
*adj.* **kexpén** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the lip + *–xpe*, unidentified element] : having a sunken lip due to missing teeth
*v.t.* **kéxtea** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut someone on the lip
*v.i.* **kéxteta** : to cut one's own lip

*adj. and n.* **kéxtokan** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *–xto*, unidentified element] *adj.* 1 : thick —Used of something flat. ⟨**Nokon papán wínti riki kextó.** My father's paddle is thick.⟩ 2 : double —Used of a boat's hull or of a certain type of house construction. ⟨**Nokon nónti riki kéxtóyora.** My canoe's hull is double.⟩ ⟨**Nokon papánra péixoboakin kéxtóxaman áke.** My father built the house well, doubled, with a leaf roof.⟩ 3 : dense —Used of clouds, fog, smoke, dust clouds, or other cloudy masses. 4 : heavy —Used of rain. ⟨**Oira kextó máanke.** The rain fell very heavily.⟩ *n.* : thickness : density ⟨**jawen kextó** its thickness⟩ *syn.* KEXTO, RASTON — both can be *translated as "thick"; but while* KEXTO implies a flat surface (e.g., of a paddle) RASTON implies a cylindrical shape (e.g., of a tree).
*adj.* **kextomanin** [from Shipibo *kextó* thick + *–ma* not] : thin : not doubled

*v.i.* **kéxtota** 1 : to become denser or stronger (e.g., of rain) 2 : to become thicker/more overgrown ⟨**Min waínkora wási kéxtotai órotanwe.** The weeds in your field are becoming very thick; that's why you should go weed it.⟩

*adj. and n.* **kéyakan** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the edge + *–ya* with, having] *adj.* : tall ⟨**Eara jíwi keyakan néeke.** I climbed a very tall tree.⟩ *n.* : height : stature —Used with a possessive adjective. ⟨**Píkeronra Kósi jawen kéyakan mawínke.** Pedro surpasses José in height.⟩ *syn.* **nenké**

*v.t.* **keyáa** *Konibo* **keyáaka** 1 : to raise : to put higher up ⟨**Nokon papánra jawen xóbotapo keyáake.** My father raised the emponado (split-palm-bark floor) of his house.⟩ 2 : to hoist (a flag)

*v.t.* **kéyana** [from Shipibo *ke(n)yá* tall + *–n* verbal derivational suf. + *–ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to put up high ⟨**Papánra jíwi bochiki táwa keyánke.** Papa put the cañabrava (a wild cane) up high in the branches.⟩ 2 : to lean upright : to stand (something) up ⟨**Nokon pápayosinra táwa keyánke.** My grandfather leaned the cañabrava cane against something and stood it upright.⟩
*v.i.* **kéyata** : to ascend : to rise up ⟨**Poinkoskora kéyatai bóchiki.** Vultures rise up very high when they fly.⟩ ⟨**Abion keyatai óini bekánwe.** Come see how high the airplane rises.⟩
See **kewé**
*adj.* **kéyeman** [from Shipibo *ke–* on the upper lip + *yenkén* smooth, hairless] : without a mustache

*n.* **keyoman** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *–yon*, unidentified element] : saliva ⟨**Keyón xéayamawe; pótawe jímibires iki.** Don't swallow your saliva; spit it out, because it's pure blood.⟩
[from Shipibo *keyón* saliva + *bóti* to bring] : to drool ⟨**Jatíbitianra nokon báke keyón bóai.** My little son is always drooling.⟩
*n.* **kéyoman** : drool, spittle
See under **keyón**
*adj.* **kéyoshin** [from Shipibo *ke–* at the mouth + *yóshoti, yosho–* to twist] : having a twisted mouth

*adv.* **kéyokin** [from Shipibo *keyot–* (from *kéyoti* to finish) + *–i* or *–kin*, verbal sufs.] : completely ⟨**Nokon bóora kéyoti máanke.** My hair has completely fallen out.⟩ ⟨**Parántara jenén kéyokin** **póxake.** The floodwaters completely knocked over the plantains.⟩

*v.t.* **kéyoa** 1 : to finish : to use up completely : to leave no leftovers in ⟨**Parántaxeatira ochítinin kéyoke.** My dog finished off all the chapo (a mashed ripe plantain drink).⟩ 2 : to kill off all (of a group) : to wipe out ⟨**Pitínra jato kéyoke.** Hunger killed them all.⟩ 3 : to carry (an action or process) through to a definitive conclusion : to do completely —Used among Konibo speakers in this sense when it governs an infinitive or a subordinate verb. —Used alternatively in the infinitive form as the complement of the verb that indicates what action is carried out. ⟨**Jonínra átapa rétekin kéyoai.** The man is killing off all the chickens.⟩ ⟨**Ochítibora máwati kéyotai jaton ísiman ikí.** All the dogs are dying off from the plague.⟩ ⟨**Nokon ráwikan ménoara nokon xóbo kéyo ménoke.** My enemy set fire to my house and completely burned it to the ground.⟩

*v.i.* **kéyota** 1 : to run out : to come to an end ⟨**Ompáx bitánwe moara keyóke.** Go bring water, because it has run out.⟩ 2 : for all to die ⟨**Nónti jíkiketianra jónibo keyóke.** When the canoe sank, everyone drowned.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *kishi* thigh] 1 : on the thigh ⟨**kibénti** to search for something on one's own thigh⟩ 2 : on a bird's leg or an animal's hind leg ⟨**kimexti** to pull the hairs out of the leg of⟩ ⟨**kimexti** to pluck the feathers from the leg of⟩ 3 : on the leg of a pair of pants ⟨**kikéxti** to sew the seam of one leg of a pair of pants⟩

*postpositional suf.* 1 : upon —Used attached to its complement to indicate that it is the point of a strong impact. ⟨**Makánra éki pakéke.** A rock fell on me.⟩ 2 : against : with —Used attached to the complement that is the object of a hostile feeling. ⟨**Pápara jawen pátoronki sináke.** Papa got angry with his boss.⟩ ⟨**Pápara títaki sináke píti metéxonyamaa.** Papa got angry with mama because she didn't serve him food.⟩ 3 : of —Used attached to the complement that is the object of fear. ⟨**Nato bákera átapaki ráketai.** This little child is afraid of the rooster.⟩ ⟨**Eara ínoki ráketai pínaketian.** I'm afraid of the jaguar because it could eat me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2 *syn.* See under **manaon**

*modal suf.* —Used as a marker of the interrogative mood after the first phrase of a sentence, provided that phrase is not the verb. ⟨–**Miaki jáwerano kái?** –**Chipónki.** —Where are you going? —Downriver.⟩ ⟨–**Papánki yamé píti cháchiwana?** –**Arawanke.** —Did papa fish last night? —Yes.⟩ —Used as an interrogative particle placed after the verb root when the verb is at the start of the sentence. ⟨–**Kákiai min pápa Rimán?** –**Kárai.** —Is your father going to Lima? —Yes.⟩ —Used after the verb root to mark certain indirect questions. ⟨**Anikiai o iamakiai, oínxon yóikanti iki.** By looking, they will say whether they are growing or not.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.2
See **-ronki**

*v.t.* **kíbita** [from Shipibo *ki–* from the leg + *bíti* to obtain] : to remove (e.g., a bandage) from one's own thigh

*v.t.* **kíchata** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *chákati* to hammer] : to strike on the thigh

*v.i.* **kíchita** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *chikóti* to spill] : to spill onto the thigh
*adj.* **kichón** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *-cho*, unidentified] : with tiny pimples on the thigh
*v.t.* **kíchosha** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *chóxati* to break by blows] : to strike hard on the thigh of
*adj.* **kiemaan** [from Shipibo *ke-* on the thigh + *yenkén* hairless] : having a hairless thigh

*verbal suf.* **–kiit** : oneself or themselves –Used attached to the verb root of certain transitive verbs that become intransitive with reflexive meaning. ⟨**Bákera méchokiitai.** The child is washing his hands.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2; 8.3.3
*v.t.* **kíisa** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *jísti* to look at] : to look at the thigh of
*v.t.* **kíkena** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *kenéati* to paint with designs] : to paint a design on the thigh of
*v.t.* **kíkexa** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *kéxeti* to sew] : to sew (trousers) along the side

*adj. and adv.* **kíkiman** [from Quechua *kikin* own, same] *adj.* 1 : genuine : high quality : the best 2 : elegant ⟨**Nato jónira kikín iki.** This man is indeed elegant.⟩ 3 : light-skinned —Used regarding mestizos or people of the white race. ⟨**Kikín áinbo riki.** She is a light-skinned woman.⟩ 4 : one's own ⟨**Páboron kikín báke riki náto.** This is Pablo's very own son.⟩ *adv.* 1 : very —Used as a modifier of the adjective bearing the suffix *-yora*. ⟨**Kikín kopíora riki chópa kéxeti mákina.** The sewing machine is very expensive.⟩ ⟨**Nato xóbo riki kikín jakón.** This house is very good.⟩ 2 : too : excessively ⟨**Eara nato chopán keenyamai; kikín kopí riki.** I don't want this cloth; it's too expensive.⟩ *syn.* ashón; -bi; -yora

*v.t.* **kikínhaka** [from Shipibo *kikín* better + *-ati* to make] : to hit the mark : to succeed at –Used mostly among speakers of the Konibo dialect. ⟨**Enra kikínhake yawísh rérakin.** I hit the mark when I machetied the carachupa (armadillo).⟩

*adv.* **kikínhakin** : truly : indeed ⟨**Oi kextó béketianra noa kikínbiresi mecháke, mánipei máyaxbi.** When it rained hard, we truly got soaked in spite of having put banana leaves over our heads.⟩ ⟨**Tinório jawen abuín betan méraxonronki, Neténtsoman kikínhakin rámiake; tsewéaxonronki yámitaxon ríshkionke.** They say that when Neténtsoma discovered his wife and Tenorio in the very act of adultery, he truly punished her; after ushatearla (catching her in the act), Neténtsoma gave her a terrible beating with an axe handle.⟩
See under **ísko**

*v.i.* **kíkina** [from Shipibo *kikín* very + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to improve one's living conditions ⟨**Non kaíbobora kikínke nóabi máwini.** Our fellow countrymen have improved their living conditions more than we have.⟩

*adj.* **kímesen** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *metsá* pretty] : having a pretty thigh
*v.t.* **kímexa** [from Shipibo *ki-* of the thigh + *méxati* to pull out hair] 1 : to pull hair from the thigh of 2 : to pluck the hair, bristles, or feathers from the leg of (a mammal or a bird)
*adj.* **kímishanin** [from Quechua *kimsha*] : three ⟨–**¿Jáwetii átapaninka báchi aká? –Kímishaninra áke.** –How many hens have laid eggs? –Three⟩
*adv.* **kímishaakin** [from Shipibo *kímisha* + *-i*, *-akin*, subordinate-verb suf.] : three times
*v.t.* **kímosha** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *móshati* to strike] : to strike so as to break a bone in the thigh of
*v.t.* **kímosa** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *mótsati* to squeeze] : to massage (e.g., a healer massaging) the thigh of

*modifying suf.* **–kiin** : to cooperate : to help ⟨**Maístorora en péi bíkinai xóboati.** I am helping the teacher bring leaves to build his house.⟩ ⟨**Enra nokon báke órokiinke jawen wái.** I have helped my son cultivate his garden.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2 *syn.* akínti
See **-i**
*n.* **kinán** [from Quechua *kina* quena] 1 : flute 2 : quena (Andean flute)
*n.* **kinaman** : vomit ⟨**Jantín bákera kínaman réteke.** Andrés's son died of vomiting.⟩

*v.i.* **kinánkasa** [from Shipibo *kinánti* to vomit + *-kas* to want] : to feel nauseous ⟨**Nato** ⟨**bákera ochíti mawa óinax kinánakasai.** This boy saw a dead dog and that's why he feels nauseous.⟩ *syn.* See under **oyáiti**

*v.t.* **kínana** : to vomit ⟨**Nokon papánra kínanai íchayora átsa pae xéaxon.** My father is vomiting because he drank a great deal of masato.⟩ ⟨**Yoshin niwénronki noa kinámai.** They say a demon's breath makes us vomit.⟩
*v.t.* **kínexa** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *néxati* to tie] : to tie on the thigh of
*n.* **kinín** 1 : hole 2 : burrow ⟨**Ochítininra mári kíni meran jíkimake.** The dog chased the añuje (agouti) into its burrow.⟩
[from Shipibo *jíwi* tree + *kíni* hole] : hole in a tree ⟨**Kapánra jíwikini meran bákeai, wetsánkobires áyamakin.** The squirrel has its young in a hole in a tree, not just anywhere.⟩

[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *kíni* hole] : hole (e.g., a dug pit or crevice) in the ground ⟨**Nato jónira máikini meran káketian, jólman rétekeanke.** When this man fell into the hole, he nearly suffocated.⟩

[from Shipibo *manán* hill + *kíni* hole] : cave ⟨**Náto riki manánkini.** This is the cave.⟩ ⟨**Wísoinoronki manánkini meran jáke; játian isónewabiribi jíwibaon jáke.** They say the yanapumas (black jaguar-spirits) live in caves, while the giant monkeys live in the trees.⟩

[from Shipibo *ketó* ravine/bluff + *kíni* hole] : cave in a ravine ⟨**Icha yáwara ketókini ikáin bóketian rétekanke.** They killed many huanganas (white-lipped peccaries) when they entered a small cave in the ravine.⟩ *syn.* See under **péke**
*v.t.* **kíniaa** *Konibo* **kíniaka** : to hollow out : to make a hole in ⟨**Xoyánra nokon sabáno** **kíniake.** Some rats made holes in my blanket.⟩ *syn.* See under **pékati**
*adj.* **kintón** [from Shipibo *kishi* thigh + *-nto* without] : without a thigh
*n.* **kínxoman** : ishpingo (a tree species) *syn.* nenkémasen

*adj.* **kíoxen** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *jóxo* white] : having a white thigh
