*v.t.* **kípisha** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *píshati* to unhook] : to dislocate one's thigh bone
*n.* **kípoman** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *póno* vein] : vein of the thigh
*v.i.* **kípota** [from Shipibo *ki-* on the thigh + *po-*, unidentified element + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to cover one's own thigh

*modifying suf.* **–beiran** –Used with the meaning "upon coming" or "and came" added to the action of the verb. –Used in the form *–quiran* with intransitive verbs and in the form *–beiran* with plural intransitive verbs as well as with transitive verbs. –Used with a reduplicated verb root to imply coordinated action and movement. ⟨**Tomása ratékiranke áni yoshínhosi méraash.** Tomás came frightened after having seen an enormous ghost.⟩ ⟨**Páena jónira béwabewakiranke jawen xobón joí.** The drunk man came singing on his way home.⟩ ⟨**Báke jéne meran káketian íshtobeirani bexón oínkana iká iki moa jenén rétea.** When the boy sank into the water, many came running; but he had already drowned.⟩ ⟨**Yamé pochinikon óxaaxa, noa rámabi jishténbeirani bekánke.** We woke up a few minutes ago even though we went to bed at midnight.⟩ ⟨**Kárasira meran ikénra nokon báke en tsékabeiranke.** I come after getting my son out of jail.⟩ ⟨**Jatón ánibo máwata shínanaxa bákebo nontín beí sión ibeiranai.** The children come in the canoe crying loudly, thinking of their parents who have died.⟩ ⟨**Jawen xóbo matsókinra jonín shanó mérake xobónko jíkia.** While sweeping his house, the man found a jergón (fer-de-lance snake) that had gotten in.⟩

*n.* **kírikanin** [from Quechua *killka* paper] 1 : paper ⟨**Kírika bitánwe non kárata anón.** Go get paper so we can write a letter.⟩ 2 : letter ⟨**Nokon báke sontáro básiora íketianra, en jáki kírika bómaibake jawen wétsa betan.** Since my son has been in the army for a very long time, yesterday I sent him a letter with his cousin.⟩ 3 : notebook ⟨**Nokon bákera en kírika mároxonhibake wíshati onánon íxon.** Yesterday I bought a notebook so that my son could learn to write.⟩ 4 : book ⟨**Nato kírikaninra jakón esé noa onámai.** This book teaches us much good advice.⟩ 5 : record ⟨**Bákeranonbaon jáne kírikanin wíshawe.** Write the names of the young people in the record book.⟩ *syn.* KIRIKA, RIBIRO — both can be translated as "book"; except that KIRIKA, the native word, unlike RIBIRO, a word derived from Spanish, has other meanings, and is more established and used in this sense. *syn.* kárata; kóarino
[from Shipibo *kírika* book + *áti* to do] : to study ⟨**Enra kírika ákai yamétibi.** I study every night.⟩
[from Shipibo *kírika* book + *onámati* to make known] : to educate ⟨**Rámara maístoron bákebo non joínbi jato kírika onámai.** Now the bilingual teacher educates the children in their own language.⟩
[from Shipibo *kírika* paper + *yóyoati* to make speak] : to read : to know how to read ⟨**Nokon bakénra kírika yóyoakai.** My son knows how to read.⟩

*also* **Krísto** *n.* **Kiríston** *also* **Kristón** *Konibo* **Kirístonin** [from Spanish] : Christ ⟨**Kiríston aká iki jonín átipanyamaabo mawábo jíriakin, bénche oímakin, chánto nímakin.** Christ did things that no other person could do: he raised the dead, made the blind see, and made the lame walk.⟩

*also* **kérosene** *n.* **kírosinin** *also* **kérosenin** [from Spanish] : kerosene ⟨**Kírosin yámaaxa nato joé onkín iki.** This lamp is burning low for lack of kerosene.⟩

*n.* **kishín** : thigh; *also* : whole leg ⟨**Monsónra Jóaman pápa kishínko cháchike.** A Spanish-speaker gave Juan's father an injection in the thigh.⟩ ⟨**Kápetenronki nete mayai niá jonibo jawen kíshi tsékanike.** They say that long ago the lagarto (caiman) took out his thigh the leg of one of the Otherworldly Travelers.⟩ *syn.* See under **witáx**

*adj. and n.* **kíshiomatonin** [from Shipibo *kishi* thigh + *-oma* without] *adj.* : legless *n.* : a constellation called "Leg-Amputee"; formed by Orion's Belt representing the amputated man and Orion's Sword representing the severed leg -In this sense used written with initial capital *Q.*
See under **peká**

*v.t.* **kíshpimeeta** : to escape : to be saved ⟨**Jenén réteti ikénbi nónti yátanaxa nato jóni kíshpinke.** This man was saved from drowning by grabbing the canoe.⟩ ⟨**Inón bíkasara ea kishpímeeke íshtoax.** When a jaguar tried to catch me, I ran and escaped.⟩ *syn.* See under **jabáti**
*adj.* **kíshpinaton** : saved : having assurance of eternal life -In this sense used mostly among believers.

*Konibo* **kói** *n.* **kobín** *Konibo* **koín** [from Quechua *kuvi*] : guinea pig ⟨**Rabé néte pímaama ikaxa, kóbi mawáke.** The guinea pig died because it was not fed for two days.⟩
*v.t.* **kobínhaa** *Konibo* **kobínhaka** : to boil ⟨**Papán róo béketianra kobínhayamakin titán xóireske.** When dad brought the howler monkey, mom did not boil it; she only roasted it.⟩

*v.i.* **kóbina** : to boil ⟨**Moa betén kobinkenbira ochítinin chíkoke.** The dog spilled the (fish) porridge that had been boiled.⟩ ⟨**Nato néinora kobín piósma iki.** This giant otter has never eaten anything cooked.⟩
*adj.* **kóbisin** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the chin + *bísi* with warts] : rash on the chin

*v.t.* **kobítaxa** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the jaw + *bítaxti* to press] : to press the jaw of ⟨**Jawen rawíra epán moa kobítaxke.** My uncle, my father's brother, stepped on the jaw of his enemy, who lay prostrate.⟩

*v.t.* **kobóaka** [from Shipibo *kobo*, imitative of the sound + *-ati* to make] : to make (the water) sound ⟨**Nato bakén jéne kobóaketianra kapé jóke.** When this child made the water splash with his hand, a caiman came.⟩

*v.i.* **kobóika** [from Shipibo *kobó*, imitative of the sound + *-iti* to make] : to make the water sound (while inside it) in the manner of the river dolphin and fish ⟨**Mia kobóikai nínkataxa awá jabáke.** The tapir fled when you made the water splash.⟩
*v.t.* **kóborana** [from Spanish *kobra-*, element of *kobrar* + *-n*, verbal-derivation suf. + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to charge (collect payment)
*n.* **kocháranin** [from Spanish] : spoon
*n.* **kochín** [from Quechua *kuchi* pig, hog, swine; and this from Old Spanish *koche*] : pig : hog : pig : swine ⟨**Kochínronki báke chíxómai.** They say that pork gives children diarrhea.⟩

[from Shipibo *restó* flat-snouted + *kóchi* pig] : a species of pig

*adj.* **kóchoman** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the chin + *chon*, unidentified element] : double-chinned ⟨**Bákeranonki bénotax káax, kochónkochonhisi aínboiba nokónike.** They tell that in ancient times a boy lost in the forest came upon a woman who had a large, double chin.⟩
*v.t.* **kóchona** : to have a large chin –Used in the preterite with a present-tense sense. ⟨**Icha píira nato jóni moa kachónke.** This man has a large chin from eating too much.⟩
*adj.* **koén** : with hard pulp –Used of fruit. ⟨**En kaímito beára kóeyora iki.** The caimitos I brought have very hard pulp.⟩

*v.i.* **kóea** : (of a tree) to bear or form fruit with hard spots in the pulp ⟨**Nato kaímitora moa koéke, jímiaixonbi aínbaon kókoa.** The fruit of this caimito has hard spots in the pulp because a menstruating woman ate one of the fruits.⟩

*v.t.* **kóeta** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the jaw + *wkkíti* to bend in the middle] : to jab someone else in the jaw ⟨**Ishto káitianra nato jóni aínbaon wetín koéke.** As this man was running past, a woman jabbed him in the jaw with a hook.⟩

*n.* **koín** 1 : jaw ⟨**Titán shípi koi téotiaara náwa mároke.** A mestizo bought the necklace of pichico jaws that mama had made.⟩ 2 : chin ⟨**Jabé bakénra nato báke koínko chíikan cháchike.** Another child of the same age burned this child on the chin with a burning stick.⟩ *syn.* támo

*n.* **kóikoironin** : caribe (a piranha) : piranha *syn.* máke

[from Shipibo *chíi* fire + *koín*] : smoke ⟨**Chíikoin meran jíkiketianra báke kóiman joín rétemakeanke.** The child nearly suffocated from getting into the middle of the smoke.⟩ *syn.* chóma
*adj.* **koínbiresen** [from Shipibo *koín* cloud + *-bi*, emphatic suf. + *-res* just] : cloudy ⟨**Pápashokon óinara jatíbiain koínbires iki.** Grandpa's eyesight is blurry all over.⟩ *syn.* kóro

*n.* **koínkoiman** [from Shipibo *koínkoin*, imitative of its squawk] : vaca-muchacho (a bird) ⟨**Yamébi koínkoin kéotaronki mawákanon róati íkai.** They say that when the vaca-muchacho sings at night, it is a bad omen; it is a sign that someone is going to die.⟩

*v.i.* **kóina** 1 : to cloud over ⟨**Moa kóinaxa kikínbires ícha ói máanke.** After it clouded over, a great deal of rain fell.⟩ 2 : to give off smoke ⟨**Papán jawen wái ménoara ochóxonbi óina koíwanke.** When we looked this morning from afar at the field papa had burned, it was smoking.⟩
See under **máke**

*v.t.* **koírana** [from Spanish *kuidar* + Shipibo *-n* verbal-derivation suf. + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to protect ⟨**Jawen bákebo koíranai ikaxa átapa sináke.** The hen gets fierce to protect her chicks.⟩

*v.i.* **koíshika** [from Shipibo *koísh*, imitative of the sound + *-iti* to do] : (of a branch) to make a sound as it falls ⟨**Sánjoan níwe pakéketianra mánkoa poyan páketi koíshike.** When the San Juan wind came, mango branches fell and made a loud crash.⟩
*v.t.* **kóisha** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the jaw + *wishati* to mark with lines] : to mark with lines on the jaw or chin

*n.* **kóitatasan** [from Shipibo *kói* jaw, mandible + *tatás*, imitative of the sound made with the mandible] : tingotero (an insect) ⟨**En poróto bánakenbira ea kóitatasan ea píanaanke.** The tingoteros ate all the beans I had planted.⟩

*also* **kókapapa** *n.* **kokán** *also* **kókapapan** : maternal uncle : uncle who is the mother's brother –Used the vocative form *papá* "dad" or *koká* to address the person indicated. ⟨**Nokon kókara sontáro káke.** My maternal uncle went off to the army to become a soldier.⟩ *syn.* KOKA, EPA both can be translated as "uncle", but whereas KOKA denotes the uncle on the mother's side, EPA is the uncle on the father's side.
See under *ísa*

*n.* **kokáiki isániton** [from Shipibo *koká*, imitative + *ikí*, subordinate form of *íti* to be + *isá* bird + *-ni* long ago] : a species of bird ⟨**Sípirianra kokáiki isáni ícha iki.** In the Sipiría stream there are many *kokáiki isáni* birds.⟩

*n.* **kokáiki isáninin** [from Shipibo *koká*, imitative + *iqui*, form of *íti* to be, to say + *isá* bird + *-ni*, past-tense suf. of the antiquity] : a mythological bird, black in color with yellow legs

*n.* **kokámen** *Konibo* **kokámenin** : Cocama : member of the Cocama ethnolinguistic group ⟨**Néno jakatiíbira nato jóni moa kokámebo xaran káa iki, jawen ánibo mawáketian.** This man lived here a long time ago, but he went to live among the Cocamas because his parents died.⟩
*n.* **kokán awiman** [from Shipibo *kóka, kokán* maternal uncle + *awín* wife] : wife of the maternal uncle –Used the vocative form *titá* to address the person indicated. –Little used nowadays.
*n.* **kokárachan** [from Spanish] : cockroach ⟨**Kokáracha ani xéaaxa chóncho mawáke.** The chick died from swallowing a large cockroach.⟩ *kokáracha*

*also* **kókobake** *n.* **kokón** *also* **kókobaken** : nephew of the mother's sister –Used in the form *kókobake* to express affection. –Used the vocative form *yosí* "old man" and the vocative form *jamó* "young man" to address the person indicated. ⟨**Jawen kóko betanra Káte keó akí kake.** Cate went to gather caimitillo fruits with his nephew.⟩ ⟨**Nokon kókobakera Ikítoain káke sontáro jíkii.** My dear nephew went to Iquitos to join the army.⟩ *syn.* KOKOBAKE, CHIOBAKE, INI, NOXA, PIA all can denote "one related to another as nephew or niece". Each, however, is distinguished from the others: CHIOBAKE, NOXA, and PIA can be translated as "nephew" or "niece"; KOKO only as "nephew", and "INI" only as "niece". All, moreover, differ in the exact kinship relationship with him or her who would be called "uncle" or "aunt" in Spanish.

*v.i.* **kokoríika** [from Shipibo *kokori*, imitative of the cackle + *-iti*, to do] : to cackle *syn.* KOKORIITI, JOTOKOITI, KEOTI all translate as "to cackle". JOTOKOITI is the term most used in Shipibo speech; KOKORIITI, on the other hand, is used more among Konibo speakers. KEOTI is a term that can refer to the noise of various animals, birds, and reptiles, among them the cackling of a rooster or hen.

*v.t.* **kókoa** : to eat (fruit) : to suck (fruit) ⟨**Rabé santírara énbicho kókoke.** I ate two watermelons with no help.⟩ ⟨**Nato bími kokó ikénbira en títa ménike, onányamaxon.** Without realizing it, I gave mama a fruit that had already been eaten.⟩ ⟨**Jatíribi bímibora kókoa bátashaman iki; jatíribi páe iki.** Some fruits, when sucked, are very sweet; and others are very sour.⟩ *syn.* KOKOTI, JAWEKIATI, PITI all have the basic sense of "to eat", but KOKOTI implies fruit that is eaten; JAWEKIATI, adding the sense of "something", suggests someone who has fasted and is now eating; PITI means to eat meat or something else that is not sweet.

*n.* **komíkonin** : a species of aquatic shrub with very small fruit ⟨**Nato komíko niá namameara papán wáme réteke.** Beneath this trunk of the *komíko* shrub papa killed a paiche (a large fish).⟩

*n.* **kónawen** *Konibo* **kónawenin** : a species of bird ⟨**Kónaweninronki bári oínbaiti átipanke.** They say the *kónawe* bird can keep its gaze fixed on the sun all day long.⟩
*n.* **konchón** : very fermented masato (a fermented drink) ⟨**Papánra jato kóncho xéati kénake.** Dad invited them to drink very fermented masato.⟩

*v.t.* **konésaka** [from Shipibo *kones*, unidentified + *-ati* to make] : to pierce the lower lip of ⟨**Títashokonra jawen bába konésake, kóri sáwemati.** The grandmother pierced her granddaughter's lip to put an ornament on her.⟩
*n.* **kónin** : eel ⟨**Rókotoronra kóni piáx chíxotaitian ráo xéamake.** The doctor had him take a medicine when he had diarrhea from having eaten eel.⟩ *syn.* konín ewa

*n.* **kónibon** *Konibo* **kónibaon** *pish.* **kónibaen** [from Shipibo *kóni* eel + *-bo*, pl. suf.] : the Konibo ethnolinguistic group : the Konibo : Konibo people ⟨**Aménwaka jónira kónibo xaran kásh wanóke.** An Amahuaca man went to live among the Konibo and married a woman of that group.⟩

*also* **koninjon** *also* **konéjo** *n.* **koníjonin** *also* **konínjonin** *also* **konéjonin** [from Spanish] : rabbit ⟨**Nato jonínra koníjo kaiyai ixonbira pimayamai.** This man raises rabbits, but he doesn't feed them.⟩

*n.* **konín ewan** [from Shipibo *kóni, konín* eel + *-ewa*, augmentative] : gymnotus (an electric eel) : eel : electric eel ⟨**Konínewan xenín wiskíxonronki non jato pirótanin kanántiki.** They say that when we paint our legs with gymnotus fat, we can win at soccer.⟩ *syn.* kóni
See under **wáste**

*n.* **konjítinin** [from Spanish *konfite*] : candy : sweet : confection ⟨**Bákera jawen titán konjíti kókomakashamai, jawen xéta payóti iketian.** The mother forbids her child to eat candy, because it ruins the teeth.⟩
*n.* **kónkishin** 1 : firefly 2 : one of the demons identified with fireflies ⟨**Nato konkíshyoshinboronki mécha iki.** They say the firefly demons are good hunters.⟩ *syn.* póitere
*n.* **kónkoman** : a species of black condor ⟨**Kónkomanra jóxokape píai.** The *konkón* condor eats the white lagarto (a caiman).⟩

*n.* **konón** : mushroom ⟨**Moátianronki jóniki kónobicho píai ikátiai.** They tell that long ago there was a man who ate only mushrooms.⟩ ⟨**Jiwi páyotaitianra, meskó kóno jókonai.** When the wood of a tree rots, various mushrooms come out.⟩
[from Shipibo *joshín* red + *kóno* mushroom] : a species of reddish-brown mushroom used for polishing pottery
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *kóno* mushroom] : a species of white mushroom
[from Shipibo *píti* food + *kóno* mushroom] : a species of brown mushroom eaten by motelos (tortoises) and sometimes by humans

*n.* **konónbin** *Konibo* **konónbinin** 1 : a species of tree; *also* : the sweet fruit of the *konónbi*, which outwardly resembles an olive 2 : the fruit of the *konónbi* tree ⟨**Konónbi máana kókoaitianra epán manánxawe ícha bíke.** My uncle, my father's brother, caught many motelos (tortoises) when they were eating *konónbi* fruits fallen from the tree.⟩
*n.* **kónroman** 1 : incira (a tree) 2 : the fruit of the incira ⟨**Bákera konrón bíi néetaitian binán tékake.** When the boy was climbing to get inciras, a wasp stung him.⟩
[from Shipibo *níshi* vine + *konrón* incira] : a species of tree or vine not yet identified
*n.* **kónroman** : guisador (a seasoning plant) : a species of plant used for seasoning food ⟨**Korákara píti kónronya aká pikáshamai.** The curaca does not like to eat food prepared with guisador.⟩
*n.* **kóntakan** [from Quechua *kunta*] : conta (a palm) ⟨**Kontá bero piáronki chikíshti iki.** They say that when we eat conta seeds, we become lazy.⟩

*n.* **kónxamanchain** [from Shipibo *kónxan, kónxaman* cedar + *chái* brother-in-law] : masha cedar ⟨**Pápashokonra íno tóoake kónxamanchain néeta.** The grandfather shot the jaguar that was high up in the masha cedar.⟩
*n.* **kónxaman** : cedar ⟨**Konxán xatera pápa jawen pátoronin bichínke.** The boss took away dad's piece of cedar.⟩
[from Shipibo *manán* hill + *konxán* cedar] : highland cedar
*n.* **kóokan** : pus : suppuration : discharge ⟨**Kishínko nónbetara kóo ícha bóke.** The boil on the thigh discharged a lot of pus.⟩
*verbal suf.* **–koot** : oneself or themselves ⟨**Yámikentira réokootai.** The pot is *tipping over.*⟩ ⟨**Nóntira réokooibake.** The canoe has tipped over.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.3
*n.* **kóojisoman** [from Shipibo *kóo* pus + *jisón* urine] : gonorrhea

*v.i.* **kóota** 1 : to suppurate : to form pus ⟨**Jimán tékaara noa kóotai.** Ant bites form pus in us.⟩ 2 : for pus to accumulate ⟨**Moa nonbé kóoketianra rókotoron xáteke.** When the boil was already full of pus, the doctor opened it with a scalpel.⟩
*n.* **kópekenin** [from Shipibo *ko–* on the lower lip + *peké* sore] : a piercing in the lower lip for placing an ornament

*n.* **kópeman** 1 : a species of tree with small, sour fruits 2 : a species of shrub with sweet, black, small fruits that fish eat 3 : the fruit of the *kopén* shrub ⟨**laman kaxónra non kopén kókoibake.** Yesterday we went to the cocha (an oxbow lake) and ate *kopén.*⟩
*v.t.* **kópeta** : to pierce the lower lip to place an ornament

*adj. and n.* **kópikan** *adj.* : expensive ⟨**Kikínbires kopíora ikénbira nato átapanin noa mároke pikáshorai.** Even though it was too expensive, we bought this hen because we were hungry.⟩ *n.* : price ⟨**Jatíbi jawékira rama jawen kopí bebónyorabo iki.** Nowadays everything has excessively high prices.⟩

*conj. and postp.* *conj.* : because : on account of –Used with the past participle. ⟨**Nokon átapanin mia yómetsoa kopira en mia ichátamashoko kopíai.** I am going to pay you less (for your work) because you have stolen my hen.⟩ *postp.* 1 : in favor of : for : for the sake of –Used with a noun or with the infinitive in *-ti* that precedes it. ⟨**Westíora kirínkoninra píchika pácha waránka sóro ea ménike, jéma akínti kopi.** A foreigner gave me five hundred thousand soles to invest in community development.⟩ ⟨**Non pápabaonra ícha jawéki noa kopi aká iki.** Our parents have done many things for us.⟩ 2 : because of (the fault of) –Used with pronouns and nouns. ⟨**Mía kopira ea jakómain banéke.** Because of you I have ended up badly off.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.1; 7.7.2 *syn.* -ain; -nox

*v.t.* **kopíaa** *Konibo* **kopíaka** 1 : to pay ⟨**Jawen pátoroninra kárasira meran níake, ishtón kopíayamaitian.** The boss put (the indebted employee) in jail because he did not soon pay what he owed.⟩ 2 : to bribe ⟨**Moa kárasira meran ákanabira kopíaax pikóke.** They put him in jail, but he got out by bribing.⟩

*transitive-verb participle* : paying : taking revenge ⟨**Ochítininra báke natéxke; játianra kópikin ríshkike.** When the dog bit the boy, he gave it a beating.⟩ ⟨**Jawen ráwikan tímaketianra, kópikin réteke.** When his enemy punched him, he knocked him out.⟩

*adj.* **kopíman** *also* **kopímaton** *Konibo* **kopímaan** *also* **kopímanin** [from Shipibo *kopí* expensive + *-ma* not] 1 : free (of charge) ⟨**Nokon shínamanbi ménikinra en mia kopímabi méniai.** I give it to you free, because that is my will.⟩ 2 : cheap : at a low price ⟨**Nato pátoronra jakómaixon noa kopímabires konxán mároxonke.** This boss bought our timber at a very low price because he is very bad.⟩ ⟨**Nato chópara Máioshiainbi kopímatani iki; ríkatonin boára kopí iki.** In Pucallpa these cloths are somewhat cheap; but when the river trader takes them to sell, he marks them up a lot.⟩

*v.t.* **kópia** : to cutipar (spiritually afflict) : to bewitch ⟨**Xonón báke kópiaronki ésteai.** They say that when the lupuna (a Ceiba tree) cutipas a baby, its belly swells.⟩ ⟨**Ronón ewan báke kópiaronki jósho chíxotai.** When the boa cutipas the baby, it gets a yellowish diarrhea.⟩ ⟨**Wakán kópiaronki báke keyón bóai.** They say that when the cow cutipas a baby, it drools a lot.⟩
*Konibo* **kópikaati** *v.i.* **kópita** *Konibo* **kópikaata** : to take revenge
*n.* **kopítson** *Konibo* **kopítsonin** : cupiso ⟨**Non kopítso piáronki chikíshti iki.** They say that when we eat cupiso, we grow weak.⟩
See under **ráo**
See under **wáste**
See **pítsokori**

*n. and adj.* **kórakan** *n.* : chapo (a plantain drink) ⟨**Pápara paránta korá xéakasi átsaxeatira akashamai.** Dad does not want to drink masato (a fermented drink), but rather chapo.⟩ *adj.* : melted by heat –Used, e.g., about the eggs of the carachama (an armored catfish).

*v.t.* **koráa** *Konibo* **koráaka** 1 : to melt (e.g., pitch or foodstuffs) ⟨**Barín koráa téri jámataxa báke wínike.** The child cried when he stepped on the pitch melted by the sun.⟩ 2 : to make (something) melt (e.g., carachama eggs) ⟨**Moára non koráake nato ipó báchi.** We have already melted these carachama eggs.⟩ 3 : to soften; *specif.* : to soften (ripe plantains) to make chapo ⟨**Titánra joshín koráakai.** The mother is softening plantains to make chapo.⟩

*n.* **korákan** *Konibo* **korákanin** [from Quechua *kuraka*] : curaca : chief : leader of the village ⟨**Kakónkonia koráka íkasi jóni nótsiketianra ímakanke.** A man who wanted to be curaca of. Caco got so angry when they would not accept him that in the end they had to make him one.⟩
*n.* **korárion** [from Spanish] : corario
*v.i.* **kórata** : to melt (e.g., eggs of carachama (an armored catfish)) ⟨**Ipó báchi en biára moa koráke.** The carachama eggs I got have already melted.⟩

*v.i.* **kórata** : to make a racket with many people talking at once ⟨**Iskoirankoniax korákanketianra maístoron jato kastíkanke.** The teacher punished them because they were making a lot of noise, talking inside the school.⟩
*n.* **korín** : an ornament worn in the piercing of the lower lip ⟨**Nato aínbora kóri sáwekashamai.** This woman does not want to put an ornament in her lower lip.⟩

*n.* **korín** [from Quechua *kori* gold] : gold –Used little nowadays. ⟨**Kóri nóntishokonronki Inkán báke jónike.** They say the Son of the Inca came in a little canoe of gold.⟩ *syn.* KORI, ORO both mean "gold", but KORI is an old-fashioned word, whereas ORO, the loanword from Spanish, is the usual one today.

*Konibo* **koríapiri** *n.* **kóriapirin** *Konibo* **koríapirinin** : capitari (a freshwater turtle) ⟨**Kóriapirin nepáx píaitianra papán cháchike.** Dad speared the capitari while it was eating guama (a fruit).⟩
*also* **koríche** *n.* **koríchinin** *also* **koríchenin** [from Spanish] : a kind of refreshing drink typically carried in a small bag
*n.* **Kóri Inkan** [from Quechua] : Inca of Gold
See under *ínka*

*n.* **koríkinin** [from Quechua *kollke* silver] : money : silver : coin –Also used in the plural form *koríkibo* in the sense of "sum of money". ⟨**Pátoronbaonra noa koríki méniamakatitai; jawékiboresa noa ménikatitai.** Years ago the bosses did not pay us with money but only with goods.⟩ ⟨**Wishawe nato koríkibo.** Write down these sums of money.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *koríki* silver] : a kind of old coin worth nine or five tenths ⟨**Jóxokoriki bénakinbira en mérayamai.** Although I look for five-tenth coins, I cannot find them.⟩
[from Shipibo *panshín* yellow + *koríki* money] : brass coin ⟨**Yómetsoninra panshínkoriki bóke, xóbo meranoa.** A thief carried off money made of brass when he got into the house.⟩
[from Shipibo *péi* leaf + *koríki* money] : banknote ⟨**Jenényoshinbaon péikorikironkiki wáme raxkan.** They say the banknotes of the water demons are the scales of paiche (a large river fish).⟩

*n.* **koríkinin titán** [from Shipibo *koríki, koríkinin* money + *títa* mother] : silver mines ⟨**Jénepanshian wéamanronki koríkinin títa iki.** They say that in the Jenepanshea stream there are silver mines.⟩

*n.* **Kórimachapanin** [from Shipibo *kóri* lip ornament + *ma-* at the upper part + *chapáti, chapa-* to fork] : a constellation called "Fork at the Outer Tip of the Lower-Lip Ornament", though not exactly located in the sky
*adj.* **korón** 1 : gray : grayish ⟨**Titán chitóntira kórokoroisi iki.** Mom's pampanilla (a wrap skirt) is a striking gray color.⟩ 2 : cloudy *syn.* koínbires
*n.* **korón** [from Spanish] : chorus : the repeated part of a song ⟨**Ikirisia bewára kóroya iki.** Church songs have choruses.⟩

*v.t.* **kóroaa** *Konibo* **kóroaka** 1 : to make gray 2 : to damage the eyesight of ⟨**Béro kóroati shinánshonra jahuen ráwikan berónko tímake. His enemy gave him a punch in the eye, because he wanted to damage his eyesight.⟩
See under **báwa**
*also* **kórcha** *n.* **kórochanin** *also* **kórchanin** [from Spanish] : cork
See under **cháxo**
See under **isokoro**
See under **kápa**
*n.* **kórokoron** [from Shipibo *kórokoro*, imitative of its call] : domestic turkey ⟨**Kórokoronra báke jamákin sión imake.** The turkey kicked the child until he started to scream.⟩
*n.* **kóronitan** [from Spanish] : bugle ⟨**Sontárobora kóronita íibeirani békanai.** The soldiers come playing their bugles.⟩
*also* **grópo** *n.* **kóroponin** *also* **gróponin** : group ⟨**Bákebora rabé kóropo íti iki.** The children will be in two groups.⟩ *syn.* tonbó; tsamá
*also* **kolóro** *n.* **koróronin** *also* **kolóronin** [from Spanish] : color ⟨**¿Jáwekeskarin parántanin koróro?** What color is the plantain?⟩

*n.* **kórosen** [from Spanish] 1 : cross ⟨**Jonínra jawen rawí korósakin peréke.** A man made a cross-shaped cut in his enemy's back with his machete.⟩ 2 : crucifix ⟨**Bákera náshimaxon páerinin korós ménike.** The priest baptized the boy and gave him a crucifix.⟩
[from Shipibo *korós*, *kórosen* cross + *áti* to make] : to crucify ⟨**Moátianronki Jísokiristo kórosen akánike.** According to the story, long ago they crucified Jesus Christ.⟩
See under **shípi**

*v.i.* **kóroa** 1 : to turn gray ⟨**Wíso ikáxbira moa kóroke.** It was black, but it turned gray.⟩ 2 : for a gray spot to form on the eye ⟨**Báke béro kóroketianra rókotoron ráonai.** The doctor treats a child who has a gray spot on the eye.⟩
*adj.* **kósesen** [from Shipibo *ko-* under the chin + *sése* freckled] : having spots on the jaw

*adj. and n.* **koshín** *adj.* 1 : strong –Used of persons and things alike. ⟨**Nato chópara nokon títana bebónbires kóshi iki.** This cloth is stronger than my mother's.⟩ 2 : sovereign ⟨**kóshi Riós** the sovereign God⟩ *n.* : chief : leader ⟨**Non koshín yóia jóibicho senénhaxonon akánwe.** Let us obey only the words of our leader.⟩ *syn.* ápo
*n.* **Koshín** [from Shipibo *kóshi* chief, strong] –Used as a male name.

*v.t.* **kóshiaa** [from Shipibo *kóshi* strong + *-ati* to make] *Konibo* **kóshiaka** : to make stronger : to strengthen : to reinforce : to train ⟨**Yósma ikénbi íshtomaxonra kóshiake.** Although he was weak, they trained him by making him run.⟩
*adv.* : strong : strongly ⟨**Koshín saíawe; min áyamaara ninkáyamai.** Shout to him loudly; otherwise, he won't hear you.⟩

*v.i.* **kóshia** 1 : to become strong ⟨**Piróta áatira moa kóshike.** He has become strong from playing so much soccer.⟩ 2 : to move ⟨**Máxkaaxbira moa kóshiai.** He had fainted, but he is moving now.⟩ 3 : to depend –Used with a complement followed by *-qui.* ⟨**Nato simánanin nontée anón akanwe, non ajíntiki kóshixon.** This week let's do the work depending on our agent.⟩ 4 : to have confidence –Used with *-qui* and its complement. ⟨**Non ápora jóai; jáki kóshixon koríki yokánon akawen.** Our president is coming; let's have confidence in him and ask him for money.⟩
*v.t.* **kóshkina** : to place crosswise
*v.i.* **kóshkita** : to place oneself crosswise : to lie across ⟨**Koshkíxonra motóronin táxa tsákake.** When the motor (motorboat) turned sideways, it crashed into the palizada (a driftwood pile).⟩

*n.* **koshón** : a kind of wooden container about two meters long, canoe-shaped, used e.g. for fermenting guarapo (fermented cane juice) ⟨**Paénxonra jonín, titán kósho tóeke.** The drunken man smashed this *kósho* container of mom's.⟩

*v.i.* **kóshomeeta** : to bewitch oneself by a method involving the action of *koshónti* ⟨**Wétsabo áti shínanira yobé janbíx kóshomeeke.** The sorcerer bewitched himself by wanting to bewitch others.⟩

*v.t.* **kóshona** : to bewitch by means of tobacco smoke that the sorcerer leaves as a trap along the path for others to step on ⟨**Néinonin kóshonaronki noa yorán chéxai.** They say that when the lobo marino (a sea lion) bewitches us, we feel pain all over the body.⟩
*n.* **kóshorin** *Konibo* **kóshorinin** : cushuri (a cormorant) ⟨**Jenényoshiman ináaronkiki kóshori.** They say the cushuri is the offspring of the water demons.⟩
*n.* **kóshorinin matsótinin** [from Shipibo *kóshori, kóshorinin* cushuri + *matsóti* broom] : a kind of grass identified only by having a vine-shaped stem

*n.* **koshóshkan** *Konibo* **koshóshkanin** 1 : bufeo (pink river dolphin) ⟨**Koshóshkanin yótoaronki noa pórokan chéxai.** They say that when the bufeo bewitches us, we feel stomach pain.⟩ 2 : a constellation called "The Bufeo", formed by the tail of the constellation Scorpio –Used in this sense with a capital initial *C.*
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *koshóshka* bufeo] : a kind of bufeo
[from Shipibo *joshín* reddish + *koshóshka* bufeo] : a kind of bufeo with a reddish-colored body
[from Shipibo *sapén* vaca marina (manatee) + *koshóshka* bufeo] : a kind of bufeo, black-colored like that of the vaca marina
[from Shipibo *xáwe* charapa (a river turtle) + *koshóshka* bufeo] : a kind of bufeo
See under **wáste**

*n.* **koshpámparon** [from Shipibo *koshpán* dewlap + *paro*, unidentified] : a kind of small fish with bulging gills ⟨**Kokánra koshpámparo ícha biá íki.** My maternal uncle got many *koshpámparo* fish.⟩

*n.* **kóshpaman** [from Shipibo *ko–* on the jaw + *shpani*, unidentified] 1 : hanging protuberances on the jaws of certain hens 2 : dewlap ⟨**Oa jónira koshpánya iki, xoáyora ikáx.** That man has a dewlap because he is very fat.⟩
*n.* **Kosín** [from Quechua *Kusi*; and this from Spanish *José*] –Used as a male name.

*n.* **kósiniran** [from Spanish] : (female) cook ⟨**Kósiniranra atapa jéne yoyóke.** The cook wasted the chicken broth.⟩ *syn.* KOSINIRA, YOA AKAI both can be translated "cook", but KOSINIRA, the form borrowed from Spanish, is less used in the language. YOA AKAI, the native word, is used more.
*v.t.* **kóskea** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the jaw + *séketi* to break] 1 : to injure the jaw of 2 : to break (a fishhook)
*v.i.* **kósketa** 1 : to break one's own lower jaw 2 : to dislocate the jaw
*v.t.* **kóskia** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the jaw + *sikati* to paint] : to paint or stain the jaw of
See under **átapa**
*n.* **Kotán** [from Spanish *Klotilde*] —Used as a female name.

*n.* **kótoman** [from Spanish *kotón*] 1 : blouse ⟨**Papán awínwetsan kotónra jéne meran káke.** Papa's sister-in-law's blouse fell into the water.⟩ 2 : shirt ⟨**Jawen kótoman yómetsoai méraxonra koáratia keshánke.** When he saw that someone was stealing his shirt, he told a guard.⟩
*adj.* : having a large hole in the lower lip
*v.t.* **kóxeta** : to offer (fermented drink) ⟨**Nokon chái en átsaxeati kóxetabira ea xéaxonkashamake.** Although I offered my brother-in-law the masato (a fermented drink), he would not drink it.⟩

*n.* **kóxkochin** *Konibo* **kóxkochinin** [from Shipibo *kóxkochi*, imitative of its call] : a kind of dove ⟨**Titán kóxkochi ináara** **misbíton píke.** The cat ate the *kóxkochi* dove that mother raised.⟩
*v.i.* **kóxkoranika** : to give a death rattle ⟨**Moa máxkaira kóxkoranike.** As he expired, he gave a death rattle.⟩

*n.* **koxkóxtobin** [from Shipibo *kóx kóx tobí*, imitative of its call] : a species of dove ⟨**Moa báriapan senénketian-ronki koxkóxtobi kéotai.** They say the *koxkóxtobi* dove sings exactly at noon to indicate the time.⟩
*n.* **kóxnín** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the chin + *ráni* body hair] : long hairs that hang below the chin
*n.* **kóxón** : wild turkey (a large forest fowl) ⟨**Papánra kóxo tóoakinbi kéneke.** Papa shot at the wild turkey, but missed.⟩ *syn.* mikárawa

*n.* **kóxónewan** [from Shipibo *kóxo, kóxón* wild turkey + *-ewa*, augmentative] : a species of guan (a forest fowl) that is ash-colored and of medium size ⟨**Titán kóxónewa píketianra jawen báke chixóke.** The mother ate meat of the *kóxónewa* guan, and her little child got sick with diarrhea.⟩

*n.* **kóxónxewan** [from Shipibo *kóxo, kóxón* wild turkey + *xewá* roofed] : a species of tree or palm whose fruit is like that of the ungurahui, but yellow in color ⟨**Manánxawen kóxónxewa píaitianra en biibake.** Yesterday I caught a motelo (a tortoise) while it was eating the fruits of the *kóxónxewa* tree.⟩

*n.* **kóxopeoxen** [from Shipibo *kóxo* wild turkey + *péi* wing, feather + *jóxo* white] : a species of tree ⟨**Kóxopeoxen báke kópiaronki wísoai.** They say that when the *kóxopeox* tree cutipa (afflicts magically) a child, its body turns black.⟩
*v.t.* **kóxtea** [from Shipibo *ko-* on the jaw + *xáteti* to cut] 1 : to cut on the jaw 2 : to cut (what will be the upper tip of a forked post) into the shape of a jaw

*n.* —Used as the name of the letter *m* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *mápo* head] 1 : on top of, to the top of, or from the top of the head ⟨**mabéx** with dirt stuck on the head⟩ 2 : on the crown of the head : to the crown of the head : from the crown of the head ⟨**mábichi** skin of the crown of the head⟩ 3 : on the crown, to the crown, or from the crown of a hat 4 : in height, of stature ⟨**máxko** short in stature⟩ 5 : over the surface, on the surface, to the surface, or from the surface of the ground or floor ⟨**mabénti** to search over the surface of the ground⟩ 6 : on the ceiling : to the ceiling : from the ceiling ⟨**mabéti** to finish the ceiling⟩ 7 : at the peak (e.g., of a house or a hill) ⟨**mabésti** to roof up to the peak of a house⟩ ⟨**mabésti** to reach the peak of a hill⟩ 8 : on top of, to the top of, or from the top of (e.g., of a tree trunk or a crossbow) 9 : at the opening, from the opening, or to the opening of a full sack ⟨**makéxti** to sew (a full sack) at the mouth⟩ 10 : on the handle, to the handle, or from the handle (e.g., of a paddle, knife, or machete) ⟨**makénti** to paint (a paddle) with designs on the handle⟩ 11 : on top : from on top ⟨**maníti** to stand on top⟩ 12 : over, above ⟨**mawínti** to surpass, to go over⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*negative suf.* : not —Used with nouns, adjectives, adverbs, and postpositions of place and time. ⟨**Nato jóni riki kikínbires yóitima bákema ikáxbi.** This man is very disobedient even though he is not a child.⟩ ⟨**Anima átapara awápanin bóke.** The ocelot carried off the small chicken.⟩ ⟨**Rámara neténma ránsakanai; moara netén ípachokanai.** Now they no longer dance during the day; but before, they did.⟩ ⟨**Rámara ea Kakónkoma iki; moátianra ea jaín ikátiai.** I no longer live in Caco, but before I lived there.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.2; 8.3.4 *syn.* ikáma

*verbal suf.* –Used added to a verb with the sense of "to make", indicating that one is the cause for another to carry out (the action of the verb). –Used with an intransitive verb, making it transitive, or with a transitive verb, which becomes doubly transitive with a direct object and an indirect object. ⟨**Jato báimakin senénhaxonra en jato jíwi réramai.** When I make them finish opening the trail, I am going to make them fell trees to get lumber.⟩ ⟨**Ea oímawe.** Show it to me.⟩ –Used to intensify the sense of "to permit" or "to let" in the action of the verb. ⟨**Átapa kéne meran awápa jíkimayamakanwe.** Don't let the ocelot get into the henhouse.⟩ ⟨**Rókotoroiba bóyamaxonra maton, nato aínbo mawámakeanke.** If you all had not taken this woman to the doctor, you would have let her die.⟩ *syn.* áresti; –ati

*v.t.* **máanhaa** [from Shipibo *máanti* to fall (many) + *-(h)ati* to do] 1 : to throw down or make fall (many things or a mass) ⟨**Bóchiki ixon shinón shekésh máanhaara non kókoke.** We ate the charichuelas (a jungle fruit) that the monkey threw down from above.⟩ ⟨**Yóashiko Inkánronki chíi bikánketian jatoki ói máanhaka iki.** They say that Stingy Inca made it rain down on those who had stolen the fire.⟩ 2 : to unload (several things) ⟨**Enra nóntimea jawéki máanhai.** I unload the things from the canoe.⟩ *syn.* MAANHATI, TININHATI both can be translated as "to make fall", with the difference that MAANHATI implies a loaded thing that is made to fall, whereas TININHATI, on the other hand, mostly refers to fruits of a tree that fall together from being shaken.

*v.i.* **máan ika** [from Shipibo *maan,* imitative of mooing + *-iti* to do] : to moo (cattle) ⟨**Jaín wáka yámaaxbi máan iki kéotaira en ninkáke; yoshínra íbiral.** I heard something; it sounded to me like the mooing of a cow, but there wasn't one there; it must have been a demon.⟩

*v.i.* **máana** : to fall (many, several, or a mass) ⟨**Játian yoshínbo bóchikiax máana iki.** Back then the demons fell from above.⟩ ⟨**Oi máanaitianra ea káyamake, moa néseken kanóx.** I stayed while the rain fell and waited until it calmed down.⟩ *syn.* MAANTI, PAKETI, POXOTI, TININTI all have the sense of "to fall". While PAKETI implies a single thing falling and POXOTI, a standing thing that falls, MAANTI implies a quantity of things or a mass falling, and TININTI a quantity of things (e.g., fruits of a tree) that fall together.

See under **wáste**

*postp. and adv.* [from Shipibo *manán* hill + *o,* element of *oke* on the other side] *postp.* 1 : in the air above ⟨**Jépeian manaonra kimisha ábion máyatai.** Three small planes are circling above Yarinacocha.⟩ 2 : on the bank or edge of ⟨**Inkán xóboronki ián manaon iki.** They say the Inca's house is on the edge of a cocha (oxbow lake).⟩ *adv.* : above : up high : in the air : on the bank ⟨**Jóni jenén réteaitianra, mapéxon moa manáon akánke.** They pulled out the man who was drowning and set him on the bank.⟩ *syn.* MANAON, -ON, -KI all are used as postpositions that can have the meaning of "on, above". MANAON, however, can imply the action of placing something on top, while -ON and -KI rather suggest something descending or falling, more forcefully if the suffix -KI is added to the complement, and less forcefully if -ON is added. It will be noted that the synonym -ON is represented by the non-basic form ending in the case of nouns. *syn.* bóchiki

*n.* **mánaponin** [from Shipibo *ma-* on top of the head + *nápo* interior] : brain : brains ⟨**Non róo mánapo piáronki noa kírika onáma íti iki.** They say that if we eat howler monkey brains, we become slow at reading anything.⟩
*v.t.* **mánaa** : to wait for ⟨**Mánati ea yóiyabira, ea moa jóke, játsanax.** Although he told me to wait for him, I came back because I got bored.⟩
*v.i.* **mánata** : to wait ⟨**Jaón manákana jónira moa nokóke.** The man they were waiting for has already arrived.⟩ *syn.* oínti

*n.* **mánchaman** [from Shipibo *ma(n)* on top of the head + *chánko* protuberance] : horn ⟨**Wáka manchan wéxaxon xéaaronki róookon ítima iki.** They say that if you drink from a cow's horn shavings scraped from a cow's [horn], whooping cough is avoided.⟩

*also* **machán** *n.* **mánchaman** *also* **máchaman** : a species of small bird that serves the shaman as a familiar spirit ⟨**Manchánronki yoshín iki; yobéjonin jóni réteti ráanai.** They say the *manchán* bird is a demon, and that the shaman sends it to kill people.⟩
*n.* **mánchexen** [from Shipibo *ma(n)-* on the top of the head + *chéxe* black] : black crown of the head
*n.* **mánchoman** : tuft of bird feathers ⟨**Nokon titánra átapa manchónya, ríkaton namánbires máromake.** My mother sold a chicken with feather tufts to a traveling trader for a very low price.⟩
*v.i.* **mánena** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the top of the head + *nénti* to feel a burning sensation] : to feel a burning sensation on the head

*v.t.* **mánea** 1 : to put into a container ⟨**Chomón xéati máneti shinánkinra bakén chómo tóeke.** The girl broke the jar trying to put the drink into it.⟩ 2 : to put (a canoe) into a canoe or boat ⟨**Yómetsobaonra nokon nónti bokánke, jaton botín mánexon.** The thieves took my canoe and put it into their boat.⟩

*v.t.* **mánexa** [from Shipibo *ma-* of the crown of the head + *néxati* to tie] 1 : to tie the hairs of the head or crown together with other hairs from the same head 2 : to tie horizontally around the head : to braid
*n.* **manín** : bijao (a broad leaf used for wrapping food) ⟨**Mánibobira ráma Máioshiain kopí iki.** Now even bijao leaves are expensive in Pucallpa.⟩
[from Shipibo *kána, kanán* macaw + *máni* bijao] : a species of bijao that is not used
[from Shipibo *wiríx* thin + *máni* bijao] : a species of bijao with a thin leaf
[from Shipibo *ino, inón* jaguar + *máni* bijao] : a species of striped or spotted bijao
[from Shipibo *xopó* fine bristles + *máni* bijao] : true bijao
[from Shipibo *tsistó* firebrand + *máni* bijao] : a species of bijao of inferior quality, purple on the underside
*n.* **mánipein** [from Shipibo *máni* bijao + *péi* leaf] : leaf of any plant ⟨**Jóni páenara mánipein mápokanke ói béaitian.** Since it was raining, they covered a drunk man with a banana leaf.⟩

*v.i.* **mánita** [from Shipibo *ma-* on top + *níti* to stand on top] : to stand on top of ⟨**Xobón maníketianra áni níweaban nokon kóka pákeke.** When my uncle stood on top of the house, a strong wind made him fall.⟩

*n. and adj.* **mánixin** [from Shipibo *ma-* on top + *níxi* vine] *n.* 1 : weeds, underbrush ⟨**Maníx meran káketianronki jóni ronón natéxke.** They say that when the man went off through the underbrush, a snake bit him.⟩ 2 : forest ⟨**Maníx sénenainra ábion pakéke; kánchis jónira mawáke.** When the forest ended, a plane crashed; seven people died.⟩ 3 : impenetrable jungle ⟨**Jatíribi máyoronabora moa maníx meranoax jokónkasai.** Some Matsés people now want to leave the jungle.⟩ *adj.* : covered with weeds ⟨**Moa kámpo maníx íketianra, ábion pakéti átipanyamake.** Since the field was covered with weeds, the small plane could not land.⟩ *syn.* xóbi
*n.* **maníx níiyaton** [from Shipibo *maníx* weeds + *níi* jungle + *-ya* with] : jungle region or zone

*v.i.* **mánixa** 1 : to become covered, or be covered, with weeds ⟨**Moa tsóa pirótanin tsíniamaitianra, moa kámpo maníxke.** Since no one played soccer anymore, the field became covered with weeds.⟩ 2 : to become forested ⟨**Jawen íbo mawáketianra, nato xóbo moa maníxke.** After the owner of this house died, this place became forested.⟩
*n.* **mankón** : baldness

*n.* **mánkoanin** [from Spanish] 1 : mango (tree); *also* : fruit of the mango tree ⟨**Mánkoa kókoaronki chikíshti iki.** They say that when we eat mangoes it makes us lazy.⟩ 2 : mangua (a species of tree) : fruit of the mangua tree
*n.* [from Shipibo *mánko* baldness + *máxe* achiote (annatto)] : a species of achiote that grows as a shrub and produces smooth fruits
[from Shipibo *máxpa* dwarf + *máxe* achiote] : a species of achiote
See under **máxe**
See under **táma**

*v.t.* **mánkoa** [from Shipibo *ma-* on top of the head + *-nko* in, on] : to go bald ⟨**Wanín xenin máskitaronki mánkotima iki.** They say that if you put pijuayo (peach palm) oil on your hair, you can avoid going bald.⟩
See under **wáste**

*n.* **manón** : a species of black alluvial clay used especially for painting handicrafts : mud at the water's edge ⟨**Páena jónira manón pakéke, titán jawen chitónti síkati biátonin.** A drunk man fell into the black clay that mother had gotten to paint her pampanilla (skirt).⟩ *syn.* See under **cháwa**

*v.i.* **mánokoxota** *Konibo* **mánokoxoa** : to rinse out : to clean one's mouth ⟨**Nétetibi mánokoxotira non xétabo ishtón payóyamai.** If we rinse our mouths every day, our teeth won't decay so quickly.⟩

*n.* **mánonokon** [from Shipibo *máno* mud + *nokóti, noko-* to arrive] : shuyo (a mud-dwelling catfish) *syn.* MANONOKO, NOSHA both denote "shuyo", but MANONOKO can sometimes imply a somewhat larger species of shuyo.
See under **paránta**

*v.t.* **mánoa** : to ask after (a person being sought) from house to house : to find out by asking ⟨**Onányamaxonbi mánoaxa noa jáki nokóke.** Even though we didn't know where he was, we asked around until we found him.⟩

*v.i.* **mánota** 1 : to get lost ⟨**Moa mánota ikénbira rabé néte bénaxon nókokanke.** He had gotten lost; they searched for him for two days and found him.⟩ 2 : to disappear from sight ⟨**Non óinabira moa ábion manóke, naíkoin meran.** As we watched, the plane disappeared from sight among the clouds.⟩

*n.* **mánsaman** 1 : moth ⟨**Moa mánsaman piá ikaxa, xéki bánaabi, xóxoyamai.** Since moths have attacked the planted corn, it isn't growing.⟩ 2 : weevil ⟨**Mánsaman piára jíwi tánoke; jatíribira akáma iki.** The weevil attacked the tree, and it dried up; but it hasn't attacked the other trees.⟩

*n.* **mánshiman** [from Shipibo *ma-* on top + *nshin*, element from *panshín*, yellow] : egg yolk ⟨**Nokon bákera mánshiman kéenyamai, námibichores ákasi.** My son doesn't like egg yolk; he only likes to eat meat.⟩
See **mashínti**
*n.* **mánxaman ewan** [from Shipibo *manxán* heron + *-ewa*, augmentative suf.] : a species of large blue-white heron

*n.* **mánxaman kawátinin** [from Shipibo *manxán, mánxaman* heron + *kawáti* bridge] : a species of shrub with bark similar to moena, with small leaves ⟨**Mánxaman kawáti rawéxon xéaaxa nokon chái méchaa iki.** My brother-in-law drank the juice from this shrub's scraped bark and became a good fisherman.⟩
*n.* **mánxaman** : heron ⟨**Manxán pikáshamaira nato báke wíniai, ísores ákasi.** This child is crying because he doesn't want to eat heron; he only wants spider monkey.⟩

[from Shipibo *júmi* blood + *manxán* heron] : pucagarza (roseate spoonbill) : pink heron ⟨**Jónikonbaonra jímimanxan píyamakanai Inkán jimiya íketian.** The Shipibo don't eat pink herons, because this heron has the blood of the Inca.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *manxán* heron] : a species of white heron
[from Shipibo *píti* food + *manxán* heron] : a species of common heron, ashy gray in color with black wings, highly prized as food

*adj.* **mánxaman** 1 : dried by the sun or fire 2 : faded, discolored ⟨**Nokon wíso kotonra moa manxányora iki; jákopira en sáweyamai.** My black shirt is very faded, and that's why I don't wear it anymore.⟩ 3 : turned gray –Used regarding the eye. ⟨**Béro manxán ikáxa rábini káyamake, kénakanabi.** They invited him but he didn't go, because he was ashamed that his eye had turned gray.⟩
See under **bóo**

*v.t.* **manxanhaa** *Konibo* **manxánhaka** 1 : to put out or dry in the sun or by the fire ⟨**Nokon tári mechá íketianra en barín manxánhake.** I put my wet cushma (tunic) out in the sun.⟩ ⟨**Oín mecháara, moa non chópa chíikan manxánhake.** We have already dried by the fire the clothes that the rain had gotten wet.⟩ 2 : to cause to fade ⟨**Nokon kotón titán nétetibi barínko akára manxánke.** Mother faded my shirt by putting it out in the sun every day.⟩

*n.* **manxánteon** [from Shipibo *manxán* heron + *teo*, element from *téoti* necklace] : tuyuyo (jabiru stork) ⟨**Manxánteon jawen báke kópinaketianra, Korín Nima oínkaxamai bepóke.** Korín Nima covered her face so as not to see the jabiru stork near her baby, afraid it would cutipar (cast a harmful spell on) her little one.⟩
*v.i.* **mánxana** 1 : to dry in the sun or by the fire 2 : to fade ⟨**Jawen chiárexti manxán iketianra rábini jóyamake.** He didn't come because he was ashamed of his faded trousers.⟩
*n.* **manxántonin** [from Old Shipibo *máka, makán* tooth + *xantó* ditch] : palate ⟨**Kirípininra ea íbirai nokon manxántora isín iki.** Maybe I have the flu, because my palate hurts.⟩
See under **wáko**

*Konibo* **maxónbina** *n.* **manxóbinakan** *Konibo* **maxónbinakan** *also* **manxóbinan** : crown of the head ⟨**Moátianron-** **ki jonín káshibo tsákanike manxónbinain.** They say that long ago a man stabbed a Cashibo man in the crown of the head.⟩ ⟨**Kímika yóitima bakénronki maxónbinaki awá tsakánike.** They say that long ago three unruly children deliberately struck a sachavaca (tapir) on the crown of its head.⟩
*n.* **Maón** [from Spanish *mau,* element from *Maura*] –Used as a woman's name.
*adj.* **máoxen** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the head + *ox*, element from *jóxo* whitish] : gray-haired, whitish-haired

*adj.* **máoxen** [from Shipibo *ma,* element from *mái* earth + *ox*, element from *jóxo* white] : white earth : a kind of clay used to whiten pottery ⟨**Xatéxon máoxen akáronki jakón iki; játian jími bóyamai.** They say it is good to put white clay on a cut, to keep the blood from flowing.⟩
*n.* **mapán** [from Spanish] : map ⟨**Nato riki Piró tsékakana mápa.** This is the map of Peru.⟩

*also* **mapáche** *n.* **mapáchinin** *also* **mapáchenin** [from Spanish] : raccoon ⟨**Mapáchira jáke Nóriti Amirikain jáinoax Sóro Amirikain. Ja riki jawéki ánima ochítitio. Ikáxbi jawen jínares nenké. Janra píti chókai, pínoxon.** The raccoon lives in North America and in South America. It is an animal about the size of a dog, not very large, with a long tail. It washes its food before eating.⟩ *syn.* bósa

*v.t.* **mápana** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the head + *pánati* to hang] : to cover (e.g., with a hat, headscarf, mat, bijao leaf, or raincoat) ⟨**Oi béaitianra nokon titán chómo en peín mapánke.** When it was raining, I covered mother's jar with a bijao leaf.⟩ *syn.* mápoti
*v.t.* **mápasa** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the head + *pátsati* to pat lightly] 1 : to put one's hand on the head 2 : to feel, palpate (e.g., a child) on the head affectionately, or for a healing

*v.i.* **mápekeeta** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the head + *pekéti* to become hollow] : to become perforated in the head or inside the head; *specif.* : to develop a cavity (a tooth) ⟨**En piaitianra nokon xéta mapekenin ea chexake.** When I was eating, my decayed tooth started to hurt.⟩

*Konibo* **mápekeeti** *v.i.* **mápemeeta** *Konibo* **mápekeeta** [from Shipibo *mápeti* to go up + *mee-* and *kee-*, reflexive sufs.] : to come uncovered ⟨**Nato xéatia chómo mápemeeketianra, xóya nanéke.** When this jar of drink came uncovered, a mouse got into it.⟩ ⟨**Yámikentira ícha xéatiaikax mapékeemeke.** The metal pot came uncovered because it had so much drink in it.⟩

*v.t.* **mápena** [from Shipibo *mápeti* to go up + *-n* verbalizing suf.] : to uncover : to open (e.g., a box with a lid) ⟨**Jawen maríta mapénketianra jawen pátoronin jóni kastíkanke.** The boss punished the man because he opened his suitcase.⟩ *syn.* kepénti

*v.i.* **mápeta** : to climb up (e.g., out of the water) at an angle ⟨**Inkán iná ainbo jénemeranoax mapéketianron**qui jonín yatánike. They say that when the Inca's servant girl came up out of the water at an angle, a man grabbed her.⟩ ⟨**Xóbo bochiki mapéketianra yómetso yatánkanke.** When the thief climbed up onto the top of the house, they caught him.⟩
*v.i.* **mápexa** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the head + *pex*, element from *péxma* laden, half-closed + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to open (the eyes) suddenly 2 : to clear away (clouds, from the sun)
*n.* **mapín** : shrimp ⟨**Moátianronki iká iki westíora mápijoni, jawen béro chánka.** They say that long ago there was a shrimp-man with bulging eyes.⟩
*v.i.* **mápishiita** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the head + *pishúti* to come unhooked] : to come loose (a cord) from the top part of a crossbow

*n.* **mapón** : head ⟨**Káchio káxonki jóni téxtekaanike; jatian jawen mápobichoki tárameeti jónike.** They say that once a man went into the jungle and cut his own throat; only his head came rolling back.⟩

*n.* **mápokan** [from Shipibo *mapóti* lid] : clay –Often used adjectivally as a modifier of the noun that follows it. ⟨**Mapó jóniakanaronki tétekan bópaonike, jóni shinánkin.** They say that long ago the hawk used to carry off clay figures shaped like people, thinking they were real people.⟩
[from Shipibo *mapó* clay + *áti* to make] : to make pottery ⟨**Mapó axón en ícha koríki bikénbira ea yómetsoakanke.** I earned a lot of money making pottery, and it was stolen from me.⟩
See under **bína**

*n.* **mapóchekerenin** [from Shipibo *mapó* clay + *chékere,* imitative of its shriek] : a species of wasp similar to the *joshínbina* wasp, but with the abdomen separated from the head by a thin, long segment ⟨**Mapóchekereninra báke xóntako tékake, jánbi méeresaitian.** A *mapóchekere* wasp stung a girl because she had disturbed it.⟩
*n.* **mápokan téetaitonin** [from Shipibo *mapó, mápokan* clay + *téetai* worker] : potter
*v.t.* **mapókeres aka** : to smooth (clay) by rubbing
*v.t.* : to polish pottery
*n.* **mapósanin** : a species of tree that yields resin

*v.t.* **mápoa** [from Shipibo *mápo* head + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to cover, to cap ⟨**Máikini mápotira ea papán yóike, jaín nokon wétsa kánaketian.** My father sent me to cover a hole in the ground so my little brother wouldn't fall into it.⟩ *syn.* mapánti
*v.i.* **mápota** 1 : to become covered ⟨**Chopán janbíx mapóketianra báke jóiman réteke.** A baby suffocated when it became covered by a blanket.⟩ 2 : to cover one's head

*n.* **mapótinin** [from Shipibo *mapóti, mapot-* to become covered + *-ti,* instrument with which] 1 : lid, cover ⟨**Yámikenti mapótira báke yóitiman chíiki pótake.** The unruly child threw the metal pot's lid into the fire.⟩ 2 : thatch roof-ridge of a roof ⟨**Níweaba pakéxonra nokon xóbo mapóti pótake.** A gust of wind came and tore off the thatch ridge of my house.⟩ 3 : almayari : pamacari (tarpaulin roof cover) ⟨**Mapótioma íketianra noa oín mecháake.** The rain soaked us because we had no pamacari (tarp cover).⟩
See under **wása**

*n.* **mápoxaon** [from Shipibo *mápo* head + *xáo* bone] : skull : cranium ⟨**Káchio kaxónra mápoxao non méranike, jóni inón piní.** We went into the jungle many years ago and found the skull of a man that a jaguar had devoured.⟩
*adj.* **mápoyenkeman** [from Shipibo *mápo* head + *yenkén*] : bald : hairless ⟨**Ja kirínkora mápoyenken iki.** That gringo is completely bald.⟩ *syn.* mayén
*n.* **Marán** [from Spanish *marga,* element from *Margarita*] –Used as a woman's name.
*v.i.* **márachana** [from Spanish] : to march ⟨**Píshtatianra sontárobo bántayabo márachanai.** On feast days the soldiers march wearing their leg wrappings.⟩
*also* **márka** *n.* **márakanin** *also* **márkanin** [from Spanish *marka*] : mark : stamp *syn.* síyo

*n.* **márakantin** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the top of the head + *rákati, raka-* to put + *-n,* verbalizing suf. *-ti* instrument with which] : ridge beam (of a roof) ⟨**Xoboakira márakantinkoniax jóni pakéke.** While building the house, a man fell from the ridge beam.⟩

*n.* **Marányanin** [from Spanish] : Marañón River ⟨**Moátianronkí Marányanimea táshi bípaokanike non rekénbaon.** They say that in the old days our ancestors used to go get salt from the Marañón River.⟩
*n.* **máratichon** [from Spanish] : hammer
*n.* **máraxen** : huaca (ancient burial mound / artifact) *syn.* áxa
*v.t.* **márena** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the crown + *rénkati* to rub] : to rub (a hat) on the crown of the head
*v.t.* **máreta** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the top of the head + *rérati* to cut] : to strike on the head hard enough to cause cuts to
*n.* **marín** : añuje (agouti) : picuro ⟨**Káshibobaonra mári xetán píai.** The Cashibo make their arrows with agouti teeth, which serve as blades.⟩
*n.* **Márianin** [from Spanish] –Used as a woman's name.
See under **bína**
*also* **márinero** *n.* **máriniron** *also* **márineron** [from Spanish] : sailor ⟨**Márinirobaon shinánkana iki, moa jabo mái kéxa taxnáti kaí.** The sailors thought they were close to land.⟩
See under **kómatsewe**

*Konibo* **máritanwis** *n.* **maríntanhisin** *Konibo* **máritanwisin** [from Shipibo *mári, marín* agouti + *tanhís,* unidentified element] : a species of tree with a straight, slender trunk and long-lasting wood, used for fishing rods and house frames
*v.t.* **maríshkia** : to hit on the head with a stick or whip
*n.* **máritanin** [from Spanish] : suitcase ⟨**Jawen maríta mapénketianra, jawen pátoronin jóni kastíkanke.** The boss punished the man because he opened his suitcase.⟩ *syn.* bonánti

*v.t.* **máromaa** [from Shipibo *mároti, maro-* to buy + *-ma,* causative] : to sell ⟨**Minra ea paránshon máromake mínama ikénbi; jahuen ibónra ea yokáke. You've deceived me by selling me something that wasn't yours; its owner has asked me about it.⟩ *syn.* MAROMATI, MAROTI can both be translated as "to sell", though MAROTI can also mean "to buy". MAROMATI is the preferred word for "to sell" when the sale is made at the direct request of the buyer.

*v.i.* **mároa** 1 : to buy ⟨**Moa mároi senénkanketianra ea katánke.** I left after they had finished buying.⟩ 2 : to sell ⟨**Aínbobora jatón téotinin mároi bokánke.** The women went to sell their necklaces.⟩
See **jaín mároti shóbo**
*v.t.* **masáaka** [from Shipibo *ma-* from the top + *sáati* to spill] : to pour out (e.g., by spilling) a quantity onto the ground

*v.t.* **masáa** *Konibo* **masáaka** 1 : to ruin ⟨**Onányamaxonbi nóntiakinra jonín masáake.** Trying to make a canoe without knowing how, the man ruined it.⟩ 2 : to damage : to spoil ⟨**Nato mikánikora rámakaya áxei ítai; jákopira nokon motóro masáake.** This mechanic is just now learning, and he has ruined my motor.⟩ *syn.* MASAATI, RAMIATI both carry the sense of "to damage"; but MASAATI mostly implies damage to a thing, while RAMIATI mostly implies mistreating a person. –Used as an ironic, joking expression to indicate that something described as "completely ruined" is in reality good and valuable.
*n.* **masábires ténetinin** [from Shipibo *masá téneti*, *tene-* to suffer + *-ti* instrument with which] : suffering : tribulation
*adj.* **masámatonbires** [from Shipibo *masabires* completely ruined + *-ma* not] : magnificent : wonderful : well done ⟨**¡Masámabiresiki nato teé!** What a job, and so well done!⟩
See under **méeti**
See under **shinánti**
See under **téneti**

*v.i.* **másata** 1 : to be at fault ⟨**Minbíxa moa mia masáke; jaskápainonra nokon jói min senénhayamake.** It's your own fault; you didn't heed my advice.⟩ 2 : to break down, to go wrong ⟨**Bóchikiaxbira ábion masáke; jaín páketara onántima iki.** The plane broke down in mid-air, and nobody knows where it crashed.⟩ ⟨**Ráo másata shéaasha nato jóni pasná iki.** This man is pale from drinking a spoiled herbal remedy.⟩ 3 : to have bad luck ⟨**Jawen jakóma shinánya kopira nato jóni masáke.** This man has had bad luck because of his evil thoughts.⟩

*v.t.* **máwaa** : to imitate (e.g., a voice or action) ⟨**Non íno kéotai máwaketianronki noa bíti iki.** They say that when we imitate a jaguar roaring, it can attack us.⟩ ⟨**En ákaikeskaakinribi máwakanwe.** Imitate what I do.⟩ ⟨**Nato jónira máwamis iki; jáskatira ishtón ásheai.** This man is a good mimic; no wonder he learns quickly.⟩ ⟨**Nato jonín xóbora jakónhira iki; rámara já mawá énribi anóxiki.** This man's house is very beautiful; now I too will try to make one just like it.⟩

*v.i.* **máwata** 1 : to faint as if dead ⟨**Mawáyoshin béchiashonki noa mawáti iki.** They say that when we encounter a ghost, we can faint.⟩ 2 : to die ⟨**Rókotoronra mawátibishoko jóni ráonai; bénxoti jisáma riki.** The doctor is treating a person who is about to die; but it seems there is no hope of recovery.⟩ ⟨**Jíria íketianra noa jóniki rakéyamai; moa máwata íketianresa noa ráketai.** When someone is alive, we are not afraid of them; but when they are dead, we are.⟩ 3 : to be (the sun or moon) in a state of eclipse ⟨**Jónibora bári mawáketian rakeérakebaini risánti xobón bokánke, jaton báchi iábaini.** Once when there was a solar eclipse, some people went to the church frightened, carrying their mosquito nets.⟩ *syn.* MAWATI, MAXKATI, REBESTI all can be translated as "to die". MAWATI and MAXKATI can additionally be translated as "to faint". MAWATI, then, in its main sense means "to die" in any manner. With the sense of "to faint", MAXKATI suggests an appearance of death (e.g., from a terrible fright). MAXKATI, when the suffix *-bain* is added, takes the form *máxkabainti* and means "to faint" and suggests a brief state of death that then passes. Where the form MAXKATI is found with the sense of "to die", this can imply a fainting that precedes death. REBESTI implies the extinction of life with emphasis on its final moment.

*v.t.* **máxkaa** 1 : to faint —Used in this sense with the suffix *-bain*, "going and doing". —Used without a direct object; however, one must understand an implied object, *join* "breath", so that the expression *join máxkati* would literally be "to cause breath to be lacking". ⟨**Jawen yóra páxnaxoko ikáxbi íxtoxonra jonín máxkabainke.** Running with a weak body, the man fainted.⟩ ⟨**Aínbaonra áni báke píkokin máxkabainke.** The woman fainted while giving birth to a large baby.⟩ 2 : to expire, to die ⟨**Moa máxkaa rabé óra wínota pekaora mia jóke. Moácha joxónra min jíria nókokeanke.** You have come two hours after he expired; if you had come a little sooner, you would have still found him alive.⟩ ⟨**Yaméra máxkawanke; bakíshara míinkanai.** He just expired tonight, and tomorrow they will bury him.⟩ *syn.* See under **máwati**
