*v.i.* **máyata** 1 : to spin, to rotate ⟨**Nato mái máyatainbira non onányamake ániora íketian.** Even though the earth is spinning, we don't notice it because it is so huge.⟩ 2 : to go around in circles ⟨**Onányamax káxa ea mayáke bénotax; jákopira ea ixtón jóyamake.** I went off without knowing the way, got lost, and wandered around in circles; that's why I couldn't get back quickly.⟩
See under xóbo
*adj.* **máyeman** [from Shipibo *ma-* on the crown of the head + *yen*, element from *yenkén* smooth, soft] 1 : bald 2 : with a shaved head *syn.* **mápoyenken**

*also* **máyorona** *n.* **mayón** *also* **máyoronan** : Matsés : Mayoruna : member of the Matsés linguistic group ⟨**Rámara moa máyobo ráea iki; jatíribira Yarínain békana iki.** Now some Matsés are already civilized, and some have come to Yarina.⟩
*adj.* **máyoshin** [from Shipibo *ma-* on top + *yóshoti, yosho-* to twist] : with a crooked ridge beam
*v.t.* **máyota** [from Shipibo, on the crown of the head + *yókati* to apply] : to apply something thick to the crown of the head of

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *mekén* hand] 1 : on the hand : to the hand : of the hand ⟨**méchokiiti** to wash one's hands⟩ 2 : on the finger : to the finger : of the finger ⟨**ménto** without fingers⟩ 3 : on the fingernail : to the fingernail : of the fingernail ⟨**méstati** to cut the nails of⟩ 4 : on the wrist : to the wrist : of the wrist ⟨**menchán** lump on the wrist⟩ 5 : on the front foot : to the front foot : of the front foot ⟨**mespó** with bushy hair on the front legs⟩ 6 : on insect legs : to insect legs : of insect legs ⟨**mébi** insect legs⟩ 7 : on the outer branches : to the outer branches : of the outer branches ⟨**metóti** to gather (fruit) from the outer branches⟩ 8 : in the shape of fingers ⟨**mexbí** a fringe of finger-shaped cords hung from something as an ornament⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*n.* **Meán** –Used as a woman's name.

*locative suf.* : from —Used in a sentence, added to a noun, adverb, or postposition that ends in a nasalized vowel, to indicate a place of origin. —Often used with *-ax* in the compound form *-meax* to indicate a place from which something comes. ⟨**Jara jemámea iki.** He is from the village.⟩ ⟨**Jára iámeax jóke.** He has come from the oxbow lake.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5; 8.3.2

*v.t.* **meánhaa** *Konibo* **meánhaka** : to spread out (leafy branches) ⟨**Jíwi mebi xátexonra, bái napon papán meánhake chóshinon ixon.** Father cut the outer branches of the tree and spread them out on the path so they would dry.⟩

*v.i.* **méana** [from Shipibo *me-* on the outer branches + *jánati* to return] : to be, become, or grow leafy/bushy ⟨**Moa meántires ikénbira jéne bexón mánkoa réteke.** When this mango tree was about to become leafy, the flood came and dried it out.⟩ ⟨**Jíwi méanainra manxánteon bákeai.** The tuyuyo (stork) nests and hatches its young in trees that grow leafy.⟩
*v.t.* **mébena** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand, on the outer branch + *bénati* to search] 1 : to examine in the hand 2 : to search in the outer branches of a tree

*n.* **mebín** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *bi*, unidentified element] 1 : finger ⟨**Jonínronki jawen mébibo yamín xátekin kéyonike, jíwi xátekin.** They say that long ago a man cut off all his fingers with the axe while cutting a tree.⟩ 2 : branches ⟨**Jiwín néetash penixon mébi sékeaxa bákeranon pakéke.** While climbing a tree, the young man stood on the twigs, broke them, and fell to the ground.⟩ 3 : insect legs ⟨**Nato xontakora shínakoxon mébiki ráketai.** This young lady is afraid of the spider's legs.⟩ *syn.* See under **mekémebi**
*v.t.* **mébichina** [from Shipibo *me-* from the hand + *bichínti* to remove] : to take out of the hands of
*adj.* **mébisin** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *bísi* skin warts] : with the hand covered in warts
*v.i.* **mebískiika** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *bískiiti* to shake in a rotating motion] : to shake one's hand with a rotating motion

*adj.* **mechán** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *cha*, unidentified element] : good hunter : good fisherman ⟨**Moátianronki mécha jóniki wánomakatikanai.** They say that in the old days they used to marry their daughters to men who were good fishermen.⟩
*adj.* **méchakan** 1 : wet 2 : damp ⟨**Bári ishtón xánayamaketianra non chópa mechábi sáweke.** We put on our clothes still damp, because the sun hadn't come out.⟩

*v.i.* **mécháa** *Konibo* **mecháaka** : to get wet, to wet (something) ⟨**Jawen titán jaskáatima yóiabira nato aínbaon jawen chitónti mecháake.** This little woman got her pampanilla (skirt) wet, even though her mother had forbidden it.⟩

*adj.* **mechámanin** [from Shipibo *mechá* wet + *-ma* not] : dry –Used regarding something that is normally wet from time to time. ⟨**Kámpo mecháma iketianra ábion pakéke non jemán.** When the airstrip was dry, the small plane landed in our village.⟩ *syn.* chóshi
See under **ráo**
*v.t.* **méchaa** : to make into, or to become, a good fisherman or hunter ⟨**Méchanoxon ráo xéaaxa jóni mawáke.** A man drank an herbal remedy to become a good hunter, and he died.⟩
*v.i.* **méchata** : to get wet ⟨**Páronapon réokootaxa non játibi chópabo méchata iki.** All our clothes got wet when we capsized in the middle of the river.⟩
See under **wáste**
*v.t.* **méchax** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *cháxati* to work with an axe] : to work (a tree) by removing the stubs of a branch
*v.t.* **méchexa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *chéxati* to hurt] : to hurt the hand of
*v.i.* **méchexa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *chéxeti* to turn black] 1 : to drop medicine onto the hand of 2 : to blacken the hand of

*v.i.* **méchia** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *chi-* backward + *-ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to bend the hand (e.g., to indicate a direction) 2 : to aim or shoot an arrow in the wrong direction ⟨**Enra jasín tsákakin kéneke, wétsaorires méchixon.** I shot my arrow at the paují (curassow), but I missed, shooting off in the wrong direction.⟩

*adj.* **mechón** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *cho*, unidentified element] : an inexperienced worker, or one who does work poorly ⟨**Noa mécho iketian osánkanaronki sinátima iki.** They say that if someone laughs at us for being inexperienced, we should not get angry.⟩ *syn.* yósma
: to not demand, or stop demanding, work ⟨**Papánra jawen báke mécho ímake jawéki ámakashamaxon.** This boy doesn't know how to do things well, because his father never demanded that he work.⟩

*adj.* **mechón** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *cho*, element also from *mácho* with boils on the head] 1 : with boils on the hand 2 : ugly : bad —Used in this sense more among speakers of Konibo. *syn.* See under jakóma
See under **mécho**
*v.i.* **méchokiita** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *chokiti*] : to wash one's hands

*v.i.* **méchoa** : to lose a habit, to become out of practice ⟨**Moátianra nato jóni nóntiati onán ikátiai; rámara moa méchoke bási áyamax.** Before, this man was an expert at making canoes, but now he has become out of practice from not having done it in a long time.⟩
*v.t.* **méchota** : to wash the hands of ⟨**Titánra báke mechóke.** The mother washed her child's hands.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.3
See **mírio**

*verbal suf.* **-meet** : to (myself, yourself, ourselves, oneself) —Used added to the verb in a small class of transitive verbs, which with this suffix become intransitive with reflexive meaning. ⟨**Jáskataxa báke kíshpimeeke.** In that way the child saved himself.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.3

*v.i.* **méekaata** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *-kaati* to do (something specific) to oneself] : to touch oneself ⟨**Titára jawen pokónko méekaake, tóoyara íbirai ixon onánox.** The mother touched her own belly to find out whether she was pregnant.⟩

*v.t.* **méeta** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *-ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to touch ⟨**Jáwebi méeyamawe; noara wétsa jonín xobón iki.** Don't touch anything; we're in someone else's house.⟩ 2 : to do (something harmful) to ⟨**Ea méeyamawepanon.** Please don't do anything to me.⟩

[from Shipibo *masá* ruined + *méeti* to touch] : to deprive oneself ⟨**Yobénoxon ónanai jónira masá méeti ónisai jatibi jawekiati, átipanyamax jakopira yobeti atipa yamake.** The apprentice becomes sad from depriving himself of food for a long time, and yet he still cannot become a shaman.⟩

*n.* **meín** : apacharama (a tree); *also* : the bark of the apacharama, which when charred gives strength to the clay used in pottery ⟨**Chéxeinkanronki jato áxeaa iki, méi betan mapó méskoti.** They say that Black Inca taught the people how to mix apacharama bark with clay.⟩ *syn.* ápacharan
*v.i.* **meíkia** [from Shipibo *me-* from the hand + *jíkiti* to enter] : to put one's hand in very deep
See **-main**

*v.t.* **méina** [from Shipibo *méi* apacharama + *-n,* verbalizing suf. + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to mix with apacharama bark ⟨**Mapó méinkonama ikénbi chómoaara básiamai tóetai.** When a large jar is made from clay that is not well mixed with apacharama bark, it doesn't take long to break.⟩

*v.t.* **méisa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *jis-* to see + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to look at the hand of (oneself or another person) 2 : to look around at (branches) 3 : to look at (a person or thing) up in the branches around

*v.t.* **méita** [from Shipibo *me-* with the hand + *jíkiti* to enter] : to put one's hand into ⟨**Mapóronki ixonra, nato aínbaon mánores meíke, yamé íketian.** Thinking it was clay, this woman put her hand into the mud, because it was very dark.⟩
See **Míjiko**

*adv. and postp.* [*me-* on the hand + *-kaya* indeed + *o*, element from *oke* on the other side] *adv.* : with the right hand, or on the right ⟨**Nato bakénra mékayao pikáshamakin mémiores píai.** This child wants to eat with his left hand, not with his right.⟩ *postp.* : to the right of –Used added to the possessive pronoun or to the noun that serves as its complement. ⟨**Káchio káxa, bái mekayao káx nokon épa benóke.** My uncle went into the jungle and got lost by going to the right of the path.⟩

*also* **mekémapoani** *n.* **mekémapon** *also* **mekémapoanin** [from Shipibo *mekén* finger + *mápo* head + *áni* big] : thumb ⟨**Jawen mekémapokira nato báke binán tékake, yatánketian.** The wasp stung this child on the thumb when he grabbed it.⟩
See **mekémapo**

*n.* **mekémebin** [from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *mébi* finger] : finger ⟨**Nato jónira mekémebi nenkébo iki, jaskábi píkota ikax.** This man has long fingers, born that way.⟩ *syn.* MEKEMEBI, MEBI can both mean "finger"; but MEBI, unlike MEKEMEBI which has only this one meaning, also has other senses.

*n.* **mekémpekaten** *Konibo* **mekémpekakan** [from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *peká* back] : back of the hand ⟨**Mekémpeka shánokan nátexara jóni mawáke.** A man died when a jergón (fer-de-lance snake) bit him on the back of the hand.⟩

*n.* **mékeman** : hand ⟨**Nokon mékayaó mekén jaínxon nokon mémiokea mekénra óinke.** He looked at my right hand, and then at my left.⟩ ⟨**Yómetso jónira mekén xátenaankanke, koríki icha bíketian.** The thief had his hand cut off for stealing a lot of money.⟩
[from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *tónkoati* to round] : to make a fist : to close the hand ⟨**Jóninra jawen rayós mekén tónkoaxon tímake paénxon.** A drunk man made a fist and punched his father-in-law.⟩
*n.* **mekénapaxen** [from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *nápax* raw] : palm of the hand ⟨**Jatiribi jóniboronki mekéna-** **pax wáchoshoko iki.** They say that some people have very soft palms.⟩

*n.* **mekénchinitaton** [from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *chiníti, chínita* to remain last] : little finger, pinky ⟨**Oroaitianra jóni ronón natéxke jawen mekénchinitain.** While farming, the man was bitten by a snake on his little finger.⟩

*n.* **mekéntechapanin** [from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *te-* at the neck + *chápata* fold of the hand] : web between two fingers ⟨**Kirínko bakera, mekéntechapain jawen ochítininbi natéxke.** A young gringo boy was bitten between his fingers by his own dog.⟩
*n.* **mekéntonkon** [from Shipibo *mekén* hand + *tónko* round] : fist
See under **mekén**

*v.t.* **mékeaa** 1 : to economize : to use little by little ⟨**Enra mékexon asókaro ákai yámaketian.** I'm rationing sugar because there's little of it.⟩ 2 : to guard jealously ⟨**Asókaro titán mékea ikénbira, báke yoitiman kéyonaanke.** The disobedient child finished off all the sugar that mother had jealously been saving.⟩ 3 : to keep in good condition : to keep or maintain (e.g., clothing for wearing) clean and nice ⟨**Nato jonínra jatíbitian jawen jawékibo mékeai.** This man always keeps his belongings in good condition.⟩ 4 : to watch over jealously or anxiously ⟨**Sarámpinin báke íketianra titán jawen báke mékeai.** The mother watches jealously over her child when he has measles.⟩ 5 : to protect from evil influences ⟨**Jonínra jawen báke pikóketian mékekin xóno xáteyamai kópinaketian.** When a son is born, the man protects him and doesn't cut lupuna (kapok tree), for fear of cutipar-ing (casting a harmful spell on) his little son.⟩

*v.i.* **méketa** 1 : to proceed carefully : to become cunning ⟨**Piti bénaira noa méketai.** When we go looking for mitayo (game meat), we become cunning.⟩ 2 : to perform rites of abstinence ⟨**Méchatiwaste xéaaxonki mekéti iki.** They say that when one drinks piripiri (a medicinal plant) to become a good fisherman, one must perform rites of abstinence.⟩ 3 : to stay inside the mosquito net fasting ⟨**Nato jónira rabé néte méketai.** This man has been fasting inside the mosquito net for two days.⟩

*Konibo* **mékexoya** *n.* **mékexeeyanin** *Konibo* **mékexeeyaton, mékexoyan** [from Shipibo *me-* on the front foot + *kexé* sewn + *-ee* reflexive suf. + *-ya* with] : a species of lizard considered poisonous, with webbed membranes between its toes : salamander : salamanca ⟨**Mékexeeyara natéxmisma iki; ikáxbira jawen mekénhain itan taénko mókaya iki.** The salamanca doesn't bite, but it has venom in its front and hind feet.⟩ ⟨**Mékexoyara xánbo jisáribi iki; ikáxbi jawen jína nenkéma iki.** The salamander looks very much like a lizard, but has a short tail.⟩ ⟨**Kakónkonia aínbora mékexoyan réteke.** A woman from Caco was killed by a salamanca.⟩ *syn.* née

*v.t.* **mékexa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the fingers or finger + *kéxeti* to sew] : to stitch up the fingers or finger of ⟨**Ochítinin natéxketianra nato báke rókotoron mekéxke.** When a dog bit the fingers of this child, the doctor stitched them up.⟩
*adj.* **mékoshin** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *kóshi* strong] 1 : with a strong hand : strong-handed 2 : with a fist strong for attacking 3 : with a fist another person cannot easily pry open
*v.i.* **mémenoota** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *ménoti* to burn] : to burn one's hand ⟨**Jara chíikan meménooke.** She burned her hand in the fire.⟩
*n.* **memín** : a species of demon resembling a maquisapa (spider monkey) or another small animal, which lives in abandoned houses and can injure or kill a person with its breath

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *me-* from the hand + *mi*, unidentified element + *oke* on the other side] *adv.* : to the left ⟨**Nato baín káx mémio bái ikátonin katánwe; ján riki min pápa.** Going along this path, turn in on the left; that's where your father is.⟩ *postp.* : to the left of –Used after the possessive adjective or a noun that serves as its complement. ⟨**Nokon mémio jowé miara yatánake.** Stay to my left so that it doesn't grab you.⟩ ⟨**Páro memiora motóro jíkike.** The motor sank on the left bank of the river.⟩
*v.t.* **mémosa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *mótsati* to squeeze, crush] 1 : to massage by squeezing the hand of 2 : to crumble by squeezing hard (something in another's hand)
*v.t.* **mémoxa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *móxati* to strike] : to hit or strike on the hand of

*modifying suf.* 1 : fast : quickly —Used added to the verb in the imperative mood. ⟨**Xobón kaméntanwe.** Go quickly to the house.⟩ 2 : beforehand : ahead of time : early —Used added to the verb in the indicative mood. ⟨**Moa píshta ikáinra ea joménke, jawékiatibo beí.** Since the feast is already approaching, I came ahead of time, bringing provisions.⟩
*v.i.* **ménatexmeeta** [from Shipibo *ménatexti* to bite the hand of + *-mee*, reflexive suf.] : to bite one's own hand ⟨**Bákera ménatexmeetai.** The child is biting his own hand.⟩
*v.t.* **ménatexa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *nátexti* to bite] : to bite the hand of ⟨**Jawen wetsánbira báke ménatexai.** The child's own brother is biting his hand.⟩
*n.* **ménchaman** [from Shipibo *me-* on the wrist + *chánko* lump] : a lump on the wrist
*v.i.* **ménexeeta** [from Shipibo *menéxti* to tie + *-ee*, reflexive suf.] : to tie one's own hand

*also* **móromenexeeti** *Konibo* **ménexeti** *n.* **ménexeetinin** *also* **móromenexeetinin** *Konibo* **ménexetin** [from Shipibo *móro* bead + *me-* on the hand, on the wrist + *nex*, element from *néxati* to tie + *-ee*, reflexive suf. + *-ti* instrument with which] : beaded bracelet ⟨**Rímameaxa jóni móromenexetin ménexeeya jóke; jáskara ikénra Ínka shinánkanke.** A man came from Lima wearing beaded bracelets, and because of that they thought he was the Inca.⟩
*v.t.* **ménexa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *néxati* to tie] : to tie the hands or fingers of

*v.i.* **ménikaata** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *níakaati* to get into] : to take something for oneself ⟨**Chíchika ménikanon ishon jato yóiabira tsónbi pápa méniamake; játianra moa janbíx ménikaake.** Father insisted that they give him the knife, but no one gave it to him; finally he took it himself.⟩
*adj.* **méniman** [from Shipibo *me-* on the fingers + *-nin*, instrumental suf.] : artistic : skilled : talented ⟨**Menín aínbo riki kené onán.** A talented woman knows how to make designs.⟩

*v.t.* **menínhaa** *Konibo* **menínhaka** : to make into an artist ⟨**Ichaakin wastén raónxonra, titán jawen báke menínhake.** By treating her many times with piripiri (a medicinal plant), the mother made her daughter into an artist.⟩
*v.i.* **ménina** : to become an artist ⟨**Rámara ea moa menínke wétsabaon jawéki aká máwaax.** I finally became an artist, by copying what others do.⟩
See under **wáste**

*v.t.* **ménia** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *níati* to put in] : to give ⟨**Pátoroninra jawen jónibo koríki ménike, xonón téekanon ishon.** The boss gave his workers money as an advance so they would go cut lupuna (kapok trees).⟩

*v.i.* **ménita** : to distribute, to hand out ⟨**Jáwenama ikénbira nato aínbo chopán ménitai; rámara jawen íbo sínatai.** This woman is handing out clothing that isn't hers; her owner might get angry.⟩

*adj.* **ménkoten** *Konibo* **ménkokan** 1 : face down —Used regarding living beings. 2 : egg-laying ⟨**Nokon nonón menkó ikénbira nokon papán pátoronin bóke.** My father's boss took my egg-laying duck.⟩ 3 : broody —Used regarding a hen. ⟨**Atapa menkokanra píamai, moa ísiman yátana ixon.** The broody hen doesn't want to eat, because the plague has taken hold of her.⟩

*v.t.* **menkómaa** [from Shipibo *menkó* broody + *-ma* to cause + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to set to brood or to lay ⟨**Titán jawen átapa menkómakenbira ochítinin jawen báchibo tóshamake.** Mother set her hen to brood, but the dog made it break its eggs.⟩

*v.t.* **ménkona** [from Shipibo *menkó* face down + *-n* verbalizing suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to put face down, upside down ⟨**Titán kentí ménkonara kochín páke, íshtoi kakín.** Running past, the pig knocked over the pot that mother had set upside down.⟩

*v.i.* **ménkota** 1 : to lie or be face down ⟨**Nónti ménkota ikáinkora, yáwa ina iki, káchiokea beá.** In the place where the canoe is turned face down, there is a young collared peccary, brought from the jungle.⟩ ⟨**Ishtoaxa jóni menkóke moa páxkinax.** The tired man lay down face down, already exhausted.⟩ 2 : to brood : to lay eggs : to incubate ⟨**Atapa ménkotara awápanin yamé boánke.** Last night the brooding hen was carried off by the ocelot.⟩ *syn.* bákeati

*adj. and n.* **ménokan** *adj.* : burned ⟨**Moa wái menó ikénbi átsa bánayamaara moa náwea iki.** Even though the field had already been burned, they didn't plant manioc, and it turned into purma (fallow secondary growth).⟩ *n.* : burn

*v.t.* **ménoa** 1 : to burn ⟨**Wái ménokinra manánxawe píchika bikánke, wétsa moa méxota.** While burning the field, they caught five motelos (tortoises), one of them already charred.⟩ 2 : to set fire to; *specif.* : to burn down and destroy ⟨**Nokon xóbora kéyo ménoke nokon ráwikan.** My enemy burned down and completely destroyed my house.⟩ *syn.* mexóati; tiríti
*v.i.* **ménota** : to get burned ⟨**Janbíx ménotara jóni óspitarain bokánke.** The man who got burned was taken to the hospital.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.3
*adj.* **ménsaman** : with a radial crack (e.g., of a mirror struck in the middle)
See **mínta**
*adj.* **mentón** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *-nto* without] 1 : maimed, one-handed : without a hand 2 : without a finger or fingers

*n.* **méntsisen** [from Shipibo *me-* on the finger + *tsisa,* unidentified element] 1 : fingernail ⟨**Jóni mentsís nenkéra Kakónko nokóke, néte máyai jóai.** A man with long fingernails, who was going around circling the world, arrived at Caco.⟩ 2 : claw
[from Shipibo *táe* foot + *mentsís* nail] : toenail ⟨**Westíora jónira yómetsoketian jawen táementsis tsekákanke.** They tore out the toenails of a certain man who had stolen.⟩

*n.* **meósotin** [from Shipibo *me-* on the finger + *osóti, oso-* to fit into a tight space + *-ti* instrument with which] : ring ⟨**Nato aínbora meósoti sáweisma iki; jákopira rábinai.** This woman never wears a ring, and so she feels ashamed.⟩
*v.t.* **mépasa** [from Shipibo *me-* with the hand + *pátsati* to pat] : to place one's open hand or open hands on
*v.t.* **mépisha** [from Shipibo *me-* from the hand + *pishínti* to be lacking] 1 : to remove from the hand of 2 : to take away one's own or another's hand

*v.i.* **mépia** [from Shipibo *me-* with the hand + *píti* to eat] : to eat together with other people ⟨**Non ashé riki, yósibaon píainko báke ikax mépitima.** It is our custom that children not eat together with grown men.⟩

*v.i.* **mépia** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *pi,* unidentified element + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to come to an end (e.g., a stretch of land) ⟨**Manán mépiainkora óro jáke.** Where the slope of the hill ends, there is gold.⟩
*n.* **mépoman** [from Shipibo *me-* from the hand + *póno* vein] : vein of the hand
*v.t.* **mépoa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *po,* element also from *mápoti* to cover + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to cover the hand of
*v.i.* **mépota** : to cover one's own hand

*v.t.* **mépota** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *pótati* to throw] : to throw something at the hand of ⟨**Jonínra ea máshi mepóke en asókaro yókata; jakóma shinánya ixon.** A mean man threw a handful of sand at my hand when I asked him for sugar.⟩

*v.i.* **méramaata** [from Shipibo *mérati, méra-* to find + *ma-* to cause + *-aa,* reflexive suf.] : to be discovered in adultery or fornication ⟨**Méramaataxa aínbo jonéke.** Upon being discovered in adultery, the woman hid.⟩ ⟨**Aínbo méramaatara jahuen benén pótake.** The woman discovered in adultery was cast off by her husband.⟩ ⟨**Méramaataxa jóni jabáke.** Upon being discovered in adultery, the man fled.⟩

*postp.* : inside of ⟨**Nokon wetsán ríkara bórosa meran iki.** My brother's cast net is inside the bag.⟩ ⟨**Xóbo meran jíkiketianra yómetso yatánkanke.** They caught the thief when he entered the house.⟩ ⟨**Pátorónin tapánra Xawánya táe meran íki.** The boss's raft is inside the Shahuaya stream.⟩

*v.t.* **méraa** 1 : to find ⟨**Empari méraketianra, nokon wetsán róno mérashokoke.** When I had already found the fer-de-lance, my brother saw it too.⟩ 2 : to catch sight of ⟨**Ochokeabira nokon pápa jóaitian en mérake.** From far away I caught sight of my father coming.⟩ ⟨**Moa merá íketian nínkataxa ea ratéke.** Hearing that I had already been found, I was astonished.⟩
*n.* **mératinin** [from Shipibo *mérati, mera-* to find + *-ti* instrument with which] : lover ⟨**Nato aínbaonra jawen benén mérati bachínke.** This woman pulled the hair of her husband's lover.⟩
*v.i.* **mérata** : to visit : to pay a visit ⟨**Mérati kakénbi tsón bíamaara noa jóke.** We went to visit them, but no one received us, so we came back.⟩ *syn.* pásianti

*n.* **meráyan** *Konibo* **meráyanin** [from Shipibo *meráti, mera-* to visit + *-ya* with] : a shaman who works with spirits : spiritist ⟨**Meráyan tárironki inín iki, béroyoshinbo betan yóyo iti kopi.** They say that shamans' magical cushmas (tunics) are perfumed so that they can thereby speak with the spirits.⟩ *syn.* MERAYA, ROA, YOBE — both can be translated as "shaman" without any difference in meaning.
See **mírikato**

*v.i.* **mesénbinata** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *senbíti* to coil up + *na* unidentified element] : for the hand to coil up or shrivel ⟨**Náto jónira ísinax mesénbinake.** When this man got sick, his hand shriveled up.⟩
*adj.* **mésesen** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *sése* freckled] : with spots on the hand

*v.t.* **méshakona** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *shakónti* to shake] : to shake hands with to squeeze the hand in greeting ⟨**Jóni méshakonti shínanira pápashoko jéne meran káke.** While trying to greet a man, the old grandfather fell into the water.⟩

*n. and adj.* **meshín** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *shi*, unidentified element] *n.* 1 : small, dry branches ⟨**Méshi bénakinra káchiokea titán íno mérake.** While looking for dry twigs, mother came across a jaguar in the jungle.⟩ ⟨**Bákera binán tékake méshi ménoaitian.** The child was stung by wasps while burning the dry branches.⟩ *adj.* : very thin : frail : very slender ⟨**Nato joníra áni ikaxbi méshishoko iki.** This man is tall, but very slender.⟩
See under **boín**

*n.* **méshipapikan** *Konibo* **méshipapin** [from Shipibo *méshi* dry branches + *pápiti, papi-* to carry] : a species of caterpillar ⟨**Méshipapinra péi píai.** The *méshipapi* caterpillar eats leaves.⟩
*v.t.* **méshkana** [from Shipibo *meshkáti* to open one's fist + *-n* verbalizing suf.] : to raise the hands or fingers of
*v.i.* **méshkata** : to open one's fist by unclenching the fingers : to raise (e.g., as a sign of greeting or an oath) one's hand
*Konibo* **mesmón** *adj.* **méshmoman** *Konibo* **mésmoman** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *shomón* swollen] : with a swollen hand

*v.t.* **meshóaa** *Konibo* **meshóaka** 1 : to burn ⟨**Titan atsa xoira meshóake.** The manioc my mother roasted got burned.⟩ 2 : to char ⟨**Kasórinan ketéxonra rabé jóni meshoáke.** When the gasoline caught fire, it charred two men.⟩ *syn.* ménoti

*v.i.* **méshota** 1 : to get burned ⟨**Moa méshotainbira en mia kóma bótéxonke** I took the panguana (a bird) off the fire for you, because it was about to burn.⟩ ⟨**Meshóbira ákai nato aínbaon pikín, yoáati onáma** **íxon**. This woman always eats burnt food because she doesn't know how to cook.⟩ 2 : to become charred ⟨**Tsákaananaxa káro meshóke.** Two cars became charred after crashing into each other.⟩
*v.t.* **méshtina** [from Shipibo *me(sh)-* in the hand + *tímati* to hit] : to strike someone's hand (e.g., with a stick), causing pain but not a wound

*n.* **mésketen** *Konibo* **méskekan** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *séketi, seke-* to break] : a species of shrub similar to the mamé, with small fruits in reddish-purple clusters that are eaten by animals and fish
*v.t.* **méskia** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hands + *síkati* to paint] 1 : to paint by rubbing paint on the hands of 2 : to stain the hand of

*v.i.* **méskita** 1 : to paint one's own hands by rubbing them with paint 2 : to get one's hands stained ⟨**Ja bákebora méskitax beskitash ikanai.** The children are getting their hands and faces stained.⟩

*adj.* **méskoten** *Konibo* **méskokan** 1 : mixed ⟨**Asókaro betan táxi meskóta ikénbira onányamaxon nato bakén Xéake.** This child swallowed sugar mixed with salt without realizing it.⟩ 2 : various : different : distinct ⟨**Píshtatianra meskó jónibo márachainbake.** Yesterday various different people marched in the feast.⟩
See under **shinánti**

*v.t.* **méskoa** : to mix (e.g., a substance that improves the quality of another) ⟨**Pítibetenya yóchi méskoara noé iki.** Fish soup mixed with chili pepper is delicious.⟩ ⟨**Mapó betan méi méskoshon chómoaaronki bási íkai.** They say that a jar made from clay mixed with apacharama bark lasts a long time.⟩

*v.t.* **méskota** 1 : to mix (one element with another) ⟨**Xénira moa ompáx betan meskóke.** At last the oil mixed with the water.⟩ ⟨**Rámara kónibo jónibo moa kámpabo betan méskotai.** Now the Konibo are mixing with the Campa.⟩ 2 : to change : to transform ⟨**Joshín joé betan jósho joéra méskoti metsáshaman iki.** It's very pretty when the red light turns to white and vice versa.⟩

*n.* **mésokan** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *soo,* element from *sóo iti* to swell] : portion; *specif.* : handful : bunch ⟨**Rabé mesó xéki bérora ea jonín ménike.** A man gave me two handfuls of dry corn.⟩
*adj.* **mespán** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hands + *sápa* flat] : with a thin or flat hand
*adj.* **mespón** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *sopóti, sopo-* to bulge] : with bulging hair bulging on the hand or on the front paws (e.g., of dogs)
*v.i.* **méspota** : to have a lot of some specific material on one's hand
*v.t.* **méstaa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut the nails of

*adj. and n.* **mestín** [from Shipibo; adjectival participle from *méstiti, mesti-*] *adj.* : afraid of an imagined danger —Used in all its senses regarding a subject who is inside something (e.g., a tree, a canoe, or an airplane). ⟨**Méstiira nato aínbo ábionin kaí betíke.** This woman closed her eyes while traveling on the plane, because she was afraid.⟩ *n.* : fear of imagined danger : fear of what might happen

*v.i.* **méstia** : to feel afraid (while inside something) of something that might happen ⟨**Bákera wíniwiniai, jiwín néeketian jawen wetsán shákona méstii pakenaketian.** The child is crying because his older brother is shaking the tree he has climbed, and he's afraid of falling.⟩
*adj.* **mestón** [from Shipibo *me-* on the finger + *sto*, unidentified element] : with fingers, or front paws, that are short and bulky or swollen

*v.i.* **métaakata** [from Shipibo *me-* of the hand + *taaka*, unidentified element + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to slip or fall out of one's hand ⟨**Ochítininra títa píti métaakata píai.** The dog is eating the food that fell from mom's hand.⟩
*v.t.* **métanea** : to bandage someone's hand
*v.t.* **métaa** : to make something slip or fall from one's own or another's hand ⟨**Ishto kakínra en títa píti métake.** By passing by quickly, I made the food fall from mom's hand.⟩
*v.i.* **metáxnameeta** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *taxnánt* to stick + *mee-* reflexive suf.] : for something sticky to stick or adhere to someone's hand
*n.* **métekinin** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *téki* joint] : wrist ⟨**Jawen méteki ikáinra yómetso méxtekanke.** They cut off the thief's wrist.⟩

*v.i.* **metexeeta** [from Shipibo *metéxti* to tear to pieces + *-ee* reflexive suf.] : to fall apart : to become tattered ⟨**Nokon chiárextira moa kímisha báritiaya iki; jákopira moa métexeekai.** My pants are already three years old, and that's why they're already falling apart.⟩

*v.t.* **métexa** [from Shipibo *metéxti* to tear to pieces] : to serve (food) ⟨**Betén métexira aínbo ráchikiike.** By accident, the woman spilled the porridge while serving it.⟩ ⟨**Píti métexara kóchi betan ochítininres píke.** Only the pig and the dog ate the food that was served.⟩
*v.i.* **métinina** [from Shipibo *me-* of the hand + *tininti* to fall] : to fall from the hand ⟨**métinina píti tsosáshokobo** crumbs of food fallen from the hand⟩
*v.i.* **métokaata** : to point at oneself ⟨**Nato yoshínbake jónira janbíx métokaake.** This crazy man points at himself.⟩
*v.t.* **metósa** : to drip —to make (something) drip onto someone's hand
*v.t.* **métoa** : to point with the finger ⟨**Yoshínkoshki métoaronki métoti, payóti iki.** They say that if we point at the rainbow, sores can appear on our fingers.⟩

*n.* **métotinin** [from Shipibo *métoti*, *meto-* to point + *-ti* instrument suf.] : finger; *specif.* : index finger ⟨**Timaanankinra nato bákeranoman jawen métoti sékeke.** In a fistfight this young man broke his index finger.⟩

*v.t.* **métota** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *tópiti* to gather] : to pick (fruit) from outer branches ⟨**Naránxa bimi ícha íibatara moa metókana iki.** Yesterday there were many oranges, but they have already been picked.⟩
*v.t.* **metóxa** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *tóxati* to burst] : to burst a boil on someone's hand
See **mítoro**

*adj.* **métsakan** : beautiful : lovely : pretty : nice-looking ⟨**Min kenéra metsáyora iki.** Your design is very beautiful.⟩ ⟨**Min póira metsá iki.** Your sister is extremely pretty.⟩ *syn.* See under **jakónshoko**
*adj.* **metsáshokon** [from Shipibo *metsá* pretty + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : pretty *syn.* See under **jakónshoko**
*v.t.* **métseta** [from Shipibo *me-* of the hand + *tséketi* to take out] : to take (something) away from someone's hand
*v.i.* **metsíta** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *tsínati* to swell] : for one's hand to go down in swelling
*v.i.* **métsisa** : to moan or sigh from pain ⟨**Mapón chéxaa métsisaitianra** **rókotoron pápa ráo xéamake.** The doctor gave my dad medicine to drink because he was moaning from a headache.⟩
*v.t.* **métsita** [from Shipibo *me-* on the finger + *tsitsíti* to suck] : to suck someone's finger
*v.t.* **méwata** [from Shipibo *me-* on the finger + *wáketi* to lift] : to lift the fingers of (a person) when they are clenched inward : to open the hand of

*n.* **mewén** : colpa (mineral salt lick) or animal wallow ⟨**Méwemeara nokon epán sókota jóno réteke wetsánra witáxki natéxke.** My uncle killed six collared peccaries at a salt lick, and one of them bit him on the leg.⟩

*v.t.* **méwea** [from Shipibo *me-* from the hand + *wéati* to take out] 1 : to take everything out of the hand of ⟨**Yómetsoninra nato báke koríki méweke.** A thief took all the money this child had in his hand.⟩ 2 : to lift (a child) by the hand or with the hand
*v.i.* **méwexeeta** : to scratch oneself with one's hand ⟨**Nato bákera méwexeetai, jawen mentsís nenkéira ikáx.** This child scratches himself with his hand because his fingernails are very long.⟩
*v.t.* **méwexa** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *wéxati* to scratch] : to scratch on the hand, or with the hand, of
*v.t.* **méwisha** [from Shipibo *me-* on the hand + *wíshati* to scrape] : to scrape the hand of

*v.t.* **méxaa** 1 : to pull out hair or fur from ⟨**Iso rétexon méxaitianra jóni inábaon yatánke.** While the man was pulling out the fur of the spider monkey he had killed, wild Indians captured him.⟩ 2 : to pluck the feathers from ⟨**Papánra jíriabi kébo méxashon béke.** Dad brought a live pucacunga (a trumpeter bird) after plucking its feathers.⟩ 3 : to pull up by the root ⟨**Moa kári méxashon béaitianra en nókoke.** I found him already bringing the sweet potatoes he had pulled up from the ground.⟩ ⟨**Nokon wétsara en átsa mexa bíti ráanai waínko.** I send my brother to the garden to bring back the pulled-up yuca.⟩
*adj.* **mexbán** [from Shipibo *me-* in the fingers + *xabáati*, *xabaa-* to open] : with the fingers spread apart

*n.* **méxbikan** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *risbí* cord] 1 : cord binding on the handle of something, or on handicraft articles (e.g., bracelets, anklets, backpacks, or bags) ⟨**Nokon chikáro mexbira wamén tésake.** A paiche (a giant Amazon fish) broke the cord binding of my harpoon.⟩ 2 : shoelace : shoestring

*v.i.* **méxeta** 1 : to fall out (hair) ⟨**Kóchi rani méxetara báinapon iki.** The fallen bristles of the pig are in the middle of the path.⟩ 2 : to shed (hair) ⟨**Moa básiora ikaxa nato íno bichi méxetai.** The little hairs of this old jaguar hide are falling out.⟩ 3 : to fall out (feathers) ⟨**Nato átapa ranira méxetai, moa máwata ikax.** The little feathers of this hen are falling out because it is dead.⟩ 4 : to uproot themselves (several or many) ⟨**Paránta bánaara méxeta iki.** The planted plantains uprooted themselves.⟩
*adj.* **mexkán** : left-handed ⟨**Méxka ixonra nato aínbaon jawen báke rerake.** Because she is left-handed, this woman cut her son.⟩

*adv. and postp.* *adv.* : on the left side ⟨**Kampónra kímisha aínbo charóke. Ja méxkao iká riki nokon pói.** Three women are standing on the sports field. The one on the left is my sister.⟩ *postp.* : to the left of —Used after the possessive adjective or the noun functioning as its complement. ⟨**Jawen axé íketianra nato bakén jawen méxkao wíshai.** This child writes with his left hand out of habit.⟩ ⟨**Weán méxkaokea iká kínira wíso inon kíni iki.** To the left of the stream there is a hole that is the den of a yanapuma (a mythical black jaguar).⟩
*n.* **méxnín** [from Shipibo *me-* of the hand + *ráni* fuzz, hair] : fine hair or fuzz on the hand or on the fingers
*v.i.* **méxokoota** [from Shipibo *méxóti*, *méxo-* to peel + *-koo*, reflexive suf.] : for one's hand to get skinned

*v.i.* **méxoa** : to crawl ⟨**Nato báke méxoaira tápomeax pakéke.** This crawling baby fell off the emponado (a split-palm-wood floor platform).⟩ ⟨**Yamín jawen táe xáteaxa nokon kóka méxomexokirani jóke.** My uncle came crawling because he cut his foot with an axe.⟩
*v.t.* **méxota** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *xókati* to peel] : to skin someone's hand
*n.* **méxtekan** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *xáte* cut] : a cut on the hand or finger
*v.t.* **méxtea** 1 : to cut someone's hand or finger 2 : to amputate someone's hand or finger
*v.i.* **mexteta** 1 : to cut oneself on the hand or finger ⟨**Aínbobakera, pónwexéetax, mextéibake.** The girl cut her hand after scraping her arm.⟩ 2 : to amputate one's own hand or finger

*adj.* **méyakan** [from Shipibo *me-* of the hand + *-ya* conj.] : skillful : dexterous : quick ⟨**Nokon chaínra, nónti ishtón jankénhake, meyáyora íshon.** My brother-in-law finished making the canoe in a short time because he is very skillful.⟩ ⟨**Nokon cháibichora meyá iki; wétsabora jáskarama iki.** Only my brother-in-law is skillful; the others are not.⟩
*adj.* **méyaman** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *yankón* bluish] 1 : bruised on the hand 2 : with a greenish-blue bruise on the hand
See under **wáste**
*adj.* **méyeman** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *yenkén* smooth] : with no hair at all on the hand : hairless-handed
*adj.* **méyoshin** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *yóshoti, yósho* to twist] : with a twisted hand
*v.t.* **méyota** [from Shipibo *me-* in the hand + *yokíti* to apply by rubbing] : to apply something thick (e.g., mentholatum) to someone's hand
*modifying pref.* : in a round or small-ball shape ⟨**míchoti** to spit⟩

*pron.* **min** : you : you (object) : to/for you : you (formal) : to/for you (formal) ⟨**Mía riki jakóma jóni; jákopira en mia kastíkanai —akinra tiníntinin jóni áke.** The lieutenant governor said to the man: —You are a bad person, and that is why I am going to punish you.⟩ ⟨**Mia jákoni téetaitianra en senén kopíai —ikira pátoron íke.** The boss said: —If you work well, I will pay you fairly.⟩ ⟨**Min shobo ákaitianra en mia akíntiki, nokon rárebo mia íketianres.** When you build the house, I will help you; but only because you are my relative.⟩ ⟨**Nokon wétsa min kastíkanaitianra, en mia koáratiaiba bóai.** If you punish my brother, I am going to take it to the guard.⟩ ⟨**Máio shiainxonra en mia óina iki; ixónbira en mia onányamaa iki.** I saw you in Pucallpa, but I didn't know you.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.1
See under **áti**
*n.* **michán** [from Spanish] : wick

*v.t.* **míchoa** [from Shipibo *mi-* in round form + *cho*, an element also seen in, e.g., *béchoti* to frown (furrow the brows)] : to spit out (liquid or solid) ⟨**Jonínra oránshin xéaxonbi míchoke, béxnaman kéenkin.** The man spat out the soda again after tasting it; he prefers liquor.⟩

*v.i.* **míimeeta** [from Shipibo *míinti, míin-* to bury + *mee-* reflexive] : to bury oneself ⟨**Moátianronki maxóki inón párana míimeeta iki.** They say that long ago the fox buried itself alive, tricked by the jaguar.⟩ ⟨**Bóchikiax páketironki manón míimeekaina iki.** They say that after falling from a height, it buried itself in the mud.⟩
*v.t.* **míina** : to bury ⟨**Mawá míinabora jatíbi kétokan píkoa iki.** All the buried corpses turned up in the cemetery because of the landslide.⟩
*also* **Méjiko** *n.* **Míjikonin** *also* **Méjikonin** [from Spanish; and this from an Aztec origin] : Mexico

*n.* **mikánikon** [from Spanish] : mechanic ⟨**Nato mikánikora rámakaya áxei ítai; jákopira nokon mótoro masáake.** This mechanic is still learning; that's why he has ruined my motor (outboard motor).⟩
*n.* **mikárawan** : pavo del monte (a wild forest turkey) *syn.* kóxo
*v.t.* **míkaa** : to dig up (earth) so that it is easier to plant
*n.* **Mikírin** *Konibo* **Mikírinin** [from Spanish *Miguel*] —Used as a masculine name.
See **mirión**
*adj.* : your —Used as a possessive modifier before a noun. ⟨**Min átapara máxokan bóke.** The fox took your hen.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.3.3
See under **-na**
*n.* **minkán** [from Quechua *minka* communal work party] : minga (a communal work party) ⟨**Otokoronkonia jónira mínka áti chániti joke.** A man from Utucuro came to invite us to a minga.⟩
*adj.* **Minón** [from Spanish *mino*, an element from *Hemninio*] —Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **minótonin** [from Spanish] : minute ⟨**Westíora órariki sókota chónka minótoya.** One hour has sixty minutes.⟩
*n.* **minóto akaiton** [from Spanish *minuto* + Shipibo *ákai*, participle of *áti* to do] : minute hand (of a clock) ⟨**óra akai, minóto akai** hour hand, minute hand⟩
*also* **ménta** *n.* **mintán** *also* **mentán** : mint

*v.t.* **mintoómaa** [from Shipibo *mintón* small ball + *-ma* to cause + *-ti*, inf. suf.] : to make (something) have, or make (something) with, small lumps ⟨**Beténti onányamaxonra nokon titán mintómake.** Not knowing how to prepare it, my mom made the porridge lumpy.⟩

*n.* **míntoman** [from Shipibo *mi-* in the shape of a small ball + *tónko* round] 1 : a small ball of matter (e.g., saliva, phlegm, or hair) that can accumulate ⟨**Keyón mintonronki yobébaon jato xéamai, jáboribi yobé ítiakin.** They say that shamans make their students swallow little balls of saliva so that they too will become shamans.⟩ 2 : small balls prepared from food ⟨**Atsa mintonra nato bakén nákaamabi píke.** This child swallowed the little balls made of yuca without chewing them.⟩ 3 : a coiled snake

*v.t.* **mintónhaa** 1 : to form a small ball from (e.g., saliva, phlegm, or hair) ⟨**Yobébaonra keyón mintónhaxon jato óyoai, ja ísinaibo.** Shamans form little balls of saliva to suck on the skin of the sick, thereby healing them.⟩ 2 : to prepare (food) with lumps or small balls ⟨**Paránta mintónhananbira titán píai.** While mom is preparing the food, she eats the lumps.⟩

*v.i.* **míntona** : to coil up (a snake) ⟨**Moa róno míntonara íkai natéxmistires.** When a snake is coiled up, it means it is ready to bite anyone.⟩ ⟨**Róno míntona en tíakabira ea nateshamake, óxaa ixon.** I touched a coiled-up snake and it didn't bite me because it was asleep.⟩
*n.* **míriaoran** [from Spanish] : half an hour
*also* **merkádo** *n.* **mírikaton** *also* **merkádon** : market ⟨**Eara mírikatonko kái, mároi.** I am going to the market to shop.⟩

*n.* **mírikotin** : a large species of motelo (tortoise)
*n.* : a species of small bird

*n.* **míroman** [from Spanish] : melon ⟨**Mirón kókoaxba báke chixóke.** From eating melon, the child got diarrhea.⟩

*noun-forming suf.* **-misnin** *also* **-miston** *also* **-misin** *also* **-misen** *also* **-misin** *also* **-mistonin** : one who always or habitually does something specific —Used as *-misen*, *-misin*, or *mistonin* sometimes after an odd number of syllables as the non-basic form, and *-misnin* or *-miston* in other cases of the form non-basic form. —Used added to the root of a transitive verb with the meaning of an agent noun. ⟨**Rétemisa moa yatánkanke.** They've already caught the murderer⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.7

*modifying suf.* : one after another —Used with a transitive verb, which will always result in an intransitive one. ⟨**Rámara wairorobo yatámiskanai.** Now the guards are catching them one after another.⟩
*n.* **misán** [from Spanish] : Mass
*n.* **misán** [from Spanish] : table ⟨**Mísa-meaxa báke óxaax pakéke.** The child fell asleep and fell off the table.⟩

*also* **mísho** *n.* **mishítonin** *also* **mishón** [from Spanish *mishito*; minus *-ito*, from Quechua *misw*; and this from Spanish *miso, mizo, micho*, a word for calling a cat] : cat ⟨**Mishíto bákebora jenén kéyoke.** The flood killed all the kittens.⟩ ⟨**Misho riki ochítinin rawí.** The cat is the dog's enemy.⟩
*n.* **míshkiman** : cane syrup ⟨**Mishkín kókoaronki chikíshti iki.** They say that if you suck on cane syrup, you become lazy.⟩

*v.t.* **míshkia** : to fish with a hook ⟨**Míshkikinra en konín ewa bíke.** I caught a gymnotid eel with a hook.⟩ ⟨**Nimánra sipán mishkixonai jawen wétsashoko.** Nima is fishing for sardines with a hook for his little brother.⟩ ⟨**Jatíbi en píti beára mishkíbires** **iki.** All the fish that I've brought have been caught with a hook.⟩
*n.* **míshkitinin** [from Shipibo *míshkiti, mishki–* to get stuck + *–ti* instrument suf.] : fishhook ⟨**Pápashokon míshkitira jawen babán potánke.** The boy threw away his grandfather's fishhook.⟩

*v.i.* **míshkita** 1 : to get stuck (e.g., a thorn or a bone) in the throat : to choke ⟨**Yarínainoaxa báke míshkitax mawáke.** In Yarina a child died after choking on a bone stuck in his throat.⟩ 2 : to get hooked by a fishhook ⟨**Bákera janbíx míshkita iki.** The child got hooked by a fishhook.⟩
See under **keré**
See under **risbí**
*n.* **misín** [from Shipibo *mi-* in ball form + *si*, unidentified element] : humita : tamale ⟨**Nato jónira mísi piósma iki.** This man has never eaten tamales.⟩ *syn.* mispán
*v.t.* **mísiaa** *Konibo* **mísiaka** : to prepare humitas (tamales) ⟨**Moa pishta íti ochómara aínbaon misiai.** The woman is preparing humitas because the feast is approaching.⟩

*n.* **mísibewekan** *Konibo* **mísibewen** [from Shipibo *mísi* humita (tamale) + *bewé* (imperative of *béti* to bring) bring!] : a species of insect sometimes called a stag beetle of *béti* to bring) bring!] : a species of insect sometimes called a stag beetle
*n.* **misionin** [from Spanish] : mission ⟨**Misiónma noa jawékiati méniara jatíribibo maxkáke.** Some of us have run short of the provisions that the mission distributed to us.⟩
*n.* **misionironin** [from Spanish] : missionary ⟨**Misionirobora jaton rárebo jénebeirani Piróri békana iki.** The missionaries came to Peru, leaving their relatives behind.⟩

*adj.* **miskón** 1 : twisted with knots ⟨**Axo yoshinronki jawen ponyán mískobires iki.** They say the demon of the capirona tree has knotted, twisted branches for arms.⟩ 2 : cramp ⟨**Westíora yobéjonira miskón réteke.** A shaman died of cramps.⟩

*n.* **miskóisiman** [from Shipibo *miskó* cramp + *isín* illness] : any of several illnesses that cause cramps ⟨**Miskóisinronki Iparianko jáke.** They say that in Iparía there is an illness that causes cramps.⟩

*v.i.* **mískoa** : to have cramps ⟨**Ishtoaxa jóni mískoi mawáke.** Because he had been running, the man got cramps and died.⟩ ⟨**Káshibobaon jawéki yátanaronki mískoti iki.** They say that when we touch something belonging to the Cashibo, we get cramps.⟩
*n.* **mísmirin** *Konibo* **mísmirinin** : a species of small bird

*n.* **míspaman** : a tamale prepared with yuca or plantain ⟨**Mispán akinra atsa xákixon peín kawati iki.** Yuca tamales are prepared by grating the yuca and wrapping it in a plantain leaf.⟩ *syn.* mísi
*v.t.* **míspana** : to prepare yuca or plantain tamales ⟨**Titánra mispáwanke, pápa jan kéenaitian.** A while ago, mom prepared yuca tamales because dad likes them.⟩
*n.* **mítaman** : Carnival ⟨**Ráma mitán nete ikénra, manón síkaanankanai.** Since today is Carnival day, people get themselves dirty painting themselves with mud.⟩

[from Shipibo *mitán* Carnival + *–iti* to do] : to play at Carnival ⟨**Eara mitán ikashamai.** I don't like playing at Carnival.⟩ ⟨**Noara jákiribi joríbai mitán iti ochóma.** We're going to go back because Carnival time is coming around again.⟩
*n.* **mítokan** [from Shipibo *mi–* in ball form + *to,* an element from *tóoti, too–* to become pregnant] : a small lump or swelling in the stomach

*also* **métro** *n.* **mítoron** *also* **metrón** [from Spanish] : meter; *also* : an object used to measure a meter ⟨**Píchika mítoroyara nokon nónti en ákai.** I am making my canoe five meters long.⟩ ⟨**Nokon konxán xatera chósko mítoro iki jawen nenké.** My cedar log is four meters long.⟩ ⟨**Mítoro yámaketianra noa konxán pátoronin topónxonyamake.** Since there was no meter stick, the boss didn't measure our cedar lumber.⟩
*v.i.* **mítota** : to have a small lump or swelling in the stomach

*n.* **míxekan** 1 : packaged things (e.g., in a roll or bundle) : package : bundle ⟨**Rímameaxa jawéki mixe nokóke.** Bundles of merchandise arrived from Lima.⟩ ⟨**Pápara jawen pátoronin chópa mixe bexónke.** Dad's boss brought him a package of clothes.⟩ 2 : a ball (e.g., of cotton) made by hand ⟨**Titán waxmen mixe ikainra xoyán náake.** A rat made its nest in the ball of cotton that mom had bundled up.⟩ 3 : a ball of thread ⟨**Titán yomán mixera jawen bakén ménonaanke.** The child burned his mom's ball of thread.⟩ *syn.* káwa

*v.t.* **mixea** [from Shipibo *mi–* in ball form + *xéwati* to roof/thatch] : to package into in the shape of a ball or bundle ⟨**Waxmén mixeketianra xoyán píamai.** Rats don't eat the cotton when it is packaged.⟩
*adv.* : already ⟨**Moara en jói bénxoake.** I have already settled the matter.⟩ *syn.* ráma
*n.* **moábaon** [from Shipibo *moa* already + *–bo,* pl. suf.] : ancestors ⟨**Non moáboronki siná ikátikanai.** They say our ancestors were fierce.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *moa* now + *–cha* something, a little] : a little while before ⟨**Janra moa máxkake. Moácha joxonra, min jíria nókokeanke.** He has already died. If you had come a little earlier, you would have found him alive.⟩
See under **káti**

*adv.* [from Shipibo *moa* already + *-tian* when] 1 : in the past : long ago ⟨**Moátianra noa Otokoronko ikátiai; rámara moa noa Kakónko iki.** Long ago we lived in Utucuro, but now we live in Caco.⟩ 2 : formerly : in ancient times ⟨**Moátianra noa onáma ikátiai.** In ancient times we were ignorant.⟩ ⟨**Moátianronki Ínkabo nato parón jápaonike.** They say that in ancient times the Incas lived in this region.⟩
*n.* **moátian join** [from Shipibo *moátian* formerly + *jói* word] : legend : myth

*adj.* **moáxenin** [from Shipibo *moa* already + *xeni*, unidentified element] : old : ancient ⟨**Moáxeniora bikana ikaxa nato motóro básimashokobo másatai.** This motor keeps breaking down because it's very old.⟩ ⟨**Moáxeni wapórobora ikátiai motórooma.** The old-time boats didn't have motors.⟩ *syn.* ántikoo
*v.i.* **móchaa** : to sing in order to obtain
*n.* **mochón** : turushuque (a type of fish) ⟨**Mócho piáxa nato aínbo jími chixóke.** From eating turushuque, this woman had bloody diarrhea.⟩
*n.* **moén** : nettle : ishanga ⟨**Nato báke yoitimara móeki rakéyamai.** This disobedient child isn't afraid of ishanga (stinging nettle).⟩
[from Shipibo *ishísh* a species of catfish + *móe* ishanga] : a species of ishanga (stinging nettle)
[from Shipibo *jénk, jenén* water + *móe* ishanga] : a species of ishanga (stinging nettle)

*v.i.* **moíshika** : to break with a noise

*adj. and n.* [from Shipibo *mokáati, mokaa*– to ferment] *adj.* **mokán** 1 : very fermented ⟨**Atsaxeati mókara korákanin xéake.** The chief drank the very fermented masato.⟩ 2 : too sour ⟨**Kikínbires móka ikénbira papán naránxa kókoke.** Dad ate the orange even though it was very sour.⟩ 3 : bitter ⟨**Rimón móka akáxa bákeshoko jánshoke.** From eating a bitter lemon, the little child got a canker sore.⟩ ⟨**Nato ráora móka iki.** This medicine is bitter.⟩ 4 : too salty ⟨**Bóe tashínaka móka piáxa ea nómiai.** I ate a very salty boquichico (a river fish) and I'm thirsty.⟩ 5 : spicy —Used, e.g., regarding chili pepper and black pepper. ⟨**Yóchi móka axónra nato bakén asókaro kókoke.** After eating very spicy chili pepper, this child ate sugar to calm the spiciness.⟩ 6 : painful —Used, e.g., for a thorn prick, a stingray sting, or the bite of a venomous snake. ⟨**Shanóra bebon mókayora iki.** The bite of the fer-de-lance is the most painful of all.⟩ 7 : strong —Used regarding the heat of the sun. ⟨**Bári mókayora íketianra noa náshinashikiranke.** Since the sun was very strong, we kept bathing throughout the trip.⟩ *n.* 1 : strength ⟨**Táshi mokanra básiayamaakin chópa páyoai.** The strength of the salt makes clothing disintegrate quickly.⟩ 2 : bile : gall ⟨**Táwi móka keskara en xéake jonín ámaa.** A man made me drink something like bile.⟩ 3 : poison ⟨**Mokánra jawen weshá xépokoke.** He coated his blowgun dart with poison.⟩ *syn.* beyá; táwi

*v.t.* **mókaa** *Konibo* **mókaaka** 1 : to ferment (something) heavily ⟨**Píshtatian xéanoxonra, Charáxmanan jónibaon jatíbitian xéati mókaai.** The people of Charashmaná always ferment the drink heavily for feasts.⟩ 2 : to poison : to intoxicate ⟨**Kirínkobaonronki níwe mókaanonxiki réteanankin.** They say that in a future war the foreigners will surely poison the air, killing everyone.⟩ *syn.* raónti
*n.* **mókabimin** [from Shipibo *móka* sour + *bini* fruit] : a species of tree with fruits like those of the uvilla

*n.* **mókaparin** [from Shipibo *móka* poisonous + *pári* still] 1 : a species of tree 2 : a species of demon identified with the *mókapari* tree ⟨**Mókaparin bákearonki mécha píkotai.** A child fathered by the demon of the *mókapari* tree turns out to be a good hunter and fisherman.⟩
See under shimón

*v.i.* **mókaa** 1 : to turn sour ⟨**Naránxa mókaketian kókoaxa ea páenai.** When I suck on an orange that has turned sour, it makes me dizzy.⟩ 2 : to turn bitter ⟨**Moa chícha mókaketianra jónibo páenax tímaanankanai.** When the chicha turns bitter and fermented, people get drunk and fight.⟩ 3 : to turn too salty ⟨**Nato aínbaonra yoáati onányamabirake; jákopira píti betén táshi mókaake.** Maybe this woman doesn't know how to cook, and that's why her fish chowder is too salty.⟩ 4 : to turn spicy ⟨**Sibóriaya méskoara moa kikínbires yóchi mókake.** The chili pepper mixed with onion turned very spicy.⟩ 5 : to turn strong (the sun) ⟨**Bári mókaketianra nato jonín kinánke, jawen yóra ísinai iken.** When the sun turned strong, this man vomited because he was ill.⟩

*v.t.* **mókoa** : to put in the mouth without chewing, to take out again later ⟨**Nato bakénra konjíti mókoke, jawen titán jishnóma** This child put a candy in his mouth without his mother seeing.⟩ ⟨**Aínbaonra píti mokobi jawen báke pímake.** A woman fed her little child the same food she had in her mouth.⟩
See **mórotipirikanti**
See **mórotipirikasion**
*n.* : a species of mullet, yellow-colored with a red head ⟨**Mómo piáronki mánkoti iki.** They say that if we eat *mómo* fish, we can go bald.⟩

*v.t.* **mónaa** 1 : to make (the ground) sink ⟨**Ishtokinra kabáyonin mái mónake.** By running, the horse made the ground sink.⟩ 2 : to dent (a metal utensil) ⟨**Yámikenti mónaketianra, titán nokon wétsa ríshkike.** Mom whipped my brother for having dented the metal pot.⟩
*n.* **mónikan** [from Spanish] : doll ⟨**Bakénra moníka chopán rákoke.** The girl wrapped the doll in a cloth.⟩ *syn.* sánto

*v.i.* **mónita** 1 : to sink in (the ground) ⟨**Níwanax mái moníketianra jóni jíkike.** With the earthquake, the ground sank in and a person was swallowed and buried.⟩ 2 : to get dented (e.g., a pot) ⟨**Nato yámikenti moniara ea kéenyamai** —iquira títa íke. Mom said: —I don't want this dented pot.⟩

*n.* **monsón** : mestizo : Spanish-speaker ⟨**Máioshiainra moa mónsobo kaíoraa iqui. In Pucallpa there are many mestizos.⟩ *syn.* MONSO, NAWA — both can be translated as "mestizo," but MONSO refers more narrowly to a mestizo or Spanish-speaker, while NAWA can refer more broadly to any outsider or foreigner.

*Konibo* **móntaria** *n.* **montárian** *Konibo* **móntarian** [from Spanish] : montería (a dugout canoe) ⟨Westíora jónironki rébokiax jónike jahuen **móntarian.** They say that long ago a person came from upriver in his montería.⟩

*Konibo* **montánti** *v.t.* **móntata** *Konibo* **móntana** 1 : to put in water to launch it : to launch (a boat) ⟨Nóntiakin **senénbaxon papán montánketianra báikan boónaanke.** When dad finished making the canoe and put it in the water to launch it, the current carried it away.⟩ 2 : to flood over (water) ⟨Ani **jénetiaxonra nokon tápo ea montánaanke.** A great flood covered my emponado (raised platform floor).⟩ 3 : to put (e.g., peeled yuca to ferment, or tamshi to soften) into water ⟨Jahuen **mekén montánketianra nato báke koshóshkanin ménatexke.** When this boy put his hand in the water, a river dolphin bit him.⟩

*v.t.* **móshaa** : to break, crack, or smash by hitting or striking ⟨**Koáratianinra jóni ríshkixon jawen xáo móshake.** The guard broke a man's bones by hitting him with a stick.⟩ ⟨**Jawen chómobo moshábo iketianra titán jawen bákebo sináake.** Mom scolded her children because their clay jars were cracked.⟩ ⟨**Nato átapa bachi moshábora namán kopíabo márokanai.** They are selling these cracked eggs at a low price.⟩
*adj.* **moshín** : brittle from being dry or toasted ⟨**Titán básiora chómo ménoara, moa móshiora íke.** The clay pot that mom left on the fire for a long time became very brittle.⟩

*adj.* **móshikan** 1 : mashed (e.g., so that it becomes crumbled or soft) ⟨**Nokon títashokonra moshí jawékires píai, xétaoma ixon.** My grandmother eats only mashed things, since she has no teeth.⟩ 2 : broken into pieces ⟨**Pátoroninra páan moshibo jato méniresai, moa kéenyamai.** The boss is giving away crumbled bread to the children, since he no longer wants it.⟩
*v.t.* **móshía** 1 : to dry until brittle 2 : to toast
*v.i.* **móshia** : to dry out until brittle or crumbly ⟨**Máioshiainoa páan békanara moa móshike, barín aká.** The bread they brought from Pucallpa dried out and crumbled because the sun hit it.⟩

*v.i.* **móshita** 1 : to sustain a blow ⟨**Jíwibochikiash páketira makánki chóshiti báke sháo moshíke.** Falling from up in a tree, the child hit a rock and broke a bone.⟩ 2 : to shatter ⟨**Nato kémpo móshita ikénra ea póntekanke en akáma ikénbi.** They blamed me when they found the shattered mocahuas (clay bowls), even though I hadn't done it.⟩
*n.* [from Quechua *muti*] : mote (boiled corn) ⟨**Nato jónira móti pikáshamai, tobánres ákasi.** This man doesn't like to eat mote; he prefers to eat toasted corn.⟩
