*n.* **motón** : ladybug ⟨**Nokon átapara móto xéaketian jóiman réteke.** When my hen swallowed a ladybug, it died of suffocation.⟩
[from Shipibo *íso* spider monkey + *móto* ladybug] : a kind of beetle
*n.* **motón** : toasted and ground corn ⟨**Titán móto aka píkasira báke wíniai.** The child is crying because he wants to eat the toasted, ground corn that mother prepared.⟩

*n.* **motóronin** [from Spanish] 1 : motor : motorized boat ⟨**Westíora motórora réboki káke, téetaibo jawékiati bóxoni.** A certain motorboat went upriver carrying supplies for the workers.⟩ 2 : motor (e.g., outboard or inboard) internal combustion engine ⟨**Rámara moa Máioshiain motórobo kopíora iki.** Nowadays in Pucallpa motors are very expensive.⟩
[from Shipibo *áni* big + *motóro* motor] : launch (boat) *syn.* wapóro

*v.t.* **mótsaa** 1 : to crush without water (e.g., ripe plantains, bread, crackers, or bird eggs) ⟨**Parántajoshinra en mótsake, ján cháchiti yámaketian.** I crushed the ripe plantains because I had nothing to mash them with.⟩ 2 : to crush in water ⟨**Atsa joa titán mótsaketianra pápa já xéakashamai.** Papa doesn't want to drink the boiled manioc that mama crushed in water.⟩ ⟨**Yobébora motsá xéatinin ráketai, jakómanaketian.** Sorcerers are afraid to drink things crushed in water and prepared by someone else, because they fear it will harm them.⟩
*v.t.* **mótsia** : to break (e.g., a pot) forcefully
*v.i.* **mótsita** : to become dented *syn.* páchoti
*n.* **moxán** 1 : thorn ⟨**Pápara tasóike, jíwi moxa jámatax.** Dad's foot swelled up when he stepped on a tree thorn.⟩ 2 : a thorny plant
[from Shipibo *kaxpán*, a plant name + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of herb with thorns on the stem and round leaves
[from Shipibo *chári, charín* shamiro (an animal) + *púti* food + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of thorny vine that the shamiro eats
[from Shipibo *cháxo, chaxón* deer + *arámpiri* barbed wire + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of thorny, vine-like herb with no use
[from Shipibo *wáki*, a plant name + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of thorny plant
[from Shipibo *ípo* carachama (an armored catfish) + *móxa* thorny plant] : a useless species of plant with leaves similar to those of the huingo (calabash tree), and a cylindrical stalk
[from Shipibo *ixné*, a plant name + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of thorny, useless vine with tiny leaves
[from Shipibo *páwetati*, unidentified element + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of thorny plant, almost vine-like in form
[from Shipibo *táko, takón* unchala (a palm) + *chiimapo* ash + *móxa* thorny plant] : a species of tree with sharp thorns on the trunk and branches similar to those of the huicungo (a spiny palm)
1 : a species of thorny plant 2 : a magic thorn that a shaman sends to bewitch someone, making them sick
See under **ísa**
See under **keré**
*v.t.* **móxaka** : to make noise while chewing (e.g., onion or raw chili pepper) ⟨**Enra yóchi móxakai.** I make noise biting into a raw chili pepper.⟩

*v.i.* **móxika** : to crunch (e.g., wood when stepped on, or a raw vegetable when bitten) ⟨**Papán átsa nátexara móxike.** When dad bit into a raw yuca, it crunched.⟩ ⟨**Ronón ewan pekáronki móxikai non jámata.** They say the boa's back crunches if we step on it.⟩
*n.* **móxokan** : topa (a balsa-like tree) ⟨**Máioshiainra ráma moxó moa kírikaakanai.** Now in Pucallpa they make paper from topa wood.⟩
See under **batón**
See under **bawín**
See under **chiwínti**
See under **níshi**

*verbal derivational suf.* –Used added to the root of a noun or adjective, giving it the transitive sense of "to make" or "to do". ⟨**ráo, ráonti** medicine, to treat (make) with medicine⟩ –Used added to the root of an intransitive verb to make it transitive, giving it the sense of "to make" or "to cause". ⟨**óxati, oxánti** to sleep, to make sleep⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2; 8.2.3 *syn.* –ati
*nominal suf.* –Used as the ending in the non-basic form of a class of nouns, pronouns, and adjectives. ⟨**mápo** head⟩ ⟨**Mapónra ea chéxai.** My head hurts.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1; 7.4.4.2.e
*n.* Used as the name of the letter *n* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *nápo* interior] 1 : inside of ⟨**nárakati** to be lying inside of (e.g., a boat)⟩ ⟨**natséti** to take out from inside⟩ 2 : in the water : of the water ⟨**natsáti** to throw (a spear or arrow) into the water to spear fish⟩ 3 : through the middle ⟨**natánke** to follow (a path) through the middle⟩ 4 : backward ⟨**naísti** to look backward⟩ 5 : downward ⟨**natsískooti** to spill (several things) below a container⟩

*modifying suf.* 1 : care that (a specific event) not happen –Used added to the main verb and followed by *-que* to express fear or a warning that an indicated action may happen due to carelessness or not having paid attention. ⟨**Miara ronón natéxnake.** Watch out, the snake will bite you.⟩ 2 : for fear that : so that ... not *–Used added to the subordinate verb ending in -quetian to indicate a feared event that one wants to avoid.* ⟨**Jawen báke ábionin kánaketian aínbaon yóiabira; káke, yóitima ikáx.** The mother fearfully advised her son not to go in the small airplane, but he stubbornly went anyway.⟩ ⟨**Aweitianin káyamawe —akinra nokon báke en áke káxibobaon rétenaketian.** I told my son not to go to the Aguaytía river, fearing that the Cashibo would kill him.⟩ ⟨**Nokon titánra jawen pói pakénaketian yóiabi, ninkáxonyamax páketi tobíke.** Although my mother told her brother to be careful not to fall, he paid no attention; he fell and got hurt.⟩

*possessive suf.* *–Used added to a noun with the sense of "of" to indicate the owner or possessor. –Used with the suffix -ton (or -tonin) at the end of its non-basic form -naton (or -natonin).* ⟨**Nokon wétsana riki.** It's my brother's.⟩ ⟨**Ono riki non átapa. Nokon títanatoninra píai.** There are our hens. The one that's eating is my mother's.⟩ ⟨**Néno riki ícha ochíti: Josíkanatonra ea natéxke.** There are many dogs around here; José's bit me.⟩ *–Used added to possessive adjectives in pronominal form. –Used in the written form -a to avoid a repeated n.* ⟨**nokon, nókona** my, mine⟩ ⟨**min, mína** your (familiar or formal), yours⟩ ⟨**jawen, jáwena** his/her, his/hers⟩ ⟨**non, nóna** our, ours⟩ ⟨**maton, mátona** your (plural), yours (plural)⟩ ⟨**jaton, játona** their, theirs⟩ ⟨**—¿Mínarin nato rirós? —Jeje, nókona riki. Ichabires iráke.** —Is this watch yours? —Yes, it's mine. Thank you very much.⟩ ⟨**Pirótara ákanai.** Nónabaonra kánánai. They are playing soccer. Ours are winning.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.3; 7.4.2

*n.* **náakan** : nest (e.g., of birds or wasps) ⟨**Náa ikáinoara bákén róno réteke.** The child killed a snake in its nest.⟩ ⟨**Binán naa jonín xobónkoxon ménoaronki ja xóbo ibo jábatai.** They say that if a wasp's nest burns in a house, the owner moves away.⟩
*n.* **náaapon** [from Shipibo *náa* nest + *ápo* mister] : a small species of mouse
*v.i.* **náabaa** : to rise (of a liquid)

*also* **-n** *modifying suf.* **-anaan; –onaan; –enaaan** *also* **-an; –on; –en** –Used postposed to the verb with the force of "to the displeasure of" to indicate deprivation and harm caused by the action of the verb. ⟨**Isakanra ea arós píanaanke.** The little birds have eaten my rice (to my detriment).⟩ ⟨**Nokon ochítira ea retenaanke.** He has killed my dog (to my detriment).⟩ ⟨**Janra ea ochíti boónke.** He has taken my dog away.⟩ ⟨**Ea jakomaanoxonra ea beénaanke.** He brought it and it harmed me.⟩ ⟨**Ea ramianoxonra ea beénke.** He brought it in order to harm me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*n.* **nabákanin** [from Spanish *navaja*] : penknife ⟨**Westíora aínbo yoxínbakenra jawen bákebi nabákanin cháchixon réteke.** A certain crazy woman killed her own child with a penknife.⟩

*v.t.* **nabeta** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *bétseti* to finish] : to cover the floor of (e.g., a boat) with something flat ⟨**Enra nóntin tabara nabéke.** I covered the floor of the boat with boards.⟩

*n.* **nábikan** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *-bi* itself] : inner wall : inside of the wall ⟨**Nato xóbora bebíori jakómashoko jisá iki; ikáxbi, jawen nabíorira jakónshamanki.** This house looks ugly on the outside, but on the inside it's very pretty.⟩

*n.* **nabíronin** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *biro,* unidentified element] : a temporary type of basket made from a single palm leaf ⟨**Nato Yarínainoa jonínra nabíro xéwati onányamake.** This man from Yarinacocha doesn't know how to weave *nabíro*-type baskets.⟩
*v.t.* **nabíroaa** : to weave a temporary basket
*n.* **náboman tsákatinin** [from Shipibo *nabón náboman* shinguto (a biting gnat) + *tsákati, tsaka-* to hit, to hit the mark + *-ti* instrumental "with which"] : tornillo caspi (a type of tree)
*n.* **náboman** : shinguto (a biting gnat) ⟨**Nato parónra íchayora nabón iki; jáskara kopira, ícharibi isínkanai.** Along the Ucayali there are many shingutos, and that's why many people get sick.⟩

*also* **náchitita** *n.* **nachín** *also* **náchititan** 1 : a man's paternal aunt : his father's sister –Used with the vocative form *titá* following the personal name to address the person. ⟨**Jowé, Meatitá.** Good morning, aunt Méa.⟩ ⟨**Nokon náchi Rimán kayántanara moa kímisha báritia iki, ráma kamanbi joáma.** It has already been three years since my aunt went to Lima, and to this day she hasn't turned up.⟩ 2 : mother-in-law (paternal side) : a man's wife's mother –Used in this sense among Shetebo speakers. ⟨**Nato jonínra jawen náchi yóyoakai, non áshekan jaskáatima ikénbi.** This man converses with his mother-in-law, although this is not permitted in our custom.⟩ *syn.* See under **wáata**
*v.t.* **náchita** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *chíkoti* to spill] : to pour into ⟨**Botírian nachíwe.** Pour it into the bottle.⟩

*n.* **náikan** 1 : sky : the upper region of the air ⟨**Naíronki níi iki; ochóira ikax yankón.** They say the sky is a forest, and since it's so far away, it's blue.⟩ ⟨**náio** to the sky⟩ 2 : heaven : the place of angels and blessed souls
*v.i.* **naíkia** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *jikiti* to enter] 1 : to enter 2 : to turn into, to become
See **koín**
*n.* **náiman** : pelejo rojo (a reddish sloth)
*v.t.* **náisa** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *jisti* to see] : to look back at (what is observed)
*n.* **naítsakaten** *Konibo* **naítsakan** [from Shipibo *naí* sky + *tsákati, tsaka-* to sting/peck] : saltón (a large grasshopper) *syn.* wakán ewa
See under **wapóro**
*n.* **nakán** : jején (a biting gnat) ⟨**Náto báke tárora náka íchaya iki; ikáxbi náshikashamai.** This dirty boy is covered in gnats, but he doesn't want to bathe.⟩
[from Shipibo *joshín* red + *náka* gnat] : fruit fly

*v.i.* **nákakaata** [from Shipibo *nákati, naka-* to cut + *-kaa,* reflexive suf.] : to cut oneself with a sawing motion ⟨**Nato bákera janbix nákakaake machítonin.** This boy cut himself with a machete.⟩

*v.t.* **nákaa** 1 : to saw : to cut with a sawing motion ⟨**Kóchi nami nákati shinánkinra, aínbaon jawen bákeres méxteke.** A woman cut off her son's hand while trying to cut pork meat.⟩ 2 : to chew ⟨**Nato jonínra nákaxomabi píai; jákopira pokón chéxai.** This man eats without chewing, and that's why he has a stomachache.⟩

*n.* **nákaxen** 1 : termite ⟨**Jatíribi jónibaonra nakáx píai, já píti yámaketian.** Some people eat termites for lack of food.⟩ ⟨**Nakáx iki ráoati.** Termites are used as medicine.⟩ 2 : termite mound : termite nest ⟨**Nakáxonki, jenén ewaitian jabáti kaí, tóoya aínbo iní iki.** They say the termite mound originated when a pregnant woman fled the flood.⟩ ⟨**Noa yóyoikaitianra nakáxen noa ákai máwakin, jóni keskaribi saí ikin.** If we speak, the termite mound answers us like an echo, and cries like those of a person are heard.⟩
See under **bóna**
*n.* **nákinin** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *kíni* hole] : a hole on the inside
*adj.* **nákoten** *Konibo* **nákokan** : sticky : muddy –Used regarding mud or muck. ⟨**Máno nakokanra páena jóni rakáke.** The drunk man is lying in the muddy mud.⟩ *syn.* **bíin**

*v.t.* **nakómaa** [from Shipibo *nákoti, nako-* to have one's feet stuck + *-ma* causative] : to put (someone else's feet) in something sticky ⟨**Nokon táera, min máno meran nakómake.** You put my feet in the mud.⟩
*v.t.* **nákoa** : to put (e.g., one's feet) into something sticky ⟨**Páena jonínra jawen taén máno nákoke.** The drunk man put his feet in the mud.⟩
*v.i.* **nákota** : to have one's feet stuck and sunk in mud ⟨**Nokon bákera manón nákotax sión iitai.** My son screams because his feet are stuck in the mud.⟩
*n.* **námakan** : dream ⟨**Namá meranronki yóshiman meráya ráo méniai.** They say that the demon gives medicine to the healer in his dream.⟩

*adv., postp. and conj.* *adv.* : below, down ⟨**Bákebora namán tsínikanai; jato jenémawe irai tita.** The mother says: "The children are playing down below; tell them to stop playing."⟩ *postp.* 1 : underneath, below ⟨**Yakáti namanxonra ea ochítinin natéxke.** A dog that was underneath the seat bit me.⟩ 2 : at the foot of ⟨**Kapéra ketó naman típike.** There are some lizards lying at the foot of the ravine.⟩ *conj.* : plus : added with (a specific number) ⟨4 **naman** 4 **páketai** 8. 4 plus 4 equals 8.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *namán* below + *-bires* no more] 1 : last : lower than the rest in a group ⟨**Piróta ákai bebónbires íkasira nokon chái namánbires íke.** My brother-in-law ended up last because he wanted to be first at soccer.⟩ 2 : at a very low price ⟨**Nokon titánra jawen átapa, ríkaton namánbires máromake.** My mother sold her hen to a trader at a very low price.⟩ 3 : least : less than : the least –Used in negative degrees of comparison of the adjective. ⟨**Nokon wétsara namánbires shinánya nénoa jóni iki.** My brother is the least intelligent man around here.⟩ *syn.* íchama
*v.t.* **námata** : to dream
[from Shipibo *jakóma* bad + *namáti* to dream] : to have a nightmare ⟨**Jakómara en namáwanke yamé.** I had a nightmare last night.⟩

*n.* **namín** : meat ⟨**Eara námi píi moa jatsánke.** I've already gotten tired of eating meat.⟩ *syn.* NAMI, PITI — both can be translated as "meat", with the difference that NAMI refers more to the meat of mammals and PITI to fish meat.
See under *jéxko*

*n.* **nanén** : huito (a fruit used for body-paint dye) ⟨**Moatianronki náne bíi kaxón jonín áni íno méranike, jáki jóaitian.** Very many years ago a man went to get huito in the forest and came across an enormous jaguar coming toward him.⟩

*v.t.* **nánea** 1 : to load onto a boat, to embark (someone/something) ⟨**Páenax jokáshamainbira jonín jawen wétsa nontín nánexon béke.** A man who was drunk didn't want to come, but his brother loaded him into a canoe and brought him.⟩ ⟨**Nokon machíto nánea ikénbira, papán bénabenai.** Even though my machete is already loaded (on the boat), my father keeps looking for it.⟩ 2 : to put in ⟨**Koríki yómetsoxonra jonín jawen bórosa meran náneke.** The man put the money in his bag after he stole it.⟩ 3 : to rock, to cradle ⟨**Titánra jawen báke jaín nánetinin náneke.** The mother rocked her baby in a cradle.⟩ *syn.* NANETI, NAPOTI — both can be translated as "to load," but NANETI implies that only one thing is loaded, while NAPOTI implies several. *syn.* NANETI, NAPOTI, NIATI — all can be translated as "to put in," but NANETI implies putting something in (e.g., a bag) to carry, NAPOTI implies a larger container (e.g., a box) for storing something, and NIATI implies putting something into a liquid.
*n.* **nánetinin** [from Shipibo *náneti, nane-* to rock/cradle + *-ti* with which] : cradle
[from Shipibo *báke, bakén* child + *náneti* cradle] 1 : cradle 2 : womb ⟨**Nato aínbora jawen bakénaneti sóoika iki.** This woman's womb has become swollen.⟩
*v.i.* **nánea** : to board (a boat), to embark ⟨**Jónira wapóronin Ikitoain kaí nanéke.** The man boarded a boat headed for Iquitos.⟩
*n.* **nanón** : huapo (a species of monkey) ⟨**Nanón báke kópiaronki jími chíxotai.** They say that when a child is cutipado (spiritually contaminated) by a huapo monkey, he gets dysentery.⟩
*v.t.* **nantáa** *Konibo* **nantáaka** : to twist : to make crooked ⟨**Xóboakinra en nantáake, onámatani ixon.** When building the house, I made it crooked because I'm not an expert.⟩
*v.t.* **nántana** : to twist, to bend (a tree or wood) ⟨**Níweaba koshin xóbo nantánketianra moa rásakanke.** They tore down the house because a strong gust of wind bent it.⟩

*v.i.* **nántata** : to bend : to give way : to lean over ⟨**Moa bími íchayora ikaxa nato kaímito jiwi moa nantáke.** This caimito (star apple) tree has bent over because it has too much fruit.⟩ ⟨**Nato isónxoma jíwira nantá iki; jáskatira tsóabi ján néeyamai pakénaketian.** This sapote tree is crooked, and that's why no one climbs it, for fear of falling.⟩
*v.i.* **nápania** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *pániti* to hang] : to hang inside the roof
*n.* **napón** : interior ⟨**Aná napora nákaxen píai.** Termites eat the inner part of the catahua tree.⟩ *syn.* chícho

*v.i.* **nápokoota** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *pokóti* to board/embark] 1 : to board, to embark (several people or a mass) ⟨**Nato nónti máxkoshoko ikénbira jónibo íchayora nápokooke.** Although the canoe was very small, a great many people boarded it.⟩ 2 : to get into or enter (several things or a mass) ⟨**En tasá jenénko áketianra, ícha sipán nápokooke.** When I put the basket in the water, many sardines got into it.⟩
*n.* **nápomeamekeman** [from Shipibo *napon,* in the middle of + *mekén* hand] : middle finger ⟨**Nato aínbaon bákera jawen nápomeameken yámake.** This woman's son doesn't have a middle finger.⟩

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *nápo, napón* interior] *adv.* 1 : in the middle : to the middle; *specif.* : in the middle of the river ⟨**Paro napón káyamawe.** Don't go to the middle of the river.⟩ *postp.* : in the middle of : to the middle of ⟨**Aniwaporora páro napon réokooke sámaman ímaa.** A steamship sank in the middle of the river because of a whirlpool.⟩ ⟨**Kakónkora jéma napon ábion páketai.** In Caco small planes land in the middle of the street.⟩

*n. and adv.* **napónbekoman** [from Shipibo *napon* in the middle + *bekon* between two] *n.* : half : middle ⟨**westíora risína jáinoax wétsa napónbekon** ten and a half⟩ *adv.* : in the middle ⟨**Bantírara jóxo iki napónbekon.** The flag is white in the middle.⟩ *syn.* benkéx; mírio

*v.i.* **nápona** : to go to the middle ⟨**Moa napónketianra nónti non bíti átipanyamake, jatíbi nónoti onámabo ixon.** When the canoe drifted to the middle of the river, we couldn't recover it because none of us knew how to swim.⟩

*v.t.* **nápota** 1 : to load (several things) onto a boat ⟨**Wapóroninra ícha jawékibo napókanke.** They loaded many things onto the boat.⟩ 2 : to put (several things or a mass) : to place inside ⟨**Jawen bakén parántajoshinbo chómo meran napóketianra, titán bénabenai.** The mother keeps looking for the ripe plantains because her son put them in a large jar.⟩ ⟨**Jíwi nichínoxon papán mái chínia ikénbi titán mái napóketianra papán sináake.** Papa scolded mama because she put dirt in the hole he had dug to set some posts.⟩ *syn.* See under **náneti**
*v.t.* **nárakana** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *rakáti* to lie down + *-n,* verbal derivational suf.] : to lay (something) down inside
*v.i.* **nárakaa** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *rakáti* to be lying down] : to be lying down inside
*v.i.* **naránbekeeta** : to turn upside down (itself)
*v.t.* **naránbea** : to turn (something) upside down
*n.* **naránxanin** [from Spanish] : orange ⟨**Naránxa xoo kókoaxa nato báke jánshoke.** This child has patco (a stomach ailment) because he ate a green orange.⟩
See **naxáati**

*v.t.* **náshimaa** 1 : to bathe (someone) ⟨**Jawen báke, aínbaon náshimaketianra, rókotoron notsínke, ísinai ikénbi ímaketian.** The woman bathed her little son while he was still sick, and the doctor scolded her for it.⟩ 2 : to baptize

*v.i.* **náshia** 1 : to bathe (oneself) ⟨**Rabé néte náshiama ikax, tsókasira ea moa náshike.** Since it had been two days since I hadn't bathed, I felt annoyed, so I bathed.⟩ ⟨**Moa náshia ikénbira, nato báke jákiribi náshimakanai.** Even though this boy already bathed, they're bathing him again.⟩ 2 : to be baptized ⟨**Noara parón náshia iki.** We were baptized in the river.⟩
*v.t.* **náshia** : to break (e.g., a rope)

*v.i.* **náshita** : to break, to snap (e.g., a rope, a cord, a vein, a hair, a belt, or an elastic band) ⟨**Ján níninakinra bákebaon nokon risbí nashíke.** Since the children were tugging at my rope in a struggle, it broke.⟩ ⟨**Nato risbí nashíra bákebaon bóke ján tsíniti.** The children took this broken rope away to play with it.⟩

*n.* **nasín** : island (e.g., in a river) ⟨**Nasínkora papán róno máwata mérawanke.** Papa found a dead snake on the river island.⟩ ⟨**Parónra moa nási íchayora iki, jénetiaibatax.** Many islands have formed in the river after the water rose.⟩
*adj.* **násikan** [from Shipibo; shortened past participle of *nasí iti* to become empty] : hollow inside
*v.i.* **nasí ika** : to become empty (e.g., a bag with a hole) ⟨**Píshara pékeya ikáx nasí ike jawékia.** The bag that was carrying things emptied out because it had a hole.⟩

*n.* [*nási* island + *máxka* upper part] : the upstream tip of an island ⟨**Násimaxkainra xóno tapan rásike; jatíbi jónira jenén jato kéyokeanke.** The lupuna (kapok-wood) raft broke apart at the upstream tip of the island, and everyone nearly drowned.⟩
*v.t.* **násoa** : to clean the inside of ⟨**Enra kentí násoai.** I'm cleaning the pot on the inside.⟩
*n.* **náspaman** : puddle –Rarely used nowadays.
*v.i.* **nátakaata** [from Shipibo *nátati, nata-* to empty + *-kaa,* reflexive suf.] : to become empty

*v.t.* **nátana** 1 : to follow (a line) ⟨**Bái natánxon awá bénai kaxonra**, jonín wísoino méraxon rétea iqui. While following a trail looking for a tapir, a man came across a black jaguar and killed it.⟩ 2 : to trace (a drawing) ⟨**Maístoronra báke jóniati onán shínanai, natánxon áketianres.** The teacher thinks his student knows how to draw, but he's only tracing.⟩

*n.* **nátapotinin** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *tápo* emponado (split-palm flooring) + *-ti* with which] : crossbeam, joist ⟨**Xóbo natapotinimeaxa báke pakéke; ikáxbi mawáyamake.** A child fell from a crossbeam of the house, but did not die.⟩
*v.t.* **nátaa** 1 : to drop, throw, or spill (several things or a mass) on the ground ⟨**Enra moa píti nátake.** I spilled all the food on the ground.⟩ 2 : to empty

*v.i.* **natáxnakaata** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *taxnáti* to dock/moor + *-kaa,* reflexive suf.] : to stick to the inside ⟨**Arós yóakara natáxnameeke.** While cooking the rice, it stuck to the inside of the pot.⟩

*n. and adj.* **natéxen** [from Shipibo *natéxti, natéx-* to bite] *n.* : bite ⟨**Bakén natéxkira ea bonán tékake.** An isula (bullet ant) stung me where the child had bitten me.⟩ *adj.* : bitten ⟨**Nato paránta natéxa moa páyotai.** This bitten plantain is already rotting.⟩

*v.i.* **natéxeeta** [from Shipibo *natéxti, natéx-* to bite + *-ee,* reflexive suf.] : to bite oneself ⟨**Westíora aínbo ísinaironki jána nátexbaini mawáke.** They say a sick woman died biting her own tongue.⟩
*adj.* **natéxmiston** [from Shipibo *natéxti, natéx-* + *-mis* one who always does] : one that always bites; *also* : venomous ⟨**Ja róno natéxmis riki.** That snake is venomous.⟩
*v.t.* **natéxa** : to bite ⟨**Westíora jonínra, paénxon jawen pápa na**téxon réteke. A drunk man killed his father by biting him.⟩

*also* **naténti** *v.i.* **nátina** *also* **nátena** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *tínati* to fill] : for an environment to fill up with (e.g., smoke) ⟨**Xóbora kóiman natínke, wái ménokanketian.** The house filled up with smoke when they burned the garden plot.⟩ ⟨**Náira kóiman naténke.** The sky filled up with clouds.⟩

*pish.* **nénto** *adj. and pron.* **natón** *pish.* **nentón** *adj.* : this; *also* : that ⟨**Náto átapa benenra átapa awin xéki píanaanai.** This rooster is eating the hen's corn.⟩ ⟨**Nénto jónira non oínyosma iki.** We have never seen this man.⟩ ⟨**Náto irimanóra óchaoma iki.** That brother in Christ is pure of heart.⟩ *pron.* : this one; *also* : that one ⟨**Náto yóikinra en mia áatai; jábira min ninkáyamake —akinra ea maístoron áke.** The teacher told me: "I was referring to this one, but you didn't understand me."⟩ –Used with any of the senses "he", "she", or "the following" within a narration or a conversation. ⟨**Náto betanra ea ochó kái —akinra ea aínbaon yóibake.** "I will go far away with him," the woman told me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.4 *syn.* See under *ja*

*v.t.* **nátsata** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *tsákati* to strike] : to spear in the water with an arrow or lance ⟨**Pián natsákinra jawen táeres jonín cháchike.** The man accidentally speared his own foot with an arrow.⟩

*v.t.* **nátseta** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *tsékati* to take out] : to take out from inside of ⟨**Jonínronki pián táe cháchike, ikáxbironki ishtón tsékake jenemeranoa.** They say a man speared his foot with an arrow, and then quickly pulled it out of the water.⟩
*v.i.* **natsískoota** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *tsískoti* to turn over + *-oo,* reflexive suf.] : to spill (the contents of a container)

*v.t.* **natsískoa** 1 : to spill (the contents of a container) 2 : to drink all the contents of (a beverage) ⟨**¿Minki ompáx natsískoa téxeayamakin?** Did you drink all the water without leaving any?⟩

*n.* **nawán** 1 : wild Indian ⟨**Náwabaon kónxaman téetaibo yamé kéyoara; jatíribishokores jabákana iki.** Some wild Indians killed the loggers at night; only a few escaped.⟩ 2 : mestizo ⟨**Kakónkora rama náwaboribi jakáskanai noóxaron.** Now some mestizos want to live in Caco, among us.⟩ 3 : white person ⟨**Náwaki ráketironki non rekénbo jabápaonike.** They say that long ago our ancestors used to flee out of fear of white people.⟩ 4 : foreigner ⟨**Westíora jónira ikai néskati: Náwabaonra jato xéni tsékai.** A man says the following: "Foreigners (who are pishtacos) extract people's fat."⟩ *syn.* See under **mónso**

*v.t.* **náwaa** *Konibo* **náwaaka** [from Shipibo *náwa* wild Indian + *-ati* to make/do] : to shoot an arrow at (a specific target) ⟨**Inkánronki jawen rayós pián náwaaka, manxánteonike.** They say that when the Inca shot his arrow at his son-in-law, the latter turned into a manshaco.⟩
*n.* **nawánbain** [from Old Shipibo *náwa, nawán* the dead + *bái* path] : rainbow *syn.* See under **chirápa**

*n.* **nawánjanen** [from Shipibo *náwa, nawán-* foreigner + *jáne* name] : a Shipibo person's name in Spanish ⟨**Nokon nawánjane riki Hiliador Dávila Rengifo.** My name in Spanish is Hiliador Dávila Rengifo.⟩
*n.* **nawánkokotinin** [from Shipibo *náwa, nawán* strangers/foreigners + *kókoti* fruit to eat] : a species of tree with fruit resembling an olive; *also* : its edible fruit
*n.* **nawarinkán** : a type of energetic dance in which men and women jump
*n.* **náwashian** : shihuango
*n.* **náwashiaman** : shihuango
See under **paránta**
See under **teté**
*n.* **nawén** : purma (fallow, secondary-growth land)
*also* **nawéki** *n. and adj.* **náwekan** *also* **nawékinin** *n.* : bend of the river *adj.* : curved : bent, stooped ⟨**Ja jóni yósira nawé bira iki.** An old man may be stooped.⟩
*n.* **náxakan** : a species of tree; *also* : the edible fruit of the *naxá* tree

*also* **nasáati** *v.t.* **náxaa** *also* **násaa** *Konibo* **nasáaka** : to empty the inside of ⟨**Nato páan játiobi ikáxbira chichó náxaa iki.** This bread, which appears whole, is hollow inside.⟩

*n.* **naxánkenin** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *xankén* ditch] : a deep hole in the ground ⟨**Westíora bákera naxánkenin káx mawákeanke; itíbira jawen títán méraxon bíke.** A child nearly died after falling into a hole; when he was about to die, his mother found him and saved him.⟩

*v.i.* **náxna** : to become empty/hollow inside : to be dried out (without juice) ⟨**Titán naranxa beábora moa náxake.** The oranges that mother mother brought are dried out (without juice).⟩ ⟨**Nato santíra rákatara moa náxaa iki.** This watermelon lying on the ground is hollow inside.⟩

*adj. and n.* **náxbakan** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *xabáti* to yawn] *adj.* 1 : widened 2 : wide between the two sides –Used, e.g., regarding a canoe, a road, a river, or a hole. ⟨**Non párora náxbá iki.** The Ucayali River is wide.⟩ *n.* : width ⟨**jawen náxbá** its width⟩ *syn.* NAXBA, PEXTIN — both are translated as "wide", but NAXBA focuses more on the space between two sides (e.g., of a river), while PEXTIN implies the large size of a wide body (e.g., of a person, a piece of wood, or a piece of cloth).
*v.t.* **náxbáa** *Konibo* **náxbáaka** : to widen ⟨**Yaŕina baira moa náxbáakanke, jakón íti akin.** They have widened the road to Yarina to make it better.⟩
*v.i.* **náxbata** : to widen (itself) ⟨**Báritiatiibira non páro náxbatai, kétokan ímaa.** Every year the Ucayali River widens because of landslides.⟩

*adj.* **naxpén** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *xpe,* unidentified element] : with a sunken/lean stomach ⟨**Píamai máwatara, jóni náxpeshoko iki.** The corpse of the man who died from lack of appetite has a sunken stomach.⟩

*v.i.* **náxpeta** : to lose weight : to become thin : to grow lean : to become skinny ⟨**Rimán boxón ráo xéamakanara nato jóni xóata iki; jáinoax joaxa moa jákiribi náxpeke ráo xéayamai.** This man was taken to Lima, made to take medicines, and he gained weight. When he returned he lost weight again because he wasn't taking the medicines.⟩ *syn.* ákoti; óxiti

*v.t.* **nayáa** *Konibo* **nayáka** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *ya,* unidentified element + *-ati* to make/do] 1 : to shake forcefully ⟨**Níwaman ompáx nayáaitianra jéne potá jókonai.** When the water is shaken by an earthquake, it turns murky.⟩ 2 : to shake (e.g., water) off the body ⟨**Jéne meranoáx pikókirankironki róniman jéne nayáakai.** They say that when the yacumama (mythical water-boa) comes out of the water, it shakes the water off its body.⟩

*v.i.* **náyakaa** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *yakáti* to sit] : to sit inside or in an enclosed thing (e.g., a boat) ⟨**—¿Jáweranoki Péna káa? —Káama riki. Oa xóbo chicho náyakaa riki.** "Where did Pena go?" "She hasn't gone anywhere. She's sitting inside that house."⟩
*v.t.* **nayásana** [from Shipibo *na-* inside + *yakáti* to sit + *san,* unidentified element] : to seat (someone) inside ⟨**Ja báke amáka meran nayasánwe.** Sit the child inside the hammock.⟩
*v.i.* **náyata** : to shake forcefully (of land or water) ⟨**Jéne náyataitianronki yoxánshokon sión ishon máxkaa iki.** They say that when the river water shook, an old woman screamed and fainted.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *jéne* water] : in the water : to the water : of the water –Used equally regarding water in its natural state (e.g., in a river) or water in a container. ⟨**nérakati** to throw oneself into the water⟩ ⟨**nepóti** to put into the water⟩
*n.* **neán** : trumpeter (bird) ⟨**Tapíchinin kaxónra, néa kéotai keskati inábo íkai** en nínkata iqui. When I went to the Tapiche river, I heard the savages imitating the trumpeter's call.⟩
[from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *néa* trumpeter] : a small species of water bird

*n.* **néakan** [from Shipibo; shortened past participle of *néati* to tie] : a tie, binding ⟨**Jatíbi xóbo neabora moa nákaxen píke.** The termites have eaten all the house's bindings.⟩ *syn.* NEA, NEXA — both mean "binding"; however, NEA is simply a binding in a general sense, while NEXA implies the cords used for the binding.

*v.t.* **néaa** 1 : to tie ⟨**Níbue koshinra en jíwi néaa moa xákaake.** The strong wind has loosened the poles I tied.⟩ 2 : to coil around ⟨**Ronón ewanronki, awá néaa iki, ompáx xeaitian.** They say the boa coiled around the tapir while it was drinking water.⟩ *syn.* néxati; xéiti; toróati

*v.t.* **nébita** [from Shipibo *ne-* from the water + *bíti* to take] : to take out of the water ⟨**Kobínhawe nato tsismán betan bóe; moa kobínketian boé nebíwe.** Boil the fasaco and the boquichico fish, and when it's boiled, take out the boquichico.⟩
*n.* **neén** : salamanca (a gecko) *syn.* mékexeeya
*v.i.* **néeta** : to climb ⟨**Jiwín néekaskimaironki aínbo nakáxnike.** They say a woman turned into a termite mound because she couldn't climb a tree.⟩
*v.i.* **néeta** : to get stained ⟨**Eara cháwa néeke.** I got stained with mud.⟩
[from Shipibo *jáwebi* nothing + *nékti, nee-* to get stained + *-oma* without] : pure : holy
See **níkoro**

*Konibo* **néino** *also* **jenén ino** *n.* **neínonin** *Konibo* **néinonin** *also* **jenén inon** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water, from *jéne, jenén* water + *íno* jaguar] 1 : sea lion 2 : wolf ⟨**Neíno jáke Orópain jaínoax Nóriti Amírikain. Ja riki áni jaínoax siná ochíti keska.** The wolf lives in Europe and North America. It is like a large, fierce dog.⟩
*n.* **neínonin chaín** [from Shipibo *neíno* sea lion + *chái* brother-in-law] : a small species of catalán

*adv.* [from Shipibo *ne-* here + *-ke* beside] : on this side –Also used with the suffixes *-a* and *-ax,* in the forms *nékea* "on this side" (lit. "of this side") and *nékeax* "from this side". ⟨**Nékea baínra móxa ícha iki; jaó káyamawe —akínra ea yóikanke, ea káchio káitian.** When I was going to the forest, they told me: "On this side of the path there are many thorns; don't go that way."⟩ –Used in arithmetic to introduce an addition. ⟨**Néke 4 benkéx 4 iki 8.** 4 plus 4 equals 8.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5

*adj.* **némiman** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water + *min,* unidentified element] : deep –Used equally regarding water or another liquid or solid substance. ⟨**Nato páro riki, jénetian kikínbires nemín; ikáxbiri iki, báritianbiribi benéshoko.** The Ucayali is very deep in the rainy season, but in the dry season, on the contrary, it has very little water.⟩ ⟨**Manánkini nemínhainoax yoxín jóxonronki jóni píti piánike.** They say that long ago a demon came out of a deep cave and ate a man's food.⟩

*v.t.* **nemínhaa** *Konibo* **nemínhaka** : to deepen : to make deeper ⟨**Pósora moa non nemínhake, jéne íchama íketian; rámara moa jéne ícha iki.** We deepened the well because there wasn't enough water; but now there's plenty.⟩
*v.i.* **némina** : to deepen (itself) : to become deeper ⟨**Jéne béketianra moa Yarína ian nemínke.** Lake Yarina has deepened due to the rise in water.⟩
*n.* **nenán** : a species of thorny plant with a stalk very similar to that of cañabrava (wild cane), used for the sides of a house, and to which the roofing leaves are tied

*v.t.* **nénana** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water + *jánati* to return] : to put or place in water ⟨**Chomómea ompáxa bakóxa iki, bakén jabón nénana.** Foam has formed in the water jar because a child put soap in it.⟩

*also* **nené** *n.* **nenén** *also* **nénekan** : the pain of a burn ⟨**Ompáxa táshi méskoxon síkaaronki néne jénetai.** They say the pain of a burn eases when salt water is poured on it.⟩ ⟨**Jawen nenéronki ténetimayora iki —ikira jóni íkai.** The man says the pain of his burn is unbearable.⟩

*v.t.* **néneaa** *Konibo* **néneaka** : to cause pain –Used especially regarding the pain of a burn. ⟨**Nokon menóra rímoman axón min néneake.** When you poured lemon on my burn, you made me feel pain.⟩
*v.i.* **nénea** : to feel the pain of a burn
*v.t.* **neníchina** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water + *nichínti* to catch/light] 1 : to catch fire in the water 2 : to drive in with a stake

*adj. and n.* **nénketen** *also* **nenkekan** *adj.* 1 : long ⟨**Bitániainoa jonínronki jína nenké jóni mérake.** They say a man from Betania saw a man with a long tail.⟩ 2 : tall ⟨**Komán jíwi riki, jatíbi jíwi bebon nenkéyora.** The shihuahuaco is the tallest of all the trees.⟩ *n.* 1 : length ⟨**Ja jonín jínaronki ike jawen nenké westíora mítorobira.** They say that man's tail was more or less a meter long.⟩ 2 : height ⟨**Kómaman yoshínronki xobón keyátio iki jawen nenké.** They say the demon of the shihuahuaco tree is as tall as a house.⟩ *syn.* keyá; tápo

*v.t.* **nenkeaa** *Konibo* **nenkéaka** 1 : to lengthen ⟨**Kakónkonia kámpora moa nenkéakanke.** They have lengthened the Caco airfield.⟩ 2 : to make taller ⟨**Papánra jawen xóbo moa nenkéake, jíbui ícha axón.** Papa made his house longer by adding more wood.⟩

*adj.* **nenkémanin** [from Shipibo *nenké* long + *-ma* not] : short ⟨**Eara nenkéma tábaranin kéenai.** I want a short board.⟩ *syn.* NENKEMA, TINKO — both can be translated as "short", but TINKO can add the sense of "too" to what is short.
See under **masén**
See under **santíra**
*v.i.* **nénketa** : to lengthen (itself), to stretch ⟨**Papán chiárextira máxko biábi pátsata nenkéke.** The small pair of pants papa bought stretched when washed.⟩
See under **warán**

*adv.* : here : around here [from Shipibo *ne-* here + *-no,* locative particle] –Also used with the suffixes *-a* "of" and *-ax* "from" in the forms *nénoa* "from here" (lit. "of here") and *nénoax* "from here". ⟨**Nénora rabé aínbo winókainke; jára íbirai yatánoxon bénakanai.** Two women have passed by here; they are possibly the ones being sought to be caught.⟩ ⟨**Nénora yámake.** He isn't here.⟩ ⟨**Yaméra rabé yómetso joni néno jowánke; jóketianra yatáwankanke.** Last night two thieves came here, and when they came, they were caught.⟩ ⟨**Eara nénoa iki.** I am from here.⟩ ⟨**Jara nénoax pikóke.** He left from here.⟩
See **náto**
*n.* **népakan** : cortadera (a sharp-edged sedge grass) ⟨**Népakanra ea xatéke.** The cortadera grass cut me.⟩

*n.* **népaxen** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water + *páxko* a sprouting branch] : guama (a fruit tree) ⟨**Nepáxtakira népaxen níibi jíkiamai.** The tuquituqui (jacana) doesn't sink when walking on the guama (leaves/branches).⟩
See under **táki**

*v.t.* **népota** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water + *pókoti* to dye] : to put (several things or a mass) into liquid ⟨**Kentí ompaxyatónra titán binón nepóke.** Mother put the aguaje fruit in a pot of water.⟩
*v.i.* **nérakaa** [from Shipibo *ne-* in the water + *rakáti* to be lying down] : to be lying in the water

*adv.* [from Shipibo *ne-* here + *-ri,* directional particle] : over here : this way –Often used with *-a* or *-ax,* with the respective senses "from around here" and "from around here". ⟨**Nima, néri jowé.** Nima, come here.⟩ ⟨**Noa néria jónibora onán iki —ikira Sán Rantsísko jónibo yóyo íkai iki, rébokiabo onámanin yóini.** The people of San Francisco say: "We who live in this place are cultured." And in this way they claim that the people upriver are uncultured.⟩
*n.* **néroman** [from Shipibo *ne-* of the water + *róno* snake] : a species of non-venomous aquatic snake
*n.* **nesán** [from Shipibo *ne-* of the water + *sa,* unidentified element] : a small species of charapa (river turtle)

*adj.* **nésekan** 1 : calm –Used regarding rain or wind, as well as waves. ⟨**Nato óiki rakéyamawe; moa neséa riki; miara mecháyamai.** Don't be afraid of this rain. It has already calmed down, and you won't get wet.⟩ 2 : at a middle point : neither at one extreme nor the other ⟨**Xeati neséshaman riki.** The masato is right at a middle point: between fermented and sweet.⟩

*v.i.* **nésea** : to calm down (rain, wind, or waves) ⟨**Oira moa néseke.** The rain has already calmed down.⟩ ⟨**Moa bechón néseketianra noa jóke; jákopira noa réokooyamake.** We came when the waves had already calmed down, and that's why we didn't capsize.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *neska,* element of *néskara* of this kind + *akin* subordinate verbal suf.] 1 : in this way : thus –Used regarding an action simultaneous with another. ⟨**Enra nóntiakin neskáakin ákai; minra wétsaresibiaxon ákai.** I make the canoe this way, while you make it another way at the same time.⟩ 2 : in the following way : the following –Used to introduce a direct quotation. ⟨**Jonínra ea áke neskáakin: —Nokon niskán Xéawe mia rayá inon —akin.** A man said the following to me: "Drink my sweat so that you become a strong worker."⟩ *syn.* NESKAAKIN, NESKATÁx, NESKAAxON are alternative forms of a single root *nesca-* with the force of "to do thus"; and all are translated as "in this way". NESKAAKIN, then, implies that an action is simultaneous with another that it imitates, while NESKATÁx, with its variant NESKAAxON, implies that the imitation follows a first action. *syn.* jáskati

*adv.* **néskaaxon** : in this way : thus –Used regarding an action done or to be done in a previously demonstrated way. ⟨**Neskáaxonra non yatánti iki.** We must grab it this way.⟩ ⟨**Néskataxa noa káti iki.** We must go this way.⟩ *syn.* neskáakin

*n.* **netén** 1 : day ⟨**Westíora neténra 24 óra bóai.** A day has 24 hours.⟩ ⟨**Amakiriainoa bintístabaonra, tomínko neténbi jato téeti yóiai.** The Adventists of Amaquiría are made to work on Sundays.⟩ 2 : world ⟨**Moa néte keyóti ochómaxokoronki áni káxibo benónxiki.** They say that when the end of the world comes, large bats will surely come.⟩ 3 : country ⟨**Jawen netén káxa, moa kirínkobo béyamanonxiki.** If the foreigners go to their own country, they will not return.⟩ 4 : life : environment ⟨**Inka joxónronki non néte jakón ímanoxiki.** They say that when the Inca returns, he will improve our lives.⟩
[from Shipibo *jawen* his/her + *néte, netén* world, country + *-mea* of] : wild ⟨**jawen netémea kánso** wild goose⟩

[from Shipibo *néte* day + *xabáti* to yawn] : to dawn ⟨**Yaméra noa káchio káa iki; káxa moa néte xabáaketian noa íaman nókota iki.** At night we went to the forest, and by the time it was dawning we arrived at the lake.⟩
*n.* **neténtsintsiman** [from Shipibo *néte, netén* day + *tsintsín,* unidentified element] : American tarantula
*v.i.* **nétea** : to become day : for the day to turn out (e.g., nice) ⟨**Jakónira néteketianra noa téekanai.** Since the day has turned out so nice, we are working.⟩

*v.i.* **néteta** : to be silent, to keep quiet ⟨**Jabuéki yókatabi netéketianra maístoron báke ríxkike.** The teacher hit a student because he stayed quiet when asked a question.⟩ *syn.* NETETI, KEKEXEETI — both are translated as "to be silent", but KEKEXEETI suggests, with more emphasis, the fact of becoming mute.
See under **wishtín**
See under **néte**

*adj.* **netéxokon** [from Shipibo *netéti, nete-* to be quiet + *-xoko* very] : quiet : calm ⟨**Sontáro káxbbi, netéxoko ítainra ja jamákanai.** If one goes into military service and is quiet, they kick him.⟩

*also* **nexé** *n.* **néxakan** *also* **néxekan** [from Shipibo *néxati, nexa-* to tie, and from Shipibo *néxéti* to tie oneself] : a binding made with a cord ⟨**Yómetsoninra nónti bóyamake, jawen nexá oínxon.** The thief didn't take the canoe when he saw how it was tied.⟩ *syn.* See under **néa**
*v.t.* **néxaa** : to tie : to bind ⟨**Ké-tokanra nónti bóyamake moa en néxakona íketian.** The landslide didn't take the canoe because I had tied it well.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1 *syn.* néati
*n.* **néxbakan** [from Shipibo *ne-* of the water + *xabáti, xabat-* to yawn] : a floodable lowland nearly free of trees and shrubs

*n.* **néxeta** : to get tangled in a cord ⟨**Sapén cháchiaxbi rísbikan nexéketianra jóni sápeman bónike.** Long ago a man was carried off by a manatee he himself had harpooned, because he got tangled in the harpoon line.⟩
*n.* **néxnexen** : hoatzin ⟨**Moa píti yámaketianra ráma nexnéxbobi píkanai.** Since food is scarce these days, things like hoatzin are eaten.⟩ [illustration: *nexnéx*]

*verbal suf.* –Used added to the verb, often followed by *-que* to indicate the preterite tense, a remote past of some years before, or to indicate mythological antiquity. ⟨**Kónxaman téetaiboronki néte xabáti ochóma yábuakanike; westíora jónires íamanike yóiti ikáx.** They say that long ago some loggers turned into white-lipped peccaries at dawn, and only one was saved for being obedient.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2; 7.4.3.1
*suf. adj.* : that becomes –Used to form an adjective from a root that is a noun. ⟨**isáni** that becomes a bird⟩

*suf. postp.* : of –Used in a sentence, added to a noun ending in *-nco*, to an adverb, or to a postposition, to indicate a place of origin. Often used together with *-ax* in the compound form *-niax* to indicate a place of provenance. ⟨**Eara Kakónkonia iki.** I am from Caco.⟩ ⟨**Eara Kankóniax jóke.** I have come from Caco.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2
See under **boánhis**
See **chóchawasha**

*v.i.* **níakaata** [from Shipibo *níati,* *nia-* to put in + *-kaa,* reflexive suf.] : to get in, to enter ⟨**Non rekénboronki móxa meran níakaatax mawápaonike.** They say our ancestors used to die when they got into thorny places.⟩

*v.t.* **níaa** : to put in : to keep, to store ⟨**Titán koríkira en moa bonánti chicho níake.** I have already put mom's money away in the trunk.⟩ ⟨**Maríta meran koríki niá ikénbira, ea yómetsoakana en shinánke.** The money was tucked away in the suitcase, but I thought it had been stolen from me.⟩ *syn.* See under **náneti** *syn.* **bénxoati**
See under **wárawasko**
*n.* **níbikan** : dew : night dampness ⟨**Bakéshoko nibí ámaaronki jánshoai.** They say that if a baby is exposed to the night dampness it gets sick with patco.⟩

*Konibo* **nínbo** *n.* **nibón** *Konibo* **ninbón** 1 : scorpion ⟨**Nibón tékaara isínyora iki.** The scorpion's sting is very painful.⟩ ⟨**Níbo betan shínakoxoronki íchakanankanai.** They say the scorpion and the spider insult each other.⟩ ⟨**Ninbón cháironki bóna iki; jákopira jáweayamai.** They say the scorpion's brother-in-law is the isula (a stinging ant) and that is why it doesn't harm him.⟩ 2 : a constellation called "The Scorpion", formed by the head of Orion. –Used in this sense written with a capital initial *N.*
[from Shipibo *wása* frailecito monkey (a small titi monkey) + *níbo* scorpion] : a very venomous species of scorpion
*n.* **nibón** : trash, garbage ⟨**Aínbaon mátsotara níbo tsamáke.** After sweeping, the woman piled up the trash.⟩

*n.* **níbopotatinin** [from Shipibo *níbo* trash + *pótati* place to throw out] : garbage dump : place where trash is thrown out ⟨**Níbopotatiainoa jakóma jawékiaira nato báke ísinke.** This boy got sick from eating spoiled things from the garbage dump.⟩

*v.i.* **níchimeeta** [from Shipibo *nichínti,* *nichín-* to plant + *-mee-* reflexive suf.] : to get stuck, embedded, driven, or planted in the ground ⟨**Jíwi réraabira poxóyamax níchimeeke; níchimeetaxa jaínbi tánoke.** The tree I cut down fell, got stuck in the ground, and dried up there.⟩

*v.t.* **níchina** 1 : to plant or drive into the ground ⟨**Xoboanoxon jíwi nichínkanara niwén jato póxanaanke.** The posts that were planted to build the house were knocked down by the wind.⟩ 2 : to make stand up ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke chíikan nichínke, paénxon.** A drunk woman made her little child stand in the fire.⟩ ⟨**Nokon jíwi nichinra ea tsékanaanxon potánkana iki.** The stick I planted, they pulled out and threw away.⟩
*n.* **níikan** : forest : jungle ⟨**Nokon cháira jawen báke betanbicho níi meran benóke.** My brother-in-law and one of his children got lost walking alone in the forest.⟩
[from Shipibo *níi* forest + *meran* inside of + *iká,* part. of *íti* to be] : wild ⟨**níi meran ika jawéki** wild animal⟩

See under **isónxoma**
See under **kásho**

*n.* **níimaxon** [from Shipibo *níi* forest + *máxo* plant] : a species of shrub or tender forest plant ⟨**Enra awá tóoakinbi réteyamaa iki, níimaxo píaitian.** I shot at the tapir while it was eating tender plants, but I didn't kill it.⟩

See under **yoshín**
*also* **négro** *n.* **níkoronin** *also* **négronin** : black : a black person *syn.* **chéxe**
*n.* **Nimán** [from Shipibo *níati, nia-* to put in + *-ma* to make] –Used as a masculine name.
*conj.* [from Spanish] : nor ⟨**jawékiati nin sawéti yorónti** not to worry about what one will eat nor what one will wear⟩

*suf. n.* –Used as an ending for the non-basic form of a class of nouns and adjectives. ⟨**ochíti, ochítinin: Ochítininra báke natéxke.** dog: The dog bit the child.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1; 7.4.4.2.e

*v.i.* **nínaa** 1 : to stand : to remain standing ⟨**Sán Rantsískoainronki moa rérakana ikaxbi jíwi nínake janbíx.** They say that in San Francisco a tree stood back up again, even though it had fallen.⟩ ⟨**Nato jóni nínaa íketianra jatíribibaon osánke.** When the man was standing, the others laughed at him.⟩ 2 : to walk ⟨**Nokon bákera níweabataitian péokooti nínake.** My little son started to walk for the first time just as a windstorm was coming.⟩ *syn.* NINATI, NITI — both can be translated as "to stand" or "to walk". However NINATI implies more a situation of standing or walking in a healthy or normal way, whereas NITI implies more the difficult action of, e.g., a sick person walking. *syn.* See under **wáketi**
See **níbo**
*n.* **nínbonishnin** [from Shipibo *nínbonish* imitative of its call] : a species of dove with brownish plumage, similar to the wild dove

*v.t.* **nínia** : to pull ⟨**Nokon kéen riki tsínikin jato níniti.** What I like is to play pulling on a rope and dragging everyone along.⟩ ⟨**Sámamanra bóti nínike.** The whirlpool pulled the boat.⟩

*v.t.* **nínkata** 1 : to hear : to listen ⟨**Motóro rónikai en ninkákenbira, nato yosín ninkáyamake, pábe ixon.** I heard the noise of the motor, but that old man didn't hear anything because he is deaf.⟩ ⟨**Moa maton nínkata íketianra, ea Rimán kátana en mato yóiamai.** I'm not going to tell you any more about my trip to Lima because you have already heard it.⟩ 2 : to understand ⟨**Nawán join kírika yóyo akinra en ninkáyamai; nón joinbi akínresa en nínkatai.** When I read something in Spanish, I don't understand; but in our own language, I do.⟩ ⟨**Enra mia ninkáyamai.** I don't understand you.⟩ ⟨**Maton ninká jawékira en moa mato yóikashamai.** I don't want to repeat again what you have already understood.⟩

[from Shipibo *jói* word + *ninkáti* to listen + *-xon* for the benefit of (another)] : to pay attention to, to heed —Used with the personal object preceding the object *jói.* ⟨**Enpachora éseai; jabira ea jói ninkáxonyamai.** I'm always the one who advises him, but he doesn't pay attention to me.⟩ *syn.* onánti
*v.i.* **nínota** : to slip, to slide (e.g., in the mud) ⟨**Manón nínoti kakáskimaitianra jóni inón bíke.** A man slipped in the mud, and while he was struggling to move, a jaguar attacked him.⟩
See **nítikoma**

*n.* **nísakan** 1 : small straw bits : dead leaves, leaf litter 2 : clothing with patches or hanging tatters ⟨**Nato bakén kotón onara nisáira iki.** This child's patched shirt has many tatters hanging from it.⟩
*n.* **níshbiman** [from Shipibo *níshi* forest vine + *bína* wasp] : a species of yellowish wasp, similar to the *máshibina* wasp

*n.* **nishín** 1 : vine ⟨**Tapán néxanoxon níshi bénai kaxa jóni níi meran benóke.** A man went to the forest to look for vines to tie up the raft, and got lost.⟩ 2 : climbing plant, creeper ⟨**Awakanra níshi píai moa jénetia íketian.** When it is rainy season, the tapir eats climbing plants.⟩ 3 : one or another of several soft-wood trees 4 : ayahuasca ⟨**Níshi xéaibora yamé béwabewashinai.** The healers who drank ayahuasca sang all night.⟩ *syn.* See under **áyawaska**
[from Shipibo *ástoro*, unidentified element + *níshi* vine] : a species of vine whose fruit is eaten by the paucar (a cacique bird)
[from Shipibo *kápe, kápeten* caiman + *ráo* plant remedy + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine used to treat rheumatism
[from Shipibo *káshi, kashín* bat + *méntsis* claws + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of climbing herb with small leaves and thorns, whose sap is drunk so that one becomes a good fisherman
[from Shipibo *káxa* crybaby + *wáro*, unidentified element + *níshi* forest vine] : granadilla (a passion fruit)
[from Shipibo *cheónrao* plant medicine + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of tree useful for house timber
[from Shipibo *chópiananti* sandeíta (a plant) + *níshi* forest vine] : sandeíta
[from Shipibo *wáme* paiche (a giant fish) + *béro* eye + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine with small, round fruit eaten by gamitana fish
[from Shipibo *inín* aromatic + *tani* a little + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of forest vine used as a remedy
[from Shipibo *jási, jasín* curassow + *táe* foot + *níshi* forest vine] : paujil-chaqui (curassow-foot vine)
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *ayáx* tamshi (a fiber vine) + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine used for tying or weaving
[from Shipibo *moxó* topa (balsa tree) + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of tree similar to the balsa tree, whose bark is used as straps for carrying things
[from Shipibo *níshporo*, unidentified element + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine with no particular use
[from Shipibo *ráo* remedy + *níshi* vine] : one of the vine species that are medicinal
[from Shipibo *xakón* centipede + *áti, áka* to do, to make + *ráo* plant remedy + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine whose sap resembles water and serves as a remedy for treating itching
[from Shipibo *xawán* macaw + *rebonti*, unidentified element + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of useless vine
[from Shipibo *xawán* macaw + *reshanti*, unidentified element + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine
[from Shipibo *xawán* macaw + *tácho* rash on the foot + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of useless vine
[from Shipibo *xáwe* charapa (a river turtle) + *póko* intestines + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine, greenish or grayish-green in color, with medium-sized leaves
[from Shipibo *xébiana, xébianan* clitoris + *ráo* plant remedy + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of vine used when cutting a woman's clitoris
[from Shipibo *xóya* mouse + *ítsa* stench + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of forest vine that gives off a stench
[from Shipibo *táxba, taxbán* seasonally-flooded lowland + *níshi* forest vine] : carahuasco (a tree) *syn.* éshi
[from Shipibo *tórapako*, unidentified element + *níshi* vine] : a species of vine with large fruit used by women for a special facial cleansing
[from Shipibo *tsitsáwa*, unidentified element + *níshi* forest vine] : a species of forest vine
*n.* **níshiboanhisin** [from Shipibo *níshi* vine + *boánhis* sacha ajo (wild garlic)] : a species of vine with leaves like those of the guaba (ice-cream-bean tree)
See under **chóchawasha**

See under **masén**
See under **wárawasko**

*adj.* **níshnón** : a faint sound barely heard or heard from afar ⟨**Níi meranra níshno tóoati pishíke, jaín jóni káama ikaxbi.** A gunshot was faintly heard far off in the forest, even though no one had gone there.⟩

*v.i.* **níshnoriria** [from Shipibo *níshno* barely perceptible sound + *ríriti* to thunder] : to thunder far off so that the thunder is barely heard ⟨**Enra níshnoriri ikai ninkáke.** I could barely hear it thundering far off.⟩

*v.i.* **níshnoa** : (of a sound) to fade away gradually until it disappears ⟨**Máioshiainoax ábion nóyaara jawen rón moa níshnoke.** The sound of the plane flying from Pucallpa gradually faded away.⟩

*n.* **níshobon** *Konibo* **níshobaon** *pish.* **níshobaen** : legendary jungle people ⟨**Níshoboronki moátian jápaonike; jaton tepón ícha ípaonike.** They say that long ago the *nísho* people used to set many traps along their trails.⟩
See under **níshi**
*n.* **Níshtón** [from Spanish *nesto*, element of *Ernesto*] –Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **nískaman** : sweat ⟨**Jonínra áke ea neskáakin: —Nokon niskán xéawe mia rayá inon —akin.** A man said this to me: —Drink my sweat so that you become a strong worker.⟩

*n.* **niskán jokonai kinishokon** [from Shipibo *niskán* sweat + *jókonai* coming out; and this from *jokónti* to come out + *kínishoko*; from *kíni* hole + *-shoko,* diminutive suf.] : pore ⟨**Bichira niskán jokonai kinishokoya iki.** The skin has pores.⟩
*v.i.* **nískana** : to sweat

*v.i.* **niá** 1 : to stand ⟨**Niásha nokon yóra ea isínke.** I stood up, and my body hurt.⟩ 2 : to walk ⟨**Nato jónira íshtomashoko níai rókotoron xátea ikax.** This man walks slowly because the doctor operated on him.⟩

[from Shipibo *jákonhax*, subordinate form of *jakónhati* to treat well + *-yon* entirely + *níti* to stand] : to go about well groomed ⟨**Jáboman chókitaxa noa jáskatax íti iki, jakónyonax níi.** We wash with soap so we can go about well groomed.⟩ *syn.* See under **nínati**

*also* **níosma** *adj.* **nítikoman** *also* **níosman** : lame [from Shipibo *níti* to walk + *-coma* difficult, or *-yosma* one who never does (the indicated thing)] ⟨**Nítikoma jónira Rimán bokánke, jawen táe moa xátenoxon.** They took a lame man to Lima to have his foot amputated.⟩ ⟨**nítikoma jaskábi píkota** lame from birth⟩ *syn.* **chánto**
*v.i.* **nítikomata** [from Shipibo *nítikoma* lame + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to become lame ⟨**Ikónbiresira nato jóni wíniai nítikomatax.** This man weeps bitterly because he became lame.⟩
*n.* **níwaman** : tremor : earthquake ⟨**Ríma ochómaika jémameabora níwaman jaton xóbo rásakanke.** The houses of the residents who live near Lima were destroyed by an earthquake.⟩
*v.i.* **níwana** : to have an earthquake ⟨**Niwánketiaura bákebaon mái tsákake.** When the earthquake happened, the children fell to the ground.⟩

*n.* **niwén** 1 : wind ⟨**Níweyoshinronkiki kikínbires jankósh.** They say the spirit of the wind has great power to blow.⟩ 2 : toxic air pollution : toxic gas or vapor ⟨**Níwe xéaaxa westíora báke ésteax mawáke.** A certain boy inhaled a toxic gas; his stomach swelled up and he died.⟩ 3 : air ⟨**Kirínkobaonronki níwe mókaanoxiki réteanankin.** They say that in a future war the foreigners will surely poison the air.⟩

[from Shipibo *mayáti, maya-* to spin, to whirl + *níwe* wind] : small whirlwind ⟨**Mayániwenra jato kinámati átipanke, játoki pakéxon.** A small whirlwind, when it catches people, can make them vomit.⟩
[from Shipibo *xabón* lizard + *mayániwe* small whirlwind] : a species of whirlwind

*n.* **níweabakan** [from Shipibo *níwe* wind + *jábati, jaba-* to flee] : windstorm, strong gust of wind ⟨**Níweabatamapari ikénra noa jóke; jákopira noa jakónbires nokóke.** We came before the windstorm rose, and that is why we arrived safely.⟩
See under **ísa**
*n.* **niwén ewan** [from Shipibo *níwe, niwén* wind + *-ewa,* augmentative suf.] : storm : cyclone : hurricane

*n.* **niwénshaman** [from Shipibo *níwe* wind + *sháman* pleasant] : breeze ⟨**Nato nétera moa jakónhira iki, ói béyamaitian níweshaman ikax.** Today is a good day; it isn't raining and there is a breeze.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *nói* abdomen] 1 : of the abdomen : through the abdomen : to the abdomen 2 : of the navel : at the navel : to the navel ⟨**nóxteti** to cut at the navel⟩ 3 : on the surface ⟨**nobé** boil⟩ 4 : toward the inside ⟨**nóati** to insert (something pointed) toward the inside⟩

*pron.* **non** : we : us : to us ⟨**Nóabora moa apón ónanabo iki —ikira San Rantsísko jónibo íkai.** The people of San Francisco say: —We are now recognized by the government.⟩ ⟨**Yáminawabora nóki sinákanike, non jaton kaíbobo rétea shínanax.** The Yaminahua got angry with us because they thought we had killed their people.⟩ ⟨**Rámaronki non Inka noa ícha jawéki rikárani joai.** They say that now our Inca is coming to give us many gifts.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.1

*v.t.* **nóaa** [from Shipibo *no—* on the inside + *áti* to do, to make] : to pierce with something pointed ⟨**Bakénra jawen wétsa pián nóake, pokónko.** A boy jabbed his little brother's belly with an arrow.⟩
*Konibo* **nonbé** *n.* **nóbekan** *Konibo* **nónbekan** : boil : furuncle; *also* : rash, welt
[from Shipibo *chichó* very deep inside + *póko* stomach + *meran* inside of + *nobé* boil] : ulcer
*Konibo* **nonbéti** *v.t.* **nóbeta** *Konibo* **nónbeta** : to have a boil : to have a furuncle; *also* : to have a rash

*Konibo* **nonbéx** *n.* **nóbexen** *Konibo* **nónbexen** : dove ⟨**Moátianronki** **nonbex yóyo ikai ipaonike, non Ínka néno janóntian.** They say that long ago the dove used to talk, back when our *Inca lived around here.⟩ *syn.* xotó
See under átsa

*n.* **nochón** : a species of medium-sized *churo (freshwater snail) –Used in a singular or collective sense with no difference in form. ⟨**Ariwara nócho pitín kéenyora iki.** The *tarahui likes eating *nócho snails very much.⟩ ⟨**Nochón kópiaronki báke jími chíxotai.** They say that when a child is *cutipado (magically affected) by a *nócho snail, he gets bloody diarrhea.⟩

*n.* **nóchopokon** [from Shipibo *nócho* churo (freshwater snail) + *póko* stomach] : a species of river fish similar to the turushuque (a fish) *syn.* NOCHOPOKO, TSANO denote the same species of fish and are used interchangeably.

*adj.* **noén** : tasty : delicious : rich : exquisite : delightful ⟨**Páan nóeyora íketianra, báke píkasai.** Since the bread is very tasty, the child wants to eat it.⟩ ⟨**Wáme namira nóeira iki.** The meat of the *paiche (giant fish) is delicious.⟩
*v.t.* **nóeaa** *Konibo* **nóeaka** : to season ⟨**Sibórianra wáme beten nóeake.** She seasoned the *paiche porridge with onion.⟩
*v.i.* **nóea** : to become tasty ⟨**Titán pítiaara moa yóchi aká nóeke.** The food that mother prepared has become tasty because she added chili pepper.⟩

*n.* **noín** 1 : the outer abdomen (e.g., of an animal or fish) 2 : the lower shell (plastron) of a turtle ⟨**Kabóri noi xoiresara nato jóni píkasai.** This man wants to eat the roasted plastron of the *taricaya (a river turtle).⟩ 3 : the white part of the rind of a fruit (e.g., watermelon) as it is about to ripen

*v.t.* **nóibaa** [from Shipibo *nóiti,* *noi–* to love + *ba,* element of *báke* child + *–ti,* infinitive suf.] 1 : to feel sorry for (a person) ⟨**Nokon chái chópa kéyota iken nóibaxonra en kotón betan chiárexti ménike.** I felt sorry for my brother-in-law because he had no clothes, so I gave him a pair of pants and a shirt.⟩ 2 : to covet (e.g., by touching) ⟨**Kórikioma ixonra, jawéki ícha en Máioshiainoa nóiabake.** I had no money, but he coveted, by touching, the merchandise that was in Pucallpa.⟩

*adj.* **nóibatishokon** [from Shipibo *nóibati* to feel sorry + *-shoko* very] : very regrettable, very pitiful ⟨**Nato páena jóni jenén réteara nóibatishoko iki.** It is regrettable that that drunk man drowned.⟩
*adj.* **nóimiston** [from Shipibo *nóiti, noi-* to love + *-mis* one who always does (the indicated action)] : an affectionate or loving person
*n.* **nóiman** : earthworm, intestinal worm

*conj.* [from Shipibo *non* our + *yoin* said + *-bi* but] : that is to say ⟨**Moa yamé pochinikonra, játikaxbi óxakanai; noínbi, tsóa níai non oínyamai.** By midnight everyone is already asleep; that is, no one is seen walking about anymore.⟩
*n.* **noín raon** [from Shipibo *noín* worm + *ráo* remedy] : remedy against worms, dewormer

*v.t.* **nóia** : to love ⟨**Wétsabo ákai bebonbiresa non bákebo non nóike.** We love our children more than anyone else.⟩ ⟨**Nokon nói bakera sontáro katáyantanax moa nokóke.** My beloved son has returned from military service after years.⟩ *syn.* kéenti
See under **ráo**
See under **wáste**

*v.t.* **nókaa** *Konibo* **nókaaka** : to put out, to extinguish ⟨**Oi kextó bexónra chíi nókaake.** A hard rain came and put out the fire.⟩ ⟨**Moa motóro nokáx masáketianra jáwekeskataxbi noa káti átipanyamake.** When the *motor is turned off and doesn't work, we can't travel by boat.⟩

*v.i.* **nókaa** : to go out, to be extinguished ⟨**Moa chíi nókaketianra non píti yóa áyamake.** We didn't prepare food because the fire went out.⟩ ⟨**Moa joé nókati ochómara, ea óxai.** When the light is about to go out, I'm going to sleep.⟩
*adj.* : my ⟨**Nokon átapabora máxokan ea píanaanke.** A *fox ate my chickens⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.3.3
See under -na

*v.i.* **nókoa** : to come upon, to encounter (a person or animal) ⟨**Káchio kaxónra kímisha yáwa tsama non nókoa iki.** We went to the *forest and came upon three herds of *white-lipped peccaries.⟩ ⟨**Nato jóni bénota iántanara moa nókota iki.** The man who got lost in the *forest three months ago has already been found.⟩

*v.i.* **nókota** : to arrive; *specif.* : to be back : to return ⟨**Moa xobón nokóxon, non piá iki.** On arriving home, we ate something.⟩ ⟨**Rimán botánhibatabora yamé nokókanke.** Those who went to Lima the other day were back last night.⟩ *syn.* báneti
*n.* **nomán** : yuto (a tinamou) : partridge
See under **átsa**
*n.* **nomín** : thirst ⟨**Noara nomín chéxayantanke.** In that time we suffered from thirst.⟩
*n.* **nómironin** [from Spanish] : number ⟨**Enra nómiro topónti onánke westíora michón kaman.** I know how to count numbers up to a million.⟩
*v.i.* **nómia** : to be thirsty ⟨**Sókota ora xéaama ikaxa ea nómiai.** I am thirsty because I haven't had anything to drink for six hours.⟩

*adj.* : our ⟨**Non rekén pápashokobora siná ípaokanike, sináti ráo xéaibo ikax.** Our ancestors used to become fierce, because they used to drink a series of plant remedies to make themselves enraged.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.3.3

*verbal suf.* –Used at the end of the subordinate verb with the force of "so that" in the subordinate clause. Often used followed by a form of the auxiliary verb *-iti* in the form *-ikáx* or *-íxon*. ⟨**Maton kokónonra, non keó beíbake.** We have brought caimitillos (a small fruit) so that you can eat them.⟩ ⟨**Nokon títa ísinai óxanon ikaxra noa xóbo meranoax pikóke.** We left the house so that my sick mother could sleep.⟩ –Used followed by *kawé* or *bokánwe* in a phrase that urges one or several people to take part in a specific action involving movement from one place to another. ⟨**Nokon títashokoiba xawén báchi pinón bokanwe.** Let's go eat charapa (river turtle) eggs at my grandmother's.⟩ ⟨**Anón kawe konxán xátekin; moara jénetiati ochóma iki.** Let's the two of us go cut wood, because the flood season is approaching.⟩ ⟨**Kanón kawé.** Let's the two of us go.⟩ –Used followed by *awé* to indicate the exhortative mood when the verb does not involve movement of the subject. ⟨**Ráma Káko jonibo rétenon akanwe —ikira yáminawabo íkai, jaton kaíbobo rétekanketian Káko jonibores pónteax.** The Yaminahua, blaming the people of Caco for the death of their kinsmen, say: —Let's kill the people of Caco.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3.2.a; 4.2.3.2.b; 4.2.3.4; 7.4.3.2

*n.* **nónoman** : duck ⟨**Jénetianra átapabo ónitsapítai mái yámaketian; játian nonónbiribi rároshaman íkai, jenén kéen ikax.** During the flood season the chickens suffer because there is no dry land; meanwhile the ducks are happy because they like water.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *nonón* duck] : a species of domestic duck, mostly white in color

*n.* **nontín** [from Shipibo *nónoti, nono-* to swim + *-ti* instrument suf.] : canoe ⟨**Yómetsobaon nónti bokánketianra non chibánxon bichínke.** When the thieves took the canoe, we chased them and took it back from them.⟩

-**nontian** *conjunctive suf.* [from Shipibo *-non*, verbal suf. + *-tian* when] : at the time that –Used at the end of the subordinate verb, indicating that it expresses an action simultaneous with that of the main clause. ⟨**Ja non Pírisirinti jonóntianra nokon báke píkota íki.** At the time our President came, my son was born.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2

*n.* **nontínbaken** [from Shipibo *nónti, nontín* canoe + *báke* child] 1 : a fishing canoe about three meters long 2 : a miniature canoe made especially for sale to tourists : small canoe ⟨**Nontínbakeshokobo má**roxon en koríki biára ea yómetsobaon bónankanke. Some thieves took the money I earned selling miniature canoes.⟩
See under **peká**

*n.* **nóntipoinkinin** [from Shipibo *nónti* canoe + *póinki* anus] : the rear part of a canoe, stern ⟨**Yakáti shínanira nóntipoinki kénebaini báke mápoori káke.** The child wanted to sit at the stern of the canoe, but fell headfirst into the water.⟩

-**nonxiki** *verbal suf.* [from Shipibo *-nonx*, variant of *-nox*, subordinate-verb suf. + *iki*, present indicative form of *íti* to be] –Used to indicate general future time. ⟨**Bakísha papa nokónonxiki.** Tomorrow dad will arrive.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.1

*v.i.* **nóoxika** : to slurp noisily –Used mostly among speakers of the Konibo dialect. ⟨**Píti jene xéai nóoxiketianra nato báke osánkanke.** They laughed at this boy because he slurped the meat broth noisily.⟩
*n.* **nópexen** : a species of large churo (freshwater snail), reddish or dark in color –Used in a singular or collective sense with no difference in form.

*v.t.* **nórea** 1 : to scrape with a knife ⟨**Jíwi nóreira báken mexteke chichikanin.** A child cut his hand while scraping a stick with a knife.⟩ 2 : to plane, to smooth with a plane ⟨**Rabé nétera tábara nórekin en jankénhake.** In two days I finished planing the boards.⟩ ⟨**Konxán tabara noré ea márokasabira ea koríkiomapari íki.** I would like to buy already-planed wooden boards, but at the moment I don't have enough money.⟩

*n.* **nóretinin** [from Shipibo *nóret, nore-* to plane + *-ti* instrument suf.] : plane (tool) ⟨**Nokon nóretira, ea masáankanke, benáyora ikénbi.** They ruined my plane, which was brand new.⟩ *syn.* sipícho
*n.* **norex ikaiton** : an animal or creature that crawls; *specif.* : reptile ⟨**Jatiribi norex ikaibaonra cháki píai.** Some reptiles eat the little cháki toad.⟩
*n.* **noréxpinin** : breastbone of a fish

*also* **nórdiste** *n.* **nóritistin** *also* **nórdesten** : northeast
*n.* **noshán** : shuyo (an edible grub) ⟨**Jatíribibaonra nósha píamai, xéna iká íketianki.** Some people don't eat shuyo because they think it forms from worms.⟩ *syn.* See under **mánonoko**
See under **ráo**

*adj. and n.* **nóshikan** [from Shipibo; shortened past participle of *nóshiti* to break] *adj.* : broken *n.* : break : opening ⟨**Nato nónti noshikanra jéne buêitai.** Water is coming in through the opening that this canoe has.⟩

*v.t.* **nóshia** : to break, to tear (e.g., cloth, leather, or a tied fence) ⟨**Kikínbiresakin tári nóshiaxa pápa sináke.** Dad got very angry because he tore his cushma (traditional tunic).⟩ *syn.* NOSHITI, TESATI, TOETI can all be translated as "to break"; but while TOETI implies pottery or glass breaking, NOSHITI implies wood and other materials less brittle than pottery, and TESATI implies thread breaking.

*v.i.* **nóshita** 1 : to break, to tear (e.g., cloth, leather, a tied fence, or something made of wood) ⟨**Jíwi noshíxonra westíora báke réteke.** When the tree's wood broke, it killed a boy.⟩ 2 : to crack, to split (something made of wood) ⟨**Nokon tábara norera moa noshíke.** My planed board split.⟩

*v.t.* **nótsina** [from Shipibo *nótsiti* to resent + *-n,* verbal derivational suf.] : to scold : to grumble at ⟨**Rókotoronra jóni notsínke, jawen báke ráomeeyamakin mawámaketian.** The doctor scolded a man because he didn't have his son treated and let him die.⟩ *syn.* wáoati

*v.i.* **nótsia** 1 : to kick one's feet in anger ⟨**Máioshiain kákasainbi jawen papán ráanyamaara báke nótsike.** The child threw a tantrum, kicking his feet in rage, because his father wouldn't let him go to Pucallpa.⟩ 2 : to get upset (e.g., at not receiving what one wants) ⟨**Páan bíkasainbi méniamakanara nato báke xontako nótsike.** This girl got upset because she wasn't given the bread she wanted.⟩ ⟨**Jawen titán bóyamaara nato báke nótsike.** This child is upset because his mother didn't take him with her.⟩ 3 : to feel resentful ⟨**Jawen béneki nótsixonra aínbaon jawen béne yóyo ayamai.** When a woman feels resentful toward her husband, she doesn't want to talk with him.⟩ ⟨**Rosíran móro ménia**maara nato aínbo nótsia iqui. This woman is resentful because doña Lucila didn't give her beads.⟩ 4 : to envy ⟨**Maístoron motóro bíketianra jónibo nótsiai.** When the teacher buys a motor, people become envious.⟩

*Konibo* **-nonx** *verbal suf.* **-noxon** *Konibo* **-nonxon** –Used at the end of the subordinate verb with the force of "in order to" in the subordinate clause. Used in the form *-nox* or *-noxon* to mark whether the main verb is intransitive or transitive, as the case may be. ⟨**Non rekénboronki mekékatikanai, inábo rétei bonox.** They say our ancestors used to practice rites of abstention before going to kill wild Indians.⟩ ⟨**Icha koríki bínoxon-** ra, non ícharibi konxbán xáteai.** To get a lot of money, we also kut a lot of wood.⟩ –Used in the form *-nox* with *iwé*, the imperative form of *íti*, to express an emphatik or urgent rekest. ⟨**Rabé simánan wínota pecao, joríbanox ihue —aquinra ea rókotoron áke.** Make an effort to come back after two weeks —the doctor told me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2 *syn.* kopí

*n.* **noxán** 1 : nephew : niece : the son or daughter of a man's brother; *also* : the son or daughter of a wife's sister –Each of the vocative forms *noxá*, *choré* "younger relative", *yosí* "old man", *yoxán* "old woman", *jomó-* "young person", and *chinín* "girl" is used to address the person indicated in this sense and the next. ⟨**Nokon nóxaboyaxonra en tapán bóai Máioshiain.** Together with my nephews I will take the raft to Pucallpa.⟩ 2 : stepson : stepdaughter ⟨**Nato jonínra bákeoma ishon jawen nóxa nóike.** This man loves his stepson very much because he has no child of his own.⟩ *syn.* chíobake

*v.t.* **nóxaa** : to carry in a sling cloth ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke nóxaxon káchio bóke.** A woman put her little child in a sling cloth and carried him through the forest.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákera noxáres óxai ikax, báchimeax óxakashamai.** This child doesn't want to sleep in bed because he is used to sleeping while being carried in a sling cloth.⟩

*also* **nóxti** *n.* **nóxatinin** *also* **nóxtin** [from Shipibo *nóxati, noxa-* to carry in a sling cloth + *-ti* instrument suf.] : a cloth carried slung across the chest ⟨**Jawen tsabén nóxatira aínbo yómetsoke.** Her own sister-in-law stole a woman's sling cloth.⟩ ⟨**Nokon titánra noxtín axón ícha kaímito béke.** My mother put many caimitos (a fruit) in the sling cloth and brought them.⟩

*n. and adj.* [from Shipibo *nóxoti, noxo-* to sip] **nóxokan** *n.* : a sip –Used without a modifier specifying which liquid is sipped. ⟨**Eara noxó kéenyamai.** I don't want to take the sip.⟩ *adj.* : sipped ⟨**Nato xóntakora yóashi ikax nato yápa jene noxó akáshamai.** The young lady doesn't want to drink the broth that others have sipped from because she is not willing to share her food.⟩
*v.t.* **nóxoa** : to sip ⟨**Poírito Kayáoainoara westíora náwa ainbo mawáke, ípo jene xána nóxoax.** A mestiza woman from Puerto Callao died from sipping very hot carachama (armored catfish) broth.⟩
*v.t.* **nóxota** [from Shipibo *no-* on the abdomen + *xókati* to skin] : to skin or peel at the abdomen
*v.t.* **nóxtea** [from Shipibo *no-* at the navel + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut the umbilical cord of

*n. and adj.* [from Shipibo *nóyati, noya-* to fly] *n.* **nóyakan** : flight ⟨**Nato isára jawen noyá jakóma iki.** This little bird's flight is ugly.⟩ *adj.* : already able to fly –Used regarding bird chicks. ⟨**Manxán bake noyábora en reteke.** I killed some heron chicks that already knew how to fly.⟩
*v.i.* **nóyaa** : to fly ⟨**Jonín báke raberonki máekawaax nóyanike.** They say a man's two sons turned into huancahuis (a bird) and flew away.⟩

*adjective suf.* **-nton** : without –Used added to a shortened form (e.g., *jan-*) of the noun (e.g., *jána* "tongue") that functions as the complement of the suffix. –Used regarding body parts. ⟨*jánto* without a tongue⟩ *syn.* -NTO, -OMA are used with the same sense of "without", but -OMA is used without restriction, while -NTO is limited in its application to body parts. Thus, e.g., one finds the two forms *jináoma* and *jínto*, both meaning "without a tail".
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *o* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1
*conj.* [from Shipibo] : or See Grammar Sketch 7.7.1
*interj.* : oh –Used as an exclamation, e.g., upon making a mistake or suddenly remembering something. See Grammar Sketch 7.8

*pron. and adj.* **oatonin** *pron.* : that (one) : that over there ⟨**¿Jáwe jánerin óa?** What is that called?⟩ *adj.* : that : that (over there) ⟨**Oa jónira yómetso iki. Maton jawékibo bénxoakanwe; matora yómetsoanake.** That man is a thief. Secure your things so he doesn't steal them.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.4 *syn.* See under **ja**

*postp. suf.* : of –Used in a sentence, added to a noun with the locative suffix *-ain* or to the postposition *meran*, to indicate a place of origin. Often used together with *-ax* in the compound form *-oax* to indicate a place of provenance. ⟨**Eara Yarínainoa iki.** I am from Yarina⟩ ⟨**Jára Yarínainoax jóke.** He came from Yarina⟩ ⟨**níi meranoa binón** aguaje palm fruits from the forest⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2

*v.i.* **óchaa** : to sin : to be at fault ⟨**Papán motóroninra jawen wétsa óchake.** His brother was at fault for dad's motor breaking down.⟩

*adv.* : far ⟨**Noíbo Iríain maístoroiti ea ráankaskanabira ea káyaamake ochóyora íketian.** They wanted to send me to Nuevo Edén as a teacher, but I didn't go because it's very far.⟩ ⟨**Rámaronki óchokeax jóni kóshibo nókotai.** They say the authorities are arriving today from far away.⟩

*v.t.* **ochóaa** *Konibo* **ochóaka** : to push away : to let (something) drift away ⟨**Nokon nónti jábatainbi bénai káyamaxonra en ochóake.** I let my canoe drift away after it came loose, because I didn't go look for it.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *ochó* far + *-oma* without, not having] : near

*adj.* **oén** : abnormally large : huge : enormous ⟨**Nato bákeshokora óe iki, xoá ikax.** This little child is abnormally big, because he is so fat.⟩ ⟨**Papán awá réteara óeoebires iki.** How enormous is the *tapir dad killed today!⟩ *syn.* See under **áni**
*n.* **oín** : rain ⟨**Nato aínbaonra ói jene xéakashamai, isínaketian.** This woman doesn't want to drink rainwater because she is afraid of getting sick.⟩
[from Shipibo *ói* rain + *béti* to come] : to rain ⟨**Oi béketianra noa káyamake min kénaabi.** Even though you invited us, we didn't go because of the rain.⟩

*v.i.* **óimeeta** [from Shipibo *oínti oin-* to see + *-mee*, reflexive suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to see oneself : to look at oneself ⟨**Ispíkonin óimeetaxonki non rekénbo ráenike.** They say our ancestors became tame by looking at themselves in a mirror.⟩

*v.t.* **óina** 1 : to see : to look at : to observe ⟨**Min jóto ea óimawe —akinra chaín ea áke.** My brother-in-law said to me: —Show me your photo.⟩ ⟨**Oínwe jaínra jóni jóai mérati.** Look! There comes a man out for a walk.⟩ ⟨**Oínreswe; miara wétsa jonín xobón iki —akinra titán jawen báke aká iki.** The mother told her little child: —Look at the things, but don't touch anything; you're in someone else's house.⟩ 2 : to pay attention to –Usually used in this sense with the suffix *-caya* "really". ⟨**Oínkayata nato pakékana.** Please pay close attention to these examples.⟩ 3 : to wait for –Used in this sense with the suffix *pari* "first". ⟨**Oímpariwe, noa senén kanómpari ea náshibanon ea mánawe.** Wait for me a moment; so we can go together, I'm going to bathe.⟩ *syn.* See under **jísti** *syn.* mánati
*n.* **óinxonmabi ikonhatinin** [from Shipibo *óinxon*, subordinate form of *oínti* to see + *-ma* not + *-bi* even though + *ikónhati* to believe] : faith *syn.* See under **jíi**

*adj.* **oínyosmaton** [from Shipibo *oínti*, *oin-* to see + *-yosma* never] : never seen : unknown ⟨**Tson oínyosma íaman káketíanra jóni cháikonin bachínike.** When a man went to an unknown oxbow lake, one of the wild *chaiconi demons pulled him by the hair.⟩
*n.* **óipoan** [from Shipibo *ói* rain + *póa* sachapapa (a wild tuber)] : a species of snail usually seen after a rain
