*n.* **óixewakan** *Konibo* **óixewan** [from Shipibo *ói* rain + *xewá* woven together] 1 : hail ⟨**Oixewa non óyaronki ishtón xéta payóyamai.** They say that if we suck on hail, our teeth won't decay quickly.⟩ 2 : snow ⟨**Ánimana óixewa** the snow of the highlands⟩
*n.* **okán** [from Shipibo *óka*, imitative of its call] : a small black bird that feeds on rice and usually flies in flocks
*n.* **okánchokan** [from Shipibo *okánchoka*, imitative of its call] : a small brown bird that feeds on rice

*adv.* : on the other side; *specif.* : on the other side of the river –Also used with the suffixes *-a* and *-ax* in the forms *ókea* "from the other side" and *ókeax* "from the other side". ⟨**Oke párokeibara jóni saí itái, báikan nónti bóonaana.** On the other side of the river a man is calling out because the current carried off his canoe.⟩ ⟨**Okeax bexónra ea béchoman réoke.** Waves came from the other side of the river and capsized my canoe.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5

*adv.* [from Shipibo *óke* on the other side + *n*, unidentified element, + *bekon* between two] : side by side : on both sides : in parallel ⟨**Okénbekonra rabé motóro ínatai parón.** Two motorboats travel up the Ucayali River side by side.⟩

*n.* **okón** [from Shipibo *óko*, imitative of spitting] 1 : phlegm ⟨**Isínya jonín óko jámataxa nocon títa ísinai.** My mother is getting sick because she stepped on the phlegm of a tuberculosis patient.⟩ 2 : cough
[from Shipibo *róo* cotomono (howler monkey) + *óko* cough] : whooping cough ⟨**Yarínainoa nawán báke rabera róookon réteke.** Whooping cough killed two children of a mestizo man in Yarinacocha.⟩
*v.i.* **ókoa** : to cough ⟨**Nato yaméra ea ókoi péokoowanke.** Last night I started coughing.⟩
See **Oríbia**

*also* **-yaoma** *adjective suf.* **-omatonin** *also* **-yaomatonin** : without : not having : that doesn't have –The form *-oma* is used with the letter *h* prefixed if it follows the letter *n*. The form *-oma* is used without restriction, and the form *-yaoma* sometimes after an odd number of syllables. Used with *íti* in the sense of "to not have". ⟨**Ea ribínhoma ikénbira nawán ea téemai, miara ribinya iki ishon.** Even though I have no debts, the mestizo forces me to work, claiming that I do.⟩ ⟨**Bákeoma rikí ea.** I have no children.⟩ ⟨**— ¿Miaki béneya iki? — Eara jayáoma iki.** —Do you have a husband? — I don't have one.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2 *syn.* See under **-nto**

*v.i.* **ómaa** : to approach stealthily ⟨**Nato kímisha yómetsobora nóki ómakiranke.** These three thieves approached us stealthily.⟩

*postp. suf.* –Used in the sense of "on" to indicate a location or destination with gentle impact. Used only added to the pronominal roots in the forms *eon*, *mion*, *jaon*, *noon*, *maton*, and *jaton* (*jabaon*). Used in every sense in place of the *non-basic form that is used where the complement is not a pronoun but a noun. ⟨**Nobéxa eón péyakake.** A dove is perched on my shoulder.⟩ ⟨**Nobéxa eón pakéke.** A dove landed gently on me.⟩ –Used added to the pronominal complement of a person to indicate a desired or wanted object. ⟨**Eara jaón maxkáke.** I need him.⟩ ⟨**Eara jaón kéenai.** I want him.⟩ ⟨**Eara jaón mároke.** I bought it.⟩ ⟨**Eara** **mión kéenai.** I want you⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2 *syn.* See under manaon
*n.* **onáibon** [from Shipibo *ónati, ona-* to mend + *ibo* owner] : the first patch or mend ⟨**Nokon kotón oná ibora moa nóshita iki.** The first patch on my shirt has torn again.⟩
*v.i.* **ónakaata** [from Shipibo *ónati, ona-* to patch, to mend + *-kaa* reflexive suf.] : to mend itself ⟨**Chópabora janbíx ónakaati átipanyamake.** Clothes cannot mend themselves.⟩

*adj.* **onámaton** *Konibo* **onámanin** [from Shipibo *onán* knowledgeable + *-ma* not] 1 : ignorant ⟨**Onámaboronki akónbireskin pátoronbaon yónopaonike.** They say that in the past the ignorant were forced by their bosses to work very hard.⟩ 2 : stupid : idiotic ⟨**Nokon bákera onáma iki, yoshínbaketani ikáx.** My son is an idiot because he's half crazy.⟩ *syn.* ONAMA, SHINANHOMA can both be translated as "stupid"; but ONAMA, unlike SHINANHOMA, implies a state of extreme stupidity, as if brought on by a demon.
[from Shipibo *kírika* book + *onáma* ignorant] : illiterate
*adj.* **onámashokon** [from Shipibo *onáma* ignorant + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : foolish : senseless ⟨**Jakóma jónibaonra aínbobo onámashoko paránkanai.** Bad men deceive foolish women.⟩

*v.t.* **onámaa** [from Shipibo *onánti, onan-* to know + *-mati* to make] : to make known : to teach ⟨**Inkabo nénobi ixonronki noa jawéki átibo onámakeanke.** They say if the Incas were here, they would teach us how to make many things.⟩ : to consult with (e.g., a doctor) ⟨**Enra rókotoro onámakasai.** I want to consult with the doctor.⟩ *syn.* áxeati

*v.i.* **ónameeta** : to guess or have a premonition (of a future event) about oneself –Used with a complement expressing the foreseen event. ⟨**Nokon mawátira ea moa ónameeke.** I have a premonition of my own death.⟩
*n.* **onámiston** [from Shipibo *onánti, onan-* to know + *-mis* one who always does (the indicated action)] : diviner, fortune-teller
*adj.* **ónaman** : knowledgeable : wise ⟨**Senényoira onán yóikanai jatíxonbi.** Everyone says that Senényoi is very wise.⟩
[from Shipibo *jatíbi* all + *jawéki* thing + *onán* wise] : one who knows everything : omniscient ⟨**Riós jatíbi jawéki onán** omniscient God⟩
*n.* **ónaman** : curuinse (a leaf-cutter ant) ⟨**Onamanra rimón pei kéyoai.** The curuinse ants cut all the leaves off the lemon tree.⟩

*also* **onánbake** *n.* **ónaman** *also* **onánbaken** [from Shipibo *onán* wise + *báke* child] : adopted child –Used in a singular or collective sense. ⟨**Nokon onánra Rimán bokánke.** They took my adopted child to Lima.⟩
See **onán**
*v.t.* **onánhaa** *Konibo* **onánhaka** : to adopt as a son or daughter ⟨**Nokon wetsán bákera en onánhaa iki, bákeoma ixon.** I adopted my brother's son, because I have no children.⟩
*n.* **onánpapan** [from Shipibo *onán* wise + *pápa* father] : stepfather; *also* : one who acts in the role of father : second father : guardian

*v.t.* **ónana** 1 : to know : to understand –Used in the past-tense form but with present-tense meaning. ⟨**Enra ja jói onánke.** I understand that language.⟩ ⟨**Náwabaon paránkatitaironki moa jónibaon onánke.** The Shipibo know that the mestizos have been exploiting them for years.⟩ 2 : to know, to be acquainted with (a person) –Used in the past-tense form but with present-tense meaning. ⟨**Enra Rimán iká rókotoro onánke, nokon papán ea onámaa.** I know a doctor in Lima whom my father introduced me to, and he lives in Lima.⟩ 3 : to learn ⟨**Min taría jako-hakin onánwe.** Learn your task well.⟩

[from Shipibo *kírika* book + *onánti* to learn] : to learn to read and write : to become literate ⟨**Yósibaonribira ráma kírika ónanai.** Now adults, too, are learning to read and write.⟩ *syn.* áxeti; ninkáti

*adj. and n.* **onántiman** [from Shipibo *onán* wise + *-tima* impossible] *adj.* : hard to make out or discern : doubtful ⟨**Yaméra xóbo onántima iki.** It's hard to make out the house at night.⟩ *n.* : difficulty or uncertainty regarding something not clearly discerned

*n.* **onántitan** [from Shipibo *onán* wise + *títa* mother] : stepmother; *also* : one who acts in the role of mother : second mother ⟨**Nokon onántitanra ea ícha akínke.** My stepmother has helped me a lot.⟩

*n.* **onányanin** *Konibo* **onányaton** [from Shipibo *onán* adopted child + *-ya* with] : a healer who uses magic songs to cure ⟨**Onánya jónira béwai játo bénxoai.** The *onánya healer sings to cure the sick.⟩ *syn.* See under míriko
*n.* **onányatinin** [from Shipibo *onánya* healer + *-ti* instrument suf.] : magic ⟨**yobéti itan onányati kírikabo** books of sorcery and magic⟩

*v.t.* **ónaa** : to mend, to patch (e.g., cloth, a tarrafa (cast net), leather, a cañabrava (cane) wall, or a ball) ⟨**Sapáto ónakinra jonín jawen mekén xómoxen cháchike.** The man pricked his hand with the needle while mending shoes.⟩

*v.t.* **ónena** 1 : to draw the string of (a bow) to shoot an arrow ⟨**Papánra kanóti onénke jóno tsákanoxon.** Dad drew the bow with the arrow to shoot at the collared peccary.⟩ 2 : to unravel down the middle ⟨**Titánra chópa onénke.** Mom unraveled the cloth down the middle.⟩
*n.* **onín** : ayahuasca ⟨**Yobébaonronki óni xéaxon Riós óinai.** They say that the sorcerers see God when they drink ayahuasca.⟩ *syn.* See under áyawaska
*also* **ónibirsidada** *n.* **ónibirisitaran** *also* **ónibirsidadan** : university

[from Shipibo *ónibirisitara* university + *áti* to do] : to do university studies : to study at the university ⟨**Onibirisitaro átira nokon báke en Rimán ráanke.** I sent my son to Lima so he could study at the university.⟩

*adj. and n.* **ónisin** *adj.* 1 : sad : melancholy : pensive 2 : evoking nostalgia : nostalgic ⟨**Senényoin jawen rárionin noa Sankénbea béwaitian ninkámaara onís íke.** When Senényoi had us listen to the Shipibo singer Sankénbea on the recorder, it seemed nostalgic.⟩ *n.* : sadness : melancholy
*n.* **onísamistonin** [from Shipibo *onísti* to feel sorrow + *-mis* one who always does (the indicated action)] : a merciful, compassionate person

*v.t.* **onísaa** *Konibo* **onísaka** : to feel compassion for : to have pity or sympathy for : to mourn for ⟨**Enra nato jóni onísake, wétsabaon jakómareskanaitian.** I felt sorry for this man because others kept mistreating him.⟩

*v.i.* **ónisa** 1 : to be sad : to feel sorrow ⟨**Nato aínbora ónisai, jawen béne sontáro káketian.** This woman is sad because her husband went off to military service.⟩ 2 : to become sad ⟨**Yobénoxon ónanai jónira masá méeti ónisai, átipanyamax.** The sorcerer's apprentice becomes sad because he has had to go without food for a long time, and still he cannot become a sorcerer.⟩ *syn.* ONISTI, MASA SHINANTI both have the sense of "to feel sorrow", but ONISTI implies a sorrow one feels for oneself, whereas with the phrase MASA SHINANTI the sorrow is felt for another person.

*adj.* **ónitsapishokon** *Konibo* **ónitsapishokotonin** [from Shipibo *ónitsapiti,* *ónitsapi-* distressed + *-shoco*, diminutive suf.] : poor : unfortunate : deserving of compassion ⟨**Jóni ónitsapishokora paénketian jenén réteke.** A poor man drowned while drunk.⟩ *syn.* jawékiaoma

*v.i.* **ónitsapita** : to suffer : to be hurt : to find oneself or be in a pitiful situation ⟨**Tapán rásiketianra jónibo ónitsapike.** When the raft fell apart, those steering it found themselves in a pitiful situation.⟩ *syn.* masá téneti

*v.i.* **ónitsaa** 1 : to move restlessly from side to side : to thrash about ⟨**Berón chéxaara nokon títa ónitsai.** My mother tosses from side to side because she has an eye ache.⟩ 2 : to become distressed or uneasy : to become anxious ⟨**Wánokasainbi jawen titán ímakashamaara nato bákeranon ónitsake.** This young man became anxious because he wanted to marry and his mother wouldn't allow it.⟩ 3 : to become desperate : to thrash about in danger ⟨**Yómetsoai mérakanara nato jóni ónitsake.** This man became desperate because he was seen at the very moment he was stealing.⟩
*adj.* **ónkiman** : slant-eyed ⟨**Nato jónira, béro onkín íketian *Chino* yóikanai.** This man is called "Chino" because his eyes are slanted.⟩

*v.t.* **onkínhaa** *Konibo* **onkínhaka** : to narrow (the eyes) : to make slant-eyed ⟨**Jawen béro onkínhaketianra nato báke bénche shinánkanke.** When this child narrowed his eyes, everyone took him for blind.⟩
*v.i.* **ónkina** : to half-close (the eyes) ⟨**Nato jonín bérora onkínke.** The man's eyes half-closed.⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *óno* there] : way over there, far off ⟨**Onnora kíni wíso sawéke.** Way over there something black can be made out: it is the entrance to a cave.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *o-* far + *-no*, locative part.] : there : over there –Also used with the suffixes *-a* "from" and *-ax* "from" in the forms *ónoa* "from there" and *ónoax* "from there". ⟨**Onoronki piróta ákaibo tsinkíke, jawékiai.** They say the soccer players have gathered over there to have a picnic.⟩ ⟨**Jara ónoa iki.** He is from there.⟩ ⟨**Onoax joxbónra nato báke ochítinin natéxke.** This boy was bitten by a dog while coming from over there.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5 *syn.* jaín

*adj.* **ónoman** 1 : cunning : sly –Used regarding animals. ⟨**Sapénra onón iki, non rekénbaon rétepaoni ikax.** The manatee is sly because it has been hunted by our ancestors since ancient times.⟩ 2 : easily startled : skittish ⟨**Nato manxán ríki kikínbires onónhira.** This heron is really skittish.⟩
*v.t.* **onónhaa** *Konibo* **onónhaka** : to startle (an animal); to scare off (an animal) ⟨**Kónxaman téetaibaonra moa yáwabo onónhakanke.** The loggers scared off the white-lipped peccaries.⟩
*v.i.* **ónona** 1 : to become skittish 2 : to become wild ⟨**Nato jóno inara moa onónke, jawen ibón pímayamaa.** This baby collared peccary has gone wild because its owner didn't feed it.⟩

*adj.* **ónsakan** : dreadful (e.g., because of great danger) ⟨**Wísoinora kikínbires onsá iki jóni píai ikax.** The yanapuma (black jaguar) is dreadful because it is an animal that attacks people.⟩ ⟨**Panáichonkora samán onsá iki, jénetian.** During the rainy season there is a dreadful whirlpool near Panaillo.⟩
*v.t.* **onsáa** *Konibo* **onsáaka** : to horrify : to frighten ⟨**Yoshínxataman onsáara báke sión ikax jabáke.** The child ran off screaming because a clown demon frightened him.⟩ *syn.* ráteti

*v.i.* **ónsatana** : to be afraid or ashamed of (e.g., speaking to someone or singing) ⟨**Min pápara en pácha waránka sóro yokáti ónsatanai; eara méniyamabirati iki.** I'm embarrassed to ask your dad for a hundred soles, because he probably won't give it to me.⟩ ⟨**Nato jónira béwati ónsatani sákiikai.** This man trembles before singing because he is embarrassed.⟩
*v.i.* **ónsata** : to become fierce or dreadful ⟨**Sináma ikénbi ríshkikanara nato íno iná moa onsáke.** This baby *jaguar was tame, but became fierce and dangerous because it was hit very hard.⟩
See under **sapén**
*verbal suf.* **-oot** : oneself or themselves ⟨**Jara máshkorootai.** He cuts his own hair.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.6
*n.* **Opín** –Used as a feminine name.
*n.* **orán** [from Spanish] : hour ⟨**Westíora netén bóai rabé chónka chósko óra.** A day has twenty-four hours.⟩
*n.* **óra akaiton** [from Spanish *hora* + Shipibo *ákai*, part. of *áti* to do] : clock face ⟨**óra akai, minóto akai** hour hand, minute hand⟩
*also* **organisasion** *n.* **órakanisasioman** *also* **organisasioman** : organization
See under **chópa**
*n.* **oránshinin** : soda pop ⟨**Rabé botíria oránshininra ea kéenai.** I want two bottles of soda pop.⟩ *syn.* See under **kásiosa**

*v.t.* **órana** [from Spanish *orar* "to pray", *ora-* + *-n*, verbal derivational suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to pray ⟨**En oránketianra nokon aínbobake ísinai moa bénxoke.** When I prayed, my sick daughter got well.⟩ *syn.* ORANTI, RISANTI both refer to the act of directing words to God, but correspond to the meanings of "orar" (to pray spontaneously) and "rezar" (to recite/read a prayer) in Spanish, with their distinct implications of a spontaneous prayer on one hand and a memorized or read prayer on the other.
*n.* **órasionman** [from Spanish] : prayer
See **órakanisasion**

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *o-*, element found in, e.g., *óke* on this side + *-ri* toward] *adv.* : in a direction indicated by words or by pointing –Also used with the suffix *-ax* in the form *óriax* "in an indicated direction". ⟨**Noara óri katánke nokon títaiba, jan kénaibata óini.** We went that way to see my mother because she had called for us the other day.⟩ ⟨**Yóirakanke —Oriaxonki koáratia jóai; bákeranonbo jabánon yóikanwe.** They said: —A pair of soldiers is coming that way to recruit young men; tell all the young men to flee.⟩ *postp.* : toward; *specif.* : in the direction indicated by upriver or downriver –Also used with the suffix *-keax* in the form *orikeax* "from a specific direction". ⟨**Motóro réokootaitianra ea máshiori chorónke.** When the *motor capsized, I jumped toward the beach.⟩ ⟨**Máshiorikeaxa níwe kóshi pakéke; rámara noa mashi bépotai.** A strong wind came from the beach, and now sand is getting into our eyes.⟩
*also* **Olíbia** *n.* **Oríbian** *also* **Olíbian** [from Spanish *Olivia*] –Used as a feminine name.
*n.* **orón** [from Spanish] : gold *syn.* See under *kóri*
*n.* **Orón** [from Spanish *or,* element of *Orfilia*] –Used as a feminine name.
*also* **órno** *n.* **órononin** *also* **órnonin** [from Spanish] : oven
*n.* **Orópanin** [from Spanish *Europa*] : Europe
*n.* **Oropampan** [from Spanish] : the Urubamba River

*v.t.* **óroa** : to cultivate : to clear, to clean ⟨**Píshta nete sénenaitianra non jéma órokanke.** We cleaned the yards because the day of the festival is approaching.⟩ ⟨**Moa mái oró iketianra jákoni átsabo xóxoai.** When the land is well cultivated, the crops grow well.⟩ ⟨**Nato kámpo oró ikáinxonra bákebaon piróta ákai.** In this cleared field, which is for sports, the children are playing soccer.⟩
[from Shipibo *jéma* village + *óroti* to cultivate, to clean] : to do communal public work required of everyone in the community

[from Shipibo *kéni* beard + *óroti* to cultivate, to clean] : to shave ⟨**Kéni órokinra en kexá xáteke.** While I was shaving, I cut my lip.⟩ ⟨**Natón kéni óroa iwanketianra bákeranon shinánkeankanke.** If he had been clean-shaven, they would have taken him for a young man.⟩ ⟨**Nokon kéni oró iketianra ea osánkanti iki.** If they see that I've shaved, they will laugh at me.⟩
*v.i.* **ósameeta** : to laugh at oneself ⟨**Ispíkonin jawen bémanan óinaxa aínbo ósameeke.** A woman saw her face in a mirror and laughed at herself.⟩
*n.* **ósaman** : laughter ⟨**Nato aínbaon osán riki jakómayoraisi.** That woman's laughter is unpleasant.⟩

[from Shipibo *osán* laughter + *téneti* to hold back] 1 : to hold back one's laughter ⟨**Iskoiranko kírika ákai bákebaonra osán ténekanai.** At school, the students hold back their laughter.⟩ 2 : to smile ⟨**Páenabo yóyo ikaitianra en osán téneke.** I kept smiling at the way the drunks talked.⟩
*v.t.* **ósana** : to laugh at ⟨**Nato yoshínbake yóyo ikaitian osánkinra en píamake.** I was laughing so hard at the way a stutterer talked that I couldn't even eat.⟩
*adj.* **oshín** : thin ⟨**Nato pan akai jonínra páanhakin óshiora ákai.** When this baker makes bread, he makes it thin.⟩ *syn.* See under áko
*v.i.* **óshia** : to become thin : to grow skinny ⟨**Nokon wétsara moa óshike, píchika óxe ísinax.** My brother has grown thin because he was sick for five months.⟩ *syn.* ákoti; náxpeti
*n.* **Oshkiman** [from Spanish *osk*, element of *Oskar* + *in*, unidentified element] –Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **óshoman** : taperiba (a fruit tree)

*adj.* **óshtakan** : dirty –Used mostly among speakers of the Shetebo dialect. ⟨**Bakén mentsísa oshtáma iki.** The student's fingernails don't look dirty.⟩ *syn.* OSHTA, KERAS, TARO can all be translated as "dirty". OSHTA and TARO are translated without distinction, but OSHTA, unlike TARO, is used by those of the Shetebo group. KERAS implies filth so extreme that it is disgusting.
*also* **Oshtá** *n.* [from Spanish *Eustasio*] –Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **óskooskon** [from Shipibo *óskoosko,* imitative of its call] : a species of bird similar to the wild dove but grayish in color, with a long tail, and tameable

*n.* **osón** [from Spanish] : bear ⟨**Osora áni yóina iki. Jénetianra manánkini meran jíkiax óxai. Jáinoax jíwibo péchokoketiampari bésoax píkotai, jáwekiaribinox.** The bear is a large animal. In the *rainy season it goes into a cave and sleeps there. When the trees start budding again, it wakes up and comes out to eat again.⟩

*v.t.* **ósona** : to tuck in among other things or in a corner : to fit in, to arrange ⟨**Nónti jawékibo bócho ikénbira nokon píabo en jaín osónke.** Even though the canoe was loaded with things, I fit my arrows in among them.⟩

*n.* **osóntinin** [from Shipibo *osónti,* oson– to insert between + *–ti* instrument suf.] : a kind of wooden knife used to insert between threads in order to separate them and have room to pass the shuttle through

*v.i.* **ósota** 1 : to enter or be (many) in a tight space 2 : to mix in (a person or animal) with a group of similar ones ⟨**Yósibo xaranra nato báke yoítima osóke.** This wicked boy mixed himself in at a gathering of adults.⟩
*n.* **ospítaron** [from Spanish] : hospital *syn.* ráoxobo
*n.* **Ostákian** [from Spanish *Eustakia*] –Used as a feminine name.

*v.i.* **óstameeta** : to squeeze into a narrow or dense place until stuck ⟨**Non rekénboronki móxa meran óstameetax mawápaonike yóshiman jato biái shínani.** They say our ancestors used to die from squeezing into and getting stuck in thorny thickets, because they thought demons were catching them.⟩

*v.t.* **óstana** 1 : to tuck in (e.g., a needle) at the side of something ⟨**Titán xomóx chopán óstanatonra báke chachíke.** The boy pricked himself with the needle that his mother had tucked into the dress.⟩ 2 : to insert between two things to wedge them tight

*n.* **otán** 1 : shadow : the shadowy part cast by a physical body ⟨**Non ótaronki roámis iki.** They say our shadow is a bad omen: a sign of death.⟩ 2 : the gloom or darkness of a cloudy, overcast day ⟨**Oi békasira, óta kawánkatitai.** When it's about to rain, it just turns gloomy.⟩ 3 : small shelter (tambo) *syn.* See under **péota** *syn.* beí; wéa
*v.t.* **ótaaka** : to shade ⟨**Naíkoin bexónra noa ótaake.** The clouds passed by and shaded us.⟩
*v.i.* **ótaa** *Konibo* **ótaaka** : to become shaded/dimmed ⟨**Bári xánayorara moa ótake.** The sun that was hot has become dimmed.⟩
*v.t.* **ótena** : to put a support on ⟨**Enra xóbo oténke niwén póxanaketian.** I put a support on the house so the wind wouldn't knock it down.⟩
*also* **ótexemeeti** *v.i.* **ótexeeta** *also* **ótexemeeta** : to pinch oneself ⟨**Nato báke yóitimara ótexemeeke.** This spoiled child pinched himself.⟩
*v.t.* **ótexa** : to pinch ⟨**Nokon wetsán bakénra nokon báke otéxke.** My nephew pinched my son.⟩
*also* **otéri** *n.* **otírinin** *also* **otérinin** [from Spanish] : hotel : hostel
*n.* : a species of small gourd shaped with a long neck that serves as a handle, used to make rattles
*n.* **ótokoron** : utucuro
*n.* **ótoronkon** [from Spanish] : jaguar (otorongo) *syn.* chabáino

*v.t.* **ótsiaa** *Konibo* **ótsiaka** 1 : to wrinkle or mark the skin of ⟨**Titánra jawen bakén ponyán néxaxon ótsiake.** Mom tied her child's arm and marked his skin.⟩ ⟨**Nokon pápashokon táera ótsi iki, ménota ikax.** My grandfather's foot is wrinkled because it got burned.⟩ 2 : to deflate ⟨**Nato bísikirita chántara en ótsiaama iki; nato jonínra áke.** I didn't deflate this bicycle's tire; this man did it.⟩ *syn.* shépaati

*v.i.* **ótsia** 1 : to become wrinkled (skin) ⟨**Matsín akára nokon póko ótsike.** Because of the cold, the skin of my belly has wrinkled.⟩ 2 : to deflate ⟨**Piróta ótsikinra báke ráteke.** The child got scared when the ball deflated.⟩ *syn.* shépati

*n. and adj.* **óxakan** *n.* 1 : sleep ⟨**Oxá téneti átipanyamaaxa báke jawen bachín moa jíkike.** The child lay down because he couldn't resist sleep any longer.⟩ ⟨**Pápashokora óxakan binsínke.** Grandfather was overcome by sleep.⟩ 2 : a daytime period of a specific activity (e.g., of making a trip or a job) ⟨**Kímisha oxaábicho riki Máioshiainoax Kakónko nokóti.** It takes only three days of travel, traveling only by day, to get from Pucallpa to Caco.⟩ *adj.* : asleep ⟨**Nato bákeshoko oxa ráteyamakanwe.** Don't wake this baby who is asleep.⟩
[from Shipibo *oxá* sleep + *téneti* to hold back] : to fight off sleep : to stay awake

[from Shipibo *oxá téneti* + *-yama* not] : to be unable to fight off sleep : to be very sleepy *syn.* OSHA TENEYAMATI, OSHAKASTI can both be translated as "to be sleepy", but OSHA TENEYAMATI implies an excessive sleepiness that is felt more intensely.

*v.i.* **óxakasa** [from Shipibo *óxati*, *oxa-* to sleep + *-kas* to want] : to be sleepy : to want to sleep ⟨**Eara píibi óxakaske nokon yorán ea chéxai kopí.** While I was eating, I felt sleepy because my body ached.⟩
*v.t.* **óxana** [from Shipibo *óxati* to sleep + *-n*, verbal derivational suf.] : to put to sleep ⟨**Titánra nokon wétsa oxánke.** My mother put my little brother to sleep.⟩
See under **oxá**
See under **oxá**
*v.i.* **óxaa** : to sleep ⟨**Oxaketíanra nokon wétsa wapóronin pótake.** My brother fell asleep and the boat left him behind.⟩

*also* **—be óxai** [from Shipibo *betan*, *-be* with + *óxai*, part. of *óxati* to sleep] : wife of (a specific man) —Used with the complement *betan* or the truncated form *-be*. ⟨**Nátora jabé óxai iki.** This is his wife.⟩
*n.* **óxatinin** [from Shipibo *óxati*, *oxa-* to sleep + *-ti* with which] : bedroom
*n.* **oxén** 1 : moon ⟨**Naíkoimanra óxe mápoke.** The clouds covered the moon.⟩ 2 : month ⟨**Nokon pápa jótira moa óxe senénke.** The month is already complete and dad will come.⟩

*also* **óxe toróti** [from Shipibo *óxe* moon + *rakáti* to be lying down, or *toróti* to become round] : for there to be a new moon ⟨**Oxe rakáketianra pápashoko tsanítsanitai.** When there is a new moon, grandfather does his exercises.⟩ ⟨**Oxe toróketianra noa yamébi tsíniai.** When there is a full moon, we play until nighttime.⟩
See under **bína**
See under **óxe**

*adj.* **óxnakan** 1 : bluish black ⟨**Papán kotónra oxná iki.** Dad's shirt is bluish black.⟩ 2 : threadbare ⟨**Nato chópara oxnáoxnatani iki páyoti.** This cloth is very threadbare because it's already old.⟩
*adj.* **oxná pánshiman** [from Shipibo *bluish blakk* + *panshín* yellow] : orange

*n.* **óxnekan** [from Shipibo *óxe* moon + *ne* elem. of *néte* day] 1 : light of the full moon ⟨**Oxné íketianra noa yamébi kakáshi-** **nai.** When there is full moonlight, we travel all night.⟩ 2 : light of dawn ⟨**Moa néte oxné iketianra ea óxakashamai.** I don't want to sleep anymore because it's already dawning.⟩ ⟨**Moa oxné iketianra átapa kéotai.** When the day breaks, the rooster crows.⟩
*v.i.* **oxnéaa** *Konibo* **oxneaka** : for the moon to shine on ⟨**Oxénra nato jéne oxnéake.** The moon was shining on this water.⟩

*v.i.* **óxneta** 1 : for the moon to shine during the full moon ⟨**Bakísha jakón íkai; moara oxnéke.** Tomorrow the weather will be good, because the full moon has been shining brightly the whole time.⟩ 2 : for the day to break

*v.i.* **oyáika** [from Shipibo *oyá*, imitative of the sound + *-iti* to do] : to retch ⟨**Eara oyáike, jakóma písi xéteax.** I retched when I smelled something foul.⟩ *syn.* OYAITI, KINANKASTI both include the sense of "feeling nauseous," but OYAITI can imply more of a sudden, violent sensation.
*v.i.* **óyokaata** : to suck on one’s own skin to cure oneself ⟨**Yobé jonira janbíx óyokaatai.** The shaman sucks his skin to cure himself.⟩

*v.t.* **óyoa** 1 : to suck (something edible) ⟨**Nato aínbora chopíti óyokasai.** This woman wants to suck on a lollipop.⟩ 2 : to suck on the skin to cure (someone) ⟨**Yóbekan óyoa bákera moa mawáke.** The child whose skin the shaman sucked has already died.⟩
*n.* Used as the name of the letter *p* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*modifying pref.* 1 : on the ear : in the ear ⟨**patéti** to peck on the ear of⟩ ⟨**pawéxti** to scratch on the ear of⟩ 2 : by the handle : by the grip ⟨**panéxti** to tie by the handles⟩ 3 : on both sides ⟨**paráxiti** to stomp noisily⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.4
*n.* **páaman** [from Spanish] : bread ⟨**Páan márowe non pinón.** Buy bread for us to eat.⟩ ⟨**Ochítininra páan píke bórosanimea.** The dog ate the bread from the bag.⟩
*v.t.* **páanhaa** *Konibo* **páanhaka** : to make bread ⟨**Kímisha sáko arína bexónra nokon papán páanhaa iki.** My dad brought three sacks of flour and made bread.⟩
*adj.* **pabén** : deaf ⟨**Nato pábe jónira yóyoiamai.** This deaf man doesn't speak either.⟩
*v.t.* **pábeaa** *Konibo* **pábeaka** : to deafen ⟨**Abion rónikaitonra ea pábeake.** The roar of the airplane deafened me.⟩
*v.i.* **pábea** : to become deaf ⟨**Jéne pabíkinin wéitaxa ea pábeke.** I became deaf because water got into my ear.⟩

*n.* **pabíkinin** : ear ⟨**Pabíkia ixonbira min ninkáyamai —akin titán aká iki.** Her mom told her: —Even though you have ears, you don't pay attention.⟩ ⟨**Pabíki áni yoshínronki jonín páxtenike.** They say that long ago a big-eared demon was made ear-less by a man.⟩ ⟨**Eara pabíkinin chéxai.** My ear hurts.⟩

*n.* **páboronin** 1 : a bend in the river where the current flows upstream, forming in various ways a backwater, a whirlpool, or a deep pool ⟨**Yamébi joíra ea páboronimeax réokooke.** Traveling at night, I capsized at the river bend where there is a whirlpool.⟩ ⟨**Páborotibironki jenényoshinbaon jéma jáke.** They say that in every river bend with a backwater there is a village of yacurunas (water spirits).⟩ 2 : cove : inlet
*adj.* **pachán** [from Quechua *páchak* hundred] : hundred ⟨**Pácha kíroya porótora en ríkaton máromake.** I sold a hundred kilos of beans to the trader.⟩ ⟨**rabé pácha** two thousand⟩
*n.* **páchexetin** [from Shipibo *pa-* in the ear + *chexe*, modified elem. of *chéxati*, *chexa-* to hurt + *-ti* with which] : a species of tree from which a remedy for earache is extracted
*adj.* **pachín** : soft by nature or after soaking ⟨**Páan páchi píketianra ea pórokan chéxai.** I have a stomachache because I ate soaked, soft bread.⟩ *syn.* báka
*v.t.* **páchiaa** *Konibo* **páchiaka** : to soften ⟨**Enra moa binón páchiake.** I have already softened the aguaje (a palm fruit).⟩ *syn.* bákaati
See under **móe**
*v.i.* **páchia** : to become soft ⟨**Jawen páan páchiketianra nokon wétsa namánshoko mároke.** When the breads became soft, my brother sold them at a reduced price.⟩
*n.* **pachón** : remocaspi (a type of tree used for making oars) ⟨**Nokon wetsán pácho wíntiaara tóeke.** The remocaspi-wood oar my brother made broke.⟩

*modifying suf.* : always ⟨**Eapachora kénakanai; rámabichora ea áyamakanke.** They always call me; but this time they didn't.⟩ ⟨**Empachora éseai; jabira ea jói ninkáxonyamai.** I'm always the one who advises him, but he doesn't listen to me.⟩ ⟨**Nato jóni betanra en mia kírika ráanxompachoai.** This is the man through whom I always send you letters.⟩ *syn.* jatíbitian
*n.* **páchokin** : a species of mollusk

*v.t.* **páchoa** : to dent ⟨**Nokon titán yámikentira papán paénxon páchoke.** Dad, while drunk, dented mom's aluminum pot.⟩ ⟨**Ochítininra nokon tasá páchoke.** The dog dented my basket.⟩ ⟨**Nato ráto pachora ea kéenyamai.** I don't like this dented plate.⟩

*v.i.* **páchota** 1 : to become dented ⟨**Moa básiora ikáxa nato yámikenti pachóke.** This aluminum pot got dented because it was already old.⟩ 2 : to bend over : to curve ⟨**Níwe pakéketianra nato jíwi pachóke.** The tree bent over when the wind suddenly came up.⟩ *syn.* mótsiti

*adj. and n.* **paén** *adj.* : sour ⟨**Nato aínbaonra paránxon noa rimón páe máromake.** This woman deceived us by selling us sour lemons.⟩ *n.* 1 : fermented thing ⟨**Páe xéamaaronki báke jánshoai.** They say that giving something fermented to a baby causes patco (an illness).⟩ 2 : strongly alcoholic liquor ⟨**Páe xéaaxbira nato jóni paényamai.** This man doesn't get drunk despite drinking strong liquor.⟩

*v.t.* **páeaa** *Konibo* **páeaka** 1 : to ferment ⟨**Xéati páeanoxonra xáwi jeneya méskokanai. To make the drink ferment, they mix in cane juice.⟩ 2 : to turn or make sour or acidic ⟨**Xéati páeaxa yómerai bokánke.** After making the drink sour, they went to look for mitayo (game meat) for the fishing trip.⟩ ⟨**Oránxira bónaya méskoxon páeakanke.** By mixing honey with soda, they made it sour.⟩ ⟨**Bári xananra nato naránxa páeake.** The heat of the sun made this orange sour.⟩

*v.i.* **páena** [from Shipibo *páe, paén* sour + *-ti* inf. suf.] 1 : to get drunk ⟨**Paénketianra nato jóni káraboso meran níakanke.** This man was put in a jail cell for getting drunk.⟩ 2 : to become dizzy (a person) ⟨**Motóro koin xéteaxa ea paénke.** I got dizzy when I inhaled the gas leaking from the motor.⟩ 3 : to get "dizzy" (a fish that comes up to the water's surface) ⟨**Pítibo paénkenbira en cháchiamake, píaoma ixon.** The fish were "dizzy," but I didn't spear them because I had no arrow.⟩

*n.* **páerinin** [from Quechua *pagri*; and this from Spanish *padre*] 1 : friar ⟨**Non ánibo ráeakaskinronki páeribaon jato móro ménipaonike.** They say that friars gave beads to our ancestors, wanting to tame them.⟩ 2 : priest : parson : parish priest
See under **rimón**

*n.* **páerinin yónotinin** [from Shipibo *páeri* priest + *yónoti, yónotinin* command] : sacristan *syn.* PAERININ YONOTI, SAKIRISTANO both can be translated as "sacristan" with no difference at all. PAERININ YONOTI, the native word, is perhaps better known.
See under **paránta**

*v.i.* **páea** 1 : to ferment ⟨**Chíchaakana moa páeketianra ea joá iki.** I came when the chicha they had prepared was already fermented.⟩ 2 : to become sour ⟨**Nato xéatira moa páeke.** This drink has turned sour.⟩ 3 : to rise (e.g., bread)
*v.i.* **paíkia** [from Shipibo *pa-* in the ear + *jikiti* to enter] : to enter the ear
*n.* **páikonin** [from Spanish] : paico (an herb, epazote)

*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *-pari, -pai* still + *-non* for] : would that : I hope that —Used regarding a specific expected event. —Used added to the verb root plus *riqui* "is". ⟨**Nokon pápara en píti kénake; jópainon riki.** I invited my dad to eat; I hope he comes.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.8
*n.* **páiran** [from Spanish] : large pan (paila) ⟨**Páiraninra pátoronin áwinin kóchi xeni xéeaibake.** Yesterday the boss's wife fried pork in a large pan to make lard.⟩

*adj.* **paísmanin** : bland : tasteless (e.g., of salt or sugar) —Used regarding liquids. ⟨**Ompáxa paísma iki; jákopira non xéayamai.** Plain water is tasteless, and that's why we don't drink it.⟩ ⟨**Eara xéati paísma xéakashamai.** I don't like to drink unsweetened drinks.⟩
*v.t.* **paísmaa** *Konibo* **paísmaaka** : to make (e.g., a drink) bland ⟨**Ompáx nechíxonra nokon áwinin jawen xéati paísmaake.** By adding water to it, my wife made her drink bland.⟩
*v.i.* **paísmaa** : to become bland ⟨**Nato xéati paísmaketianra non xéayamai.** We no longer drink this drink because it has become bland.⟩

*n.* **pájinanin** [from Spanish] : page ⟨**Nato pájinainra bákebaon jaton taría mérati** iqui. On this page the students will find their homework.⟩ *syn.* PAJINA, PEI both can be translated as "page," but PEI, the native word, is the more usual and established one.
*n.* **pakán** : paca cane ⟨**Koshóshkaronki páka piaki ráketai.** They say that river dolphins are afraid of paca-cane arrows.⟩
See under **kawín**
See under **ronín**
See under **shípi**

*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *páketi, pake-* to drop] : one after another in a distributive manner —Used added to a transitive action verb. ⟨**Yómetsoninra jato koríki ménipakeke.** The thief distributed the money to his companions.⟩

*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo *pakéti*, *paket-* to fall] **-paket** : downward; *specif.* : downstream —Used added to the intransitive verb. —Used in the form *-paque* before a consonant and in the form *-paquet* before a vowel. ⟨**Rabé tapánra moa toxbápakeke baikanbea.** Two rafts floated downstream because of the current.⟩ ⟨**Jáinoaxa konxán toxbáta iki.** Then the cedar logs floated.⟩
*v.t.* **pakémaa** [from Shipibo *pakéti* + *ma-* to cause] : to take out : to remove : to subtract ⟨**31-nkonia non 8 pakémati ikai.** From 31 we subtract 8.⟩ *syn.* pikoti; siwínti; tsékati

*v.t.* **páketa** 1 : to drop : to let go of ⟨**Abioninra kírika pákeke.** The small plane dropped a letter.⟩ ⟨**En koríki páketa bikénbira, ea yómetsoa yóikanke.** When I picked up a coin that had fallen, they accused me of stealing it.⟩ 2 : to solve : to work out ⟨**Náto múltiplikasionbo pákewe.** Solve these multiplication problems.⟩ *syn.* píshati

*v.i.* **páketa** 1 : to fall (a person) ⟨**Jíwi bochikiaxa ea pakéke.** I fell from the top of a tree.⟩ 2 : to equal : to result in —Used in multiplications and divisions. ⟨**4 akín 2 páketai 8.** 4 times 2 equals 8.⟩ ⟨**21 íketian 3 tsamá akára páketai 7.** 21 divided by 3 equals 7.⟩
[from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *pakéti* to fall] : to land on water (of an aircraft) ⟨**Jenén páketaitibira ábion másatai.** Every time the small plane lands on water, it breaks down.⟩
[from Shipibo *mái, maín* land + *pakéti* to fall] : to land (an aircraft) ⟨**Maín páketaxa ábion kasórina keyóke.** The plane ran out of gasoline as it was landing.⟩

[from Shipibo *táe* foot + *pakéti* to fall] : to come out (to a specific measurement) in feet ⟨**En xóno xatebo tóponara chónka waránka táe pákeke.** The lupuna (a large tree) logs I measured came out to ten thousand board feet.⟩ *syn.* See under **báneti** and **máanti**
*n.* **pákexen** [from Shipibo *pa-* of the ear + *kexá* song] : piece ⟨**Konxán pakexenra ea yóshiman tsákake.** A demon deliberately hit me with a piece of cedar.⟩
*v.i.* **pákexeeta** : to take out a piece for oneself ⟨**Jóno námira pákexeeke.** A piece of collared peccary meat was taken out.⟩
*v.t.* **pákexa** : to take out a piece of (something) ⟨**Ochítininra námi pakéxke.** The dog took out a piece of meat.⟩
*v.i.* **pákina** : to faint ⟨**Jónobake píamawe, pakínti riki.** Don't eat baby collared peccary; you might faint.⟩
*n.* **pákopakon** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : a species of small toad
*n.* **pamán** : a species of tree
[from Shipibo *íno* jaguar + *méken* paw + *páma* species of tree] : a species of tree
[from Shipibo *pítso, pitsón* pihuicho (a parakeet) + *páma* species of tree] : a species of tree
*v.i.* **pámeweaa** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + (by metathesis) *wémeti* to hook] : to hook onto the ear of ⟨**Enra jóni míshkitinin pámeweke.** I hooked the man's ear with a fishhook.⟩

*verbal suf.* —Used added to the end of the verb with the sense of "to be able to" or "to have permission". —Used in the sentence as a marker of interrogative mood. ⟨**¿Nato cháxo nami pipán?** May I eat this deer meat?⟩ ⟨**¿Earibi kapan?** Can I go too?⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.2.5
*n.* **pánakan** 1 : a curtain made of matting, palm leaves, or banana leaves 2 : tapaje (a woven fish barrier)
*v.i.* **pánakaata** : to cover oneself with something flat that is hung up
*n.* **pánaa** : huasaí (the açaí palm)
See under **yoshín**

*v.t.* **pánaa** 1 : to cover (e.g., a wall, window, door, hole, cave, or path) ⟨**Káshibobaon bái pánaketianra non mérayamake.** We couldn't find the path because the cashibo had covered it.⟩ 2 : to protect (e.g., with an outstretched arm)
*n.* **pánatinin** : a temporary fence

*adj.* **pánchakan** [from Shipibo *pa(n)-* of the ear + *cha-* elem. of *chákati* to crush] : flat ⟨**Nokon wétsara táe panchá ikax sontáro káyamai.** My brother won't go into the army because he has flat feet.⟩
*v.t.* **pancháa** *Konibo* **pancháaka** : to flatten ⟨**Titánra jawen kenchá pancháake.** Mom flattened her clay griddle.⟩ *syn.* sápati

*v.i.* **pánchata** 1 : to become flattened ⟨**Nokon arós sakora pancháke, jaón péyakakana.** My sack of rice got flattened because someone sat on it.⟩ 2 : to become level ⟨**Oi béketianra mái mato pancháke.** The mound of earth became level when it rained.⟩

*v.t.* **pánexa** [from Shipibo *pa-* by the handles + *néxati* to tie] 1 : to tie by the handles ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen yámikenti panéxon ompáx béke.** A woman tied her aluminum pots by the handles and carried water in them.⟩ 2 : to tie by the corners

*n.* **panín** : huicungo (a spiny palm) ⟨**xebónra páni jisáribi iki, ikaxbi móxaomares.** The xebón is very similar to the huicungo, except it has no spines.⟩ ⟨**Páni bero píaitianra en jóno réteke, tóoatin.** I killed a collared peccary with my shotgun when it was eating huicungo seeds.⟩ ⟨**Moátlanronki páni bimi xéatiapaokanike.** They say that long ago people used to make a drink from huicungo fruit.⟩
See under **ípo**
*v.t.* **pánina** : to hang : to suspend ⟨**Jonínra báke taén yatánshon panínke.** A man grabbed a boy by the foot and hung him up.⟩ *syn.* See under **weónti**
*v.i.* **pánia** : to be suspended : to hang : to be hanging or hung ⟨**Jíwi ponyamanra róo pánike.** The howler monkey is hanging among the branches of the tree.⟩
*n.* **pánixaman** : a species of palm whose leaves are used to make the small basket *sintán*
*n.* **panón** [from Old Shipibo *pano* person] : godson : goddaughter ⟨**Aínbora jawen páno sontáro káketian wíniwiniai.** The woman keeps crying because her godson went off to the army.⟩
*n.* **panón** : yangunturo (an armadillo) ⟨**Nokon pápashokora panón máikini meran bókeana iki.** The yangunturo almost pulled my grandfather into a hole.⟩
*n.* **panón** : a species of small aquatic toad with a granular back ⟨**Jénetianra panó kéotai.** The *panó* toad sings during the rainy season.⟩
*modifying suf.* : fast : quickly ⟨**Piménwepanon noa isbtón kaménon.** Eat quickly, so we can leave soon.⟩
See under **pempén**

*adj. and n.* **pánshiman** *adj.* : yellow : yellowish ⟨**Nato ísinai jonín yórara panshín iki.** The body of this sick man is yellowish.⟩ *n.* : a species of fish that is yellow and similar to the sábalo (a type of fish)
See under **átsa**
*v.t.* **panshínhaa** *Konibo* **pánshinhaka** : to make yellow ⟨**Titánra jawen kotón panshínhake.** Mom made her blouse yellow.⟩
See under **ípo**
See under **kári**
See under **koríki**
*v.t.* **panshímaa** : to ripen (something that turns yellowish) ⟨**Parántara en moa panshímake.** I have already ripened the plantains.⟩
See under **máxe**

*v.i.* **pánshina** 1 : to turn yellow ⟨**Nokon yórara panshínke.** My body turned yellow.⟩ 2 : to ripen or be ripe (beans, corn, rice, or other grain) ⟨**Moa arós pánshina ikénbira jawen ibón tsékayamai.** Even though the rice field is ripe, its owner doesn't harvest it.⟩ ⟨**Poróto non xóo tsékaabira moa panshínke.** Even though we harvested the beans while still green, they have already ripened.⟩
*n.* **pántionin** [from Spanish] : cemetery : graveyard ⟨**Pántioainoara en yoshín mérake** I saw a ghost in the cemetery.⟩
*n.* : handkerchief *syn.* bésoikiiti
*n.* **paón** : clam : churo (a freshwater snail) ⟨**Páo píkasira nokon báke wíniai.** My son cries because he wants to eat churos.⟩

*modifying suf.* —Used added to the verb root followed by *-ni* to indicate the imperfect tense of the remote past. ⟨**Non rekénbaonronki wáme píamapaonike.** They say our ancestors did not eat paiche (a large Amazonian fish).⟩ ⟨**Yoáshiko Inkaronki jónibo xaran jápaonike básibires.** They say that the Stingy Inca lived for a long time among many people.⟩
*n.* **páoman** : breadfruit

*v.t.* **páoa** : to put on (a sash) —Used as a complement in the sentence with *páoti* "sash to be worn on the chest". ⟨**Nokon epánra kómokomo páoti páoke.** My uncle put on his sash of rattling seeds.⟩ ⟨**Nokon páoti páoaxa jóni rároke.** The man was happy when he put on my sash.⟩ ⟨**Moa paó iketianra nokon páoti bóyamake.** They didn't take my sash because I was wearing it.⟩
*n.* **páotinin** : chest sash : bandolier ⟨**Nokon páotira ea jonín tésanaanke.** My sash was torn to pieces by a man.⟩
[from Shipibo *arokota*, unidentified elem. + *páoti* sash] : a species of sash
[from Shipibo *xéka* vanilla + *bími* fruit + *páoti* sash] : a sash made from the vanilla fruit
[from Shipibo *yóno* moena (a type of tree) + *páoti* sash] : a sash made of moena
*adj.* **paóyaton** [from Shipibo *páoti, pao-* to put on (a sash) + *-ya* with] : wearing (a sash) ⟨**Jawen páoti paóyara nato jóni ránsai.** This man is dancing wearing his sash.⟩

*n.* **papán** 1 : father : dad ⟨**Nokon pápara Ikítoain káke móro mároi.** My father went to Iquitos to buy beads.⟩ ⟨**Papán kókara sontáro iiti nokóke.** Dad's uncle has returned from military service.⟩ —Used in the vocative form *papá* addressed to the father, the maternal uncle, the husband of the maternal aunt, the paternal uncle, the stepfather, or the husband of the maternal aunt. 2 : male relatives of the first ascending generation —Used in the plural form *pápabo* to indicate the whole group of relatives of the parents' generation. 3 : Father : Lord —Used regarding God and with a capital initial *P*.

*honorific suf.* **-papan** [from Shipibo *pápa* father] —Used with the sense of "don" added to a male name as a sign of respect or esteem for a young relative or for any elder. ⟨**Jowé, Ompipapa.** Greetings, Don Humberto.⟩
See **pápayosi**

*adj.* **pápaoman** *Konibo* **pápaomatonin** [from Shipibo *pápa* father + *-oma* without] 1 : fatherless : one who has no father ⟨**Nato pápaoma aínbora bénokasai.** This fatherless woman wants to marry.⟩ 2 : illegitimate child ⟨**Nato bákera pápaoma iki.** This boy is an illegitimate child.⟩

*also* **pápaisi** *also* **yósipapa** *Konibo* **pápashoko** *n.* **pápayosin** *also* **pápaisin** *also* **pápaisin** *also* **yósipapan** *Konibo* **pápashokon** 1 : grandfather; also : grandfather's brother ⟨**Nokon pápashokoronki téetai jóni ikátiai.** They say my grandfather was a very hardworking man.⟩ ⟨**Papashokonra ea yóikatitai, moátian non rekénbo ípaonibo.** Grandfather used to tell me stories about our ancestors.⟩ 2 : grandfather of the husband or wife; also : brother of the grandfather of the husband or wife 3 : brother-in-law of the grandfather of the husband or wife 4 : male relatives of the second ascending generation —Used in the plural form *pápayosibo* or *pápashokobo* to indicate the whole group of elders of the grandparents' generation.
*v.i.* **pápekeeta** [from Shipibo *papéti* to make a hole in the ear of + *-kee,* refl. suf.] : to make a hole in one's own ear ⟨**Títara pápekeeke.** The mother made a hole in her own ear.⟩
*v.t.* **pápeta** : to make a hole in the ear of ⟨**Titánra jawen báke pápetai.** Mom makes a hole in her daughter's ear.⟩

*adj.* **papíatonin** [from Shipibo *pápiti, papi-* to carry on the back + *-ya* having] : carrying : having (something) loaded on the back ⟨**Nokon bórosa papíara ea kirínkonin jóto tsékake.** A foreigner took a photo of me while I was carrying my bag.⟩ [illustration, caption: *papía*]

*v.t.* **pápia** : to carry on the back ⟨**Eara paránta pápikasai, íwema íketian.** I want to carry the plantains on my back, because the bunch isn't heavy.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákeshokora káchiokeashbi pápia jóke.** This little boy came carried by someone from deep in the forest.⟩
*v.t.* **pápota** : to cover one's ears
See under **ínka**
*v.i.* **párameeta** : to deceive oneself —Used mostly among speakers of Konibo. ⟨**Nato jónira janbíx párameeke, jato paránkasibi.** This man deceived himself when he wanted to deceive others.⟩
*v.t.* **páranan aka** : to defend —Used with the complement placed before the verb and in the non-basic form. ⟨**Enra nokon bakén paranan iki.** I defended my son.⟩

*v.i.* **páranan ika** : to defend —Used in the sentence with a pronoun bearing the postpositional suffix *-on* or with a noun in the non-basic form as a preceding complement. ⟨**Pákayoshinronki nóa joni méeyamai noon párananres ikai.** They say that the demons of the paca (a rodent) do not harm us but rather defend us.⟩ ⟨**Nokon báke tímakanaitianra ea jaómparanan ike.** When they were punching my son, I defended him.⟩

*v.i.* **páranaa** 1 : to deny falsely ⟨**Wáirorobaon yóka-** **tara yómetso páranake.** This thief falsely denied it when the guards interrogated him.⟩ 2 : to falsely blame : to wrongly accuse —Used with the complement in the basic form with *-qui*, the suffix of opposition, placed after it. ⟨**Nato aínbora yómetsoaxa jawen tsábeki páranake.** After stealing, this woman blamed her sister-in-law.⟩

*n.* **parántanin** [from Quechua *palanda*, and this from Spanish] : plantain; *specif.* : a species of plantain whose fruit is eaten cooked ⟨**Rámara moa Máioshiain paránta kopíora iki.** Right now plantains are expensive in Pucallpa.⟩
[from Shipibo *áni* big + *paránta* plantain] : bellaco plantain (a large variety)
[from Shipibo *báwa* parrot + *paránta* plantain] : silk banana
[from Shipibo *bími* fruit + *paránta* plantain] : a species of plantain
[from Shipibo *kantsín* shapaja (a palm) + *paránta* plantain] : apple banana
[from Shipibo *kashímpo* cashimbo, and this from Spanish *kachimbo* (pipe) + *paránta* plantain] : a species of guineo (banana)
[from Shipibo *kóchi* pig + *jína* tail + *paránta* plantain] : a species of plantain with a curved shape
[from Shipibo *chi-* at the tip + *wero*, unidentified elem. + *paránta* plantain] : a species of bellaco plantain that is very thick, not very long, and with somewhat curved ends
[from Shipibo *chixó* diarrhea + *paránta* plantain] : a species of thick, medium-length guineo (banana)
[from Shipibo *isokoro* coro monkey + *paránta* plantain] : a species of dark red guineo (banana) of medium length
[from Shipibo *máno* mud + *paránta* plantain] : a species of plantain with brown-colored skin
[from Shipibo *náwashian*, náhuashian shihuango (a bird) + *paránta* plantain] : a species of plantain similar to the *mánoparanta* but with black stripes on the skin
*Konibo* **páerinin paranta** [from Shipibo *páeri* friar + *paránta* plantain] : a species of guineo plantain
*Konibo* **paránta joshin** [from Shipibo *paránta* plantain + *joshín* red] : ripe : ripe plantain ⟨**Parántaoshinra noa bokán kókonanke.** The manco (a monkey) ate our ripe plantain.⟩
[from Shipibo *paró* square + *paránta* plantain] : a species of plantain sometimes called "toad plantain"
[from Shipibo *Ríma* Lima + *paránta* plantain] : isleño (a plantain variety)
: a species of small, medium-thick guineo plantain similar to the silk banana but shorter
[from Shipibo *sapén* manatee, sea cow + *paránta* plantain] : a species of guineo plantain
[from Shipibo *xóiti*, *xoi-* to roast + *-ti* with which + *paránta* plantain] : a commonly cultivated species of plantain
[from Shipibo *yákati*, *yaka-* to sit + *paránta* plantain] : a species of small, compact-shaped guineo plantain
See under **paránta**
*v.t.* **párana** : to deceive ⟨**Nato yómetso jónira en paránke, ea yómetsoanaketian.** I deceived this thief so that he wouldn't rob me.⟩
*also* **plása** *n.* **párasanin** *also* **plásanin** [from Spanish] : plaza *syn.* jéma xabá
*also* **plástiko** *n. and adj.* **parástikon** *also* **plástikon** [from Spanish] : plastic ⟨**parástiko písha** plastic bag⟩
*n.* **páratain** [from Quechua *palta*] : avocado ⟨**Páratai piáronki chikíxti iki.** They say that eating avocado makes you lazy.⟩

*v.t.* **paráxaka** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + *rax*, imitative of the sound + *-ati* to do] : to stomp : to make a loud noise by stomping ⟨**Awakanronki sinákin mái paráxakai.** They say that the tapir stomps its feet loudly on the ground when it is angry.⟩
*v.i.* **paráxika** 1 : to make noise with one's feet while running 2 : to stamp or stomp noisily ⟨**Nato jónira kikínbiresi sínatax paráxikai.** When this man is very angry, he stomps noisily.⟩

*xet.* **–pai** *modifying suf.* : first —Used added to any part of the sentence except the verb. ⟨**Papámparira konxán xátekin péoa iki; jápekaora íchaxon ákana iki.** Dad was the first to cut the wood; afterward, many others did too.⟩ —Used with the sense of "immediately" or "without delay" with the verb, noun, or adverb. ⟨**Eara kaménpariai; moara básiora iki ea joá.** I'm leaving immediately, because I've already been here a long time.⟩ ⟨**Ayamapariwe.** Don't do it yet.⟩ ⟨**Rámapariresa en mia onánke.** I've only just now gotten to know you.⟩ ⟨**Jomémpariwe.** Come still.⟩ *syn.* bebón
*n.* **parón** : river ⟨**Nato báritiara páro áni jénetiake.** This year there was a strong flood in the river.⟩ ⟨**Parón káxa, nokon wétsa réokoooke.** My brother went to the river and capsized.⟩

*adj. and n.* **parón** *adj.* : square : square-shaped *n.* : squareness *syn.* PARO, PAROYA, RASENEN can all be translated "square"; but PARO and PARO-YA, as adjectives, are distinguished in function and meaning from RASENEN, which is a noun. RASENEN denotes the square thing or shape while PARO and PAROYA denote the quality of having that square shape.
*n.* [from Shipibo *páro* river + *máxka* upper part] : the headwaters of a river ⟨**Westíora motórora páromaxka ikáinoax réokooke.** A certain motor (boat) capsized at the headwaters of the river.⟩

*n.* **páronotin** : earring —Used mostly in the plural or collective sense with no difference in form. ⟨**Moátianronki bénboboribi páronotia ikátiai.** They say that long ago Shipibo men also used to wear earrings.⟩ ⟨**Rámatianra páronoti sáweyamatanikanai.** Nowadays they hardly wear earrings anymore.⟩
See under **paránta**
*n.* **párorebon** [from Shipibo *páro* river + *rébo* tip] : the headwaters of a river that originates in the highlands
See under **tóro**

*adj.* **paróyaton** *Konibo* **paróyanin** [from Shipibo *paró* squareness + *-ya* with] : square —Used regarding a solid object. ⟨**Nato jonín wíshpora paróya iki.** This man's shinbone is almost square.⟩ *syn.* See under **páro**
*also* **pásajero** *n.* **pásajiron** *also* **pásajeron** : passenger
See under **kankán**

*adj.* 1 : raw, uncooked ⟨**Pásha piásha nokon báke chíshotai.** My son has diarrhea from eating something raw.⟩ 2 : green, unseasoned —Used regarding trees and wood. ⟨**Papán xóno xáteara pásha ikax jíkike.** The lupuna log that Dad cut sank in the water because it was still green.⟩ *syn.* shépa; xoó
*n.* **pashpín** : the barb of an arrow
*n.* : a species of tree whose fruits are eaten by fish

*also* **páseanti** *v.i.* **pásiana** *also* **páseana** [from Shipibo *pasea*, elem. of *pasear* + *-n*, verbal derivation suf.] : to stroll : to visit ⟨—¿**Miaki jawén kéeni joá?** —**Eara jóke pásiani** —"What did you come here for?" —"I came to visit."⟩ *syn.* mérati
*v.i.* **pásketa** [from Shipibo *pa-* ear-shaped + *sekéti* to break] : to fall out (e.g., a tooth or ripe fruit) ⟨**Nato bakén xétara paskéke.** This child's molar fell out.⟩
*also* **páskoa** *n.* **páskoapishtan** *also* **páskoanin** [from Spanish *paskua* + Shipibo *pishta* feast; and this from Spanish *fiesta*] : Easter : Easter celebration
*adj.* **pásnakan** 1 : pale ⟨**Moa kímisha néte ísinaxa nato aínbaon kebí pasná iki.** This woman's lip pale because she was sick for three days.⟩ 2 : anemic : posheco *syn.* sháo

*v.i.* **pásnata** 1 : to turn pale : to become or be pale ⟨**Ichayora rimón kókoaxa nato xóntako pasnáke.** This young lady turned pale from sucking on so much lime.⟩ 2 : to become or be anemic ⟨**Ompax kobínhaama xéaira pápa pasnáke.** Dad is anemic from drinking unboiled water.⟩

*n.* **pastón** [from Spanish] : pasture, grass —Used in the sense of place or food. ⟨**Pastónkoniara wáka binán tékake.** In the pasture, the cow was stung by a wasp.⟩ ⟨**Pásto yámaketianra Xawányainoa wákabo mawáke.** For lack of pasture, Shahuaya's cattle died.⟩
*n.* **pastóronin** *also* **pastórnin** [from Spanish] : shepherd, pastor
[from Shipibo *pastóro* pastor + *bínirisinti* to bless] : to ordain as pastor
[from Shipibo *pastóro* pastor + *tée* work + *méniti* to give] : to install as pastor

*modifying suf.* : doing (a specific action) at intervals —Used with one of the verbal suffixes *jo-* or *be-* "on coming" or *ca-* or *bo-* "on going" affixed after it. ⟨**Káchiokeáx jokínra en íso rétepatanbeke.** Coming back from the forest, I killed spider monkeys along the way.⟩ ⟨**Nontín kakínra en isábo oímpatanboke.** Traveling by canoe, I went along watching several little birds.⟩

*postp.* 1 : beside, next to ⟨**Nokon pápa patax iká jónira yómetso iki.** The man standing next to my dad is a thief.⟩ 2 : near ⟨**Xóbo pataxa mayániwe pakéke.** Near the house, a whirlwind of dust appeared and passed by.⟩

*v.i.* **patáxa** : to approach, to get close to ⟨**Aínbaonra jóni ríshki(ke) wastén náshixonbi patáxketian onánxon.** A woman beat a man because she knew he was approaching her after bathing with piripiri.⟩
*v.t.* **páteta** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + *tékati* to sting, to pierce] : to sting or pierce on the ear
*v.t.* **patíaka** [from Shipibo *patéti* to sting on the ear + *-ati* to make, to do] : to touch on the ear
*n.* **patónkonin** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + *tónko* ball] : a small piece of cartilage in the ear
*n.* **pátoronin** [from Spanish] : boss, patrón; *also* : owner : master ⟨**Jakóma shinánya patóroninra jóni ríxkixon réteke.** An evil-minded boss beat one of his workers to death with a stick.⟩
*v.i.* **pátsakaata** : to pat oneself lightly ⟨**Nato bákera óxakasi janbíx pátsakaake.** This child was sleepy and was given some light pats.⟩
*v.t.* **pátsaa** : to give a light pat to

*v.t.* **pátsata** : to wash (clothing or jute) ⟨**Chópa pátsatainra westíora aínbo kánakan réteke.** Lightning struck and killed a woman while she was washing clothes.⟩ ⟨**Nokon awínra chópa patsá sáwekasiki.** My wife always likes to wear washed clothes.⟩ [illustration: *patsáti*]
*adj.* **pawéstiatonin** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + *wésti,* few + *-ya* having] : odd (number) ⟨**Kímishara nómiro pawéstia iki.** Three is an odd number.⟩
See under **móxa**
*v.t.* **páwexa** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + *wéxati* to scratch] : to scratch on the ear of
*v.t.* **páxaa** *Konibo* **páxaaka** : to leave raw or half-cooked ⟨**Ompáx yámaketianra en betén páxaake.** I ran out of water, and carelessly left the fish chowder still undercooked.⟩
*n.* **páxainintinin** [from Shipibo *páxa* green + *inínti, inín-* to perfume + *-ti* instrument suffix] : estoraque (a fragrant resin tree) *syn.* kásho
*v.i.* **páxaa** : to remain half-raw : to not cook properly ⟨**Nokon titán paránta jóaara páxake.** The plantains my mom boiled came out undercooked.⟩
*adj.* **páxkiman** : exhausting, tiring ⟨**Nato tée paxkín ikénbira pátoronin noa íchamashoko kopíake.** Even though the work was very exhausting, the boss paid us very little.⟩
*v.t.* **paxkínhaa** *Konibo* **paxkínhaka** : to tire : to make tired ⟨**Jonínra jawen wétsa paxkínhake téemakin.** A man made his brother work until he was tired.⟩ *syn.* pinímati
*v.i.* **páxkina** : to get tired ⟨**Ochóyora íshtoaxa nokon wétsa paxkínke.** My brother ran a long distance and got tired.⟩ ⟨**Páxkinaxa ea** óxai rakáke. When I got tired, I lay down to sleep.⟩
*n.* **paxkón** : a small branch sprouting from a stalk
*n.* **Páxmiman** —Used as a male name.
*adj.* **paxnán** : weak : exhausted ⟨**Nokon yórara páxna iki, ísini.** My body is weak from illness.⟩ *syn.* yósma
*adj.* **páxnakan** : light, pale —Used regarding colors. *syn.* bexnán
*v.i.* **páxnaa** *Konibo* **páxnaaka** : to weaken : to exhaust ⟨**Jamákin páxnaaxonra atapa nónoman réteke.** Exhausting its strength, a duck kicked a hen to death.⟩
*v.i.* **páxnaa** : to become or be weak or exhausted ⟨**Iorai téetaxa ea páxnai.** I feel weak from working too much.⟩ ⟨**Páxnaaxa nato jóni mawákeanke.** That man nearly died from exhaustion.⟩
*v.t.* **páxtea** [from Shipibo *pa-* on the ear + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut on the ear

*also* **payáti** *v.i.* **páyameeta** *also* **páyata** [from Shipibo *pa-* ear-shaped + *-ya* with + *-mee* reflexive suf. + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to fan oneself ⟨**Páyameeketianra nato aínbo barín ménoyamake.** This woman was not hot because she fanned herself.⟩
*v.t.* **páyana** 1 : to fan 2 : to winnow ⟨**Nokon papánra arós panyánke.** My dad winnowed the rice.⟩

*n.* **payárin** *also* **payárinin** 1 : arahuana (a large scaled river fish) ⟨**Nato bákera payári beten píkashamai.** That boy doesn't want to eat arahuana chowder.⟩ 2 : the constellation called "Arahuana," made up of the last four stars in the tail of the constellation Scorpio —In this sense, used capitalized as *P.* [illustration: *payári*]

*v.i.* **páyata** 1 : to fan oneself ⟨**Payákinra en payáti sékeke.** While fanning myself, I broke the fan.⟩ 2 : to blow (the wind) ⟨**Níwe páyataitianra ea matsín ákai.** When the wind blows, I feel cold.⟩ ⟨**Níwe payáketianra nato báke ráketai.** This child is afraid when the wind blows.⟩

*n.* **payátinin** [from Shipibo *payáti*, *paya-* to fan oneself + *-ti* instrument suffix] : a fan made of natural materials ⟨**Titánra jawen báke payátinin ríshkike.** Mom hit her child with the fan.⟩
See **páyameeti**

*adj.* **panyón** : old-fashioned : old : deteriorated : worn-out —Used regarding things that deteriorate. ⟨**Nato chópa páyo jónira téekashamai wetsa binox.** This man in old clothes doesn't want to work to get new ones.⟩ *syn.* PAYO, YOSI — both can be translated as "old," but PAYO applies to things and YOSI to elderly people.

*n.* **páyoman** [from Spanish *paño*] 1 : handkerchief ⟨**Titánra joshín payón téoke.** Mom has a red handkerchief tied around her neck.⟩ 2 : towel ⟨**Eara náshiax páyoman rásoikike.** I bathed and dried myself with the towel.⟩ *syn.* bésoikiiti; rásoikiiti
See under **róno**

*v.t.* **páyoa** 1 : to tear to pieces ⟨**Parántajoshinra en jamákin páyoke.** When I stepped on a ripe plantain, I mashed it to pieces.⟩ 2 : to ulcerate : to cause sores on ⟨**Nato bakén mápora ián páyoke.** Lice caused sores on this child's head.⟩ 3 : to digest : to grind up by digesting ⟨**Non píketianra pokón jawékiati páyoai.** The stomach digests the food we eat.⟩ *syn.* beshéati

*v.i.* **páyota** 1 : to grow old —Used regarding things that deteriorate. ⟨**Nokon wetsán motórora páyoti moa pishíamiai.** My brother's motor no longer starts because it's getting old.⟩ 2 : to rot ⟨**Yápa páyotara ochítinin píke.** The dog ate the rotten fish.⟩ 3 : to ulcerate : to develop sores ⟨**Yoshínkoshki non métoketianronki non mekén páyotai.** They say that if we point at the rainbow with our finger, our finger gets ulcerated.⟩
[from Shipibo *bási* for a long time + *payóti* to grow old] : to last a long time ⟨**Yóti chópaakanara bási páyotai.** Cloth made from jute lasts a long time.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *peká* back] 1 : on the back : from the back ⟨**péyakati** to sit on the back of⟩ 2 : on the shoulder : at the shoulder : from the shoulder ⟨**petsíti** to suck on the shoulder of⟩ 3 : on the wing : to the wing : from the wing ⟨**peméxti** to pluck (feathers from the wings)⟩ 4 : on the back/spine : over the back : from the back ⟨**pexkán** shell, carapace⟩ 5 : on the dorsal surface : to the back : from the back ⟨**pékoro** gray on the back⟩ 6 : on the surface : from the surface : to the surface ⟨**pétsoti** to suck (something) from the surface of a finger⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*v.t.* **péana** : to spread out over a surface ⟨**Titánra chópa peánke jéma napon.** Mom spread the clothes out in the middle of the yard.⟩

*n.* **peáraxtin** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the shoulder + *aráxti*, *arax-* to squeeze, to tighten] : coat : jacket ⟨**Nato jonínra peáraxti ícha Rímamea béke.** That man brought many jackets from Lima.⟩
*n.* **pécharonin** : a branch placed on an improvised roof to provide shade
*v.i.* **péchia** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *chi-* backward + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to turn one's back 2 : to come to feel contempt or disdain
See under **wáste**

*v.i.* **péchokoa** [from Shipibo *péi* leaf + *choko*, unidentified element + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to sprout leaves : to grow new leaves ⟨**Moátianra nato jíwi péioma iántanke; rámara moa péchokoke.** In the past this tree had no leaves, but now it has grown new ones.⟩
See **Píkero**

*n.* **peín** 1 : leaf ⟨**Máni pei bixónra non bawín xoi káwal.** We get a bijao leaf and wrap the súngaro catfish in it.⟩ ⟨**Máni pei táriaaxonki yoxinxatan jónike.** They say that long ago the payaso demon made a cushma robe out of plantain leaves and came dressed that way.⟩ 2 : page : sheet of paper ⟨**Nokon kírika peira bakén wáxake.** The child tore a page out of my book.⟩ 3 : wing ⟨**Yoxínteteronki chósko péia iki.** They say the ghost hawk has four wings.⟩ ⟨**Poínkoskobaonronki yawíx péi axónike.** They say that in the old days the vultures made wings for the armadillo.⟩ 4 : feather ⟨**Atapa peira en pía peiake.** I fletched my arrows with chicken feathers.⟩ *syn.* See under **pájina** *syn.* ráni
See under **koríki**
*n.* **pékaten** *Konibo* **pékakan** : back ⟨**Káshibobaonra nokon pápashoko pekáin rérakanike.** In the old days the Cashibo machete-hacked my grandfather in the back.⟩
[from Shipibo *chíxo* buttock + *peká* back] : the upper part of the buttock
[from Shipibo *chópa* clothing + *peká* back] : the outer part of clothing
[from Shipibo *mísa* table + *peká* back] : the top surface of a table
[from Shipibo *nónti* canoe + *peká* back] : the outer hull of a canoe
[from Shipibo *kírika* book + *peká* back] : the cover of a book
[from Shipibo *kíshi* thigh + *peká* back] : the upper part of the thigh
[from Shipibo *xóbo* house + *peká* back] : roof : rooftop : flat roof ⟨**Xóbopekakameaxa báke pakéke.** A child fell off the roof.⟩

*postp. and conj.* [from Shipibo *peká* back + *-o*, locative suf.] *postp.* 1 : behind 2 : after ⟨**Jónira jawen awín pekao káke.** The man went after his wife.⟩ 3 : after —Used postposed to the noun indicating time, generally defined by a number. ⟨**Moa mitán wínota rabé néte pekaora jéne tsosínke.** After two days had passed since Carnival, the river went down.⟩ —Used with a number as a preceding complement in a phrase that indicates an ordinal number one greater than the complement. —Used from the number *rabé* "two" onward. ⟨**ja rabé pekao jálnoax ja kímisha pekao** the second and the third⟩ *conj.* : after —Used postposed to a subordinate clause with the subordinate verb ending in *-a*. ⟨**Nato jóni Rímameax joá pekáora niwánke.** After this man came from Lima, there was an earthquake.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.1; 7.7.2

*v.t.* **pékaa** 1 : to hollow out : to perforate ⟨**Jíwi borokanra nónti pékake.** The quiruma beetle perforated the canoe.⟩ 2 : to tear, to rip ⟨**Sontároninra jawen amígo rishkíkin pékake.** A soldier tore into his friend with lashes.⟩ 3 : to open up (a path) ⟨**Káchio kaxónra non bái pékake.** We went to the forest and opened up a path.⟩ *syn.* PEKATI, KINIATI, SHOKITI — all three can have the sense of "to hollow out." However, while PEKATI implies a violent action (e.g., perforating a canoe in a river), KINIATI implies a gentler action. SHOKITI means "to hollow out" specifically in the sense of "to drill." See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*n.* **pekén** : hole ⟨**Nato péke meranra shanó jíkike.** The fer-de-lance snake went in through this hole.⟩ *syn.* PEKE, KINI — both can be translated as "hole"; but PEKE implies a smaller size (e.g., one a snake can barely fit through), whereas KINI refers to a larger hole (e.g., an animal's burrow).
*n.* **péketen** *Konibo* **pékekan** : ulcer : sore ⟨**Jawen peké isín íketianra nokon pápa jóyamake.** My dad didn't come because his ulcer hurts a lot.⟩
*v.i.* **péketa** 1 : to have an ulcer or sore ⟨**Nato aínbora jawen ponyáin pekéke.** This woman has a sore on her arm.⟩ 2 : to develop a hole ⟨**Nokon nóntira pekéke.** My canoe developed a hole.⟩
*n.* **pékoron** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *kóro* gray] : a species of ant resembling the isula (a large stinging ant)
See under **wáste**
See **piróta**
*v.i.* **pémexeeta** : to have one's feathers plucked (wing feathers) : to molt
*v.t.* **pémexa** [from Shipibo *pe-* of the wings + *méxati* to pluck] : to pluck or pull feathers from (wings) : to defeather (wings)

*n.* **pémpeman** 1 : butterfly ⟨**Pempénronki xénoamis iki.** They say that the butterfly can give us scabies.⟩ 2 : a type of decorative figure made of two small crossed sticks woven with thread in the shape of a diamond and placed together with another one like it in a headdress
[from Shipibo *áwa, awán* tapir + *pempén* butterfly] : a species of gigantic-sized butterfly that can be black, green, or white in color
[from Shipibo *joshín* red + *pempén* butterfly] : any of several species of red-colored butterfly
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *pempén* butterfly] : a species of white butterfly
[from Shipibo *panshín* yellow, orange + *pempén* butterfly] : a species of yellow or orange-colored butterfly
[from Shipibo *yankón* blue, green + *pempén* butterfly] : a species of blue or green-colored butterfly
*n.* **Penán** —Used as a female name.
*adj.* **pénekan** : bright, shiny ⟨**Nokon meósotira kikínbires penéyora iki, kopí ikax.** My ring is very shiny because it's valuable.⟩ *syn.* xéna
*v.t.* **penéaa** *Konibo* **penéaka** : to give shine to : to make shine ⟨**Nokon áwininra yámikenti penéai.** My wife makes her aluminum pot shine.⟩
*v.i.* **péneta** : to take on a shine : to shine ⟨**Barín ténaara, jéne penéke.** The water shone from the sunlight.⟩ *syn.* joéti
*n.* **penichinin** : a species of plant not yet identified
*v.t.* **penichina** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *nichínti* to make stand] : to place on top of

*n.* **penínkoron** [from Shipibo *penín,* unidentified element + *kóro* ashen] : a species of bijao (Heliconia) with leaves longer and wider than the common bijao, and with a white powder on the underside
*v.i.* **pénita** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *níti* to stand] : to stand on the back or on the surface of
*v.t.* **pénkona** : to rock (a canoe) in the water
*v.i.* **pénkota** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *-nko* on, in + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to rock back and forth on one's back

*adv.* [from Shipibo *péoti, peo-* to begin + *bená* new + *-tian* when] : at the beginning : for the first time ⟨**Kírika peóbenatianra noa kikínbiresi onitsapikana iki.** When we first study, we suffer a lot because it is hard to learn.⟩

*v.i.* **péokoota** [from Shipibo *péoti* to begin + *koo-* reflexive suf.] : to begin, to start, to commence —Used in a sentence with a complement in the form of the intransitive verb ending in *-i.* ⟨**Rámara jéne beí péokooke.** Now the water has begun to rise.⟩ ⟨**Nato yaméra ránsai peokookanke.** Last night they began to dance.⟩

*n.* **péotanin** [from Shipibo *péi* leaf + *óta* shade] : a small shelter made of a few cañabrava (wild cane) leaves ⟨**Yaméketianra ea péotanin óxake.** When night fell I slept in a little cañabrava-leaf shelter.⟩ *syn.* PEOTA, PEXEWA, OTA — all three mean "small shelter," but PEOTA implies a less substantial structure, distinguishing it from PEXEWA, which is a construction specifically made of cañabrava leaves. OTA is used mostly among the Shetebo with the same meaning of *"small cañabrava shelter"* as PEOTA.

*v.t.* **péoa** 1 : to begin to make (e.g., a construction) ⟨**Nokon shóbora en moa péoke.** I have already begun building my house.⟩ 2 : to begin, to start, to commence (an action) —Used in the form of the main verb with a subordinate verb in *-i* indicating the action begun; or, alternatively, used in subordinate form in *-i* as a complement of the main verb indicating the action begun. ⟨**Emparira chícha xéakin péoke.** I was the first to begin drinking the chicha.⟩ ⟨**Emparira chícha péokin xea-** que. I was the first to start drinking the chicha.⟩
See under **pítso**

*v.t.* **pérakana** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *rakánti* to lay down] : to lay (one thing) down on top of *syn.* PERAKANTI, PETIPINTI mean identically "to lay down on top of"; but PERAKANTI implies one thing laid down while PETIPINTI implies several things laid down.
*v.t.* **pérakana** : to be lying (one thing) on top

*v.t.* **perén aka** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *ren*, imitative of the sound + *-ati* to make, to do] : to give a shake to : to shake ⟨**Papánra janwen tári perénake.** Dad shook out his cushma robe loudly and forcefully.⟩
*v.i.* **perén ika** : to shake, to be shaken ⟨**Nato chópara níweaitibires perén ikai.** Every time there is wind, these clothes shake.⟩

*v.t.* **péreta** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *rérati* to hack with a machete] : to hack with a machete across the back ⟨**Joninra jawen rawí korós akin peréke.** A man hacked cross-shaped cuts into his enemy's back.⟩
*n.* **perín** 1 : a species of oily palm tree from the highlands 2 : a torch made from the *péri* palm
See **piríto**
See **pírira**
*n.* **perón** : toayo (a small crab found on river beaches) ⟨**Yaméra péro mashín ícha íki.** At night, toayo crabs are abundant on the beaches.⟩
See **Píroano**
*v.i.* **peróntameeta** [from Shipibo *pe-* from the back + *róntameeti* to hang oneself] : to be hanging from the back
See **píro**
*v.t.* **pésoa** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the outside + *sóo iti* to soften] : to rub on the outside

*v.i.* **péstita** : to become hunchbacked —Used mostly among Konibo speakers. ⟨**Nokon cháira moa yósiax pestíke.** My brother-in-law has become hunchbacked because he is already old.⟩ ⟨**Nato jónira pestíora iki.** This man is very hunchbacked.⟩
*v.i.* **pétana** : to veer off, to detour (e.g., to avoid an obstacle or danger) ⟨**Petánnira ea jóke.** I came by taking a detour.⟩
*v.t.* **pétipina** [from Shipibo *pétipiti* to be lying on top + *-n,* verbal derivation suf.] : to lay (several things) down together on top, in a bundle or group *syn.* See under **pérakanti**
*v.i.* **pétipia** : to be (several things) lying on top

*n.* **pétokan** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the outside + *totó* stain, spot] 1 : tapestry : a design woven into cloth 2 : a sewn or embroidered design —Often used in reduplicated form. ⟨**Nato petóra jakónyora iki.** This man's shirt embroidery is very beautiful.⟩ ⟨**Nato chópapeka petópetotanira jakónyora iki.** This clothing has a very beautiful design on its outer surface.⟩
*v.i.* **pétsata** : to descend : to go down ⟨**Jónira botímeax jenénko pétsata iki.** The man got down from the boat into the water.⟩
*v.t.* **pétsita** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *tsítsiti* to suck] : to suck (e.g., a shaman during a healing) on the shoulder
*v.t.* **pétsoa** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the outside + *tsóati* to make a sound with the lips] : to suck from one's own finger ⟨**Enra bónajene pétsoke.** I sucked honey from my finger.⟩
*n.* **Pexékean** —Used as a male name.
*v.t.* **péxea** : to clear of clouds (the sun or moon)
*v.t.* **péxeta** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *xéwati* to sniff] : to sniff on the back ⟨**Ochítininra manánxawe pexéke.** The dog sniffed the motelo tortoise on its back.⟩

*n.* **péxewanin** [from Shipibo *péi* leaf + *xewati*, *xewa-* to weave] : small shelter : a small structure with a frame and roof that can serve, e.g., as a temporary small house, workshop, or lodging : a campsite or travel shelter ⟨**Péxewanin noa óxaketianra, oín noa mecháayamake.** The rain didn't get us wet because we slept in a small shelter.⟩ *syn.* See under **péota**

*n.* **péxkaman** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *xaká* shell] 1 : shell, carapace of a turtle ⟨**Xábue pexkamanra beténkanai yapa, ícha inón íxon.** They prepare fish chowder in a charapa turtle shell so it tastes better.⟩ 2 : the cover or jacket of a book ⟨**Non kírika pexkányan íketianra, ishtón tároyamai.** If our books are covered, they don't get dirty quickly.⟩

*v.i.* **péxmaa** *Konibo* **péxmaaka** : to have (one's eyes) half closed ⟨**Nato jónibaonra jaton béro péxmaakai óxakashorakin.** These men have their eyes half closed because they are very sleepy.⟩

*v.i.* **péxmaa** : to be half heavy with sleep (the eyes) ⟨**Nokon bérora moa péxmake.** My eyes are already heavy with sleep.⟩ ⟨**Jawen béro péxmaa ixonra nato jonín oínkonyamai.** This man doesn't see well because his eyes are half closed.⟩

*n.* **pexón** : shoulder blade : scapula ⟨**Nokon pápara yómetsobaon pexónko ríshkike.** Some thieves whipped my dad and hit him on the shoulder blade.⟩ ⟨**Nokon pékatenra ea chéxai, néno, pexónko.** My back hurts here, in the shoulder-blade area.⟩

*adj. and n.* **péxtiman** *adj.* : wide ⟨**Nokon pekára pextínyora iki.** My back is very wide.⟩ *n.* : width ⟨**Titán rakótira jawen pextín áni iki.** Mom's blanket is very wide.⟩ *syn.* See under **nashbá**
*v.t.* **pextinhaa** *Konibo* **pextínhaka** : to widen or expand on the outside ⟨**Nokon wáira en moa pextínhake.** I have already expanded the outer edge of my garden plot.⟩

*v.i.* **péyakaa** [from Shipibo *pe-* on the back + *yákati* to seat] : to sit on top of —Used with a complement in non-basic form. ⟨**Ani bonántinin péyakaxa báke pakéke, jawen wetsán wérana.** When the little boy sat on top of the big trunk, he fell off because his brother pushed him.⟩
*v.t.* **peyásana** : to place seated on top of ⟨**Kémpora titán peyásanke.** Mom set the mocahua bowl on the barbacoa platform.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *pishi* rib] : to the ribs : along the ribs : around the ribs : from the ribs ⟨**pinéxti** to tie (e.g., a belt) around the ribs⟩ ⟨**píxteti** to cut in half, through the ribs⟩
*n.* **pián** : arrow ⟨**Rámara moa pián kopí néeke.** Now the price of arrows has gone up.⟩

*n.* **píakan** : nephew : niece : the son or daughter of a man's sister; *also* : the son or daughter of a wife's brother —Each of the vocative forms *piá* or *piaká*, *choré* "relative," *yosí* "old man," *yoxán* "old woman," *jomó* "young person," and *chinín* "girl" is used to address the indicated person. ⟨Nocon **píakan bénera sontáro káke**. My niece's husband went off to the army.⟩ *syn.* chíobake
*n., vocative* [from Shipibo *píakan*, non-basic form of *piá* nephew] : nephew : niece —Used as the vocative form of *piá* "nephew" or "niece." *syn.* chíobake

*n.* **píakenyantinin** [from Shipibo *pía* arrow + *kenyánti, kenyan–* to put up high + *-ti* instrument suffix] : an arrow rack ⟨Nocon **píakenyantininra pítso yakáke**. The pihuicho parakeet is perched on top of my arrow rack.⟩
See under **keré**
*n.* **piámpiaman** [from Shipibo *pián*, imitative of its call] : a species of medium-sized bird
*n.* **píchakan** : palometa (a piranha-like fish) ⟨**Píchakanra nokon wétsa kópia iki**. A palometa fish afflicted my little brother with cutipo (a spirit-caused illness).⟩
*adj.* **píchikanin** [from Quechua *pichka* five] : five ⟨**Píchikanin ea kéenkebira min ea sókota bexónke**. Even though I only wanted five, you brought me six.⟩

*v.i.* **píkasa** [from Shipibo *píti* to eat + *-kas* to want] 1 : to want or crave to eat : to have an appetite for —Used in this sense with a complement in basic form. ⟨amaquiri kobínra ea **píkasai** I crave stewed gamitana fish⟩ 2 : to be hungry or feel like eating —Used in this sense without a complement. ⟨**Aínbaon wáme bétenai óinaxa ea pikáske.** When I saw the woman preparing paiche fish chowder, I felt like eating.⟩

*also* **Pedro** *n.* **Píkeron** *Konibo* **Píkeronin** *also* **Pedrón** [from Spanish *Pedro*] —Used as a male name. ⟨**Píkerora chikísh iká iki; jábira non ráona rayáke.** Pedro was very lazy; but we gave him a plant remedy and he became hardworking.⟩

*adj.* **pikóbenakan** [from Shipibo *pikóti, piko–* to come out + *bená* new] : newborn ⟨Báke **pikóbenakanra jáwebi onányamaparike; jákopira wíniaitian notsíntima iki**. A newborn baby doesn't know anything, and so should not be scolded when it cries.⟩
*v.t.* **píkoa** : to take out ⟨**Janra jawen kírika píkoai**. He is taking out his book.⟩ *syn.* See under **pakémati**

*v.i.* **píkota** 1 : to come out (alone, by oneself) ⟨Nato **simánaninra nokon wétsa píkotai, téetiainoax**. This week my brother is going to finish (come out of) his job.⟩ 2 : to appear or emerge (alone) ⟨**Rámaronki meráyabo píkotai**. They say that nowadays sorcerers who work magic appear one by one.⟩ 3 : to be born ⟨Jahuen báke **pikóketianra jonín sámatai jatiribi jawakibo piamakin**. When a child is born, the father goes on a diet, abstaining from certain foods.⟩ *syn.* See under **jokónti**
