[from Shipibo *jaská* thus + *-bi* even though + *píkota*, participle of *pikóti* to be born] : from birth, congenital ⟨**nítikoma jaskábi píkota** lame from birth⟩
*v.t.* **pínexa** [from Shipibo *pi–* along the ribs + *néxati* to tie] : to tie (e.g., a belt) along the ribs
*n.* **pínikan** 1 : tiredness, exhaustion ⟨**Cháxo íorai íxtoketianronki pínikan rétenike**. They say that long ago the deer ran so fast that exhaustion killed it.⟩ 2 : panting

*v.t.* **pinímaa** 1 : to make tired : to tire ⟨**Ichayora téemaxonra ea pátoronin pinímake**. The boss tired me out by making me work too much.⟩ 2 : to make pant ⟨**Enra átapa chibánkin pinímake**. I made the hen pant by chasing it to catch it.⟩ *syn.* paxkínhati

*v.i.* **pínita** 1 : to get tired : to be tired ⟨**Ichayora íxtoaxa, moa ea pínitai**. I'm already tired from running so much.⟩ 2 : to pant ⟨**Íxtoaxa nato aínbo píníke**. That woman panted when she ran.⟩ ⟨**Ea piníketianra nokon wetsán ea pótake.** When I was already panting, my brother left me behind.⟩ ⟨**Sarámpinin ikíra báke pínitai.** The child pants because he has measles.⟩ ⟨**Títa betan papán cháxo píketianronki báke pínitai.** They say that when the father eats deer meat, the little child gets sick and pants.⟩ 3 : to breathe hoarsely (as when about to die) *syn.* PINITI, XANXAN ITI — both are translated as "to pant," with no difference in meaning.
*n.* **pinón** 1 : hummingbird 2 : a mythical figure identified with the hummingbird ⟨**Pinónronki chíikan ewa bebánike.** They say that long ago the hummingbird flew through hell.⟩
[from Shipibo *xóchi* chest + *jóxo* white + *píno* hummingbird] : a species of hummingbird
[from Shipibo *yankón* blue-green + *píno* hummingbird] : a species of bright green hummingbird
*n.* **pínojiwin** [from Spanish *pino* + Shipibo *jíwi* tree, wood] : pine tree
See under **wáste**
*n.* : a species of tree with bark like that of the ubo, a trunk that is almost reddish on the outside, and used for making canoes and boats

*n.* **piónisnin** [from Spanish *piñones*] : a species of shrub with leaves and stem similar to those of the amasisa, with beautiful flowers, and a milky sap used as a remedy ⟨**Báke wínira titán piónis xéa-** **make.** The mother made the crying child drink milk-sap from the *piónis* tree.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *piónis* a species of tree] : a species of tree or plant used to treat fever, whose resin is used as an eye remedy
*n.* **pírapiran** [from Shipibo *pírapira*, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *pírapira* a species of bird] : a species of small bird
[from Shipibo *yankón* blue-green + *pírapira* a species of bird] : a species of small bird
*n.* **pírasen** [from Spanish *perlas*] : colored hollow glass beads ⟨**Nokon títara pírasen kéenyorai.** My mom really wants to have colored glass beads.⟩
*also* **pregónta** *n.* **pírikontan** *also* **pregóntan** [from Spanish] : question *syn.* yoká

*also* **pregónta ati** *v.t.* **pírikonta aka** [from Spanish *pregunta* + Shipibo *áti* to do] : to ask *syn.* PIRIKONTA ATI, YOKATI both mean "to ask"; but YOKATI, the native word, is the more established and usual one.
*n.* **pírimison** : permission
[from Spanish *permiso* + Shipibo *áti* to do] : to ask for permission
*also* **pérla** *n.* **pírora** [from Spanish] : pearl —Also used in the regular plural form *pírirabo*, and the irregular plural forms *píriras* and *–pírirasbo*.

*also* **présidente** *n.* **pírisirintinin** *also* **présidentenin** [from Spanish] : president ⟨**Ja non Pírisirinti jonóntianra, nokon báke píkota iki.** At the time our President came, my child was born.⟩ *syn.* See under *ápo*
*also* **préso** *n.* **pírisonin** *also* **présonin** [from Spanish] : prisoner

*also* **préso ati** *v.t.* **píriso aka** *also* **préso aka** [from Spanish *preso* + Shipibo *-ati* to do] : to take prisoner : to arrest ⟨**Porísiabaonra jóni píriso akánke.** The police took the man prisoner.⟩

*also* **prédikanti** *v.t.* **píritikana** *also* **prédikana** [from Spanish *predikar* + *-n*, verbal derivation suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to preach *syn.* PIRITIKANTI, RIOSEN JOI YOITI both translate as "to preach" with no difference in meaning, but the native expression RIOSEN JOI YOITI is more usual.
*also* **períto** *n.* **pirítonin** *also* **perítonin** [from Spanish *perito*] : surveyor : expert ⟨**Pirítoninra non mái noa topónxonke.** The surveyor measured our land boundaries for us.⟩

*also* **pítipiro** *n.* **pirón** *also* **pítipiron** [from Shipibo *píti* food + *píro* cahuara (a type of fish)] : cahuara fish ⟨**Píro icháira piáxxa bake chíxotai.** The child has diarrhea because he ate too much cahuara fish.⟩

*also* **Perú** *n.* **Píronin** *also* **Pérunin** [from Spanish] : Peru ⟨**Yáma riki kaíakanai jawéki Piróain jáa.** The llama is a domestic animal native to Peru.⟩
*also* **Péroano** *n. and adj.* **Píroanon** *also* **Péroano** [from Spanish] : Peruvian ⟨**Piroanobaon iskóro riki kímisha toróya.** The Peruvian coat of arms has three fields.⟩
*also* **pelota** *n.* **pirótanin** *also* **pelótanin** [from Spanish *pelota*] : soccer : ball ⟨**Nokon títara pirótanin tsakka maín pakéke.** My mom fell to the ground when the ball hit her.⟩

[from Shipibo *piróta* ball + *áti* to do] : to play soccer ⟨**Bíntiochotianra noa pi-** **róta akí kái, Iparianko.** On "the 28th of July" (Peru's Independence Day) we will go to Iparía to play soccer.⟩
[from Shipibo *piróta* soccer + *tsíniai*, present participle of *tsíniti* to play] : soccer player
*n.* **pisán** : pinsha (a small parrot) ⟨**Kampánra písa rani máitiakai.** The Campa (Asháninka) make a headdress from pinsha feathers.⟩
[from Shipibo *bonchón* with bristled hair + *písa* pinsha] : a species of pinsha parrot
[from Shipibo *manán* hill + *písa* pinsha] : a species of pinsha parrot that frequents the hills

*n.* **pisáranin** [from Spanish] : slate, chalkboard ⟨**wíso pisára** black chalkboard⟩

*n.* **pishán** : bag : backpack; *specif.* : a small type of bag, woven from cotton, with a strap for carrying ⟨**Rámatian bákeranonbora píshaoma iki.** Young people today no longer have little *písha* bags like the people of old.⟩ *syn.* See under **bórosa**

*v.t.* **píshaa** : to unhook : to loosen : to release ⟨**Papánra jawen tapán píshake.** Dad untied his raft and it floated downriver.⟩ ⟨**Nónti píshaara jábatai.** The canoe came loose and drifted away.⟩ *syn.* páketi
*n.* **pishín** : rib ⟨**Pirótaninra nokon píshi sékeke** The ball hit me and broke my rib.⟩
[from Shipibo *xóbo* house + *pishi* rib] : cañabrava (wild cane) roof beams

*adj. and n.* **píshikan** *adj.* : running, functioning ⟨**Motóro pishíra janbíx jenéke.** The motor was running and it suddenly stopped.⟩ *n.* : starting, ignition ⟨**Nato motórora jawen pishí jakómatani iki.** This motor's starting isn't very good.⟩

*n.* **píshiman** : a species of mat woven from strips of a single shapaja or shebón palm leaf ⟨**Níbo máwexonra papán pótake, píshiman axón.** Dad raked up the trash, put it on a shapaja-leaf mat, and threw it out.⟩ *syn.* See under kawín

*v.i.* **píshina** [from Quechua *pixi-* to be lacking + Quechua *-n*, third-person singular suf.] : to be lacking : to be needed —Used with a complement in basic form. —Used in the preterite form with present-tense meaning. ⟨**Noara joé pishínke.** We are lacking a lamp.⟩ ⟨**Non jéma óroti ikáxbira noa jóni pishínke.** We should cultivate our yard, but we are short of people.⟩ *syn.* bismánti
See under **ípo**
*v.i.* **píshita** 1 : to come unhooked : to come loose 2 : to set sail, to depart ⟨**Ramara wapóro pishíke, Ikítoain kaí.** Today the steamship set sail, headed for Iquitos.⟩

*n.* **píshkibon** *Konibo* **pishkibaon** *pisc.* **pishkibaen** [from Shipibo *Píshki* Pisqui River + *-bo*, pl. suf.] : the Pisquino ethnolinguistic group : the Pisquinos : Pisquino people ⟨**Píshkibaonra shípibo jónibo réteke náwaboyaxon.** Some Pisquinos and some mestizos killed some Shipibo people.⟩
*n.* **pishpachinin** [from Shipibo *pish*, element of *pishi* rib + *páchi* soft] : flank, side (of the body) ⟨**Enra titán píshpachi tíake.** I touched Mom's side.⟩ *syn.* ispi
*n.* **píshpishin** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : a species of small bird, dark brown in color, with a white spot below its beak
[from Shipibo *waxunén* cotton + *pishpish* a species of bird] : a species of small, whitish-colored bird
[from Shipibo *xawan* large-headed macaw + *pishpish* a species of bird] : a species of small, red-colored bird
*n.* **pishtán** [from Spanish] : festival, party ⟨**Píshta neténra, awá rétekanai.** On the day of the festival, they will kill the tapir.⟩
*v.t.* **píshtaa** *Konibo* **píshtaaka** : to hold a party ⟨**Jonínra píshtaai jawen báke sontáro íiti jóketian.** The man is holding a party for his son's return from the army.⟩

*n.* **píshtakonin** [from Quechua] : pishtaco (a legendary fat-stealing bogeyman) ⟨**Rónoyainxonra westíora jóni ispáraya mérakanke; méraxonra pishtáko shinánkanai.** In Runuya they saw a man with a sword, and having seen him, they think he is a pishtaco.⟩
*n.* **pishtókenin** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : víctor-díaz (a bird) ⟨**Pishtókeninra xénabo píai.** Víktor-díaz birds eat various kinds of worms.⟩
*n.* **píshtoman** : chotacabras (a nightjar bird)

*adj. and n.* **písín** *adj.* : stinking, foul-smelling ⟨**Jóni máwatara písi iki.** The corpse is foul-smelling.⟩ *n.* : stench ⟨**Bákera písi póatai; póiara íbirai.** The baby is giving off a stench; he has surely had a bowel movement.⟩ *syn.* jánxo
*v.t.* **písiaa** *Konibo* **písiaka** : to make stink ⟨**Nato bakénra betén písiake, átapa pói nenánxon.** This child made the fish chowder stink by putting chicken droppings in it.⟩
*v.i.* **písia** : to become foul-smelling ⟨**Táshi máxkataxa nato píti tashín aka písike.** For lack of salt, this fish has gone rotten and smells bad.⟩
*n.* **pískaten** *Konibo* **piskakan** : afaninga (a nonvenomous snake) ⟨**Pískakan noa nátexara noa chéxayamai.** When the afaninga snake bites us, it doesn't hurt.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *piská* afaninga snake] : a species of black afaninga snake
[from Shipibo *joshín* reddish + *piská* afaninga snake] : a species of reddish afaninga snake
[from Shipibo *yankón* blue-green + *piská* afaninga snake] : a species of common green afaninga snake

*adj. and n.* **pískoten** *Konibo* **pískokan** [from Shipibo *pískoti* to cut completely into pieces] *adj.* : completely cut into pieces ⟨**Moa piskóbires en xóno tóponara íke chónkares.** I counted only the ten lupuna logs that had been completely cut into pieces.⟩ *n.* : a piece (e.g., of wood) completely separated ⟨**Nokon wetsánra piskó béke.** My brother carried off a piece completely separated from the trunk.⟩
*v.t.* **pískoa** : to cut into pieces ⟨**Enra jíwi rérakin pískoke.** When I felled the tree, I cut it into pieces.⟩
*v.i.* **pískota** : to be completely cut into pieces ⟨**Moara konxán réraa piskóke.** Another piece of wood was cut off to complete the felled cedar tree.⟩

*v.t.* **piá** : to eat (meat or something else that is not sweet) ⟨**Moátianra non sapén pikátiai.** In the old days we used to eat manatee.⟩ ⟨**Enra asápa xoi píai.** I eat roasted paco fish.⟩ *syn.* See under kókoti

*n.* **pitín** [from Shipibo *píti, pi-* to eat + *-ti* instrument suffix] 1 : meat : meat food; *specif.* : fish ⟨**Nato óxebaonra en píti píamake, yámaketian.** These past months I haven't eaten meat, because it's scarce.⟩ ⟨**Rikánxonra en ícha píti biwanke.** This morning I caught many fish with a tarrafa net.⟩ 2 : hunger ⟨**Eara pitín réteai.** I'm dying of hunger.⟩ ⟨**Ochó jemánronki pitín mawákanai.** They say that in places far from the community, people die of hunger.⟩ *syn.* yápa *syn.* See under námi
: to be hungry ⟨**Pitín ikíra jóni yokámisai.** This man begs because he is hungry.⟩
See under **choín**
See under **kóno**
*n.* **pítimaton** [from Shipibo *píti* food + *-ma* not] : something forbidden or unfit to eat
See under **manxán**
See under **píti**
See **píro**
*n.* **pítirikin** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : a species of bird resembling a swallow, dark black in color
*n.* **pítixeatinin** [from Shipibo *píti* meat food + *xéati, xka-* to drink, to swallow + *-ti* instrument suffix] : esophagus
*n.* **pitsón** [from Quechua *piwikw*] : perico (parakeet) : pihuicho ⟨**Pítsoronki nákaxen amígo iki.** They say the pihuicho parakeet is the termite's friend.⟩
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *pítso* pihuicho parakeet] : a species of pihuicho parakeet
[from Shipibo *péi* feather + *jóxo* white + *pítso* pihuicho parakeet] : a species of pihuicho parakeet with whitish wings

*also* **kopítsori** *n.* **pítsokorin** *also* **kopítsorin** [from Shipibo *pítso* pihuicho parakeet + *kori* gold; and this from Quechua *kuri*] : matamata (a turtle species) ⟨**Pítsokorin báke kópiara nónbetai.** When a child is cutipoed by the matamata turtle, boils tend to break out on him.⟩ ⟨**Pítsokori pikáshamaira nokon báke wíniai.** My son cries because he doesn't want to eat matamata turtle.⟩ ⟨**Non kopítsori ósanaronki noa nónbetai.** They say that if we laugh at the matamata turtle, we get boils.⟩ *syn.* See under chánkoxawe
See under **bóna**
See under **páma**

*n.* **pitsómpitin** [from Shipibo *pitso, pitsón* pihuicho parakeet + *píti* food] : loromicuna (a plant, "parrot food") ⟨**Pitsómpiti namánra jóni paena rakáke.** A drunk man is lying under the loromicuna plant.⟩
*v.t.* **pítsona** [from Shipibo *pi-* along the ribs + *tsómati* to hold] : to hold by the ribs
*n.* **pítsoreshiman** [from Shipibo *pítso* pihuicho parakeet + *re-* on the beak + *panshín* yellow] : a species of pihuicho parakeet with yellow stripes on its beak
*v.t.* **píxtea** [from Shipibo *pi-* along the ribs + *xateti* to cut] 1 : to cut along the ribs 2 : to cut in half
See **párasa**
See **parástiko**
*n.* **poán** : sachapapa (a wild yam) ⟨**Nato bákera póa piáx xóata iki.** This child is fat from eating sachapapa yam.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *póa* sachapapa yam] : a species of blackish-colored sachapapa yam
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *póa* sachapapa yam] : a species of whitish-colored sachapapa yam
[from Shipibo *táe* foot + *póa* sachapapa yam] : a species of sachapapa yam shaped like a foot

*v.i.* **póata** 1 : to have or give off (e.g., raw or packaged fish) a stench : to stink : to smell ⟨**Nato yobé jónira róme itsa póatai.** This shaman smells of tobacco.⟩ ⟨**Mawáyoshinronki písi póatai.** They say the soul of the deceased stinks.⟩ 2 : to give off (e.g., boiling water) heat : to steam ⟨**Ompaxa shana póatai. Tíi ayamawe.** The water is steaming. Don't touch it.⟩
*n.* **pochán** : papaya ⟨**Ochítininra pócha kókoai.** The dog eats papaya.⟩ ⟨**Pochán yómetsoa íketianra pápashoko kóborankanke.** They charged grandfather because he stole the papayas.⟩
*postp.* : by the middle of (something specific) ⟨**Papánra jawen nónti pochínikon yatánke.** Dad grabbed his canoe by the middle.⟩
*n.* **poín** : excrement : dung ⟨**Non pói ménoaronki noa xenón ákai.** They say that if we burn our excrement, it gives us scabies.⟩

*n.* **poín** 1 : brother or sister of the opposite sex; *also* : nephew or niece of the opposite sex to the referenced uncle or aunt –Used each of the vocative forms *poí*, *jochí* "older brother", *yosí* "old man", *chipí* "older sister", and *yoxán* "old woman" to address the person indicated in all the meanings given. ⟨**Bakísha nokon pói bénoibake.** My sister got married yesterday.⟩ ⟨**Aínbora jawen pói betan Rimán káke.** The woman went to Lima with her brother.⟩ 2 : male or female first cousin of the opposite sex ⟨**Nokon poínbichoresa ea chópa patsáxonai.** Only my female cousin washes my clothes for me.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbaonra jawen póibi béneake.** This woman married her own first cousin.⟩ 3 : great-grandson or great-granddaughter of the opposite sex to the grandfather or grandmother 4 : relatives of the same sex and generation that is neither ascending nor descending –Used in the plural form *póibo* to indicate the whole group of relatives who are of the same generation as a specific relative. *syn.* See under **wétsa**
*n.* **poínkinin** [from Shipibo *pói* excrement + *kíni* hole] : anus : rectum : butt
*n.* **poínkoskon** : vulture ⟨**Póinkoskonra pítimawa pisi píai.** The vulture eats dead, rotten fish.⟩
*n.* **poínkosko machítonin** [from Shipibo *poínkosko* vulture + *machíto* machete] : a species of tree with a blackish, machete-shaped pod
*n.* **poínkosko kenchakan** [from Shipibo *poínkosko* vulture + *kenchá* mocahua (a clay bowl)] : kneecap, patella –Rarely used nowadays.
See under **sébe**
See under **jíma**
*n.* **póipoitekerin** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : a species of bluish bird similar to the vaca-muchacho
See under **ráo**
*n.* **poíshinin** : a species of catfish similar to the cunchi but smaller, with blackish-striped fins
*n.* **póitaraman** [from Shipibo *pói* dung + *taránti* to turn over] : beetle
*n.* **póiteren** : firefly *syn.* konkísh

*v.i.* **póia** 1 : to defecate : to relieve oneself : to have a bowel movement ⟨**Rábetira ea westíora néte póiai.** I have a bowel movement twice a day.⟩ 2 : to rust ⟨**Titán xomóxa póike.** Mom's needle has rusted.⟩
See **Pokárapa**

*also* **Pokállpa** *n.* **Pokarapan** *also* **Pokállpanin** [from Quechua *puka* red + *allpa* earth] : Pucallpa ⟨**Maístoro betan ronki bákebo Pokárapain bokánke.** The teacher and his students went to Pucallpa.⟩

*n.* **pokón** 1 : stomach : belly ⟨**Nokon pápashokon shírojane ikátiai Wákapoko.** My grandfather's nickname in Spanish was "cow's stomach."⟩ 2 : guts, intestines *syn.* POKO, ANIPOKO, PORO can all be translated as "belly" or "stomach" with no difference; but POKO and ANIPOKO also have other meanings.
*also* **pókoani** [from Shipibo *áni* big + *póko* stomach] 1 : large intestine 2 : stomach 3 : potbellied : fat
[from Shipibo *beshé* small + *póko* stomach] : small intestine
See **póko**

*n.* **pókotexen** [from Shipibo *póko* stomach + *téxe* left over] : navel ⟨**Báke pikóketian ákanai jawen póko xátekin; jára non ákai pókotexe —akin.** When a child is born, its umbilical cord is cut, and the scar that forms is called the "navel."⟩
*v.t.* **pókoa** : to dye ⟨**Nokon áwininra jawen chitónti pókoke.** My wife dyed her pampanilla skirt.⟩ ⟨**Nokon titán chitóntira moa pokó iki.** Mom's pampanilla skirt is already dyed.⟩
*v.i.* **pókota** : to become dyed, to take dye ⟨**En chópa pókoara jakónhira pokóke.** The cloth I dyed came out looking very nice.⟩ ⟨**Títara pokóke jawen chopa.** Mom dyed her dresses.⟩

*n.* **pokótinin** [from Shipibo *pokóti, poko-* to dye + *-ti* instrument suffix] : dye : coloring agent ⟨**Pokóti bénai káketianra jóni inón chibánke.** A jaguar chased the man when he went to look for dye.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *pokóti* dye] 1 : a species of tree 2 : a species black dye extracted from the *wísopokoti* tree
[from Shipibo *joshín* red + *pokóti* dye] 1 : a species of tree 2 : a species of tan-colored dye extracted from the *joshímpokoti* tree
[from Shipibo *róme* tobacco + *pokóti* dye] : a species of large tree with reddish or brown bark
[from Shipibo *yapá* ochomullaca + *pokóti* dye] : a species of dye made from the bark of the ochomullaca

*n.* **pókoxaten** [from Shipibo *póko* stomach + *xáte* log, chunk] : a species of worm ⟨**Pókoxate méraaxa nokon wétsa ratéke, jáskara oínyosma ikax.** My brother got scared when he saw a *pókoxate* worm for the first time, since he had never seen such a thing.⟩
See under **xáteti**

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *ponyán* arm] 1 : to the arm : on the arm : of the arm ⟨**ponkósh** strong-armed⟩ ⟨**ponskéti** to break one's arm⟩ 2 : to the branch : on the branch : of the branch ⟨**pónxteti** to cut the branch of⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*n.* **ponán** : a species of vine from which fish poison is extracted
*v.i.* **ponchokíita** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *chokíiti* to wash oneself] : to wash one's arm
*v.t.* **pónchota** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *cho,* element of *chókati* to wash] : to wash the arm of
*n.* **ponkán** : punga (a sloping river landing)
*n.* **pónkoron** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : porotohuango (a species of bird) ⟨**Pónkoro bachi piáxa nokon báke chixóke.** My son got diarrhea after eating porotohuango eggs.⟩
*adj.* **pónkoshin** [from Shipibo *pon-* of the arm + *kóshi* strong] : strong-armed : brawny

*n.* **ponón** 1 : vein 2 : artery ⟨**Nokon wetsánra póno xáteke, níshi xáteti shinánkin.** My brother cut an artery when he was trying to cut a vine in the forest.⟩ 3 : tendon ⟨**Pápara ponón chéxaa jóyamake.** Dad didn't come because he has pain in a tendon.⟩

*n.* **pónseman** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arms + *sen,* element of *senénbires* equal] : sloth : pelejo ⟨**Pónseman báke kópiaronki pásnatai.** They say that when a sloth cutipas a child (harms it through spiritual contagion), the child turns pale.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *ponsén* sloth, pelejo] : a species of pelejo (sloth)
*v.i.* **pónsketa** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *sekéti* to break] : to break (an arm or a branch). See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*adj. and n.* **póntekan** [from Shipibo *pónteti, ponte-* to straighten] *adj.* 1 : straight in space ⟨**Janín jíwira ponté iki.** The trunk of the tangarana is quite straight.⟩ 2 : correct ⟨**Rámara moa nokon shinán ponté iki.** At last I have a correct idea.⟩ *n.* : column (e.g., in addition or subtraction operations) ⟨**westíorabo ika ponté** the units column.⟩

*postp.* [from Shipibo *pónteti* to straighten] 1 : right in front of –Also used with the compound suffix *-quea* and *-ax* "from" in the form *póntekeax* "from a place in front of". ⟨**Xóbo pontera jóni yakáke.** A man is sitting right in front of the house.⟩ 2 : in the direction of ⟨**Nato pontera jóni kái.** A man is walking in that direction.⟩ *syn.* See under **bebón**

*v.t.* **póntea** 1 : to straighten ⟨**Joninra jawen métoti yósho pónteai.** The man straightens his crooked index finger.⟩ 2 : to point out as guilty : to accuse : to blame ⟨**En akáma ikenmabira ea póntekanke.** Even though I didn't do it, they accused me.⟩
*v.i.* **pónteta** : to straighten (oneself) ⟨**Nato bakén táera moa janbíx póntetai.** This child's foot is straightening out by itself.⟩
*v.i.* **póntita** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *jotíti* to have a palpitation] : to have a palpitation in the arm
*n.* **pontónkonin** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *tónko* protuberance] : elbow ⟨**Nokon** **pontónkora sóo ike.** My elbow has swollen.⟩
*v.i.* **pónwexeeta** : to scrape one's arm
*v.t.* **pónwexa** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *wéxati* to scrape] : to scrape the arm of. See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*v.t.* **pónxtea** [from Shipibo *pon-* on the arm + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut the arm or branch of : to cut on the arm or on the branch
*n.* **popón** [from Shipibo, imitative of its call] : owl ⟨**Néte xábataitian pópo kéotara nóiba mérati bekánon íkai.** When an owl hoots at dawn, it means someone will come to visit us.⟩
[from Shipibo *káshibo, káshibaon* Cashibo] : a species of owl
*n.* **pópokan** : cocona (a sour orange-fleshed fruit) ⟨**Popóxeatira rama Máioshiain ícha márokanai.** Now they sell a lot of cocona chicha in Pucallpa.⟩
[from Shipibo *bóna* bee + *popó* cocona] : a species of cocona that is not very sour
See under **shimón**
*n.* **Porín** [from Spanish *Apolinario*] –Used as a masculine name.

*n.* **pórisian** [from Shipibo *polikía*] 1 : police; *specif.* : village police ⟨**Róaboyankoniara báritiatibi tiníntinin pórisiabo jíkimakatiai.** Every year the lieutenant governor would install police in **Roaboya**.⟩ 2 : civil guard officer ⟨**Pórisiabora Kakónko bokánke bákeranonbo bénai sóntaro iti.** The guards went to **Kako** looking for young men for military service.⟩
*n.* **pórokan** [from Shipibo *poró* belly] : huingo (a gourd); *specif.* : a hollowed-out huingo *syn.* See under **masén**
*n.* **pórokan** : belly ⟨**Nato bakén poróra kerás iki.** This child's belly is dirty.⟩ *syn.* See under **póko**
*n.* **póroboran** [from Spanish] : gunpowder ⟨**Pórobora kétetaxxa tóo ike. Noara ráteke.** We were startled when the gunpowder exploded as it was lit.⟩
*also* **prófesoro** *n.* **pórojisoronin** [from Spanish] : teacher, professor ⟨**Pórojisoroninra bákebo jawen jáne yóiti iki.** The teacher must tell the students his name.⟩
*n.* **porótonin** [from Quechua *purutu* bean] : bean ⟨**Moara ráma poróto kopíora iki, jénetian ikax.** Now that it's the rainy season, beans are very expensive.⟩

*also* **pósake** *adj.* **pósakanin** *also* **pósaken** [from Quechua *púsak* eight] : eight –The variant *pósake* is rarely used nowadays. ⟨**Pósaka báritia pekaora nokon pápa téetiainoax jóke.** After eight years, my dad returned from work.⟩
See **pósaka**
*n.* **posíchonin** [from Spanish] : small cup, mug ⟨**Westíora rosína posíchora ea mároke nokon jónibo xéamati.** I bought a dozen cups to give my workers something to drink from.⟩
*n.* **posón** [from Spanish] : well (for water)
*n.* **postán** [from Spanish] : health post : medical post

*adj.* **pótakan** : murky, cloudy (of water) ⟨**Jéne potá íketianra yápabo paényamai.** When the water is murky, the fish don't get dazed (disoriented by the murk).⟩ *syn.* POTA, SERO — both can be translated as "murky". POTA suggests a state of water that is less murky, more or less clear, while SERO suggests water that is more opaque and silt-laden.
*v.t.* **potáa** *Konibo* **potáaka** : to make murky : to muddy ⟨**Bákebaonra náshikin jéne potáake.** While bathing, the children muddied the river water.⟩
*v.i.* **pótakaata** [from Shipibo *pótati* to throw away + *-kaa*, reflexive suf.] : to throw oneself away : to be thrown away

*v.t.* **pótaa** 1 : to throw away : to abandon ⟨**Aínbaonra sináxon jawen kotón jenénko pótai.** The woman got angry and is throwing her blouse into the river.⟩ ⟨**Nato bakénra titán koríki potá boónke.** This child took the money his mother had left behind, and she was displeased.⟩ ⟨**Koríki potá biáxa báke ratéke.** The child was left puzzled when he picked up the money that had been abandoned.⟩ 2 : to leave (behind) ⟨**Nokon bákera min xobón en pótai, káchio kakín.** I'm going to leave my child at your house while I go to the forest.⟩ 3 : to divorce ⟨**Wétsa aínboki yoshínxonra jonín jawen awín pótake.** Driven crazy over another woman, the man divorced his wife.⟩ ⟨**Potá aínbora en awínhaa iki.** I have a divorced woman as my wife.⟩

[from Shipibo *ja* that + *potá* thrown away + *-bicho* only + *-res* no more] : just this once : for the first and last time ⟨**Rámara en já potábichores nokon pátoron pácha waránka sóro yókatai, nokon báke isínketian.** For the first and last time, I am going to ask my boss for a hundred thousand soles, since my child is sick.⟩
*v.i.* **pótata** : to become or turn murky –Used regarding water. ⟨**Moara páro potáke.** Now the river water has turned murky.⟩
*n.* **potén** : wooden fishing float
*adj.* **pótekan** [from Shipibo *póteti* to gut] : gutted or disemboweled, partly or completely ⟨**Moa poté pítibora kopí iki.** Fish that have already been gutted are expensive.⟩
*v.i.* **pótekaata** : to be gutted, partly or completely ⟨**Bákera chíchikanin pótekaake.** The child was partly disemboweled by the knife.⟩
*v.t.* **pótea** 1 : to gut ⟨**Nokon poínra bóe póteai.** My sister is gutting the boquichico fish.⟩ 2 : to operate on; *specif.* : to perform surgery on the abdominal cavity of (a patient)
*n.* **potón** : dust of any kind

[from Shipibo *átsa* manioc + *póto* powder/flour] : fariña (toasted manioc flour) ⟨**Kónxaman téekinra non átsapotores pikátiai.** When we worked in the cedar, we ate only fariña.⟩ ⟨**Rashíkobaonronki átsapotoati onányorake.** They say Brazilians are real experts at making fariña.⟩
[from Shipibo *mái* earth + *póto* dust] : dust from the ground ⟨**Máioshinyainra máipoto íchaira iki.** There is a lot of dust in Pucallpa.⟩

*adj.* **pótokan** 1 : full : stuffed : satiated : sated ⟨**Manxánra potó ikax nóyayamai.** The heron doesn't fly when it's stuffed.⟩ 2 : gluttonous 3 : pot-bellied : fat ⟨**Potó ínaketianra en ichátama píai.** I don't eat much because I don't want to become pot-bellied.⟩ *syn.* bócho; bónaya
*v.t.* **potóaa** *Konibo* **potóaka** : to fill up : to make full : to stuff ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke potóake.** The woman fed her child until he was full.⟩
See under **chámpo**
*v.i.* **pótoa** : to become dusty ⟨**Oi béyamaketianra moa bái pótoke.** Since it didn't rain, the path became dusty.⟩
*v.i.* **pótota** : to be satisfied (with food or drink) : to be full : to be sated ⟨**Eara chichán potóke.** I got full from the chicha.⟩

*v.t.* **pótsia** : to squeeze in order to extract the contents of; *specif.* : to milk ⟨**Enra piróta pótsixon éxpaake.** I deflated the ball by squeezing it.⟩ ⟨**Nokon titánra wákaxoma pótsiai.** My mother is milking the cow.⟩ *syn.* See under **bitáxti**

*v.i.* **pótsita** : to squeeze oneself to release contents; *specif.* : to be milked ⟨**Nato báke ésteara janbíx pótsitai, níwe jokónhakasi.** This child with a bloated belly squeezes himself to force the air out of his stomach.⟩ ⟨**Yamékiritibira wákaxoma pótsitai.** The milk cow is milked every day.⟩
*v.i.* **pótsita** : to take shape with a nice contour (e.g., a canoe)
*n.* 1 : a species of tree 2 : a type of dye extracted from the *potsótsori* tree

*v.t.* **póxaa** : to knock down : to bring down : to fell ⟨**Ea póxaketianra ea ochítinin natéxke.** The dog bit me when someone knocked me down.⟩ ⟨**Papánra rabé néte xóno póxake.** Dad felled the lupuna tree in two days.⟩ ⟨**Jiwi poxá ikáinra ochíti siná iki.** Where the fallen tree is, there is a fierce dog.⟩ *syn.* taréti

*n.* **poxkón** : a species of shirúe similar to the carachamillo, but about four or five centimeters long ⟨**Póxkora báke pimayamakanai, chixónaketian.** Children are forbidden to eat the *póxko* type of shirúe so that it doesn't give them diarrhea.⟩
*v.i.* **póxota** : to fall over (something standing) ⟨**Pirótanin pénitaxa ea poxóke.** I fell when I stepped on the ball.⟩ *syn.* See under **máanti**

*n.* **póyaman** 1 : arm ⟨**Kóshi jónibaon poyánronki mískomiskobires iki.** They say strong men's arms are very muscular.⟩ 2 : branch ⟨**Shankón bíaitianra jóni jabuen póyaman réteke.** The branch of the uvilla (a tree grape) fell and killed the man while he was gathering its fruit.⟩

*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *r* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *yóra* body] 1 : on the body : to the body : in the body : from the body ⟨**racháti** to bruise on the body⟩ 2 : on the outside : over the outside : from the outside ⟨**rachóti** to wash on the outside⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.4

*mood suf.* –Used to mark the indicative mood of the sentence. –Used added to the first word or phrase of the sentence, provided this is not the main verb. –Used after the root of the main verb when it comes first in the sentence. –Used in the prefixed form *r-* added to *iqui*, the present indicative form of *íti* "to be," giving the form *ríki*. ⟨**Eara moa kái.** I'm already going.⟩ ⟨**–¿Kákia min títa réboki? –Kárake.** –Did your mother go upriver? –Yes; she went.⟩ ⟨**Nokon pápa riki.** He is my father.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.1
*v.t.* ráana : to send ⟨**Onibirisitaro átira nokon báke en Rimán ráanke.** I sent my son to Lima to do university studies.⟩
[from Shipibo *jéne meran* into the water + *ráanti* to send] : to let fall into the water ⟨**Píkeronra jawen báke jéne meran ráanke.** Pedro let his son fall into the water.⟩

*v.i.* ráaxea [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *áxeti* to learn] : for the body to get used to or acclimatize ⟨**Epán yórara moa barín iki ráaxeke.** My uncle's body is already getting used to the sunny climate.⟩

*adj.* rábekan *Konibo* rábetan [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *betan* with] : two ⟨**Eara átapa rábekan kéenai; mónsora kéenai rábe ochítibaken.** I want two hens, and at the same time the mestizo wants two puppies.⟩

*modifying suf.* –Used to indicate imperfect tense for a period from nine or ten months up to three or four years in the past. ⟨**Máioshiainra péixobo járabeke, ramara yámake.** Before, about three years ago, there were indeed palm-thatch houses in Pucallpa, but now there are none.⟩
See under **shinán**
*v.i.* rábeta : to be together (two people) : to stay close ⟨**Píkerora jawen pápa betan rábetai jóni tímakasi.** Pedro and his father stay close together because a man wants to hit him.⟩
*adv.* **rebéakin** [from Shipibo *rabé, rabet-* + *-i, -akin*, subordinate-verb suf.] : twice
*adj.* **rabétiatonin** [from Shipibo *rabéti* twice + *-ya* having] : even (of a number) ⟨**Chóskora nómiro rabétia iki.** Four is an even number.⟩

*also* **rabíti** *v.i.* **rábikaata** *also* **rábita** [from Shipibo *rabíti* to praise + *-kaa* also *-t*, reflexive suf.] : to boast ⟨**Antónyora rábikaatai kírika onán ikax áni jémabo ónanax.** Antonio boasts because he knows how to read and knows big cities.⟩ ⟨**Enbíxa ea rabíamai.** I don't boast about myself.⟩

*adj.* **rabíman** 1 : ashamed : shameful ⟨**Rabín riki noa yómetsoa onánkanti.** It is shameful for us to be found out that we have stolen something.⟩ 2 : shy ⟨**Tomás riki rabín joni; aínbo keska.** Tomás is a shy man; like a woman.⟩
*adj.* **rabínhomatonin** : shameless ⟨**Jóni rabínhoma ixónra ea yométsoake.** A shameless man robbed me.⟩

*n.* **rabín jawekinin** [from Shipibo *rabín* shameful + *jawéki* thing] : private parts : body parts used for sexual relations, defecation, and urination —Used in the singular form but with plural meaning.

*v.i.* **rábina** 1 : to be or feel ashamed ⟨**Nokon nónti jakóma íketianra ea rabínke.** I have been ashamed of my canoe because it is poorly made.⟩ 2 : to be shy (e.g., before a person) ⟨**Eara Tomáski rábinai, katánwe míabicho.** I am shy before Tomás; that's why you go alone.⟩
*also* **Tabíri** *also* **Dabídi** *n.* **Rabírin** *also* **Tabírin** *also* **Dabídin** [from Spanish *David*] —Used as a masculine name.

*v.t.* **rábia** : to praise : to compliment; *also* : to worship ⟨**Nonra Riós rábiai.** We worship God.⟩ ⟨**Titánra nokon pói métsakan rábike.** Mother praised my sister for her beauty.⟩ ⟨**Xekán piára mechán rábi-** **kanai.** They praise Sheca's nephew for his skill at fishing.⟩
*n.* **rabón** [from Spanish] : nail ⟨**Rabón tábara tásanon awe.** Let's nail the board with the nails.⟩
*Konibo* **ránboxo** *n.* **ráboxonin** *Konibo* **ránboxon** *also* **ránboxonin** : knee ⟨**Mia riki ránboxo áni.** You have a big knee.⟩
*v.t.* **ráchata** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *chákati* to bruise] : to bruise the body of
*v.i.* **ráchokiita** [from Shipibo *rachóti* to wash the body of + *-kii*, reflexive suf.] : to wash one's own body
*v.t.* **ráchota** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *chókati* to wash] 1 : to wash the body of 2 : to wash on the outside
*adj.* **raén** : tame
*n.* **ráenanaiton** : close friend : special companion
*v.i.* **ráeanana** [from Shipibo *ráe* tame + *-anan* mutually + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to play together as companions

*v.t.* **ráeaa** *Konibo* **ráeaka** : to tame ⟨**Nokon epánra bína ráeai.** My uncle, my maternal aunt's husband, tames wasps.⟩ ⟨**Meráyaninra onsá yoshínbo ráeai.** The shaman tames terrible demons.⟩
*v.i.* **ráea** : to become tame ⟨**En yáwa báke biára ráeke ishtónbires.** The baby huangana (white-lipped peccary) I caught has become tame very quickly.⟩
*n.* **ráibon** *Konibo* **ráibaon** *pish.* **ráibaen** : kings ⟨**Moátianra ípaonike áni jemánkobo ráibo jaí.** Long ago there were kings in the big towns.⟩

*v.t.* **raínshaka** [from Shipibo *raínsh*, imitative of the sound + *-ati* to make] : to let slip ⟨**Enra wáme cháchikin raínshake, yópa ixon.** When I speared a paiche (arapaima), I let it slip because I'm clumsy at fishing.⟩
*v.i.* **raínshika** : to fall while slipping ⟨**Westíora xóntakonra jawen ránboxo bishkóke raínshikin.** A certain young lady, slipping, fell on her knees and scraped them.⟩
*v.i.* **ráisikiita** : to check oneself over ⟨**Jónira chópa sáweax ráisikiitai.** The man checks himself over after getting dressed.⟩
See **Ráwaira**
*v.t.* **rákana** : to lay down : to make lie down ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke rakánke.** The woman made her little son lie down.⟩

*v.i.* **rákata** 1 : to lie down ⟨**Eara yoná akí báchi meran rakáke.** I am lying in the mosquito net with a fever.⟩ 2 : to lie stretched out ⟨**Kapéisira óonno rakáke.** A big lagarto (caiman) is lying far off there.⟩

*n.* **rakátinin** [from Shipibo *rakáti, raka-* to lie down + *-ti* instrument with which] : bed : stretcher ⟨**Jóni ísinaira rakátinin ápake kana iki.** They brought the sick man down on a stretcher.⟩
*n.* **rákatoron** [from Spanish] : tractor
*v.t.* **rákawaa** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *káwati* to wrap] : to wrap the body of ⟨**Enra nokon báke chopán rákawai.** I wrap my little son in a cloth.⟩

*adj.* **ráketen** *Konibo* **rákekan** [from Shipibo *rakéti, rake-* to be afraid] 1 : fearful : timid ⟨**Non ániboronki raké ípaonike.** They say our ancestors were a fearful people.⟩ 2 : cowardly ⟨**Mía riki raké; éa riki rakéma.** You are a coward; I am brave.⟩ *syn.* RAKE, YOSMA — both can be translated as "coward." RAKE, then, tends to imply a momentary fear, while YOSMA implies a more permanent condition of being fearful.

*v.t.* **rakéaa** *Konibo* **rakéaka** 1 : to frighten ⟨**Eara inón rakéake.** The jaguar frightened me.⟩ 2 : to threaten ⟨**Titánra nokon wétsa rakéake, ráo xéanon ixon.** Mother threatened my little brother so he would take the medicine.⟩
*v.i.* **ráketa** : to be afraid ⟨**Béne ikaxa noa tsókibi rakéyamai.** Because we are real men, we are not afraid of anyone.⟩ ⟨**Eara nokon rawíki ráketai.** I am afraid of my enemy.⟩

*n.* **rákexto paróyaton** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *kextó* thick + *paróya* square] : cube ⟨**Rákexto paróyariki kája keska: jatíbi jawen paróbo senénbires.** A cube is like a box, and all its sides are equal.⟩

*adj.* **rakéyosman** [from Shipibo *rakéti, rake-* to be afraid + *-yosma* one who never does (a specific thing)] : one who knows no fear : fearless ⟨**Nato rakéyosmanra ochíti siná chíbanai.** This fearless man is following the fierce dog.⟩
*n.* **Rakírin** *Konibo* **Rakírinin** [from Spanish *Rakel*] –Used as a feminine name.

*v.t.* **rákota** : to wrap : to cover up ⟨**Bakenra mónika chopán rákoke.** The girl wrapped the doll in a cloth.⟩ ⟨**Moa rakóra en chópabo béke.** I brought the cloths already wrapped.⟩ *syn.* káwati
*v.i.* **rákota** : to wrap oneself up : to cover oneself ⟨**Matsínakara nokon títayoxan rákotai rakótinin.** My grandmother covers herself with the blanket when she is cold.⟩
*n.* **rakótinin** [from Shipibo *rakóti, rako-* to wrap, to cover + *-ti* instrument with which] : blanket ⟨**Rakótinin mápowe ja pítso.** Cover that pihuicho (parrot chick) with the blanket.⟩
*adv.* : now : already ⟨**Rámara non káibobo káochonin téeyamai.** Now our fellow countrymen no longer work with rubber.⟩ *syn.* moa
[from Shipibo *ráma* now + *néte, netén* day] : today : nowadays ⟨**Ráma neténra ea Maióshiain kái.** Today I am going to Pucallpa.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.5
*adv.* [from Shipibo *ráma* now + *-ma* not] : a long time ago : years ago ⟨**— ¿Jáwetian mia Ikítoainoax joárin? —Ramáma ea joní riki.** —When did you come from Iquitos? —I came years ago.⟩
See under **ráma**
*v.t.* **rámana** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *manánti* to feel/palpate] : to feel the body of
*adv.* [from Shipibo *ráma* now + *-tian* when] : at this time
*adj.* **rámayan** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *mayá* curve, turn] : circular in shape
*v.t.* **rámayaa** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *máyati* to turn] : to twist : to twist the stem of ⟨**Papánra níshi rámayai.** Papa twists the vine.⟩

*v.i.* **raménoota** [from Shipibo *raménoti* to burn the body of + *-oo*, reflexive suf.] : to burn one's own body ⟨**Chíiki páketaxa, báke íorai raménooke.** Falling onto the fire, the girl burned her body badly.⟩
*v.t.* **raménoa** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *ménoti* to burn] : to burn the body of. See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*adj.* **ramín** 1 : bad : evil : wicked ⟨**Pikeró mía riki rámi.** Pedro, you are bad.⟩ 2 : cursed –In this sense used as a vocative in the form *ramí*. *syn.* See under **jakóma**

*v.t.* **rámiaa** *Konibo* **rámiaka** 1 : to ruin : to break ⟨**Enra nokon pátoron móto rámiake.** I ruined my boss's motorbike.⟩ 2 : to mistreat ⟨**Nokon áwininra ea rámiai.** My wife treats me very badly.⟩ 3 : to make a mistake in (a task to be done) ⟨**En wishaa iki chónka jói. Kímisha en rámia iki.** I wrote ten words, and I made mistakes in three.⟩ *syn.* See under **masáati**
*v.t.* **ramíaka** : to curse ⟨**Bakénra jabé báke ramíake.** The boy cursed his companion.⟩ *syn.* jakómati
*v.i.* **rámita** 1 : to break down ⟨**Abionra bóchikiax ramíke.** *The airplane broke down in flight.*⟩ 2 : to become bad ⟨**Anara jabé aínboki ramíke.** Ana has become mean toward her companion.⟩
*n.* **Rámoman** [from Spanish] –Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **rampán** [from Spanish] : hoe ⟨**Ráo bitánwe, rampánra ea taxbtéke.** Go get medicine; I've cut my foot with the hoe.⟩
*n.* **rampáran** [from Quechua *lampára*, itself from Spanish] : lamp ⟨**Rampára néri bewé.** Bring the lamp over here.⟩
*n.* **rampárinin** [from Spanish *lamparín*] : oil lamp; *also* : torch ⟨**Rampárin ketéatanwe yaméyora riki.** Light the oil lamp because it's very dark.⟩
*n.* **rampépinin** [from Shipibo *ran-* on the knee + *pépi*, unidentified element] : back of the knee ⟨**Rampépi kerásbiresiki mía.** The back of your knee is very dirty.⟩
*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *ránboxo* knee] : on the knee : of the knee : to the knee ⟨**rantsínti** for one's knee to become less swollen⟩
*v.t.* **ranáwea** : to hide ⟨**nin jawébi ranáweyamai** not hiding anything⟩
*v.t.* **ránbea** : to turn over : to flip ⟨**Non ánibaonronki xáwe ránbekatikanai máshimea.** They say our ancestors used to flip charapas (river turtles) over to catch them.⟩

*v.i.* **ránbeta** : to turn over ⟨**Nokon bótira ranbéke, béchoman ompáx bóchoaka.** My boat capsized because the wave filled it with water.⟩ ⟨**Nokon bákera moa ránbetai píchika óxeyanix.** My son already rolls over at five months of age.⟩
*n.* **ranchón** : female friend; *also* : female cousin -Used especially in the vocative form *ranchó* to call someone.
*v.i.* **ránchoshita** [from Shipibo *ran-* on the knee + *choshíti* to bump oneself] : to bump one's own knee
*n.* **ranénkenin** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *nenké* long] : rectangle ⟨**Ranénke senéma iki jawen paróbo.** A rectangle has unequal sides.⟩

*n.* **ranín** 1 : body hair ⟨**Papán ponyán rani riki kextó.** Papa has thick hair on his arms.⟩ 2 : bristles ⟨**Kóchira ránia iki.** Pigs have bristles.⟩ 3 : wool ⟨**Káraniro ráni riki já chópaati.** Sheep's wool is used to make cloth.⟩ 4 : feather ⟨**Bakénra átapa rani ménoke yóitima ixon; ménoxonra já píke.** The boy burned a hen's feathers because he's very mischievous, and after burning them he ate them.⟩ *syn.* péi
*also* **Dáníiri** *n.* **Raníirin** *also* **Daníirin** [from Spanish *Daniel*] -Used as a masculine name.
*n.* **Rankón** –Used as a masculine name.

*n.* **ránokan** : jealousy *syn.* RANOYA, RANOMIS, YOIMIS all carry the sense of "jealous" or "with jealousy," but YOIMIS, unlike RANOYA or RANOMIS, implies continuous jealousy even without an evident cause.

*adj.* **ránomiston** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *nóiti, noi-* to love, to want + *-mis* one who always does (a specific thing)] : jealous ⟨**Eara ránomis iki; nokon awínra en ránoai.** I am jealous; I feel jealousy over my wife.⟩
*n.* **ránoman** : boy : youth under thirteen years old ⟨—**Jakón yamékiri, ranón.** —**Jakón yamékiri, koshí.** —Good morning, young man. —Good morning, boss.⟩ *syn.* bákebenbo
*v.t.* **ránoa** : to be jealous of : to feel jealousy over ⟨**Jóamanra jawen awín ránoai.** Juan feels jealous over his wife.⟩
*n.* **ransán** [from Spanish *danza*] : dance
*v.i.* **ránsaa** : to dance ⟨**Píkerora ránsai kái.** Pedro is going to dance.⟩
*n.* **rantónkonin** [from Shipibo *ran-* on the knee + *tónko* bump/protuberance] : kneecap ⟨**Rantónkoninra ea chéxai ea xeyówe.** My kneecap hurts; rub it for me.⟩
*v.i.* **rántsina** [from Shipibo *ran-* on the knee + *tsínati* to reduce swelling] : for one's knee to become less swollen
*n.* **Rantsískonin** *also* **Rantsín** [from Spanish *Frankisko*] -Used as a masculine name.
*v.i.* **ránxika** : to snore ⟨**Nokon pápara óxaax ránxikai.** My father snores when he sleeps.⟩

*n.* **raón** 1 : plant-based medicine ⟨**Ráo bitánwe non Moísis raónon.** Go get plant medicine to cure Moisés.⟩ 2 : medicine; *specif.* : pill ⟨**Botikainra ráo ícha jáke.** There are many medicines at the pharmacy.⟩ 3 : plant poison 4 : antidote ⟨**Báwarono riki ráooma.** The bite of the loro machaco (a venomous snake) has no antidote.⟩
[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *ráo* medicine] : a species of tree with soft wood, bark similar to that of cedro (cedar), and resin like that of chuchuhuasi, used to treat gonorrhea
[from Shipibo *kapé, kápeten* lagarto (caiman) + *ráo* medicine] : a species of plant whose sap is mixed with water and drunk as a potion to induce ferocity
[from Shipibo *kapé, kápeten* lagarto (caiman) + *táwi* bile/gall + *ráo* medicine] : a species of plant not yet well identified
[from Shipibo *kapé, kápeten* lagarto (caiman) + *tséwe* cut + *ráo* medicine] : espintana (a tree species)
[from Shipibo *kopítso, kopítsonin* cupiso + *ráo* medicine] : a species of plant not yet well identified
[from Shipibo *wanín* pijuayo (peach palm) + *káya* soul + *ráo* medicine] : huara caspi (a tree species)

[from Shipibo *wísoino* yanapuma (black jaguar-spirit) + *ráo* medicine] : a species of blackish shrub, with leaves shaped like animal ears, from whose bark a juice is extracted that, boiled and drunk, makes one fierce
[from Shipibo *jíwi* tree + *ráo* medicine] : any of various tree-derived remedies
[from Shipibo *máwati, mawa-* to die + *ráo* poison] : deadly poison
[from Shipibo *maín, máiman* acarahuasú] : a species of tree used as a house post
[from Shipibo *máke, makén* paña (piranha)] : a species of plant not yet well identified
[from Shipibo *mécha* good hunter + *ráo* medicine] : any of various potions used to make one a good hunter
[from Shipibo *nóiti, noi-* to love + *-ti* instrument with which + *ráo* medicine] : any of various potions for making someone fall in love
[from Shipibo *nósha, noshán* shuyo + *ráo* medicine] : a species of plant whose boiled bark juice is used to treat diarrhea
[from Shipibo *pói* excrement + *ráo* medicine] : plant-based purgative
[from Shipibo *rayáti, raya-* to become hardworking + *-ti* instrument with which] : any of various potions given to cure the lazy
[from Shipibo *ronón ewa, ronón ewan* boa + *tséwe* cut of ushate (machete) + *ráo* medicine] : a species of plant used to treat various illnesses or dislocations
[from Shipibo *sináti, sina-* to become angry + *-ti* instrument with which + *ráo* medicine] : any of various potions one drinks to become furious
[from Shipibo *xae, xaén* anteater + *ráo* medicine] : a species of plant not yet well identified
[from Shipibo *yoná* fever + *ráo* medicine] : lancetilla (a medicinal plant)
*v.t.* **raóaa** *Konibo* **raóaka** : to decorate ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen xóbo raóai píshtaanonxon.** The woman decorates her house for the party.⟩
*n.* **ráomaton** [from Shipibo *ráo* medicine + *-ma* not] : any of various non-medicinal plant species

*v.i.* **ráomeeta** [from Shipibo *ráo, raón* medicine, poison + *-mee* reflexive suf. + *-ti* infinitive suf.] 1 : to treat oneself with medicine or a magic potion 2 : to poison oneself ⟨**Jónira janbïsh ráomeeke.** A man poisoned himself.⟩

*n.* **raómiston** [from Shipibo *raónti, raon-* to treat with medicine + *-mis* one who always does] : an herbalist who prepares remedies to cure or potions to cause harm -Often used as a modifier of the following noun. ⟨**Ráonmis aínbaonra jato réteai.** The herbalist woman kills people.⟩
See under **níshi**

*v.t.* **ráona** 1 : to treat with medicine or a magic potion 2 : to give pills to ⟨**Raómistonra nokon báke ísinai raónke.** The health worker gave pills to my sick son.⟩ 3 : to poison ⟨**Aínboanra jawen rawí raónke.** The woman poisoned her rival.⟩ 4 : to apply poison to (e.g., a weapon) ⟨**Nokon papánra wéxati ráonai, jawen rawí wéxaa mawánon ixon.** My father is applying poison to his ushate (machete) so that his enemy will die when he cuts him on the neck.⟩ *syn.* mókaati
*n.* : a species of tree with bark and trunk similar to those of huito, and reddish wood
*also* **Láora** *n.* **Ráoranin** *also* **Láoranin** [from Spanish *Laura*] -Used as a feminine name.
*also* **Kláodio** *n.* **Ráorion** *also* **Kláodion** [from Spanish *Klaudio*] –Used as a masculine name.
*v.i.* **ráota** : to put on adornments ⟨**Aínbora ráota iki mérati kánox.** The woman put on her adornments to go for a walk.⟩
*n.* **raótinin** : adornments ⟨**Nokon titán raóti riki ícha.** My mother's adornments are many.⟩

*adj.* **ráoxan** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *jóxo* white] 1 : half-ripe : starting to ripen 2 : of a skin tone halfway between brown and white ⟨**Min báke píkotara raóxtani iki.** Your baby was born with a half-white skin tone.⟩
*n.* **ráoxobon** [from Shipibo *ráo* medicine + *xóbo* house] : center (e.g., hospital, clinic, health post, or pharmacy) where medicines are found *syn.* járamasia; ospítaro
*adj.* **ráoyanin** : having plant medicines, amulets, potions, or other magical objects ⟨**Nato jónira ráoya iki.** This man has plant medicines.⟩
*adj.* **raóyaton** : adorned : having adornments ⟨—**¡Oínta aínbo raóya! —Méeyamawe ibánonka raóya.** —Look at that adorned woman! —Leave her be with her adornments.⟩

*v.t.* **rapéstea** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *pe-* on the back + *xáteti* to cut] : to shear ⟨**Papánra ochíti rapésteke chíkiri néeketian jawen píshpachiain.** Papa sheared the dog because gum had stuck to its side.⟩

*also* **trapíche** *n.* **rapíchinin** *also* **trapíchinin** [from Spanish] : sugar-cane press ⟨**Páeribaonronki non ánibo rapíchiati onámanike.** They say that long ago the friars taught our ancestors to build sugar-cane presses.⟩ ⟨**Nokon papán rapíchi. Rapíchininra non xáwi móxai.** This is my father's sugar-cane press. The cane is ground with the press.⟩
*n.* **rápisin** [from Spanish] : pencil ⟨**Eara rapís kéenai titá.** Mama, I want a pencil.⟩

*n.* **rápoinin** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *pói* excrement] : mold : rust ⟨**Bixón óina tóo ati moa rápoia íketianra, en pótaibake.** When I picked up the shotgun, I saw it was already rusted, and I threw it away.⟩ *syn.* RAPOI, YAMIPOI — both can be translated as "mold" or "rust" without any difference. Note that EMO can also be translated as "mold," but with emphasis on mold produced by fungi.

*n.* **rárebon** *Konibo* **rárebaon** *pish.* **rárebaen** : relative ⟨**Non rárebobaonra noa nóike.** Our relatives love us.⟩ ⟨**Misionirobora jaton rárebo jénebeirani Piróri békana iki.** The missionaries came to Peru leaving their relatives behind.⟩

*adj.* **rárebokeskatonin** [from Shipibo *rárebo* relative + *keska* like] : friend ⟨**Noa jábo betan ráenanai ikax iki misionirobo non rárebokeska; Ríosen janénko non rárebo.** Since we have become friends with the missionaries, they are our friends; in other words, our relatives in the name of God.⟩ *syn.* jóncho

*n.* **rárionin** [from Spanish] 1 : radio 2 : tape recorder ⟨**Senényoin jawen rárionin noa Sankénbea béwaitian ninkámaara, onís iki.** When Senényoi played Sankénbea for us on his tape recorder, it was nostalgic.⟩
*v.i.* **rároa** : to be glad ⟨**Jawen báke Rimámeax nokóketianra, títa rároke.** When her son arrived from Lima, the mother was glad.⟩ *syn.* See under **béneti**
*also* **Lásaro** *n.* **Rásaron** *also* **Lásaron** *Konibo* **Rásaronin** [from Spanish *Lázaro*] –Used as a masculine name.

*n.* **rásaro isiman** [from Shipibo *rásaro* Lazarus (the sick beggar of Luke 16:20 in the New Testament) + *isín* sickness] : leprosy ⟨**Rásaro isinra néno yámatanike; Ajírika jemánres ícha jónibo rásaroya iki.** Leprosy barely exists around here; in Africa, though, there are many people with leprosy.⟩

*adj.* **rásaroyatonin** [from Shipibo *rásaro*, element of *rásaroya isin* leprosy + *-ya* without] : sick with leprosy : leprous ⟨**Joán riki rásaroya; ochó ráankanwe jáinoax mawánon.** Juan is a leper; send him far away so he can die over there.⟩ ⟨**Miara rásaroya iki** **akin Tomás ákanara sináke.** When they told Tomás he was a leper, he became bitter.⟩
*v.t.* **rásaka** : to destroy : to tear apart ⟨**Niwénra xóbo rásake.** The wind tore the house apart.⟩
*n.* **ráseneman** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *senén* equal] : square ⟨**Rásenenra senénbobires iki jawen chósko paróbo.** A square always has its four sides equal.⟩ *syn.* See under **páro**

*n.* **rashíkon** *Konibo* **rashíkonin** [from regional Spanish brashico; itself from Spanish *brasilero* + *-ico* *suf.* *adj.*] 1 : brashico : Brazilian 2 : Brazilian –Used in this sense with an initial capital *R.* ⟨**Rashikoninronki boí jóniakana tímanike.** They say that in ancient times the Brazilian punched an image made of pitch.⟩ 3 : black man : person of the black race

*v.i.* **rásika** : to fall apart ⟨**Táxa tsákaaxara tapán rásike.** Upon hitting a log, the raft fell apart.⟩ ⟨**Robíriton xóbora rásikai páyo ikax.** Roberto's house is already falling apart because it's very old.⟩

*v.i.* **rásoikiita** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *sóikiiti* to rub oneself] : to rub (e.g., dry) one's body ⟨**Kósira chopán rásoikitai jawen yóra mechá iketian.** José is drying himself with a towel because he is wet.⟩
*n.* **rásoikiitinin** [from Shipibo *rásoikiiti, rásoikii-* to rub + *-ti* instrument with which] : towel ⟨jabón, **rásoikiiti jáinoax bóexeeti** soap, towel, and comb⟩ *syn.* payón

*n. and adj.* **rástoman** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *-s*, unidentified element + *tónko* protuberance] *n.* : girth of a circumference ⟨**Nato jiwín rastón non topónke rabé chónka píchika táeya.** We measured the circumference of this tree and it was twenty-five feet.⟩ *adj.* 1 : thick in circumference ⟨**xóno xate riki rastónyora.** The lupuna log is very thick.⟩ 2 : deep *syn.* See under **kextó**
*v.i.* **rástona** : to grow thicker in width ⟨**Nato xónora moa rástonai réranon akanwe.** This lupuna (tree) is already getting thicker; let's cut it down together.⟩
*n.* **ratán** [from Spanish] : tin can ⟨**Ráta meranra non ícha jawéki bénxoai.** We keep many things in cans.⟩ ⟨**Chónka ráta ea bexonwe jawéoma.** Bring me ten empty cans.⟩
*n.* **rátekan** [from Shipibo *ráteti, rate-* to scare] : fright ⟨**Rátekanra títayoxan mawáke.** The grandmother died of fright.⟩

*v.t.* **rátea** 1 : to scare ⟨**Mínra ea ráteke.** You scared me.⟩ 2 : to wake up (someone) ⟨**Mínra min wétsa óxaketian ráteke.** You woke up your little brother while he was sleeping.⟩ 3 : to surprise; *also* : to leave perplexed or confused syn. jishténhati; onsáati
*v.i.* **ráteta** 1 : to get scared ⟨**Ratéyamawe baké.** Don't be scared, son.⟩ 2 : to wake up with a start 3 : to be surprised : to be left perplexed or confused
*also* **latín joi** *n.* **ratín join** *also* **latín join** [from Spanish *latín* + Shipibo *jói* language] : Latin : the language of the Romans
*n.* **ratón** [from Spanish] : plate ⟨**Ea rabé ráto máromawe.** Sell me two plates.⟩ syn. See under **kenchá**
*n.* **rátokan** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *totó* speckled] : body speckled with small spots
*adj. and n.* **rátonronin** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *tonrón* sphere] *adj.* : cylindrical *n.* : cylinder
*v.i.* **rátota** : to become dotted with spots on the body
*v.t.* **rátota** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *tópiti* to go gathering] : to pick (e.g., flies) off a surface one by one –Used, e.g., of an chuncho (a jungle fowl) chick.

*v.i.* **rátsokasa** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *tsokásti* to be uncomfortable] : to have an uncomfortable or grimy body ⟨**Eara rátsokasai, náshiama ikáx.** My body feels uncomfortable because I haven't bathed.⟩
*v.i.* **rátsota** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *tso-*, unidentified element (cf. *mátsoti* to rub one's head) + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to rub one's own body
*n.* **Rawán** –Used as a masculine name.
*also* **Rájaira** *n.* **Ráwairon** *also* **Rájairon** [from Spanish *Rafael*] –Used as a masculine name.
*v.i.* **ráwaa** : to walk (of an insect) on something specific ⟨**Jímara nokon pokónko ráwake.** An ant was walking on my belly.⟩
*n.* **ráwikan** : enemy (e.g., through rivalry); *specif.* : either of two men who are rivals or enemies ⟨**Nokon ráwikanra ea tímake paénketian.** My enemy hit me when I was drunk.⟩
*v.t.* **rawíaa** *Konibo* **rawíaka** : to become an enemy of : to have as an enemy ⟨**Enra Sína rawíake.** I have Sína as an enemy.⟩

*v.i.* **ráwinana** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *-anan*, indicating reciprocity + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to pass each other going in opposite directions ⟨**Abion rabéra bóchikiax ráwinananke íjirisisio aki.** Two airplanes passed each other performing maneuvers in the air.⟩

*v.t.* **ráwina** [from Shipibo *ran-* on the knee + *wínoti* to pass] : to pass in the same direction as : to overtake (someone caught up to) ⟨**Motóronin kakínra nontín bóaibo non rawínke.** Going by motor (motorboat), we caught up to and passed those going by canoe.⟩
*v.i.* **ráwita** : to become an enemy ⟨**Ja jóninra ea rawíake.** That man has become my enemy.⟩

*Konibo* **raxká** *n.* **ráxkaman** *Konibo* **ráxkakan** [from Shipibo *ra-* on the body + *xaká* shell] : large scale ⟨**Wáme raxka riki áni; bóe maín, payári, ámakiri, keshó jábo riki raxkáya.** The scales of the paiche (a giant Amazon fish) are large; the boquichico, the acarahuasú, the arahuana, the gamitana, and the bujurqui also have scales.⟩ ⟨**Jenényoshinbaon péikorikironkiki wáme raxkan.** They say that the banknotes of the yacurunas (water spirits) are the large scales of the paiche.⟩

*adj.* **ráyakan** [from Shipibo *rayáti, raya-* to become hardworking] 1 : hardworking : one who works hard and willingly ⟨**Icha jónibora rároai, jaton awínbo rayá íketian.** Many men are happy because their wives are hardworking.⟩ 2 : a constellation called "The Worker," not yet identified with certainty. –Used in this sense written with an initial capital *R.* syn. RAYA, TEETAI, TEEYA all translate as "hardworking," but RAYA implies more the love of work of one who never wants to be idle, while TEEYA implies only the disposition to properly carry out necessary tasks. TEETAI means "hardworking" without implying anything about the quality of the work.
*v.i.* **ráyata** : to become industrious or hardworking ⟨**Nokon bákera rayáke, chikísh ítibi.** My son has become industrious even though he used to be lazy.⟩
See under **ráo**
See under **wáste**
*n.* **ráyoman** : llavarachi (a type of frog) ⟨**Rayónra jojóiamai keóresai jéne meranoax.** The llavarachi doesn't bark, it croaks in the water.⟩

*n.* **ráyosin** *Konibo* **ráyosen** [from Shipibo *ra-* kinship element + *-yosi* elder] 1 : father-in-law; *also* : mother-in-law ⟨**Nokon rayós iki nóimis.** My father-in-law is kind.⟩ 2 : son-in-law –Used in this sense more among speakers of Konibo. *syn.* RAYOS, BAKENKI both translate as "father-in-law"; but BAKENKI, although now little used, denotes a woman's father-in-law; while RAYOS, although it can also denote a woman's father-in-law, traditionally denotes a man's father-in-law. It should also be noted that RAYOS, unlike BAKENKI, has other kinship senses besides "father-in-law".

*n.* **rayósainbaon** [from Shipibo *rayós* mother-in-law + *aìnbo* woman] : a man's mother-in-law –Used mostly among speakers of Konibo. ⟨**Nokon wetsán rayósainbora jakóma shinánya iki.** My brother's mother-in-law is very mean.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *rekín* nose] 1 : to the nose : on the nose : through the nose : of the nose ⟨**rechóshti** to bump someone on the nose⟩ ⟨**reskéti** to break one's nose⟩ 2 : to the nasal septum : on the nasal septum : through the nasal septum : of the nasal septum ⟨**répeti** perforation through the nasal septum⟩ 3 : to the nose : on the nose : of the nose ⟨**réxni** nose hairs⟩ 4 : to the snout : on the snout : through the snout : of the snout ⟨**renénkekochi** long-snouted pig⟩ 5 : to the beak : on the beak : through the beak : of the beak –Used, e.g., of a bird. ⟨**rextébawa** short-beaked loro (parrot)⟩ 6 : to the mouth and neck : on the mouth and neck : through the mouth and neck : of the mouth and neck –Used, e.g., of a bottle, jar, or demijohn. ⟨**réniti** to cork⟩ 7 : to the tip : on the tip : through the tip : of the tip –Used, e.g., of the front part of a boat, a vehicle, or an instrument; or, otherwise, of the source of a river. ⟨**rekénsho** sharp at the tip⟩ ⟨**réyakati** to sit in the bow⟩ ⟨**réboki** upriver⟩ 8 : to the vertical extremity : through the vertical extremity : of the vertical extremity. ⟨**rebésti** to reach the top⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*n.* **reán** : leech : callocallo ⟨**Náto riki réa; reánra jími óyoai.** This is the callocallo; the callocallo sucks blood.⟩ *syn.* sháo
See **riára**
See **Ribíka**

*v.t.* **rébesa** [from Shipibo *re–* to the vertical extremity + *bétsati* to finish] 1 : to reach the top ⟨**Enra jiwín néekin rebéske.** Climbing the tree, I reached the top.⟩ 2 : to reach life's final moment : to expire ⟨**Jóni máwatibishokotoninra moa rebéske.** The man who was on the verge of death expired.⟩ *syn.* See under **máwati**
*v.t.* **rébita** [from Shipibo *re–* from the front tip + *bíti* to travel] : to paddle from the bow ⟨**Nokon papánra nónti rébitai.** My father paddles the canoe from the bow.⟩

*n.* **rebón** : front tip; *specif.* : bow (of a boat) ⟨**Bótirebonko katánwe** Go to the bow of the boat.⟩ ⟨**wapóro rebo** bow of a launch or motorboat⟩ ⟨**machítorebo** tip of a machete⟩ ⟨**Enra nónti rebo réskeke.** I smashed the bow of the canoe.⟩ ⟨**píarebo** arrow tip⟩

*adv. and postp.* [from Shipibo *rébo* front tip + *-ki* to, against] *adv.* 1 : upriver –Used in all its senses especially in reference to the Ucayali River. ⟨**Nokon cháira moa réboki káke.** My brother-in-law has already gone upriver.⟩ ⟨**Rébokiasha ea jóke.** I have come from upriver.⟩ 2 : to the south *postp.* : in the upper (specific river) ⟨–¿**Jaweranoaxki mia jóai?** –Páro rebokiax. –Where do you come from? –From the Upper Ucayali.⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *réboki* upriver + *-ri* toward] : a little upriver ⟨**Rébokiri kanón kawe mérati.** Let's the two of us go a little upriver for a walk.⟩
*Konibo* **renchán** *n.* **réchaman** *also* **rénchaman** [from Shipibo *re-* on the nose] : aquiline or curved nose ⟨**Xetebora renchánya iki.** The **shetebo** have aquiline noses.⟩
*v.t.* **réchosha** [from Shipibo *re-* on the nose + *chóshati* to break] : to bash (someone) on the nose

*adj. and n.* **rékeman** [from Shipibo *rekénti, reken-* to go ahead] *adj.* 1 : ahead ⟨**Nokon bákera íshtoi rekén iki.** My son has gone ahead because he's running.⟩ 2 : first ⟨**Non rekén pápara iká iki Arán.** Our first father was Adam.⟩ 3 : elder ⟨**wétsa rekén** older brother⟩ *n.* : ancestor ⟨**Non rekénboronki ikátikanai táriabicho torósaoma.** They say our ancestors used to wear only cushmas (traditional robes) and not trousers.⟩ *syn.* bebón; yósi
See under **rekénti**

*adv.* **rékeni** : first : firstly : for the first time ⟨**Rekénhakinra en rabé witá bóke; jápekao westíorabicho.** First I carried two shungo baskets; afterward only one.⟩ ⟨**Rékeni Ikítoainoax wapóro jónike.** Many years ago a steamship came from Iquitos for the first time.⟩
*adj.* **rekénshonin** [from Shipibo *re-* on the nose + *kénsho* sharp] : pointed ⟨**Jíwi rekénshoninra nokon épa kéenai.** My uncle wants the pointed stick.⟩ *syn.* kénsho

*v.i.* **rékena** 1 : to go ahead : to be first ⟨**Eaparira rékenai ishtón nokónox.** I'll go ahead first so I arrive quickly.⟩ 2 : to go in front or first ⟨— ¿**Jáakan min báke?** —**Móara rekénke.** —Where is your son? —He's already gone ahead.⟩
[from Shipibo *rékena,* ahead, first + *pekao* after] 1 : second (e.g., in a line) 2 : second child ⟨**Nato bákera nokon rékena pekao iki.** This child is my second child.⟩
*n.* **rékiman** : nose : noses ⟨**Rékimanra non jóinai.** We breathe through our nose.⟩ ⟨**Wétsa yoshínboronki rekín nenké iki.** They say other demons have long noses.⟩
[from Shipibo *rekín* nose + *re-* on the nose + *toshnón* bulge] : tip of the nose ⟨**Mía riki rekín retoshmon áni.** The tip of your nose is very big.⟩
*n.* **rekínkinin** [from Shipibo *rekín* nose + *kíni* hole] : one of the two nostrils ⟨**Eara rekínkini naxbáma iki.** My nostrils are very narrow.⟩
See under **rekín**
*adj.* **renénkenin** [from Shipibo *re-* on the snout + long] : long-snouted
See under **kóchi**

*v.t.* **rénea** : to grind with a stone ⟨**Aínbaonra xéki réneke chíchaanoxon.** The woman ground the corn to make chicha (fermented corn drink).⟩ ⟨**Nokon poínra átapa pímati xéki réneai.** My sister is grinding corn to feed the chickens.⟩ ⟨**Méi rené pótatanwe.** Go throw out the ground apacharama.⟩

*v.t.* **rénia** [from Shipibo *re-* on the nose + *níati* to insert] 1 : to insert into (someone's) nose ⟨**Bakénra jabé báke jíwi rekín meran réniai.** The child is putting a small stick into the other child's nose.⟩ 2 : to cork (a bottle) ⟨**Enra botíria réniai.** I am corking the bottle.⟩

*n.* **rénitinin** [from Shipibo *réniti, réni-* to cork + *-ti* instrument suf.] : stopper : cork ⟨—¿**Jáweakiki mia ítai?** —**Kárajon réniti akira ea ítai** —What are you doing? —I'm making a stopper for the demijohn.⟩ *syn.* RENITI, REPOTI both can be translated as "cork," but RENITI can imply a corncob and REPOTI can imply topa (balsa-like wood) or sticks as the material it is made from.

*Konibo* **rénketi** *v.t.* **rénkaa** *Konibo* **rénkea** : to smooth (pottery) by rubbing with a small stone ⟨**Titánra chómo makán maxkon rénkeai.** Mom is smoothing the large jar with a small stone.⟩

*v.i.* **réokoota** 1 : to capsize / overturn (a boat or vehicle) ⟨**Wapórora jíwi tsákaax réokooke.** After hitting a log, the launch capsized.⟩ ⟨**Károra íchayora jawéki boi réokooke Aweitia poíntiain.** A truck carrying too heavy a load overturned on the Aguaytía bridge.⟩ 2 : to be capsized (a person in a boat or vehicle)

*v.t.* **réoa** 1 : to capsize (something) ⟨**Nóntira béchoman réoke.** The wake capsized the canoe.⟩ 2 : to empty out (solid contents) ⟨**Titánra tásakamea binón maín réoke.** Mom emptied the aguaje fruits from the basket onto the ground.⟩
*n.* **répekenin** [from Shipibo *re-* on the nose + *péke* hole] : perforation of the nasal septum ⟨**Répeke naxbá riki mía.** Your nasal perforation is very wide.⟩
*v.t.* **répina** : to dock : to pull alongside –Used of a boat. ⟨**Monsónra jawen bóti nokon repíntiain repínke.** A Spanish speaker docked his boat at my port.⟩ *syn.* répiti
*n.* **repíntinin** [from Shipibo *repínti, repín-* to dock + *-ti* instrument suf.] : port ⟨**Repínti óronon kawe.** Let's the two of us go cultivate (the land near) the port.⟩

*v.i.* **répia** : to dock ⟨**Tapánra répiai, néno óxai.** The raft is docking; we're going to sleep here.⟩ *syn.* REPITI, TAXNATI both have the sense of "to dock," but while TAXNATI implies the actual riverbank land where one docks, REPITI implies the port as the mooring place.

*n.* **repótinin** [from Shipibo *re-* on the nose + *po-* unidentified + *-ti* instrument suf.] : stopper ⟨**Náto riki repóti; botíria répotanwe.** Here is the stopper; go plug the mouth of the bottle.⟩ *syn.* See under **réniti**
*v.i.* **rérakaata** : to cut oneself by striking ⟨**Papán machítoninra ea rérakaake.** I cut myself with Dad's machete.⟩

*v.t.* **réraa** 1 : to cut by striking : to chop at with an axe ⟨**Nokon papánra wái akin jíwi rérake.** While clearing the garden, my father chopped down the trees.⟩ 2 : to hack at with a machete ⟨**Nokon titánra kóchi rérake átsa píaitian.** My mother machete-struck the pig because it was eating the manioc.⟩ *syn.* RERATI, SENOTI, XATETI, TSEKANTI can all be translated as "to cut"; but XATETI has the meaning of cutting with any cutting instrument; RERATI implies the action of cutting (e.g., with a machete) by striking blows; SENOTI implies a light cut produced by pressure (e.g., of a knife) drawn across; and TSEKANTI implies an incision (e.g., surgical) to remove the cut part.
*v.i.* **réreika** : to make noise (e.g., a motor, huangana (white-lipped peccary), rain, storm, river current, naval ship, launch, motorboat, car, motor scooter, or airplane)

*modifying suf.* : just : only : merely ⟨**Min bákeres motóronin ráanwe.** Send just your son on the motor (outboard-motor boat).⟩ ⟨**Ochíti non keiba pótaabira jóresai.** Even though we left the dog on the other side of the river, it just keeps coming.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2; 8.3.6 *syn.* -bicho

[from Shipibo *jéne*, *jenén* water + *réteti* to kill] : to drown –Used in a construction where *réteti*, a transitive verb, together with its subject *jenén*, is equivalent in meaning to an intransitive, reflexive verb. ⟨**Páena aínbora jenén réteke.** A drunk woman drowned.⟩

*also* **Románkoniabo** *pl. n.* **Róma joniboan** *also* **Románkoniaboan** [from Shipibo *Róma* Rome + *–nkonia* locative suf. + *jónibo* people, pl. of *jóni* man] : Romans –Used in the non-basic form with the sense of the adjective "Roman". ⟨**Moátianra Róma jonibaon nómiro akín akátiai: 1 akín rítira I, jaínxon 5 akín rítira V.** In ancient times, Roman numerals worked like this: 1 corresponded to the letter I, and 5 corresponded to the letter V.⟩
*n.* **romén** : tobacco ⟨**Nokon pápayosi riki romén chéata yobé ikáxmabi.** My grandfather is addicted to tobacco, even though he is not a shaman.⟩
[from Shipibo *róme* tobacco + *jótiti* to smoke] : to smoke ⟨**Nokon bakénra róme jótiai, jawen wétsa betan jonéxon.** My son is smoking, hidden together with his brother.⟩ *syn.* See under *jótiti*
See under **pókoti**

*n.* **rómexein** [from Shipibo *róme* tobacco + *xéiti* to roll (e.g., a cigarette)] 1 : cigar ⟨**Rómexei jótiamawe, miara yobéma iki.** Don't smoke a cigar; you are not a shaman.⟩ 2 : cigarette ⟨**Náto riki nokon papán rómexei.** This is my father's cigarette.⟩ ⟨**Jaton báke ísinatianra yobébo rómexeixon xoón ama kanai; já chíte akanai téomakin.** When their children get sick, the parents make a cigarette so shamans can blow the smoke on the children and then hang the cigarette butts around their necks.⟩
*n.* **Ronán** –Used as a female name.
*v.i.* **rónata** : to collapse or slide (earth/land) ⟨**Xómira ketó ronaax poxóke.** When the ground gave way, the ojé tree fell into the ravine.⟩

*also* **wákaronin** *also* **jéneronin** *also* **róniman títa** *n.* **róniman** *also* **wákaroniman** *also* **jéneroniman** *also* **róniman titan** [from Shipibo *wáka* fish + or *jéne* water + *ronín, róniman*; cf. *róno* snake] : anaconda : yacumama (a mythical water-boa) ⟨**Ronín riki áni, nenké, rastón, jáinoax kenéya.** The yacumama is large, long, thick, and patterned.⟩ ⟨**Jéneronin riki jenénkonia,** **jaín jáabiribi.** the yacumama lives in the water; that's where it dwells.⟩

*also* **maímea ronín** [from Shipibo *mái, maín* earth + *-mea* from + *ronín* anaconda] : a type of terrestrial yacumama that lives far off in the mountains and grows up to nine or ten meters long ⟨**Máironin riki wíso, ikaxbi natéxmisma.** The terrestrial yacumama is black in color and is not venomous.⟩

*n.* **rónkeman** [from Shipibo *róno* snake + *kené* design] : a type of small bowl (e.g., of gourd, huingo, or pottery) ⟨**Titán ronkén riki metsáshoko.** The little bowl Mom made is very pretty.⟩

*also* **-ki** *modal suf.* –Used with the sense of "they say" or "it is said" to express the reportative mood of someone who is repeating a story or an opinion or a statement about unspecified people, or a widely held belief. –Used added to the end of the first element of the sentence. –Used added before the last suffix of the verb if it is the only word in the sentence. –Used with *-a*, which is added if it is a verb suffix following as a response to a direct quote. –Used in the shortened form *-qui* in some narrative texts. ⟨**Miaronki yómetso iki irákanai jatíbi aínbobo.** All the women say that you're a thief.⟩ ⟨**Papánronki píchika sapén jáinoax chósko wáme réteke.** They say papá has killed five manatees and four paiche.⟩ ⟨**Min jawéki Tomásen xobón pótayamawe; yómetsoronkiai.** Don't leave your things at Tomás's house; they say he steals.⟩ ⟨**–¿Min benémein nokon báke oínyamake? –Oínronkiake.** –Might your husband have seen my son? –They say he has.⟩ ⟨**Játianki jóni káa iki, jákiribi jawen xobón.** Then, according to the story, the man returned to his house.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.1

*v.t.* **rótoa** : to reject ⟨**Ja xóntakora jatíbi jónibaon moa rótoke, jakóma íketian.** That young woman has been rejected by all the men because she is bad.⟩ ⟨**Nato konxán xatera moa rotó iki; páyo íketian rótokana.** This cedar log has been rejected because it is rotten.⟩
