*v.t.* **sáwemaa** 1 : to dress (someone) ⟨**Nokon bákera en chópa bená sáwemake.** I dressed my son in new clothes.⟩ 2 : to put on (someone) ⟨**Akáshamainbira nokon báke, óshaketian en sapáto sáwemai.** My son doesn't want to put on his shoes, but I put them on him while he sleeps.⟩ *syn.* áti

*v.i.* **sáwea** 1 : to dress oneself in (e.g., a cushma, shirt, pants, shorts, underpants, blouse, or skirt) ⟨**Papánra jawen tári bená sáweai.** Papá is dressing himself in his new cushma.⟩ 2 : to put on (e.g., a nose ornament, adornment, ring, bracelet, wristwatch, stockings, or shoes) ⟨**Nokon sapátora en sáweai.** I put on my shoes.⟩
*n.* **sáwetinin** [from Shipibo *sáweti, sawe-*, to dress + *-ti* that with which] : garment, dress ⟨**Nokon titán sáwetininra yómetsobo yómetsoke.** The thieves stole my mother's garments.⟩

*v.t.* **sáweta** : to be visible (e.g., the mouth of a hole) ⟨**Manánkinira ochóxonbi óina sawéke.** The mouth of a cave can still be seen from far away.⟩ ⟨**Jénechichokea máikinira tsósinaitian moá sáwetai.** The mouth of a hole that is deep underwater appears when the water level drops.⟩

*n.* **sayán** [from Spanish *saya*] 1 : women's outer garment 2 : skirt-like garment (*saya*) 3 : skirt ⟨**Moátianronki sáya nenké sáwepaokanike.** They say that long ago women wore a floor-length skirt.⟩
*v.t.* **sáyana** : to sprinkle
See **síbara**
*n.* **sebén** : manta blanca (a kind of catfish) ⟨**Aokiasenen rébokira sébe íchayora iki.** From Auquía on upstream, there are abundant *manta blanca* catfish.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *sébe* manta blanca] : a kind of *manta blanca* catfish
[from Shipibo *poínkosko, poínkoskon* vulture + *sébe* manta blanca] : a kind of *manta blanca* catfish

*Konibo* **sénbiti** *v.t.* **sébia** *Konibo* **sénbia** [from Shipibo *se-*, prefixed form of *seré* stripe + *bi-*, unidentified element + *-ti* inf. suf.] 1 : to coil, twist, or wrinkle up (something long and flexible) 2 : to coil up (e.g., a vine, rope, cord, or wire) into a pile by twisting or coiling ⟨**Papánra moa risbí sénbike.** Papá has already coiled up the rope.⟩ 3 : to gather (e.g., cloth, clothing, or a mosquito net) into a wrinkled pile 4 : to break (a long, hard object)
*Konibo* **senbíti** *v.i.* **sébita** *Konibo* **sénbita** : to coil up, to become coiled
See **sibória**
See **síbara**
See **síra**
See under **kóma**
See **Sikóntina**

*v.i.* **séika** [from Shipibo *se*, imitative of the sound + *-iti* to do] 1 : to bubble (something coming out from inside) ⟨**Enra kabóri réteke séikaitian.** I killed the taricaya turtle while it was bubbling as it came out.⟩ 2 : to come out or be outside (several at once) ⟨**Bónara séikai.** There are isula ants outside.⟩
*v.t.* **sékena** [from Shipibo *se-*, prefixed form of *seré* parallel lines + *kéneati* to paint designs] : to cut lightly
*v.t.* **sékea** : to break (something hard and long) ⟨**Nato bakénra íso xao sékeke.** This boy broke a spider monkey's bone.⟩
*v.i.* **séketa** : to break, to snap (something hard and long) ⟨**Nokon chíchika benára moa sekéke.** My brand-new knife has already broken.⟩
See **simánan**
See **simínto**
*n.* **sempán** : a kind of tree that produces a fine copal resin; *also* : the copal resin of the *sémpa* tree
[from Shipibo *báwa, bawán* parrot + *sémpa* *sémpa* tree] : an inferior kind of copal resin

*v.i.* **sénata** [from Shipibo *se-*, prefixed form of *seré* stripe + *na-*, unidentified element + *-ti* inf. suf.] : to bathe while playing among children ⟨**Bákera jenén réteke sénataitian.** The child drowned while bathing and playing with his companions.⟩
See **sébiti**

*postp.* : entirely up to, or exactly up to (a specific point) : exact ⟨**Rabé néte senénra en píamake, yonáxon.** For two whole days I have not eaten, because I had a fever.⟩ ⟨**Rámara píchika mítoro senén xóno xátekanai.** Now they are cutting the lupuna trees down to exactly five meters.⟩
*adj.* **séneman** : equal ⟨**Rásenenra senénbobires iki jawen paróbo.** A square has equal sides.⟩ *syn.* senénbires
*adv.* [from Shipibo *senén* entirely + *-ain* at] : at the end of a specific time or space ⟨**Móara óxe kéyoti sénenain.** Now the end of the month is approaching.⟩

*postp.* [from Shipibo *sénenain* at the end of a specific time + *-nko* at a specific place] 1 : at the end of a stretch of (a specific distance) ⟨**Náto bái sénenainko riki nokon xóbo.** At the end of this road is my house.⟩ 2 : throughout (a specific space or extent) ⟨**Móara icha jónibo jáke néte sénenainko.** Nowadays there are many people throughout the world.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *senén* up to a certain point + *-bi*, emphasis suf. + *-res* only] : the same, equal ⟨**Nokon bákebora íwe senénbires iki.** My children weigh the same.⟩ ⟨**Noa senénbires téekenbira ea íchamashoko kopíakanke.** Even though we worked equally, they paid me less than the others.⟩ *syn.* senén

*v.t.* **senénhaa** *Konibo* **senénhaka** : to finish (doing something) –Always used with a subordinate transitive verb ending in *-quin*. ⟨**Nokon wáira en órokin senénhake.** I finished cultivating my garden.⟩ ⟨**Non píkín senénhaketianra, kóshi niwánke.** Just as we finished eating, a strong earthquake occurred.⟩ *syn.* See under **jankénhati**
*adv.* : exactly, on the dot ⟨**westíora óra senénshaman** exactly one hour⟩

*v.i.* **sénena** 1 : to fit ⟨**Icha ikáxa nato táshi botíria meran senényamake.** This salt doesn't fit in the bottle because is a lot.⟩ 2 : to be enough ⟨**Nato pítira ícha jóni senéntima iki.** This food is not going to be enough for everyone.⟩ 3 : to be completed (a specified time) ⟨**Bakísha nokon píkota báritia sénenai.** Tomorrow I turn a year older.⟩ 4 : to finish : to finish doing : to be about to finish : to come to an end *-Used governing the infinitive of the subordinate verb.* ⟨**Eara moa téeti sénenai.** I am already finishing working.⟩ ⟨**Mánkoa bimibora moa kéyoti sénenai.** The mangoes are already almost gone.⟩ *syn.* See under **jankénti**
*n.* **senkán** : a kind of centipede

*v.t.* **sénoa** : to cut superficially through the skin with light pressure ⟨**Bakénra jawen ponyán chichikanin sénoke.** The boy made a superficial cut on his arm with a knife.⟩ *syn.* See under **rérati**
See **sintábo**
See **sinyóra**
See **sinyóro**
*n.* **sépakan** : cleared plot (of land) ⟨**Nokon sepá ikénbira, ea jonín bichínke.** Even though it was my cleared plot, a man took it from me.⟩
*v.t.* **sépaa** : to clear (e.g., a cañabrava cane patch, monte forest, brush, or purma old fallow field) ⟨**Rabé jonínra sépake nato báritian.** Two men cleared land this year.⟩
See **sipícho**
*n.* **serén** : a species of súngaro (a large Amazonian catfish)

*n. and adj.* **sérekan** *n.* 1 : parallel lines or stripes ⟨**Jawen pátoronin táronario meranra serébo jáke.** The stub of his ticket book has his design has parallel stripes.⟩ 2 : stripe ⟨**Rírora jawen betónkoain seréya iki.** The night monkey has a single stripe on its forehead.⟩ *adj.* : striped ⟨**Nato jonín kotónra seré iki.** This man's shirt is striped.⟩ *syn.* See under **wishá**
*v.t.* **seréaa** *Konibo* **seréaka** : to stripe, to draw lines on *syn.* **wíshati**
*adj.* **sérokan** 1 : muddy, dirty, and wet 2 : thick : solid ⟨**Paránta xéatira seró iki.** Chapo (a ripe-plantain drink) is thick.⟩ 3 : murky, cloudy *syn.* See under **potá**

*v.t.* **seróaa** *Konibo* **seróaka** 1 : to dirty with something muddy ⟨**Bakénra jawen tári seróai.** The child dirties his cushma (tunic) with mud.⟩ 2 : to thicken : to make solid ⟨**Titánra chícha seróai, páenaketian.** Mom thickens the chicha so it won't ferment.⟩
See **sirócho**

*v.i.* **sérota** 1 : to get dirty with something wet and thick that stains (e.g., mud, dung, or blood) ⟨**Titán chitóntininra átapa poi seróke.** Mom's pampanilla (wraparound skirt) got dirty with chicken dung.⟩ 2 : to thicken : to become solid ⟨**Nato aínbaon beténra seróke.** This woman's fish porridge has thickened.⟩

*adj.* **sesén** 1 : speckled with dots ⟨**Nato aínbaon kotónra sése iki.** This woman's blouse has a speckled pattern.⟩ 2 : freckled : with freckles ⟨**Bákera bémanáin sése iki.** The child's face is freckled.⟩
See under **átapa**
*v.t.* **séseaa** *Konibo* **séseaka** : to splash, to spatter ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke pikóketian nanén séseai.** The woman spatters her newborn child with huito (a black body-paint dye).⟩
See under **máke**

*v.i.* **sésea** 1 : to turn out two-colored ⟨**Atapaninronki xawáwaran pímaa** **báke séseai.** They say that if we feed hens pejetorres, their chicks are born two-colored.⟩ 2 : to be freckled ⟨**Nato aínbaonra nexnéx báchi píai; rámara jawen báke séseai.** This woman eats hoatzin eggs; now her child will be freckled.⟩
*v.t.* **sétena** [from Shipibo *se-* by extension + *tekínhati* to make sit] : to seat or make (several people) sit down

*v.i.* **séteta** [from Shipibo *se-*, prefixed form of *seré* extension + *tékiti* to sit down] 1 : to be seated (several) ⟨**Nokon xóbo meranra aínbobo setéke.** Inside my house some women are sitting.⟩ ⟨**Xéai beáxa jónibo setéke.** Some men are sitting because they have come to drink.⟩ 2 : to be perched (several birds of the same species) 3 : to stand together (several trees of the same species) 4 : to be grouped together (several things of the same kind)

*adj. and n.* **séyakan** [from Shipibo *se-*, prefixed form of *seré* extension + *-ya* conj.] *adj.* : ticklish ⟨**Titara seyá iki.** Mom is ticklish.⟩ *n.* 1 : tickling : the effect of being tickled ⟨**Bákera seyá ténema iki.** The child can't stand being tickled.⟩ 2 : shudder, shiver

*v.i.* **séyata** 1 : to feel ticklish ⟨**Eara seyáke.** I felt ticklish.⟩ 2 : to shudder ⟨**Kátera séyatai, noín óinax.** Káte shudders on seeing an earthworm.⟩ ⟨**Jawen pápa nónbeta óinaxa nato aínbo seyáke.** This woman shuddered on seeing that her father's boil had grown.⟩
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *sh* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1
*v.t.* **shákaaka** : to rattle (a rattle or maraca) ⟨**Enra shákaati shákaakai.** I am rattling the little rattle.⟩

*n.* **shákaatin** [from Shipibo *shákaati, shákaa-* to rattle + *-ti* instrument with which] 1 : a type of vine plant that produces small gourds from which little rattles are made 2 : rattle, maraca ⟨**Shákaatinra báke paránkanai tsokasaitian.** They entertain babies with the little rattle when they get restless.⟩

*v.i.* **shákaika** : to rattle (a maraca or rattle) ⟨**Shákaati shákaikaitianra báke wíniamai.** While the little rattle rattles, the baby doesn't cry.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákeranoman shákaatira shákashakaikai.** This young man's rattle rattles noisily.⟩
*v.i.* **shákomeeta** : to shake, to be shaken –Used mostly among Conibo speakers. ⟨**Nato jíwi niára shákomeeke.** This tree was shaken.⟩
*v.t.* **shákona** : to shake ⟨**Nokon bákera kóshi jóni iki; jánra jíwi shákonai.** My son is a strong man; he shakes trees.⟩
*v.i.* **shákota** 1 : to shake : to tremble ⟨**Níwanaitianra manánbo shákotai.** When an earthquake happens, the hills shake.⟩ 2 : to move

*modifying suf.* 1 : very; *specif.* : very pleasantly –Used in this sense when added to an adjective or adverb. ⟨**Nato báira naxbáshaman iki, jatíbi jónibo jaín wínotai ikax.** This road is very wide because a lot of people pass through there.⟩ ⟨**Paránta joshínshamanra nokon báke xéakasai.** My son likes to drink chapo made from pleasantly ripe plantain.⟩ ⟨**Nokon papánra manánxawe ánishaman káchiokea bíke.** My father got a big tortoise in the forest.⟩ 2 : exactly –Used in this sense when added to the interrogative word of a question. ⟨**¿Jáwetianshamanki min báke néno nókota iki?** Exactly when did your child arrive here?⟩ 3 : completely : completely to one's liking : very well –Used in this sense when added to the verb. ⟨**Eara keénshamanai Rimán katín.** I am very happy to go to Lima.⟩ ⟨**Rámara en moa wíshati onánshamanke.** Now I already know how to write very well.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.6 *syn.* **ashón**; **-kon**

*suf.* *adv.* **-shamanhakin** : well : to one's liking ⟨**Sontárobora jakónshamani márachankanai.** The soldiers march well.⟩ ⟨**Noa jakónshamanhakin yóiwe non onánon.** Tell it to us with perfect clarity so that we understand it.⟩ *syn.* **-kon**
*n.* **shankán** : rock ⟨**Wéamanra shánka ícha iki.** There are many rocks in the streams.⟩
*n.* **shánokan** : jergón (a venomous pit viper) ⟨**Kakónkonia jónira shánokan natéxon rétea iki.** Once a man from Caco was bitten by a fer-de-lance and died.⟩
[from Shipibo *jéne* water + *sháno* jergón] : yacu jergón (a water snake, lit. "water fer-de-lance")
*also* **Sánti** *n.* **Shantín** *also* **Santín** [from regional Spanish *Shanti, Santi*; and this from *Santiago*] –Used as a masculine name.
*adj.* **sháokan** : yellowish pale : anemic : posheco (sickly-looking) *syn.* **pasná**; **réa**
*v.i.* **sháota** : to turn pale; to become anemic ⟨**Mái píai ikaxa nato jóni sháoai.** This man is becoming anemic from having gotten into the habit of eating dirt.⟩

*v.i.* **sháraika** [from Shipibo *shara*, imitative of the sound + *-iti* to make/do] 1 : to shrill, to screech (insect) ⟨**Shanó kéotira sháraikai, shiríchampo keska.** The baby fer-de-lance shrills like the shrilling cricket.⟩ 2 : to crackle (lightning) 3 : to make a faint sound with the engine nearly off (airplane) at altitude 4 : to make a faint sound with the engine nearly off; to hum faintly ⟨**Nóomanaonra ábion sháraikawanke.** The airplane passed overhead making a faint sound.⟩
*n.* **Shawánon** *Konibo* **Shawánonin** [from regional Spanish *Shawano*] –Used as a masculine name.
*v.t.* **shéaka** [from Shipibo *she*, imitative of the sound + *-ati* to cause] : to fry ⟨**Nokon títara sibória shéaka pikáshamai.** My mom doesn't like to eat fried onion.⟩

*v.i.* **shéika** 1 : to be fried, to fry (intr.) ⟨**Amakiri xénira shéikai.** The gamitana fish's fat is frying.⟩ 2 : to make a sound (e.g., a canoe) passing through the water ⟨**Jonín koshín wínaara nónti shéiikainai.** When people paddle the canoe hard, it makes a sound.⟩ *syn.* See under **komón iti**
*n.* **shékeshin** *Konibo* **shékeshen** : charichuela (a small tropical fruit) ⟨**Nato bákera shekésh kókokasai.** This child likes to eat charichuela fruit.⟩

*adj.* **shepán** : green : unripe : in the thin or green stage –Used, e.g., regarding plantains and shimbillo fruit. *syn.* See under **áko** ⟨**Paránta shépapari íketianra non bíamake.** We didn't bring the plantains because they were still green.⟩
*n.* **shépaaa** : to deflate : to make deflate ⟨**Enra piróta shépaake.** I made the ball deflate.⟩ *syn.* **ótsiati**
*v.i.* **shépaa** : to become deflated or flattened : to deflate ⟨**Nato pirótara moa shépake, íchaxon jamákana.** This ball has deflated because many people have kicked it.⟩ *syn.* **ótsiti**
*v.i.* **shéreika** [from Shipibo *shére*, imitative of the presumed sound + *-iti* to make/do] : to unroll ⟨**Titán yomán xéiara shéreike.** The thread mom rolled up has come unrolled.⟩

*n.* **shíarinin** : shiari (a plant used to make cord); *also* : the bark of the shiari that is extracted to make cord ⟨**Shiari jiwira rastóma iki, machítoninbi rerati.** The shiari's stem is not thick; it can be cut with a machete.⟩

*interj.* –Used with the meaning of "oh!" as an expression of fright or surprise upon encountering something strange, dangerous, or unpleasant. ⟨**¡Shíi! Nato róno rákata riki shanó.** Oh! This snake lying on the ground is a fer-de-lance.⟩ *syn.* See under **ápo**
*n.* **shímoman** : mullaca (a small berry) ⟨**Shimónya parántajoshin méskoxon kobínhaxon xéaara nóeshaman iki.** Ripe plantains mixed with mullaca berries and cooked are very delicious to drink.⟩
[from Shipibo *móka* bitter + *shimón* mullaca] : a type of mullaca whose bitter leaves are used to treat siso (a skin fungus) and white blotches on the face
[from Shipibo *popó* cocona + *shimón* mullaca] : a type of mullaca whose thorny stem and leaves resemble the corresponding parts of the cocona plant
[from Shipibo *xáe, xaén* anteater + *shimón* mullaca] : a type of mullaca
[from Shipibo *xáwe, xawén* charapa (river turtle) + *shimón* mullaca] : a type of mullaca
*modifying suf.* : all night –Used added to the verb. ⟨**Titánra jawen báke ísinai kóiranshinke.** Mom took care of her sick child all night.⟩
*n.* **shínakoxon** [from Old Shipibo *shínaxoko*] : a type of spider ⟨**Shínakoxo betan nínboronki jakómaananai.** They say that the *shínakoxo* spider and the scorpion offend each other.⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *shinán, shínaman* thought + *-res* only] : miraculously ⟨**Non Inkánronki shínamanres jawékibo ápaonike.** They say that our Inca did things miraculously.⟩

*v.i.* **shínameeta** 1 : to take care of oneself : to look after oneself ⟨**Jawen báke shinántitianbira, nato jóni janbíx shínameetai.** Instead of taking care of his child, this man takes care of himself.⟩ 2 : to examine oneself ⟨**Eara shínameeke nokon jóintiain. Rámara Bíbiria meran wixá en ikón akai.** I examine my heart, because now I believe what is written in the Bible.⟩

*n.* **shínaman** 1 : mind ⟨**Non shinán jakón íketianronki básiamaakin non jawéki ónanai.** They say that if we have a good mind, we learn things easily.⟩ 2 : thought ⟨**Nokon shinánbiribira wétsabaon shínana keskama iki.** My thoughts are different from those of others.⟩
[from Shipibo *jakóma* bad + *shinán* thought + *-ya* with] : malicious : ill-intentioned : in bad faith
[from Shipibo *jakón* good + *shinán* thought + *-ya* with] : kind : well-intentioned : in good faith

[from Shipibo *rabé* two + *shinán* thought + *-ya* with] : to have doubts : to doubt ⟨**Máioshiainronki ápo jókasai; ikáxbironki jawen awín rabé shinánya iki.** They say the President wants to come to Pucallpa, but his wife has doubts.⟩

[from Shipibo *shinán* mind + *áti* to make/do] : to have recently come of age (e.g., at eighteen years old) ⟨**Móara nato bákeranon ríbiritaya iki, shinán ákai ikáx.** This young man already has his ID booklet because he has come of age.⟩

*v.i.* **shinánbenota** [from Shipibo *shinán* thought + *bénoti* to get lost] : to forget something needed –Used with the complement in the basic form. ⟨**Ishtónresira ea yabínti shinánbenoke.** I forgot my key because I was in a hurry.⟩
*v.t.* **shinánhaa** *Konibo* **shinánhaka** : to dry by heat ⟨**Nato aínbaonra jawen chitónti méchata chíikan shínanhai.** This woman is drying her wet pampanilla (wraparound skirt) by the fire.⟩

*adj.* **shináomatonin** [from Shipibo *shinán* thought + *-oma* without] 1 : foolish : silly : stupid ⟨**Nato aínbo shinánhomatoninra jawen béne jawéki axónyamai.** This stupid woman is of no use to her husband in anything.⟩ 2 : forgetful ⟨**Nato bákeranonra shinánhoma iki; jákopira shinánbenoke.** This young man is forgetful; that's why he forgot his things.⟩ *syn.* See under **onáma**

*adv.* [from Shipibo *shinánti, shinan-* to think + *-kaya* in reality + *-a,* past-participle suf.] : for example ⟨**Jatíbi rasénenbires tonrón iki. Shinánkayata, piróta jáskara tonrón.** Anything perfectly round is a sphere. For example, a ball is a sphere.⟩
*v.i.* **shínana** : to dry (e.g., cloth, leaf, or paper) in the heat ⟨**Titán chópapisabo pátsatara moa shinánke.** The clothes mom washed have already dried in the sun.⟩

*v.t.* **shínana** 1 : to think of (a person) ⟨**Moátianronki yoshánshokobo tirín ikaitian wínipaonike; jaton rárebo máwata shínani.** They say that in the old days grandmothers used to cry whenever there was thunder, thinking of their loved ones who had already died.⟩ 2 : to remember : to recall ⟨**Moa mawákinbi nokon pápashokon ea yóini jóibo shínanaxa ea wínikasai.** When I remember the last words my grandfather said to me before he died, I want to cry.⟩ 3 : to think : to decide : to have decided ⟨**Yóashiko Inkán shinánketianronki rabé jóni kapénike.** When the stingy Inca decided it would be so, two men turned into caimans.⟩ ⟨**Nato báritian xonón téetira en shínanai.** I have decided to work at the lupuna (giant ceiba tree) this year.⟩

[from Shipibo *masáti, masa-* to damage, to spoil + *shinánti* to think] : to feel sorrow : to be grieved or sorrowful : to feel sadness : to grieve : to become sad ⟨**Nokon pápashoko mawáketianra en westíora simánan masá shínana iki.** When my grandfather died, I grieved for a week.⟩ ⟨**Jawen báke mawáketianra masá shinánkin jéneyamai.** He keeps grieving over his child's death.⟩ ⟨**Rároshaman ikénbira já joxón ea masá shinámake.** I was very happy, but he came and that made me sad.⟩ *syn.* See under **onísti**

[from Shipibo *méskoti, mesko-* to mix + *shínanti* to think] : to be perplexed : to be confused ⟨**Koríki yómetsoakanara en meskóbo shínana iki; ján jawékiati yámaketian.** When my money was stolen from me, I was left perplexed, thinking I had nothing to feed myself with.⟩

*adj.* **shinányanin** *Konibo* **shinányaton** [from Shipibo *shinán* thought + *-ya* with] 1 : intelligent ⟨**Nato jóni shinányatonra ónibirisitaro akai.** This intelligent man is doing university studies.⟩ 2 : experienced
*n.* **shínikan** : supernatural power
*n.* **shínikan** : a type of small palm with very thin, sharp spines and edible fruit in small bunches
*n.* **shinípentsiman** [from Shipibo *shiní* a type of palm + *pentsín*, unidentified element] : ñejilla (a small palm fruit)

*n.* **shinítapoman** [from Old Shipibo *shiní* supernatural power + *tapón* root] : pipe : cashimbo (a traditional pipe) ⟨**Nokon pápashokonra shinítapon ati onán ikátiai.** My grandfather was very skilled at making cashimbo pipes.⟩ ⟨**Nokon papánra róme jótiai shinítapoman napóxon.** My father smokes tobacco by putting it in his cashimbo pipe.⟩ ⟨**Pápashokon shinítaponra jawen babán jenénko pótanaanke.** The grandson threw his grandfather's cashimbo pipe into the water.⟩
*v.i.* **shín ika** [from Shipibo *shin*, imitative of the song + *-iti* to make/do] : to sing (parrot)

*n.* **shinkán** [from Shipibo *shínka*, imitative of the cry] : pucaloro (a type of bird) ⟨**Rámara shínka píkanai. Moátianra píamakatikanai.** Nowadays people eat pucaloros; in the old days they didn't eat them.⟩

*n.* **shinón** : a type of monkey (e.g., white monkey or black monkey) : one or another of several medium-sized, very playful monkey species ⟨**Shinónronki húasa kómpa ake.** They say the black monkey is the frailecito (titi monkey)'s buddy.⟩
[from Shipibo *wíso* black + *shino* a type of monkey] : machín (capuchin monkey)
[from Shipibo *joshín* pink + *shino* monkey] : huapo colorado (red uakari monkey)
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *shino* monkey] : mono blanco (white monkey)

*n.* **shínshiman** [from Old Shipibo *shin*, element of *shiní* supernatural power + *shin*, reduplication] : a type of tiny mite that stings and causes extensive suppuration; *also* : the skin condition caused by the *shinshín* mite ⟨**Yoshínkoshkitenronki jísonkin shinshín nóki máanhai; jákopira títashokobo xobón wéitai; yoshínkoshki iketian ói máanaitian.** They say that the rainbow, when it urinates, sends *shinshín* down on us; that's why elderly women take shelter in their houses when the rainbow is out and it's raining.⟩
*n.* **shíntín** : a type of large cricket ⟨**Shinobaonronki shínti píai.** They say monkeys eat the *shínti* cricket.⟩
*n.* **shión** : manta blanca (a white stingray) ⟨**Shión piára báke wíniai.** The child cries because the white stingray has stung him.⟩
*n.* **shipín** : tití : leoncito : pichín : pichico (a small tamarin monkey) ⟨**Shípi riki kikínbires raké.** The pichico tamarin is very easily frightened.⟩
[from Shipibo *kóro* gray + *shípi* pichico] : a type of gray-colored pichico tamarin
[from Shipibo *íso* spider monkey + *shípi* pichico] : a type of black, white-mouthed pichico tamarin
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *shípi* (with the *sh* assimilated to the preceding *x*) pichico] : a type of pichico tamarin
[from Shipibo *páka* a type of bamboo + *shípi* pichico] : a type of pichico tamarin

*n.* **shípibon** *Konibo* **shípibaon** *pish.* **shípibaen** [from Shipibo *shípi* pichico + *-bo* people] : members of the Shipibo linguistic group : the Shipibo : Shipibo people ⟨**Kikín shípiboronki sinábo ikátiai.** They say that the true Shipibo were fierce men.⟩
*n.* **shípimabichin** [from Shipibo *shípi* pichico + *ma-* on the head + *bíchi* skin/hide] : a type of tree whose thin branches are used as fishing rods
*n.* **Shirákonin** [from Spanish; a regionalism from Ucayali] –Used as a masculine name.
See under **chámpo**
*v.i.* **shíriika** [from Shipibo *shíri*, imitative of the song + *-iti* to make/do] : to chirp (cricket) ⟨**Oi béai yóiironki chámpobo shíriikai.** They say crickets chirp to announce rain.⟩
*n.* **shirínkanin** [from Spanish *shiring-*, element of *shiringuero*] : shiringuero (a rubber tapper)

*v.t.* **shíroaa** *Konibo* **shíroaka** 1 : to joke around with, to tease ⟨**Papánra jawen chái shíroake.** Dad teased his brother-in-law.⟩ 2 : to court playfully with jokes ⟨**Jonínra aínbo shíroake.** The man courted the woman with little jokes.⟩
*See under* **bewá**

*n.* **shírojanen** [from Shipibo *shíro* joke + *jáne* name] : nickname ⟨**Nokon poín shírojane riki Chámpoxeni; nato chámpo xéati kóbinai meran káketian tsékayamaxonra jawen xéniabi mato xéati iki —akin áketian.** My sister's nickname is Chámpoxeni, which means Cricket Grease, because once she said: —This cricket fell into the boiling chicha; and if they don't take it out, they'll drink the chicha with its fat in it.⟩ ⟨**Báketianbi noa shírojane ákanara non tóxkoti átipanyamake.** If we're given a nickname since childhood, we won't be able to erase it when we grow up.⟩
*v.i.* **shíroa** 1 : to tell a joke ⟨**Papára shíroke.** Dad told a joke.⟩ 2 : to play a practical joke
*n.* **shishákon** *Konibo* **shishákonin** [from regional Spanish] : shishaco
*n.* **shishín** : coati : achuni ⟨**Shíshibaonra xáko píai.** Coatis eat centipedes.⟩
*See under* **máke**
*See under* **róno**
*v.t.* **shítaa** : to cross : to ford : chimbar ⟨**Enra páro shítake.** I crossed the river.⟩
*v.i.* **shítata** : to cross water ⟨**Ochítira kéibakeax shitáke.** The dog crossed over from the other bank.⟩
*n.* **shiwéwen** : a type of small heron –Rarely used nowadays.

*v.t.* **shóaka** : to spill a small amount of (e.g., water, fruit juice, or tears) ⟨**Nato aínbaonra chómomea ompáx shóarike; játoki rabínkin.** This woman suddenly spilled water from her clay jar, because she was embarrassed in front of those around her.⟩
*v.i.* **shóika** : to spill (small amount of liquid) ⟨**Titán chíchara shóikai; kentí tóetax.** Mom's chicha is spilling because the clay pot has cracked.⟩ *syn. See under* **chikóti**
*v.i.* **shókikaata** : to drill oneself (accidentally) ⟨**Nato kárapintirora konxán ati shínani janbíx shókikaake mekénki.** This carpenter, trying to drill a board, drilled through his own hand.⟩

*v.t.* **shókia** : to drill : to bore through : to make a hole in ⟨**Pápashokonra ísoxeta shókiai méneshetianoxon.** Grandfather drills the teeth of the spider monkey to make a bracelet with them.⟩ ⟨**Kárapintironinra witá shókiai chorísh íketian.** The carpenter drills into the heartwood because it is hard.⟩ *syn. See under* pékati
*n.* **shókitinin** [from Shipibo *shókiti shoki-*, to drill + *-ti* instrument for] : drill; *specif.* : a small type of drill typically made from an umbrella rib

*also* **-sonko** *modifying suf.* **-shokon** *also* **-sonkon** –Used attached to a noun, pronoun, adjective, or adverb with the meaning of "-ito, -cito" [diminutive], for to form the diminutive. –Used in the form *-sonco* or *-soncon* mostly among Pishquibo or Shetebo speakers. ⟨**Nato bákeshokora chopíti kókokasai.** This little child wants to suck on a pacifier.⟩ ⟨**Xonáyoshinronki beshéshoko iki.** They say the spirits of the renaco (a strangler fig) are little dwarfs.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákeranon rakéshokora sontáro kakáshamai.** This cowardly young man doesn't want to go into the army.⟩ ⟨**Jáshokora jóai.** The one who is dear to us is coming.⟩ ⟨**jáshoko** that little bit⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.2.3; 8.3.6 *syn.* -tsi

*modifying suf.* : in the same way as another : also –Used between the verb root and the final suffix. ⟨**Earibira Rimán káshokoai nato óxe wínotapekao.** I'm also going to Lima next month.⟩ ⟨**En chópabo bíaitianra nokon chaín bíshokoke.** My brother-in-law got several pieces of clothing, just like I did.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*adv.* [from Shipibo *-shóko*, diminutive suf. + *-res* no more] : only a very little ⟨**Shókoresea chíchikanin xatéke.** I cut myself with the knife just a tiny bit.⟩

*adj. and n.* **shómoman** *adj.* [from Shipibo *sho-* (element of *shóati* to spill) + *-mon*, unidentified element] : blistered : with blisters ⟨**Nato báke ménotara jawen bémanan shomón iki.** This child who got burned has blisters on his face.⟩ *n.* : swollen part of the body : blister *syn.* toxbá

*v.i.* **shómona** 1 : to blister ⟨**Ompásh shanan ménotara nokon pápashokon ponyán shomónke.** My grandfather's arm blistered from being burned with boiling water.⟩ 2 : to swell ⟨**Jibuin ríshkiara jóni mekén shomónke.** The man's hand is swelling because he hit it with a stick.⟩ ⟨**Rábo jámataxa nokon táe shomónke.** I stepped on a nail and my foot swelled up.⟩ *syn. See under* somónti
*n.* [from Shipibo *shinó*, vocative form of *shúno* a species of monkey] –Used as a vocative form to call the mono blanco, the machín (capuchin monkey), or the pucahuapo.

*n.* **shontán** [from Shipibo *xónta* young lady, from imitation of infant babbling] : girl : **wawa** –Used as a term of endearment. ⟨**Nokon shontán ochítira kikínbires mécha iki.** My little girl's dog is very clever.⟩ ⟨**Shontá —ikira noa íkai nokon báke aínbo akí.** We say, "Little girl!" when addressing our daughter.⟩ ⟨**—Ea píti axonwe shontá en mia kopíanon.** "Fix me some food, little girl; I'll pay you."⟩ *syn.* chibá
*n.* **shóntirin** : a small mythological bird species
*n.* **shórokan** [from Shipibo *sho-*, imitative of dripping + *roo*, imitative] : drop ⟨**Nokon báchira shórokan mecháake.** My mosquito net got wet from the leak.⟩ *syn.* tosó
*v.t.* **shóroaka** : to blow a whistle at : to whistle at ⟨**Wáiroron shóroaketianra ea ratéke.** When the guard whistled at me, I got scared.⟩

*n.* **shóroatin** [from Shipibo *shóroati, shoroa-* to whistle + *-ti* instrument for] : whistle : instrument for whistling ⟨**Maístoron noa shóroatin kénaketianra, noa ískoira meran wéitai.** When the teacher calls us with the whistle, we go into the school.⟩ ⟨**Nokon amígora wáiroron shóroatin yómetsoke.** My friend stole a guard's whistle.⟩
*v.t.* **shoróaa** *Konibo* **shoróaka** : to make drip
*v.i.* **shóroika** : to whistle : to blow the whistle : to give a whistle blast ⟨**Wáirorobora yatámisi shóroikatiai.** The guards would blow their whistles when recruiting.⟩
See under **kóma**
*v.i.* **shórota** : to drip ⟨**Oi bexónra, moa shórokin noa mecháake.** When it rained, the dripping rain got us wet.⟩ *syn.* tosóti
*n.* **showáwan** : a species of bird ⟨**Showáwara yamé kéotai.** The *showáwa* bird sings at night.⟩

*adj.* **síbakan** [from Shipibo *síiti, síi-* to slip + *ba-* (from *báka* smooth)] 1 : slippery ⟨**Oi béketianra bái sibá iki.** When it rains, the path gets slippery.⟩ 2 : smooth ⟨**Axoyoshinronki síbá iki.** They say the demon of the capirona (a smooth-barked tree) is smooth.⟩ *syn.* See under *báka; bicha*

*v.t.* **sibáa** *Konibo* **sibáaka** 1 : to make slippery ⟨**Bákebaonra nónti sibáake ómpaxen mecháaxon.** The children wet the canoe with water and made it slippery.⟩ 2 : to smooth, to sand (e.g., to give shine or a slick finish) ⟨**Kárapintirobaonra mísa sibáai.** The carpenters are smoothing the table.⟩

*also* **sébra** *n.* **síbaranin** *also* **sebrán** [from Spanish] : zebra ⟨**Síbara riki kabáyo keskátanishamanribi. Ikáxbi riki jawen yóra jóxo betan wisón seré serétani.** The zebra looks very much like the horse; the only difference is that its whole body is covered with white and black stripes.⟩
*also* **sebára** *n.* **sibáranin** *also* **sebáranin** [from Spanish] : barley ⟨**sibára páanhati** barley for making bread⟩ ⟨**sibára aká páan** barley bread⟩
*v.i.* **síbata** 1 : to become slippery ⟨**Oi béketianra bái sibáke.** Since it rained, the path became slippery.⟩ 2 : to become smooth (to the point of shining or being slick)
*n.* **síbokan** [from Spanish] : zebu (a type of cattle) ⟨**Jónira síbokan máchaman akín rétekeanke.** A zebu gored a man with its horn and almost killed him.⟩

*also* **sebóya** *n.* **sibórian** *also* **sebóyanin** [from Spanish] : onion ⟨**Sibória pikáshamaira báke wíniai.** The child cries because he doesn't want to eat onions.⟩ ⟨**Non sibóriaya jóno piáronki ochíti mecha nótsiai.** They say that if we eat collared peccary seasoned with onions, the hunting dog gets offended.⟩
See **síkino**
*n.* **síiman** [from Spanish *zink*] : corrugated zinc roofing sheets ⟨**Jonínra síi xóboai.** The man is building his house with zinc roofing sheets.⟩
*v.t.* : to whistle, to blow (a whistle) ⟨**Bakénra sínko síin akai.** The child blows a whistle.⟩
*v.i.* **síin ika** : to whistle (small bird) ⟨**Niwe abánonra xáne síin ikai.** To announce that wind is coming, the little *xáne* bird whistles.⟩

*v.i.* **síiika** [from Shipibo *síi* imitative + *-iti* to make/do] : to trickle out or spill making a sound ⟨**Asókaro sakora xoyán pékake; ja pekénra asókaro síike.** The rat made a hole in the sugar sack, and as it spilled the sugar made a trickling sound.⟩
*adj. and n.* **síkakan** *adj.* : painted : covered in paint ⟨**Nokon papán xóbora moa siká iki.** My father's house is already painted.⟩ *n.* : paint : painted color

*v.t.* **síkaa** 1 : to paint : to cover with paint ⟨**Jonínra jawen xóbo síkake.** The man painted his house.⟩ 2 : to color ⟨**Bakebaonra yóina ríbojanxon síkati iki.** The students are to draw and color animals.⟩ 3 : to put liquid on ⟨**Píara non méchawasten síkai.** We use the good fisherman's piripiri (a medicinal plant) to apply to the arrow.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*n.* **sikín** : a type of tree similar to the pashaca (a thorny tree) but without thorns

*also* **signo** *n.* **síkinonin** *also* **sígnonin** [from Spanish] : sign ⟨**Piá síkinoninra noa yoiaí bóchiki, naman, mékayao, jáinoax mémio iká jóibo.** The arrow is a sign that indicates direction, e.g., something upward, downward, to the right, or to the left.⟩

*v.i.* **síkita** : to get stained : to get painted : to become covered in paint ⟨**Nato bákera manón síkitai.** This child gets stained with mud.⟩ ⟨**Nato bákera nanén sikí iki.** This child is painted with huito.⟩ *syn.* SIKITI and YOKITI can both be translated as "to get painted"; but SIKITI implies something watery like paint (e.g., huito or mud), while YOKITI implies something thicker used to paint (e.g., achiote or vegetable fat).
*also* **Segóndina** *n.* **Sikóntinan** *also* **Segóndinan** [from Spanish *Segundina*] –Used as a feminine name.
See **Síras**
*also* **semána** *n.* **simánanin** *also* **semánanin** [from Spanish] : week ⟨**Nato simánaninra nokon wétsa Rímameax nókotai.** This week my brother will arrive from Lima.⟩
*also* **seménto** *n.* **simíntonin** *also* **seméntonin** [from Spanish] : cement ⟨**simínto xóbo** cement house⟩
*n.* **Símoman** [from Spanish] –Used as a masculine name.
*n.* : a type of demon with a long, foldable right arm which it uses to seize its victims
*n.* **Sinán** [from Shipibo *siná* angry] –Used as a masculine name.

*adj. and n.* **sínakan** [from Shipibo *sináti, sina-* to anger] *adj.* 1 : angry ⟨**Siná jonín shinánra jakóma iki.** An angry man's intentions are malicious.⟩ 2 : fierce ⟨**Wísoinoronki siná iki.** They say the yanapuma (a black-jaguar spirit) is fierce.⟩ ⟨**siná jawéki** fierce animal⟩ *n.* 1 : anger ⟨**Sinakánra jóni moa jawen isin wekómake.** The man's anger made his health worse.⟩ 2 : ferocity ⟨**Yobébaonronki wísoinon siná bíchinai.** They say sorcerers take away the yanapuma's ferocity for their own purposes.⟩
*v.i.* **sináa** *Konibo* **sináaka** : to scold angrily ⟨**Bákera en sináake nokon koríkinin yómetsoa kopí.** I scolded the boy angrily because he stole my money.⟩

*v.i.* **sínata** 1 : to get angry ⟨**Sinákinra ea jonín rabé néte yóyoayamake.** The man didn't speak to me for two days because he was angry.⟩ ⟨**Kikínbiresi sínatara jóni káke.** The man left very angry.⟩ 2 : to get mad (at someone) –Used with the opposition complement preceded by *-qui* "against." ⟨**Nato jónira éki sínatai, jawen machíto yómetsoakana ea pónteax.** This man is mad at me and blamed me because someone stole his machete.⟩ 3 : to become fierce or wild ⟨**Táma pímaara átapa sínatai.** If we feed a hen peanuts, it becomes fierce.⟩
See under **ráo**
*n.* **sinkón** : reed (carrizo) ⟨**Bakénra sínko síin akái.** The child blows the whistle made of reed.⟩

*n.* **sinón** : pona (a palm split into strips for flooring and walls) ⟨**Sínoyoshinronki óshitani ikaxbi nenké jóni iki.** They say that the pona-palm demon, although somewhat thin, is a man of great height.⟩

*n.* **sínopepon** [from Shipibo *síno* pona palm + *pépo* frame/structure] : emponado (pona-strip flooring) made of genuine pona ⟨**Nokon sínopepo senénra jenén mápoke.** The flood covered the neighborhood and reached up to my pona floor.⟩ *syn.* SINOPEPO and TAPO both translate as "emponado" (pona-strip flooring), but SINOPEPO specifically implies construction from pona, whereas TAPO can imply different building materials.
*n.* **sintán** [from Spanish] : ribbon, tape ⟨**Maístoronra ískoiranko sínta mítoro beti iki.** The teacher is to bring a measuring tape to school.⟩
*also* **sentábo** *n.* **sintábonin** *also* **sentábonin** [from Spanish] : cent, centavo
*n.* **síntaman** : small basket ⟨**Titánra jabuen íwi síntaman bénxoai.** Mom keeps her spindles in the small basket.⟩ *syn.* **kakín**
*n.* **Sintín** [from Spanish *Inokente*] –Used as a masculine name.

*also* **sintorón** *n.* **sintóranin** *also* **sintóronin** [from Spanish *cintura*; a variant form of Spanish *kinturón* (belt)] : belt ⟨**Bákera sintóranin yómetsoke jawen papán jishnóma.** The child stole the belt without his father noticing.⟩

*also* **senyóra** *n.* **sinyóranin** *also* **senyóranin** [from Spanish] : madam, missus –Used as a form of address given to any woman as a sign of respect. *syn.* SINYORA and YOXAN can both be translated as "madam," but YOXAN, the native word, is used more among Shipibo people.

*also* **senyóro** *n.* **sinyóronin** *also* **senyóronin** 1 : sir, mister –Used as a form of address given to any man as a sign of respect. ⟨**Sinyóro, ea máromawe rabé karíti yomán.** Sir, sell me two spools of thread.⟩ 2 : Lord –Used with a capital *L* as an honorific title for God. *syn.* SINYORO and YOSI can both be translated as "sir/Lord," but YOSI, the native word, is used more in social settings (e.g., within the family), while SINYORO, the borrowed word, is more appropriate in a place of business (e.g., a store).
*n.* **sión** : daledale (a cultivated plant) ⟨**Nokon sío banara jénetiaxon réteke.** My daledale plot was destroyed by the flood.⟩

*n.* **síoman** 1 : stripe ⟨**Nokon kotónra siónya iki.** My shirt has stripes.⟩ 2 : line ⟨**sión pónteaka** straightened line⟩ 3 : color in the form of a line ⟨**Chirápa riki kánchis siónya: joshín, oxna panshin, panshin, yankón, yankón paxná, amíkeska, joshín oxná.** The rainbow has seven colors: red, orange, yellow, blue, light green, violet, and pink.⟩ *syn.* See under **wishá**

*v.t.* **siyón aka** *Konibo* **siyón aka** : to stripe : to make stripes on ⟨**Nokon titánra nanén jawen chitónti siyón ake.** My mom made little stripes on her pampanilla (wraparound skirt) with huito dye.⟩ *syn.* **wíshati**

*v.i.* **sión ika** : to scream (e.g., from pain, fright, or fear) : to let out a sharp cry ⟨**Jónira yamé sión ikai pórokan chéxaa, jato oxá rátei.** The man screams at night and wakes others, because he has a stomachache.⟩ ⟨**Non kóchi réteara sión ikai.** When we kill a pig, it lets out sharp screams.⟩ *syn.* See under **saíiti**
*n.* **sípaman** : sardine ⟨**Nokon pápaisinra isínxon sipán betan paránta xoires píai.** When he's sick, my grandfather eats only sardine and roasted plantain so as not to get worse.⟩
[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *sipán* sardine] : sapamama (a type of fish)
*also* **sepícho** *n.* **sipíchonin** *also* **sepíchonin** [from Spanish] : brush ⟨**Jakón riki sipíchonin noa xechokiiti.** It is good to brush one's teeth with a brush.⟩ *syn.* **nóreti**

*n.* **sipón** [from Spanish] : stocks (a restraint device); *also* : punishment by stocks ⟨**Moátianronki non pápashokobo sipón ápaokanike.** They say that long ago our ancestors were put in stocks.⟩
*n.* **sípoman** : wrinkle : fold *syn.* **chóre**
*also* **siéra** *n.* **sirán** *also* **siéranin** [from Spanish] : saw ⟨**Jonínra sirán mekén xáteke.** The man cut his hand with the saw.⟩
*also* **séda** *n.* **sirán** *also* **sedán** [from Spanish] : silk ⟨**síra chopabo** silk fabrics⟩
See under **keré**
*v.t.* **sírana** [from Spanish *serra(r)* + Shipibo *-n* verbalizing suf. + *-ti* infinitive suf.] : to saw ⟨**Nato tábarara en síranai.** I'm going to saw this board.⟩
*also* **Sílas** *n.* **Sírasen** *also* **Sílasen** [from Spanish *Silas*] –Used as a masculine name.

*also* **sirbínti** *v.t. and v.i.* **síribina** *also* **sírbina** [from Spanish *servir, sirve-, servi-* + Shipibo *-n*, verbalizing suf. + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] *v.t.* : to serve : to be of service to ⟨**Nokon papánra jawen pátoron síribinke.** My father served his boss.⟩ *v.i.* : to serve : to be worth : to have value ⟨**Ea moa yósishoko ikénbira nokon mekénbo síribimparike wétsa jawéki átibo.** Even though I am already very old, my hands still serve to do many things.⟩ ⟨**Nato machítora páyotax moa síribinyamai.** This machete, once old, no longer serves any purpose.⟩
*n.* **Sirón** [from Spanish *Kiro*] –Used as a masculine name.

*adj.* **sirón** 1 : very thin : quite skinny ⟨**Nato jónira síro iki, ísinai ikax.** This man is skinny because he has been sick for a long time.⟩ 2 : stuck flat, plastered down ⟨**Ea náshiara nokon bóo síroke.** When I bathed, my hair got wet and stuck flat to my head.⟩
*v.t.* **síroaa** *Konibo* **síroaka** : to make thin : to make lose weight ⟨**Kirípi koshínra ea síroake.** A bad flu has made me lose weight.⟩
*also* **serócho** *n.* **siróchonin** *also* **seróchonin** [from Spanish] : handsaw ⟨**Kirínkoninra noa siróchobo máromake.** The foreigner sold us the handsaws.⟩

*n.* **sisán** : sisa (a flower) ⟨**Meráyaninronki rimón jenen jónibo náshikiinke, sísaya méskoshon, korós naman móchanoxon.** They say that a pagan prophet bathed with some people in lemon juice mixed with sisa flowers as a ritual at the foot of a cross.⟩
*n.* **Sísarinin** [from Spanish *Késar*] –Used as a masculine name.
*n.* [from Spanish] : Cesarea
See under **róno**
*v.t.* **síwaa** : to singe ⟨**Káshibobaonra, síwaamabi awá kobinhaxon píkanai.** The Cashibo eat boiled tapir meat without first singeing it over the fire.⟩

*v.i.* **síwaa** 1 : to wither ⟨**Santíra bánaxonbi non kapé tílaketianronki ja baná síwatai.** They say that if we plant watermelon and then touch a caiman, the crop withers.⟩ 2 : to grow abnormally (from lack of cultivation or irrigation)

*v.t.* **síwina** [from Shipibo *síi iti, sii-* to drain/slip out + *wínoti* to pass to the side] 1 : to pick out : to take out from inside ⟨**Enra jíwi néaa ikáinoa westíora xáwi siwínke.** I easily pulled out one cane from among the bundled poles.⟩ ⟨**Yómetsoninra nokon kírika meranoa koríki siwínke.** A thief took the money out from inside my book.⟩ 2 : to extract ⟨**Kíni meranoara en níshi siwínke.** I pulled and extracted a vine from the hole.⟩ 3 : to unsheathe (e.g., a sword) ⟨**Koáratianínra jawen ispára siwínke, jóni rakéakin.** The guard unsheathed his sword to scare the man.⟩ 4 : to pull out (e.g., thread from a needle) ⟨**Xomóxkini meranoara nato bakén yomán siwínke.** This boy pulled and took the thread out of the needle's eye.⟩ *syn.* **pakémati**
*also* **séyo** *n.* **siyón** *also* **seyón** [from Spanish] : stamp, seal *syn.* **máraka**

*v.t.* **sóaa** 1 : to clean or dry by rubbing ⟨**Titánra jawen chómobo sóai.** Mom is cleaning her clay jars.⟩ ⟨**Nokon ponyánra moa soá iki niskanoma.** My arm is already dry and free of sweat.⟩ 2 : to erase ⟨**Nato bakénra sóakin kírika wáxbake.** This child was erasing his notebook and tore it.⟩ ⟨**Nokon jáne moa soá ikénra, en moa Kakónko káyamai.** My name has already been erased, so now I won't go to Caco.⟩
*n.* **sóatinin** [from Shipibo *sóati, soa-* to erase] : eraser ⟨**Káocho bepón bixónra sóatibo ákanai.** Erasers are made from rubber.⟩
See **Soróma**

*adj.* **sóikan** 1 : pleasing to look at for being smooth and well-formed ⟨**Báke xóntakon yórara soí iki.** A young lady's body is pleasing, smooth, and well-formed.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbora kikínbires soí iki; jákopira jaón kéenkanai.** This woman is very charming, and that's why men love her a lot.⟩ 2 : glossy : shiny ⟨**Nokon titán bóora soí iki.** My mom's hair is very glossy.⟩
*v.i.* **sóikiita** : to rub oneself
*v.i.* **sóita** : to become shiny : to become glossy ⟨**Nanén ikáronkinon bóo sóitai.** They say that if we dye our hair with huito, it becomes glossy.⟩ *syn.* **joéti**

*adj.* **sókotanin** [from Quechua *sukta*] : six ⟨**Chónka jónira téeti káke káchio; sókotara ísini banéke.** Ten men went to work in the forest, and six ended up sick.⟩ ⟨**Sókota mayápekaora nokon jéma iki.** My community is six river bends away.⟩
*n.* **somán** [from Spanish] : sum, addition
*v.t.* **sómana** [from Spanish] : to add up ⟨**Sománti iki "+"–ya.** Addition is represented with the sign "+".⟩ *syn.* **áti**

*v.i.* **sómona** : to swell : to thicken ⟨**Bonán tékaara nokon bakén rekín somónke.** My child's nose swelled up because a isula (bullet ant) bit him.⟩ ⟨**Binán tékaara nokon mekén somón iki.** My hand is swollen because a wasp stung me.⟩ ⟨**Ménotaxa nokon ponyán somónke.** When I burned my arm, it swelled up.⟩ ⟨**Nato jonín táera somónyora iki tatoxbatax.** This man's foot has swollen because he has blisters.⟩ *syn.* SOMONTI, SOOITI, and SHOMONTI can all be translated as "to swell," but SOMONTI is also translated as "to thicken." SOOITI implies swelling caused from inside the body, while SOMONTI and SHOMONTI refer to swelling caused externally, e.g., by a wound, a cut, or the friction that produces a blister.
See **-shoko**
*also* **soldádo** *n.* **sontáronin** *also* **soldádonin** [from Spanish] : soldier ⟨**Sontárobora yamékiritibi íshtokanai.** The soldiers do exercises every morning.⟩
*v.i.* **sóoika** [from Shipibo *sóo*, imitative of a swelling sound + *-iti* to make/do] : to swell ⟨**Eara bémanan sóoike, xetán chéxaa.** My face swelled up from a toothache.⟩
*v.t.* **sopóaa** *Konibo* **sopóaka** : to bulk up or give volume to (hair or plumage) ⟨**Náwa ainbaonra jawen bóo sopóai.** The mestiza woman gives volume to her hair with a perm.⟩
See under **ochíti**
*v.i.* **sópota** : to bulk up, to puff out (hair or plumage) ⟨**Nato aínbaon bóora sopó iki, bóexeeyamai ikax.** This woman's hair is puffed out because she doesn't comb it.⟩
*n.* **sorímanin** [from Spanish] : solima (a type of powdered medicine)

*n.* **sorón** [from Spanish] : sol (the Peruvian currency unit) ⟨**Moátianronki sóro jóxokoriki ikátiai.** They say that in the old days the sol coin was nine-tenths silver.⟩ ⟨**Westíora pácha sorónra ráma noa jawéki mároti átipanyamake.** With a hundred soles you can no longer buy anything.⟩
*n.* **sorón** [from Spanish] : south
See under **Amírika**
*also* **Sodóma** *n.* **Sorómanin** *also* **Sodómanin** [from Spanish] : Sodom

*v.i.* **sórota** 1 : to crouch, to squat (animal) ⟨**Matsín ikíra mari sórotai.** The agouti crouches down from the cold.⟩ 2 : to be (a woman) fat and without a nice figure ⟨**Nato aínbora yoxán jisá iki, sórota ikax.** This woman looks like a grandmother, because she is very fat and without a nice figure.⟩
*n.* **Sosánan** *Konibo* **Sosánanin** [from Spanish *Susana*] –Used as a feminine name.
*v.t.* **sótana** : to spy from a hiding place ⟨**Sontárobaonra jaton rawíbo sótanai.** The soldiers spy on their enemies from a hiding place.⟩

*adj.* **sótokan** [from Shipibo *sóoiti, soo-* to swell + *tóoti, too-* to become pregnant] : small : short and plump in body or mass ⟨**Rámara páan sotóbires márokanai.** Now only small loaves of bread are sold.⟩ *syn.* See under **ánima**
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *t* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1
*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *táe* foot] : on the foot : to the foot : of the foot ⟨**taxtéti** to cut the foot of⟩

*suf. of mood* : let's see : please —Used added to the end of the verb to indicate the polite imperative mood of a request or entreaty. ⟨**Noa oímata.** Let's see; show us.⟩ ⟨**Eapari akínta.** Help me, please.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3.3

*verbal suf.* —Used at the end of a subordinate verb with the force of "upon/as soon as". ⟨**Nokótaananra, noa tántiai.** Upon arriving, we will rest.⟩ ⟨**Orotaananra, papán píke.** Immediately after farming, dad ate.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.3.2
*also* **tábla** *n.* **tábaranin** *also* **táblanin** : board : plank
See **Rabíri**
*v.t.* **táchita** : to water : to irrigate

[from Shipibo *ompáx* water + *táchiti* to water] : to water ⟨**En jóa bánaara moa barín wekánhake en ompáx táchiamaa.** The flowers I planted wilted from the sun because I hadn't watered their roots.⟩
*v.t.* **táchita** : to pour (water) while watering
[from Shipibo *ompáx* water + *tachíti* to pour] : to water ⟨**banáshokobo ompáx táchitai** the one who waters the seedlings⟩
*adj.* **tachón** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *-cho* with boils] : having a rash on the foot
*v.t.* **táchota** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *chókati* to wash] : to wash the feet of
*n.* **taén** 1 : foot : paw ⟨**Nokon táera isín iki chóshita.** My foot is dislocated because I hit it.⟩ 2 : foot : unit of measure equal to twelve inches
[from Shipibo *ián* lagoon, cocha (oxbow lake) + *táe* foot] : caño (channel) of a lake ⟨**Ián taénra yápa páenai.** In the channel the fish become dazed.⟩
*n.* **táechipoman** [from Shipibo *táe* foot + *chipon*, element of *chipónki* downriver] : heel
*n.* [from Shipibo *táe* caño (channel) + *máxka* upper part] : head of a channel ⟨**Táemaxkainra yápa páeni ícha ike.** At the head of the channel there were many fish getting dazed.⟩
*n.* **táemebin** : toe
See under **mentsís**
See under **móxa**
*n.* **táenapaxan** [from Shipibo *táe* foot + *napáx* raw] : sole of the foot
*also* **táenoxpe** *n.* **táenoachonin** *also* **táenoxpekan** [from Shipibo *táe* foot + *noacho*, *noxpk*, unidentified element] : arch of the foot
See under **páketi**
*also* **táepexke** *n.* **táe patonkonin** *also* **táepexkekan** [from Shipibo *táe* foot + *patónko* ear cartilage] : ankle
*n.* **táepekakan** [from Shipibo *táe* foot + *peká* back] : upper part of the foot
See under **póa**
*n.* **takán** : liver ⟨**Enra wáka taka shéakai pínoxon.** I'm frying beef liver to eat.⟩
*n.* **takáchonin** [from Spanish] : tacacho (mashed fried plantain with pork) ⟨**Enra takácho ákai.** I'm preparing tacacho.⟩
*n.* **takárinin** : a large fish species that lives mostly in springs
*n.* **takárinin** : small mallet ⟨**Enra átsa takárinin cháchiai.** I'm mashing manioc with the mallet.⟩
*v.i.* **takáshika** : to make a splashing sound (of liquid) upon striking ⟨**Bechón máikiniki tsákatira takáshitai.** The waves make a splashing sound as they hit the shore.⟩
*n.* **takáshitinin** : heartbeat
See **kátoti**
*v.t.* **tákexa** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *kéxeti* to sew] : to sew (pants) at the hem
*n.* **takín** : tibe (a river turtle) ⟨**Takínra báchiakai mashín.** The tibe lays its eggs on the beach.⟩
[from Shipibo *nepáx* guama (a fruit tree) + *táki* tibe] : tuquituqui (a shorebird) ⟨**Nepáxtakinra xéna píai jisónanti méranoa.** The tuquituqui eats worms found amid the sedge grass.⟩
See under **wáste**
*n.* **takón** : unchala (a large owl) ⟨**Takónra bákebo ráteke íno keskati kéokin.** The unchala owl scared the children by imitating the tigre's (jaguar's) roar.⟩
See under **móxa**
See under **wáme**
*n.* **tamán** : peanut ⟨**Táma wáira en óroai.** I'm cultivating a peanut field.⟩
[from Shipibo *mánko* baldness + *táma* peanut] : a species of peanut with a very red shell
[from Shipibo *kéne* design + *táma* peanut] : a species of patterned peanut
See under **átsa**
*n.* **támaxakan** [from Shipibo *táma* peanut + *xaká* scale] : maparate (a catfish species) ⟨**Támaxaka xáoma ikaxsha noéira iki.** The maparate has no bones (spines) and is delicious.⟩
*v.i.* **taménoota** [from Shipibo *taménoti* to burn the foot of + *-oo*, reflexive suf.] : to burn one's foot ⟨**Xána ompáx pákeaxra, taménooke.** He burned his foot when he dropped the hot water.⟩
*v.t.* **taménoa** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *ménoti* to burn] : to burn the foot of ⟨**Bakénra ochíti taménoai.** The child is burning the dog's foot.⟩
*n.* **tamón** : cheek : side of the face : jaw ⟨**Xetán chéxaara ea tamónko sóolke.** When my tooth hurt, my cheek swelled up.⟩ *syn.* kói
*n.* **tampéxkonin** : jaw or gill of a fish
*also* **tambóro** *n.* **tampóranin** *also* **tambóronin** : drum

*modifying suf.* —Used with an intransitive verb with the force of "to go and come back" or with a transitive verb with the force of "to go and do". ⟨**Binón bitanwe.** Go get some aguajes (Mauritia palm fruits).⟩ ⟨**Níi meranra ea katánhibake.** I went to the forest yesterday.⟩
*v.i.* **tánakaata** [from Shipibo *tánati* to try, to taste + *-kaa*, reflexive suf.] : to be tempted
*v.t.* **tánaa** : to try : to taste ⟨**Enra sápato tánake.** I tried on the shoes.⟩ ⟨**Enra kobín tánake táshi onánoxon.** I tasted the soup to find out if it had salt or not.⟩
See under **báwa**
*v.t.* **tánexa** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *néxati* to tie] : to tie the feet of ⟨**Jábaonra jóni tánexai.** They are tying the man's feet.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*modifying suf.* —Used with a meaning that in many cases can be translated as "a little" or "barely". —Added to an adjective, adverb, or verb, with no fixed position in the order of suffixes. ⟨**Eara katánike.** I have barely left.⟩ ⟨**Yámatanike píti.** There is almost no food.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2; 8.3.6

*also* **tanóa** *adj.* **tanón** *also* **tanóanin** : dried out to the point of being blackened and unusable —Used, e.g., regarding wood. ⟨**Jíwi tanónkora bawán bákeaka iki.** The loro (parrot) laid its young in the dry, dead wood.⟩
*v.i.* **tánoa** : to dry out
*n.* **tánsharinan** : mandarin orange ⟨**Bakénra tánsharina xókai.** The child is peeling the mandarin orange.⟩
*v.i.* **tansóoika** : [from Shipibo *tan-*, element of *tampéxko* jaw + *sóoiti* to swell] to have a swollen cheek ⟨**Bákera tansóoikai.** The child has a swollen cheek.⟩
*v.t.* **tántimaa** [from Shipibo *tántiti* to rest + *ma-* to cause] : to soothe (e.g., pain)
*v.i.* **tántia** : to rest : to take a break ⟨**Jáinoaxa noa tántiibake, móa báriapan senénketian.** So then we took a break because it was already noon.⟩
See under **yápa**
*v.t.* **tányana** : to shape with an axe (e.g., the keel of a canoe) ⟨**Papánra nónti táyanai.** Dad is shaping the canoe's keel.⟩

*n.* **táokan** : huacrapona (a stilt palm) ⟨**Taóra nónti áti iki.** Canoes are made from huacrapona.⟩ ⟨**Epánra taó chákai tápo ati.** Uncle is chopping huacrapona to make emponado flooring (split-palm flooring).⟩

*v.i.* **táoskeanana** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *oxánti, oxan-* to put to sleep + *-ken,* unidentified element] : to have one's feet fall asleep ⟨**Eara táoskenanke bási chiránkotax maístoron kastíkana.** When the teacher punished me, I knelt for a while and my feet fell asleep.⟩
*n.* **tápaman** : logs tied together : raft ⟨**Móatianronki pápabaon tapán bokátikanai Ikítoain.** They say that long ago our ancestors used to take rafts to Iquitos.⟩
*n.* **tápasan** : a large basket made of vines that, when hung in the house, is used to store provisions
*n.* **tápashan** : a type of trap set in the caño (channel) to catch fish and turtles
*n.* **tapítinin** 1 : ladder 2 : stairway ⟨**Tapítininra ea mápetai.** I'm climbing the stairway.⟩
*n.* **tapón** : emponado (split-palm flooring) ⟨**Tapónkora ochíti rakáke.** The dog is lying on the emponado floor.⟩ *syn.* See under **sínopepo**

*n. & adj.* **tápokan** *n.* : long clothing (e.g., a skirt or pants); *specif.* : a type of traditional long garment *adj.* : long —*Used regarding clothing.* ⟨**Nokon chiárexti tapó íketianra, en takátoai.** Since my pants are long, I'll fold them up.⟩ *syn.* nenké

*n.* **tápoaka** [from Shipibo *tápo* emponado + *-ati* to do] : to make a floor or barbacoa (raised platform) for a house ⟨**Níi meranra ea katanhíbake, tápoanoxon síno bénai.** I went to the monte (forest) to get pona (palm bark) to make my floor.⟩
*n.* **tápoman** : root
See under **awá**
*v.i.* **tárameeta** : to roll around : to wallow
*also* **trámpa** *n.* **tarámpanin** *also* **trámpanin** [from Spanish] : trap
*n.* **taránkinin** : shirúe (a fish species) ⟨**Enra rikánkin taránki bíke.** I caught a shirúe by casting a net.⟩ *syn.* báxo
*v.t.* **tárana** : to roll (something) : to make roll ⟨**Jónibaonra xóno taránke.** The men rolled the lupuna (giant ceiba tree).⟩

*v.i.* **táraxa** : to dry up : to undergo evaporation (e.g., of water) ⟨**Ronín pikóketianronki, ián táraxai.** They say that if the yacumama (mythical water-boa) emerges, the cocha (oxbow lake) dries up.⟩
*n.* **taréshpinin** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the leg + *reshpi*, unidentified element] : leg of a turtle
*v.t.* **táreta** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *rérati* to knock down] : to fell : to knock down ⟨**Papánra jíwi táretai.** Dad is felling the tree.⟩ *syn.* póxati

*n.* **tarín** : cushma (a traditional tunic) ⟨*Móatianronki jóni xóxoti káketian oínyamaketian,* **jawen tarí meran xawan néeta iki.** It's told that some years ago a man went to visit his sweetheart at night; and, without him noticing, a guacamayo (macaw) climbed up inside his cushma⟩
*n.* **taríanin** [from Spanish] : homework ⟨**Taría áyamaketianra, maistoron bákebo kastíkanke.** The teacher punished the students because they didn't do their homework.⟩
*adj.* **tarón** : dirty ⟨**Wáinko kátanax nokon yóra táro iki jakopira, ea náshiai.** I come back from the garden plot with a dirty body, so I bathe.⟩ *syn.* See under **oshtá**
*n.* **táronarion** [from Spanish] : receipt book ⟨**Jawen pátoronin táronario meranra serébo jáke.** In his boss's receipt book there are parallel lines.⟩
*n.* **tásakan** : basket ⟨**Tásakan napónxonra kári béke.** He put the sweet potatoes in the basket and brought them.⟩
*adj.* **tásesen** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *sése* freckled] : having spots on the foot

*v.t.* **táshaa** *cont.* **táshaka** [from Shipibo *tash*, imitative of the sound + *-ati* to do] : to hit (e.g., with the hand) ⟨**Bákebora tsíniai máno táshaa iki; jaínxonra jawen papán oínxon notsínke.** The children were playing in the mud and hitting each other; then their father saw them and scolded them.⟩
*n.* **tashín** : salt ⟨**Non yósipapaboronki bópaonike chipónki táshi bíi.** They say our ancestors used to go downriver to get salt⟩
*v.t.* **tashín aka** [from Shipibo *táshi, tashín* salt + *-ati* to do] : to preserve fish with salt

*v.i.* **tásketa** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *sekéti* to break] : to dislocate one's foot ⟨**Mái chaká ikain jámataxa, jóni taskéke.** Stepping where the ground was cracked, the man dislocated his foot.⟩
*n.* **tásoman** [from Spanish] : bowl ⟨**Nato bakénra jawen titán tasón áraake, rabón pékaxon.** This boy put a hole in his mother's bowl with a nail.⟩
*v.t.* **tásoa** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *sóati* to rub] : to wipe dry the feet of
*v.i.* **tátekeika** : to make an involuntary movement of the foot ⟨**Eara táteke ike.** I moved my foot involuntarily.⟩
*v.t.* **tátea** : to shape with an adze ⟨**Nóntira en táteai.** I'm shaping my canoe with an adze.⟩
*n.* **tátetinin** [from Shipibo *táteti, tate-* to adze + *-ti* instrument suf.] : adze ⟨**Tátetira ea mároai ríkatonimea.** I'm buying an adze from the trader.⟩
*v.t.* **tátina** : to string (beads) ⟨**Títanra móro tátinai.** Mom is stringing the beads.⟩

*n.* **tawán** : cañabrava (wild cane) : cane thicket ⟨**Náwabaonra táwa sépai, poróto bánati.** The mestizos are clearing cane thickets to plant beans.⟩
See under **ísko**
*n.* **tawámparin** : manitoa (a riverbank fruit tree) ⟨**Nokon papánra tanwámpari tashínakai mároti.** My dad makes manitoa preserves to sell.⟩
*v.t.* **táwasana** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *wasánti* to clean (e.g., dust)] : to clean the feet of ⟨**jato máipoto táwasanti** to clean the dust off their feet⟩

*n.* **tawín** : gall : bile; *also* : gallbladder ⟨**Manánxawe tawínra ea bechéxke nokon titán táka chókakin oínyamaxon.** When my mom was washing the motelo's (tortoise's) liver, she wasn't careful and the bile burst and got into my eye.⟩ ⟨**Yóashiko Inkán táwironki jorín tokó-** **nike.** They say the little *jóri* bird perched on top of the stingy Inca's gallbladder.⟩ *syn.* móka

*n.* **taxán** : dry driftwood found especially on the riverbank beach ⟨**Táxa mashín rákatatonra manxán yakáke.** A heron is perched on the dry driftwood lying on the beach.⟩

See under **káshi**

*n.* **táxbakan** : tahuampa (seasonally flooded forest) ⟨**Kokánra yóike táxbakan yápa páenai amákiri, mócho, bawín, píro.** My uncle says that in the tahuampa the gamitanas, súngaros, turushuques, and cahuaras (all fish species) are getting dazed.⟩
See under **jóno**
See under **níshi**
*n.* **taxkánwapan** : a species of nocturnal bird ⟨**Taxkánwapan báchiakai manánkini meran.** The bird *taxkánwapa* lays its eggs in caves in the hills.⟩
*v.t.* **táxkea** : to move : to shift from one place to another : to relocate ⟨**Nokon nóntira en táxkeai síwanoxon.** I move my canoe to burn it quickly.⟩

*v.i.* **táxkona** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *xko*, unidentified element + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to stretch out one's foot ⟨**Enra táxkonai nokon pápashoko tobíamai.** I'm stretching out my foot so my grandfather can rub it.⟩
See under **bína**

*v.t.* **táxnana** [from Shipibo *taxnáti* to dock (a boat) + *-n*, verbal derivation suf.] : to glue : to stick ⟨**Bákebaonra wétsa kírika kírakaki taxnánti iki.** The students have to glue one paper onto another.⟩
*v.i.* **táxnata** : to dock (a boat) ⟨**Ríkatonra taxnáke jato máromai.** The trader docked to do his business.⟩ *syn.* See under **répiti**
*n.* **taxón** : handle (e.g., of an axe) ⟨**Nokon yámi táxora en sékeke.** I broke the handle of my axe.⟩
*v.i.* **táxoa** : to lick ⟨**Ochítininra jawen báke táxoai.** The mother dog licks her pup.⟩
*v.t.* **táxteta** [from Shipibo *ta-* on the foot + *xáteti* to cut] : to cut the foot or toes of ⟨**Bidirionra ea taxtéke.** The glass cut my foot.⟩
*v.t.* **táyana** : to shape (wood) ⟨**Jan rastón áti yóiabira witá, tayánkin papán wiríshake.** Dad made the posts thin while shaping them, even though he was told to make them thick.⟩
*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo; element of *téxo* neck] : on the neck ⟨**téxteti** to cut through the neck⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*n.* **téamiston** [from Shipibo *téati, tea-* to commit adultery with + *-mis* one who always does (the indicated thing)] : adulterer
*v.i.* **téamisa** [from Shipibo *téamis* adulterer + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to be an adulterer : to commit adultery
*v.t.* **téaa** *Konibo* **téaka** : to bother : to annoy ⟨**Bakénra jawen pói téake, ríshkikaskin.** The boy was bothering his little sister, wanting to hit her.⟩ *syn.* jatsánbati

*n.* **téchapanin** [from Shipibo *te-* on the neck + *chapáti, chapat-* to fork] : a species of tree with forking branches ⟨**Jíwi téchapaninra jóni yakáke.** The man sat on the tree with forking branches.⟩
*n.* **téekan** : work
*n.* **téetaitonin** [from Shipibo; participle of *téeti* to work] : worker : laborer *syn.* See under **rayá**

*v.i.* **téeta** : to work —Often used with the complement of means. ⟨**Jóniboronki téetai káritiranko pátoron wáiaxoni.** They say the men are working near the road, making the boss's garden plot.⟩ ⟨**Moátian káochonin téeti kax ítira, moa jóke.** He finally came after having worked rubber for a long time.⟩ *syn.* TEETI and YONOTI both mean "to work", but YONOTI refers more to work done to fulfill an order; also, YONOTI is no longer much used.
*adj.* **téeyaton** [from Shipibo *téeti, tee-* to work + *-ya* having] : hardworking : industrious *syn.* See under **rayá**
*n.* **téipan** : a small bird species ⟨**Téipa báchi bíaintianra ea binán tékake.** While I was taking the eggs from the little *téipa* bird, a wasp stung me.⟩
*adj.* **tékamisnin** : stinging : venomous —Used regarding insects and animals that sting with their tail. ⟨**Bóna riki tékamis.** The isula (bullet ant) is venomous.⟩

*v.t.* **tékaa** : to sting ⟨**Nibónra báke tékake.** A scorpion stung the child.⟩ *syn.* TEKATI and TSAKATI can both be translated as "to sting", but in Shipibo the senses aren't confused. TEKATI implies something venomous (e.g., a wasp) that stings, while TSAKATI implies a person who pricks/stings, e.g., with an arrow.
*v.i.* **tekéika** : to react (e.g., by jerking in fright) with the head, face, or body when something unexpected happens ⟨**Rátetaxa ea tekéike nókon mápo.** When I got scared, my head jerked.⟩
*v.i.* **tekéyana** : to run aground : to strand on the shore ⟨**Márinirobaonra wapóro tekéyankana iki.** The sailors ran the ship aground.⟩
*n.* **tékikan** : joint
*v.t.* **tekíaa** *Konibo* **tekíaka** : to join by tying a knot ⟨**Nokon sapáto pásador teséketianra en tekíake.** When my shoelace broke, I joined it with a knot.⟩

*v.i.* **tékita** 1 : to heal —Used regarding a body with an injury that scars over. ⟨**Eara tóbitax tekíke.** I healed after a while of having been injured.⟩ 2 : to knit back together (of an injured bone) ⟨**Xáora tekíke.** The bone knit back together.⟩ 3 : to gather (people) in a line —Used in this sense in the infinitive form with imperative force. ⟨**¡Tekíti!** Line up!⟩
See **tímpiro**
*v.t.* **ténaa** : to illuminate ⟨**Barín ténaara, jéne penéke.** The water sparkled because the sun was illuminating it.⟩

*v.t.* **ténea** : to endure : to bear (e.g., pain) —Usually used with the past participle describing the subject's state. ⟨**Xetán chéxara en téneai.** I bear my toothache.⟩ ⟨**Ménotaxa ja chéxaa téneyamai.** He got burned and can't bear the pain.⟩
: to suffer ⟨**Jonínra moa rabé néte masá téneai, píti yámaketian.** The man has been suffering for two days because there is no food.⟩ *syn.* ónitsapiti
*adj.* **ténetiman** [from Shipibo *téneti* to endure + *-ma* without] : intense : unbearable

*n.* **teón** [from Shipibo *te-*, element of *téxo* neck + *-o*, unidentified element] : necklace : choker *syn.* TEO and TEOTI can both be translated as "necklace", but TEO specifically means "choker".
*n.* **téoteon** : a small hawk species ⟨**Téoteonra isá bixon píai.** The eagle eats birds when it hunts.⟩

*v.t.* **téoa** [from Shipibo *téo* necklace + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to tie around the neck —Used in the past-tense form (e.g., *téoke*) with the sense of "to have tied around the neck". ⟨**Titánra joshín panyón téoke.** The mother put a red kerchief around (her) neck.⟩

*n.* **téotinin** [from Shipibo *teo*; cf. *téo* necklace + *-ti* instrument suf.] : necklace ⟨**Metsákatenra koríki téoti sáwekatitai xóntakotian.** Metsákate used to wear a cast-silver necklace when she was a young lady.⟩ *syn.* See under **téo**
*v.i.* **tépata** : to move (e.g., a canoe) by beaching or launching it ⟨**Nokon bótira en tépatai towé bóyanoxon.** I'm going to beach the boat in order to patch what's broken.⟩

*n.* **tepín** : pucuna (blowgun) : blowgun ⟨**Móatian yósibaon tepín jawéki rétekatikanai íso, jasín, jainoax meskó jawékibo.** Long ago the elders used to kill maquisapas (spider monkeys), paujiles (curassows), and various other animals with the blowgun.⟩
See under **bóna**
*n.* **tépikotin** [from Shipibo *te*, element of *téxo* neck + *pikóti, pikot-* to come out] : sacarita

*v.i.* **tépia** [from Shipibo *te*, element of *téxo* neck + *pi*, unidentified element + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to lie on a pillow ⟨**Bákera tépike tépitinin.** The child is lying on the pillow.⟩

*n.* **tépitinin** [from Shipibo *tépiti, tepi-* to lie on a pillow + *-ti* instrument suf.] : pillow ⟨**Rámatianra náwabo tépitinin mároai.** Nowadays the mestizos sell pillows.⟩ ⟨**Bákera jisónke papán tépitiki.** The child urinated on dad's pillow.⟩

*n.* **tépochinin** [from Shipibo *te-* on the neck + *pochini*, unidentified element] : neck (e.g., of a bottle) ⟨**Ompásha botíria tépochinin senén iki.** The water is right at the neck of the bottle.⟩
*n.* **térakanin** : a large rat species ⟨**Papán wái ménoaínra téraka meshó íbake.** When dad burned the garden plot, the *téraka* rat got charred.⟩
*n.* **terénkenin** : black caiman ⟨**Terénkeninronki xáe biá iki; ikáxbi xáe kóshiora íxón wáxaa iki.** They say the black caiman caught the anteater; but the anteater, being strong, tore it apart⟩
See under **móe**
*v.t.* **tésaa** *Konibo* **tésaka** : to break : to tear apart ⟨**Yománra en tésake.** I broke the thread.⟩ *syn.* See under **nóshiti** *syn.* **beshéati**
*adj. & n.* **tésekan** *adj.* : broken *n.* : piece ⟨**Kábo tesé óinaxa ea rátéke, rónora íbirai ikáx.** When I saw a piece of rope cable, I got scared thinking it was a snake.⟩ *syn.* **tsósa**
*adj.* **tésesan** [from Shipibo *te-*, element of *téxo* neck + *sése* speckled] : having spots on the neck
*v.i.* **téseta** : to break

*n.* **tésharantinin** [from Shipibo *te-*, on the neck + *sharanti*, unidentified element] : trachea ⟨**Titánra mánxaman tésharanti pótake, ochítinin pinón íxón.** Mom threw out the heron's trachea for the dog to eat.⟩
*n.* **teshpin** [from Shipibo *te-* on the neck + *shpi*, unidentified element] : uvula
[from Shipibo *téshpi* uvula + *isínti* to be sick] : to have or be down with tonsillitis ⟨**Bákera téshpi isínke.** The child had tonsillitis.⟩
*v.i.* **tésketa** [from Shipibo *te-*, element of *téxo* neck + *sekéti* to break] : to have or end up with a neck injury; to dislocate one's neck ⟨**Eara teskéke.** I dislocated my neck.⟩
*n.* **tétekan** : hawk : falcon ⟨**Tétekanra chónchobake píke.** The hawk ate the chick.⟩
[from Shipibo *kóma* godmother/close female friend + *teté* hawk] : a species of hawk with a long tail and a striped chest
[from Shipibo *jasín* paujil (curassow) + *teté* hawk] : a large, black-colored hawk species
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *teté* hawk] : a white-colored hawk species
[from Shipibo *náwa* foreigner + *teté* hawk] : a large hawk species with prominent ear tufts
See under **wáste**
*n.* **tétoman** [from Shipibo *te-* on the neck + *ton*, element of *tónko* protuberance] : Adam's apple
[from Shipibo *tetón* throat + *isínti* to be sick] : to have a sore, hoarse, or infected throat

*v.i.* **tetón ika** [from Shipibo *tetón* Adam's apple + *iti* to do] : to have a serious throat illness ⟨**Kókapapara tetón ikax joí pikóyamai, óspitarain bokánke.** My uncle can't come out because he has a serious throat illness; they took him to the hospital.⟩

*v.i.* **téwana** : to lean : to prop oneself up (e.g., with a post) ⟨**Xobo niwén póxakeana tánxatara wítakan non téwamake.** When the wind almost blew down the house that was leaning, we propped it up with a post.⟩
*adj. & n.* **texén** [from Shipibo *téxeti, téxe-* to be left over] *adj.* : left over *n.* : leftover piece

*v.t.* **téxeaa** *Konibo* **téxeaka** : to leave extra of : to set aside ⟨**Nokon pápashokora bawinbeten téxeaxonke wái orói kawánketian.** I set aside súngaro (catfish) porridge for my grandfather, who went to work the garden plot.⟩ *syn.* **bénxoati**; **chíteati**
*v.i.* **téxea** : to be left over : to remain ⟨**Chícharonki téxeke.** They said there was leftover chicha (fermented drink).⟩ *syn.* chíteti

*n.* **téxkaman** [from Shipibo *tex*, element of *téxe-* to be left over + *kan*, unidentified element] : bunch (of fruit) ⟨**Betanía jemanronki paranta ani téxkan iki, píchika chónka waránka sóro.** They said that in Betania a large bunch of plantains costs fifty thousand soles.⟩
See under **átapa**
*n.* **texón** : neck; *also* : nape ⟨**Jóni yótoara texónko chéxai.** The bewitched man has a bad neck.⟩ ⟨**Ochítininra átapa texo píai.** The dog is eating chicken neck.⟩

*n.* **téxokan** [from Shipibo *téxeti, texe-* to be left over + *o*, unidentified element] : quinilla (a hardwood tree) ⟨**Bitániain jónibo texó káxkei íbakanke, wáka chikénoxon.** Recently, the people of Betania split quinilla logs to fence in the cattle.⟩
*v.i.* **téxtekaata** : to have one's throat cut : to be beheaded

*n.* **téxtemisnin** [from Shipibo *téxeti, téxte-* to cut through the neck] : one who beheads; *also* : strangler ⟨**Yoshínxatanronki téxtemis ípaonike.** They say the payaso (clown) demon was a strangler.⟩

*v.t.* **téxtea** [from Shipibo *te-* on the neck + *xte*, element of *xate-, xáteti* to cut + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to cut through the neck : to behead; *specif.* : to decapitate ⟨**Titánra átapa téxteke.** Mom beheaded the hen.⟩ 2 : to hang : to strangle *syn.* bóxteti

*infinitive suf.* —Used as the complement of certain verbs. ⟨**Enra mia akínti atipanyamake.** I can't help you.⟩ ⟨**Nokon pápa betanra káti jáke, ea íaman.** I have to go with my dad to the cocha (oxbow lake).⟩ —Used with the suffix *-n* or *-nin* also as the complement of certain verbs. ⟨**Eara kéenai Rimán katín.** I want to go to Lima.⟩ ⟨**Eara yokátinin rábinai.** I'm ashamed to ask him.⟩ —Used as a verb ending to indicate an anticipated or proposed action or event. ⟨**Jatian nokon papán, jíwi bochiki, tápoa iki, jain noa óxati.** So my dad built a floor up in the tree for us to sleep on.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.4.2

*nominal suf.* —Used with the force of "instrument with which" in some nouns derived from their corresponding verbs. —Added to the verb root. ⟨**Tóoatinra en íso tóoake.** I shot the maquisapa (spider monkey) with a shotgun.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.7

*conjunctive suf.* —Used with the sense of "when", "because", or "if" as the ending of the subordinate verb after any of the verbal suffixes: *-que, -ai,* and *-non.* ⟨**Ja jóketianra, ea kái.** When he comes, I will go.⟩ ⟨**Nokon báke ísinai bénxoama íketianra ea káyamai.** I'm not going because my sick child isn't getting better.⟩ –Used added to the noun to express "at the time of" in a subordinate clause without a verb. ⟨**Metsákatenra koríki téoti sáwekatitai xóntakotian.** Metsákate used to wear a silver necklace at the time when she was a young woman.⟩ ⟨**báketian** when he/she was a child⟩ See Grammar Sketch 5.3.2.2; 7.5; 8.3.6 *syn.* -ain; -ken

*v.t.* **tian aka** [from Shipibo *tian*, imitative + *–ati* to do] : to gargle with (e.g., tobacco) –Used mostly regarding a shaman. ⟨**Yóbekanra jakoma tsékanoxon róme tian akai.** The shaman, to draw out evil, gargles with tobacco.⟩ *syn.* See under **káshkakashka ati**
*v.t.* **tíaka** [from Shipibo *ti*, imitative of the sound + *–ati* to do] 1 : to touch 2 : to sound (a musical instrument)

*n.* **tíatinin** [from Shipibo *tíati*, *tia–* to sound + *–ti* instrument with which] : a type of thick horn blown as a signal, used by certain native groups to call people (e.g., to a meeting) ⟨**Ajíntininra tíati ákai jawen káibo kénakin.** The community leader blows the *tíati* horn to call his fellow villagers.⟩
*also* Tibet *n.* **Tibítonin** *also* **Tibétnin** : Tibet ⟨**Rínsira jáke Tibítoain.** The lynx lives in Tibet.⟩
*n.* **tíboron** : yanzasúngaro
*v.t.* **tíí aka** : to touch ⟨**Jara mékeman tíí ake.** He touched it with his hand.⟩

*modifying suf.* **–tibi** : all : each –Used added to the noun or pronoun that it modifies. ⟨**Páborotiibi jenényoshinbaon jéma jáke.** They say that in every river bend where there is a backwater pool there is a village of yacurunas (a mythical water-dwelling being in Amazonian folklore).⟩ ⟨**Nétetibira ea píkotai íshtoi.** Every day I go out running.⟩ *syn.* kára
*n.* **tíkoman** : a species of small bird ⟨**Tikómanra báchiakai máikini meran.** The *tikón* bird lays its eggs in a hole in the ground.⟩
*v.t.* **tímaa** *Konibo* **tímaka** : to strike : to hit : to beat ⟨**Eara jonín tímake, westíora aínbo jánsoa kopí.** A man hit me when a woman slandered me.⟩ *syn.* See under **chóshati**
*n.* **tímoman** [from Spanish] : rudder
*also* **témplo** *n.* **timpironin** *also* **témplonin** [from Spanish] : temple : church *syn.* See under **xóbo**

*v.t.* **tínaa** *Konibo* **tínaka** : to pack : to fill (an empty container) ⟨**Enra yóchi botírian tínai, bóe kobín jayá pínoxon.** I'm filling the chili-pepper bottle, to eat it with boquichico broth.⟩ *syn.* TINATI and TISATI are used and translated the same way, as "to fill (an empty receptacle)," without distinction; but TINATI also carries the added sense of "to pack what has been filled."
*v.t.* **tininhaa** : to make (e.g., fruits) fall together *syn.* See under **máanhati**
*v.i.* **tínina** : to fall together (e.g., the fruits of a tree) ⟨**Mánkoara tíninke moa wáchoax.** The mangoes fell together when they ripened.⟩ *syn.* See under **máanti**

*n. and adj.* **tinkón** *n.* : small piece : small thing *adj.* : short : too short ⟨**Nokon kanóti risbí tínko iketianra, wétsa rísbikan en tekíake.** Since my slingshot's cord was too short, I joined it with another, longer cord.⟩ *syn.* See under **nenkéma**
*also* **tienda** *n.* **tintán** *also* **tiéndanin** [from Spanish] : store : shop ⟨**Pápara káa iki tintánko kírosinin mároi.** Dad went to the store to buy kerosene.⟩ *syn.* See under **xóbo**
*suf. adj.* : of a specific size ⟨**—¿Jáwetio ánirin? —Ja riki áni ochítitio.** —How big is it? —It's the size of a big dog.⟩
*v.i.* **típina** : to lay down a group of similar things ⟨**Enra witá tipínke xóbo naman.** I laid the house posts down under the house.⟩
*v.i.* **típia** : to be lying down (things or animals of a single kind) ⟨**Wákara típike pastónko.** The cows are lying down in the pasture.⟩
*also* **trígo** *n.* **tírikonin** *also* **trígonin** [from Spanish] : wheat ⟨**tíriko páanhati** wheat for making bread⟩ ⟨**Wákanra tíriko xémeai.** The ox is threshing the wheat.⟩

*v.i.* **tirín ika** [from Shipibo *tirin*, imitative of the sound] : to thunder ⟨**Oi bénoxa tirín ikai; jáinoax kaná chópetai onsábires.** When it's about to rain, it thunders and there is lightning, which is very dangerous.⟩ *syn.* ríriiti

*v.i.* **tírita** : to burn : to give off heat and light ⟨**Neténra bári tíritai.** By day the sun gives light.⟩ : to blaze ⟨**Ja neténra wishtínbo tiríti keyóti iki.** On that day the stars will be destroyed, consumed in fire.⟩ *syn.* ketéti
*v.t.* **tísaa** *Konibo* **tísaka** : to fill (an empty container) *syn.* See under **tínati**
*v.i.* **tíshia** : to be stained ⟨**Nokon báchira tíshia iki.** My mosquito net is stained.⟩

*n.* **titán** 1 : mother : mom ⟨**Nokon titánra chómo kéneakai.** My mother is painting designs on the clay jar.⟩ —Used suffixed or prefixed to a woman's name with the meaning of "aunt," to express affection. ⟨**Méatita** Aunt Mea⟩ 2 : female relatives of the second ascending generation —Used in the plural form *títabo* to indicate the whole group of relatives on the mother's side.
