*Konibo* **títashoko** *n.* **títayoxaman** *Konibo* **títashokon** 1 : grandmother; *also* : sister of a grandfather or grandmother ⟨**Títashokonra cashímpo jótiai.** The grandmother is smoking a pipe.⟩ 2 : husband's grandmother; *also* : sister of the husband's grandmother 3 : grandfather's sister-in-law 4 : female relatives of the second ascending generation —Used in the plural form *títayoxanbo* or *titashocobo* to indicate the whole group of female relatives of the grandmothers' generation.
*n.* **tóakan** : scar ⟨**Báke ménotara bénxoaxbi toá toxkóyamai.** Although the burned child has healed, his scar has not gone away.⟩
*v.t.* **tóaa** *Konibo* **tóaka** 1 : to sift (e.g., grain) with a sifter 2 : to strain ⟨**Nokon poínra xéati tóake.** My sister strained the chapo (a sweet drink made from ripe plantains).⟩
*n.* **tóatinin** : sifter

*n.* **tóbaman** [from Shipibo *tobánti*, *toban–* to roast] : toasted corn or manioc : toasted-corn snack ⟨**Nato ainbora móti pikáshamai, tobánresa ákasai.** This woman doesn't like to eat boiled corn; she prefers toasted-corn snacks.⟩
*v.t.* **tóbana** : to toast —Used, e.g., regarding corn or peanuts. ⟨**Enra xéki tobánres píai.** I'm just eating toasted corn.⟩
*v.t.* **tóbaa** : to break : to split ⟨**Tóbaxonra, jonín páan piá iki.** The man broke the bread and ate it.⟩
*v.t.* **tóea** 1 : to split (e.g., firewood or pottery) 2 : to break ⟨**Enra chómo toéke.** I broke the clay jar.⟩ *syn.* See under **nóshiti**
*v.i.* **tóeta** 1 : to split/crack (e.g., pottery or firewood) 2 : to break : to shatter
*n.* **tokárinin** : a species of edible bird that feeds on the churo *nócho* (a type of freshwater snail)
*n.* **tokáyonin** [from Spanish] : namesake ⟨**Róaboyakoxonra nokon tokáyonin xóboayantanke.** Last year in Roaboya my namesake built a house.⟩
*v.t.* **tókona** : to hold or keep in the mouth (e.g., a ball of food) ⟨**Enra konjíti tokónke.** I had a candy in my mouth that I was sucking on.⟩
See under **kári**
*n.* **tókoronin** 1 : toad ⟨**Enra tókoro baín kakín mérake.** Walking along the path, I found a toad.⟩ 2 : frog
*v.i.* **tókoa** : to get stuck : to stick ⟨**Oxá ónitsa ikaxa báke tókoke bachín.** The child moved to one side while sleeping and got stuck to the mosquito net.⟩
*v.i.* **tokóxika** : to retch, to strain to vomit (e.g., upon smelling something foul) ⟨**Irimano Irías tokóxitai písi xéteax kinánkasi.** Brother Elías retches because he smelled something foul.⟩
*n.* **Tomásin** *also* **Tomásen** [from Spanish] –Used as a man's name.
*n.* **tomáyanin** : palillo (a plant whose root is used as a yellow dye/seasoning); *also* : fruit of the palillo
*n.* **tomín** : a species of small parrot whose female is called *tósha* ⟨**Tomínra xenán píai.** The little *tómi* parrot eats guaba (a legume with sweet pulp).⟩
*n.* **tomótomokan** : a species of small heron ⟨**Tomótomonra sanín píai.** The little *tomótomo* heron eats *sanín* sardines.⟩

*participial suf.* **-tonin** –Used at the end of the non-basic form of the participle. ⟨**Jíwi naman yákatatonra ea óinai.** The one who is under the tree is looking at me.⟩ ⟨**Jan píaitonra ea óinai.** The one who is eating is looking at me.⟩ ⟨**Jan piátoninra ea óinai.** The one who has already eaten is looking at me.⟩
*n.* **tónbokan** : group; *specif.* : herd/troop (of animals) ⟨**Kaxón jónin nókoa iki westíora** **tonbó íso.** While walking along, the man came across a troop of spider monkeys.⟩ *syn.* kóropo
*n.* **tonkón** 1 : knot ⟨**Jíwi tónkora chorish iki.** The tree's knot is hard.⟩ 2 : ball : bump/protuberance
*v.t.* **tónkoaka** : to round : to make round
*n.* **tónkomoron** [from Shipibo *tónko* round + *móro* bead] : beads ⟨**Tónkomoron kéenkinra nokon titán chómoake.** My mother made clay jars to sell because she wanted to buy beads.⟩
See under **santíra**
*n.* **tónoman** : cunchi (a species of catfish) ⟨**Tonónbetenra Rójirin píai.** Róger is eating cunchi-catfish porridge.⟩

*n.* **tonónkenin** [from Shipibo *tonón* cunchi-catfish + *kení* beard/whiskers] : a member of a religious sect known as "the Israelites," whose members are found mostly in Peru –Used in a slightly derogatory manner.

*n.* **tónroman** [from Shipibo *ton*, element of *tónko* round + *ron*, unidentified element] : sphere ⟨**Jatíbi rásenenbires toró íketian non ákai tonrón akín.** We call anything that is perfectly round a sphere.⟩
*v.t.* **tóoaka** : to shoot ⟨**Kománbimi píaitianra papán kanán ewa tóoake.** While the *kanán ehua* macaw was eating shihuahuaco fruit, dad shot it.⟩
*n.* **tóoatinin** : shotgun ⟨**Nokón pápashokonra tóoati bená mároke Ikítoainoa.** My grandfather bought a new shotgun from Iquitos.⟩
*adj.* **tóoismatonin** [from Shipibo *tóoti*, *too–* to become pregnant + *-isma* one who never does (the indicated thing)] : sterile : unable to conceive

*v.i.* **tóoika** 1 : to shoot oneself to death : to commit suicide by gunshot ⟨**Jónira tóoike.** The man shot himself to death.⟩ 2 : to make a sharp, loud, or piercing sound (e.g., a tree as it falls) ⟨**Jíwi bochikiax páketira tóorike.** As it fell, the tree made a sound.⟩ ⟨**Jónira károai tóoitai.** The man is making noise cutting wood.⟩ 3 : to have a sharp, penetrating sound or noise –*Used, e.g., regarding explosions, gunshots, or a small firecracker going off.* ⟨**Níi meranra tóoike.** There was a penetrating sound in the forest.⟩
See under **róno**
*v.i.* **tóota** : to become pregnant ⟨**Moa bénoa pekaora áinbo toóke.** Shortly after marrying, the woman became pregnant.⟩
See under **wáste**
*also* **tóota** *adj.* **tóoyanin** *also* **tóotanin** : pregnant ⟨**Nato aínbora sókota óxeya tóoya iki.** This woman has been pregnant for six months.⟩
*v.t.* **tópia** : to gather up or collect (e.g., fallen fruit) ⟨**Enra mánkoa tópiti iki.** I'm going to gather mangoes.⟩

*n.* **topón** [from Spanish] : mole ⟨**Tópora jáke jatíbiain. Ikáxbi Ajírikanko itan néke non maínres yámake. Ja topónra mái chíniai jawen mékena taén jaínoax jawen rekíman. Westíora yaméra mái kíniati átipanke ískon chónka mítoro, xéna bénakin.** The mole lives in every part of the world, except in Africa and here in Peru. With its front paws and its snout, it digs into the earth. In one night it can dig a tunnel of about ninety meters, searching for worms.⟩
*v.t.* **tópona** 1 : to count; *also* : to calculate ⟨**Bakénra topónti onánke.** The child knows how to count.⟩ 2 : to measure
*n.* **torán** : corvina (a freshwater drum fish) ⟨**Enra tóra kobin píai.** I'm eating corvina stew.⟩
See under **níshi**
*v.i.* **tórata** : to lose a small piece that flakes off (of pottery while it is being fired) ⟨**Titán chómo oíara toráke.** A small piece flaked off the clay jar that the mother was firing.⟩
*n.* **torístanin** [from Spanish] : tourist ⟨**Jóxo chópa kenéyara torísta aínbo kéenai.** A tourist woman wants white cloth with designs.⟩
*n.* **torón** [from Spanish] : bull ⟨**Tórora siná iki.** The bull is fierce.⟩ *syn.* wákabene
*n. and adj.* **tórokan** *n.* : circle : circumference *adj.* : having circular spots ⟨**Ja ríoparora toró torótani iki.** The leopard has spots all over its body.⟩

[from Shipibo *páro* river + *toró* circle] : water pooled in a deep part of a river ⟨**Párotoro chichóra roníman títa nérakake.** In the deep river pool there is a yacumama (a mythical water-boa) lurking.⟩

*v.t.* **toróaa** [from Shipibo *toró* circle + *-ati* to do] *Konibo* **toróaka** 1 : to make a circle on ⟨**Enra kámpo toróake maxén.** I made a circle on the field with achiote (annatto dye).⟩ 2 : to wind/coil; *also* : to make by winding ⟨**Titán toróaka mabánra, jawen babán ménonaanke.** The grandson burned the warp thread that his grandmother had wound.⟩ *syn.* néati
See under **masén**
*also* **trómpo** *n.* **torómponin** *also* **trómponin** [from Spanish] : spinning top ⟨**Bákebaonra torómpo o piróta mayáati iki.** The students are to roll a spinning top or a ball.⟩
*v.i.* **tórota** : to form a circle or ring (a group of people)
*v.i.* **tórotoroika** [from Shipibo *toro,* imitative of the sound + *-iti* to make] 1 : to purr (e.g., a cat or jaguar) 2 : to make a buzzing sound (e.g., a shushupe (a bushmaster snake))
See under **wínti**

*n.* **tóroxan** : "pez novia" (bride fish) : a species of fish similar to the suchi catfish, the bagre catfish, or the dolphin, whose meat is highly prized ⟨**Toróx kobinra noéira iki.** Stewed *toróx* fish is delicious.⟩
*n.* **toshán** : female of the parrot *tómi* ⟨**Tóshara apáshiron yakáke jíwi xamara íbirai ikax.** The little *tósha* parrot landed on a chameleon, thinking it was a twig.⟩
*v.t.* **tóshaa** *Konibo* **tóshaka** : to burst (something)
*v.t.* **toshbáaa** *Konibo* **toshbáaka** : to spit at ⟨**Bakénra jawen wétsa toshbáake tsínikin.** The child spat at his brother while playing.⟩
*modifying suf.* [from Shipibo; cf. *toshíti* to burst] : unexpectedly : suddenly ⟨**Jónibora shepótiain nokótoshikana iki.** The men arrived unexpectedly at the door.⟩
*v.i.* **tóshita** : to burst ⟨**Nokon nobéra moa toshíke.** My boil has already burst.⟩
*n.* **toshmón** : tushmo (a tree species); *also* : fruit of the tushmo ⟨**Enra tóshmo rérai jawen bími kókonoshon.** I am felling the tushmo tree to eat its fruit.⟩
*adj. and n.* **tóshmoman** *adj.* : about to burst –Used of a furuncle (boil). *n.* : swelling (e.g., from a blister)
*v.t.* **toshmón aa** *Konibo* **toshmón aka** : to inflate *syn.* ésteati
*v.t.* **tóshmona** : to form a swelling (e.g., from a blister) : to become inflated
*also* **tosóshoko** *n.* **tósokan** *also* **tosóshokon** [from Shipibo *tosóti, toso-* to drip + *-shoko,* diminutive suf.] : drop *syn.* shoró
*v.i.* **tósota** : to drip ⟨**Mishkínra nokon kotóman tosóke.** Honey dripped onto my shirt.⟩ *syn.* shoróti
*n.* **tótishan** : gramalote grass; *specif.* : alfalfa ⟨**Amemanra totísh píai.** The capybara eats gramalote grass.⟩
*adj. and n.* **tótokan** *adj.* : ripened : very ripe –Used, e.g., of mangoes and bananas. ⟨**Mánkoara totótotobires siki.** The mango is very ripe.⟩ *n.* : blemish on fruit
*n.* **tótokan** : a fish species similar to the súngaro (a catfish) but smaller ⟨**Cháchimis riki totó, íspia, ikax.** The *totó* fish, having a spine, is a fish that pricks you.⟩
*v.i.* **tótota** 1 : to ripen (e.g., a banana) until it turns yellow ⟨**Báwaparantara totóke.** The banana has already ripened to its yellow color.⟩ 2 : to be blemished
*n.* **tóxbakan** : blister ⟨**Nato jónira jawen yoránko toxbábo jokónke.** Blisters broke out on this man's hand. A this man broke out in blisters all over his body.⟩ *syn.* shomón
*v.i.* **tóxbata** 1 : to float ⟨**Wapórora toxbáibake nawékiain.** The boat was anchored in the bay.⟩ 2 : to form a blister
*n.* **tóxkaman** : cluster of matching fruits joined in a row or tied together –Rarely used nowadays.
See under **toxkóti**

*v.i.* **tóxkota** : to be erased : to be annulled : to be removed : to disappear ⟨**Báke ménotara benxoaxbi toá toxkóyamai.** Although the child who got burned has healed, his scar has not disappeared.⟩

*also* **toxkóti** [from Shipibo *toxkóti, toxkot-* to disappear + *pakéti* to fall] 1 : to lose color : to fade –Used of fabric. ⟨**Nokon chíarextira jawen siká toxkó páketai.** My pants are losing their color.⟩ ⟨**Nokon joshín kotónra pátsata toxkóke.** My red shirt that I had washed lost its color.⟩ 2 : to feel nausea pass ⟨**Kinánkasi íwanaxa, ea toxkópakeke.** I wanted to vomit, but I felt the nausea pass.⟩
*n.* **toxpín** : wart ⟨**Táepatonkoain tóxpiya íxonra en rókotoro tsékamake.** I had a wart on my ankle and asked the doctor to remove it.⟩
See **tarámpa**
See **rapíchi**
See **tíriko**
See **torómpo**
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *ts* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*v.i.* **tsáakaata** : to chip : to break –Used, e.g., of a plate or bowl that falls. ⟨**Rátora tsáakaake páketax.** The plate chipped when it fell.⟩ *syn.* TSAAKAATI, TSOSITI both can be translated as "to break"; but TSAAKAATI implies ceramic, TSOSITI implies glass breaking.
*v.t.* **tsán aka** [from Shipibo *tsan*, imitative + *áti* to make] : to ring/sound (e.g., a bell) ⟨**Báke yóitimanra páerin kampánan tsáan ake.** The disobedient boy rang the monk's bell.⟩

*v.t.* **tsáaa** *Konibo* **tsáaka** 1 : to chip : to break –Used, e.g., of a plate or bowl that falls. ⟨**Bakenra ráto tsáake.** The child broke the plate.⟩ 2 : to take (a banana) from a bunch ⟨**Enra páranta tsáake.** I took a banana from the bunch.⟩
*v.t.* **tsáaka** : to remove : to gather –Used with a plural-sense object. ⟨**Papánra paránta tsáake.** Dad is gathering bananas.⟩ *syn.* bichínti; bíti
*n.* **tsabén** : a woman's sister-in-law ⟨**Aínbora jawen tsábe betan károai káke.** The woman went with her sister-in-law to cut firewood.⟩

*v.t.* **tsaísaka** [from Shipibo *tsaís*, imitative of the sound + *áti*, *-ati* to make] : to make a cracking/snapping sound ⟨**Wái naponxonra inón jawen jína tsaísake.** The jaguar snapped its tail in the middle of the field.⟩
*n.* **tsaísatin** [from Shipibo *tsaísati*, *tsaís* a- to make a cracking sound + *-ti* instrument for] : a tree species whose crown has traditionally been known as the "hat of the Cashibo"

*v.i.* **tsaís ika** [from Shipibo *tsaís*, imitative + *-iti* to make] : to make a cracking sound when opening ⟨**Táma xakara barín aká tsaís ike.** The peanut shell cracked open because the sun had heated it.⟩

*v.t.* **tsáia** 1 : to influence someone's character or behavior; *specif.* : to pass on a bad habit to : to corrupt with a bad example ⟨**Miara jawen ikátonin tsáinake. Néri johúe.** He can pass his bad behavior on to you; come here.⟩ 2 : to stain with another color (one fabric onto another) when it fades in water ⟨**Nokon joshín kótomanra jóxo kotón tsáike.** My red shirt, as it faded, stained another shirt that was white.⟩ 3 : to give a specific taste or flavor to –Used, e.g., regarding sweetness or saltiness. –Used in the preterite form with present-tense meaning. ⟨**¿Moáki batán tsáia iki kají?** Is the coffee sweet yet?⟩
*v.i.* **tsákakaata** [from Shipibo *tsákati* to hit + *-kaa*, reflexive suf.] : to hit oneself ⟨**Eara máratichon tsákakaake.** I hit myself with the hammer.⟩
*n.* **tsákanani** : collision : accident ⟨**Jónibora tsamáke tsákanana óini.** People crowded together to see what had happened in the accident.⟩
*v.i.* **tsákanana** [from Shipibo *tsákati* to hit by throwing + *-anan* harming] : to have an accident

*v.t.* **tsákaa** *Konibo* **tsákaka** 1 : to sting : to wound ⟨**Enra yawísh tsákake pián.** I struck the armadillo with an arrow.⟩ 2 : to hit by throwing ⟨**Eara bakén isán beron tsákake.** The child hit me with an ungurahui (palm) seed.⟩ 3 : to fall onto : to throw oneself into ⟨**Rikánkinra jonín jéne tsákake.** Casting a net, the man threw himself into the water.⟩ ⟨**Jawen bobónki pirótanin tsákaara nato jonín máxkaxon mái tsákake.** This man fell to the ground fainting when the ball hit him in a spot that was infected.⟩ *syn.* TSAKATI, TSEWEATI both can be translated as "to wound," but TSAKATI refers more specifically to stinging (e.g., with an arrow), while TSEWEATI refers to cutting, specifically with the knife called ushate. *syn.* See under **tékati**

*n.* **tsámakan** : pile : gathering (of people) ⟨**jíwi metáx tsamá** piles of tree branches⟩ ⟨**Jóni tsamá ikáinoaxara nokon koríki yómetsokanke.** They stole my money over there where there is a crowd of people.⟩ *syn.* kóropo

*v.t.* **tsamáaka** 1 : to pile up : to gather together 2 : to divide –Used in the passive-participle form *tsamá aca* in division equations. –Used after the number of the divisor. ⟨**21 íketian, 3 tsamá aka páketai 7.** 21 divided by 3 equals 7.⟩ *syn.* tsamánti

*v.t.* **tsámana** [from Shipibo *tsamáti* to pile up + *-n*, verbalizing derivation suf.] 1 : to pile up : to gather together ⟨**Jonínra kabóri tsamánke jawen xóbo meran.** The man gathered taricayas (river turtles) in his house.⟩ 2 : to classify ⟨**Nonra tsamánti iki ja xóxoai píti.** We must classify the food plants.⟩

*v.i.* **tsámata** : to be piled up ⟨**Misánra kírika tsamáke.** There were books piled up on the table.⟩ ⟨**Jénetiaketian beaxa táxa mashín tsamaáke.** The logs of driftwood piled up on the riverbank after being carried there by the river's current.⟩
*n.* **tsánasan** : punchana (an animal species) ⟨**Ochítininra tsanás báke píke.** The dog ate the punchana's young.⟩

*v.t.* **tsánimaa** [from Shipibo *tsániti*, root *tsani-* to stretch + *-n*, verbalizing derivation suf.] : to make (someone) stretch ⟨**Nokon báke óxaketian rátexonra, en tsanímayonke.** I made my child stretch when I woke him from his sleep.⟩
*v.t.* **tsán ika** : to make a sound or noise (e.g., when stepping on dry branches or leaves) ⟨**Awára tsán ikiranai.** When the tapir comes, it makes noise stepping on the dry branches.⟩

*v.i.* **tsánita** 1 : to stretch (e.g., standing on tiptoe with arms raised) ⟨**Yamékiritibi oxá bésoax ea tsánitai.** Every morning when I wake up, I stretch my whole body.⟩ 2 : to do physical exercise : to do bodily exercises –Used in this sense with a subordinate clause of orientation (e.g., *íjirisisio akí* "doing exercise"). ⟨**Yamékiritibira kírika ákaibo íjirisisio akí tsaníkanai.** The students do exercises every morning.⟩
*v.i.* **tsánkata** : to rock : to wobble (e.g., a boat or canoe) ⟨**Béchoman akára bóti tsánkatai.** The boat rocks when there are waves.⟩
*n.* tsanón : a small species of shell
*n.* tsánokan : a fish species similar to the turushuque (a fish) that lives in rivers ⟨**Enra tsanó míshkikin bíke.** I caught a *tsanó* fish with a hook.⟩ *syn.* See under **nóchopoko**
*v.t.* tsáona [from Shipibo *tsáoti* to squat + -n, verbalizing derivation suf.] : to make (someone) squat ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen báke tsaónke.** The woman made her child squat.⟩
*n.* tsáorinin : saurín (a fish species) ⟨**Enra tsáori tóoake.** I shot a saurín fish.⟩
[from Shipibo *nii* forest + *tsáori* saurín] : a species of saurín
*v.i.* tsáota : to squat ⟨**Márira nokon papán wái napo tsáoke.** The agouti is sitting squatted in the middle of my father's field.⟩

*v.t.* tsásiaka : to stop (an object in motion) ⟨**Nokon wetsánra báikan nónti béai tsásiake.** My brother stopped the canoe that the current had brought.⟩ *syn.* TSASIATI, TSASIMATI, YATANTI can all be translated as "to stop"; but TSASIATI implies an intercepted object, TSASIMATI refers to braking the movement of, e.g., a horse; and YATANTI indicates the detention of an arrested person.

*v.t.* tsásimaa *Konibo* tsásiaka [from Shipibo *tsásiti, tsasi* to stop + -ma, causative] : to stop : to make stop : to brake ⟨**Kabáyora tsásimake, íshto káaibi.** While the horse was passing by quickly, he stopped it.⟩

*v.i.* tsásia : to stop ⟨**Páro naponra bóti tsásike.** In the middle of the river the boat stopped.⟩ ⟨**Parón ináinakinra non oínke manánxawe toxbápake**tai. Jaínoax noa tsásike ja bíi. When we were traveling upriver, we saw a tortoise that was floating. Then we stopped to pick it up.⟩
*n.* tsatsán : fish –Used mostly among the Shetebo. *syn.* See under **wáka**

*n.* tsátsitaxon [from Shipibo *tsá* sound of bursting + *tsi,* sound + *táxo* handle of an instrument] : spear ⟨**Non pápara wanín tsátsitaxoya iki.** My dad has a spear made from pijuayo (palm) wood.⟩
*n.* **tsawín** : a fish species similar to the sardine but a meter long, that feeds by devouring other fish small ⟨**Tsawínra sipán píai.** The *tsáwi* fish eats the *sipán* sardine.⟩
*also* **káyatsawi** [from Shipibo *kayán* + *tsáwi*] : a fish species with bright yellowish scales, and large eyes and mouth
*v.t.* tsékana [from Shipibo *tsékati* to harvest + -n, verbal suf.] : to cut making an incision *syn.* See under **rérati**

*v.t.* tsékaa 1 : to harvest (e.g., wheat or rice) ⟨**Nokon papánra arós tsékai.** My dad is harvesting rice.⟩ 2 : to take out ⟨**Nokon wetsánra ea yóike ráta manón mílmeeta tsékati.** My brother told me to take the can that had sunk in the mud out.⟩ *syn.* pakémati

*v.i.* tséketa : to come out : to come off; *specif.* : to be pulled out ⟨**Manánxawera jawen náinoax tsékeke.** The tortoise's came out of its nest.⟩ ⟨**Nokon xétara tsekéke.** My tooth came out.⟩ ⟨**Nonón péira tsekéke.** The duck's feather came out.⟩
See under ísa

*n.* tsehuecan : wound : cut; *specif.* : a wound or cut made by an ushate (a type of knife) ⟨**Ránkora tsewé íchaya iki jawen mapónko, jawen mérati kopí ákana.** Franco had many wounds on his head, which had been made with the ushate over his girlfriends.⟩ *syn.* bishkó

*v.t.* tséwea : to wound; *specif.* : to ushate (cut with an ushate knife) ⟨**Aníxeatininxonra jonín jawen chál tsewéake.** During the *ánixeati* festival, the man slashed his brother-in-law with an ushate knife.⟩ *syn.* See under **tsákati**

*v.i.* tséweta 1 : to be wounded; *specif.* : to be ushateado (cut with an ushate knife) ⟨**Jónira jawen ráwikan tsewéake.** A man was slashed with an ushate knife by his enemy.⟩ 2 : to cut oneself (e.g., with glass) ⟨**Páena jónira tsewéke botirian.** The drunk man cut himself with the bottle.⟩
*modifying pref.* : on the rear parts ⟨**tsískiti** to paint on the rear parts⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1
*modifying suf.* –Used added to a name with the sense of *-ito* or *-cito*, marking a diminutive of affection or friendship. ⟨**Nímatsi, néri jowé.** Little Nima, come here.⟩ *syn.* -shoko
*modal suf.* –Used added to the first constituent of an interrogative sentence. ⟨**¿Jabotsi benówankana níi meran?** Is it true that they got lost in the forest?⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.2
*n.* **tsikéspoton** : an insect species similar to a beetle, found on the riverbank

*n. and adj.* **tsímesan** [from Shipibo *tsi-* on the rear parts + *mes*; cf. *mesó* portion] *n.* : residue : what is left over ⟨**kaji tsimes** coffee residue⟩ *adj.* : pretty in the rear; *specif.* : having pretty buttocks
*v.t.* **tsínamaa** : to deflate ⟨**Báke ésteara rókotoron chínoxon tsínamake.** The doctor gave the child, who had a swollen belly, an enema to bring the swelling down.⟩
*v.i.* **tsínaa** : to deflate : to go down (swelling) ⟨**Nobéra tsínake.** The boil went down.⟩
*n.* **tsíniaitonin** : player ⟨**piróta tsíniai** soccer player⟩
*n.* **tsíniainbon** *Konibo* **tsíniainbaon** *pish.* **tsíniainbaen** : harlot : prostitute : whore ⟨**Tsíniainboronki ishtón bénoyamai.** They say prostitutes cannot marry quickly.⟩

*v.t.* **tsíniaa** : to drive crazy : to make (someone) go crazy ⟨**Jonínra jawen awínwetsa** **wastén tsíniake.** A man drove his sister-in-law crazy by giving her piripiri (a medicinal plant) to drink.⟩

*v.i.* **tsínikaata** : to be wrung out (e.g., clothing) ⟨**Enra Yarínain oínyantanke chópa patsáti mákina, chópabo tsínikaaketian, janbíx jénetai.** In Yarina I saw the washing machines turn off by themselves after wringing out the clothes.⟩
*v.i.* **tsínia** 1 : to play ⟨**Tomínko neténra noa tsínike pirótanin.** On Sunday we played ball.⟩ 2 : to go crazy (of a woman)
*v.t.* **tsínia** : to wring out (e.g., clothing) ⟨**Titánra máyaanan chópa tsínike.** The mother wrung out the clothes by twisting them.⟩

*v.t.* **tsínkia** : to gather : to collect ⟨**Rimán kánoxonra náto báritia en koríki tsínkike.** This year I saved up money to go to Lima.⟩ ⟨**Káritira bénxoanoxonra, károbaon máxi tsínkiai.** They are gathering sand in the trucks to fix the road.⟩
*v.i.* **tsínkita** : to gather together : to congregate ⟨**Jónibora tsinkíke Diosen Joi nínkati.** The people gathered to listen to the Word of God.⟩
*n.* **tsínkítinin** : meeting
*n.* **tsínokan** : a small bird species similar to the paucar (an oropendola/cacique bird)
*n.* **tsíoman** : cicada ⟨**Káchio kakínra, en tsíón kéotai ninkáke.** As I was walking through the forest, I heard a cicada shrieking.⟩ [illustration: *tsíón*]
See under róno
*n.* **tsípaman** : a type of river sardine, of several species, prized as food and served fried ⟨**Tsipán xéera en píai.** I am eating fried sardine.⟩
*n.* **tsípisan** [from Shipibo *tsi-* on the rear parts + *pisi* stinky] : fart
*v.i.* **tsípisa** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *písiti* to become stinky] : to expel intestinal gas : to fart
*n.* **tsirín** : a tiny, multicolored bird species ⟨**Tsíri isára kéotai.** The little *tsíri* bird sings.⟩

*adj.* **tsirín** : pretty : beautiful : lovely –Used as a term of affection or praise (e.g., for a child), especially in a song. ⟨**Tsíri bakéra, Nokon tsíri bakéra** Oh lovely little son, Oh my lovely little son⟩ *syn. See under jakónshoko*
See under **ísa**
*v.i.* **tsíria** : to become pretty –Used especially of a woman. ⟨**Náto aínbora ráotax tsírike.** This woman has made herself pretty by adorning herself.⟩
*n.* **tsisán** : blemishes on the body; *specif.* : freckles ⟨**Náto bákera, tsísaya ikáxa, jakóma iki.** This child is ugly because he has freckles.⟩
*v.i.* **tsísaa** : to develop blemishes or become spotted (e.g., a plant affected by a worm) ⟨**Károra tsísake.** The sweet potato has become blemished.⟩
See under **bóna**

*n.* **tsíseneman** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *senén* entirely] : the rear end (e.g., of a boat or canoe); *specif.* : stern ⟨**Tsísenenain játixonbi yatánkanwe.** Everyone pull from the stern.⟩ *syn. wapóropoinki*

*v.t.* **tsískia** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *síkati* to paint] : to paint on the tail or on the private/rear parts of ⟨**Nato aínbobakera jawen titán tsískike.** This girl's mother painted her groin.⟩
*n.* **tsískokan** : slope : descent ⟨**Tsiskó ikáinra báke pakéke.** The child fell on the slope.⟩
*v.t.* **tsískoa** : to drink (a beverage) completely ⟨**Náto jonínra westíora tasón bócho xéakin tsískoke.** That man drank a whole bowl of the drink, all of it.⟩

*v.i.* **tsískota** 1 : to be wasted by tipping over or spilling : to spill ⟨**Titán beténra tsiskóke.** The porridge the mother had made spilled.⟩ 2 : to lean improperly to one side : to tilt ⟨**Nokon papán xóbora niwén aká wétsakiri tsiskóke.** My father's house tilted because of a strong wind.⟩
*n.* **tsísmaman** : fasaco (a fish) : puñuisiqui ⟨**Tsísmamanra ea natéxke.** A fasaco bit me.⟩ ⟨**Tsísmaman yóra riki kikínbires sibá.** The fasaco's body is very slippery.⟩
*n.* **tsísokan** : a small animal species similar to a mouse
*n.* **tsísoikitinin** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *sóikiti* to rub oneself] : toilet paper

*v.i.* **tsísoa** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *sóati* to rub] : to clean the feces off (e.g., a baby) ⟨**Bákera jawen titán tsísoai poíketian.** The mother cleans her baby after it defecates.⟩

*adj.* **tsispán** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *shépa* skinny] : having skinny or thin buttocks ⟨**¡Oínwe aínbo oshíshoko tsíspa!** Look at that woman, so thin she barely has any buttocks!⟩
*n.* **tsíspiman** : stinger of a wasp or other insect ⟨**Pápa binán tékara tsíspín banéke.** A wasp stung dad and left its stinger.⟩
*v.i.* **tsíspota** : to close up (e.g., a lizard) a hole with dirt ⟨**Xábo ochítinin chíbana káaxa tsíspota iki.** The lizard was chased by the dog and closed up its hole with dirt.⟩
*n.* **tsistén** : charcoal ⟨**Tsístera en bóai jan wíshanoxon.** I'm carrying charcoal to paint with.⟩

*v.t.* **tsístina** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *stin*, unidentified element + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] : to lift the tail or buttock of ⟨**Rókotoronra jóni tsistínke, jawen chíxo páyota íketian, ráonoxon.** The doctor lifted the man's buttock to treat his wound.⟩

*v.i.* **tsístita** [from Shipibo *tsi–* on the rear parts + *sti*, unidentified element + *–ti*, infinitive suf.] : to bend down : *also* : to put (e.g., jokingly) one's buttocks in a raised position
*n.* **tsístokan** : burning coal/ember ⟨**Jawen titán kóiranyamaara náto bakén tsistó yatánke.** This child grabbed the burning coal because his mother wasn't watching him.⟩
See under **máni**
See under **níshi**

*n.* **tsítsimitsan** [from Shipibo *tsítsiti*, *tsitsi–* to suck + *mitsa*, unidentified element] : canero (a small parasitic catfish) ⟨**Jéne beáitianra tsítsimitsa onsá íki.** During flood season, caneros are dangerous.⟩

*v.t.* **tsítsia** 1 : to suck hard ⟨**Xáwira en tsítsiai jawen jéne.** I am sucking the juice from the sugarcane.⟩ 2 : to get (something) stuck fast (e.g., sticky mud) ⟨**Jónira manón tsítsike.** The mud got the man stuck fast.⟩
*v.i.* **tsítsita** : to get stuck ⟨**Nokon bótira tsitsíke tapán xaran.** My boat got stuck among the rafts.⟩

*n.* **tsítsoman** : curve; *specif.* : one of a series of curves in a river ⟨**Paro riki ícha tsitsónyares.** The Ucayali River has many curves.⟩ ⟨**Shípibo aínbaon kené riki tsitsón áni.** The curves in a Shipibo woman's design are large.⟩ *syn.* See under **mayá**
*v.t.* **tsíwaa** : to lay an egg ⟨**Nato báritianra ícha kabórinin tsíwake.** This summer many taricayas (river turtles) laid eggs.⟩

*pron.* **tson** 1 : who? : to whom? –Used as an interrogative word in the sentence. –Used in the contracted form *tso–* before a postposition or postpositional suffix. ⟨**¿Tsóarin óa?** Who is that?⟩ ⟨**¿Tsóaki ráma non jemán kóshi jíkimati íki?** Whom shall we name as chief of the town?⟩ ⟨**¿Tsoibaki ícha árosan márokanai?** In whose shop is a lot of rice sold?⟩ 2 : someone –Used in the sentence with *–ma* or *–yama* "not" with the sense of "no one." ⟨**Moa yamé pochinikonra, tsóa níai non oínyamai.** At midnight we no longer see anyone walking around.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.2.2
*pron.* **tsónbi** [from Shipibo *tsóa* who + *–bi* even though] : nobody ⟨**Tsóabi jemán kóshi ikáshamaitianra, ea íkai.** If nobody wants to be chief of the town, I will be.⟩
See under **yáma**
*v.t.* **tsóaka** : to make a noise with the mouth (e.g., a kiss or a whistle) ⟨**Noara tsóike metsá aínbo oínax.** We were the ones who whistled when we saw the pretty woman.⟩
*n.* **tsoáwanin** : a bird species
*v.t.* **tsoís ika** : to have a sharp pain : to hurt badly ⟨**Nokon xetánra ea tsoís ake.** My tooth hurts badly.⟩
*v.i.* **tsoís ika** : to feel a sharp pain

*adj.* **tsókasan** [from Shipibo; root of *tsokásti* to feel uncomfortable] : uncomfortable : annoyed ⟨**Rabé néte náshiama ikáxa ea tsokás íki.** I feel uncomfortable because it's been two days since I bathed.⟩

*v.i.* **tsókasa** [from Shipibo *tso–*, unidentified element (cf. *mátson* to rub one's head) + *–kas* to want + *–ti* infinitive suf.] : to feel (oneself) annoyed or uncomfortable –Used in the sentence with *shinán* "in the mind." ⟨**Eara shinán tsókasai bákebo íchaira tsínikanaitian.** I feel annoyed when the children play too much.⟩

*v.t.* **tsómaa** 1 : to grab : to take in one's hand ⟨**Enra báke tsómake.** I grabbed the child.⟩ 2 : to hold in one's hand ⟨**Náto bakénra átapa báchi tsómake.** This child held the hen's egg in his hand.⟩ *syn.* **yatánti**
*adj.* : whose ⟨**¿Tson bákerin náto?** Whose son is this?⟩
*n.* **tsonkíronin** : kingfisher ⟨**Tsonkíroninra yápa bíke.** The kingfisher took the fish.⟩
*n.* **tsóntsoronin** : yulilla (a small fish) ⟨**Tsóntsorora páenai íaman.** The yulillas are getting dizzy in the oxbow lake.⟩
[from Shipibo *jína* tail + *joshín* reddish + *tsóntsoro* yulilla] : a species of yulilla with reddish fins on its tail that is not fit to eat
*n.* **tsosán** : a grayish-brown bird species that sings ⟨**Tsosán náa ríki mái aká.** The nest of the *tsósa* bird is made of mud.⟩
*adj. and n.* **tsósakan** *adj.* : broken : shattered *n.* : chipped piece ⟨**Bídirio tsósakanra nokon táe en xáteke.** A piece of glass cut my foot.⟩
*n.* **tsosáshokon** [from Shipibo *tsosá* chipped piece + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : crumb ⟨**métinina píti tsosáshokobo** crumbs fallen from the hand⟩
*v.t.* **tsósaa** : to break into small pieces : to smash to bits
*n.* **tsósikan** : the main part left over from a broken container

*n.* **tsósiman** : decrease (in water level) ⟨**Jéne tsosín ikénbira, nokon papán konxán xáteke.** Even though the water level had dropped and there wasn't enough water for transport, my dad cut the wood into pieces.⟩
*v.i.* **tsósina** : to decrease : to be at low water or dried up ⟨**Báritia íketianra ían tsosín iki.** Since it's summer, the oxbow lake is at low water.⟩
*v.i.* **tsósita** : to break (e.g., a bowl) partially ⟨**Nokon básora tsósita iki.** My glass has broken a little.⟩ *syn.* See under tsáakaati
*n.* : name of the letter *hu* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*also* **wáatatita** *n.* **wáatanin** *also* **wáatatitan** : maternal aunt; *also* : the father's non-maternal wife or sister-in-law -The vocative form *titá* following the personal name is used to address the person indicated. ⟨**Jowé, Meatitá.** Good morning, aunt Méa.⟩ ⟨**Nokon wáatan benénra westíora sapén réteke.** My aunt's husband killed a sea cow (manatee).⟩ *syn.* WAATA, NACHI, YAYA can all be translated as "aunt"; while WAATA denotes the aunt on the mother's side, NACHI and YAYA mean the aunt on the father's side. NACHI is the term used by a nephew for the paternal aunt; and YAYA, by a niece.
See **wáata**

*v.i.* **wáata** : to cook (become cooked) ⟨**Benkéx wáanon íxon bóe rábea iki.** She turned the boquichico (a fish) over so it would cook on the other side.⟩ ⟨**Moa átapa wáakenbira kochín piánke.** She had cooked the hen, but the pig ate it.⟩
*adj.* **wachón** : soft ⟨**Bakísha nato paránta wáchoyora íibake; ráma moa páyota iki.** Yesterday this plantain was very soft, and today it is already rotten.⟩ *syn.* **báka**
*v.t.* **wáchoaa** *Konibo* **wáchoaka** : to make soft : to soften ⟨**Chorísh ikénbira, kobínhaxon poróto titán wáchoake.** Even though the beans were hard, mom softened them by cooking them.⟩
[from Shipibo *yóra* body + *wáchoati* to soften] : to exercise *syn.* **bákaati**
*n.* **waín** : garden plot (chacra) ⟨**Wái napomeara kokán awá réteke.** My maternal uncle killed a tapir in the middle of the garden plot.⟩
*v.t.* **wáiaa** *Konibo* **wái aka** : to make a garden plot ⟨**En wáiakenbira jatíribibaon áyamake.** Although I made a garden plot, the others did not make theirs.⟩
*n.* **waín téetaitonin** [from Shipibo *wái*, *waín* garden plot + *téetai*, participle of *téeti*, to work] : farmer : garden-plot worker
*n.* **wáiraontinin** [from Shipibo *wái* garden plot + *ráonti* remedy] : fertilizer; *specif.* : guano

*n.* **wáiroron** [from Quechua *wayruru* huaíruro] : huairuro (a red-and-black seed) : civil guard —Used rarely nowadays. ⟨**Moátianronki wáiroroboki joshín sáwetiabo ikátikanai.** They say that in the old days the guards wore red uniforms.⟩
*n.* **wáitinin** : a species of caterpillar that builds its nest from cocoons made of spiderweb and dry twigs
[from Shipibo *kabóri* taricaya (a river turtle) + *wáiti* a species of caterpillar] : a species of cocoon used to tame the taricaya
[from Shipibo *wáme* paiche + *wáiti* a species of caterpillar] : a species of cocoon used to tame the paiche
[from Shipibo *íso* spider monkey + *wáiti* a species of caterpillar] : a species of cocoon used to attract spider monkeys
[from Shipibo *jasín* paujil (curassow) + *wáiti* a species of caterpillar] : a species of cocoon used to tame the paujil
[from Shipibo *sapén* vaca marina (manatee) + *wáiti* a species of caterpillar] : a species of cocoon used to tame the manatee
[from Shipibo *xáwe* charapa (river turtle) + *wáiti* a species of caterpillar] : a species of cocoon used to tame the charapa
*n.* **wáiwantin** : a species of cane used to make the *réwe* flute

*n.* **wakán** -Used mostly among speakers of Shetebo. : fish ⟨**Jónironki wáka áxani káa iki.** They tell that a man went to poison the fish with barbasco (a fish-poison plant).⟩ *syn.* WAKA, JAWEKI, TSATSA, YAPA can all be translated as "fish" with no difference at all; but YAPA is the word in general use while WAKA and TSATSA are practically Shetebo synonyms. JAWEKI is a word that can denote "fish" as well as "animal", "bird" or "tree" among living beings.
*n.* **wakán** [from Quechua *waka*; and this from Spanish] : cow ⟨**Wakán kópia bákeronki keyón bóai.** They say the baby cutipado (afflicted by an animal spirit) by the cow drools a lot.⟩
*n.* **wákabaken** [from Spanish *vaka* + Ship. *báke* offspring] : calf
*n.* **wákabenen** [from Shipibo *wáka* cow + *béne* male] : bull ⟨**Non chikéaabira wákabenen rásake.** The bull knocked down the fence we put up.⟩ *syn.* tóro
*n.* **wákanawan** [from Old Shipibo *wáka* fish + *náwa* wild native] : mijanada (a fish run) ⟨**Ronónewa wákanawaronki chipónki béai.** They say a mijanada (school) of boas is coming downriver.⟩
See under **bína**

*n.* **wakán ewan** [from Shipibo *wáka, wakán* fish + *-ewa*, augmentative] : saltón (a large migratory catfish) ⟨**Wakán ewan báke kópiaronki ésteai.** They say that when the saltón cutipa (afflicts spiritually) a baby, its little belly swells.⟩ *syn.* naítsaka
*n.* **wakáponin** : huacapú (a hardwood tree) ⟨**Non wákapo xóbo iníchintiaara kóshi iki.** If we use wakapú wood to build the house posts, they will be strong.⟩
See **ronín**
*n.* **wákaxoman** : cow's milk

*v.t.* **wákea** : to lift : to make higher ⟨**Jánbicho wáketi átipanyamaketianra en akínke.** When he could not lift it by himself, I helped him carry it.⟩ ⟨**Moa tápo waké iketianra jenén mápoyamake.** The emponado (a raised platform) was not covered by the flood because it was higher up.⟩

*v.i.* **wáketa** : to get up, to rise ⟨**Maín rákataxa báke janbíx wakéke.** The child got up from the ground by himself.⟩ *syn.* WAKETI, NINATI both mean "to get up", but with different reference. Thus WAKETI is used about fallen or inert bodies that rise or are raised, while NINATI denotes the action of a person who is not standing getting to their feet in order to walk.
See under **ísa**
*n.* **wakín** : a kind of tree with thorny bark ⟨**Nato kampánra wákixena píke.** This *campa* (an Asháninka person) ate the *suris* (edible palm grubs) of the *wáki* tree.⟩
See under **móxa**
*n.* **Wákiman** [from Spanish *Joakín*] –Used as a male name.
*n.* **wakón** : a species of tree frog
[from Shipibo *kabóri* taricaya (a river turtle) + *wáko* a species of frog] : a species of frog
[from Shipibo *wáme* paiche (a large fish) + *wáko* a species of frog] : a species of frog
[from Shipibo *ino* jaguar + *wáko* frog] : a species of frog
[from Shipibo *manxár* heron + *wáko* a species of frog] : a small species of frog
[from Shipibo *sapén* sea cow (manatee) + *wáko* a species of frog] : a species of frog
*n.* **wakón** : a species of bat
[from Shipibo *íso* spider monkey + *wáko* a species of frog] : a species of bat that screeches like the spider monkey and that, according to some reports, secretes a liquid while hanging in a tree
*n.* **wamén** : paiche ⟨**Wáme rétekanonronki poínkosko jemán níai.** They say the sign that someone is going to kill a paiche is when a vulture walks around the yard.⟩
: a ghost paiche that appears with flames of fire
[from Shipibo *jósho* white + *wáme* paiche] : a species of paiche
[from Shipibo *máxe* achiote + *wáme* paiche] : a species of paiche the color of achiote

[from Shipibo *táko*, *takón* unchala + *wáme* paiche] : a kind of small fish resembling the shuyo but smaller ⟨**Takónwame piáxa nato báke jími chíxotai.** This child has bloody diarrhea from eating *takónwame*.⟩

*n.* **wámeberon** [from Shipibo *wáme* paiche + *béro* eye] : a kind of climbing plant with an edible, sour fruit resembling the eye of the paiche in shape and size ⟨**Iaman kaxónra wámebero bimi bakén kókoke.** The child went to the cocha (an oxbow lake) and ate the fruit of the *wámebero* plant.⟩
See under **níshi**
See under **wáiti**
See under **wáko**

*modifying suf.* : a while ago : recently : during the present day –Used added to the verb. ⟨**Títara paránta bénai kawánke, nokon wétsa betan.** Mama has just gone to look for plantains with my brother.⟩ ⟨**Yamékirira pápashoko jowánke téemanoxon jónibo bénai.** This morning grandpa came looking for men for the work.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
*n.* **wanánan** [from Quechua *wanana*] : a kind of small wild duck

*n.* **wániman** 1 : pijuayo (a peach palm) : chonta (palm heart) 2 : fruit of the pijuayo ⟨**Oa pápashokora wanínxeatinin paénke.** That grandpa got drunk on masato (a fermented drink) made from pijuayo.⟩
[from Shipibo *áni* big + *wanin* fruit of the pijuayo] : a kind of pijuayo
See under **ráo**

*also* **wanínxeni** *n.* **wanínxenianin** *also* **wanínxenin** [from Shipibo *wanín* pijuayo + *xéni* fat + *-ya* having] : suisuy (a kind of bird) ⟨**Wétsa jiwínbires ayamakinra, wanínxenianin wánimanres náa ákai.** The suisuy does not build its nest in just any tree; it only makes it in the pijuayo.⟩

*n.* **wanón** [from Old Shipibo *wano* woman] : very tiny : leftover, second-rate : the smallest of all –Used in a phrase with *jahuen* "its". ⟨**Ea binón ménikinbira jawen wánobichores ea ménike.** He gave me aguajes (a palm fruit), but only the tiny ones.⟩
*n.* **Wanón** –Used as a female name.

*v.t.* **wánomaata** [from Shipibo *wáno* smallest (formerly, woman) + *mawáti* to die] : to become widowed ⟨**Nato jónira moa chóskoi wánomaake.** This man has been widowed four times.⟩ ⟨**Wánomaata jónira wánokasai.** The widower wants to marry.⟩

*adj.* **wánooman** *Konibo* **wánoomatonin** [from Shipibo *wáno* smallest (formerly, woman) + *-homa* without] : unmarried, single ⟨**Wánooma iketianra koáratianin bóke.** The guard took him away because he was single.⟩
*v.i.* **wánoa** : to marry (of a man) ⟨**Nato oxénbira moa wánoke.** He got married this very month.⟩
*n.* **wánotinin** [from Shipibo *wánoti*, *wano* to marry + *-ti* with what] : wedding : marriage : matrimony

*adj.* **wánoyan** *Konibo* **wánoyanin** *also* **wánoyaton** [from Shipibo *wáno* smallest (formerly, woman) + *-ya* having] : married –Used about a man. ⟨**Moa wánoya ikáxbira jawen awínhoma jóke.** He came without his wife, even though he is married.⟩

*n.* **wantán** [from Old Shipibo *wanota*] : potential wife –Rarely used nowadays. ⟨**Rámatianra jawen wántanbi awínyakin bíkanai.** These days, men marry women who are not the right match for them.⟩

*v.t.* **wáoaka** [from Shipibo *wao*, imitative of the shout + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] 1 : to speak loudly to : to shout at ⟨**Pábe íketianra wáoake; játianra ninkáke.** Since he was deaf, she spoke to him in a loud voice and that way he understood.⟩ 2 : to scold ⟨**Min ea wáoakara** ea sinátl iqui. If you scold me, I will get angry.⟩ *syn.* notsínti
*v.i.* **wáoika** : to speak loudly : to make noise talking ⟨**Mia wáoikaitianra en ochóxonbi ninkáke.** When you spoke loudly, I heard you from far away.⟩

*n.* **wapán** [from Shipibo *wápa*, imitative of its call] : a kind of bird resembling the owl ⟨**Wápa kini meranronki wíso ino jáke.** They say the yanapumas (black jaguars) live in the cave of the *wápa* birds.⟩
See under **bína**
*n.* **wápawapan** : espátula (roseate spoonbill) : huapapa ⟨**Papánra wápawapa pei máitiai, mároti.** Papa makes a feather crown from huapapa feathers to sell.⟩
See under **bóo**

*n.* **wapín** : a kind of flat-bodied aquatic toad that sometimes burrows into the mud ⟨**Wapín báke kópiaronki pánshinai.** They say that when the *wápi* toad cutipas (casts a harmful spell on) a baby, the baby turns yellow.⟩ ⟨**Wapín báke kópiaronki jími chíxotai.** They say that when the *wápi* toad cutipas a child, it causes bloody diarrhea.⟩

*n.* **wapínkenaman** [from Shipibo *wápi, wapín* a kind of toad + *kenán* bench] : renaco (a kind of fig tree) ⟨**Wapínkenaman ikára epán íso tonbo méraxon rabé réteke.** My paternal uncle found a troop of maquisapas (spider monkeys) in the renaco and killed two.⟩

*n.* **wapóronin** [from Quechua *wapuru*, itself from Spanish] 1 : steamboat ⟨**Oínyosma ikáxa wapóro óinax nato báke ráketai.** This child had never seen a steamboat and was afraid when he saw it.⟩ 2 : launch, boat ⟨**Ikítoainra kaíbake, wapóronin.** Yesterday he went to Iquitos by launch.⟩ 3 : motor vessel ⟨**Máioshiain ténamanra wapóro jíkike.** A motor vessel sank at the port of Pucallpa.⟩ *syn.* ánimotoro (motóro)
[from Shipibo *mái* land + *wapóro* steamboat] : train ⟨**Ikítoainra máiwaporo jakátiai.** There is no train in Iquitos.⟩
[from Shipibo *naí* sky + *wapóro* steamboat] : airplane ⟨**Naíwaporo jóaitian jabáyamakanwe.** When the airplane comes, please do not flee.⟩ *syn.* ábion

*n.* [from Shipibo *wapóro* steamboat + *-máxka* upper part] : *bridge of a steamboat* ⟨**Wapóromaxkatemeáxonki komántanti pakéke jenénko.** They say that a commander fell from the bridge of the steamboat into the water.⟩

*n.* **wapóropoinkinin** [from Shipibo *wapóro* steamboat + *póinki* anus] : stern of a steamboat, launch, or motor vessel ⟨**Nokon nóntira wapóropoinki naman jíkike.** My canoe went in under the stern of the launch.⟩ *syn.* tsísenen

*n.* **wárakenin** [from Shipibo *wara,* unidentified element + *kéni* beard] : a kind of tree used for house frames ⟨**Wárakenira xóbo kánoaa bási íkai.** The house frame made from the wood of the *wárakeni* tree lasts a long time.⟩
*n.* **wáraman** : squash, pumpkin ⟨**Bákera warán joa xanán menóke.** The child burned himself on the hot boiled squash.⟩ ⟨**Nonra warán xeatiai.** We make chicha (a fermented drink) from squash.⟩
[from Shipibo *masén* huingo + *warán* squash] : a kind of squash shaped like a huingo (a gourd)
[from Shipibo *nenké* long + *warán* squash] : zucchini : a kind of elongated squash
[from Shipibo *yaká* sitting + *warán* squash] : a kind of squash
*adj.* **waránkan** *Konibo* **waránkanin** [from Quechua *waranka*] : thousand ⟨**Nokon papánra píchika pácha waránka sóro ribínke.** My father owes fifty thousand soles.⟩

*n.* **warápon** *Konibo* **waráponin** [from Quechua *warapu*] : guarapo (a fermented sugarcane drink) ⟨**Waráponin páe-** naxa aínbobo báchinananke.** The women fought pulling each other's hair when they got drunk on guarapo.⟩ *syn.* bínti
*n.* **wárawaskon** [from Quechua *warwasku*; itself from Spanish] : barbasco (a fish-poison plant) ⟨**Sináxon wárawasko xéaaxa jóni mawáke.** A man, full of rage, drank barbasco and died.⟩
[from Shipibo *niá* standing + *wárawasko* barbasco] : a kind of tree from which ordinary barbasco is obtained
[from Shipibo *níshi* vine + *wárawasko* barbasco] : a kind of vine
*n.* **warín** : a kind of small ash-colored heron
[from Shipibo *chóma* clouds + *wári* a kind of heron] : a kind of small heron
*n.* **warókanin** : tipití (a woven tube for squeezing manioc) ⟨**Papánra warókanin axón átsa xáki pótsiai.** Papa squeezes the grated manioc by putting it in the tipití.⟩

*adj.* **wároman** : drunk –Used in poetic form. ⟨**Amaabira je, min ámaabira, je, warón rakáyamai, je. Eara rakáyamai, je.** Although I take to drinking, although I drink for you, drunk I do not lie down. I do not lie down.⟩
*n.* **waróronin** [from Spanish *farol*] : lantern : flashlight ⟨**Jawen pátoroninra pápa waróro ménike.** The boss gave papa a lantern.⟩ *syn.* intírinan

*n.* **wasán** : frailecito monkey (a small monkey) ⟨**Westíora wása tonbo oínxonbira en réteyamake tóoatioma íxon.** I found a troop of frailecito monkeys, but I did not kill them because I had no shotgun.⟩
[from Shipibo *kaíati, kaí–* to grow up (young animal) + *wása* frailecito monkey] : a kind of small frailecito monkey
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *wása* frailecito monkey] : a kind of frailecito monkey
[from Shipibo *mapó* clay + *wása* frailecito monkey] : a kind of frailecito monkey

[from Shipibo *wása* frailecito monkey + *báke* young + *pápiti, pápia* to carry] : a constellation called "The One Who Carries Baby Frailecito Monkeys on His Back," made up of stars in pairs within a circular area, located in the Prow of Argo Navis
See under **bína**
See under **íno**

*v.i.* **wásameeta** : to brush dust or other dirt off oneself ⟨**Ino jóaitianronki jóni máshi meran míimeenike; játian moa káa pekao máshi wásameeta iki.** Long ago, a man buried himself in the sand of the beach when he saw a jaguar; when the jaguar had gone, the man brushed the sand off his body.⟩
*n.* **Wásananton** [from Spanish *Fasanando*] –Used as a male name.
See under **níbo**

*Konibo* **wásati** *v.t.* **wásana** *Konibo* **wásaa** 1 : to remove (dust or other dirt) ⟨**Titánra jawen chitóntinin ika máipoto wásake.** Mama brushed the dust off her pampanilla (loincloth).⟩ 2 : to sweep ⟨**Nato matsótinin tápo wásawe.** Sweep the emponado (palm-slat floor) with this broom.⟩ 3 : to scatter : to spread out (a pile) ⟨**Nato bakénra en kaímito tsamana ea wásanaanke.** This child scattered the caimitos I had piled up.⟩

*n.* **wasányakatinin** [from Shipibo *wása, wasán* frailecito monkey + *yákati* seat] : a kind of vine with leaves similar to those of the caimito ⟨**Wasányakati xéaaxa nato jóni mécha iki.** This man is a good fisherman because he drank the sap of the *wasányakati* vine.⟩
See under **róno**

*v.t.* [from Old Shipibo *washikoti*] : to deny : to refuse out of jealousy, stinginess, or distrust ⟨**Ráma min awín washínoxiwe —akinki shinón ánike.** It is said that long ago the monkey said to a man: —Now you are going to deny your wife before the others.⟩ ⟨**Jawen átapa washíketianra yobé jonín aínbo réteke.** A sorcerer killed a bewitched-ed woman because she had refused him her hen.⟩
*n.* **wasín** : a kind of tall grass that grows in the highlands ⟨**Bakénra jahuen papán machíto wásinapon pótake.** The child threw his father's machete into the middle of the tall *wási* grass.⟩

*Konibo* **wásikoma chiáxkan** *n.* **wásikaman chiáxkan** *Konibo* **wásikoma chíáxkanin** [from Shipibo *wási* a kind of grass + *kamán* ghost in the form of a jaguar, or *kóma* tinamou + *chiáxka* forked tail] : a kind of bird ⟨**Non wásikoma chiáxka óinaronki jawéki akín kéxmiati iki.** They say that when we see a *wásikaman chiáxka* bird, our garden plot or something similar may turn out uneven.⟩

*n.* **wásimanaman** [from Shipibo *wási* a kind of grass + *manán* hill] : Gran Pajonal ⟨**Wásimanamamea kámpabora siná ikátikanai ráeamabo ikásh.** The campa (Asháninka people) of the Gran Pajonal were fierce because they had not been civilized.⟩
*n.* **wásnoman** : spiderweb ⟨**Nato xóbora moa wásnoman wéxea iki.** This house is already full of spiderwebs.⟩
*n.* **wastén** : piripiri (a medicinal/magic plant) ⟨**Bénxokaskin wáste xéaaxa mawáke.** He drank piripiri hoping to cure himself, and he died.⟩
[from Shipibo *bakénkonti* that which greatly eases childbirth + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri that a woman takes grated or crushed to ease childbirth
[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *kái* going + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri that a man takes so he can work well all day
[from Shipibo *béro* eye + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used to treat an irritated eye
[from Shipibo *bóo* hair + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri with thread-like leaves, whose crushed root, mixed with huito or alone, is applied to the hair to help it grow
[from Shipibo *kabáyo* horse + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri whose root is taken straight to give strength and vigor
[from Shipibo *konínewa* electric eel + *wáste*] : a kind of piripiri taken to give strength in fistfighting
[from Shipibo *kopítso, kopítsonin* cupiso + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of calming piripiri given to an angry man to drink without his knowing
[from Shipibo *koshóshka* river dolphin + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used against the smell of the river dolphin, which can bewitch a baby
[from Shipibo *chikáro* harpoon + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri whose crushed root is applied to the harpoon so that a speared fish cannot escape
[from Shipibo *chikóro* a kind of demon + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri that one takes to become a sorcerer
[from Shipibo *chixó* diarrhea + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri taken to cure diarrhea or dysentery
[from Shipibo *wísoino* black panther + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri taken crushed to give strength
[from Shipibo *íno* jaguar + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri taken to give strength
[from Shipibo *jénekawe* a kind of aquatic toad + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri taken to be a good fisherman during the fish scarcity caused by the aquatic toad *jénekawe*
[from Shipibo *jóno* collared peccary + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of grated or crushed piripiri that one puts into a shirt one wears, in order to tame the collared peccary in the forest
[from Shipibo *máekawa* huancahui (a kind of snake) + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used to prevent a snake bite
[from Shipibo *manánxawe, manánxawen* tortoise + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri whose crushed root is applied to a dog or a person, so that he becomes a better hunter of tortoises
[from Shipibo *mánko* baldness + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used to prevent or cure baldness
[from Shipibo *mátataon* atatay (an exclamation of pain/heat) + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri applied to the body to make a woman fall in love with a man
[from Shipibo *méchati* that which makes one a good hunter + *wáste* piripiri] : any of several kinds of piripiri used to make one a good hunter
[from Shipibo *menín* talented + *wáste* piripiri] : any of several kinds of piripiri used to train the hands
[from Shipibo *meyá* quick + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri applied to the arm or body, and also to one's work tools, to make one work faster
[from Shipibo *nói* beloved + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used to make someone fall in love
[from Shipibo *pékoshonti* that with which to bewitch + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri whose root, chewed and blown toward an enemy, serves to kill him within a few days
[from Shipibo *péchi* backward + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used to drive away one's wife
[from Shipibo *píno* hummingbird + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri
[from Shipibo *kené* design + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri whose resin is applied to the eyes so that one paints better designs
[from Shipibo *rayáti* that with which to work + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used to make one a better worker
[from Shipibo *róno* snake + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used against snake bite
[from Shipibo *ronón ewa* boa + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used so that the boa does not cutipe (cause sympathetic harm to) the baby, when its parents see it or smell its odor
[from Shipibo *xáe* anteater + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri
[from Shipibo *xoá* fat, robust + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri given to a baby
[from Shipibo *xóno* lupuna (kapok tree) + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri taken to gain weight
[from Shipibo *xóya* mouse + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri used so that a barren woman may conceive
[from Shipibo *táki* tibe (a fish species) + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri whose grated root juice is applied to the eyes so that one becomes a good fisherman
[from Shipibo *teté* hawk + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri taken to give strength
[from Shipibo *tóoti, tóo–* to conceive + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri
[from Shipibo *yoshín* demon + *wáste* piripiri] : a kind of piripiri

*adj. and n.* **wáxakan** *adj.* : torn, broken ⟨**Nokon kotón waxá íketianra ea ránsatiain káyamake.** I did not go to the dance because my shirt was torn.⟩ *n.* : crack, split ⟨**Nónti waxara áni iki; rámara noa jéne bóchoai —iki iká iki.** He said: —The crack in the canoe is big, and now it's going to fill up with water on us.⟩ *syn.* chaká

*v.t.* **wáxaa** 1 : to tear, to rip (e.g., cloth or paper) ⟨**Nokon chiárextira en wáxake, yómetsonin chíbana íshtokin.** I tore my pants when I ran fleeing from a thief.⟩ 2 : to split (wood) ⟨**Tóoaka bóchikiax pakékinronki jonín nónti rebo róokan wáxanike.** They say that once a shot howler monkey fell onto the bow of a man's canoe and split it.⟩

*v.i.* **wáxata** 1 : to tear, to rip (e.g., cloth or paper) ⟨**Moa waxáketianra en chitónti pótake.** I threw away the pampanilla because it had already torn.⟩ 2 : to split (wood) ⟨**Papán konxán réraara póxoti waxákainke.** The cedar that papa felled (with an axe) split when it fell.⟩ ⟨**Papán ícha mapó beára nónti waxáke.** The canoe split because my papa carried too much clay in it.⟩
See under **pishpish**
*n.* **waxmémpokon** [from Shipibo *waxmén* cotton + *póko* gut] : loom heddle ⟨**Jawen bakénra titán wexmémpoko ménonaanke.** The son burned his mother's loom heddle.⟩
*n.* **wáxmeman** : cotton ⟨**Papánra títa waxmén wai áxonai.** My papa is making a cotton garden plot for my mama.⟩
*imperative suf.* –Used added to the end of a verb to express a command or a request. ⟨**Néno yakáwe.** Sit here.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3.1; 4.2.3.2
*n.* **weán** : shadow ⟨**Non káya bichínxonronki yóshiman pótai weánko.** They say that when a demon takes our soul, he throws it into a shadow.⟩ *syn.* beí; wéa
*n.* **wéakan** : a measure of liquid or powder approximating a handful

*n.* **wéaman** 1 : a small or medium-sized river ⟨**Támpo wéamameaxa joshín jéne béke.** Reddish water came from the Tambo River.⟩ 2 : stream, creek ⟨**Jénepanshinya wéamanra báritian kabóri ícha iki.** In the dry season taricaya turtles are abundant in the Jenepanshea creek.⟩
*v.t.* **wéaa** : to remove (liquid or powder) in small amounts from : to bail out ⟨**Nato bakénra jakóma ómpax wéake.** This child bailed out the dirty water.⟩

*v.i.* **wéita** 1 : to enter (several) ⟨**Rámabira béwatiain weíkanke.** Right now they entered the worship service.⟩ 2 : to sink in, to be sunken (more than one) ⟨**Xétaoma ikaxa nokon títashokon kebí wéita iki.** My grandmother's lips are sunken because she has no molars.⟩ 3 : to get into (a mass, e.g., of dust, liquid, air, or fire) ⟨**Icha táshi wéita ikaxbira nato mísi táshioma iki.** Although a lot of salt went into it, this humita (corn tamale) is not salty.⟩ ⟨**Kikínhakin xépoyamaara xéni botirian ompáx weíke.** Water got into the oil bottle because it wasn't well covered.⟩ *syn.* WEITI, JIKITI both translate as "to enter," but JIKITI, unlike WEITI, refers only to a single thing entering.

*v.t.* **wekánhaa** *Konibo* **wekánhaka** : to wilt (something) ⟨**En jóa bánaara moa barín wekánhake en ompáx tachíamaa.** The flowers I planted wilted from the sun and because I didn't water the roots.⟩
*v.i.* **wékana** : to wilt

*adj. and n.* **wékiten** *Konibo* **wékikan** *adj.* 1 : bowed : bent, crooked ⟨**Chóyachakin witáxonki wekíosi iki; ikáxbi benkéx táe máxkoshoko.** They say the legs of the chullachaqui demon are very bowed, and that one foot is smaller than the other.⟩ 2 : bent halfway over ⟨**Ja rábo wekíra bakén jamáke, íshto kakín.** While running, the child stepped on that bent nail.⟩ *n.* 1 : bend, curvature ⟨**Min táe wekía íketianra mia wáiroron bóyamake.** The guard hasn't taken you away because your foot is bowed.⟩ 2 : hook ⟨**Yoshínxatanronki jawenwetía iki, ján jóni yatánti.** They say the clown demon has his hook for grabbing people.⟩
*v.i.* **wékita** : to bend in the middle ⟨**Chíixanan akára nato rábo wekíke.** From the heat of the fire, this nail bent in the middle.⟩
See under ísa
*v.i.* **wékota** : to stagger, to totter ⟨**Nato jónira wékoti níai, páenama ikaxbi.** This man walks staggering, without being drunk.⟩

*v.i.* **wékota** 1 : to worsen (in illness) ⟨**Moa kímisha óxe ríki nato jóni ísina; jákopira moa wekóke.** It's been three months since this man got sick, and now he has gotten worse.⟩ 2 : to worsen in character : to become bad ⟨**Moátianra nato jóni sinámatani iká iki; rámara moa wekóyorake.** Before, this man was a bit hot-tempered, but now he is worse.⟩
*v.i.* **wémekaata** : to get hooked, to get caught (on something) ⟨**Nato báke yóitimara wémekaake.** This disobedient child got caught on something.⟩

*v.t.* **wémea** : to hook ⟨**Bakénra jawen pabíki mishkitinin wémeke.** The child hooked his ear with the fishhook.⟩ ⟨**Míshkiti námi weméya íketianra átapanin námi píamake.** The hen couldn't eat the meat because it was hooked on a fishhook.⟩
*n.* **wéneman** : a partly cleared patch of forest : campsite ⟨**Yamé nókotaxa noa wenénhain óxaa iki.** Arriving at night, we slept in a cleared spot.⟩

*v.t.* **wenénhaa** *Konibo* **wenénhaka** 1 : to partly clear the forest (e.g., during a trip) ⟨**Jaín chíi ketéati epán wenénhaketianra titán áke.** Mama lit the fire to cook after that my uncle had cleared the forest.⟩ 2 : to make camp in the forest ⟨**Kónxaman téetaibaon wenénhainra noa nókota iki.** We arrived at the place where the loggers had made camp.⟩
*v.t.* **wénina** : to make stand : to stand (something) up ⟨**Moa níti átipanyamaketianra en wenínke.** I made him stand even though he could no longer walk.⟩
*v.i.* **wénita** : to stand up ⟨**Páketaxbira ishtón weníke.** When he fell, he stood up again instantly.⟩ ⟨**Jónikoshi jóaitianra jónibo weníke.** When the authority arrived, the people stood up.⟩

*Konibo* **wéntanameti** *v.i.* **wéntameeta** *Konibo* **wéntanameta** 1 : to become agitated, to riot (people) ⟨**Bexnán xéaaxa jónibo wéntameetai tímaanani.** After drinking liquor, the men get agitated and fight.⟩ ⟨**Ránsatiainra jónibo wéntanameke.** There was a commotion at the dance.⟩ 2 : to swarm (wasps) –Used in this sense mainly among Shipibo speakers. ⟨**Wéntameexonra binán rabé jóni tékake; wétsara jabáketian áyamake.** The wasps swarmed and stung two men; the third escaped and nothing happened to him.⟩ 3 : to scatter (people or animals) ⟨**Tóoakara manxan wéntameeke.** When the shotgun went off, the herons scattered.⟩

*v.t.* **wéntana** 1 : to agitate, to stir up (people) ⟨**Píshtatian tsinkíkanketianra wáiroron jato wentánke.** The police stirred up the people when they were gathered at a party.⟩ 2 : to make (wasps) swarm ⟨**Yóashiko Inkanronki bína wentánkatitai jaíba mérati bókanaitian.** They say the Stingy Inca made the wasps swarm when people went walking near where he was.⟩ 3 : to scatter, to disperse ⟨**Atapa wentanyamawe.** Don't scatter the hens.⟩

*v.t.* **wéona** : to hang (something) from a horizontal support ⟨**En néno weónketianra bakén bénabenai.** When I hung it here, the child kept looking for it.⟩ *syn.* WEONTI, PANINTI, RONTANTI can all be translated as "to hang," but RONTANTI is to hang in general, PANINTI can imply more specifically that something is suspended or hung up high, and WEONTI, that the thing (e.g., a pole) used for hanging is in a horizontal position.

*v.i.* **wéota** : to hang (oneself/itself) ⟨**Papán íso tóoakara jíwi póyaman weóke.** The spider monkey my papa shot hung itself from the branch.⟩ ⟨**Oa paránta texkan wéotara pitsón píai.** That hanging bunch of bananas is being eaten by the parakeet.⟩
*v.i.* **wérameeta** : to fall by oneself ⟨**Nato jónira janbíx wérameeke, páenama ikáxbi.** This man fell on his own, but he wasn't drunk.⟩
*v.t.* **wérana** : to push ⟨**Paénxonra papán chómo wéránke.** When he was drunk, papa pushed the large jar.⟩

*adj.* **werén** 1 : thin, sparse : threadbare ⟨**En kotón biára wérewerekoinsi iki.** The shirt I bought is very threadbare.⟩ 2 : protruding from thinness ⟨**Básiora ísinaxa jawen píshi wére iki.** From being sick for a long time, his ribs stick out.⟩ *syn.* westí; xécha
See **wírita**
*n.* **Wesnán** –Used as a female name.
*v.t.* **wésnaa** : to stir up, spreading apart ⟨**Károra keyónake chíi wésnawe.** The firewood will run out; spread out the logs of the fire.⟩

*v.i.* **wésnata** : to clear up (clouds) –Little used nowadays. ⟨**Oi béti keska ikáxbira moa naíkoin wésnata iki.** Although it looked like it was going to rain, in the end the clouds cleared away.⟩

*adj.* **wéstikan** 1 : little : few ⟨**Rámara wéstiakin yónatai; bakíxa íoraa íibake.** Today he has very little fever; yesterday he was worse.⟩ 2 : sparse : scattered ⟨**Xéki bánara westíxoko xóxoke.** The corn I planted grew sparse.⟩ *syn.* wére; xécha

*adj.* **westíoran** [from Shipibo *westí* few + *-yora* very] : one : a ⟨**Kakín, non rétea iki westíora yawíx, rabé jóno.** On the trail, we killed one armadillo and two collared peccaries.⟩ *syn.* WESTIORA, JABICHO both can be translated as "one," but JABICHO means or implies "only one" or "one and no more." See Grammar Sketch 7.1.6
*n.* **westíora ikaton** [from Shipibo *westíora* one + *ti, iká* to be] : unit
*n.* **westíoran janen** [from Shipibo *westíora, westíoran* one + *jáne* name] : singular number –Used as a grammatical term.
*n.* **wétakan** 1 : a kind of basket hung from the roof ⟨**Wétakameara mishítonin yonán bóke.** The cat took the smoked meat from the hanging basket.⟩ 2 : cupboard

*adj. and n.* **wetsán** *adj.* 1 : other, another ⟨**Nátora ea kéenyamai; wétsakaya ea méniwe.** I don't want this one; give me another.⟩ 2 : some ⟨**Wétsa nétebaonra ea mírikatonko kái.** Some days I go to the market.⟩ —Used repeated in parallel clauses so as to have the senses of "some" and "other" respectively. ⟨**Atapa riki, wétsa áni, wétsa ánima.** Some hens are big and others are small.⟩ *n.* 1 : brother or sister of the same sex; *also* : nephew or niece of the same sex as the reference uncle or aunt ⟨**Nokon wetsánra motóro bená bíke.** My brother bought a new motor.⟩ ⟨**Jawen wétsa betan káxa réokooke.** He was going by canoe with his sister and it capsized along with her, alongside her.⟩ 2 : first cousin of the same sex ⟨**Jawen wetsán chópa yámaketian nóibaxonra, jawen kotónbi nato jonín ménike.** This man took pity on his cousin who had no clothes, and gave him his own shirt.⟩ ⟨**Moa jenén réteainbira jawen wetsán bíke.** When he was drowning, his cousin saved him.⟩ ⟨**Nokon titánra jawen wétsa kenéati onámaa iki.** My mama taught her cousin to make designs.⟩ ⟨**Jawen wétsabi onányamaxonra, náwares shinánke, sáyayaiketian.** He did not recognize his own cousin; he thought she was just a mestiza because of the dress she was wearing.⟩ 3 : relatives of the same sex who are neither of an ascending nor a descending generation —Used in the plural form *wétsabo* to indicate the whole group of same-sex relatives of the same generation as a specific relative. 4 : a great-grandchild of the same sex as a specific grandparent *syn.* WETSA, POI both can denote "brother" or "sister," but WETSA implies the same sex while POI implies the opposite sex of the relatives. *syn.* WETSA, JATIRIBI both can be translated as "some," but WETSA implies an alternative among several possibilities, while JATIRIBI implies a part of a group.
*modifying suf.* : again : once more —Used added to the verb and followed by *-yama* "not". ⟨**Nato báritianra ea moa jiwín téewetsayamai.** This year I am not going to work in timber again.⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *wétsa* other + *bakísh*] : the day before yesterday

*n.* **wéxakan** 1 : wood shaving ⟨**Wanín wexáya non bóo méskoxon ménoaronki bóshtiti iki.** They say that to make our hair curly we must burn pijuayo palm shavings mixed with our hair.⟩ 2 : dart for a pucuna or blowgun ⟨**Nókona ícha wexá jáaxbira mókaoma iki.** I have many darts, but they are not poisoned.⟩
*n.* **Wexábitan** [from Shipibo *wexáti, wexa-* to scrape + *Bíta,* male name] –Used as a male name.

*n.* **wexáchitaranin** [from Shipibo *wexá* wood shaving + *chi-* at the rear part + *taránti, taran-* to roll] : cotton cone on a dart ⟨**Jawen wexáchitaran átira en waxmén béke.** I have brought cotton to make cones on the darts.⟩
*v.i.* **wéxakaata** [from Shipibo *wéxati, wexa-* to scrape oneself + *-kaa,* reflexive suf.] : to scrape oneself : to graze oneself
*n.* **Wexákaisan** [from Shipibo *wexáti, wexa-* to scrape + *Kaís,* female name] –Used as a female name.
*n.* **Wexásaman** [from Shipibo *wexati* to scrape + *Sáma* female name] –Used as a female name.
*v.t.* **wéxaa** : to scratch : to claw : to scrape ⟨**En mishíto yátanara ea wéxake.** When I grabbed the cat, it scratched me.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*n.* **wéxatinin** [from Shipibo *wéxati, wéxa-* to scratch + *-ti* that with which] : ushate (a scarifying comb) ⟨**Wéxati riki ján jóni mapónko xáteti sinákin.** The ushate is used to make cuts on a person's head.⟩ *syn.* xáxati
*v.i.* **wéxata** : to flash repeatedly

*adj. and n.* **wéxekan** *adj.* : tangled ⟨**Jáskara wexébira jaton ríka xobon bokánke chóroti átipanyamaxon.** They took the tangled net home because they could not untangle it.⟩ *n.* : tangle ⟨**Ja wexé chóroti onányamaxonra jato nóshikanke.** Because they could not untangle their net, they broke it.⟩

*v.t.* **wéxea** : to tangle : to cause to tangle ⟨**Anirikan ákaibaonra jaton ríka wéxekanke ícha jóxobawin mápoxon.** The net fishermen tangled their net when they caught many white súngaro catfish.⟩ ⟨**Papán risbíra nato bakén wéxeke; rámara noa nótsinai.** This child tangled papa's rope; now he's going to be angry with us.⟩
*v.i.* **wéxeta** : to get tangled ⟨**Titánra nato yomán pótake moa wéxeta íketian.** Mama threw away this thread because it was already tangled.⟩
*v.i.* **wéxeta** : to scratch oneself ⟨**Nokon méntsisenbira ea wéxéke.** I scratched myself with my own fingernail.⟩
*n.* **wéxuexan** : a kind of rodent
*v.t.* **wéyona** : to rock (someone) in a hammock ⟨**Koshín weyónkinra titán jawen báke pákeke.** The mother made her little daughter fall by rocking her too hard in the hammock.⟩
*v.i.* **wéyota** : to rock, to swing ⟨**Weyóweyotaitianra, nokon wétsa ochítinin na-** **téshke, siná ishon.** While my brother was swinging, a rabid dog bit him.⟩

*n.* **weyótinin** [from Shipibo *weyóti, weyo-* to swing + *-ti* that with which] : hammock ⟨**Nato ronónewaronki jenényoshiman weyóti ikí.** They say the boa is the hammock of the water spirits.⟩ *syn.* amáka
*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo *witáx* leg] : to the leg : on the leg : of the leg ⟨**wiskíti** to apply (achiote/annatto) to the leg⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.4
*adj.* **wián** : strong-smelling ⟨**Nato awá xenira wía póatai.** This tapir fat gives off a strong smell.⟩
*v.t.* **wíaa** *Konibo* **wíaaka** : to leave with a strong smell ⟨**Anirikan ákaibaonra nokon nónti wíaake.** The net fishermen left my canoe with a strong smell.⟩
*v.i.* **wíaa** : to have a strong smell ⟨**Nato kampán tárira wíake, ícha néte pátsatama ikax.** This campa's cushma (robe) has a strong smell because he hasn't washed it for many days.⟩
*v.i.* **wíikia** [from Shipibo *wi-* to the leg + *jikiti* to enter] : to enter the leg
*v.t.* **wínaa** : to paddle, to row ⟨**Niweaba béaitianra non koshín wínawanke.** When a gale came, we began to paddle hard.⟩
*adj.* **winín** : crybaby, whiny ⟨**Nato báke riki kikínbires wíni.** This child is a big crybaby.⟩ *syn.* káxa
*v.t.* **wínia** : to cry, to weep ⟨**Jaton kaíbo shínanaxa wínikanke.** Thinking of their fellow countrymen, they wept.⟩ *syn.* beónti
*adj.* **wínkasen** [from Shipibo *wíniti, wini-* to cry + *-kas* to want] : about to cry

*v.i.* **wínkasa** : to be about to cry ⟨**Oa jónira wínkasa ikí; yóyoayamakanwe.** That man is about to cry; don't speak to him.⟩ ⟨**Kímisha pácha waránka sóro yómetsoakanara ea winkáske.** I felt like crying when they robbed me of three hundred thousand soles.⟩
*n.* **winón** : war club ⟨**Jonínra jawen rawí waníwinon réteke.** A man killed his enemy with a pijuayo-palm war club.⟩
*v.t.* **wínona** : to dodge ⟨**Kámparonki bára winónti onán iki.** They say the campa know how to dodge their enemies' bullets.⟩
*v.t.* **wínoa** : to pass by (someone/something) ⟨**En oinyamaara ea wínobainke.** He passed by me, but I didn't see him.⟩

*v.i.* **wínota** 1 : to pass by, to travel through (a person or thing) ⟨**Moara wapóro winóke.** The riverboat already passed by.⟩ 2 : to pass (a day or days) ⟨**Rabé nétera noa jakónbires winókanke, nokon epán báke sontáro kátanax jóketian rároi.** We spent two very happy days celebrating my cousin's return from military service.⟩ 3 : to happen : to occur ⟨**¿Jáweki mia winóta?** What happened to you?⟩ ⟨**Moa winó jawékira yóiyoitima ikí.** A thing of the past should not be mentioned often.⟩

[from Shipibo *jawébi* nothing + *winóti, winota* to happen + *-ma* not] : without incident : safe and sound ⟨**Jaínoaxa noa jojóinake, jawébi wínotama.** We have come paddling upstream from there and are safe and sound.⟩ *syn.* kawánti; íti
*n.* **wintín** [from Shipibo *wínati, wina-* to paddle + *-ti* that with which] : paddle, oar ⟨**Jawen ráyosen wíntiaxonara bóke.** He took the paddle his father-in-law had made for him.⟩
[from Shipibo *toró* round + *wínti* paddle] : a kind of non-Shipibo paddle with a round blade
*n.* **wípokon** *Konibo* **wípokonin** [from Shipibo *wi-* of the leg + *póko* gut] : leg muscle ⟨**Paénxonra jonín jawen wípokobi rérake.** A drunk man cut his own leg muscle with a machete.⟩
*n.* **wirákochan** [from Quechua *wirakocha* white man] : a white man ⟨**Nato wirákochakí ráketíra báke jonéke.** Out of fear of this white man, the child hid.⟩

*adj.* **wírishin** 1 : very thin in diameter 2 : very high-pitched (voice) : falsetto ⟨**Wírishokotonin béwakanara nokon kéen iki; náxbakan íkanara nokon kéema iki.** I like it when someone sings in falsetto, but not when they sing bass.⟩ *syn.* See under **áko**

*v.t.* **wiríshaa** *Konibo* **wiríshaka** : to make very thin ⟨**Rastón áti yóiabira witá tayánkin papán wiríshake.** Although he was told to make the posts thick, papa carved them and they came out too thin.⟩
See under **máni**

*v.i.* **wírisha** 1 : to become thin ⟨**Nato jónira moa wiríshke xoá ikáti ibi.** This man has become thin after having been fat for a long time.⟩ 2 : to become very high-pitched or falsetto (voice) ⟨**Moa íchayora béwaaxa jawen jói moa wiríshke.** His voice has become falsetto from singing so much.⟩

*also* **wérta** *n.* **wíritanin** *also* **wértanin** [from Spanish] : garden : orchard ⟨**Bákebora wíritain káti iki jawéki xóxoai oíni.** The students will go to the orchard to see the plants growing.⟩

*n.* **wíroxen** : a kind of small tree with bark like that of the shihuahuaco, whose wood some people use for house frames ⟨**Moátianronki kóshi jónibo jakátiai, wiróx sékeaibo.** They say that long ago there were strong men who broke the *wiróx* tree with just their hands.⟩
*v.t.* **wísaka** : to whistle at ⟨**Ishto ea káinbira, wísaka ea banéke.** While I was running, I turned around when someone whistled at me.⟩

*n. and adj.* **wíshakan** *n.* 1 : stripe, line ⟨**Maístoronra ea kírika wisháya mároti yóike.** The teacher told me to buy a lined notebook.⟩ 2 : writing ⟨**Kírikara nokóke Rímameax; ja wishá oínxonra en onánke ján bémaa.** A letter has arrived from Lima; by looking at the writing, I can tell who sent it.⟩ *adj.* : written : scribbled ⟨**Nato kírika moa wishá íketian tsóabi mároyamai.** Nobody is going to buy this book since it's scribbled on.⟩ *syn.* WISHA, WISHI, SERE, SION can all be translated as "stripe," but WISHA can imply something handwritten or printed; WISHI and SERE refer more to a natural mark (e.g., on the body of an animal or fish); and SION implies more something painted or dyed.

*v.t.* **wíshaa** 1 : to draw lines on, to stripe ⟨**Oi béaitianronki mái wíshati iki béyamanon ixon.** They say that when it rains, you can draw a line on the ground so it won't rain anymore.⟩ 2 : to slit (meat) for drying ⟨**Papán jakómaakin wíshaara nato wáme nami písike.** This paiche meat spoiled because papa slit it badly.⟩ 3 : to write ⟨**Enra wíshake jatíbi nato jóibo, tée ikénbi.** I have written all these sentences, although it has cost me much effort.⟩ *syn.* seréati; sión áti
[from Shipibo *rítira* letter + *wíshati* to write] : to know how to write ⟨**Náto bákenra rítira wíshati onányamake.** This child doesn't know how to write.⟩

*adj. and n.* **wíshikan** *adj.* : striped *n.* 1 : stripe ⟨**Wishía íketianra nato ochíti en onányamake, íno keska íketian.** I didn't realize it was a dog, because it had stripes like a jaguar's.⟩ 2 : wake (of a boat) ⟨**Yamébi motóro jóaitianra en mérayamake; jawen wishíbichoresa en oínke.** Since the launch came at night, I couldn't make it out; I only saw its wake.⟩ *syn.* See under **wishá**
See under **awápa**

*v.i.* **wíshita** 1 : to stripe oneself : to get striped ⟨**Nato bákera janbíx nanén wishíke.** This girl striped herself with huito dye.⟩ 2 : to get striped by cutting the skin : to cut oneself ⟨**Nato bákera janbíx chíchikanin wishíke.** This child cut himself with a knife.⟩

*n.* **wishkóntin** : wild guaba (ice-cream-bean tree); *also* : the fruit of the wild guaba ⟨**Wishkónti kókoaitianra papán róo réteke.** Papa killed the howler monkey while it was eating wild guabas.⟩
*n.* : a constellation called "Raft of the Seven Kids" formed by the Great Square of Pegasus
*n.* **Wíshmabaon** 1 : mythological "Otherworldly Travelers" : "Seven Kids" 2 : a constellation called the "Otherworldly Travelers," formed by the Pleiades
*n.* **wíshniman** : fog, mist ⟨**Póronapon wishnín íketianra en táxa tsákake.** Since there was fog in the middle of the river, I crashed my boat against a logjam.⟩
*v.i.* **wíshnina** : to form fog, to be foggy ⟨**Nato yamékirira wishníwanke, iósma ikáxbi.** This morning it was foggy for the first time.⟩

*n.* **wishpón** [from Shipibo *wi-* on the leg + *shpo* unidentified element] : shinbone : the larger bone of the leg ⟨**Pápashokonra machítonin** **jawen bába wíshpoki rérake.** The grandfather cut his grandson's shin with a machete.⟩
*n.* **wíshtiman** : star ⟨**Non wishtín topónketianronki non báke pói ícha íkai.** They say that when we count the stars, our children will later have a lot of excrement.⟩
[from Shipibo *néte* day + *wishtin* star] : morning star
[from Shipibo *yantán* afternoon + *wishtín* star] : evening star
*n.* **wíshtinintin** : mahogany ⟨**Nóiwastera non wíshtininti xakaya méskoai.** We mix piripiri *noíwaste* with mahogany bark.⟩

*n.* **wishtín méxoaitonin** [from Shipibo *wishtín* star + *méxoai* (from *méxoti* to crawl) crawling] : satellite ⟨**Nokon pápashokora wishtín méxoai óinax ratéke jáskara oínyosma ikáx.** My grandfather was amazed when he saw a satellite, because he had never seen one before.⟩
*n.* **wishtín paketaitonin** [from Shipibo *wishtín* star + *páketai* (from *páketi* to fall) falling] : shooting star
*v.i.* **wísika** : to give a whistle ⟨**Párokeibakeaxa jóni wísitai.** A man is whistling from the other side of the river.⟩
*v.i.* **wískia** [from Shipibo *wi-* on the leg + *sikíti* to paint oneself] : to paint oneself on the leg

*adj. and n.* **wisón** *adj.* : black : black-colored ⟨**Chéxeinkaronki wíso jóni ikátiai.** They say the Dark Inca was a black man.⟩ *n.* : a black person ⟨**Moátianronki kirínkoboki wísobo betan meskókashamakana iki.** They say that in the past the gringos did not want to mix with black people.⟩

*v.t.* **wísoaa** *Konibo* **wísoaka** : to blacken : to dye black : to turn black ⟨**Chitóntira manón síkaxon wísoake, nato aínbaon.** This woman dyed her pampanilla black with the special *máno* mud.⟩

*n.* **wísobimin** [from Shipibo *wíso* black + *búni* fruit] : a kind of small vine-like plant with small black fruits; *also* : the fruit of the *wísobimi* plant ⟨**Wísobimi máanai namanra sipán icha iki.** Where the little black *wísobimi* fruit falls, sardines are abundant.⟩
