*v.t.* **wísoa** [from Shipibo *wíso* black + *-ti,* infinitive suf.] : to cloud over : to become overcast ⟨**Oiara bekásbirai; moara naí wísoke.** It might rain; the sky has already grown overcast.⟩

*n.* **witakan** 1 : shungo (a palm heart) ⟨**Min ea pinómpari nato witá tóewe —akinronki jonín íno aká iki.** They say a man told the jaguar: —Before you eat me, first split this shungo.⟩ 2 : forked post *syn.* iníchinti

*n.* **wítaxen** : leg ⟨**Jaskábi píkota ikaxa nato bakén witáx yósho iki.** This child has had a crooked leg since birth.⟩ *syn.* WITAX, KISHI — both can be translated as "leg," but WITAX always refers to the whole leg, while KISHI mostly denotes just the thigh.
*n.* **witótonin** : Huitoto : member of the Huitoto ethnolinguistic group ⟨**Witóto jónibaon-** **ra paranta xóixon píai.** The Huitoto roast plantains and eat them.⟩
*n.* **wíwaman** : remocaspi (a tree) ⟨**Títara jawen tsábe betan wiwán károai kake.** Mama went with her sister-in-law to gather remocaspi firewood.⟩
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *x* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1
*n.* **xábakan** : open space

*v.t.* **xábaata** [from Shipibo *xabá* open space + *-ati* to make] : to clear (e.g., a plot of land) : to clear the weeds from ⟨**Bakíxa en wái xabáibake.** Yesterday I cleared the weeds from my garden plot.⟩
*v.i.* **xábaa** : to yawn ⟨**Oxakasira ea xábai.** I'm yawning because I want to sleep.⟩
*n.* **xabín** 1 : groin 2 : lap *syn.* chixána
See under **níwe**
*n.* **xachín** : cortadera (a sharp-edged sedge grass) ⟨**Xáchira kestóyora iki.** The cortadera grass grows very densely.⟩
*v.i.* **xáchia** : to expose one's groin
*n.* **xaén** : anteater ⟨**Xaénra bóna píai.** The anteater eats isula (bullet ants).⟩
See under **bóna**

*n.* **xaén mapaman** [from Shipibo *xáe, xaén* anteater + *mapán* unidentified element] : a small tree species similar to achiote (annatto); *also* : the fruit of the *xaén mapán* tree ⟨**Manánxawenra xaén mapán bími píai.** The motelo (tortoise) eats the fruit of the little *xaén mapán* tree.⟩

*n.* **xaén meyarinin** [from Shipibo *xáwe, xawén* anteater + *meyari* unidentified element] : anona (a fruit similar to soursop); *also* : the fruit of the anona, similar to the chirimoya (custard apple) ⟨**Xaén meyári riki báta.** The anona is sweet.⟩
See under **ráo**
See under **shimón**
*n.* **xákakan** 1 : tree bark 2 : fish scale ⟨**Wámera jókakin jawen xaká ratsáti iki.** To skin the paiche (a giant Amazon fish), the scales are removed first.⟩
*n.* **xakácharon** [from Shipibo *xaká* fish scale + *cháro* baby turtle] : crab ⟨**Xakácharo riki táxameran itín kéen.** The crab likes to be in the palizada (a log jam).⟩
*v.t.* **xákia** : to grate ⟨**Aínbaonra átsa xákiai poróroka anóxon.** The woman is grating cassava to make chicha.⟩ *syn.* xáxati
*n.* **xakitinin** : a type of instrument used for grating ⟨**páranta xákiti** plantain grater⟩
*n.* **xakón** : a species of black centipede
See under **níshi**
See under **wáste**

*n.* **xamán** : cluster of tender young shoots that grow at the tip of certain plants (e.g., banana, shapaja (a palm), shebón (a palm), and caimito (star apple)) : bud ⟨**Shebón xáma riki pishín áti.** Mats are made from the bud of the shebón palm.⟩
See under **átsa**

*n.* **xampóshanin** : a species of plant used to cure skin irritations, which, according to some, cutipates (spiritually afflicts) anyone who cuts it without knowing it ⟨**Títara xampóshanin mérake.** Mom was cutipated by the *xampósha* plant.⟩

*modifying pref.* [from Shipibo; element of *xáni* a woman's pubic hair] : in the groin area : of the groin : to the groin ⟨**xanwíxti** to scratch the groin of⟩ ⟨**xanwis** dark groin area⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.1

*adj. and n.* **xanán** *adj.* : hot : warm ⟨**Ráta xóbora xána iki.** The house with the tin roof is hot.⟩ *n.* : heat : fever ⟨**Bárira jíkiai jawen xánayabi.** The sun sets and takes all its heat with it.⟩
*n.* **xánakan** : tamamuri (a fruit tree) ⟨**Xaná bimi riki kókoti.** The fruit of the tamamuri is edible.⟩
*v.t.* **xánaaka** : to heat ⟨**Nokon áwininra yápa jéne xánaake. Kawé pinón.** My wife has heated the fish broth. Let's go eat.⟩
*v.i.* **xánaa** : to feel hot ⟨**Bári xánaketianra, ea xánai.** During the dry season I feel hot.⟩
[from Shipibo *bári* sun + *xánati* to burn] : to be hot (weather) ⟨**Bári ishtón xánayamaketianra, non chópa mechábi sáweke.** We put on our damp clothes because there was no sun to dry them.⟩
*n.* **xánbaman** : placenta ⟨**Bákera xanbányabi pikóke.** That child was born still wrapped in the placenta.⟩
*n.* **xánbiman** : a species of black bee ⟨**Xanbínra paránta jóshiman kéen iki.** The black bee likes ripe bananas.⟩
*n.* **xanbón** : lagartija (lizard) ⟨**Xanbónra mái chíniai.** The lizard digs in the ground.⟩
[from Shipibo *níi* monte (forest) + *xánbo* lagartija (lizard)] : a species of wild lizard
*n.* **xanén** : a small sky-blue bird species ⟨**Níweabanonra xáne síin ikai.** The little *xáne* bird whistles to announce a windstorm.⟩
*n.* **Xáneman** –Used as a man's name.
*n.* **xáneoton** : mantona (a woven cloth) ⟨**Xáneoto riki kenéya.** The mantona has designs on it.⟩
*n.* **xanín** : a woman's pubic hair
*n.* **xanín** : maracana (a parrot species) ⟨**Xanínra bákeai jíwi táno kíni meran.** The maracana gives birth to its young inside a dry, hollow tree.⟩
*n.* **xánikan** : a type of ceramic vessel used for storing or transporting beverages
See under **kári**
*n.* **xanínyanin** : a type of large mocahua (drinking bowl) used for drinking beverages ⟨**Xanínya riki jan raóti nápoti.** The *xanínya* mocahua is used to store ornaments.⟩
*n.* **xánkeman** : small ditch : hollow where water collects ⟨**Mái xankén bócho awé.** Fill in that little ditch with dirt.⟩
*n.* **xánkoman** : uvilla (a type of berry)
[from Shipibo *níi* monte (forest) + *xankón* uvilla] : a species of wild uvilla ⟨**Níi xankón riki beshéshoko.** The wild uvilla is tiny.⟩

*v.i.* **xóxoa** : to grow ⟨**Xékira básima xóxoax ániax bimiai.** Corn germinates and grows fast and bears fruit.⟩ *syn.* aníti
*n.* **xoyán** : rat; *also* : mouse ⟨**Xoyánra yométsoxon táma píai.** The rat steals peanuts and eats them.⟩
[from Shipibo *jóxo* white + *xóchi* chest + *-ya* with + *xóya* rat] : a species of white-chested, tailless rodent
[from Shipibo *máka* rat + *xóya* rat] : bayano (a large rat species) : rat
See under **níshi**
See under **wáste**
*n.* –Used as the name of the letter *y* in the Shipibo alphabet. See Grammar Sketch 2.1

*verbal suf.* **-yat** –Used added to the verb as a marker of the definite future tense with the sense of "tomorrow." ⟨**Bakísha Máioshiain kayáribiai.** Tomorrow he will go to Pucallpa.⟩ ⟨**Bakénra binón béyatai.** Tomorrow the child will bring aguaje fruits.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2 *syn.* bakísh

*postp. suf.* **-yaton** : with : having –Used postposed to the pronoun or noun, indicating possession or extension. –Used before or after the plural suffix *-bo*. ⟨**Kírikaya jowé.** Come with the book.⟩ ⟨**Píshtatianra sontárobo bántayabo márachanai.** During the festival the soldiers march with their leggings.⟩ ⟨**Wétsa netén westíora kánsa iká iki íaman nónononoi jawen bákeboya.** One day a goose was swimming in the oxbow lake with her young.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.2 *syn.* betan

[from Shipibo *ja* it, that + *-ya* with + *iti* to be] 1 : to have –Used with the object placed before the suffix *-ya*. ⟨**—¿Miaki awínya iki? —Eara jayá iki.** —Do you have a wife? —Yes, I do.⟩ ⟨**Nato aínbaon bákera róokoya iki; jáskara ikáxa, járibi jayá iki.** This woman's child has whooping cough; therefore, she must have it too.⟩ ⟨**Bákera binónya iki.** The child has aguajes.⟩ 2 : to contain ⟨**Titán chómora xéatioma iki; ja nokon wáatan chómoresa jayá iki.** Mom's jar doesn't contain any drink; only my aunt's does.⟩
*n.* **yáaman** : tick ⟨**Nokon ochítira manánxawen yáaman piá iki** **pábikiain.** The tortoise's tick has stuck itself to my dog's ear⟩
See **chábi**
*v.t.* **yábina** : to lock : to close with a key ⟨**Enra nokon xóbo yabínke, yómetsobo jíkinaketian.** I locked my house so thieves would not get in.⟩
See **chábi**

*n.* **yaén** : a jungle fruit species similar to the cherimoya and the soursop, sometimes called wild cherimoya ⟨**Nokon títashokora yáe bénai kawánke níi meran.** My grandmother went to the forest to look for the fruit called wild cherimoya.⟩
See under **-ya**
*v.t.* **yakámaa** [from Shipibo *yakáti* to sit + *-ma* causative] : to seat : to make sit *syn.* **yasánti**
See under **paránta**

*v.i.* **yákata** 1 : to be seated : to sit down –Used in all its senses in the preterite form but with present-tense meaning. ⟨**Aínbora yakáke.** The woman is sitting.⟩ ⟨**Jíwi naman yákatatonra ea óinai.** The one sitting under the tree is looking at me.⟩ 2 : to be (located) ⟨**Titán áni chomora jéma napon yakáke.** Mother's big jar is in the yard.⟩ 3 : to reside : to live ⟨**Páoyamanra westíora náwa yakáke non kaíbo xaran.** In Paococha a mestizo lives among our countrymen.⟩ *syn.* See under **játi**

*n.* **yakátinin** 1 : seat 2 : chair ⟨**Westíora yakátira ráma kikínbires kopí iki.** Nowadays a chair is quite expensive.⟩ 3 : community ⟨**Jaínra non bená yakáti iki.** Over there is our new community.⟩ *syn.* See under **jéma**
See under **warán**
*v.t.* **yakíaa** : to shake : to agitate ⟨**Níwamanra jéne yakíake.** The earthquake shook the water.⟩
*v.i.* **yákita** : to shake violently ⟨**Jéne meranoax yoshín píkotainronki, jéne yakíke.** They say that when a ghost came out of the water, it shook itself violently.⟩
*n.* **yákoanin** [from Spanish] : Yagua : member of the Yagua ethnic group
*n.* **yamán** [from Quechua] : llama ⟨**Yáma riki kaíakanai jawéki Piróain jaá.** The llama is an animal native to Peru.⟩
*adv.* [from Shipibo *-ya* with + *-ma* not] : no ⟨**Yáma riki.** There is none.⟩ ⟨**Yáma riki.** It isn't there.⟩
*also* **jóni yamánko** [from Shipibo *tsóabi* nobody (or *jóni* man) + *yáma* not + *-nko* in] : in a deserted place ⟨**Jónira tsóabi yamanko nokóke.** The man arrived at a deserted place.⟩
*negative suf.* : not –Used added to the verb. ⟨**Jára káyamake.** He did not go.⟩ ⟨**Jaín tsíniamawe.** Don't play there.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2; 8.3.4.2
*v.i.* **yámaa** : to not exist : to not be present ⟨**Jénetianra Bitániain paránta yámake.** In the winter there are no bananas in Betania.⟩
*n. and adv.* **yámekan** *n.* : night : darkness *adv.* : at night : by night ⟨**Yaméra íno kéotai.** At night the jaguar roars.⟩
[from Shipibo *yamé* night + *bási* delayed] : around eleven o'clock at night
[from Shipibo *yamé* darkness + *káti* to go] : to cloud over with storm darkness ⟨**Jénetianra yamékawankatital.** In the winter the sky suddenly clouds over with dark clouds.⟩
[from Shipibo *yamé* night + *pochínikon* in the middle of] : midnight : at midnight

*n.* **yámekan ewan** [from Shipibo *yamé, yámekan* night, + *-ewa*, augmentative suf.] : a long-duration type of eclipse ⟨**Yámekan ewakitianronki káshi ícha béti iki.** They say that multitudes of bats can invade us when there is a long-duration eclipse.⟩
See under **yamé**

*adv.* **yamékirin** [from Shipibo *yamé* night + *kiri*, unidentified element] : early in the morning –Often used with *-shoco*, which gives it the sense of "in the early morning" or "very early." ⟨**Yamékirira ea íshtoai, nokon yóra jakón kopi.** I run in the mornings to keep my body healthy.⟩

*adv.* [from Shipibo *yamékiri* in the morning + *-shoko*, diminutive] : very early in the morning : at dawn ⟨**Eara káa iki níi meran yamékirishoko jawékiaamabi.** I went to the forest early in the morning without breakfast.⟩
See under **yamé**

*v.i.* **yámeta** 1 : to become night : to grow dark : to turn to nightfall 2 : to spend the night ⟨**Eara yaméke Amakiria nawékinin. Jáskarabi joáxa ea Kakónko nokóke.** I spent the night in the bay of Amaquiría, and then arrived at Caco.⟩

*n.* **yamín** 1 : axe ⟨**Enra yámi taxo ánoxon en texó káxke béke.** I brought a quinilla-wood post to make the axe handle.⟩ 2 : iron ⟨**Ikítoainoax joá wapóroninra yámi ícha máanhake.** The boat that came from Iquitos unloaded the iron.⟩ 3 : metal; *specif.* : aluminum
*n.* **yámi boikan** [from Shipibo *yámi* metal + *boí*, participle of *bóti* to carry] : solder metal; *specif.* : tin
*n.* **yámichakatinin** [from Shipibo *yámi* axe + *chákati* hammer] : sledgehammer : mallet –Rarely used nowadays.
*n.* **yámichopan** [from Shipibo *yámi* metal + *chópa* cloth] : metal mesh/screen ⟨**¿Jawetíí mítoro pextínrin yámichopa?** How many meters wide is the metal mesh?⟩
*n.* **yámikentin** [from Shipibo *yámi* metal + *kénui* pot] : aluminum or other metal pot

*n.* **yáminawan** [from Shipibo *yámi* axe + *náwa* wild Indian] : Yaminahua : member of the Yaminahua ethnolinguistic group ⟨**Yáminawabaonronki jáka píamai, kópinaketian.** They say that the Yaminahua don't eat pumagarza (a heron species), because they fear being cutipados (spiritually harmed).⟩ ⟨**Yáminawabora nóki sinákanike, non jaton kaíbobo rétea shínanax.** The Yaminahua got angry with us because they thought we had killed their countrymen.⟩
*n.* **yamín téetaiton** [from Shipibo *yámi, yamín* axe, aluminum + *téetai,* participle of *téeti* to work] : blacksmith ⟨**Jatíbi yamín téetaibora yónkia iki.** All blacksmiths have their anvil.⟩
*n.* **yámipoin** [from Shipibo *yámi* metal + *pói* excrement] : rust : oxidation : corrosion ⟨**Yámipoironki mawáti iki.** They say rust causes death.⟩ *syn.* See under **rápoi** *syn.* ára
*n.* **yámixakitinin** [from Shipibo *yámi* metal + *xakiti* grater] : file (tool) *syn.* ríma

*n.* **yámixetan** [from Shipibo *yámi* axe + *xéta* tooth] : metal-tipped arrow used to spear taricayas (river turtles) ⟨**Papánra yámixeta ákai, kabóri tsákati.** Dad is making arrows to spear taricayas.⟩
*n.* **yámixoitinin** [from Shipibo *yámi* axe + *xóiti, xoi-* to roast + *-ti* instrument for] : grill ⟨**Yámixoitininra píti yonán tsamáke.** The smoked fish is piled up on the grill.⟩
*n.* **yanchámanin** : llanchama (a bark-cloth tree) ⟨**Yanchámara Aóiti páro kexa ícha iki.** Llanchama trees are abundant on the bank of the Aguaytía River.⟩

*adv.* 1 : in vain : for nothing ⟨**Eara yánka jóke; tsóabira en mérayamake.** I came in vain because I didn't find anyone.⟩ 2 : for free (unpaid) ⟨**Pátoroninra jawen jónibo yánka téemapaonike.** The boss made his *workers* work for nothing.⟩
*adj.* **yánkamanin** [from Shipibo *yánka* in vain + *-ma* not] : free ⟨**Rámara noa Píroanobo yánkama iki.** Nowadays we Peruvians are free.⟩
See under **pempén**
See under **píno**
See under **pírapira**
See under **piská**

*adj.* **yánkoman** 1 : blue : blue-colored ⟨**Náira yankón iki.** The sky is blue.⟩ ⟨**Eara mároai kotón yankón.** I am buying a blue shirt.⟩ 2 : green : blue-green : green or blue-green colored ⟨**Enra chópa yankón mároke.** I bought green-colored cloth.⟩
See under **chóno**
*adj.* **yankón oxnakan** [from Shipibo *yankón* green + *oxná*] : dark green : dark green colored
*adj.* **yankón paxnakan** [from Shipibo *yankón,* blue, green + *paxná* light] : light green : light green colored
See under **main**

*adv.* 1 : in the afternoon ⟨**Nokon kókara jóke yantán.** My uncle, my father's brother, came in the afternoon.⟩ 2 : late –Commonly used with *-yora, -ira* ⟨**Miara yantánhira jóke.** You have come very late.⟩ *syn.* bási
[from Shipibo *yantán* in the afternoon + *bási* for a long time] : at night, very late ⟨**Yantán basira motóro nokówanke.** At night, very late, the motorboat arrived.⟩
[from Spanish *yantán* afternoon + *kaman* until] : all day ⟨**Jónira yantán kaman téeke.** The man worked all day.⟩
*modifying suf.* : some time ago (e.g., months or years) See Grammar Sketch 7.4.2
See under **yantán**
*adv.* [from Shipibo *yantánti* to grow late (dusk) + *-kain* moving] : around seven in the evening
See under **yantán**
*adv.* : around two in the afternoon ⟨**Tántixonra, yantánpake, non róo méraibake.** After resting, around two in the afternoon, we saw a howler monkey.⟩
*v.i.* **yántana** 1 : to grow late in the day (dusk) ⟨**Rámara mátsi yantánke.** Today it grew late and turned cold.⟩ 2 : to delay into the afternoon
See under **wishtín**

*adv.* [from Shipibo *yantán* in the afternoon + *-yora* very] : very late in the afternoon : during the last hours of the afternoon ⟨**Moa yantányora íketian, noa banékirana iki.** When it was already very late in the afternoon, we returned.⟩
See **-oma**
*n.* **yapán** : fish ⟨**Mátsi íketianra, yápa íaman páenai.** When it is cold, the fish get sluggish in the oxbow lake.⟩ *syn.* See under **wáka** *syn.* **píti**
[from Shipibo *komári* chambira palm + *yápa* fish] : chambira fish
[from Shipibo *chána* a species of paucar + *yápa* fish] : a fish species
: mojarra (a fish)

*n.* **yapán** [from Quechua *yapa*] : an increase : a little extra (yapa) –Used followed by a noun to specify the amount added. ⟨**Chónka kiro ea asókaron mároketianra, jawen yápa mesó ea pátoronin ménike.** Because I bought ten kilos of sugar, the boss gave me an extra handful as yapa.⟩
*n.* **yápakan** : ochomullaca (a shrub) ⟨**Enra yapá károai.** I am cutting ochomullaca for firewood.⟩
*n.* **yapán ewan** [from Shipibo *yápa* fish + *-ewa*, augmentative suf.] : sábalo (a fish)
See under **pókoti**

*v.t.* **yásana** [from Shipibo; cf. the syllable *ya* of *yakáti* to sit] : to seat : to make sit; *also* : to place ⟨**Titánra chómo yasánke nontín ompax bíi kaxon.** The mother placed the jar in the canoe when she went to fetch water.⟩ *syn.* **yakámati**
*v.t.* **yatámaa** [from Shipibo *yatánti* to grab + *-ma* causative] : to hand over to (a person)

*v.t.* **yátana** 1 : to catch : to grab ⟨**Enra jóno báke yatánke.** I caught a baby collared peccary.⟩ 2 : to detain ⟨**Nokon wétsara koáritiabaon yatánke.** My brother was detained by the guards.⟩ *syn.* See under **tsásiati** *syn.* **tsómati**
*n.* **yawán** : huangana (white-lipped peccary) : wild boar ⟨**Ochítininra yáwa chíbanai.** The dog is chasing the peccary.⟩
[from Shipibo *chána* a species of paucar + *yawa* huangana] : a small species of huangana (peccary) with a strong smell
See under **ísko**
*n.* **yawámaseman** [from Shipibo *yáwa* huangana + *masén* gourd] : a large bird species ⟨**Taxbáinra yawámasen jíi ike.** From among the tahuampas (flooded forest), a *yawámasen* bird cried out.⟩

*n.* **yawámaseman** [from Shipibo *yáwa* huangana + *masén* gourd] 1 : toropisco (horned screamer) ⟨**Papánra jenén kaxón yawámasen mérake.** When dad went to the oxbow lake, he found a toropisco.⟩ 2 : a species of tree fruit used as a pate (gourd bowl)
*n.* **yáwarankin** : a palm species with spines all over the trunk, whose wood is used as the base of a house. ⟨**Shinónra yáwaranki bími píai.** The monkey eats the fruit of the *yáwaranki* palm.⟩

*n.* **yáwishan** *also* **yáwishen** 1 : quirquincho (a type of armadillo) : carachupa : armadillo ⟨**Enra yawísh máikinin meranoa tsékai.** I am pulling an armadillo out of the hole it made in the ground.⟩ 2 : a constellation called "Armadillo," not yet adequately identified –Used in this sense written with a capital initial *Y*.

*n.* **yáwishan ewan** [from Shipibo *yawish, yáwishan* armadillo + *ewa*, augmentative] : yanguaturi (a giant armadillo) ⟨**Yawíshan ewara máikini meran jáke.** The yanguaturi lives in holes in the ground.⟩
See under **bína**
See under **bokón**

*also* **yáyatita** *n.* **yayán** *also* **yáyatitan** : a woman's paternal aunt : her father's sister; *also* : the wife of a woman's legitimate uncle –Used in the vocative form *titá* that follows the personal name to address the person. ⟨**Jowé, Meatitá.** Hello, Aunt Méa.⟩ ⟨**Nokon yáyara ménexeeti kéenai.** *My paternal aunt wants a bracelet.*⟩ *syn.* See under **wáata**

*adj.* **yénkeman** 1 : smooth : soft ⟨**Ishmíman ewan kiní yóikanai yenkén.** They say the giant condor's den is smooth.⟩ 2 : hairless (e.g., due to lack of development) ⟨**Nato bákeranoman witáx riki yenkén.** This child has no hair on his calf.⟩ *syn.* **báka**
*v.t.* **yénshika** : to grind/gnash (one's teeth) ⟨**Enra xéta yenshikai isín ténekin.** I grind my teeth enduring the pain.⟩
*v.t.* **yexkea** : to twist ⟨**Maístoronra yóitima bákebaon pabíki yéxkeke.** The teacher twisted the ears of his mischievous students.⟩ *syn.* **éxpaati**
*n.* **yóakan** : food : nourishment : foodstuffs : provisions ⟨**Yoára jenén kéyoke.** The flood destroyed the food.⟩
*n.* **yoá akaiton** [from Shipibo *yóa* food + *ákai*, form of *áti* to make] : cook (male or female) *syn.* See under *kósinira*
*v.t.* **yoá aka** : to cook
*adj.* **yóashinin** : stingy : miserly ⟨**Náto jónira kikínbires yóashi ikáx sínatai jáiba bokánketian.** Because he is so stingy, this man gets angry when there are visitors in his house.⟩
See under *ínka*
*v.i.* **yóashia** : to be stingy : to stingily refuse ⟨**Nokon pápashokora nokon wétsaki míshkitinin yóashike.** My grandfather stingily refused to give my brother the fishhook.⟩
*n.* **yóbaman** : a tree species with thorny bark and small leaves ⟨**Yobán bímira poróto keska iki.** The fruit of the *yobán* tree is like a bean.⟩

*n.* **yóbekan** 1 : sorcerer ⟨**Nokon yósipara yobé iki.** My grandfather is a sorcerer.⟩ ⟨**Yóbekanra róme kaxkákaxka ákai.** The sorcerer gargles a liquid with tobacco.⟩ 2 : an enchanted animal or plant ⟨**Bonsín riki ochíti keska, ikáxbi yobé.** The otter looks like a dog, but it is an enchanted animal.⟩ *syn.* See under *meráya*
*n.* **yobémiston** [from Shipibo *yobéiti* to ask improperly + *-mis* one who always does (a specified thing)] : one who always asks improperly

*v.i.* **yóbena** : to ask improperly ⟨**Jónira aínbaon yóbenai.** The man is improperly asking that woman's father for her.⟩ ⟨**Nopatáx ikára yámikentin yobénke, mároti átipanyamáx.** Our neighbor improperly asked us for a pot; he could not afford to buy one.⟩
*n.* **yobétinin** [from Shipibo *yobé* sorcerer + *-ti* instrument for] : sorcery ⟨**yobéti itan onányati kírikabo** books of sorcery and magic⟩
*n.* **yóbiman** : edible fruit(s) eaten raw ⟨**Yobín kókonon kawé.** Let's go eat some fruit.⟩ *syn.* See under *kósinira*
*n.* **yochín** : chili pepper ⟨**Yóchira en bánai.** I am planting chili peppers.⟩

*n.* **yólaman** [from Shipibo *yóia*, past participle of *yóiti* to say] : word; *also* : promise ⟨**Nokon yóiabora en sénenhai; mínkayara senénayamai.** I keep my promises; but you don't.⟩ *syn.* jói
*n.* **yóia join** [from Shipibo *yóia*, past participle of *yóiti* to say + *jói* word] : declarative sentence –Used as a grammar term. See Grammar Sketch 4.2.1

*v.i.* **yóimeeta** [from Shipibo *yóiti* to say + *-mee,* reflexive suf.] : to pretend to be ⟨**Píti tsakaitúbira, nokon wétsa mécha jóniboki yóimeetai.** Every time a fish bites, my brother pretends to be an expert at mitayando (hunting)⟩
*n.* **yóimiston** [from Shipibo *yóiti, yoi-* to talk + *-mis,* agentive suf.] : gossipy person ⟨**Nato aínbora yóimis iki.** This woman is a gossip.⟩
*adj.* **yoímiston** [from Shipibo *yoínti, yoin-* to be jealous + *-mis,* one who always does (a specified thing)] : jealous *syn.* See under **ranó**

*n.* **yóinanin** : animal —Used regarding mammals and birds, but not reptiles. ⟨**Ino riki westíora yóina kikínbires siná, raké ikáxbi.** The jaguar is a very fierce animal, but also very timid.⟩ *syn.* See under **jawéki**

*v.t.* **yóina** [from Shipibo *yóiti* to say + *-n,* verbalizing derivation suf.] : to be jealous of ⟨**Aínbaonra jawen béne wétsa aínboki yoínke.** The woman was jealous of her husband over another woman.⟩

*v.t.* **yóia** 1 : to speak to ⟨**Janra ea yóike.** He spoke to me.⟩ 2 : to say ⟨**Janra ea yóike: —Kátima.** He said to me: —Don't go.⟩ 3 : to explain ⟨**Maístoron mia yóiti iki jaskáaxon áti.** The teacher will explain to you how to do this.⟩ 4 : to order ⟨**Papán yóiara, en átapa bénai.** If dad orders me, I'll bring the hen.⟩ 5 : to accuse ⟨**Tson yómetsoaketianki, nato jonín ea yóia.** When someone robbed him, this man accused me.⟩ *syn.* áti; bémati; ráanti
: preacher
[*Ríosen Jói* Word of God + *yóiti* to speak] : to preach : to deliver a sermon *syn.* See under **píritikanti**
*adj.* **yóitinin** [from Shipibo *yóiti* to say] : obedient ⟨**Yóiti bákera jawen titán moén áyamai.** The mother doesn't spank the child who is obedient.⟩

*v.i.* **yóiti ika** [from Shipibo *yóiti* obedient + *íti, -iti* to be] : to obey : to be obedient ⟨**Kónxaman téetaiboronki néte xabáti óchoma yáwakanike; westíora jónires íamanike yóiti ikáx.** They say that long ago some loggers turned into huanganas at dawn, and only one was saved because he was obedient.⟩ *syn.* kásoati

*adj.* **yóitiman** [from Shipibo *yóiti* obedient + *-ma* not] 1 : disobedient ⟨**Yóitima bákera chíiki pakéke.** The disobedient child fell into the fire.⟩ 2 : misbehaved : mischievous ⟨**Yóitima bákera titán ríxkiai.** The mother punishes the misbehaved child with a spanking.⟩ 3 : bad : wicked : cursed ⟨**Yóitima íxónra, bakén jawen papán xóbo ménoke.** Because he was bad, the boy burned down his father's house.⟩ *syn.* See under **jakóma**

*v.i.* **yóitimaa** 1 : to become, or go back to being, disobedient ⟨**Náto chíiki páketa, bákera jákiribi yóitimake.** The boy who fell into the fire went back to being disobedient.⟩ 2 : to rebel ⟨**Ja jónibora Díosen Jóiki yóitamake.** Those men rebelled against the Word of God.⟩

*n.* **yókaman** 1 : question ⟨**Rókotoron yoká riki kikínbires onántima.** The doctor's question is very difficult.⟩ 2 : request ⟨**Nokon kokán yoká íketianra, náto átapa en bóai.** I am bringing this hen according to my uncle's request.⟩ *syn.* YOKA, YONO can both be translated as "request" with no difference, but it will be noted that both words have different additional senses. *syn.* pírikonta
*n.* **yokámiston** 1 : one who is always asking questions ⟨**Jatíbi jawéki yokámis riki náto jóni.** He is a very inquisitive man; he asks about everything.⟩ 2 : beggar : almsseeker
*v.i.* **yokámisa** [from Shipibo *yokámis* beggar + *-ti*, infinitive suf.] : to beg : to ask for alms ⟨**Pitín ikíra jóni yokámisai.** Because he is hungry, the man begs.⟩
*n.* **yókata join** [from Shipibo *yókata*, past participle of *yokáti* to ask] : interrogative sentence –Used as a grammar term. See Grammar Sketch 4.2.2
*v.t.* **yókata** 1 : to ask for ⟨**Enra ómpax yokáke.** I asked for water⟩ 2 : to ask (a question) ⟨**—¿Minki onányama? —Níma yokáwe.** —Don't you know? —Ask Nima.⟩ *syn.* See under *pírikonta ati*
See under **main**

*v.i.* **yókita** 1 : to paint oneself, typically with achiote, fat, or vegetable shortening 2 : to get stained : to get dirty ⟨**Náto bákera míshkiman yokíke.** This child has gotten dirty with honey.⟩ *syn.* See under **sikíti**
See **Yoránta**
*n.* **yómaman** : thread : yarn ⟨**Nokon awínra en yomán mároxonke.** I bought thread for my wife.⟩

*pish.* **yománti** *v.t.* **yóman aka** *pish.* **yómana** [from Shipibo *yomán* thread + *-ati* to make] : to spin (thread) ⟨**Nokon títashokonra yomán ake jawen bába táriaxonti.** My grandmother made cotton thread to make a cushma (traditional tunic) for her grandson.⟩
*n.* **yómeman** : a tree species ⟨**Yomén bépoman nóa méskitaronki tobí onánti iki.** They say that if we apply the resin of the *yomén* tree, we become masseurs and can heal fractures.⟩

*v.t.* **yómeraa** : to mitayar (hunt/fish an expedition) : to fish : to hunt ⟨**Jonínra yómerake bawín, moxóbaton, jainoax wetsa yapaboribi.** The man caught súngaro (a catfish), mullet, and other fish.⟩
*v.t.* **yómetsoaa** : to steal –Used with direct and indirect objects. ⟨**Aínbora yómetsobaon jawen písha yómetsoake.** A thief stole a woman's bag from her.⟩

*v.i.* **yómetsoa** : to steal : to pilfer –Used with an object indicating the thing stolen, but without an object indicating the person robbed. ⟨**Náwara yómetsoke non santíranin.** A mestizo stole our watermelons.⟩
*n.* **yómoxonin** : sealing wax (from a tree species); *also* : tree resin

*n.* **yompán** : red chameleon; a species of chameleon that goes into the water ⟨**Maxóchanto taxbá naman káketianronki yompán jenénko pakekin rátenike, játianbi káwetsatimakin.** They say that Maxóchanto went into the tahuampa (flooded forest); and that when a red chameleon fell into the water, it got scared and never came back.⟩

*modifying suf.* 1 : in great quantity or manner : quite a lot –Used added to the verb. ⟨**Móara báke rishkíonke.** He gave the child quite a few beatings.⟩ 2 : completely : entirely ⟨**Jara bénxoyonke.** He has healed completely.⟩
*n.* **yónakan** : fever ⟨**Sarámpira yoná kóshi iki.** Measles causes a high fever.⟩

*v.t.* **yónaa** : to develop a fever ⟨**En yónataitianra, ea matsín ákai.** Since I have a fever, I feel cold.⟩ ⟨**Nokon wétsanra yoná ake, kirípi koshín ikín.** My brother had a fever from a bad flu.⟩

*adj. and n.* **yónaman** [from Shipibo *yonánti, yonan-* to smoke] *adj.* : smoked ⟨**píti yonán** smoked fish⟩ *n.* : smoked food ⟨**Wétakameara mishítonin yonán bóke.** The cat took the smoked food from the hanging plate.⟩
*xet.* **yonán ati** *v.t.* **yónana** *xet.* **yonán aka** : to smoke (e.g., fish or meat), typically on a grill ⟨**Titánra píti yonánke.** Mom smoked the fish.⟩
See under **ráo**
*n.* **yonínanin** : a plant species about a meter and a half tall, with a bushy frond and pleasant-smelling leaves, that is used to dye and perfume cloth
*n.* **yonkín** [from Spanish] : anvil ⟨**Jatíbi yamín téetaibora yónkia iki.** All blacksmiths have an anvil.⟩
*n.* **yonón** : moena (a tree) ⟨**Yóno bími máanaira píchakan píai.** The palometa (a fish) feeds on the fruit that falls from the moena tree.⟩

*n.* **yónokan** 1 : order/request ⟨**Nato asókaro sákora en yonó bóai.** I am carrying this sack of sugar because it's an order.⟩ 2 : mandate ⟨**Bená kóshi jíkiaton yonóra senénhaxonkanai.** The new chief's mandate is carried out by the people.⟩ 3 : work; *specif.* : assigned work ⟨**Jawen yonóra jonín axónke.** The man fulfilled his job.⟩ *syn.* See under **yoká**
See under **páoti**

*v.t.* **yónoa** 1 : to place an order for ⟨**Jánra yónoke paránta bíti.** He ordered bananas to be brought.⟩ 2 : to command; *specif.* : to send to work ⟨**Níiresa bákebora** **wáiroron yatánxon yónoke.** The guard caught the street kids and sent them to work.⟩ *syn.* bémati
*v.i.* **yónota** : to work; *specif.* : to work under orders *syn.* See under **téeti**
*n.* **yónoti join** [from Shipibo *yónoti* to command + *joi* word] : imperative sentence –Used as a grammar term. See Grammar Sketch 4.2.3
*adj.* **yónotiman** [from Shipibo *yónoti* to command + *-ma* not] : independent ⟨**Rámara noa Píroanobo yónotima iki.** Nowadays we Peruvians are independent.⟩
*n.* **yónshiman** : pashaca (a tree) ⟨**Titánra yonshín jíbui káro ákai.** Mom is making firewood from pashaca wood.⟩ *syn.* awápishi
*v.i.* **yóota** : to warm oneself ⟨**Nokon ochítira matsín aká yóotai chíi kexa.** My dog, when it's cold, warms itself near the fire.⟩

*n.* **yopán** : one who doesn't want to hunt, or who has poor aim ⟨**Nokon wétsa yópa ixonra tóo akin xarára kéneke.** Since my brother has poor aim, he shot at the xarara (a snake) and it got away.⟩
*n.* **yopánanin** : yupana (an Incan counting device)
*n.* **yópatatin** : a type of war dance in which a defeat or a victory was traditionally celebrated

*v.i.* **yópaa** : to become a poor hunter : to lose one's aim –Used regarding a man or a hunting dog. ⟨**Mécha ikátiibira, náto jóni yopáke.** This man used to be a good hunter, but now he has lost his aim.⟩ ⟨**Nokon ochítininra ícha manánxawe bikátiai. Ikáxbira móa yópake.** My dog used to catch many tortoises. But now it has become used to track down many tortoises, but now it has become a poor hunter.⟩

*n.* **yorán** 1 : body ⟨**Non piá iki; ikáxbi non yóra yósmares iká iki.** We ate; nevertheless, our bodies were weak.⟩ 2 : trunk ⟨**Axón yóra sibá iki, néetikoma.** The trunk of the capirona (a tree) is slippery; that's why it's hard to climb.⟩ 3 : stem ⟨**Baná jawéki riki tapónya, yóraya.** Plants have roots and stems.⟩

*also* **-ira** *adj. and n. suf.* [from Shipibo *yóra* body] : very : well : a lot; *also* : too much –Used in the form *-ira*, preceded by the letter *h*, if *-ira* follows the letter *n*. ⟨**Jakónyora riki.** It is very good.⟩ ⟨**Ikónhira yóiketianra, ea jóke.** I came because he said something very true.⟩ ⟨**Nokon mapónra chéxayorai.** My head hurts a lot.⟩ See Grammar Sketch 8.3.6 *syn.* ashón; kikín
See under **isín**
*also* **Yolánda** *n.* **Yorántanin** *also* **Yolándanin** [from Spanish *Yolanda*] –Used as a female name.
See under **wáchoati**
*v.i.* **yórona** : to suffer economic need; *also* : to struggle ⟨**jawékinin itan chópabaon yorónti** to struggle for food and clothing⟩
[from Shipibo *jáwebi, jawénbi* nothing + *yorónti, yoron* to struggle + *-yama* not + *-ai*, participial suf.] : prosperous : not in need
*v.i.* **yórona** : to be in need –Used with an object in the non-basic form. ⟨**jawékiatin yorónkin** having a need for food⟩ ⟨**Rámara ea jawénbi yorónyamai.** I no longer need anything.⟩

*n.* **yóshiman boéxetinin** [from Shipibo *yoshín, yóshiman* demon + *boéxeti* comb] : a small fish species ⟨**Enra jéne meranoa yóshiman boéxeti mérake.** I found a little *yóshiman boéxeti* fish in the water.⟩
*Konibo* **yóshiman pabískiriati** *n.* **yóshiman páxokiritinin** *Konibo* **yóshiman pabískiriatinin** : a fish species similar to the *yóshiman boéxeti* fish but longer

*n.* **yóshiman** 1 : demon : devil –*yoshín* is often used in all its senses with a modifying noun placed before it. 2 : spirit : ghost –The expression *mawá yoshín* "dead spirit" is also used in this sense. ⟨**Jéne meranoáx yoshín pikotainronki, jéne yakíke.** They say that when a ghost came out of the water, it shook itself.⟩
[from Shipibo *kaná* thunder + *yoshín* spirit] : spirit of thunder

[from Shipibo *jéne, jenén* water + *yoshín* spirit] : yacuruna (a mythical water spirit) ⟨**Jenényoshinronki yamé mashín pikotai.** They say that the yacurunas come out onto the riverbanks at night.⟩
[from Shipibo *mawá* deceased + *yoshín* spirit] : ghost ⟨**Mawáyoshinra jóxo chópa sawéya iki, páeri keska.** The ghost wears white clothing like a monk's.⟩
[from Shipibo *níi* forest + *yoshín* demon] : demon of the forest ⟨**Níiyoshinronki wíso chópa sawéya iki.** They say the forest demon dresses in black.⟩
[from Shipibo *panán* huasaí (a palm) + *yoshín* demon] : a species of demon identified with the huasaí palm
[from Shipibo *xóno* lupuna (a giant tree) + *yoshín* spirit] : mother spirit of the lupuna

*n.* yoshínbaken 1 : stutterer : one who cannot speak ⟨**Náto báke, yoshínbake iki, yóyoiamai.** This child is not able to speak.⟩ 2 : deformed; *specif.* : having a deformed foot ⟨**Aínbaon yoshínbakeronki pikóke tánto.** They say a woman gave birth to a baby with a deformed foot.⟩ 3 : crazy : a crazy person ⟨**Jatíbi yoshínbakebora yóitima iki.** All crazy people are disobedient.⟩ *syn.* See under jóikoma
*n.* **Yoshínbaon Koshin** [from Spanish *yoshínbaon*, plural form of *yoshín* devil + *kóshi* chief] : Devil : Satan *syn.* Sátanas
*v.t.* yoshínhaa [from Shipibo *yoshín* demon + *-ati, -aa* to make] : to possess with a demon
See under **ípo**
See under **kápa**

*n.* yoshínkoshkin *also* yoshínkoshkikan [from Shipibo *yoshín* spirit + *koshkíti, koshki-* to place across] : rainbow ⟨**Yoshínkoshki non métotinin métoaronkin non métoti payóti iki.** They say that if we point at the rainbow with our fingers, we can get hurt.⟩ *syn.* See under chirápa

*n.* yoshíntetekan [from Shipibo *yoshín* ghost + *teté* hawk] : a species of ghost in the form of a hawk ⟨**Yoshíntetekanronki mékayao iká mapón ísobires píai.** They say the ghost hawk eats only spider monkeys, turning its head only to the right.⟩

*v.i.* yóshina 1 : to go crazy : to become insane; *specif.* : to go crazy or become deranged from drugs ⟨**Jónira aínboki yoshínke. Yoshínbekonrake.** The man went crazy over a woman. The two of them drove each other crazy.⟩ ⟨**Sanánko xéaaxa jóni yoshínke, samá xáteax.** When the man drank sanango (a medicinal plant), having broken his diet, he became intoxicated.⟩ 2 : to become contaminated ⟨**Jónira jóboai pontónkoain, yóshini nawán jawéki méetax.** The man, having become contaminated by touching things belonging to other tribes, now has a tumor on his elbow.⟩
See under **wáste**

*also* **yoshínxetaya** *n.* **yoshínxataman yoshínxetayanin** [from Shipibo *yoshín* demon + *xatán* shaved head, or *xetaya* toothy] 1 : a species of demon with many teeth ⟨**Yoshínxatanronki téxtemis ípaonike.** They say the clown demon used to strangle people.⟩ 2 : a disguise of banana or peanut leaves and a mask used to scare misbehaving children ⟨**Yoshínxetaya keskara ián kexakea en mérake.** I found someone resembling the clown demon on the bank of the oxbow lake.⟩
*v.t.* yóshoa : to twist, to bend ⟨**Nokon kanótira, yósho ikax, jakóma iki.** My crossbow has bent and it's no longer useful to me.⟩ *syn.* éxpaati
*n.* yoshpén : ashipa (an edible tuber) ⟨**Kámpabaonra yóshpe ícha kókoai.** The Campa eat a lot of ashipa.⟩

*n.* and *adj.* **yosín** *n.* 1 : old man ⟨**Yósira jóke.** The old man came.⟩ 2 : young single man (e.g., around thirty years old) with life experience 3 : sir –Used as a respectful form of address (e.g., for a father-in-law or an unfamiliar young man). ⟨**Papánra bákeranonbo jóketian jato bikín —jowé, yósi— ápakeke.** My dad received the young men and greeted them respectfully, saying: —Good day, sirs.⟩ 4 : adult 5 : church elder 6 : grandparents : great-grandparents : blood relatives of the second or third ascending generation; *also* : forebears : ancestors –Used in the plural form *yósibo* to indicate the whole group of elderly relatives or the whole group of ancestors. *adj.* : old : mature ⟨**Ja jónira moa yósiora iki; jákopira míaareske.** That man is very mature; that's why he has beaten you.⟩ *syn.* See under **páyo** and **sinyóro** *syn.* jóchiyosi; rekén
*v.t.* **yósiaa** : to make (someone) look older ⟨**Jawen kenínbira náto jóni móa yósiake.** This man's beard makes him look older.⟩
See **pápayosi**
*n.* **yósishokon** [from Shipibo *yósi* old + *-shoko*, diminutive suf.] : grandfather : granddad : old man : little old man –Used to convey affection or fondness.
*v.i.* **yósia** : to become old : to age ⟨**Nokon pápara móa yósiai.** My dad is already getting old.⟩

*adj.* **yosmán** [from Shipibo *yósi* adult + *-ma* not] 1 : weak : lacking strength ⟨**Non piá iki; ikáxbi non yóra yósmares iká iki.** We have eaten; but nevertheless, our bodies remained weak.⟩ ⟨**Kókara ísinax yósma iki.** My uncle got sick, and that's why he looks weak.⟩ 2 : cowardly : fearful ⟨**Yósma ikáxa, nato sontáro ráketai jawen rawíki.** This soldier is afraid of his enemy because he is a coward.⟩ 3 : inexperienced : unfamiliar with a specified activity *syn.* See under **raké** *syn.* mécho; páxna

*also* **-isma** *modifying suf.* **-yosman** [from Shipibo *yósma* weak] : one who never does (a specified thing) –Used added to the verb root in the derived noun. ⟨**jóyosma** one who never comes⟩ ⟨**Náto jónira sináisma iki. Jáskara íketianra, játixonbi nóikanai.** That man is one of those who never gets angry. Because of that, everyone loves him.⟩ ⟨**Nato rakéyosmanra siná ochíti chíbanai.** That fearless one is following the fierce dog.⟩ ⟨**onánhisma** one who never knows⟩ See Grammar Sketch 7.1.7
*n.* **yótaman** : hairy spider; *specif.* : tarantula

*n.* **yótaman** : the season of cold and wind that occurs in the forest ⟨**Sánjoan píshta ochómaitian yotán pakétara kikínbires mátsi iki, eára xéta sákisaki íkai.** When the feast of San Juan approaches, the season of intense wind and cold arrives, and I am shivering with cold.⟩
*n.* **yotékanin** : yateca
*v.i.* **yóteta** : to walk on the side of one's foot ⟨**Nokon wétsara yotéke. Taskérabirake.** My brother was walking only on the side of his foot; he must have sprained it.⟩
*n.* **yotín** [from Spanish; and this from English *jute*; of Sanskrit origin] : jute ⟨**Yóti chópaakanara bási páyotai.** Cloth made of jute lasts a long time.⟩

*n.* **yótokan** : state of being bewitched –Used preceded by the possessive adjective *jahuen* "his/her". ⟨**Jawen yotó nítikoma íketianra, pápa jóyamake.** Dad didn't come because he was unable to walk, having been bewitched.⟩
*v.t.* **yótoa** : to bewitch ⟨**Rabé yobékanra nókon pápa yótoke.** Two sorcerers bewitched my father.⟩

*n. and adj.* yóxaman 1 : old woman : elderly ⟨**Yoxán jóaira nokon rayós iki.** The old woman who is coming is my mother-in-law.⟩ 2 : lady : young lady –Used as a respectful way to address or greet someone (e.g., a young woman of age but unmarried, or a married woman). ⟨**Jowé, yoxán.** Good morning, miss.⟩ *syn.* See under sinyóra *syn.* xóntako

*v.i.* **yóyo ika** 1 : to speak ⟨**Máioshiain nókotaxa, ápo yóyo ike.** When the President arrived in Pucallpa, he spoke.⟩ 2 : to converse ⟨**Noara ápo betan yóyo ike.** We conversed with the President.⟩
*v.i.* **yóyokoota** : to go to waste ⟨**Náto báritianra mánkoa bími yóyokooke.** This year the mango fruits went to waste.⟩
*v.t.* **yóyota** : to waste ⟨**Kósiniranra átapa jéne yoyóke.** The cook wasted the chicken soup.⟩
